verses.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
And the earth as aste and void; and darkness as upon the face of the deep: and the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the aters.
And God said, Let there be light: and there as light.
And God sa the light, that it as good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And there as evening and there as morning, one day.
And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the aters, and let it divide the aters from the aters.
And God made the firmament, and divided the aters hich ere under the firmament from the aters hich ere above the firmament: and it as so.
And God called the firmament Heaven. And there as evening and there as morning, a second day.
And God said, Let the aters under the heavens be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it as so.
And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the aters called he Seas: and God sa that it as good.
And God said, Let the earth put forth grass, herbs yielding seed, \add and\add* fruit-trees bearing fruit after their kind, herein is the seed thereof, upon the earth: and it as so.
And the earth brought forth grass, herbs yielding seed after their kind, and trees bearing fruit, herein is the seed thereof, after their kind: and God sa that it as good.
And there as evening and there as morning, a third day.
And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days and years:
and let them be for lights in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth: and it as so.
And God made the to great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: \add he made\add* the stars also.
And God set them in the firmament of heaven to give light upon the earth,
and to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God sa that it as good.
And there as evening and there as morning, a fourth day.
And God said, Let the aters sarm ith sarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.
And God created the great sea-monsters, and every living creature that moveth, hereith the aters sarmed, after their kind, and every inged bird after its kind: and God sa that it as good.
And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the aters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.
And there as evening and there as morning, a fifth day.
And God said, Let the earth bring forth living creatures after their kind, cattle, and creeping things, and beasts of the earth after their kind: and it as so.
And God made the beasts of the earth after their kind, and the cattle after their kind, and everything that creepeth upon the ground after its kind: and God sa that it as good.

And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the heavens, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
And God created man in his on image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.

And God blessed them: and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it; and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the heavens, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.
And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, hich is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in hich is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for food:

and to every beast of the earth, and to every bird of the heavens, and to everything that creepeth upon the earth, herein there is life, \add I have given\add* every green herb for food: and it as so.
And God sa everything that he had made, and, behold, it as very good. And there as evening and there as morning, the sixth day.
And the heavens and the earth ere finished, and all the host of them.
And on the seventh day God finished his ork hich he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his ork hich he had made.
And God blessed the seventh day, and halloed it; because that in it he rested from all his ork hich God had created and made.
These are the generations of the heavens and of the earth hen they ere created, in the day that Jehovah God made earth and heaven.
And no plant of the field as yet in the earth, and no herb of the field had yet sprung up; for Jehovah God had not caused it to rain upon the earth: and there as not a man to till the ground;
but there ent up a mist from the earth, and atered the hole face of the ground.
And Jehovah God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
And Jehovah God planted a garden eastard, in Eden; and there he put the man hom he had formed.

And out of the ground made Jehovah God to gro every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knoledge of good and evil.
And a river ent out of Eden to ater the garden; and from thence it as parted, and became four heads.
The name of the first is Pishon: that is it hich compasseth the hole land of Havilah, here there is gold;
and the gold of that land is good: there is bdellium and the onyx stone.
And the name of the second river is Gihon: the same is it that compasseth the hole land of Cush.
And the name of the third river is Hiddekel: that is it hich goeth in front of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
And Jehovah God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.
And Jehovah God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:
but of the tree of the knoledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
And Jehovah God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I ill make him a help meet for him.

And out of the ground Jehovah God formed every beast of the field, and every bird of the heavens; and brought them unto the man to see hat he ould call them: and hatsoever the man called every living creature, that as the name thereof.
And the man gave names to all cattle, and to the birds of the heavens, and to every beast of the field; but for man there as not found a help meet for him.
And Jehovah God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and he slept; and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof:
and the rib, hich Jehovah God had taken from the man, made he a oman, and brought her unto the man.
And the man said, This is no bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she as taken out of Man.
Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his ife: and they shall be one flesh.
And they ere both naked, the man and his ife, and ere not ashamed.
No the serpent as more subtle than any beast of the field hich Jehovah God had made. And he said unto the oman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of any tree of the garden?
And the oman said unto the serpent, Of the fruit of the trees of the garden e may eat:
but of the fruit of the tree hich is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.
And the serpent said unto the oman, Ye shall not surely die:
for God doth kno that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as God, knoing good and evil.

And hen the oman sa that the tree as good for food, and that it as a delight to the eyes, and that the tree as to be desired to make one ise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat; and she gave also unto her husband ith her, and he did eat.
And the eyes of them both ere opened, and they kne that they ere naked; and they seed fig-leaves together, and made themselves aprons.
And they heard the voice of Jehovah God alking in the garden in the cool of the day: and the man and his ife hid themselves from the presence of Jehovah God amongst the trees of the garden.
And Jehovah God called unto the man, and said unto him, Where art thou?
And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I as afraid, because I as naked; and I hid myself.
And he said, Who told thee that thou ast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, hereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?
And the man said, The oman hom thou gavest to be ith me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.
And Jehovah God said unto the oman, What is this thou hast done? And the oman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

And Jehovah God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, cursed art thou above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:
and I ill put enmity beteen thee and the oman, and beteen thy seed and her seed: he shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
Unto the oman he said, I ill greatly multiply thy pain and thy conception; in pain thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.

And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy ife, and hast eaten of the tree, of hich I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in toil shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life;
thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field;
in the seat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it ast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
And the man called his ife’s name Eve; because she as the mother of all living.
And Jehovah God made for Adam and for his ife coats of skins, and clothed them.
And Jehovah God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to kno good and evil; and no, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever—
therefore Jehovah God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from hence he as taken.
So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden the Cherubim, and the flame of a sord hich turned every ay, to keep the ay of the tree of life.
And the man kne Eve his ife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man ith \add the help of\add* Jehovah.
And again she bare his brother Abel. And Abel as a keeper of sheep, but Cain as a tiller of the ground.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto Jehovah.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And Jehovah had respect unto Abel and to his offering:
but unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain as very roth, and his countenance fell.
And Jehovah said unto Cain, Why art thou roth? and hy is thy countenance fallen?
If thou doest ell, shall it not be lifted up? and if thou doest not ell, sin coucheth at the door; and unto thee shall be its desire; but do thou rule over it.
And Cain told Abel his brother. And it came to pass, hen they ere in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and sle him.
And Jehovah said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I kno not: am I my brother’s keeper?
And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.
And no cursed art thou from the ground, hich hath opened its mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand;
hen thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee its strength; a fugitive and a anderer shalt thou be in the earth.
And Cain said unto Jehovah, My punishment is greater than I can bear.

Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the ground; and from thy face shall I be hid; and I shall be a fugitive and a anderer in the earth; and it ill come to pass, that hosoever findeth me ill slay me.
And Jehovah said unto him, Therefore hosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And Jehovah appointed a sign for Cain, lest any finding him should smite him.
And Cain ent out from the presence of Jehovah, and delt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.
And Cain kne his ife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.
And unto Enoch as born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael; and Mehujael begat Methushael; and Methushael begat Lamech.
And Lamech took unto him to ives: the name of the one as Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
And Adah bare Jabal: he as the father of such as dell in tents and \add have\add* cattle.
And his brother’s name as Jubal: he as the father of all such as handle the harp and pipe.
And Zillah, she also bare Tubal-cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal-cain as Naamah.
And Lamech said unto his ives: Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; Ye ives of Lamech, hearken unto my speech: For I have slain a man for ounding me, And a young man for bruising me:
If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, Truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.
And Adam kne his ife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For, \add said she\add*, God hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel; for Cain sle him.
And to Seth, to him also there as born a son; and he called his name Enosh. Then began men to call upon the name of Jehovah.
This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him;
male and female created he them, and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day hen they ere created.
And Adam lived a hundred and thirty years, and begat \add a son\add* in his on likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:
and the days of Adam after he begat Seth ere eight hundred years: and he begat sons and daughters.
And all the days that Adam lived ere nine hundred and thirty years: and he died.
And Seth lived a hundred and five years, and begat Enosh:
and Seth lived after he begat Enosh eight hundred and seven years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Seth ere nine hundred and telve years: and he died.
And Enosh lived ninety years, and begat Kenan:
and Enosh lived after he begat Kenan eight hundred and fifteen years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Enosh ere nine hundred and five years: and he died.
And Kenan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalalel:
and Kenan lived after he begat Mahalalel eight hundred and forty years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Kenan ere nine hundred and ten years: and he died.
And Mahalalel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jared:
and Mahalalel lived after he begat Jared eight hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Mahalalel ere eight hundred ninety and five years: and he died.
And Jared lived a hundred sixty and to years, and begat Enoch:
and Jared lived after he begat Enoch eight hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Jared ere nine hundred sixty and to years: and he died.
And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah:
and Enoch alked ith God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Enoch ere three hundred sixty and five years:
and Enoch alked ith God: and he as not; for God took him.
And Methuselah lived a hundred eighty and seven years, and begat Lamech:
and Methuselah lived after he begat Lamech seven hundred eighty and to years, and begat sons and daughters:
and all the days of Methuselah ere nine hundred sixty and nine years: and he died.
And Lamech lived a hundred eighty and to years, and begat a son:
and he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us in our ork and in the toil of our hands, \add hich cometh\add* because of the ground hich Jehovah hath cursed.
And Lamech lived after he begat Noah five hundred ninety and five years, and begat sons and daughters:
And all the days of Lamech ere seven hundred seventy and seven years: and he died.
And Noah as five hundred years old: and Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And it came to pass, hen men began to multiply on the face of the ground, and daughters ere born unto them,
that the sons of God sa the daughters of men that they ere fair; and they took them ives of all that they chose.
And Jehovah said, My Spirit shall not strive ith man for ever, for that he also is flesh: yet shall his days be a hundred and tenty years.

The Nephilim ere in the earth in those days, and also after that, hen the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them: the same ere the mighty men that ere of old, the men of renon.
And Jehovah sa that the ickedness of man as great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart as only evil continually.
And it repented Jehovah that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.
And Jehovah said, I ill destroy man hom I have created from the face of the ground; both man, and beast, and creeping things, and birds of the heavens; for it repenteth me that I have made them.
But Noah found favor in the eyes of Jehovah.
These are the generations of Noah. Noah as a righteous man, \add and\add* perfect in his generations: Noah alked ith God.
And Noah begat three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And the earth as corrupt before God, and the earth as filled ith violence.
And God sa the earth, and, behold, it as corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted their ay upon the earth.
And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled ith violence through them; and, behold, I ill destroy them ith the earth.
Make thee an ark of gopher ood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it ithin and ithout ith pitch.
And this is ho thou shalt make it: the length of the ark three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
A light shalt thou make to the ark, and to a cubit shalt thou finish it upard; and the door of the ark shalt thou set in the side thereof; ith loer, second, and third stories shalt thou make it.
And I, behold, I do bring the flood of aters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, herein is the breath of life, from under heaven; everything that is in the earth shall die.
But I ill establish my covenant ith thee; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy ife, and thy sons’ ives ith thee.
And of every living thing of all flesh, to of every sort shalt thou bring into the ark, to keep them alive ith thee; they shall be male and female.
Of the birds after their kind, and of the cattle after their kind, of every creeping thing of the ground after its kind, to of every sort shall come unto thee, to keep them alive.
And take thou unto thee of all food that is eaten, and gather it to thee; and it shall be for food for thee, and for them.
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
And Jehovah said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
Of every clean beast thou shalt take to thee seven and seven, the male and his female; and of the beasts that are not clean to, the male and his female:
of the birds also of the heavens, seven and seven, male and female, to keep seed alive upon the face of all the earth.
For yet seven days, and I ill cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and every living thing that I have made ill I destroy from off the face of the ground.
And Noah did according unto all that Jehovah commanded him.
And Noah as six hundred years old hen the flood of aters as upon the earth.
And Noah ent in, and his sons, and his ife, and his sons’ ives ith him, into the ark, because of the aters of the flood.
Of clean beasts, and of beasts that are not clean, and of birds, and of everything that creepeth upon the ground,
there ent in to and to unto Noah into the ark, male and female, as God commanded Noah.
And it came to pass after the seven days, that the aters of the flood ere upon the earth.

In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on the same day ere all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the indos of heaven ere opened.
And the rain as upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
In the selfsame day entered Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah’s ife, and the three ives of his sons ith them, into the ark;

they, and every beast after its kind, and all the cattle after their kind, and every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth after its kind, and every bird after its kind, every bird of every sort.
And they ent in unto Noah into the ark, to and to of all flesh herein is the breath of life.
And they that ent in, ent in male and female of all flesh, as God commanded him: and Jehovah shut him in.
And the flood as forty days upon the earth; and the aters increased, and bare up the ark, and it as lifted up above the earth.
And the aters prevailed, and increased greatly upon the earth; and the ark ent upon the face of the aters.
And the aters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth; and all the high mountains that ere under the hole heaven ere covered.
Fifteen cubits upard did the aters prevail; and the mountains ere covered.
And all flesh died that moved upon the earth, both birds, and cattle, and beasts, and every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth, and every man:
all in hose nostrils as the breath of the spirit of life, of all that as on the dry land, died.

And every living thing as destroyed that as upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and creeping things, and birds of the heavens; and they ere destroyed from the earth: and Noah only as left, and they that ere ith him in the ark.
And the aters prevailed upon the earth a hundred and fifty days.
And God remembered Noah, and all the beasts, and all the cattle that ere ith him in the ark: and God made a ind to pass over the earth, and the aters assuaged;
the fountains also of the deep and the indos of heaven ere stopped, and the rain from heaven as restrained;
and the aters returned from off the earth continually: and after the end of a hundred and fifty days the aters decreased.
And the ark rested in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
And the aters decreased continually until the tenth month: in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, ere the tops of the mountains seen.
And it came to pass at the end of forty days, that Noah opened the indo of the ark hich he had made:
and he sent forth a raven, and it ent forth to and fro, until the aters ere dried up from off the earth.
And he sent forth a dove from him, to see if the aters ere abated from off the face of the ground;

but the dove found no rest for the sole of her foot, and she returned unto him to the ark; for the aters ere on the face of the hole earth: and he put forth his hand, and took her, and brought her in unto him into the ark.
And he stayed yet other seven days; and again he sent forth the dove out of the ark;
and the dove came in to him at eventide; and, lo, in her mouth an olive-leaf plucked off: so Noah kne that the aters ere abated from off the earth.
And he stayed yet other seven days, and sent forth the dove; and she returned not again unto him any more.

And it came to pass in the six hundred and first year, in the first month, the first day of the month, the aters ere dried up from off the earth: and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and, behold, the face of the ground as dried.
And in the second month, on the seven and tentieth day of the month, as the earth dry.
And God spake unto Noah, saying,
Go forth from the ark, thou, and thy ife, and thy sons, and thy sons’ ives ith thee.

Bring forth ith thee every living thing that is ith thee of all flesh, both birds, and cattle, and every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth; that they may breed abundantly in the earth, and be fruitful, and multiply upon the earth.
And Noah ent forth, and his sons, and his ife, and his sons’ ives ith him:
every beast, every creeping thing, and every bird, hatsoever moveth upon the earth, after their families, ent forth out of the ark.
And Noah builded an altar unto Jehovah, and took of every clean beast, and of every clean bird, and offered burnt-offerings on the altar.

And Jehovah smelled the seet savor; and Jehovah said in his heart, I ill not again curse the ground any more for man’s sake, for that the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth; neither ill I again smite any more everything living, as I have done.
While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and inter, and day and night shall not cease.
And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth.

And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every bird of the heavens; ith all hereith the ground teemeth, and all the fishes of the sea, into your hand are they delivered.
Every moving thing that liveth shall be food for you; as the green herb have I given you all.
But flesh ith the life thereof, \add hich is\add* the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.

And surely your blood, \add the blood\add* of your lives, ill I require; at the hand of every beast ill I require it: and at the hand of man, even at the hand of every man’s brother, ill I require the life of man.
Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.
And you, be ye fruitful, and multiply; bring forth abundantly in the earth, and multiply therein.
And God spake unto Noah, and to his sons ith him, saying,
And I, behold, I establish my covenant ith you, and ith your seed after you;
and ith every living creature that is ith you, the birds, the cattle, and every beast of the earth ith you; of all that go out of the ark, even every beast of the earth.
And I ill establish my covenant ith you; neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the aters of the flood; neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.
And God said, This is the token of the covenant hich I make beteen me and you and every living creature that is ith you, for perpetual generations:
I do set my bo in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant beteen me and the earth.
And it shall come to pass, hen I bring a cloud over the earth, that the bo shall be seen in the cloud,
and I ill remember my covenant, hich is beteen me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the aters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
And the bo shall be in the cloud; and I ill look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant beteen God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth.
And God said unto Noah, This is the token of the covenant hich I have established beteen me and all flesh that is upon the earth.
And the sons of Noah, that ent forth from the ark, ere Shem, and Ham, and Japheth: and Ham is the father of Canaan.
These three ere the sons of Noah: and of these as the hole earth overspread.
And Noah began to be a husbandman, and planted a vineyard:
and he drank of the ine, and as drunken; and he as uncovered ithin his tent.
And Ham, the father of Canaan, sa the nakedness of his father, and told his to brethren ithout.

And Shem and Japheth took a garment, and laid it upon both their shoulders, and ent backard, and covered the nakedness of their father; and their faces ere backard, and they sa not their father’s nakedness.
And Noah aoke from his ine, and kne hat his youngest son had done unto him.
And he said, Cursed be Canaan; A servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.
And he said, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Shem; And let Canaan be his servant.
God enlarge Japheth, And let him dell in the tents of Shem; And let Canaan be his servant.
And Noah lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.
And all the days of Noah ere nine hundred and fifty years: and he died.
No these are the generations of the sons of Noah, \add namely\add*, of Shem, Ham, and Japheth: and unto them ere sons born after the flood.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.
And the sons of Javan: Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
Of these ere the isles of the nations divided in their lands, every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.
And the sons of Ham: Cush, and Mizraim, and Put, and Canaan.
And the sons of Cush: Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabteca; and the sons of Raamah: Sheba, and Dedan.
And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.
He as a mighty hunter before Jehovah: herefore it is said, Like Nimrod a mighty hunter before Jehovah.
And the beginning of his kingdom as Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
Out of that land he ent forth into Assyria, and builded Nineveh, and Rehoboth-Ir, and Calah,
and Resen beteen Nineveh and Calah ( the same is the great city).
And Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,
and Pathrusim, and Casluhim (hence ent forth the Philistines), and Caphtorim.
And Canaan begat Sidon his first-born, and Heth,

Haste thee, escape thither; for I cannot do anything till thou be come thither. Therefore the name of the city as called Zoar.
The sun as risen upon the earth hen Lot came unto Zoar.
Then Jehovah rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Jehovah out of heaven;
and he overthre those cities, and all the Plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that hich gre upon the ground.
But his ife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
And Abraham gat up early in the morning to the place here he had stood before Jehovah:
and he looked toard Sodom and Gomorrah, and toard all the land of the Plain, and beheld, and, lo, the smoke of the land ent up as the smoke of a furnace.
And it came to pass, hen God destroyed the cities of the Plain, that God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthro, hen he overthre the cities in hich Lot delt.
And Lot ent up out of Zoar, and delt in the mountain, and his to daughters ith him; for he feared to dell in Zoar: and he delt in a cave, he and his to daughters.
And the first-born said unto the younger, Our father is old, and there is not a man in the earth to come in unto us after the manner of all the earth:
come, let us make our father drink ine, and e ill lie ith him, that e may preserve seed of our father.
And they made their father drink ine that night: and the first-born ent in, and lay ith her father; and he kne not hen she lay don, nor hen she arose.

And it came to pass on the morro, that the first-born said unto the younger, Behold, I lay yesternight ith my father: let us make him drink ine this night also; and go thou in, and lie ith him, that e may preserve seed of our father.
And they made their father drink ine that night also: and the younger arose, and lay ith him; and he kne not hen she lay don, nor hen she arose.
Thus ere both the daughters of Lot ith child by their father.
And the first-born bare a son, and called his name Moab: the same is the father of the Moabites unto this day.
And the younger, she also bare a son, and called his name Ben-ammi: the same is the father of the children of Ammon unto this day.
And Abraham journeyed from thence toard the land of the South, and delt beteen Kadesh and Shur; and he sojourned in Gerar.
And Abraham said of Sarah his ife, She is my sister: and Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night, and said to him, Behold, thou art but a dead man, because of the oman hom thou hast taken; for she is a man’s ife.
No Abimelech had not come near her: and he said, Lord, ilt thou slay even a righteous nation?
Said he not himself unto me, She is my sister? and she, even she herself said, He is my brother: in the integrity of my heart and the innocency of my hands have I done this.
And God said unto him in the dream, Yea, I kno that in the integrity of thy heart thou hast done this, and I also ithheld thee from sinning against me: therefore suffered I thee not to touch her.

No therefore restore the man’s ife; for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live: and if thou restore her not, kno thou that thou shalt surely die, thou, and all that are thine.
And Abimelech rose early in the morning, and called all his servants, and told all these things in their ears: and the men ere sore afraid.

Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said unto him, What hast thou done unto us? and herein have I sinned against thee, that thou hast brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? thou hast done deeds unto me that ought not to be done.
And Abimelech said unto Abraham, What saest thou, that thou hast done this thing?
And Abraham said, Because I thought, Surely the fear of God is not in this place; and they ill slay me for my ife’s sake.
And moreover she is indeed my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my ife:

and it came to pass, hen God caused me to ander from my father’s house, that I said unto her, This is thy kindness hich thou shalt sho unto me: at every place hither e shall come, say of me, He is my brother.
And Abimelech took sheep and oxen, and men-servants and omen-servants, and gave them unto Abraham, and restored him Sarah his ife.
And Abimelech said, Behold, my land is before thee: dell here it pleaseth thee.
And unto Sarah he said, Behold, I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver: behold, it is for thee a covering of the eyes to all that are ith thee; and in respect of all thou art righted.
And Abraham prayed unto God: and God healed Abimelech, and his ife, and his maid-servants; and they bare children.
For Jehovah had fast closed up all the ombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah, Abraham’s ife.
And Jehovah visited Sarah as he had said, and Jehovah did unto Sarah as he had spoken.
And Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of hich God had spoken to him.
And Abraham called the name of his son that as born unto him, hom Sarah bare to him, Isaac.
And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac hen he as eight days old, as God had commanded him.
And Abraham as a hundred years old, hen his son Isaac as born unto him.
And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh; every one that heareth ill laugh ith me.
And she said, Who ould have said unto Abraham, that Sarah should give children suck? for I have borne him a son in his old age.
And the child gre, and as eaned: and Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac as eaned.
And Sarah sa the son of Hagar the Egyptian, hom she had borne unto Abraham, mocking.
Wherefore she said unto Abraham, Cast out this handmaid and her son: for the son of this handmaid shall not be heir ith my son, even ith Isaac.
And the thing as very grievous in Abraham’s sight on account of his son.

And God said unto Abraham, Let it not be grievous in thy sight because of the lad, and because of thy handmaid; in all that Sarah saith unto thee, hearken unto her voice; for in Isaac shall thy seed be called.
And also of the son of the handmaid ill I make a nation, because he is thy seed.

And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and took bread and a bottle of ater, and gave it unto Hagar, putting it on her shoulder, and \add gave her\add* the child, and sent her aay: and she departed, and andered in the ilderness of Beer-sheba.
And the ater in the bottle as spent, and she cast the child under one of the shrubs.

And she ent, and sat her don over against him a good ay off, as it ere a boshot: for she said, Let me not look upon the death of the child. And she sat over against him, and lifted up her voice, and ept.
And God heard the voice of the lad; and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said unto her, What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad here he is.
Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him in thy hand; for I ill make him a great nation.
And God opened her eyes, and she sa a ell of ater; and she ent, and filled the bottle ith ater, and gave the lad drink.
And God as ith the lad, and he gre; and he delt in the ilderness, and became, as he gre up, an archer.
And he delt in the ilderness of Paran: and his mother took him a ife out of the land of Egypt.
And it came to pass at that time, that Abimelech and Phicol the captain of his host spake unto Abraham, saying, God is ith thee in all that thou doest:

no therefore sear unto me here by God that thou ilt not deal falsely ith me, nor ith my son, nor ith my son’s son: but according to the kindness that I have done unto thee, thou shalt do unto me, and to the land herein thou hast sojourned.
And Abraham said, I ill sear.
And Abraham reproved Abimelech because of the ell of ater, hich Abimelech’s servants had violently taken aay.
And Abimelech said, I kno not ho hath done this thing: neither didst thou tell me, neither yet heard I of it, but to-day.
And Abraham took sheep and oxen, and gave them unto Abimelech; and they to made a covenant.
And Abraham set seven ee lambs of the flock by themselves.
And Abimelech said unto Abraham, What mean these seven ee lambs hich thou hast set by themselves?
And he said, These seven ee lambs shalt thou take of my hand, that it may be a itness unto me, that I have digged this ell.
Wherefore he called that place Beer-sheba; because there they sare both of them.
So they made a covenant at Beer-sheba: and Abimelech rose up, and Phicol the captain of his host, and they returned into the land of the Philistines.
And \add Abraham\add* planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of Jehovah, the Everlasting God.
And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.
And it came to pass after these things, that God did prove Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham; and he said, Here am I.

And he said, Take no thy son, thine only son, hom thou lovest, even Isaac, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt-offering upon one of the mountains hich I ill tell thee of.

And Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took to of his young men ith him, and Isaac his son; and he clave the ood for the burnt-offering, and rose up, and ent unto the place of hich God had told him.
On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and sa the place afar off.
And Abraham said unto his young men, Abide ye here ith the ass, and I and the lad ill go yonder; and e ill orship, and come again to you.
And Abraham took the ood of the burnt-offering, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took in his hand the fire and the knife; and they ent both of them together.
And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, Behold, the fire and the ood: but here is the lamb for a burnt-offering?
And Abraham said, God ill provide himself the lamb for a burnt-offering, my son: so they ent both of them together.
And they came to the place hich God had told him of; and Abraham built the altar there, and laid the ood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, upon the ood.
And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.
And the angel of Jehovah called unto him out of heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here am I.
And he said, Lay not thy hand upon the lad, neither do thou anything unto him; for no I kno that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not ithheld thy son, thine only son, from me.

And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, behind \add him\add* a ram caught in the thicket by his horns: and Abraham ent and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt-offering in the stead of his son.
And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah-jireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of Jehovah it shall be provided.
And the angel of Jehovah called unto Abraham a second time out of heaven,
and said, By myself have I sorn, saith Jehovah, because thou hast done this thing, and hast not ithheld thy son, thine only son,

that in blessing I ill bless thee, and in multiplying I ill multiply thy seed as the stars of the heavens, and as the sand hich is upon the sea-shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;
and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.
So Abraham returned unto his young men, and they rose up and ent together to Beer-sheba; and Abraham delt at Beer-sheba.
And it came to pass after these things, that it as told Abraham, saying, Behold, Milcah, she also hath borne children unto thy brother Nahor:
Uz his first-born, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
and Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.
And Bethuel begat Rebekah: these eight did Milcah bear to Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
And his concubine, hose name as Reumah, she also bare Tebah, and Gaham, and Tahash, and Maacah.
And the life of Sarah as a hundred and seven and tenty years: these ere the years of the life of Sarah.
And Sarah died in Kiriath-arba ( the same is Hebron), in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to eep for her.
And Abraham rose up from before his dead, and spake unto the children of Heth, saying,
I am a stranger and a sojourner ith you: give me a possession of a burying-place ith you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.
And the children of Heth ansered Abraham, saying unto him,
Hear us, my lord; thou art a prince of God among us: in the choice of our sepulchres bury thy dead; none of us shall ithhold from thee his sepulchre, but that thou mayest bury thy dead.
And Abraham rose up, and boed himself to the people of the land, even to the children of Heth.
And he communed ith them, saying, If it be your mind that I should bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and entreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,
that he may give me the cave of Machpelah, hich he hath, hich is in the end of his field; for the full price let him give it to me in the midst of you for a possession of a burying-place.
No Ephron as sitting in the midst of the children of Heth: and Ephron the Hittite ansered Abraham in the audience of the children of Heth, even of all that ent in at the gate of his city, saying,
Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I thee, and the cave that is therein, I give it thee; in the presence of the children of my people give I it thee: bury thy dead.
And Abraham boed himself don before the people of the land.
And he spake unto Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, But if thou ilt, I pray thee, hear me: I ill give the price of the field; take it of me, and I ill bury my dead there.
And Ephron ansered Abraham, saying unto him,
My lord, hearken unto me: a piece of land orth four hundred shekels of silver, hat is that betixt me and thee? bury therefore thy dead.

And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham eighed to Ephron the silver hich he had named in the audience of the children of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current \add money\add* ith the merchant.

So the field of Ephron, hich as in Machpelah, hich as before Mamre, the field, and the cave hich as therein, and all the trees that ere in the field, that ere in all the border thereof round about, ere made sure
unto Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all that ent in at the gate of his city.
And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his ife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre ( the same is Hebron), in the land of Canaan.
And the field, and the cave that is therein, ere made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a burying-place by the children of Heth.
And Abraham as old, \add and\add* ell stricken in age: and Jehovah had blessed Abraham in all things.
And Abraham said unto his servant, the elder of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:
and I ill make thee sear by Jehovah, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that thou ilt not take a ife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among hom I dell:
but thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a ife for my son Isaac.
And the servant said unto him, Peradventure the oman ill not be illing to follo me unto this land: must I needs bring thy son again unto the land from hence thou camest?
And Abraham said unto him, Beare thou that thou bring not my son thither again.

Jehovah, the God of heaven, ho took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my nativity, and ho spake unto me, and ho sare unto me, saying, Unto thy seed ill I give this land; he ill send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a ife for my son from thence.
And if the oman be not illing to follo thee, then thou shalt be clear from this my oath; only thou shalt not bring my son thither again.
And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and sare to him concerning this matter.
And the servant took ten camels, of the camels of his master, and departed, having all goodly things of his master’s in his hand: and he arose, and ent to Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor.
And he made the camels to kneel don ithout the city by the ell of ater at the time of evening, the time that omen go out to dra ater.
And he said, O Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, send me, I pray thee, good speed this day, and sho kindness unto my master Abraham.
Behold, I am standing by the fountain of ater; and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to dra ater:

and let it come to pass, that the damsel to hom I shall say, Let don thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I ill give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I kno that thou hast shoed kindness unto my master.
And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, ho as born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the ife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, ith her pitcher upon her shoulder.
And the damsel as very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man knon her: and she ent don to the fountain, and filled her pitcher, and came up.
And the servant ran to meet her, and said, Give me to drink, I pray thee, a little ater from thy pitcher.
And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let don her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink.
And hen she had done giving him drink, she said, I ill dra for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.
And she hasted, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again unto the ell to dra, and dre for all his camels.
And the man looked stedfastly on her, holding his peace, to kno hether Jehovah had made his journey prosperous or not.
And it came to pass, as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden ring of half a shekel eight, and to bracelets for her hands of ten shekels eight of gold,
and said, Whose daughter art thou? tell me, I pray thee. Is there room in thy father’s house for us to lodge in?
And she said unto him, I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, hom she bare unto Nahor.
She said moreover unto him, We have both stra and provender enough, and room to lodge in.
And the man boed his head, and orshipped Jehovah.

And he said, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, ho hath not forsaken his lovingkindness and his truth toard my master: as for me, Jehovah hath led me in the ay to the house of my master’s brethren.
And the damsel ran, and told her mother’s house according to these ords.
And Rebekah had a brother, and his name as Laban: and Laban ran out unto the man, unto the fountain.

And it came to pass, hen he sa the ring, and the bracelets upon his sister’s hands, and hen he heard the ords of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spake the man unto me; that he came unto the man; and, behold, he as standing by the camels at the fountain.
And he said, Come in, thou blessed of Jehovah; herefore standest thou ithout? for I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.
And the man came into the house, and he ungirded the camels; and he gave stra and provender for the camels, and ater to ash his feet and the feet of the men that ere ith him.
And there as set food before him to eat: but he said, I ill not eat, until I have told mine errand. And he said, Speak on.
And he said, I am Abraham’s servant.
And Jehovah hath blessed my master greatly; and he is become great: and he hath given him flocks and herds, and silver and gold, and men-servants and maid-servants, and camels and asses.
And Sarah my master’s ife bare a son to my master hen she as old: and unto him hath he given all that he hath.
And my master made me sear, saying, Thou shalt not take a ife for my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, in hose land I dell:
but thou shalt go unto my father’s house, and to my kindred, and take a ife for my son.
And I said unto my master, Peradventure the oman ill not follo me.
And he said unto me, Jehovah, before hom I alk, ill send his angel ith thee, and prosper thy ay; and thou shalt take a ife for my son of my kindred, and of my father’s house:
then shalt thou be clear from my oath, hen thou comest to my kindred; and if they give her not to thee, thou shalt be clear from my oath.
And I came this day unto the fountain, and said, O Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, if no thou do prosper my ay hich I go:
behold, I am standing by the fountain of ater; and let it come to pass, that the maiden that cometh forth to dra, to hom I shall say, Give me, I pray thee, a little ater from thy pitcher to drink;
and she shall say to me, Both drink thou, and I ill also dra for thy camels: let the same be the oman hom Jehovah hath appointed for my master’s son.
And before I had done speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came forth ith her pitcher on her shoulder; and she ent don unto the fountain, and dre: and I said unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee.
And she made haste, and let don her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, Drink, and I ill give thy camels drink also: so I drank, and she made the camels drink also.
And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter art thou? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, hom Milcah bare unto him: and I put the ring upon her nose, and the bracelets upon her hands.
And I boed my head, and orshipped Jehovah, and blessed Jehovah, the God of my master Abraham, ho had led me in the right ay to take my master’s brother’s daughter for his son.
And no if ye ill deal kindly and truly ith my master, tell me: and if not, tell me; that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.
Then Laban and Bethuel ansered and said, The thing proceedeth from Jehovah: e cannot speak unto thee bad or good.
Behold, Rebekah is before thee, take her, and go, and let her be thy master’s son’s ife, as Jehovah hath spoken.
And it came to pass, that, hen Abraham’s servant heard their ords, he boed himself don to the earth unto Jehovah.
And the servant brought forth jeels of silver, and jeels of gold, and raiment, and gave them to Rebekah: he gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things.
And they did eat and drink, he and the men that ere ith him, and tarried all night; and they rose up in the morning, and he said, Send me aay unto my master.
And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide ith us \add a fe\add* days, at the least ten; after that she shall go.
And he said unto them, Hinder me not, seeing Jehovah hath prospered my ay; send me aay that I may go to my master.
And they said, We ill call the damsel, and inquire at her mouth.
And they called Rebekah, and said unto her, Wilt thou go ith this man? And she said, I ill go.
And they sent aay Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham’s servant, and his men.
And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Our sister, be thou \add the mother\add* of thousands of ten thousands, and let thy seed possess the gate of those that hate them.
And Rebekah arose, and her damsels, and they rode upon the camels, and folloed the man: and the servant took Rebekah, and ent his ay.
And Isaac came from the ay of Beer-lahai-roi; for he delt in the land of the South.
And Isaac ent out to meditate in the field at the eventide: and he lifted up his eyes, and sa, and, behold, there ere camels coming.
And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and hen she sa Isaac, she alighted from the camel.
And she said unto the servant, What man is this that alketh in the field to meet us? And the servant said, It is my master: and she took her veil, and covered herself.
And the servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.
And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his ife; and he loved her. And Isaac as comforted after his mother’s death.
And Abraham took another ife, and her name as Keturah.
And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan ere Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim.
And the sons of Midian: Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these ere the children of Keturah.
And Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac.
But unto the sons of the concubines, that Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts; and he sent them aay from Isaac his son, hile he yet lived, eastard, unto the east country.
And these are the days of the years of Abraham’s life hich he lived, a hundred threescore and fifteen years.
And Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full \add of years\add*, and as gathered to his people.
And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, hich is before Mamre;
the field hich Abraham purchased of the children of Heth: there as Abraham buried, and Sarah his ife.
And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blessed Isaac his son: and Isaac delt by Beer-lahai-roi.
No these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, hom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid, bare unto Abraham:
and these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the first-born of Ishmael, Nebaioth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
and Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
Hadad, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
these are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their villages, and by their encampments; telve princes according to their nations.
And these are the years of the life of Ishmael, a hundred and thirty and seven years: and he gave up the ghost and died, and as gathered unto his people.
And they delt from Havilah unto Shur that is before Egypt, as thou goest toard Assyria: he abode over against all his brethren.
And these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham begat Isaac:
and Isaac as forty years old hen he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Syrian, to be his ife.
And Isaac entreated Jehovah for his ife, because she as barren: and Jehovah as entreated of him, and Rebekah his ife conceived.
And the children struggled together ithin her; and she said, If it be so, herefore do I live? And she ent to inquire of Jehovah.

And Jehovah said unto her, To nations are in thy omb, And to peoples shall be separated from thy boels: And the one people shall be stronger than the other people; And the elder shall serve the younger.
And hen her days to be delivered ere fulfilled, behold, there ere tins in her omb.
And the first came forth red, all over like a hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.
And after that came forth his brother, and his hand had hold on Esau’s heel; and his name as called Jacob: and Isaac as threescore years old hen she bare them.
And the boys gre: and Esau as a skilful hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob as a quiet man, delling in tents.
No Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: and Rebekah loved Jacob.
And Jacob boiled pottage: and Esau came in from the field, and he as faint:
and Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, ith that same red \add pottage\add*; for I am faint: therefore as his name called Edom.
And Jacob said, Sell me first thy birthright.
And Esau said, Behold, I am about to die: and hat profit shall the birthright do to me?
And Jacob said, Sear to me first; and he sare unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob.
And Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentils; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and ent his ay: so Esau despised his birthright.
And there as a famine in the land, besides the first famine that as in the days of Abraham. And Isaac ent unto Abimelech king of the Philistines, unto Gerar.
And Jehovah appeared unto him, and said, Go not don into Egypt; dell in the land hich I shall tell thee of:
sojourn in this land, and I ill be ith thee, and ill bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I ill give all these lands, and I ill establish the oath hich I sare unto Abraham thy father;
and I ill multiply thy seed as the stars of heaven, and ill give unto thy seed all these lands; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;
because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my las.
And Isaac delt in Gerar:

and the men of the place asked him of his ife; and he said, She is my sister: for he feared to say, My ife; lest, \add said he\add*, the men of the place should kill me for Rebekah; because she as fair to look upon.
And it came to pass, hen he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a indo, and sa, and, behold, Isaac as sporting ith Rebekah his ife.
And Abimelech called Isaac, and said, Behold, of a surety she is thy ife: and ho saidst thou, She is my sister? And Isaac said unto him, Because I said, Lest I die because of her.
And Abimelech said, What is this thou hast done unto us? one of the people might easily have lain ith thy ife, and thou ouldest have brought guiltiness upon us.
And Abimelech charged all the people, saying, He that toucheth this man or his ife shall surely be put to death.
And Isaac soed in that land, and found in the same year a hundredfold: and Jehovah blessed him.
And the man axed great, and gre more and more until he became very great:
and he had possessions of flocks, and possessions of herds, and a great household: and the Philistines envied him.
No all the ells hich his father’s servants had digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped, and filled ith earth.
And Abimelech said unto Isaac, Go from us; for thou art much mightier than e.
And Isaac departed thence, and encamped in the valley of Gerar, and delt there.

And Isaac digged again the ells of ater, hich they had digged in the days of Abraham his father; for the Philistines had stopped them after the death of Abraham: and he called their names after the names by hich his father had called them.
And Isaac’s servants digged in the valley, and found there a ell of springing ater.
And the herdsmen of Gerar strove ith Isaac’s herdsmen, saying, The ater is ours: and he called the name of the ell Esek, because they contended ith him.
And they digged another ell, and they strove for that also: and he called the name of it Sitnah.

And he removed from thence, and digged another ell; and for that they strove not: and he called the name of it Rehoboth; and he said, For no Jehovah hath made room for us, and e shall be fruitful in the land.
And he ent up from thence to Beer-sheba.
And Jehovah appeared unto him the same night, and said, I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I am ith thee, and ill bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham’s sake.
And he builded an altar there, and called upon the name of Jehovah, and pitched his tent there: and there Isaac’s servants digged a ell.
Then Abimelech ent to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath his friend, and Phicol the captain of his host.
And Isaac said unto them, Wherefore are ye come unto me, seeing ye hate me, and have sent me aay from you?
And they said, We sa plainly that Jehovah as ith thee: and e said, Let there no be an oath betixt us, even betixt us and thee, and let us make a covenant ith thee,
that thou ilt do us no hurt, as e have not touched thee, and as e have done unto thee nothing but good, and have sent thee aay in peace: thou art no the blessed of Jehovah.
And he made them a feast, and they did eat and drink.
And they rose up betimes in the morning, and sare one to another: and Isaac sent them aay, and they departed from him in peace.
And it came to pass the same day, that Isaac’s servants came, and told him concerning the ell hich they had digged, and said unto him, We have found ater.
And he called it Shibah: therefore the name of the city is Beer-sheba unto this day.
And hen Esau as forty years old he took to ife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:
and they ere a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah.
And it came to pass, that hen Isaac as old, and his eyes ere dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his elder son, and said unto him, My son: and he said unto him, Here am I.
And he said, Behold no, I am old, I kno not the day of my death.
No therefore take, I pray thee, thy eapons, thy quiver and thy bo, and go out to the field, and take me venison;
and make me savory food, such as I love, and bring it to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless thee before I die.
And Rebekah heard hen Isaac spake to Esau his son. And Esau ent to the field to hunt for venison, and to bring it.
And Rebekah spake unto Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak unto Esau thy brother, saying,
Bring me venison, and make me savory food, that I may eat, and bless thee before Jehovah before my death.
No therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that hich I command thee.
Go no to the flock, and fetch me from thence to good kids of the goats; and I ill make them savory food for thy father, such as he loveth:
and thou shalt bring it to thy father, that he may eat, so that he may bless thee before his death.
And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
My father peradventure ill feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.
And his mother said unto him, Upon me be thy curse, my son; only obey my voice, and go fetch me them.
And he ent, and fetched, and brought them to his mother: and his mother made savory food, such as his father loved.
And Rebekah took the goodly garments of Esau her elder son, hich ere ith her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son;
and she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck:
and she gave the savory food and the bread, hich she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.
And he came unto his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I; ho art thou, my son?
And Jacob said unto his father, I am Esau thy first-born; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.
And Isaac said unto his son, Ho is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? And he said, Because Jehovah thy God sent me good speed.
And Isaac said unto Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, hether thou be my very son Esau or not.
And Jacob ent near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
And he discerned him not, because his hands ere hairy, as his brother Esau’s hands: so he blessed him.
And he said, Art thou my very son Esau? And he said, I am.
And he said, Bring it near to me, and I ill eat of my son’s venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought it near to him, and he did eat: and he brought him ine, and he drank.
And his father Isaac said unto him, Come near no, and kiss me, my son.
And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son Is as the smell of a field hich Jehovah hath blessed:
And God give thee of the de of heaven, And of the fatness of the earth, And plenty of grain and ne ine:

Let peoples serve thee, And nations bo don to thee: Be lord over thy brethren, And let thy mother’s sons bo don to thee: Cursed be every one that curseth thee, And blessed be every one that blesseth thee.
And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, and Jacob as yet scarce gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
And he also made savory food, and brought it unto his father; and he said unto his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his son’s venison, that thy soul may bless me.
And Isaac his father said unto him, Who art thou? And he said, I am thy son, thy first-born, Esau.

And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who then is he that hath taken venison, and brought it me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, \add and\add* he shall be blessed.
When Esau heard the ords of his father, he cried ith an exceeding great and bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, even me also, O my father.
And he said, Thy brother came ith guile, and hath taken aay thy blessing.

And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these to times: he took aay my birthright; and, behold, no he hath taken aay my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?

And Isaac ansered and said unto Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and ith grain and ne ine have I sustained him: and hat then shall I do for thee, my son?
And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and ept.
And Isaac his father ansered and said unto him, Behold, of the fatness of the earth shall be thy delling, And of the de of heaven from above;
And by thy sord shalt thou live, and thou shalt serve thy brother; And it shall come to pass, hen thou shalt break loose, That thou shalt shake his yoke from off thy neck.
And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing hereith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then ill I slay my brother Jacob.

And the ords of Esau her elder son ere told to Rebekah; and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said unto him, Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, \add purposing\add* to kill thee.
No therefore, my son, obey my voice; and arise, flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran;
and tarry ith him a fe days, until thy brother’s fury turn aay;
until thy brother’s anger turn aay from thee, and he forget that hich thou hast done to him: then I ill send, and fetch thee from thence: hy should I be bereaved of you both in one day?

And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am eary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a ife of the daughters of Heth, such as these, of the daughters of the land, hat good shall my life do me?
And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a ife of the daughters of Canaan.
Arise, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother’s father; and take thee a ife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother’s brother.
And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a company of peoples;
and give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed ith thee; that thou mayest inherit the land of thy sojournings, hich God gave unto Abraham.
And Isaac sent aay Jacob: and he ent to Paddan-aram unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.

No Esau sa that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him aay to Paddan-aram, to take him a ife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a ife of the daughters of Canaan;
and that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and as gone to Paddan-aram:
and Esau sa that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father;
and Esau ent unto Ishmael, and took, besides the ives that he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebaioth, to be his ife.
And Jacob ent out from Beer-sheba, and ent toard Haran.
And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun as set; and he took one of the stones of the place, and put it under his head, and lay don in that place to sleep.
And he dreamed; and behold, a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
And, behold, Jehovah stood above it, and said, I am Jehovah, the God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land hereon thou liest, to thee ill I give it, and to thy seed;

and thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the est, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.
And, behold, I am ith thee, and ill keep thee hithersoever thou goest, and ill bring thee again into this land; for I ill not leave thee, until I have done that hich I have spoken to thee of.
And Jacob aaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely Jehovah is in this place; and I kne it not.
And he as afraid, and said, Ho dreadful is this place! this is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.
And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put under his head, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.
And he called the name of that place Beth-el: but the name of the city as Luz at the first.
And Jacob voed a vo, saying, If God ill be ith me, and ill keep me in this ay that I go, and ill give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on,
so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, and Jehovah ill be my God,
then this stone, hich I have set up for a pillar, shall be God’s house: and of all that thou shalt give me I ill surely give the tenth unto thee.
Then Jacob ent on his journey, and came to the land of the children of the east.
And he looked, and, behold, a ell in the field, and, lo, three flocks of sheep lying there by it; for out of that ell they atered the flocks: and the stone upon the ell’s mouth as great.
And thither ere all the flocks gathered: and they rolled the stone from the ell’s mouth, and atered the sheep, and put the stone again upon the ell’s mouth in its place.
And Jacob said unto them, My brethren, hence are ye? And they said, Of Haran are e.
And he said unto them, Kno ye Laban the son of Nahor? And they said, We kno him.
And he said unto them, Is it ell ith him? And they said, It is ell: and, behold, Rachel his daughter cometh ith the sheep.
And he said, Lo, it is yet high day, neither is it time that the cattle should be gathered together: ater ye the sheep, and go and feed them.
And they said, We cannot, until all the flocks be gathered together, and they roll the stone from the ell’s mouth; then e ater the sheep.
While he as yet speaking ith them, Rachel came ith her father’s sheep; for she kept them.

And it came to pass, hen Jacob sa Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother, that Jacob ent near, and rolled the stone from the ell’s mouth, and atered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.
And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and ept.
And Jacob told Rachel that he as her father’s brother, and that he as Rebekah’s son: and she ran and told her father.

And it came to pass, hen Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister’s son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.
And Laban said to him, Surely thou art my bone and my flesh. And he abode ith him the space of a month.
And Laban said unto Jacob, Because thou art my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for nought? tell me, hat shall thy ages be?
And Laban had to daughters: the name of the elder as Leah, and the name of the younger as Rachel.
And Leah’s eyes ere tender; but Rachel as beautiful and ell favored.
And Jacob loved Rachel; and he said, I ill serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.
And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide ith me.
And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a fe days, for the love he had to her.
And Jacob said unto Laban, Give me my ife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.
And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he ent in unto her.
And Laban gave Zilpah his handmaid unto his daughter Leah for a handmaid.
And it came to pass in the morning that, behold, it as Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve ith thee for Rachel? herefore then hast thou beguiled me?
And Laban said, It is not so done in our place, to give the younger before the first-born.
Fulfil the eek of this one, and e ill give thee the other also for the service hich thou shalt serve ith me yet seven other years.
And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her eek: and he gave him Rachel his daughter to ife.
And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his handmaid to be her handmaid.
And he ent in also unto Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served ith him yet seven other years.
And Jehovah sa that Leah as hated, and he opened her omb: but Rachel as barren.
And Leah conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Reuben: for she said, Because Jehovah hath looked upon my affliction; for no my husband ill love me.
And she conceived again, and bare a son: and said, Because Jehovah hath heard that I am hated, he hath therefore given me this \add son\add* also: and she called his name Simeon.
And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, No this time ill my husband be joined unto me, because I have borne him three sons: therefore as his name called Levi.
And she conceived again, and bare a son: and she said, This time ill I praise Jehovah: therefore she called his name Judah; and she left off bearing.
And hen Rachel sa that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister; and she said unto Jacob, Give me children, or else I die.
And Jacob’s anger as kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God’s stead, ho hath ithheld from thee the fruit of the omb?
And she said, Behold, my maid Bilhah, go in unto her; that she may bear upon my knees, and I also may obtain children by her.
And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid to ife: and Jacob ent in unto her.
And Bilhah conceived, and bare Jacob a son.
And Rachel said, God hath judged me, and hath also heard my voice, and hath given me a son: therefore called she his name Dan.
And Bilhah Rachel’s handmaid conceived again, and bare Jacob a second son.
And Rachel said, With mighty restlings have I restled ith my sister, and have prevailed: and she called his name Naphtali.
When Leah sa that she had left off bearing, she took Zilpah her handmaid, and gave her to Jacob to ife.
And Zilpah Leah’s handmaid bare Jacob a son.
And Leah said, Fortunate! and she called his name Gad.
And Zilpah Leah’s handmaid bare Jacob a second son.
And Leah said, Happy am I! for the daughters ill call me happy: and she called his name Asher.
And Reuben ent in the days of heat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them unto his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, Give me, I pray thee, of thy son’s mandrakes.

And she said unto her, Is it a small matter that thou hast taken aay my husband? and ouldest thou take aay my son’s mandrakes also? And Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie ith thee to-night for thy son’s mandrakes.
And Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah ent out to meet him, and said, Thou must come in unto me; for I have surely hired thee ith my son’s mandrakes. And he lay ith her that night.
And God hearkened unto Leah, and she conceived, and bare Jacob a fifth son.
And Leah said, God hath given me my hire, because I gave my handmaid to my husband: and she called his name Issachar.
And Leah conceived again, and bare a sixth son to Jacob.
And Leah said, God hath endoed me ith a good dory; no ill my husband dell ith me, because I have borne him six sons: and she called his name Zebulun.
And afterards she bare a daughter, and called her name Dinah.
And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her omb.
And she conceived, and bare a son: and said, God hath taken aay my reproach:
and she called his name Joseph, saying, Jehovah add to me another son.
And it came to pass, hen Rachel had borne Joseph, that Jacob said unto Laban, Send me aay, that I may go unto mine on place, and to my country.
Give me my ives and my children for hom I have served thee, and let me go: for thou knoest my service hereith I have served thee.
And Laban said unto him, If no I have found favor in thine eyes, \add tarry\add*: \add for\add* I have divined that Jehovah hath blessed me for thy sake.
And he said, Appoint me thy ages, and I ill give it.
And he said unto him, Thou knoest ho I have served thee, and ho thy cattle have fared ith me.
For it as little hich thou hadst before I came, and it hath increased unto a multitude; and Jehovah hath blessed thee hithersoever I turned: and no hen shall I provide for mine on house also?
And he said, What shall I give thee? And Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me aught: if thou ilt do this thing for me, I ill again feed thy flock and keep it.

I ill pass through all thy flock to-day, removing from thence every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and \add of such\add* shall be my hire.

So shall my righteousness anser for me hereafter, hen thou shalt come concerning my hire that is before thee: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the sheep, that, \add if found\add* ith me, shall be counted stolen.
And Laban said, Behold, I ould it might be according to thy ord.

And he removed that day the he-goats that ere ringstreaked and spotted, and all the she-goats that ere speckled and spotted, every one that had hite in it, and all the black ones among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons;
and he set three days’ journey betixt himself and Jacob: and Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.
And Jacob took him rods of fresh poplar, and of the almond and of the plane-tree; and peeled hite streaks in them, and made the hite appear hich as in the rods.
And he set the rods hich he had peeled over against the flocks in the gutters in the atering-troughs here the flocks came to drink; and they conceived hen they came to drink.
And the flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks brought forth ringstreaked, speckled, and spotted.
