And Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toard the ringstreaked and all the black in the flock of Laban: and he put his on droves apart, and put them not unto Laban’s flock.
And it came to pass, hensoever the stronger of the flock did conceive, that Jacob laid the rods before the eyes of the flock in the gutters, that they might conceive among the rods;
but hen the flock ere feeble, he put them not in: so the feebler ere Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.
And the man increased exceedingly, and had large flocks, and maid-servants and men-servants, and camels and asses.
And he heard the ords of Laban’s sons, saying, Jacob hath taken aay all that as our father’s; and of that hich as our father’s hath he gotten all this glory.
And Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban, and, behold, it as not toard him as beforetime.
And Jehovah said unto Jacob, Return unto the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred; and I ill be ith thee.
And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field unto his flock,
and said unto them, I see your father’s countenance, that it is not toard me as beforetime; but the God of my father hath been ith me.
And ye kno that ith all my poer I have served your father.
And your father hath deceived me, and changed my ages ten times; but God suffered him not to hurt me.
If he said thus, The speckled shall be thy ages; then all the flock bare speckled: and if he said thus, The ringstreaked shall be thy ages; then bare all the flock ringstreaked.
Thus God hath taken aay the cattle of your father, and given them to me.
And it came to pass at the time that the flock conceive, that I lifted up mine eyes, and sa in a dream, and, behold, the he-goats hich leaped upon the flock ere ringstreaked, speckled, and grizzled.
And the angel of God said unto me in the dream, Jacob: and I said, Here am I.
And he said, Lift up no thine eyes, and see: all the he-goats hich leap upon the flock are ringstreaked, speckled, and grizzled: for I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee.
I am the God of Beth-el, here thou anointedst a pillar, here thou voedst a vo unto me: no arise, get thee out from this land, and return unto the land of thy nativity.
And Rachel and Leah ansered and said unto him, Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father’s house?
Are e not accounted by him as foreigners? for he hath sold us, and hath also quite devoured our money.
For all the riches hich God hath taken aay from our father, that is ours and our children’s: no then, hatsoever God hath said unto thee, do.
Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his ives upon the camels;
and he carried aay all his cattle, and all his substance hich he had gathered, the cattle of his getting, hich he had gathered in Paddan-aram, to go to Isaac his father unto the land of Canaan.
No Laban as gone to shear his sheep: and Rachel stole the teraphim that ere her father’s.
And Jacob stole aay unaares to Laban the Syrian, in that he told him not that he fled.
So he fled ith all that he had; and he rose up, and passed over the River, and set his face toard the mountain of Gilead.
And it as told Laban on the third day that Jacob as fled.
And he took his brethren ith him, and pursued after him seven days’ journey; and he overtook him in the mountain of Gilead.
And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream of the night, and said unto him, Take heed to thyself that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
And Laban came up ith Jacob. No Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain: and Laban ith his brethren encamped in the mountain of Gilead.
And Laban said to Jacob, What hast thou done, that thou hast stolen aay unaares to me, and carried aay my daughters as captives of the sord?
Wherefore didst thou flee secretly, and steal aay from me, and didst not tell me, that I might have sent thee aay ith mirth and ith songs, ith tabret and ith harp;
and didst not suffer me to kiss my sons and my daughters? no hast thou done foolishly.
It is in the poer of my hand to do you hurt: but the God of your father spake unto me yesternight, saying, Take heed to thyself that thou speak not to Jacob either good or bad.
And no, \add though\add* thou ouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy father’s house, \add yet\add* herefore hast thou stolen my gods?
And Jacob ansered and said to Laban, Because I as afraid: for I said, Lest thou shouldest take thy daughters from me by force.
With homsoever thou findest thy gods, he shall not live: before our brethren discern thou hat is thine ith me, and take it to thee. For Jacob kne not that Rachel had stolen them.
And Laban ent into Jacob’s tent, and into Leah’s tent, and into the tent of the to maid-servants; but he found them not. And he ent out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.
No Rachel had taken the teraphim, and put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat upon them. And Laban felt about all the tent, but found them not.
And she said to her father, Let not my lord be angry that I cannot rise up before thee; for the manner of omen is upon me. And he searched, but found not the teraphim.
And Jacob as roth, and chode ith Laban: and Jacob ansered and said to Laban, What is my trespass? hat is my sin, that thou hast hotly pursued after me?
Whereas thou hast felt about all my stuff, hat hast thou found of all thy household stuff? Set it here before my brethren and thy brethren, that they may judge betixt us to.
These tenty years have I been ith thee; thy ees and thy she-goats have not cast their young, and the rams of thy flocks have I not eaten.
That hich as torn of beasts I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it; of my hand didst thou require it, hether stolen by day or stolen by night.
Thus I as; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from mine eyes.
These tenty years have I been in thy house; I served thee fourteen years for thy to daughters, and six years for thy flock: and thou hast changed my ages ten times.

Except the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the Fear of Isaac, had been ith me, surely no hadst thou sent me aay empty. God hath seen mine affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked thee yesternight.

And Laban ansered and said unto Jacob, The daughters are my daughters, and the children are my children, and the flocks are my flocks, and all that thou seest is mine: and hat can I do this day unto these my daughters, or unto their children hom they have borne?
And no come, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a itness beteen me and thee.
And Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.
And Jacob said unto his brethren, Gather stones; and they took stones, and made a heap: and they did eat there by the heap.
And Laban called it Jegar-saha-dutha: but Jacob called it Galeed.
And Laban said, This heap is itness beteen me and thee this day. Therefore as the name of it called Galeed:
and Mizpah, for he said, Jehovah atch beteen me and thee, hen e are absent one from another.
If thou shalt afflict my daughters, and if thou shalt take ives besides my daughters, no man is ith us; see, God is itness betixt me and thee.
And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and behold the pillar, hich I have set betixt me and thee.
This heap be itness, and the pillar be itness, that I ill not pass over this heap to thee, and that thou shalt not pass over this heap and this pillar unto me, for harm.
The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge betixt us. And Jacob sare by the Fear of his father Isaac.
And Jacob offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his brethren to eat bread: and they did eat bread, and tarried all night in the mountain.
And early in the morning Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them: and Laban departed, and returned unto his place.
And Jacob ent on his ay, and the angels of God met him.
And Jacob said hen he sa them, This is God’s host: and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.
And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother unto the land of Seir, the field of Edom.
And he commanded them, saying, Thus shall ye say unto my lord Esau: Thus saith thy servant Jacob, I have sojourned ith Laban, and stayed until no:
and I have oxen, and asses, \add and\add* flocks, and men-servants, and maid-servants: and I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find favor in thy sight.
And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to thy brother Esau, and moreover he cometh to meet thee, and four hundred men ith him.
Then Jacob as greatly afraid and as distressed: and he divided the people that ere ith him, and the flocks, and the herds, and the camels, into to companies;
and he said, If Esau come to the one company, and smite it, then the company hich is left shall escape.
And Jacob said, O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, O Jehovah, ho saidst unto me, Return unto thy country, and to thy kindred, and I ill do thee good:
I am not orthy of the least of all the lovingkindnesses, and of all the truth, hich thou hast shoed unto thy servant; for ith my staff I passed over this Jordan; and no I am become to companies.
Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he come and smite me, the mother ith the children.
And thou saidst, I ill surely do thee good, and make thy seed as the sand of the sea, hich cannot be numbered for multitude.
And he lodged there that night, and took of that hich he had ith him a present for Esau his brother:
to hundred she-goats and tenty he-goats, to hundred ees and tenty rams,
thirty milch camels and their colts, forty cos and ten bulls, tenty she-asses and ten foals.
And he delivered them into the hand of his servants, every drove by itself, and said unto his servants, Pass over before me, and put a space betixt drove and drove.
And he commanded the foremost, saying, When Esau my brother meeteth thee, and asketh thee, saying, Whose art thou? and hither goest thou? and hose are these before thee?
then thou shalt say, \add They are\add* thy servant Jacob’s; it is a present sent unto my lord Esau: and, behold, he also is behind us.
And he commanded also the second, and the third, and all that folloed the droves, saying, On this manner shall ye speak unto Esau, hen ye find him;

and ye shall say, Moreover, behold, thy servant Jacob is behind us. For he said, I ill appease him ith the present that goeth before me, and afterard I ill see his face; peradventure he ill accept me.
So the present passed over before him: and he himself lodged that night in the company.
And he rose up that night, and took his to ives, and his to handmaids, and his eleven children, and passed over the ford of the Jabbok.
And he took them, and sent them over the stream, and sent over that hich he had.
And Jacob as left alone; and there restled a man ith him until the breaking of the day.
And hen he sa that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollo of his thigh; and the hollo of Jacob’s thigh as strained, as he restled ith him.
And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I ill not let thee go, except thou bless me.
And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob.
And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for thou hast striven ith God and ith men, and hast prevailed.
And Jacob asked him, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, thy name. And he said, Wherefore is it that thou dost ask after my name? And he blessed him there.
And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for, \add said he\add*, I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.
And the sun rose upon him as he passed over Penuel, and he limped upon his thigh.
Therefore the children of Israel eat not the sine of the hip hich is upon the hollo of the thigh, unto this day: because he touched the hollo of Jacob’s thigh in the sine of the hip.
And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau as coming, and ith him four hundred men. And he divided the children unto Leah, and unto Rachel, and unto the to handmaids.
And he put the handmaids and their children foremost, and Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph hindermost.
And he himself passed over before them, and boed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.
And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they ept.
And he lifted up his eyes, and sa the omen and the children; and said, Who are these ith thee? And he said, The children hom God hath graciously given thy servant.
Then the handmaids came near, they and their children, and they boed themselves.
And Leah also and her children came near, and boed themselves: and after came Joseph near and Rachel, and they boed themselves.
And he said, What meanest thou by all this company hich I met? And he said, To find favor in the sight of my lord.
And Esau said, I have enough, my brother; let that hich thou hast be thine.

And Jacob said, Nay, I pray thee, if no I have found favor in thy sight, then receive my present at my hand; forasmuch as I have seen thy face, as one seeth the face of God, and thou ast pleased ith me.
Take, I pray thee, my gift that is brought to thee; because God hath dealt graciously ith me, and because I have enough. And he urged him, and he took it.
And he said, Let us take our journey, and let us go, and I ill go before thee.
And he said unto him, My lord knoeth that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds ith me have their young: and if they overdrive them one day, all the flocks ill die.

Let my lord, I pray thee, pass over before his servant: and I ill lead on gently, according to the pace of the cattle that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come unto my lord unto Seir.
And Esau said, Let me no leave ith thee some of the folk that are ith me. And he said, What needeth it? let me find favor in the sight of my lord.
So Esau returned that day on his ay unto Seir.
And Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built him a house, and made booths for his cattle: therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.
And Jacob came in peace to the city of Shechem, hich is in the land of Canaan, hen he came from Paddan-aram; and encamped before the city.
And he bought the parcel of ground, here he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for a hundred pieces of money.
And he erected there an altar, and called it El-Elohe-Israel.
And Dinah the daughter of Leah, hom she bare unto Jacob, ent out to see the daughters of the land.
And Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, sa her; and he took her, and lay ith her, and humbled her.
And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.
And Shechem spake unto his father Hamor, saying, Get me this damsel to ife.
No Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter; and his sons ere ith his cattle in the field: and Jacob held his peace until they came.
And Hamor the father of Shechem ent out unto Jacob to commune ith him.

And the sons of Jacob came in from the field hen they heard it: and the men ere grieved, and they ere very roth, because he had rought folly in Israel in lying ith Jacob’s daughter; hich thing ought not to be done.
And Hamor communed ith them, saying, The soul of my son Shechem longeth for your daughter: I pray you, give her unto him to ife.
And make ye marriages ith us; give your daughters unto us, and take our daughters unto you.
And ye shall dell ith us: and the land shall be before you; dell and trade ye therein, and get you possessions therein.
And Shechem said unto her father and unto her brethren, Let me find favor in your eyes, and hat ye shall say unto me I ill give.
Ask me never so much dory and gift, and I ill give according as ye shall say unto me: but give me the damsel to ife.
And the sons of Jacob ansered Shechem and Hamor his father ith guile, and spake, because he had defiled Dinah their sister,
and said unto them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that ere a reproach unto us.
Only on this condition ill e consent unto you: if ye ill be as e are, that every male of you be circumcised;
then ill e give our daughters unto you, and e ill take your daughters to us, and e ill dell ith you, and e ill become one people.
But if ye ill not hearken unto us, to be circumcised; then ill e take our daughter, and e ill be gone.
And their ords pleased Hamor, and Shechem Hamor’s son.
And the young man deferred not to do the thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter: and he as honored above all the house of his father.
And Hamor and Shechem his son came unto the gate of their city, and communed ith the men of their city, saying,

These men are peaceable ith us; therefore let them dell in the land, and trade therein; for, behold, the land is large enough for them; let us take their daughters to us for ives, and let us give them our daughters.
Only on this condition ill the men consent unto us to dell ith us, to become one people, if every male among us be circumcised, as they are circumcised.
Shall not their cattle and their substance and all their beasts be ours? only let us consent unto them, and they ill dell ith us.
And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all that ent out of the gate of his city; and every male as circumcised, all that ent out of the gate of his city.

And it came to pass on the third day, hen they ere sore, that to of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sord, and came upon the city unaares, and sle all the males.
And they sle Hamor and Shechem his son ith the edge of the sord, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and ent forth.
The sons of Jacob came upon the slain, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.
They took their flocks and their herds and their asses, and that hich as in the city, and that hich as in the field;
and all their ealth, and all their little ones and their ives, took they captive and made a prey, even all that as in the house.

And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me, to make me odious to the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and, I being fe in number, they ill gather themselves together against me and smite me; and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.
And they said, Should he deal ith our sister as ith a harlot?
And God said unto Jacob, Arise, go up to Beth-el, and dell there: and make there an altar unto God, ho appeared unto thee hen thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.
Then Jacob said unto his household, and to all that ere ith him, Put aay the foreign gods that are among you, and purify yourselves, and change your garments:
and let us arise, and go up to Beth-el; and I ill make there an altar unto God, ho ansered me in the day of my distress, and as ith me in the ay hich I ent.
And they gave unto Jacob all the foreign gods hich ere in their hand, and the rings hich ere in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak hich as by Shechem.
And they journeyed: and a terror of God as upon the cities that ere round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
So Jacob came to Luz, hich is in the land of Canaan ( the same is Beth-el), he and all the people that ere ith him.
And he built there an altar, and called the place El-beth-el; because there God as revealed unto him, hen he fled from the face of his brother.
And Deborah Rebekah’s nurse died, and she as buried belo Beth-el under the oak: and the name of it as called Allon-bacuth.
And God appeared unto Jacob again, hen he came from Paddan-aram, and blessed him.
And God said unto him, Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name: and he called his name Israel.
And God said unto him, I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins;
and the land hich I gave unto Abraham and Isaac, to thee I ill give it, and to thy seed after thee ill I give the land.
And God ent up from him in the place here he spake ith him.
And Jacob set up a pillar in the place here he spake ith him, a pillar of stone: and he poured out a drink-offering thereon, and poured oil thereon.
And Jacob called the name of the place here God spake ith him, Beth-el.
And they journeyed from Beth-el; and there as still some distance to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labor.
And it came to pass, hen she as in hard labor, that the midife said unto her, Fear not; for no thou shalt have another son.
And it came to pass, as her soul as departing ( for she died), that she called his name Ben-oni: but his father called him Benjamin.
And Rachel died, and as buried in the ay to Ephrath ( the same is Beth-lehem).
And Jacob set up a pillar upon her grave: the same is the Pillar of Rachel’s grave unto this day.
And Israel journeyed, and spread his tent beyond the toer of Eder.
And it came to pass, hile Israel delt in that land, that Reuben ent and lay ith Bilhah his father’s concubine: and Israel heard of it. No the sons of Jacob ere telve:
the sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob’s first-born, and Simeon, and Levi, and Judah, and Issachar, and Zebulun;
the sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin;
and the sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid: Dan and Naphtali;
and the sons of Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid: Gad and Asher: these are the sons of Jacob, that ere born to him in Paddan-aram.
And Jacob came unto Isaac his father to Mamre, to Kiriath-arba ( the same is Hebron), here Abraham and Isaac sojourned.
And the days of Isaac ere a hundred and fourscore years.
And Isaac gave up the ghost, and died, and as gathered unto his people, old and full of days: and Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.
No these are the generations of Esau ( the same is Edom).
Esau took his ives of the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite,
and Basemath Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebaioth.
And Adah bare to Esau Eliphaz; and Basemath bare Reuel;
and Oholibamah bare Jeush, and Jalam, and Korah: these are the sons of Esau, that ere born unto him in the land of Canaan.

And Esau took his ives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the souls of his house, and his cattle, and all his beasts, and all his possessions, hich he had gathered in the land of Canaan; and ent into a land aay from his brother Jacob.
For their substance as too great for them to dell together; and the land of their sojournings could not bear them because of their cattle.
And Esau delt in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.
And these are the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites in mount Seir:
these are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz the son of Adah the ife of Esau, Reuel the son of Basemath the ife of Esau.
And the sons of Eliphaz ere Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
And Timna as concubine to Eliphaz Esau’s son; and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek: these are the sons of Adah, Esau’s ife.
And these are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, and Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah: these ere the sons of Basemath, Esau’s ife.
And these ere the sons of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, Esau’s ife: and she bare to Esau Jeush, and Jalam, and Korah.
These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the first-born of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek: these are the chiefs that came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah.

And these are the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah: these are the chiefs that came of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, Esau’s ife.
And these are the sons of Oholibamah, Esau’s ife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah: these are the chiefs that came of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau’s ife.
These are the sons of Esau, and these are their chiefs: the same is Edom.
These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan and Shobal and Zibeon and Anah,
and Dishon and Ezer and Dishan: these are the chiefs that came of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.
And the children of Lotan ere Hori and Heman; and Lotan’s sister as Timna.
And these are the children of Shobal: Alvan and Manahath and Ebal, Shepho and Onam.
And these are the children of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah; this is Anah ho found the hot springs in the ilderness, as he fed the asses of Zibeon his father.
And these are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah.
And these are the children of Dishon: Hemdan and Eshban and Ithran and Cheran.
These are the children of Ezer: Bilhan and Zaavan and Akan.
These are the children of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
These are the chiefs that came of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
chief Dishon, chief Ezer, chief Dishan: these are the chiefs that came of the Horites, according to their chiefs in the land of Seir.
And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel.
And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom; and the name of his city as Dinhabah.
And Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead.
And Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his stead.
And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, ho smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city as Avith.
And Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.
And Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the River reigned in his stead.
And Shaul died, and Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.
And Baal-hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his stead: and the name of his city as Pau; and his ife’s name as Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-zahab.
And these are the names of the chiefs that came of Esau, according to their families, after their places, by their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, chief Iram: these are the chiefs of Edom, according to their habitations in the land of their possession. This is Esau, the father of the Edomites.
And Jacob delt in the land of his father’s sojournings, in the land of Canaan.

These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, as feeding the flock ith his brethren; and he as a lad ith the sons of Bilhah, and ith the sons of Zilpah, his father’s ives: and Joseph brought the evil report of them unto their father.
No Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he as the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colors.
And his brethren sa that their father loved him more than all his brethren; and they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.
And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brethren: and they hated him yet the more.
And he said unto them, Hear, I pray you, this dream hich I have dreamed:
for, behold, e ere binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves came round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.
And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his ords.
And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed yet a dream; and, behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars made obeisance to me.

And he told it to his father, and to his brethren; and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bo don ourselves to thee to the earth?
And his brethren envied him; but his father kept the saying in mind.
And his brethren ent to feed their father’s flock in Shechem.
And Israel said unto Joseph, Are not thy brethren feeding the flock in Shechem? come, and I ill send thee unto them. And he said to him, Here am I.
And he said to him, Go no, see hether it is ell ith thy brethren, and ell ith the flock; and bring me ord again. So he sent him out of the vale of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
And a certain man found him, and, behold, he as andering in the field: and the man asked him, saying, What seekest thou?
And he said, I am seeking my brethren: tell me, I pray thee, here they are feeding \add the flock\add*.
And the man said, They are departed hence; for I heard them say, Let us go to Dothan. And Joseph ent after his brethren, and found them in Dothan.
And they sa him afar off, and before he came near unto them, they conspired against him to slay him.
And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer cometh.
Come no therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into one of the pits, and e ill say, An evil beast hath devoured him: and e shall see hat ill become of his dreams.
And Reuben heard it, and delivered him out of their hand, and said, Let us not take his life.
And Reuben said unto them, Shed no blood; cast him into this pit that is in the ilderness, but lay no hand upon him: that he might deliver him out of their hand, to restore him to his father.
And it came to pass, hen Joseph as come unto his brethren, that they stripped Joseph of his coat, the coat of many colors that as on him;
and they took him, and cast him into the pit: and the pit as empty, there as no ater in it.

And they sat don to eat bread: and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and, behold, a caravan of Ishmaelites as coming from Gilead, ith their camels bearing spicery and balm and myrrh, going to carry it don to Egypt.
And Judah said unto his brethren, What profit is it if e slay our brother and conceal his blood?
Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother, our flesh. And his brethren hearkened unto him.
And there passed by Midianites, merchantmen; and they dre and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for tenty pieces of silver. And they brought Joseph into Egypt.
And Reuben returned unto the pit; and, behold, Joseph as not in the pit; and he rent his clothes.
And he returned unto his brethren, and said, The child is not; and I, hither shall I go?
And they took Joseph’s coat, and killed a he-goat, and dipped the coat in the blood;
and they sent the coat of many colors, and they brought it to their father, and said, This have e found: kno no hether it is thy son’s coat or not.
And he kne it, and said, It is my son’s coat: an evil beast hath devoured him; Joseph is ithout doubt torn in pieces.
And Jacob rent his garments, and put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I ill go don to Sheol to my son mourning. And his father ept for him.
And the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard.
And it came to pass at that time, that Judah ent don from his brethren, and turned in to a certain Adullamite, hose name as Hirah.
And Judah sa there a daughter of a certain Canaanite hose name as Shua; and he took her, and ent in unto her.
And she conceived, and bare a son; and he called his name Er.
And she conceived again, and bare a son; and she called his name Onan.
And she yet again bare a son, and called his name Shelah: and he as at Chezib, hen she bare him.
And Judah took a ife for Er his first-born, and her name as Tamar.
And Er, Judah’s first-born, as icked in the sight of Jehovah; and Jehovah sle him.
And Judah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother’s ife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother unto her, and raise up seed to thy brother.
And Onan kne that the seed ould not be his; and it came to pass, hen he ent in unto his brother’s ife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest he should give seed to his brother.
And the thing hich he did as evil in the sight of Jehovah: and he sle him also.

Then said Judah to Tamar his daughter-in-la, Remain a ido in thy father’s house, till Shelah my son be gron up; for he said, Lest he also die, like his brethren. And Tamar ent and delt in her father’s house.
And in process of time Shua’s daughter, the ife of Judah, died; and Judah as comforted, and ent up unto his sheep-shearers to Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
And it as told Tamar, saying, Behold, thy father-in-la goeth up to Timnah to shear his sheep.

And she put off from her the garments of her idohood, and covered herself ith her veil, and rapped herself, and sat in the gate of Enaim, hich is by the ay to Timnah; for she sa that Shelah as gron up, and she as not given unto him to ife.
When Judah sa her, he thought her to be a harlot; for she had covered her face.

And he turned unto her by the ay, and said, Come, I pray thee, let me come in unto thee: for he kne not that she as his daughter-in-la. And she said, What ilt thou give me, that thou mayest come in unto me?
And he said, I ill send thee a kid of the goats from the flock. And she said, Wilt thou give me a pledge, till thou send it?
And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet and thy cord, and thy staff that is in thy hand. And he gave them to her, and came in unto her, and she conceived by him.
And she arose, and ent aay, and put off her veil from her, and put on the garments of her idohood.
And Judah sent the kid of the goats by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the oman’s hand: but he found her not.
Then he asked the men of her place, saying, Where is the prostitute, that as at Enaim by the ayside? And they said, There hath been no prostitute here.
And he returned to Judah, and said, I have not found her; and also the men of the place said, There hath been no prostitute here.
And Judah said, Let her take it to her, lest e be put to shame: behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her.

And it came to pass about three months after, that it as told Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter-in-la hath played the harlot; and moreover, behold, she is ith child by horedom. And Judah said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.

When she as brought forth, she sent to her father-in-la, saying, By the man, hose these are, am I ith child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, hose are these, the signet, and the cords, and the staff.
And Judah acknoledged them, and said, She is more righteous than I, forasmuch as I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he kne her again no more.
And it came to pass in the time of her travail, that, behold, tins ere in her omb.
And it came to pass, hen she travailed, that one put out a hand: and the midife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.
And it came to pass, as he dre back his hand, that, behold, his brother came out: and she said, Wherefore hast thou made a breach for thyself? therefore his name as called Perez.
And afterard came out his brother, that had the scarlet thread upon his hand: and his name as called Zerah.
And Joseph as brought don to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hand of the Ishmaelites, that had brought him don thither.
And Jehovah as ith Joseph, and he as a prosperous man; and he as in the house of his master the Egyptian.
And his master sa that Jehovah as ith him, and that Jehovah made all that he did to prosper in his hand.
And Joseph found favor in his sight, and he ministered unto him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

And it came to pass from the time that he made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that Jehovah blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of Jehovah as upon all that he had, in the house and in the field.
And he left all that he had in Joseph’s hand; and he kne not aught \add that as\add* ith him, save the bread hich he did eat. And Joseph as comely, and ell-favored.
And it came to pass after these things, that his master’s ife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie ith me.
But he refused, and said unto his master’s ife, Behold, my master knoeth not hat is ith me in the house, and he hath put all that he hath into my hand:
he is not greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back anything from me but thee, because thou art his ife: ho then can I do this great ickedness, and sin against God?
And it came to pass, as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, \add or\add* to be ith her.
And it came to pass about this time, that he ent into the house to do his ork; and there as none of the men of the house there ithin.
And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie ith me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.
And it came to pass, hen she sa that he had left his garment in her hand, and as fled forth,
that she called unto the men of her house, and spake unto them, saying, See, he hath brought in a Hebre unto us to mock us: he came in unto me to lie ith me, and I cried ith a loud voice:
and it came to pass, hen he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment by me, and fled, and got him out.
And she laid up his garment by her, until his master came home.
And she spake unto him according to these ords, saying, The Hebre servant, hom thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me:
and it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment by me, and fled out.
And it came to pass, hen his master heard the ords of his ife, hich she spake unto him, saying, After this manner did thy servant to me; that his rath as kindled.
And Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, the place here the king’s prisoners ere bound: and he as there in the prison.
But Jehovah as ith Joseph, and shoed kindness unto him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
And the keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners that ere in the prison; and hatsoever they did there, he as the doer of it.
The keeper of the prison looked not to anything that as under his hand, because Jehovah as ith him; and that hich he did, Jehovah made it to prosper.
And it came to pass after these things, that the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord the king of Egypt.
And Pharaoh as roth against his to officers, against the chief of the butlers, and against the chief of the bakers.
And he put them in ard in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place here Joseph as bound.
And the captain of the guard charged Joseph ith them, and he ministered unto them: and they continued a season in ard.

And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, ho ere bound in the prison.
And Joseph came in unto them in the morning, and sa them, and, behold, they ere sad.
And he asked Pharaoh’s officers that ere ith him in ard in his master’s house, saying, Wherefore look ye so sad to-day?
And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it. And Joseph said unto them, Do not interpretations belong to God? tell it me, I pray you.
And the chief butler told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, In my dream, behold, a vine as before me;
and in the vine ere three branches: and it as as though it budded, \add and\add* its blossoms shot forth; \add and\add* the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes:
and Pharaoh’s cup as in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.
And Joseph said unto him, This is the interpretation of it: the three branches are three days;
ithin yet three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head, and restore thee unto thine office: and thou shalt give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, after the former manner hen thou ast his butler.
But have me in thy remembrance hen it shall be ell ith thee, and sho kindness, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:
for indeed I as stolen aay out of the land of the Hebres: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.
When the chief baker sa that the interpretation as good, he said unto Joseph, I also as in my dream, and, behold, three baskets of hite bread ere on my head:
and in the uppermost basket there as of all manner of baked food for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head.
And Joseph ansered and said, This is the interpretation thereof: the three baskets are three days;
ithin yet three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.

And it came to pass the third day, hich as Pharaoh’s birthday, that he made a feast unto all his servants: and he lifted up the head of the chief butler and the head of the chief baker among his servants.
And he restored the chief butler unto his butlership again; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand:
but he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.
Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.
And it came to pass at the end of to full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the river.
And, behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, ell-favored and fat-fleshed; and they fed in the reed-grass.
And, behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, ill-favored and lean-fleshed, and stood by the other kine upon the brink of the river.
And the ill-favored and lean-fleshed kine did eat up the seven ell-favored and fat kine. So Pharaoh aoke.
And he slept and dreamed a second time: and, behold, seven ears of grain came up upon one stalk, rank and good.
And, behold, seven ears, thin and blasted ith the east ind, sprung up after them.
And the thin ears salloed up the seven rank and full ears. And Pharaoh aoke, and, behold, it as a dream.

And it came to pass in the morning that his spirit as troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the ise men thereof: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but there as none that could interpret them unto Pharaoh.
Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:
Pharaoh as roth ith his servants, and put me in ard in the house of the captain of the guard, me and the chief baker:
and e dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; e dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.
And there as ith us there a young man, a Hebre, servant to the captain of the guard; and e told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; to each man according to his dream he did interpret.
And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it as; me he restored unto mine office, and him he hanged.
Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it: and I have heard say of thee, that hen thou hearest a dream thou canst interpret it.
And Joseph ansered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: God ill give Pharaoh an anser of peace.
And Pharaoh spake unto Joseph, In my dream, behold, I stood upon the brink of the river:
and, behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, fat-fleshed and ell-favored: and they fed in the reed-grass:
and, behold, seven other kine came up after them, poor and very ill-favored and lean-fleshed, such as I never sa in all the land of Egypt for badness:
and the lean and ill-favored kine did eat up the first seven fat kine:
and hen they had eaten them up, it could not be knon that they had eaten them; but they ere still ill-favored, as at the beginning. So I aoke.
And I sa in my dream, and, behold, seven ears came up upon one stalk, full and good:
and, behold, seven ears, ithered, thin, \add and\add* blasted ith the east ind, sprung up after them:
and the thin ears salloed up the seven good ears: and I told it unto the magicians; but there as none that could declare it to me.
And Joseph said unto Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh is one: hat God is about to do he hath declared unto Pharaoh.
The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one.
And the seven lean and ill-favored kine that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty ears blasted ith the east ind; they shall be seven years of famine.
That is the thing hich I spake unto Pharaoh: hat God is about to do he hath shoed unto Pharaoh.
Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt:
and there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;
and the plenty shall not be knon in the land by reason of that famine hich folloeth; for it shall be very grievous.
And for that the dream as doubled unto Pharaoh, it is because the thing is established by God, and God ill shortly bring it to pass.
No therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and ise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
Let Pharaoh do \add this\add*, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt in the seven plenteous years.
And let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and lay up grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.
And the food shall be for a store to the land against the seven years of famine, hich shall be in the land of Egypt; that the land perish not through the famine.
And the thing as good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can e find such a one as this, a man in hom the spirit of God is?
And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shoed thee all this, there is none so discreet and ise as thou:
thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy ord shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne ill I be greater than thou.
And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;
and he made him to ride in the second chariot hich he had; and they cried before him, Bo the knee: and he set him over all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I am Pharaoh, and ithout thee shall no man lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-paneah; and he gave him to ife Asenath, the daughter of Poti-phera priest of On. And Joseph ent out over the land of Egypt.
And Joseph as thirty years old hen he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph ent out from the presence of Pharaoh, and ent throughout all the land of Egypt.
And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth by handfuls.
And he gathered up all the food of the seven years hich ere in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, hich as round about every city, laid he up in the same.
And Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left off numbering; for it as ithout number.
And unto Joseph ere born to sons before the year of famine came, hom Asenath, the daughter of Poti-phera priest of On, bare unto him.
And Joseph called the name of the first-born Manasseh: For, \add said he\add*, God hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.
And the name of the second called he Ephraim: For God hath made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.
And the seven years of plenty, that as in the land of Egypt, came to an end.
And the seven years of famine began to come, according as Joseph had said: and there as famine in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there as bread.
And hen all the land of Egypt as famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said unto all the Egyptians, Go unto Joseph; hat he saith to you, do.
And the famine as over all the face of the earth: and Joseph opened all the store-houses, and sold unto the Egyptians; and the famine as sore in the land of Egypt.
And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph to buy grain, because the famine as sore in all the earth.
No Jacob sa that there as grain in Egypt, and Jacob said unto his sons, Why do ye look one upon another?
And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt: get you don thither, and buy for us from thence; that e may live, and not die.
And Joseph’s ten brethren ent don to buy grain from Egypt.
But Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, Jacob sent not ith his brethren; for he said, Lest peradventure harm befall him.
And the sons of Israel came to buy among those that came: for the famine as in the land of Canaan.
And Joseph as the governor over the land; he it as that sold to all the people of the land. And Joseph’s brethren came, and boed don themselves to him ith their faces to the earth.
And Joseph sa his brethren, and he kne them, but made himself strange unto them, and spake roughly ith them; and he said unto them, Whence come ye? And they said, From the land of Canaan to buy food.
And Joseph kne his brethren, but they kne not him.
And Joseph remembered the dreams hich he dreamed of them, and said unto them, Ye are spies; to see the nakedness of the land ye are come.
And they said unto him, Nay, my lord, but to buy food are thy servants come.
We are all one man’s sons; e are true men, thy servants are no spies.
And he said unto them, Nay, but to see the nakedness of the land ye are come.
And they said, We thy servants are telve brethren, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and, behold, the youngest is this day ith our father, and one is not.
And Joseph said unto them, That is it that I spake unto you, saying, Ye are spies:
hereby ye shall be proved: by the life of Pharaoh ye shall not go forth hence, except your youngest brother come hither.
Send one of you, and let him fetch your brother, and ye shall be bound, that your ords may be proved, hether there be truth in you: or else by the life of Pharaoh surely ye are spies.
And he put them all together into ard three days.
And Joseph said unto them the third day, This do, and live; for I fear God:
if ye be true men, let one of your brethren be bound in your prison-house; but go ye, carry grain for the famine of your houses:
and bring your youngest brother unto me; so shall your ords be verified, and ye shall not die. And they did so.
And they said one to another, We are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that e sa the distress of his soul, hen he besought us, and e ould not hear; therefore is this distress come upon us.
And Reuben ansered them, saying, Spake I not unto you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and ye ould not hear? therefore also, behold, his blood is required.
And they kne not that Joseph understood them; for there as an interpreter beteen them.
And he turned himself about from them, and ept; and he returned to them, and spake to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.
Then Joseph commanded to fill their vessels ith grain, and to restore every man’s money into his sack, and to give them provision for the ay: and thus as it done unto them.
And they laded their asses ith their grain, and departed thence.
And as one of them opened his sack to give his ass provender in the lodging-place, he espied his money; and, behold, it as in the mouth of his sack.

And he said unto his brethren, My money is restored; and, lo, it is even in my sack: and their heart failed them, and they turned trembling one to another, saying, What is this that God hath done unto us?
And they came unto Jacob their father unto the land of Canaan, and told him all that had befallen them, saying,
The man, the lord of the land, spake roughly ith us, and took us for spies of the country.
And e said unto him, We are true men; e are no spies:
e are telve brethren, sons of our father; one is not, and the youngest is this day ith our father in the land of Canaan.
And the man, the lord of the land, said unto us, Hereby shall I kno that ye are true men: leave one of your brethren ith me, and take \add grain for\add* the famine of your houses, and go your ay;
and bring your youngest brother unto me: then shall I kno that ye are no spies, but that ye are true men: so ill I deliver you your brother, and ye shall traffic in the land.
And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks, that, behold, every man’s bundle of money as in his sack: and hen they and their father sa their bundles of money, they ere afraid.
And Jacob their father said unto them, Me have ye bereaved of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye ill take Benjamin aay: all these things are against me.
And Reuben spake unto his father, saying, Slay my to sons, if I bring him not to thee: deliver him into my hand, and I ill bring him to thee again.
And he said, My son shall not go don ith you; for his brother is dead, and he only is left: if harm befall him by the ay in hich ye go, then ill ye bring don my gray hairs ith sorro to Sheol.
And the famine as sore in the land.
And it came to pass, hen they had eaten up the grain hich they had brought out of Egypt, their father said unto them, Go again, buy us a little food.
And Judah spake unto him, saying, The man did solemnly protest unto us, saying, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be ith you.
If thou ilt send our brother ith us, e ill go don and buy thee food:
but if thou ilt not send him, e ill not go don; for the man said unto us, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be ith you.
And Israel said, Wherefore dealt ye so ill ith me, as to tell the man hether ye had yet a brother?

And they said, The man asked straitly concerning ourselves, and concerning our kindred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have ye \add another\add* brother? and e told him according to the tenor of these ords: could e in any ise kno that he ould say, Bring your brother don?
And Judah said unto Israel his father, Send the lad ith me, and e ill arise and go; that e may live, and not die, both e, and thou, and also our little ones.
I ill be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not unto thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever:
for except e had lingered, surely e had no returned a second time.

And their father Israel said unto them, If it be so no, do this: take of the choice fruits of the land in your vessels, and carry don the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spicery and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;
and take double money in your hand; and the money that as returned in the mouth of your sacks carry again in your hand; peradventure it as an oversight:
take also your brother, and arise, go again unto the man:
and God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release unto you your other brother and Benjamin. And if I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.
And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and rose up, and ent don to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
And hen Joseph sa Benjamin ith them, he said to the steard of his house, Bring the men into the house, and slay, and make ready; for the men shall dine ith me at noon.
And the man did as Joseph bade; and the man brought the men to Joseph’s house.

And the men ere afraid, because they ere brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, Because of the money that as returned in our sacks at the first time are e brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, and fall upon us, and take us for bondmen, and our asses.
And they came near to the steard of Joseph’s house, and they spake unto him at the door of the house,
and said, Oh, my lord, e came indeed don at the first time to buy food:

and it came to pass, hen e came to the lodging-place, that e opened our sacks, and, behold, every man’s money as in the mouth of his sack, our money in full eight: and e have brought it again in our hand.
And other money have e brought don in our hand to buy food: e kno not ho put our money in our sacks.
And he said, Peace be to you, fear not: your God, and the God of your father, hath given you treasure in your sacks: I had your money. And he brought Simeon out unto them.
And the man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave them ater, and they ashed their feet; and he gave their asses provender.
And they made ready the present against Joseph’s coming at noon: for they heard that they should eat bread there.
And hen Joseph came home, they brought him the present hich as in their hand into the house, and boed don themselves to him to the earth.
And he asked them of their elfare, and said, Is your father ell, the old man of hom ye spake? Is he yet alive?
And they said, Thy servant our father is ell, he is yet alive. And they boed the head, and made obeisance.
And he lifted up his eyes, and sa Benjamin his brother, his mother’s son, and said, Is this your youngest brother, of hom ye spake unto me? And he said, God be gracious unto thee, my son.
And Joseph made haste; for his heart yearned over his brother: and he sought here to eep; and he entered into his chamber, and ept there.
And he ashed his face, and came out; and he refrained himself, and said, Set on bread.

And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, that did eat ith him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread ith the Hebres; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.
And they sat before him, the first-born according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth: and the men marvelled one ith another.
And he took \add and sent\add* messes unto them from before him: but Benjamin’s mess as five times so much as any of theirs. And they drank, and ere merry ith him.
And he commanded the steard of his house, saying, Fill the men’s sacks ith food, as much as they can carry, and put every man’s money in his sack’s mouth.
And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, and his grain money. And he did according to the ord that Joseph had spoken.
As soon as the morning as light, the men ere sent aay, they and their asses.

\add And\add* hen they ere gone out of the city, and ere not yet far off, Joseph said unto his steard, Up, follo after the men; and hen thou dost overtake them, say unto them, Wherefore have ye rearded evil for good?
Is not this that in hich my lord drinketh, and hereby he indeed divineth? ye have done evil in so doing.
And he overtook them, and he spake unto them these ords.
And they said unto him, Wherefore speaketh my lord such ords as these? Far be it from thy servants that they should do such a thing.
Behold, the money, hich e found in our sacks’ mouths, e brought again unto thee out of the land of Canaan: ho then should e steal out of thy lord’s house silver or gold?
With homsoever of thy servants it be found, let him die, and e also ill be my lord’s bondmen.
And he said, No also let it be according unto your ords: he ith hom it is found shall be my bondman; and ye shall be blameless.
Then they hasted, and took don every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.
And he searched, \add and\add* began at the eldest, and left off at the youngest: and the cup as found in Benjamin’s sack.
Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and returned to the city.
And Judah and his brethren came to Joseph’s house; and he as yet there: and they fell before him on the ground.
And Joseph said unto them, What deed is this that ye have done? kno ye not that such a man as I can indeed divine?

And Judah said, What shall e say unto my lord? hat shall e speak? or ho shall e clear ourselves? God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold, e are my lord’s bondmen, both e, and he also in hose hand the cup is found.
And he said, Far be it from me that I should do so: the man in hose hand the cup is found, he shall be my bondman; but as for you, get you up in peace unto your father.
Then Judah came near unto him, and said, Oh, my lord, let thy servant, I pray thee, speak a ord in my lord’s ears, and let not thine anger burn against thy servant; for thou art even as Pharaoh.
My lord asked his servants, saying, Have ye a father, or a brother?
And e said unto my lord, We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loveth him.
And thou saidst unto thy servants, Bring him don unto me, that I may set mine eyes upon him.
And e said unto my lord, The lad cannot leave his father: for if he should leave his father, his father ould die.
And thou saidst unto thy servants, Except your youngest brother come don ith you, ye shall see my face no more.
And it came to pass hen e came up unto thy servant my father, e told him the ords of my lord.
And our father said, Go again, buy us a little food.
And e said, We cannot go don: if our youngest brother be ith us, then ill e go don; for e may not see the man’s face, except our youngest brother be ith us.
And thy servant my father said unto us, Ye kno that my ife bare me to sons:
and the one ent out from me, and I said, Surely he is torn in pieces; and I have not seen him since:
and if ye take this one also from me, and harm befall him, ye ill bring don my gray hairs ith sorro to Sheol.
No therefore hen I come to thy servant my father, and the lad is not ith us; seeing that his life is bound up in the lad’s life;
it ill come to pass, hen he seeth that the lad is not \add ith us\add*, that he ill die: and thy servants ill bring don the gray hairs of thy servant our father ith sorro to Sheol.
For thy servant became surety for the lad unto my father, saying, If I bring him not unto thee, then shall I bear the blame to my father for ever.
No therefore, let thy servant, I pray thee, abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up ith his brethren.
For ho shall I go up to my father, if the lad be not ith me? lest I see the evil that shall come on my father.

Then Joseph could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me. And there stood no man ith him, hile Joseph made himself knon unto his brethren.
And he ept aloud: and the Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.
And Joseph said unto his brethren, I am Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not anser him; for they ere troubled at his presence.
And Joseph said unto his brethren, Come near to me, I pray you. And they came near. And he said, I am Joseph your brother, hom ye sold into Egypt.
And no be not grieved, nor angry ith yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life.
For these to years hath the famine been in the land: and there are yet five years, in hich there shall be neither ploing nor harvest.
And God sent me before you to preserve you a remnant in the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.
So no it as not you that sent me hither, but God: and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
Haste ye, and go up to my father, and say unto him, Thus saith thy son Joseph, God hath made me lord of all Egypt: come don unto me, tarry not;
and thou shalt dell in the land of Goshen, and thou shalt be near unto me, thou, and thy children, and thy children’s children, and thy flocks, and thy herds, and all that thou hast:
and there ill I nourish thee; for there are yet five years of famine; lest thou come to poverty, thou, and thy household, and all that thou hast.
And, behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaketh unto you.
And ye shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that ye have seen: and ye shall haste and bring don my father hither.
And he fell upon his brother Benjamin’s neck, and ept; and Benjamin ept upon his neck.
And he kissed all his brethren, and ept upon them: and after that his brethren talked ith him.
And the report thereof as heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, Joseph’s brethren are come: and it pleased Pharaoh ell, and his servants.
And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Say unto thy brethren, This do ye: lade your beasts, and go, get you unto the land of Canaan;
and take your father and your households, and come unto me: and I ill give you the good of the land of Egypt, and ye shall eat the fat of the land.
No thou art commanded, this do ye: take you agons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your ives, and bring your father, and come.
Also regard not your stuff; for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.

that they may believe that Jehovah, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee.

And Moses ent and returned to Jethro his father-in-la, and said unto him, Let me go, I pray thee, and return unto my brethren that are in Egypt, and see hether they be yet alive. And Jethro said to Moses, Go in peace.

And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith Jehovah, Israel is my son, my first-born:
and I have said unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me; and thou hast refused to let him go: behold, I ill slay thy son, thy first-born.
And it came to pass on the ay at the lodging-place, that Jehovah met him, and sought to kill him.

So he let him alone. Then she said, A bridegroom of blood \add art thou\add*, because of the circumcision.
And Jehovah said to Aaron, Go into the ilderness to meet Moses. And he ent, and met him in the mountain of God, and kissed him.

and Aaron spake all the ords hich Jehovah had spoken unto Moses, and did the signs in the sight of the people.

And they said, The God of the Hebres hath met ith us: let us go, e pray thee, three days’ journey into the ilderness, and sacrifice unto Jehovah our God, lest he fall upon us ith pestilence, or ith the sord.

Ye shall no more give the people stra to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather stra for themselves.

And the number of the bricks, hich they did make heretofore, ye shall lay upon them; ye shall not diminish aught thereof: for they are idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our God.

and they said unto them, Jehovah look upon you, and judge: because ye have made our savor to be abhorred in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sord in their hand to slay us.

and I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, as God Almighty; but by my name Jehovah I as not knon to them.

And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Go in, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.

And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, and gave them a charge unto the children of Israel, and unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
These are the heads of their fathers’ houses. The sons of Reuben the first-born of Israel: Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the families of Reuben.
And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish oman; these are the families of Simeon.
And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari; and the years of the life of Levi ere a hundred thirty and seven years.
The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, according to their families.
And the sons of Kohath: Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel; and the years of the life of Kohath ere a hundred thirty and three years.
And the sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their generations.
And Amram took him Jochebed his father’s sister to ife; and she bare him Aaron and Moses: and the years of the life of Amram ere a hundred and thirty and seven years.
And the sons of Izhar: Korah, and Nepheg, and Zichri.
And the sons of Uzziel: Mishael, and Elzaphan, and Sithri.
And Aaron took him Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, to ife; and she bare him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
And the sons of Korah: Assir, and Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the families of the Korahites.

And it came to pass on the day hen Jehovah spake unto Moses in the land of Egypt,

When Pharaoh shall speak unto you, saying, Sho a onder for you; then thou shalt say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and cast it don before Pharaoh, that it become a serpent.

and thy houses shall be filled, and the houses of all thy servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians; as neither thy fathers nor thy fathers’ fathers have seen, since the day that they ere upon the earth unto this day. And he turned, and ent out from Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh’s servants said unto him, Ho long shall this man be a snare unto us? let the men go, that they may serve Jehovah their God: knoest thou not yet that Egypt is destroyed?
And Moses and Aaron ere brought again unto Pharaoh: and he said unto them, Go, serve Jehovah your God; but ho are they that shall go?

and it came to pass, hen Pharaoh ould hardly let us go, that Jehovah sle all the first-born in the land of Egypt, both the first-born of man, and the first-born of beast: therefore I sacrifice to Jehovah all that openeth the omb, being males; but all the first-born of my sons I redeem.

and the name of the other as Eliezer; for \add he said\add*, The God of my father as my help, and delivered me from the sord of Pharaoh.
And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-la, came ith his sons and his ife unto Moses into the ilderness here he as encamped, at the mount of God:
and he said unto Moses, I, thy father-in-la Jethro, am come unto thee, and thy ife, and her to sons ith her.
And Moses ent out to meet his father-in-la, and did obeisance, and kissed him: and they asked each other of their elfare; and they came into the tent.
And Moses told his father-in-la all that Jehovah had done unto Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel’s sake, all the travail that had come upon them by the ay, and ho Jehovah delivered them.
And Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness hich Jehovah had done to Israel, in that he had delivered them out of the hand of the Egyptians.
And Jethro said, Blessed be Jehovah, ho hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of Pharaoh; ho hath delivered the people from under the hand of the Egyptians.
No I kno that Jehovah is greater than all gods; yea, in the thing herein they dealt proudly against them.
And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-la, took a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God: and Aaron came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread ith Moses’ father-in-la before God.
And it came to pass on the morro, that Moses sat to judge the people: and the people stood about Moses from the morning unto the evening.

And hen Moses’ father-in-la sa all that he did to the people, he said, What is this thing that thou doest to the people? hy sittest thou thyself alone, and all the people stand about thee from morning unto even?
And Moses said unto his father-in-la, Because the people come unto me to inquire of God:
hen they have a matter, they come unto me; and I judge beteen a man and his neighbor, and I make them kno the statutes of God, and his las.
And Moses’ father-in-la said unto him, The thing that thou doest is not good.
Thou ilt surely ear aay, both thou, and this people that is ith thee: for the thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.
Hearken no unto my voice, I ill give thee counsel, and God be ith thee: be thou for the people to God-ard, and bring thou the causes unto God:
and thou shalt teach them the statutes and the las, and shalt sho them the ay herein they must alk, and the ork that they must do.

Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating unjust gain; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens:

and let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge themselves: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear \add the burden\add* ith thee.
If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so, then thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people also shall go to their place in peace.
So Moses hearkened to the voice of his father-in-la, and did all that he had said.
And Moses chose able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.

And Moses ent up unto God, and Jehovah called unto him out of the mountain, saying, Thus shalt thou say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel:
Ye have seen hat I did unto the Egyptians, and ho I bare you on eagles’ ings, and brought you unto myself.
No therefore, if ye ill obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be mine on possession from among all peoples: for all the earth is mine:
and ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation. These are the ords hich thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.
And Moses came and called for the elders of the people, and set before them all these ords hich Jehovah commanded him.

no hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned, or shot through; hether it be beast or man, he shall not live: hen the trumpet soundeth long, they shall come up to the mount.

And it came to pass on the third day, hen it as morning, that there ere thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of a trumpet exceeding loud; and all the people that ere in the camp trembled.
And Moses brought forth the people out of the camp to meet God; and they stood at the nether part of the mount.
And mount Sinai, the hole of it, smoked, because Jehovah descended upon it in fire; and the smoke thereof ascended as the smoke of a furnace, and the hole mount quaked greatly.
And hen the voice of the trumpet axed louder and louder, Moses spake, and God ansered him by a voice.
And Jehovah came don upon mount Sinai, to the top of the mount: and Jehovah called Moses to the top of the mount; and Moses ent up.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Go don, charge the people, lest they break through unto Jehovah to gaze, and many of them perish.
And let the priests also, that come near to Jehovah, sanctify themselves, lest Jehovah break forth upon them.
And Moses said unto Jehovah, The people cannot come up to mount Sinai: for thou didst charge us, saying, Set bounds about the mount, and sanctify it.

And Jehovah said unto him, Go, get thee don; and thou shalt come up, thou, and Aaron ith thee: but let not the priests and the people break through to come up unto Jehovah, lest he break forth upon them.
So Moses ent don unto the people, and told them.
And God spake all these ords, saying,
I am Jehovah thy God, ho brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
Thou shalt not make unto thee a graven image, nor any likeness \add of any thing\add* that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the ater under the earth:

thou shalt not bo don thyself unto them, nor serve them; for I Jehovah thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, upon the third and upon the fourth generation of them that hate me,
and shoing lovingkindness unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.
Thou shalt not take the name of Jehovah thy God in vain; for Jehovah ill not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.
Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy ork;

but the seventh day is a sabbath unto Jehovah thy God: \add in it\add* thou shalt not do any ork, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy man-servant, nor thy maid-servant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is ithin thy gates:
for in six days Jehovah made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: herefore Jehovah blessed the sabbath day, and halloed it.
Honor thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be long in the land hich Jehovah thy God giveth thee.
Thou shalt not kill.
Thou shalt not commit adultery.
Thou shalt not steal.
Thou shalt not bear false itness against thy neighbor.
Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbor’s ife, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything that is thy neighbor’s.
And all the people perceived the thunderings, and the lightnings, and the voice of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking: and hen the people sa it, they trembled, and stood afar off.
And they said unto Moses, Speak thou ith us, and e ill hear; but let not God speak ith us, lest e die.
And Moses said unto the people, Fear not: for God is come to prove you, and that his fear may be before you, that ye sin not.
And the people stood afar off, and Moses dre near unto the thick darkness here God as.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Thus thou shalt say unto the children of Israel, Ye yourselves have seen that I have talked ith you from heaven.
Ye shall not make \add other gods\add* ith me; gods of silver, or gods of gold, ye shall not make unto you.

An altar of earth thou shalt make unto me, and shalt sacrifice thereon thy burnt-offerings, and thy peace-offerings, thy sheep, and thine oxen: in every place here I record my name I ill come unto thee and I ill bless thee.
And if thou make me an altar of stone, thou shalt not build it of hen stones; for if thou lift up thy tool upon it, thou hast polluted it.
Neither shalt thou go up by steps unto mine altar, that thy nakedness be not uncovered thereon.
No these are the ordinances hich thou shalt set before them.
If thou buy a Hebre servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.
If he come in by himself, he shall go out by himself: if he be married, then his ife shall go out ith him.
If his master give him a ife and she bear him sons or daughters; the ife and her children shall be her master’s, and he shall go out by himself.
But if the servant shall plainly say, I love my master, my ife, and my children; I ill not go out free:
then his master shall bring him unto God, and shall bring him to the door, or unto the door-post; and his master shall bore his ear through ith an al; and he shall serve him for ever.
And if a man sell his daughter to be a maid-servant, she shall not go out as the men-servants do.
If she please not her master, ho hath espoused her to himself, then shall he let her be redeemed: to sell her unto a foreign people he shall have no poer, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully ith her.
And if he espouse her unto his son, he shall deal ith her after the manner of daughters.
If he take him another \add ife\add*; her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish.
And if he do not these three things unto her, then shall she go out for nothing, ithout money.
He that smiteth a man, so that he dieth, shall surely be put to death.
And if a man lie not in ait, but God deliver \add him\add* into his hand; then I ill appoint thee a place hither he shall flee.
