And if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbor, to slay him ith guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.
And he that smiteth his father, or his mother, shall be surely put to death.
And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.
And he that curseth his father or his mother, shall surely be put to death.
And if men contend, and one smite the other ith a stone, or ith his fist, and he die not, but keep his bed;
if he rise again, and alk abroad upon his staff, then shall he that smote him be quit: only he shall pay for the loss of his time, and shall cause him to be thoroughly healed.
And if a man smite his servant, or his maid, ith a rod, and he die under his hand; he shall surely be punished.
Notithstanding, if he continue a day or to, he shall not be punished: for he is his money.

And if men strive together, and hurt a oman ith child, so that her fruit depart, and yet no harm follo; he shall be surely fined, according as the oman’s husband shall lay upon him; and he shall pay as the judges determine.
But if any harm follo, then thou shalt give life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burning for burning, ound for ound, stripe for stripe.
And if a man smite the eye of his servant, or the eye of his maid, and destroy it; he shall let him go free for his eye’s sake.
And if he smite out his man-servant’s tooth, or his maid-servant’s tooth, he shall let him go free for his tooth’s sake.
And if an ox gore a man or a oman to death, the ox shall be surely stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the oner of the ox shall be quit.

But if the ox as ont to gore in time past, and it hath been testified to its oner, and he hath not kept it in, but it hath killed a man or a oman; the ox shall be stoned, and its oner also shall be put to death.
If there be laid on him a ransom, then he shall give for the redemption of his life hatsoever is laid upon him.
Whether it have gored a son, or have gored a daughter, according to this judgment shall it be done unto him.
If the ox gore a man-servant or a maid-servant, there shall be given unto their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox shall be stoned.
And if a man shall open a pit, or if a man shall dig a pit and not cover it, and an ox or an ass fall therein,
the oner of the pit shall make it good; he shall give money unto the oner thereof, and the dead \add beast\add* shall be his.
And if one man’s ox hurt another’s, so that it dieth, then they shall sell the live ox, and divide the price of it; and the dead also they shall divide.
Or if it be knon that the ox as ont to gore in time past, and its oner hath not kept it in; he shall surely pay ox for ox, and the dead \add beast\add* shall be his on.
If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
If the thief be found breaking in, and be smitten so that he dieth, there shall be no bloodguiltiness for him.
If the sun be risen upon him, there shall be bloodguiltiness for him; he shall make restitution: if he have nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
If the theft be found in his hand alive, hether it be ox, or ass, or sheep, he shall pay double.

If a man shall cause a field or vineyard to be eaten, and shall let his beast loose, and it feed in another man’s field; of the best of his on field, and of the best of his on vineyard, shall he make restitution.
If fire break out, and catch in thorns, so that the shocks of grain, or the standing grain, or the field are consumed; he that kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.
If a man shall deliver unto his neighbor money or stuff to keep, and it be stolen out of the man’s house; if the thief be found, he shall pay double.
If the thief be not found, then the master of the house shall come near unto God, \add to see\add* hether he have not put his hand unto his neighbor’s goods.

For every matter of trespass, hether it be for ox, for ass, for sheep, for raiment, \add or\add* for any manner of lost thing, hereof one saith, This is it, the cause of both parties shall come before God; he hom God shall condemn shall pay double unto his neighbor.
If a man deliver unto his neighbor an ass, or an ox, or a sheep, or any beast, to keep; and it die, or be hurt, or driven aay, no man seeing it:
the oath of Jehovah shall be beteen them both, hether he hath not put his hand unto his neighbor’s goods; and the oner thereof shall accept it, and he shall not make restitution.
But if it be stolen from him, he shall make restitution unto the oner thereof.
If it be torn in pieces, let him bring it for itness: he shall not make good that hich as torn.
And if a man borro aught of his neighbor, and it be hurt, or die, the oner thereof not being ith it, he shall surely make restitution.
If the oner thereof be ith it, he shall not make it good: if it be a hired thing, it came for its hire.
And if a man entice a virgin that is not betrothed, and lie ith her, he shall surely pay a dory for her to be his ife.
If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dory of virgins.
Thou shalt not suffer a sorceress to live.
Whosoever lieth ith a beast shall surely be put to death.
He that sacrificeth unto any god, save unto Jehovah only, shall be utterly destroyed.
And a sojourner shalt thou not rong, neither shalt thou oppress him: for ye ere sojourners in the land of Egypt.
Ye shall not afflict any ido, or fatherless child.
If thou afflict them at all, and they cry at all unto me, I ill surely hear their cry;
and my rath shall ax hot, and I ill kill you ith the sord; and your ives shall be idos, and your children fatherless.
If thou lend money to any of my people ith thee that is poor, thou shalt not be to him as a creditor; neither shall ye lay upon him interest.
If thou at all take thy neighbor’s garment to pledge, thou shalt restore it unto him before the sun goeth don:
for that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin: herein shall he sleep? and it shall come to pass, hen he crieth unto me, that I ill hear; for I am gracious.
Thou shalt not revile God, nor curse a ruler of thy people.
Thou shalt not delay to offer of thy harvest, and of the outflo of thy presses. The first-born of thy sons shalt thou give unto me.
Likeise shalt thou do ith thine oxen, \add and\add* ith thy sheep: seven days it shall be ith its dam; on the eighth day thou shalt give it me.
And ye shall be holy men unto me: therefore ye shall not eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs.
Thou shalt not take up a false report: put not thy hand ith the icked to be an unrighteous itness.
Thou shalt not follo a multitude to do evil; neither shalt thou speak in a cause to turn aside after a multitude to rest \add justice\add*:
neither shalt thou favor a poor man in his cause.
If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again.
If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt forbear to leave him, thou shalt surely release \add it\add* ith him.
Thou shalt not rest the justice \add due\add* to thy poor in his cause.
Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I ill not justify the icked.
And thou shalt take no bribe: for a bribe blindeth them that have sight, and perverteth the ords of the righteous.
And a sojourner shalt thou not oppress: for ye kno the heart of a sojourner, seeing ye ere sojourners in the land of Egypt.
And six years thou shalt so thy land, and shalt gather in the increase thereof:

but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie fallo; that the poor of thy people may eat: and hat they leave the beast of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal ith thy vineyard, \add and\add* ith thy oliveyard.
Six days thou shalt do thy ork, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest; that thine ox and thine ass may have rest, and the son of thy handmaid, and the sojourner, may be refreshed.
And in all things that I have said unto you take ye heed: and make no mention of the name of other gods, neither let it be heard out of thy mouth.
Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year.

The feast of unleavened bread shalt thou keep: seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, as I commanded thee, at the time appointed in the month Abib ( for in it thou camest out from Egypt); and none shall appear before me empty:
and the feast of harvest, the first-fruits of thy labors, hich thou soest in the field: and the feast of ingathering, at the end of the year, hen thou gatherest in thy labors out of the field.
Three times in the year all thy males shall appear before the Lord Jehovah.
Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice ith leavened bread; neither shall the fat of my feast remain all night until the morning.
The first of the first-fruits of thy ground thou shalt bring into the house of Jehovah thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.
Behold, I send an angel before thee, to keep thee by the ay, and to bring thee into the place hich I have prepared.
Take ye heed before him, and hearken unto his voice; provoke him not; for he ill not pardon your transgression: for my name is in him.
But if thou shalt indeed hearken unto his voice, and do all that I speak; then I ill be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.
For mine angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in unto the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Canaanite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite: and I ill cut them off.
Thou shalt not bo don to their gods, nor serve them, nor do after their orks; but thou shalt utterly overthro them, and break in pieces their pillars.
And ye shall serve Jehovah your God, and he ill bless thy bread, and thy ater; and I ill take sickness aay from the midst of thee.
There shall none cast her young, nor be barren, in thy land: the number of thy days I ill fulfil.
I ill send my terror before thee, and ill discomfit all the people to hom thou shalt come, and I ill make all thine enemies turn their backs unto thee.
And I ill send the hornet before thee, hich shall drive out the Hivite, the Canaanite, and the Hittite, from before thee.
I ill not drive them out from before thee in one year, lest the land become desolate, and the beasts of the field multiply against thee.
By little and little I ill drive them out from before thee, until thou be increased, and inherit the land.

And I ill set thy border from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the ilderness unto the River: for I ill deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand: and thou shalt drive them out before thee.
Thou shalt make no covenant ith them, nor ith their gods.
They shall not dell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me; for if thou serve their gods, it ill surely be a snare unto thee.
And he said unto Moses, Come up unto Jehovah, thou, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; and orship ye afar off:
and Moses alone shall come near unto Jehovah; but they shall not come near; neither shall the people go up ith him.
And Moses came and told the people all the ords of Jehovah, and all the ordinances: and all the people ansered ith one voice, and said, All the ords hich Jehovah hath spoken ill e do.
And Moses rote all the ords of Jehovah, and rose up early in the morning, and builded an altar under the mount, and telve pillars, according to the telve tribes of Israel.
And he sent young men of the children of Israel, ho offered burnt-offerings, and sacrificed peace-offerings of oxen unto Jehovah.
And Moses took half of the blood, and put it in basins; and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar.
And he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people: and they said, All that Jehovah hath spoken ill e do, and be obedient.
And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, hich Jehovah hath made ith you concerning all these ords.
Then ent up Moses, and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel:
and they sa the God of Israel; and there as under his feet as it ere a paved ork of sapphire stone, and as it ere the very heaven for clearness.
And upon the nobles of the children of Israel he laid not his hand: and they beheld God, and did eat and drink.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Come up to me into the mount, and be there: and I ill give thee the tables of stone, and the la and the commandment, hich I have ritten, that thou mayest teach them.
And Moses rose up, and Joshua his minister: and Moses ent up into the mount of God.
And he said unto the elders, Tarry ye here for us, until e come again unto you: and, behold, Aaron and Hur are ith you: hosoever hath a cause, let him come near unto them.
And Moses ent up into the mount, and the cloud covered the mount.
And the glory of Jehovah abode upon mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days: and the seventh day he called unto Moses out of the midst of the cloud.
And the appearance of the glory of Jehovah as like devouring fire on the top of the mount in the eyes of the children of Israel.
And Moses entered into the midst of the cloud, and ent up into the mount: and Moses as in the mount forty days and forty nights.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, that they take for me an offering: of every man hose heart maketh him illing ye shall take my offering.
And this is the offering hich ye shall take of them: gold, and silver, and brass,
and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ \add hair\add*,
and rams’ skins dyed red, and sealskins, and acacia ood,
oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil, and for the seet incense,
onyx stones, and stones to be set, for the ephod, and for the breastplate.
And let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dell among them.
According to all that I sho thee, the pattern of the tabernacle, and the pattern of all the furniture thereof, even so shall ye make it.
And they shall make an ark of acacia ood: to cubits and a half shall be the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
And thou shalt overlay it ith pure gold, ithin and ithout shalt thou overlay it, and shalt make upon it a cron of gold round about.
And thou shalt cast four rings of gold for it, and put them in the four feet thereof; and to rings shall be on the one side of it, and to rings on the other side of it.
And thou shalt make staves of acacia ood, and overlay them ith gold.
And thou shalt put the staves into the rings on the sides of the ark, hereith to bear the ark.
The staves shall be in the rings of the ark: they shall not be taken from it.
And thou shalt put into the ark the testimony hich I shall give thee.
And thou shalt make a mercy-seat of pure gold: to cubits and a half \add shall be\add* the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof.
And thou shalt make to cherubim of gold; of beaten ork shalt thou make them, at the to ends of the mercy-seat.
And make one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end: of one piece ith the mercy-seat shall ye make the cherubim on the to ends thereof.
And the cherubim shall spread out their ings on high, covering the mercy-seat ith their ings, ith their faces one to another; toard the mercy-seat shall the faces of the cherubim be.
And thou shalt put the mercy-seat above upon the ark; and in the ark thou shalt put the testimony that I shall give thee.

And there I ill meet ith thee, and I ill commune ith thee from above the mercy-seat, from beteen the to cherubim hich are upon the ark of the testimony, of all things hich I ill give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel.
And thou shalt make a table of acacia ood: to cubits \add shall be\add* the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
And thou shalt overlay it ith pure gold, and make thereto a cron of gold round about.
And thou shalt make unto it a border of a handbreadth round about; and thou shalt make a golden cron to the border thereof round about.
And thou shalt make for it four rings of gold, and put the rings in the four corners that are on the four feet thereof.
Close by the border shall the rings be, for places for the staves to bear the table.
And thou shalt make the staves of acacia ood, and overlay them ith gold, that the table may be borne ith them.
And thou shalt make the dishes thereof, and the spoons thereof, and the flagons thereof, and the bols thereof, hereith to pour out: of pure gold shalt thou make them.
And thou shalt set upon the table shobread before me alay.
And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten ork shall the candlestick be made, even its base, and its shaft; its cups, its knops, and its floers, shall be of one piece ith it:
and there shall be six branches going out of the sides thereof; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side thereof, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side thereof:

three cups made like almond-blossoms in one branch, a knop and a floer; and three cups made like almond-blossoms in the other branch, a knop and a floer: so for the six branches going out of the candlestick:
and in the candlestick four cups made like almond-blossoms, the knops thereof, and the floers thereof;

and a knop under to branches of one piece ith it, and a knop under to branches of one piece ith it, and a knop under to branches of one piece ith it, for the six branches going out of the candlestick.
Their knops and their branches shall be of one piece ith it; the hole of it one beaten ork of pure gold.
And thou shalt make the lamps thereof, seven: and they shall light the lamps thereof, to give light over against it.
And the snuffers thereof, and the snuffdishes thereof, shall be of pure gold.
Of a talent of pure gold shall it be made, ith all these vessels.
And see that thou make them after their pattern, hich hath been shoed thee in the mount.
Moreover thou shalt make the tabernacle ith ten curtains; of fine tined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, ith cherubim the ork of the skilful orkman shalt thou make them.
The length of each curtain shall be eight and tenty cubits, and the breadth of each curtain four cubits: all the curtains shall have one measure.
Five curtains shall be coupled together one to another; and \add the other\add* five curtains shall be coupled one to another.
And thou shalt make loops of blue upon the edge of the one curtain from the selvedge in the coupling; and likeise shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain that is outmost in the second coupling.
Fifty loops shalt thou make in the one curtain, and fifty loops shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain that is in the second coupling; the loops shall be opposite one to another.
And thou shalt make fifty clasps of gold, and couple the curtains one to another ith the clasps: and the tabernacle shall be one \add hole\add*.
And thou shalt make curtains of goats’ \add hair\add* for a tent over the tabernacle: eleven curtains shalt thou make them.
The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the breadth of each curtain four cubits: the eleven curtains shall have one measure.
And thou shalt couple five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves, and shalt double over the sixth curtain in the forefront of the tent.
And thou shalt make fifty loops on the edge of the one curtain that is outmost in the coupling, and fifty loops upon the edge of the curtain hich is \add outmost in\add* the second coupling.
And thou shalt make fifty clasps of brass, and put the clasps into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.
And the overhanging part that remaineth of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remaineth, shall hang over the back of the tabernacle.

And the cubit on the one side, and the cubit on the other side, of that hich remaineth in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it.
And thou shalt make a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of sealskins above.
And thou shalt make the boards for the tabernacle of acacia ood, standing up.
Ten cubits shall be the length of a board, and a cubit and a half the breadth of each board.
To tenons shall there be in each board, joined one to another: thus shalt thou make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
And thou shalt make the boards for the tabernacle, tenty boards for the south side southard.
And thou shalt make forty sockets of silver under the tenty boards; to sockets under one board for its to tenons, and to sockets under another board for its to tenons:
and for the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, tenty boards,
and their forty sockets of silver; to sockets under one board, and to sockets under another board.
And for the hinder part of the tabernacle estard thou shalt make six boards.
And to boards shalt thou make for the corners of the tabernacle in the hinder part.
And they shall be double beneath, and in like manner they shall be entire unto the top thereof unto one ring: thus shall it be for them both; they shall be for the to corners.
And there shall be eight boards, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets; to sockets under one board, and to sockets under another board.
And thou shalt make bars of acacia ood: five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle, for the hinder part estard.
And the middle bar in the midst of the boards shall pass through from end to end.
And thou shalt overlay the boards ith gold, and make their rings of gold for places for the bars: and thou shalt overlay the bars ith gold.
And thou shalt rear up the tabernacle according to the fashion thereof hich hath been shoed thee in the mount.
And thou shalt make a veil of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen: ith cherubim the ork of the skilful orkman shall it be made:
and thou shalt hang it upon four pillars of acacia overlaid ith gold; their hooks \add shall be\add* of gold, upon four sockets of silver.
And thou shalt hang up the veil under the clasps, and shalt bring in thither ithin the veil the ark of the testimony: and the veil shall separate unto you beteen the holy place and the most holy.
And thou shalt put the mercy-seat upon the ark of the testimony in the most holy place.
And thou shalt set the table ithout the veil, and the candlestick over against the table on the side of the tabernacle toard the south: and thou shalt put the table on the north side.
And thou shalt make a screen for the door of the Tent, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen, the ork of the embroiderer.
And thou shalt make for the screen five pillars of acacia, and overlay them ith gold: their hooks shall be of gold: and thou shalt cast five sockets of brass for them.
And thou shalt make the altar of acacia ood, five cubits long, and five cubits broad; the altar shall be foursquare: and the height thereof shall be three cubits.
And thou shalt make the horns of it upon the four corners thereof; the horns thereof shall be of one piece ith it: and thou shalt overlay it ith brass.
And thou shalt make its pots to take aay its ashes, and its shovels, and its basins, and its flesh-hooks, and its firepans: all the vessels thereof thou shalt make of brass.
And thou shalt make for it a grating of netork of brass: and upon the net shalt thou make four brazen rings in the four corners thereof.
And thou shalt put it under the ledge round the altar beneath, that the net may reach halfay up the altar.
And thou shalt make staves for the altar, staves of acacia ood, and overlay them ith brass.
And the staves thereof shall be put into the rings, and the staves shall be upon the to sides of the altar, in bearing it.
Hollo ith planks shalt thou make it: as it hath been shoed thee in the mount, so shall they make it.
And thou shalt make the court of the tabernacle: for the south side southard there shall be hangings for the court of fine tined linen a hundred cubits long for one side:
and the pillars thereof shall be tenty, and their sockets tenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets \add shall be\add* of silver.

And likeise for the north side in length there shall be hangings a hundred cubits long, and the pillars thereof tenty, and their sockets tenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
And for the breadth of the court on the est side shall be hangings of fifty cubits; their pillars ten, and their sockets ten.
And the breadth of the court on the east side eastard shall be fifty cubits.
The hangings for the one side \add of the gate\add* shall be fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
And for the other side shall be hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
And for the gate of the court shall be a screen of tenty cubits, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen, the ork of the embroiderer; their pillars four, and their sockets four.
All the pillars of the court round about shall be filleted ith silver; their hooks of silver, and their sockets of brass.
The length of the court shall be a hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty every here, and the height five cubits, of fine tined linen, and their sockets of brass.
All the instruments of the tabernacle in all the service thereof, and all the pins thereof, and all the pins of the court, shall be of brass.
And thou shalt command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.

In the tent of meeting, ithout the veil hich is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep it in order from evening to morning before Jehovah: it shall be a statute for ever throughout their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.

And bring thou near unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons ith him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office, even Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.
And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, for glory and for beauty.
And thou shalt speak unto all that are ise-hearted, hom I have filled ith the spirit of isdom, that they make Aaron’s garments to sanctify him, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.

And these are the garments hich they shall make: a breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a coat of checker ork, a mitre, and a girdle: and they shall make holy garments for Aaron thy brother, and his sons, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.
And they shall take the gold, and the blue, and the purple, and the scarlet, and the fine linen.
And they shall make the ephod of gold, of blue, and purple, scarlet, and fine tined linen, the ork of the skilful orkman.
It shall have to shoulder-pieces joined to the to ends thereof, that it may be joined together.
And the skilfully oven band, hich is upon it, hereith to gird it on, shall be like the ork thereof \add and\add* of the same piece; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen.
And thou shalt take to onyx stones, and grave on them the names of the children of Israel:
six of their names on the one stone, and the names of the six that remain on the other stone, according to their birth.

With the ork of an engraver in stone, like the engravings of a signet, shalt thou engrave the to stones, according to the names of the children of Israel: thou shalt make them to be inclosed in settings of gold.

And thou shalt put the to stones upon the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the children of Israel: and Aaron shall bear their names before Jehovah upon his to shoulders for a memorial.
And thou shalt make settings of gold,
and to chains of pure gold; like cords shalt thou make them, of reathen ork: and thou shalt put the reathen chains on the settings.

And thou shalt make a breastplate of judgment, the ork of the skilful orkman; like the ork of the ephod thou shalt make it; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen, shalt thou make it.
Foursquare it shall be \add and\add* double; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span the breadth thereof.
And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, four ros of stones: a ro of sardius, topaz, and carbuncle shall be the first ro;
and the second ro an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond;
and the third ro a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
and the fourth ro a beryl, and an onyx, and a jasper: they shall be inclosed in gold in their settings.

And the stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, telve, according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, every one according to his name, they shall be for the telve tribes.
And thou shalt make upon the breastplate chains like cords, of reathen ork of pure gold.
And thou shalt make upon the breastplate to rings of gold, and shalt put the to rings on the to ends of the breastplate.
And thou shalt put the to reathen chains of gold in the to rings at the ends of the breastplate.
And the \add other\add* to ends of the to reathen chains thou shalt put on the to settings, and put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod in the forepart thereof.
And thou shalt make to rings of gold, and thou shalt put them upon the to ends of the breastplate, upon the edge thereof, hich is toard the side of the ephod inard.

And thou shalt make to rings of gold, and shalt put them on the to shoulder-pieces of the ephod underneath, in the forepart thereof, close by the coupling thereof, above the skilfully oven band of the ephod.

And they shall bind the breastplate by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod ith a lace of blue, that it may be upon the skilfully oven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate be not loosed from the ephod.
And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart, hen he goeth in unto the holy place, for a memorial before Jehovah continually.

And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be upon Aaron’s heart, hen he goeth in before Jehovah: and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before Jehovah continually.
And thou shalt make the robe of the ephod all of blue.
And it shall have a hole for the head in the midst thereof: it shall have a binding of oven ork round about the hole of it, as it ere the hole of a coat of mail, that it be not rent.
And upon the skirts of it thou shalt make pomegranates of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, round about the skirts thereof; and bells of gold beteen them round about:
a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, upon the skirts of the robe round about.
And it shall be upon Aaron to minister: and the sound thereof shall be heard hen he goeth in unto the holy place before Jehovah, and hen he cometh out, that he die not.
And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLY TO JEHOVAH.
And thou shalt put it on a lace of blue, and it shall be upon the mitre; upon the forefront of the mitre it shall be.

And it shall be upon Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron shall bear the iniquity of the holy things, hich the children of Israel shall hallo in all their holy gifts; and it shall be alays upon his forehead, that they may be accepted before Jehovah.
And thou shalt eave the coat in checker ork of fine linen, and thou shalt make a mitre of fine linen, and thou shalt make a girdle, the ork of the embroiderer.
And for Aaron’s sons thou shalt make coats, and thou shalt make for them girdles, and head-tires shalt thou make for them, for glory and for beauty.
And thou shalt put them upon Aaron thy brother, and upon his sons ith him, and shalt anoint them, and consecrate them, and sanctify them, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office.
And thou shalt make them linen breeches to cover the flesh of their nakedness; from the loins even unto the thighs they shall reach:

and they shall be upon Aaron, and upon his sons, hen they go in unto the tent of meeting, or hen they come near unto the altar to minister in the holy place; that they bear not iniquity, and die: it shall be a statute for ever unto him and unto his seed after him.
And this is the thing that thou shalt do unto them to hallo them, to minister unto me in the priest’s office: take one young bullock and to rams ithout blemish,
and unleavened bread, and cakes unleavened mingled ith oil, and afers unleavened anointed ith oil: of fine heaten flour shalt thou make them.
And thou shalt put them into one basket, and bring them in the basket, ith the bullock and the to rams.
And Aaron and his sons thou shalt bring unto the door of the tent of meeting, and shalt ash them ith ater.
And thou shalt take the garments, and put upon Aaron the coat, and the robe of the ephod, and the ephod, and the breastplate, and gird him ith the skilfully oven band of the ephod;
and thou shalt set the mitre upon his head, and put the holy cron upon the mitre.
Then shalt thou take the anointing oil, and pour it upon his head, and anoint him.
And thou shalt bring his sons, and put coats upon them.
And thou shalt gird them ith girdles, Aaron and his sons, and bind head-tires on them: and they shall have the priesthood by a perpetual statute: and thou shalt consecrate Aaron and his sons.
And thou shalt bring the bullock before the tent of meeting: and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the bullock.
And thou shalt kill the bullock before Jehovah, at the door of the tent of meeting.
And thou shalt take of the blood of the bullock, and put it upon the horns of the altar ith thy finger; and thou shalt pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.
And thou shalt take all the fat that covereth the inards, and the caul upon the liver, and the to kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and burn them upon the altar.
But the flesh of the bullock, and its skin, and its dung, shalt thou burn ith fire ithout the camp: it is a sin-offering.
Thou shalt also take the one ram; and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the ram.
And thou shalt slay the ram, and thou shalt take its blood, and sprinkle it round about upon the altar.
And thou shalt cut the ram into its pieces, and ash its inards, and its legs, and put them ith its pieces, and ith its head.
And thou shalt burn the hole ram upon the altar: it is a burnt-offering unto Jehovah; it is a seet savor, an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
And thou shalt take the other ram; and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the ram.

Then shalt thou kill the ram, and take of its blood, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of Aaron, and upon the tip of the right ear of his sons, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot, and sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about.

And thou shalt take of the blood that is upon the altar, and of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it upon Aaron, and upon his garments, and upon his sons, and upon the garments of his sons ith him: and he shall be halloed, and his garments, and his sons, and his sons’ garments ith him.

Also thou shalt take of the ram the fat, and the fat tail, and the fat that covereth the inards, and the caul of the liver, and the to kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, and the right thigh ( for it is a ram of consecration),
and one loaf of bread, and one cake of oiled bread, and one afer, out of the basket of unleavened bread that is before Jehovah:
and thou shalt put the hole upon the hands of Aaron, and upon the hands of his sons, and shalt ave them for a ave-offering before Jehovah.
And thou shalt take them from their hands, and burn them on the altar upon the burnt-offering, for a seet savor before Jehovah: it is an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
And thou shalt take the breast of Aaron’s ram of consecration, and ave it for a ave-offering before Jehovah: and it shall be thy portion.

And thou shalt sanctify the breast of the ave-offering, and the thigh of the heave-offering, hich is aved, and hich is heaved up, of the ram of consecration, even of that hich is for Aaron, and of that hich is for his sons:

and it shall be for Aaron and his sons as \add their\add* portion for ever from the children of Israel; for it is a heave-offering: and it shall be a heave-offering from the children of Israel of the sacrifices of their peace-offerings, even their heave-offering unto Jehovah.
And the holy garments of Aaron shall be for his sons after him, to be anointed in them, and to be consecrated in them.
Seven days shall the son that is priest in his stead put them on, hen he cometh into the tent of meeting to minister in the holy place.
And thou shalt take the ram of consecration, and boil its flesh in a holy place.
And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram, and the bread that is in the basket, at the door of the tent of meeting.
And they shall eat those things hereith atonement as made, to consecrate \add and\add* to sanctify them: but a stranger shall not eat thereof, because they are holy.
And if aught of the flesh of the consecration, or of the bread, remain unto the morning, then thou shalt burn the remainder ith fire: it shall not be eaten, because it is holy.
And thus shalt thou do unto Aaron, and to his sons, according to all that I have commanded thee: seven days shalt thou consecrate them.
And every day shalt thou offer the bullock of sin-offering for atonement: and thou shalt cleanse the altar, hen thou makest atonement for it; and thou shalt anoint it, to sanctify it.
Seven days thou shalt make atonement for the altar, and sanctify it: and the altar shall be most holy; hatsoever toucheth the altar shall be holy.
No this is that hich thou shalt offer upon the altar: to lambs a year old day by day continually.
The one lamb thou shalt offer in the morning; and the other lamb thou shalt offer at even:
and ith the one lamb a tenth part \add of an ephah\add* of fine flour mingled ith the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil, and the fourth part of a hin of ine for a drink-offering.

And the other lamb thou shalt offer at even, and shalt do thereto according to the meal-offering of the morning, and according to the drink-offering thereof, for a seet savor, an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
It shall be a continual burnt-offering throughout your generations at the door of the tent of meeting before Jehovah, here I ill meet ith you, to speak there unto thee.
And there I ill meet ith the children of Israel; and \add the Tent\add* shall be sanctified by my glory.
And I ill sanctify the tent of meeting, and the altar: Aaron also and his sons ill I sanctify, to minister to me in the priest’s office.
And I ill dell among the children of Israel, and ill be their God.
And they shall kno that I am Jehovah their God, that brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, that I might dell among them: I am Jehovah their God.
And thou shalt make an altar to burn incense upon: of acacia ood shalt thou make it.
A cubit shall be the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof; foursquare shall it be; and to cubits shall be the height thereof: the horns thereof shall be of one piece ith it.
And thou shalt overlay it ith pure gold, the top thereof, and the sides thereof round about, and the horns thereof; and thou shalt make unto it a cron of gold round about.
And to golden rings shalt thou make for it under the cron thereof; upon the to ribs thereof, upon the to sides of it shalt thou make them; and they shall be for places for staves hereith to bear it.
And thou shalt make the staves of acacia ood, and overlay them ith gold.
And thou shalt put it before the veil that is by the ark of the testimony, before the mercy-seat that is over the testimony, here I ill meet ith thee.
And Aaron shall burn thereon incense of seet spices: every morning, hen he dresseth the lamps, he shall burn it.
And hen Aaron lighteth the lamps at even, he shall burn it, a perpetual incense before Jehovah throughout your generations.
Ye shall offer no strange incense thereon, nor burnt-offering, nor meal-offering; and ye shall pour no drink-offering thereon.

And Aaron shall make atonement upon the horns of it once in the year; ith the blood of the sin-offering of atonement once in the year shall he make atonement for it throughout your generations: it is most holy unto Jehovah.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

When thou takest the sum of the children of Israel, according to those that are numbered of them, then shall they give every man a ransom for his soul unto Jehovah, hen thou numberest them; that there be no plague among them, hen thou numberest them.

This they shall give, every one that passeth over unto them that are numbered, half a shekel after the shekel of the sanctuary; ( the shekel is tenty gerahs), half a shekel for an offering to Jehovah.
Every one that passeth over unto them that are numbered, from tenty years old and upard, shall give the offering of Jehovah.
The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than the half shekel, hen they give the offering of Jehovah, to make atonement for your souls.

And thou shalt take the atonement money from the children of Israel, and shalt appoint it for the service of the tent of meeting; that it may be a memorial for the children of Israel before Jehovah, to make atonement for your souls.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Thou shalt also make a laver of brass, and the base thereof of brass, hereat to ash. And thou shalt put it beteen the tent of meeting and the altar, and thou shalt put ater therein.
And Aaron and his sons shall ash their hands and their feet thereat:
hen they go into the tent of meeting, they shall ash ith ater, that they die not; or hen they come near to the altar to minister, to burn an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
So they shall ash their hands and their feet, that they die not: and it shall be a statute for ever to them, even to him and to his seed throughout their generations.
Moreover Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Take thou also unto thee the chief spices: of floing myrrh five hundred \add shekels\add*, and of seet cinnamon half so much, even to hundred and fifty, and of seet calamus to hundred and fifty,
and of cassia five hundred, after the shekel of the sanctuary, and of olive oil a hin;
and thou shalt make it a holy anointing oil, a perfume compounded after the art of the perfumer: it shall be a holy anointing oil.
And thou shalt anoint thereith the tent of meeting, and the ark of the testimony,
and the table and all the vessels thereof, and the candlestick and the vessels thereof, and the altar of incense,
and the altar of burnt-offering ith all the vessels thereof, and the laver and the base thereof.
And thou shalt sanctify them, that they may be most holy: hatsoever toucheth them shall be holy.
And thou shalt anoint Aaron and his sons, and sanctify them, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office.
And thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, This shall be a holy anointing oil unto me throughout your generations.
Upon the flesh of man shall it not be poured, neither shall ye make any like it, according to the composition thereof: it is holy, \add and\add* it shall be holy unto you.
Whosoever compoundeth any like it, or hosoever putteth any of it upon a stranger, he shall be cut off from his people.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Take unto thee seet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; seet spices ith pure frankincense: of each shall there be a like eight;
and thou shalt make of it incense, a perfume after the art of the perfumer, seasoned ith salt, pure \add and\add* holy:
and thou shalt beat some of it very small, and put of it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, here I ill meet ith thee: it shall be unto you most holy.
And the incense hich thou shalt make, according to the composition thereof ye shall not make for yourselves: it shall be unto thee holy for Jehovah.
Whosoever shall make like unto that, to smell thereof, he shall be cut off from his people.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
See, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah:
and I have filled him ith the Spirit of God, in isdom, and in understanding, and in knoledge, and in all manner of orkmanship,
to devise skilful orks, to ork in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
and in cutting of stones for setting, and in carving of ood, to ork in all manner of orkmanship.

And I, behold, I have appointed ith him Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and in the heart of all that are ise-hearted I have put isdom, that they may make all that I have commanded thee:
the tent of meeting, and the ark of the testimony, and the mercy-seat that is thereupon, and all the furniture of the Tent,
and the table and its vessels, and the pure candlestick ith all its vessels, and the altar of incense,
and the altar of burnt-offering ith all its vessels, and the laver and its base,
and the finely rought garments, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office,
and the anointing oil, and the incense of seet spices for the holy place: according to all that I have commanded thee shall they do.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

Speak thou also unto the children of Israel, saying, Verily ye shall keep my sabbaths: for it is a sign beteen me and you throughout your generations; that ye may kno that I am Jehovah ho sanctifieth you.

Ye shall keep the sabbath therefore; for it is holy unto you: every one that profaneth it shall surely be put to death; for hosoever doeth any ork therein, that soul shall be cut off from among his people.
Six days shall ork be done, but on the seventh day is a sabbath of solemn rest, holy to Jehovah: hosoever doeth any ork on the sabbath day, he shall surely be put to death.
Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant.
It is a sign beteen me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days Jehovah made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and as refreshed.
And he gave unto Moses, hen he had made an end of communing ith him upon mount Sinai, the to tables of the testimony, tables of stone, ritten ith the finger of God.

And hen the people sa that Moses delayed to come don from the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, hich shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, e kno not hat is become of him.
And Aaron said unto them, Break off the golden rings, hich are in the ears of your ives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me.
And all the people brake off the golden rings hich ere in their ears, and brought them unto Aaron.
And he received it at their hand, and fashioned it ith a graving tool, and made it a molten calf: and they said, These are thy gods, O Israel, hich brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
And hen Aaron sa \add this\add*, he built an altar before it; and Aaron made proclamation, and said, To-morro shall be a feast to Jehovah.
And they rose up early on the morro, and offered burnt-offerings, and brought peace-offerings; and the people sat don to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, Go, get thee don; for thy people, that thou broughtest up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves:

they have turned aside quickly out of the ay hich I commanded them: they have made them a molten calf, and have orshipped it, and have sacrificed unto it, and said, These are thy gods, O Israel, hich brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people:
no therefore let me alone, that my rath may ax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I ill make of thee a great nation.
And Moses besought Jehovah his God, and said, Jehovah, hy doth thy rath ax hot against thy people, that thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt ith great poer and ith a mighty hand?

Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, saying, For evil did he bring them forth, to slay them in the mountains, and to consume them from the face of the earth? Turn from thy fierce rath, and repent of this evil against thy people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants, to hom thou sarest by thine on self, and saidst unto them, I ill multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and all this land that I have spoken of ill I give unto your seed, and they shall inherit it for ever.
And Jehovah repented of the evil hich he said he ould do unto his people.
And Moses turned, and ent don from the mount, ith the to tables of the testimony in his hand; tables that ere ritten on both their sides; on the one side and on the other ere they ritten.
And the tables ere the ork of God, and the riting as the riting of God, graven upon the tables.
And hen Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted, he said unto Moses, There is a noise of ar in the camp.
And he said, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither is it the voice of them that cry for being overcome; but the noise of them that sing do I hear.
And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he sa the calf and the dancing: and Moses’ anger axed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.
And he took the calf hich they had made, and burnt it ith fire, and ground it to poder, and streed it upon the ater, and made the children of Israel drink of it.
And Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought a great sin upon them?
And Aaron said, Let not the anger of my lord ax hot: thou knoest the people, that they are \add set\add* on evil.
For they said unto me, Make us gods, hich shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, e kno not hat is become of him.
And I said unto them, Whosoever hath any gold, let them break it off: so they gave it me; and I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf.
And hen Moses sa that the people ere broken loose, ( for Aaron had let them loose for a derision among their enemies,)
then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Whoso is on Jehovah’s side, \add let him come\add* unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.

And he said unto them, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Put ye every man his sord upon his thigh, and go to and fro from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbor.
And the sons of Levi did according to the ord of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.
And Moses said, Consecrate yourselves to-day to Jehovah, yea, every man against his son, and against his brother; that he may besto upon you a blessing this day.
And it came to pass on the morro, that Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin: and no I ill go up unto Jehovah; peradventure I shall make atonement for your sin.
And Moses returned unto Jehovah, and said, Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made them gods of gold.
Yet no, if thou ilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book hich thou hast ritten.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him ill I blot out of my book.
And no go, lead the people unto \add the place\add* of hich I have spoken unto thee: behold, mine angel shall go before thee; nevertheless in the day hen I visit, I ill visit their sin upon them.
And Jehovah smote the people, because they made the calf, hich Aaron made.

And Jehovah spake unto Moses, Depart, go up hence, thou and the people that thou hast brought up out of the land of Egypt, unto the land of hich I sare unto Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, Unto thy seed ill I give it:
and I ill send an angel before thee; and I ill drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite:
unto a land floing ith milk and honey: for I ill not go up in the midst of thee, for thou art a stiffnecked people, lest I consume thee in the ay.
And hen the people heard these evil tidings, they mourned: and no man did put on him his ornaments.

And Jehovah said unto Moses, Say unto the children of Israel, Ye are a stiffnecked people; if I go up into the midst of thee for one moment, I shall consume thee: therefore no put off thy ornaments from thee, that I may kno hat to do unto thee.
And the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from mount Horeb onard.

No Moses used to take the tent and to pitch it ithout the camp, afar off from the camp; and he called it, The tent of meeting. And it came to pass, that every one that sought Jehovah ent out unto the tent of meeting, hich as ithout the camp.
And it came to pass, hen Moses ent out unto the Tent, that all the people rose up, and stood, every man at his tent door, and looked after Moses, until he as gone into the Tent.
And it came to pass, hen Moses entered into the Tent, the pillar of cloud descended, and stood at the door of the Tent: and \add Jehovah\add* spake ith Moses.
And all the people sa the pillar of cloud stand at the door of the Tent: and all the people rose up and orshipped, every man at his tent door.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend. And he turned again into the camp: but his minister Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the Tent.

And Moses said unto Jehovah, See, thou sayest unto me, Bring up this people: and thou hast not let me kno hom thou ilt send ith me. Yet thou hast said, I kno thee by name, and thou hast also found favor in my sight.
No therefore, I pray thee, if I have found favor in thy sight, sho me no thy ays, that I may kno thee, to the end that I may find favor in thy sight: and consider that this nation is thy people.
And he said, My presence shall go \add ith thee\add*, and I ill give thee rest.
And he said unto him, If thy presence go not \add ith me\add*, carry us not up hence.

For herein no shall it be knon that I have found favor in thy sight, I and thy people? is it not in that thou goest ith us, so that e are separated, I and thy people, from all the people that are upon the face of the earth?
And Jehovah said unto Moses, I ill do this thing also that thou hast spoken; for thou hast found favor in my sight, and I kno thee by name.
And he said, Sho me, I pray thee, thy glory.
And he said, I ill make all my goodness pass before thee, and ill proclaim the name of Jehovah before thee; and I ill be gracious to hom I ill be gracious, and ill sho mercy on hom I ill sho mercy.
And he said, Thou canst not see my face; for man shall not see me and live.
And Jehovah said, Behold, there is a place by me, and thou shalt stand upon the rock:
and it shall come to pass, hile my glory passeth by, that I ill put thee in a cleft of the rock, and ill cover thee ith my hand until I have passed by:
and I ill take aay my hand, and thou shalt see my back; but my face shall not be seen.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, He thee to tables of stone like unto the first: and I ill rite upon the tables the ords that ere on the first tables, hich thou brakest.
And be ready by the morning, and come up in the morning unto mount Sinai, and present thyself there to me on the top of the mount.
And no man shall come up ith thee; neither let any man be seen throughout all the mount; neither let the flocks nor herds feed before that mount.
And he heed to tables of stone like unto the first; and Moses rose up early in the morning, and ent up unto mount Sinai, as Jehovah had commanded him, and took in his hand to tables of stone.
And Jehovah descended in the cloud, and stood ith him there, and proclaimed the name of Jehovah.
And Jehovah passed by before him, and proclaimed, Jehovah, Jehovah, a God merciful and gracious, slo to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness and truth;

keeping lovingkindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin; and that ill by no means clear \add the guilty\add*, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, upon the third and upon the fourth generation.
And Moses made haste, and boed his head toard the earth, and orshipped.

And he said, If no I have found favor in thy sight, O Lord, let the Lord, I pray thee, go in the midst of us; for it is a stiffnecked people; and pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us for thine inheritance.

And he said, Behold, I make a covenant: before all thy people I ill do marvels, such as have not been rought in all the earth, nor in any nation; and all the people among hich thou art shall see the ork of Jehovah; for it is a terrible thing that I do ith thee.
Observe thou that hich I command thee this day: behold, I drive out before thee the Amorite, and the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
Take heed to thyself, lest thou make a covenant ith the inhabitants of the land hither thou goest, lest it be for a snare in the midst of thee:
but ye shall break don their altars, and dash in pieces their pillars, and ye shall cut don their Asherim;
( for thou shalt orship no other god: for Jehovah, hose name is Jealous, is a jealous God);
lest thou make a covenant ith the inhabitants of the land, and they play the harlot after their gods, and sacrifice unto their gods, and one call thee and thou eat of his sacrifice;
and thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters play the harlot after their gods, and make thy sons play the harlot after their gods.
Thou shalt make thee no molten gods.

The feast of unleavened bread shalt thou keep. Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, as I commanded thee, at the time appointed in the month Abib; for in the month Abib thou camest out from Egypt.
All that openeth the omb is mine; and all thy cattle that is male, the firstlings of co and sheep.

And the firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem ith a lamb: and if thou ilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break its neck. All the first-born of thy sons thou shalt redeem. And none shall appear before me empty.
Six days thou shalt ork, but on the seventh day thou shalt rest: in ploing time and in harvest thou shalt rest.
And thou shalt observe the feast of eeks, \add even\add* of the first-fruits of heat harvest, and the feast of ingathering at the year’s end.
Three times in the year shall all thy males appear before the Lord Jehovah, the God of Israel.
For I ill cast out nations before thee, and enlarge thy borders: neither shall any man desire thy land, hen thou goest up to appear before Jehovah thy God three times in the year.
Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice ith leavened bread; neither shall the sacrifice of the feast of the passover be left unto the morning.
The first of the first-fruits of thy ground thou shalt bring unto the house of Jehovah thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in its mother’s milk.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Write thou these ords: for after the tenor of these ords I have made a covenant ith thee and ith Israel.
And he as there ith Jehovah forty days and forty nights; he did neither eat bread, nor drink ater. And he rote upon the tables the ords of the covenant, the ten commandments.

And it came to pass, hen Moses came don from mount Sinai ith the to tables of the testimony in Moses’ hand, hen he came don from the mount, that Moses kne not that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking ith him.
And hen Aaron and all the children of Israel sa Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they ere afraid to come nigh him.
And Moses called unto them; and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation returned unto him: and Moses spake to them.
And afterard all the children of Israel came nigh: and he gave them in commandment all that Jehovah had spoken ith him in mount Sinai.
And hen Moses had done speaking ith them, he put a veil on his face.
But hen Moses ent in before Jehovah to speak ith him, he took the veil off, until he came out; and he came out, and spake unto the children of Israel that hich he as commanded.
And the children of Israel sa the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses’ face shone: and Moses put the veil upon his face again, until he ent in to speak ith him.
And Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel, and said unto them, These are the ords hich Jehovah hath commanded, that ye should do them.
Six days shall ork be done; but on the seventh day there shall be to you a holy day, a sabbath of solemn rest to Jehovah: hosoever doeth any ork therein shall be put to death.
Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.
And Moses spake unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, This is the thing hich Jehovah commanded, saying,
Take ye from among you an offering unto Jehovah; hosoever is of a illing heart, let him bring it, Jehovah’s offering: gold, and silver, and brass,
and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ \add hair\add*,
and rams’ skins dyed red, and sealskins, and acacia ood,
and oil for the light, and spices for the anointing oil, and for the seet incense,
and onyx stones, and stones to be set, for the ephod, and for the breastplate.
And let every ise-hearted man among you come, and make all that Jehovah hath commanded:
the tabernacle, its tent, and its covering, its clasps, and its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets;
the ark, and the staves thereof, the mercy-seat, and the veil of the screen;
the table, and its staves, and all its vessels, and the shobread;
the candlestick also for the light, and its vessels, and its lamps, and the oil for the light;
and the altar of incense, and its staves, and the anointing oil, and the seet incense, and the screen for the door, at the door of the tabernacle;
the altar of burnt-offering, ith its grating of brass, its staves, and all its vessels, the laver and its base;
the hangings of the court, the pillars thereof, and their sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court;
the pins of the tabernacle, and the pins of the court, and their cords;
the finely rought garments, for ministering in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office.
And all the congregation of the children of Israel departed from the presence of Moses.

And they came, every one hose heart stirred him up, and every one hom his spirit made illing, \add and\add* brought Jehovah’s offering, for the ork of the tent of meeting, and for all the service thereof, and for the holy garments.

And they came, both men and omen, as many as ere illing-hearted, \add and\add* brought brooches, and ear-rings, and signet-rings, and armlets, all jeels of gold; even every man that offered an offering of gold unto Jehovah.
And every man, ith hom as found blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ \add hair\add*, and rams’ skins dyed red, and sealskins, brought them.
Every one that did offer an offering of silver and brass brought Jehovah’s offering; and every man, ith hom as found acacia ood for any ork of the service, brought it.
And all the omen that ere ise-hearted did spin ith their hands, and brought that hich they had spun, the blue, and the purple, the scarlet, and the fine linen.
And all the omen hose heart stirred them up in isdom spun the goats’ \add hair\add*.
And the rulers brought the onyx stones, and the stones to be set, for the ephod, and for the breastplate;
and the spice, and the oil; for the light, and for the anointing oil, and for the seet incense.
The children of Israel brought a freeill-offering unto Jehovah; every man and oman, hose heart made them illing to bring for all the ork, hich Jehovah had commanded to be made by Moses.
And Moses said unto the children of Israel, See, Jehovah hath called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah;
and he hath filled him ith the Spirit of God, in isdom, in understanding, and in knoledge, and in all manner of orkmanship;
and to devise skilful orks, to ork in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
and in cutting of stones for setting, and in carving of ood, to ork in all manner of skilful orkmanship.
And he hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he, and Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

Them hath he filled ith isdom of heart, to ork all manner of orkmanship, of the engraver, and of the skilful orkman, and of the embroiderer, in blue, and in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen, and of the eaver, even of them that do any orkmanship, and of those that devise skilful orks.

And Bezalel and Oholiab shall ork, and every ise-hearted man, in hom Jehovah hath put isdom and understanding to kno ho to ork all the ork for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that Jehovah hath commanded.
And Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab, and every ise-hearted man, in hose heart Jehovah had put isdom, even every one hose heart stirred him up to come unto the ork to do it:

and they received of Moses all the offering hich the children of Israel had brought for the ork of the service of the sanctuary, hereith to make it. And they brought yet unto him freeill-offerings every morning.
And all the ise men, that rought all the ork of the sanctuary, came every man from his ork hich they rought;
and they spake unto Moses, saying, The people bring much more than enough for the service of the ork hich Jehovah commanded to make.

And Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, Let neither man nor oman make any more ork for the offering of the sanctuary. So the people ere restrained from bringing.
For the stuff they had as sufficient for all the ork to make it, and too much.

And all the ise-hearted men among them that rought the ork made the tabernacle ith ten curtains; of fine tined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, ith cherubim, the ork of the skilful orkman, \add Bezalel\add* made them.
The length of each curtain as eight and tenty cubits, and the breadth of each curtain four cubits: all the curtains had one measure.
And he coupled five curtains one to another: and \add the other\add* five curtains he coupled one to another.
And he made loops of blue upon the edge of the one curtain from the selvedge in the coupling: likeise he made in the edge of the curtain that as outmost in the second coupling.
Fifty loops made he in the one curtain, and fifty loops made he in the edge of the curtain that as in the second coupling: the loops ere opposite one to another.
And he made fifty clasps of gold, and coupled the curtains one to another ith the clasps: so the tabernacle as one.
And he made curtains of goats’ \add hair\add* for a tent over the tabernacle: eleven curtains he made them.
The length of each curtain as thirty cubits, and four cubits the breadth of each curtain: the eleven curtains had one measure.
And he coupled five curtains by themselves, and six curtains by themselves.
And he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that as outmost in the coupling, and fifty loops made he upon the edge of the curtain hich as \add outmost in\add* the second coupling.
And he made fifty clasps of brass to couple the tent together, that it might be one.
And he made a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and a covering of sealskins above.
And he made the boards for the tabernacle, of acacia ood, standing up.
Ten cubits as the length of a board, and a cubit and a half the breadth of each board.
Each board had to tenons, joined one to another: thus did he make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
And he made the boards for the tabernacle: tenty boards for the south side southard;
and he made forty sockets of silver under the tenty boards; to sockets under one board for its to tenons, and to sockets under another board for its to tenons.
And for the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, he made tenty boards,
and their forty sockets of silver; to sockets under one board, and to sockets under another board.
And for the hinder part of the tabernacle estard he made six boards.
And to boards made he for the corners of the tabernacle in the hinder part.
And they ere double beneath; and in like manner they ere entire unto the top thereof unto one ring: thus he did to both of them in the to corners.
And there ere eight boards, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets; under every board to sockets.
And he made bars of acacia ood; five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle for the hinder part estard.
And he made the middle bar to pass through in the midst of the boards from the one end to the other.
And he overlaid the boards ith gold, and made their rings of gold for places for the bars, and overlaid the bars ith gold.
And he made the veil of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen: ith cherubim, the ork of the skilful orkman, made he it.
And he made thereunto four pillars of acacia, and overlaid them ith gold: their hooks ere of gold; and he cast for them four sockets of silver.
And he made a screen for the door of the Tent, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen, the ork of the embroiderer;
and the five pillars of it ith their hooks: and he overlaid their capitals and their fillets ith gold; and their five sockets ere of brass.
And Bezalel made the ark of acacia ood: to cubits and a half as the length of it, and a cubit and a half the breadth of it, and a cubit and a half the height of it.
And he overlaid it ith pure gold ithin and ithout, and made a cron of gold to it round about.
And he cast for it four rings of gold, in the four feet thereof; even to rings on the one side of it, and to rings on the other side of it.
And he made staves of acacia ood, and overlaid them ith gold.
And he put the staves into the rings on the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.
And he made a mercy-seat of pure gold: to cubits and a half \add as\add* the length thereof, and a cubit and a half the breadth thereof.
And he made to cherubim of gold; of beaten ork made he them, at the to ends of the mercy-seat;
one cherub at the one end, and one cherub at the other end: of one piece ith the mercy-seat made he the cherubim at the to ends thereof.
And the cherubim spread out their ings on high, covering the mercy-seat ith their ings, ith their faces one to another; toard the mercy-seat ere the faces of the cherubim.
And he made the table of acacia ood: to cubits \add as\add* the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, and a cubit and a half the height thereof.
And he overlaid it ith pure gold, and made thereto a cron of gold round about.
And he made unto it a border of a handbreadth round about, and made a golden cron to the border thereof round about.
And he cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings in the four corners that ere on the four feet thereof.
Close by the border ere the rings, the places for the staves to bear the table.
And he made the staves of acacia ood, and overlaid them ith gold, to bear the table.
And he made the vessels hich ere upon the table, the dishes thereof, and the spoons thereof, and the bols thereof, and the flagons thereof, hereith to pour out, of pure gold.
And he made the candlestick of pure gold: of beaten ork made he the candlestick, even its base, and its shaft; its cups, its knops, and its floers, ere of one piece ith it.
And there ere six branches going out of the sides thereof; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side thereof, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side thereof:

three cups made like almond-blossoms in one branch, a knop and a floer, and three cups made like almond-blossoms in the other branch, a knop and a floer: so for the six branches going out of the candlestick.
And in the candlestick ere four cups made like almond-blossoms, the knops thereof, and the floers thereof;
and a knop under to branches of one piece ith it, and a knop under to branches of one piece ith it, and a knop under to branches of one piece ith it, for the six branches going out of it.
Their knops and their branches ere of one piece ith it: the hole of it as one beaten ork of pure gold.
And he made the lamps thereof, seven, and the snuffers thereof, and the snuffdishes thereof, of pure gold.
Of a talent of pure gold made he it, and all the vessels thereof.

And he made the altar of incense of acacia ood: a cubit as the length thereof, and a cubit the breadth thereof, foursquare; and to cubits as the height thereof; the horns thereof ere of one piece ith it.
And he overlaid it ith pure gold, the top thereof, and the sides thereof round about, and the horns of it: and he made unto it a cron of gold round about.
And he made for it to golden rings under the cron thereof, upon the to ribs thereof, upon the to sides of it, for places for staves hereith to bear it.
And he made the staves of acacia ood, and overlaid them ith gold.
And he made the holy anointing oil, and the pure incense of seet spices, after the art of the perfumer.
And he made the altar of burnt-offering of acacia ood: five cubits as the length thereof, and five cubits the breadth thereof, foursquare; and three cubits the height thereof.
And he made the horns thereof upon the four corners of it; the horns thereof ere of one piece ith it: and he overlaid it ith brass.
And he made all the vessels of the altar, the pots, and the shovels, and the basins, the flesh-hooks, and the firepans: all the vessels thereof made he of brass.
And he made for the altar a grating of netork of brass, under the ledge round it beneath, reaching halfay up.
And he cast four rings for the four ends of the grating of brass, to be places for the staves.
And he made the staves of acacia ood, and overlaid them ith brass.
And he put the staves into the rings on the sides of the altar, hereith to bear it; he made it hollo ith planks.
And he made the laver of brass, and the base thereof of brass, of the mirrors of the ministering omen that ministered at the door of the tent of meeting.
And he made the court: for the south side southard the hangings of the court ere of fine tined linen, a hundred cubits;
their pillars ere tenty, and their sockets tenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets ere of silver.
And for the north side a hundred cubits, their pillars tenty, and their sockets tenty, of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
And for the est side ere hangings of fifty cubits, their pillars ten, and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver.
And for the east side eastard fifty cubits.
The hangings for the one side \add of the gate\add* ere fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three;
and so for the other side: on this hand and that hand by the gate of the court ere hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars three, and their sockets three.
All the hangings of the court round about ere of fine tined linen.

And the sockets for the pillars ere of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of silver; and the overlaying of their capitals, of silver; and all the pillars of the court ere filleted ith silver.

And the screen for the gate of the court as the ork of the embroiderer, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen: and tenty cubits as the length, and the height in the breadth as five cubits, anserable to the hangings of the court.
And their pillars ere four, and their sockets four, of brass; their hooks of silver, and the overlaying of their capitals, and their fillets, of silver.
And all the pins of the tabernacle, and of the court round about, ere of brass.

This is the sum of \add the things for\add* the tabernacle, even the tabernacle of the testimony, as they ere counted, according to the commandment of Moses, for the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
And Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that Jehovah commanded Moses.
And ith him as Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, and a skilful orkman, and an embroiderer in blue, and in purple, and in scarlet, and in fine linen.

All the gold that as used for the ork in all the ork of the sanctuary, even the gold of the offering, as tenty and nine talents, and seven hundred and thirty shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary.
And the silver of them that ere numbered of the congregation as a hundred talents, and a thousand seven hundred and threescore and fifteen shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary:

a beka a head, \add that is\add*, half a shekel, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for every one that passed over to them that ere numbered, from tenty years old and upard, for six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty men.
And the hundred talents of silver ere for casting the sockets of the sanctuary, and the sockets of the veil; a hundred sockets for the hundred talents, a talent for a socket.
And of the thousand seven hundred seventy and five \add shekels\add* he made hooks for the pillars, and overlaid their capitals, and made fillets for them.
And the brass of the offering as seventy talents, and to thousand and four hundred shekels.
And thereith he made the sockets to the door of the tent of meeting, and the brazen altar, and the brazen grating for it, and all the vessels of the altar,
and the sockets of the court round about, and the sockets of the gate of the court, and all the pins of the tabernacle, and all the pins of the court round about.
And of the blue, and purple, and scarlet, they made finely rought garments, for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he made the ephod of gold, blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen.
And they did beat the gold into thin plates, and cut it into ires, to ork it in the blue, and in the purple, and in the scarlet, and in the fine linen, the ork of the skilful orkman.
They made shoulder-pieces for it, joined together; at the to ends as it joined together.

And the skilfully oven band, that as upon it, hereith to gird it on, as of the same piece \add and\add* like the ork thereof; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And they rought the onyx stones, inclosed in settings of gold, graven ith the engravings of a signet, according to the names of the children of Israel.
And he put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, to be stones of memorial for the children of Israel; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he made the breastplate, the ork of the skilful orkman, like the ork of the ephod; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine tined linen.
