It as foursquare; they made the breastplate double: a span as the length thereof, and a span the breadth thereof, being double.
And they set in it four ros of stones. A ro of sardius, topaz, and carbuncle as the first ro;
and the second ro, an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond;
and the third ro, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
and the fourth ro, a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper: they ere inclosed in inclosings of gold in their settings.
And the stones ere according to the names of the children of Israel, telve, according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, every one according to his name, for the telve tribes.
And they made upon the breastplate chains like cords, of reathen ork of pure gold.
And they made to settings of gold, and to gold rings, and put the to rings on the to ends of the breastplate.
And they put the to reathen chains of gold in the to rings at the ends of the breastplate.
And the \add other\add* to ends of the to reathen chains they put on the to settings, and put them on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod, in the forepart thereof.
And they made to rings of gold, and put them upon the to ends of the breastplate, upon the edge thereof, hich as toard the side of the ephod inard.
And they made to rings of gold, and put them on the to shoulder-pieces of the ephod underneath, in the forepart thereof, close by the coupling thereof, above the skilfully oven band of the ephod.

And they did bind the breastplate by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod ith a lace of blue, that it might be upon the skilfully oven band of the ephod, and that the breastplate might not be loosed from the ephod; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he made the robe of the ephod of oven ork, all of blue;
and the hole of the robe in the midst thereof, as the hole of a coat of mail, ith a binding round about the hole of it, that it should not be rent.
And they made upon the skirts of the robe pomegranates of blue, and purple, and scarlet, \add and\add* tined \add linen\add*.
And they made bells of pure gold, and put the bells beteen the pomegranates upon the skirts of the robe round about, beteen the pomegranates;
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, upon the skirts of the robe round about, to minister in; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And they made the coats of fine linen of oven ork for Aaron, and for his sons,
and the mitre of fine linen, and the goodly head-tires of fine linen, and the linen breeches of fine tined linen,
and the girdle of fine tined linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, the ork of the embroiderer; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And they made the plate of the holy cron of pure gold, and rote upon it a riting, like the engravings of a signet, HOLY TO JEHOVAH.
And they tied unto it a lace of blue, to fasten it upon the mitre above; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
Thus as finished all the ork of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting: and the children of Israel did according to all that Jehovah commanded Moses; so did they.
And they brought the tabernacle unto Moses, the Tent, and all its furniture, its clasps, its boards, its bars, and its pillars, and its sockets;
and the covering of rams’ skins dyed red, and the covering of sealskins, and the veil of the screen;
the ark of the testimony, and the staves thereof, and the mercy-seat;
the table, all the vessels thereof, and the shobread;
the pure candlestick, the lamps thereof, even the lamps to be set in order, and all the vessels thereof, and the oil for the light;
and the golden altar, and the anointing oil, and the seet incense, and the screen for the door of the Tent;
the brazen altar, and its grating of brass, its staves, and all its vessels, the laver and its base;

the hangings of the court, its pillars, and its sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court, the cords thereof, and the pins thereof, and all the instruments of the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;
the finely rought garments for ministering in the holy place, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office.
According to all that Jehovah commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did all the ork.
And Moses sa all the ork, and, behold, they had done it; as Jehovah had commanded, even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
On the first day of the first month shalt thou rear up the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
And thou shalt put therein the ark of the testimony, and thou shalt screen the ark ith the veil.
And thou shalt bring in the table, and set in order the things that are upon it; and thou shalt bring in the candlestick, and light the lamps thereof.
And thou shalt set the golden altar for incense before the ark of the testimony, and put the screen of the door to the tabernacle.
And thou shalt set the altar of burnt-offering before the door of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
And thou shalt set the laver beteen the tent of meeting and the altar, and shalt put ater therein.
And thou shalt set up the court round about, and hang up the screen of the gate of the court.
And thou shalt take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle, and all that is therein, and shalt hallo it, and all the furniture thereof: and it shall be holy.
And thou shalt anoint the altar of burnt-offering, and all its vessels, and sanctify the altar: and the altar shall be most holy.
And thou shalt anoint the laver and its base, and sanctify it.
And thou shalt bring Aaron and his sons unto the door of the tent of meeting, and shalt ash them ith ater.
And thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments; and thou shalt anoint him, and sanctify him, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.
And thou shalt bring his sons, and put coats upon them;

and thou shalt anoint them, as thou didst anoint their father, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office: and their anointing shall be to them for an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.
Thus did Moses: according to all that Jehovah commanded him, so did he.
And it came to pass in the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle as reared up.
And Moses reared up the tabernacle, and laid its sockets, and set up the boards thereof, and put in the bars thereof, and reared up its pillars.
And he spread the tent over the tabernacle, and put the covering of the tent above upon it; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he took and put the testimony into the ark, and set the staves on the ark, and put the mercy-seat above upon the ark:
and he brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the veil of the screen, and screened the ark of the testimony; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he put the table in the tent of meeting, upon the side of the tabernacle northard, ithout the veil.
And he set the bread in order upon it before Jehovah; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he put the candlestick in the tent of meeting, over against the table, on the side of the tabernacle southard.
And he lighted the lamps before Jehovah; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he put the golden altar in the tent of meeting before the veil:
and he burnt thereon incense of seet spices; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he put the screen of the door to the tabernacle.
And he set the altar of burnt-offering at the door of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, and offered upon it the burnt-offering and the meal-offering; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he set the laver beteen the tent of meeting and the altar, and put ater therein, hereith to ash.
And Moses and Aaron and his sons ashed their hands and their feet thereat;
hen they ent into the tent of meeting, and hen they came near unto the altar, they ashed; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he reared up the court round about the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the screen of the gate of the court. So Moses finished the ork.
Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of Jehovah filled the tabernacle.
And Moses as not able to enter into the tent of meeting, because the cloud abode thereon, and the glory of Jehovah filled the tabernacle.
And hen the cloud as taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel ent onard, throughout all their journeys:
but if the cloud as not taken up, then they journeyed not till the day that it as taken up.
For the cloud of Jehovah as upon the tabernacle by day, and there as fire therein by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.
And Jehovah called unto Moses, and spake unto him out of the tent of meeting, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When any man of you offereth an oblation unto Jehovah, ye shall offer your oblation of the cattle, \add even\add* of the herd and of the flock.
If his oblation be a burnt-offering of the herd, he shall offer it a male ithout blemish: he shall offer it at the door of the tent of meeting, that he may be accepted before Jehovah.
And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the burnt-offering; and it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him.
And he shall kill the bullock before Jehovah: and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall present the blood, and sprinkle the blood round about upon the altar that is at the door of the tent of meeting.
And he shall flay the burnt-offering, and cut it into its pieces.
And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire upon the altar, and lay ood in order upon the fire;
and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall lay the pieces, the head, and the fat, in order upon the ood that is on the fire hich is upon the altar:
but its inards and its legs shall he ash ith ater. And the priest shall burn the hole on the altar, for a burnt-offering, an offering made by fire, of a seet savor unto Jehovah.
And if his oblation be of the flock, of the sheep, or of the goats, for a burnt-offering; he shall offer it a male ithout blemish.
And he shall kill it on the side of the altar northard before Jehovah: and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall sprinkle its blood upon the altar round about.
And he shall cut it into its pieces, ith its head and its fat; and the priest shall lay them in order on the ood that is on the fire hich is upon the altar:
but the inards and the legs shall he ash ith ater. And the priest shall offer the hole, and burn it upon the altar: it is a burnt-offering, an offering made by fire, of a seet savor unto Jehovah.
And if his oblation to Jehovah be a burnt-offering of birds, then he shall offer his oblation of turtle-doves, or of young pigeons.
And the priest shall bring it unto the altar, and ring off its head, and burn it on the altar; and the blood thereof shall be drained out on the side of the altar;
and he shall take aay its crop ith the filth thereof, and cast it beside the altar on the east part, in the place of the ashes:

and he shall rend it by the ings thereof, \add but\add* shall not divide it asunder. And the priest shall burn it upon the altar, upon the ood that is upon the fire: it is a burnt-offering, an offering made by fire, of a seet savor unto Jehovah.
And hen any one offereth an oblation of a meal-offering unto Jehovah, his oblation shall be of fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense thereon:

and he shall bring it to Aaron’s sons the priests; and he shall take thereout his handful of the fine flour thereof, and of the oil thereof, ith all the frankincense thereof. And the priest shall burn \add it as\add* the memorial thereof upon the altar, an offering made by fire, of a seet savor unto Jehovah:
and that hich is left of the meal-offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’: it is a thing most holy of the offerings of Jehovah made by fire.
And hen thou offerest an oblation of a meal-offering baken in the oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mingled ith oil, or unleavened afers anointed ith oil.
And if thy oblation be a meal-offering of the baking-pan, it shall be of fine flour unleavened, mingled ith oil.
Thou shalt part it in pieces, and pour oil thereon: it is a meal-offering.
And if thy oblation be a meal-offering of the frying-pan, it shall be made of fine flour ith oil.
And thou shalt bring the meal-offering that is made of these things unto Jehovah: and it shall be presented unto the priest, and he shall bring it unto the altar.
And the priest shall take up from the meal-offering the memorial thereof, and shall burn it upon the altar, an offering made by fire, of a seet savor unto Jehovah.
And that hich is left of the meal-offering shall be Aaron’s and his sons’: it is a thing most holy of the offerings of Jehovah made by fire.
No meal-offering, hich ye shall offer unto Jehovah, shall be made ith leaven; for ye shall burn no leaven, nor any honey, as an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
As an oblation of first-\add fruits\add* ye shall offer them unto Jehovah: but they shall not come up for a seet savor on the altar.

And every oblation of thy meal-offering shalt thou season ith salt; neither shalt thou suffer the salt of the covenant of thy God to be lacking from thy meal-offering: ith all thine oblations thou shalt offer salt.
And if thou offer a meal-offering of first-fruits unto Jehovah, thou shalt offer for the meal-offering of thy first-fruits grain in the ear parched ith fire, bruised grain of the fresh ear.
And thou shalt put oil upon it, and lay frankincense thereon: it is a meal-offering.
And the priest shall burn the memorial of it, part of the bruised grain thereof, and part of the oil thereof, ith all the frankincense thereof: it is an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
And if his oblation be a sacrifice of peace-offerings; if he offer of the herd, hether male or female, he shall offer it ithout blemish before Jehovah.
And he shall lay his hand upon the head of his oblation, and kill it at the door of the tent of meeting: and Aaron’s sons the priests shall sprinkle the blood upon the altar round about.
And he shall offer of the sacrifice of peace-offerings an offering made by fire unto Jehovah; the fat that covereth the inards, and all the fat that is upon the inards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat that is on them, hich is by the loins, and the caul upon the liver, ith the kidneys, shall he take aay.
And Aaron’s sons shall burn it on the altar upon the burnt-offering, hich is upon the ood that is on the fire: it is an offering made by fire, of a seet savor unto Jehovah.
And if his oblation for a sacrifice of peace-offerings unto Jehovah be of the flock; male or female, he shall offer it ithout blemish.
If he offer a lamb for his oblation, then shall he offer it before Jehovah;
and he shall lay his hand upon the head of his oblation, and kill it before the tent of meeting: and Aaron’s sons shall sprinkle the blood thereof upon the altar round about.

And he shall offer of the sacrifice of peace-offerings an offering made by fire unto Jehovah; the fat thereof, the fat tail entire, he shall take aay hard by the backbone; and the fat that covereth the inards, and all the fat that is upon the inards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, hich is by the loins, and the caul upon the liver, ith the kidneys, shall he take aay.
And the priest shall burn it upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
And if his oblation be a goat, then he shall offer it before Jehovah:
and he shall lay his hand upon the head of it, and kill it before the tent of meeting; and the sons of Aaron shall sprinkle the blood thereof upon the altar round about.
And he shall offer thereof his oblation, \add even\add* an offering made by fire unto Jehovah; the fat that covereth the inards, and all the fat that is upon the inards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, hich is by the loins, and the caul upon the liver, ith the kidneys, shall he take aay.
And the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire, for a seet savor; all the fat is Jehovah’s.
It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dellings, that ye shall eat neither fat nor blood.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If any one shall sin unittingly, in any of the things hich Jehovah hath commanded not to be done, and shall do any one of them:
if the anointed priest shall sin so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin, hich he hath sinned, a young bullock ithout blemish unto Jehovah for a sin-offering.
And he shall bring the bullock unto the door of the tent of meeting before Jehovah; and he shall lay his hand upon the head of the bullock, and kill the bullock before Jehovah.
And the anointed priest shall take of the blood of the bullock, and bring it to the tent of meeting:
and the priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle of the blood seven times before Jehovah, before the veil of the sanctuary.

And the priest shall put of the blood upon the horns of the altar of seet incense before Jehovah, hich is in the tent of meeting; and all the blood of the bullock shall he pour out at the base of the altar of burnt-offering, hich is at the door of the tent of meeting.
And all the fat of the bullock of the sin-offering he shall take off from it; the fat that covereth the inards, and all the fat that is upon the inards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat that is upon them, hich is by the loins, and the caul upon the liver, ith the kidneys, shall he take aay,
as it is taken off from the ox of the sacrifice of peace-offerings: and the priest shall burn them upon the altar of burnt-offering.
And the skin of the bullock, and all its flesh, ith its head, and ith its legs, and its inards, and its dung,
even the hole bullock shall he carry forth ithout the camp unto a clean place, here the ashes are poured out, and burn it on ood ith fire: here the ashes are poured out shall it be burnt.
And if the hole congregation of Israel err, and the thing be hid from the eyes of the assembly, and they have done any of the things hich Jehovah hath commanded not to be done, and are guilty;
hen the sin herein they have sinned is knon, then the assembly shall offer a young bullock for a sin-offering, and bring it before the tent of meeting.
And the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands upon the head of the bullock before Jehovah; and the bullock shall be killed before Jehovah.
And the anointed priest shall bring of the blood of the bullock to the tent of meeting:
and the priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle it seven times before Jehovah, before the veil.

And he shall put of the blood upon the horns of the altar hich is before Jehovah, that is in the tent of meeting; and all the blood shall he pour out at the base of the altar of burnt-offering, hich is at the door of the tent of meeting.
And all the fat thereof shall he take off from it, and burn it upon the altar.
Thus shall he do ith the bullock; as he did ith the bullock of the sin-offering, so shall he do ith this; and the priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.
And he shall carry forth the bullock ithout the camp, and burn it as he burned the first bullock: it is the sin-offering for the assembly.
When a ruler sinneth, and doeth unittingly any one of all the things hich Jehovah his God hath commanded not to be done, and is guilty;
if his sin, herein he hath sinned, be made knon to him, he shall bring for his oblation a goat, a male ithout blemish.
And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the goat, and kill it in the place here they kill the burnt-offering before Jehovah: it is a sin-offering.

And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin-offering ith his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of burnt-offering; and the blood thereof shall he pour out at the base of the altar of burnt-offering.
And all the fat thereof shall he burn upon the altar, as the fat of the sacrifice of peace-offerings; and the priest shall make atonement for him as concerning his sin, and he shall be forgiven.
And if any one of the common people sin unittingly, in doing any of the things hich Jehovah hath commanded not to be done, and be guilty;
if his sin, hich he hath sinned, be made knon to him, then he shall bring for his oblation a goat, a female ithout blemish, for his sin hich he hath sinned.
And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the sin-offering, and kill the sin-offering in the place of burnt-offering.
And the priest shall take of the blood thereof ith his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of burnt-offering; and all the blood thereof shall he pour out at the base of the altar.

And all the fat thereof shall he take aay, as the fat is taken aay from off the sacrifice of peace-offerings; and the priest shall burn it upon the altar for a seet savor unto Jehovah; and the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven.
And if he bring a lamb as his oblation for a sin-offering, he shall bring it a female ithout blemish.
And he shall lay his hand upon the head of the sin-offering, and kill it for a sin-offering in the place here they kill the burnt-offering.

And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin-offering ith his finger, and put it upon the horns of the altar of burnt-offering; and all the blood thereof shall he pour out at the base of the altar.

And all the fat thereof shall he take aay, as the fat of the lamb is taken aay from the sacrifice of peace-offerings; and the priest shall burn them on the altar, upon the offerings of Jehovah made by fire; and the priest shall make atonement for him as touching his sin that he hath sinned, and he shall be forgiven.
And if any one sin, in that he heareth the voice of adjuration, he being a itness, hether he hath seen or knon, if he do not utter \add it\add*, then he shall bear his iniquity.

Or if any one touch any unclean thing, hether it be the carcass of an unclean beast, or the carcass of unclean cattle, or the carcass of unclean creeping things, and it be hidden from him, and he be unclean, then he shall be guilty.
Or if he touch the uncleanness of man, hatsoever his uncleanness be hereith he is unclean, and it be hid from him; hen he knoeth of it, then he shall be guilty.

Or if any one sear rashly ith his lips to do evil, or to do good, hatsoever it be that a man shall utter rashly ith an oath, and it be hid from him; hen he knoeth of it, then he shall be guilty in one of these \add things\add*.
And it shall be, hen he shall be guilty in one of these \add things\add*, that he shall confess that herein he hath sinned:

and he shall bring his trespass-offering unto Jehovah for his sin hich he hath sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, for a sin-offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him as concerning his sin.

And if his means suffice not for a lamb, then he shall bring his trespass-offering for that herein he hath sinned, to turtle-doves, or to young pigeons, unto Jehovah; one for a sin-offering, and the other for a burnt-offering.
And he shall bring them unto the priest, ho shall offer that hich is for the sin-offering first, and ring off its head from its neck, but shall not divide it asunder:
and he shall sprinkle of the blood of the sin-offering upon the side of the altar; and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar: it is a sin-offering.
And he shall offer the second for a burnt-offering, according to the ordinance; and the priest shall make atonement for him as concerning his sin hich he hath sinned, and he shall be forgiven.

But if his means suffice not for to turtle-doves, or to young pigeons, then he shall bring his oblation for that herein he hath sinned, the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin-offering: he shall put no oil upon it, neither shall he put any frankincense thereon; for it is a sin-offering.
And he shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take his handful of it as the memorial thereof, and burn it on the altar, upon the offerings of Jehovah made by fire: it is a sin-offering.

And the priest shall make atonement for him as touching his sin that he hath sinned in any of these things, and he shall be forgiven: and \add the remnant\add* shall be the priest’s, as the meal-offering.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

If any one commit a trespass, and sin unittingly, in the holy things of Jehovah; then he shall bring his trespass-offering unto Jehovah, a ram ithout blemish out of the flock, according to thy estimation in silver by shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, for a trespass-offering:

and he shall make restitution for that hich he hath done amiss in the holy thing, and shall add the fifth part thereto, and give it unto the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him ith the ram of the trespass-offering, and he shall be forgiven.
And if any one sin, and do any of the things hich Jehovah hath commanded not to be done; though he kne it not, yet is he guilty, and shall bear his iniquity.

And he shall bring a ram ithout blemish out of the flock, according to thy estimation, for a trespass-offering, unto the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning the thing herein he erred unittingly and kne it not, and he shall be forgiven.
It is a trespass-offering: he is certainly guilty before Jehovah.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
If any one sin, and commit a trespass against Jehovah, and deal falsely ith his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of bargain, or of robbery, or have oppressed his neighbor,
or have found that hich as lost, and deal falsely therein, and sear to a lie; in any of all these things that a man doeth, sinning therein;

then it shall be, if he hath sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that hich he took by robbery, or the thing hich he hath gotten by oppression, or the deposit hich as committed to him, or the lost thing hich he found,

or any thing about hich he hath sorn falsely; he shall even restore it in full, and shall add the fifth part more thereto: unto him to hom it appertaineth shall he give it, in the day of his being found guilty.
And he shall bring his trespass-offering unto Jehovah, a ram ithout blemish out of the flock, according to thy estimation, for a trespass-offering, unto the priest:
and the priest shall make atonement for him before Jehovah; and he shall be forgiven concerning hatsoever he doeth so as to be guilty thereby.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

Command Aaron and his sons, saying, This is the la of the burnt-offering: the burnt-offering shall be on the hearth upon the altar all night unto the morning; and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning thereon.

And the priest shall put on his linen garment, and his linen breeches shall he put upon his flesh; and he shall take up the ashes hereto the fire hath consumed the burnt-offering on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.
And he shall put off his garments, and put on other garments, and carry forth the ashes ithout the camp unto a clean place.

And the fire upon the altar shall be kept burning thereon, it shall not go out; and the priest shall burn ood on it every morning: and he shall lay the burnt-offering in order upon it, and shall burn thereon the fat of the peace-offerings.
Fire shall be kept burning upon the altar continually; it shall not go out.
And this is the la of the meal-offering: the sons of Aaron shall offer it before Jehovah, before the altar.

And he shall take up therefrom his handful, of the fine flour of the meal-offering, and of the oil thereof, and all the frankincense hich is upon the meal-offering, and shall burn it upon the altar for a seet savor, as the memorial thereof, unto Jehovah.
And that hich is left thereof shall Aaron and his sons eat: it shall be eaten ithout leaven in a holy place; in the court of the tent of meeting they shall eat it.
It shall not be baken ith leaven. I have given it as their portion of my offerings made by fire; it is most holy, as the sin-offering, and as the trespass-offering.

Every male among the children of Aaron shall eat of it, as \add his\add* portion for ever throughout your generations, from the offerings of Jehovah made by fire: hosoever toucheth them shall be holy.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

This is the oblation of Aaron and of his sons, hich they shall offer unto Jehovah in the day hen he is anointed: the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering perpetually, half of it in the morning, and half thereof in the evening.
On a baking-pan it shall be made ith oil; hen it is soaked, thou shalt bring it in: in baken pieces shalt thou offer the meal-offering for a seet savor unto Jehovah.
And the anointed priest that shall be in his stead from among his sons shall offer it: by a statute for ever it shall be holly burnt unto Jehovah.
And every meal-offering of the priest shall be holly burnt: it shall not be eaten.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto Aaron and to his sons, saying, This is the la of the sin-offering: in the place here the burnt-offering is killed shall the sin-offering be killed before Jehovah: it is most holy.
The priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it: in a holy place shall it be eaten, in the court of the tent of meeting.
Whatsoever shall touch the flesh thereof shall be holy; and hen there is sprinkled of the blood thereof upon any garment, thou shalt ash that hereon it as sprinkled in a holy place.
But the earthen vessel herein it is boiled shall be broken; and if it be boiled in a brazen vessel, it shall be scoured, and rinsed in ater.
Every male among the priests shall eat thereof: it is most holy.
And no sin-offering, hereof any of the blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place, shall be eaten: it shall be burnt ith fire.
And this is the la of the trespass-offering: it is most holy.
In the place here they kill the burnt-offering shall they kill the trespass-offering; and the blood thereof shall he sprinkle upon the altar round about.
And he shall offer of it all the fat thereof: the fat tail, and the fat that covereth the inards,
and the to kidneys, and the fat that is on them, hich is by the loins, and the caul upon the liver, ith the kidneys, shall he take aay;
and the priest shall burn them upon the altar for an offering made by fire unto Jehovah: it is a trespass-offering.
Every male among the priests shall eat thereof: it shall be eaten in a holy place: it is most holy.
As is the sin-offering, so is the trespass-offering; there is one la for them: the priest that maketh atonement thereith, he shall have it.
And the priest that offereth any man’s burnt-offering, even the priest shall have to himself the skin of the burnt-offering hich he hath offered.
And every meal-offering that is baken in the oven, and all that is dressed in the frying-pan, and on the baking-pan, shall be the priest’s that offereth it.
And every meal-offering, mingled ith oil, or dry, shall all the sons of Aaron have, one as ell as another.
And this is the la of the sacrifice of peace-offerings, hich one shall offer unto Jehovah.

If he offer it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer ith the sacrifice of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mingled ith oil, and unleavened afers anointed ith oil, and cakes mingled ith oil, of fine flour soaked.
With cakes of leavened bread he shall offer his oblation ith the sacrifice of his peace-offerings for thanksgiving.
And of it he shall offer one out of each oblation for a heave-offering unto Jehovah; it shall be the priest’s that sprinkleth the blood of the peace-offerings.
And the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace-offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten on the day of his oblation; he shall not leave any of it until the morning.
But if the sacrifice of his oblation be a vo, or a freeill-offering, it shall be eaten on the day that he offereth his sacrifice; and on the morro that hich remaineth of it shall be eaten:
but that hich remaineth of the flesh of the sacrifice on the third day shall be burnt ith fire.

And if any of the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace-offerings be eaten on the third day, it shall not be accepted, neither shall it be imputed unto him that offereth it: it shall be an abomination, and the soul that eateth of it shall bear his iniquity.
And the flesh that toucheth any unclean thing shall not be eaten; it shall be burnt ith fire. And as for the flesh, every one that is clean shall eat thereof:
but the soul that eateth of the flesh of the sacrifice of peace-offerings, that pertain unto Jehovah, having his uncleanness upon him, that soul shall be cut off from his people.

And hen any one shall touch any unclean thing, the uncleanness of man, or an unclean beast, or any unclean abomination, and eat of the flesh of the sacrifice of peace-offerings, hich pertain unto Jehovah, that soul shall be cut off from his people.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, Ye shall eat no fat, of ox, or sheep, or goat.
And the fat of that hich dieth of itself, and the fat of that hich is torn of beasts, may be used for any other service; but ye shall in no ise eat of it.
For hosoever eateth the fat of the beast, of hich men offer an offering made by fire unto Jehovah, even the soul that eateth it shall be cut off from his people.
And ye shall eat no manner of blood, hether it be of bird or of beast, in any of your dellings.
Whosoever it be that eateth any blood, that soul shall be cut off from his people.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, He that offereth the sacrifice of his peace-offerings unto Jehovah shall bring his oblation unto Jehovah out of the sacrifice of his peace-offerings:
his on hands shall bring the offerings of Jehovah made by fire; the fat ith the breast shall he bring, that the breast may be aved for a ave-offering before Jehovah.
And the priest shall burn the fat upon the altar; but the breast shall be Aaron’s and his sons’.
And the right thigh shall ye give unto the priest for a heave-offering out of the sacrifices of your peace-offerings.
He among the sons of Aaron that offereth the blood of the peace-offerings, and the fat, shall have the right thigh for a portion.

For the ave-breast and the heave-thigh have I taken of the children of Israel out of the sacrifices of their peace-offerings, and have given them unto Aaron the priest and unto his sons as \add their\add* portion for ever from the children of Israel.

This is the anointing-portion of Aaron, and the anointing-portion of his sons, out of the offerings of Jehovah made by fire, in the day hen he presented them to minister unto Jehovah in the priest’s office;
hich Jehovah commanded to be given them of the children of Israel, in the day that he anointed them. It is \add their\add* portion for ever throughout their generations.
This is the la of the burnt-offering, of the meal-offering, and of the sin-offering, and of the trespass-offering, and of the consecration, and of the sacrifice of peace-offerings;
hich Jehovah commanded Moses in mount Sinai, in the day that he commanded the children of Israel to offer their oblations unto Jehovah, in the ilderness of Sinai.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Take Aaron and his sons ith him, and the garments, and the anointing oil, and the bullock of the sin-offering, and the to rams, and the basket of unleavened bread;
and assemble thou all the congregation at the door of the tent of meeting.
And Moses did as Jehovah commanded him; and the congregation as assembled at the door of the tent of meeting.
And Moses said unto the congregation, This is the thing hich Jehovah hath commanded to be done.
And Moses brought Aaron and his sons, and ashed them ith ater.

And he put upon him the coat, and girded him ith the girdle, and clothed him ith the robe, and put the ephod upon him, and he girded him ith the skilfully oven band of the ephod, and bound it unto him thereith.
And he placed the breastplate upon him: and in the breastplate he put the Urim and the Thummim.
And he set the mitre upon his head; and upon the mitre, in front, did he set the golden plate, the holy cron; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And Moses took the anointing oil, and anointed the tabernacle and all that as therein, and sanctified them.
And he sprinkled thereof upon the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its vessels, and the laver and its base, to sanctify them.
And he poured of the anointing oil upon Aaron’s head, and anointed him, to sanctify him.
And Moses brought Aaron’s sons, and clothed them ith coats, and girded them ith girdles, and bound head-tires upon them; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he brought the bullock of the sin-offering: and Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon the head of the bullock of the sin-offering.

And he sle it; and Moses took the blood, and put it upon the horns of the altar round about ith his finger, and purified the altar, and poured out the blood at the base of the altar, and sanctified it, to make atonement for it.
And he took all the fat that as upon the inards, and the caul of the liver, and the to kidneys, and their fat; and Moses burned it upon the altar.
But the bullock, and its skin, and its flesh, and its dung, he burnt ith fire ithout the camp; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he presented the ram of the burnt-offering: and Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon the head of the ram.
And he killed it; and Moses sprinkled the blood upon the altar round about.
And he cut the ram into its pieces; and Moses burnt the head, and the pieces, and the fat.

And he ashed the inards and the legs ith ater; and Moses burnt the hole ram upon the altar: it as a burnt-offering for a seet savor: it as an offering made by fire unto Jehovah; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And he presented the other ram, the ram of consecration: and Aaron and his sons laid their hands upon the head of the ram.
And he sle it; and Moses took of the blood thereof, and put it upon the tip of Aaron’s right ear, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot.

And he brought Aaron’s sons; and Moses put of the blood upon the tip of their right ear, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot: and Moses sprinkled the blood upon the altar round about.
And he took the fat, and the fat tail, and all the fat that as upon the inards, and the caul of the liver, and the to kidneys, and their fat, and the right thigh:
and out of the basket of unleavened bread, that as before Jehovah, he took one unleavened cake, and one cake of oiled bread, and one afer, and placed them on the fat, and upon the right thigh:
and he put the hole upon the hands of Aaron, and upon the hands of his sons, and aved them for a ave-offering before Jehovah.
And Moses took them from off their hands, and burnt them on the altar upon the burnt-offering: they ere a consecration for a seet savor: it as an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
And Moses took the breast, and aved it for a ave-offering before Jehovah: it as Moses’ portion of the ram of consecration; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

And Moses took of the anointing oil, and of the blood hich as upon the altar, and sprinkled it upon Aaron, upon his garments, and upon his sons, and upon his sons’ garments ith him, and sanctified Aaron, his garments, and his sons, and his sons’ garments ith him.

And Moses said unto Aaron and to his sons, Boil the flesh at the door of the tent of meeting: and there eat it and the bread that is in the basket of consecration, as I commanded, saying, Aaron and his sons shall eat it.
And that hich remaineth of the flesh and of the bread shall ye burn ith fire.
And ye shall not go out from the door of the tent of meeting seven days, until the days of your consecration be fulfilled: for he shall consecrate you seven days.
As hath been done this day, so Jehovah hath commanded to do, to make atonement for you.
And at the door of the tent of meeting shall ye abide day and night seven days, and keep the charge of Jehovah, that ye die not: for so I am commanded.
And Aaron and his sons did all the things hich Jehovah commanded by Moses.
And it came to pass on the eighth day, that Moses called Aaron and his sons, and the elders of Israel;
and he said unto Aaron, Take thee a calf of the herd for a sin-offering, and a ram for a burnt-offering, ithout blemish, and offer them before Jehovah.
And unto the children of Israel thou shalt speak, saying, Take ye a he-goat for a sin-offering; and a calf and a lamb, both a year old, ithout blemish, for a burnt-offering;
and an ox and a ram for peace-offerings, to sacrifice before Jehovah; and a meal-offering mingled ith oil: for to-day Jehovah appeareth unto you.
And they brought that hich Moses commanded before the tent of meeting: and all the congregation dre near and stood before Jehovah.
And Moses said, This is the thing hich Jehovah commanded that ye should do: and the glory of Jehovah shall appear unto you.

And Moses said unto Aaron, Dra near unto the altar, and offer thy sin-offering, and thy burnt-offering, and make atonement for thyself, and for the people; and offer the oblation of the people, and make atonement for them; as Jehovah commanded.
So Aaron dre near unto the altar, and sle the calf of the sin-offering, hich as for himself.
And the sons of Aaron presented the blood unto him; and he dipped his finger in the blood, and put it upon the horns of the altar, and poured out the blood at the base of the altar:
but the fat, and the kidneys, and the caul from the liver of the sin-offering, he burnt upon the altar; as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And the flesh and the skin he burnt ith fire ithout the camp.
And he sle the burnt-offering; and Aaron’s sons delivered unto him the blood, and he sprinkled it upon the altar round about.
And they delivered the burnt-offering unto him, piece by piece, and the head: and he burnt them upon the altar.
And he ashed the inards and the legs, and burnt them upon the burnt-offering on the altar.
And he presented the people’s oblation, and took the goat of the sin-offering hich as for the people, and sle it, and offered it for sin, as the first.
And he presented the burnt-offering, and offered it according to the ordinance.
And he presented the meal-offering, and filled his hand therefrom, and burnt it upon the altar, besides the burnt-offering of the morning.
He sle also the ox and the ram, the sacrifice of peace-offerings, hich as for the people: and Aaron’s sons delivered unto him the blood, hich he sprinkled upon the altar round about,
and the fat of the ox and of the ram, the fat tail, and that hich covereth \add the inards\add*, and the kidneys, and the caul of the liver:
and they put the fat upon the breasts, and he burnt the fat upon the altar:
and the breasts and the right thigh Aaron aved for a ave-offering before Jehovah; as Moses commanded.
And Aaron lifted up his hands toard the people, and blessed them; and he came don from offering the sin-offering, and the burnt-offering, and the peace-offerings.
And Moses and Aaron ent into the tent of meeting, and came out, and blessed the people: and the glory of Jehovah appeared unto all the people.
And there came forth fire from before Jehovah, and consumed upon the altar the burnt-offering and the fat: and hen all the people sa it, they shouted, and fell on their faces.
And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took each of them his censer, and put fire therein, and laid incense thereon, and offered strange fire before Jehovah, hich he had not commanded them.
And there came forth fire from before Jehovah, and devoured them, and they died before Jehovah.
Then Moses said unto Aaron, This is it that Jehovah spake, saying, I ill be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I ill be glorified. And Aaron held his peace.
And Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron, and said unto them, Dra near, carry your brethren from before the sanctuary out of the camp.
So they dre near, and carried them in their coats out of the camp, as Moses had said.

And Moses said unto Aaron, and unto Eleazar and unto Ithamar, his sons, Let not the hair of your heads go loose, neither rend your clothes; that ye die not, and that he be not roth ith all the congregation: but let your brethren, the hole house of Israel, beail the burning hich Jehovah hath kindled.
And ye shall not go out from the door of the tent of meeting, lest ye die; for the anointing oil of Jehovah is upon you. And they did according to the ord of Moses.
And Jehovah spake unto Aaron, saying,
Drink no ine nor strong drink, thou, nor thy sons ith thee, hen ye go into the tent of meeting, that ye die not: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations:
and that ye may make a distinction beteen the holy and the common, and beteen the unclean and the clean;
and that ye may teach the children of Israel all the statutes hich Jehovah hath spoken unto them by Moses.

And Moses spake unto Aaron, and unto Eleazar and unto Ithamar, his sons that ere left, Take the meal-offering that remaineth of the offerings of Jehovah made by fire, and eat it ithout leaven beside the altar; for it is most holy;
and ye shall eat it in a holy place, because it is thy portion, and thy sons’ portion, of the offerings of Jehovah made by fire: for so I am commanded.

And the ave-breast and the heave-thigh shall ye eat in a clean place, thou, and thy sons, and thy daughters ith thee: for they are given as thy portion, and thy sons’ portion, out of the sacrifices of the peace-offerings of the children of Israel.

The heave-thigh and the ave-breast shall they bring ith the offerings made by fire of the fat, to ave it for a ave-offering before Jehovah: and it shall be thine, and thy sons’ ith thee, as a portion for ever; as Jehovah hath commanded.
And Moses diligently sought the goat of the sin-offering, and, behold, it as burnt: and he as angry ith Eleazar and ith Ithamar, the sons of Aaron that ere left, saying,

Wherefore have ye not eaten the sin-offering in the place of the sanctuary, seeing it is most holy, and he hath given it you to bear the iniquity of the congregation, to make atonement for them before Jehovah?
Behold, the blood of it as not brought into the sanctuary ithin: ye should certainly have eaten it in the sanctuary, as I commanded.

And Aaron spake unto Moses, Behold, this day have they offered their sin-offering and their burnt-offering before Jehovah; and there have befallen me such things as these: and if I had eaten the sin-offering to-day, ould it have been ell-pleasing in the sight of Jehovah?
And hen Moses heard \add that\add*, it as ell-pleasing in his sight.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses and to Aaron, saying unto them,
Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, These are the living things hich ye may eat among all the beasts that are on the earth.
Whatsoever parteth the hoof, and is clovenfooted, \add and\add* cheeth the cud, among the beasts, that may ye eat.
Nevertheless these shall ye not eat of them that che the cud, or of them that part the hoof: the camel, because he cheeth the cud but parteth not the hoof, he is unclean unto you.
And the coney, because he cheeth the cud but parteth not the hoof, he is unclean unto you.
And the hare, because she cheeth the cud but parteth not the hoof, she is unclean unto you.
And the sine, because he parteth the hoof, and is clovenfooted, but cheeth not the cud, he is unclean unto you.
Of their flesh ye shall not eat, and their carcasses ye shall not touch; they are unclean unto you.
These may ye eat of all that are in the aters: hatsoever hath fins and scales in the aters, in the seas, and in the rivers, that may ye eat.
And all that have not fins and scales in the seas, and in the rivers, of all that move in the aters, and of all the living creatures that are in the aters, they are an abomination unto you,
and they shall be an abomination unto you; ye shall not eat of their flesh, and their carcasses ye shall have in abomination.
Whatsoever hath no fins nor scales in the aters, that is an abomination unto you.
And these ye shall have in abomination among the birds; they shall not be eaten, they are an abomination: the eagle, and the gier-eagle, and the ospray,
and the kite, and the falcon after its kind,
every raven after its kind,
and the ostrich, and the night-hak, and the sea-me, and the hak after its kind,
and the little ol, and the cormorant, and the great ol,
and the horned ol, and the pelican, and the vulture,
and the stork, the heron after its kind, and the hoopoe, and the bat.
All inged creeping things that go upon all fours are an abomination unto you.
Yet these may ye eat of all inged creeping things that go upon all fours, hich have legs above their feet, hereith to leap upon the earth;
even these of them ye may eat: the locust after its kind, and the bald locust after its kind, and the cricket after its kind, and the grasshopper after its kind.
But all inged creeping things, hich have four feet, are an abomination unto you.
And by these ye shall become unclean: hosoever toucheth the carcass of them shall be unclean until the even;
and hosoever beareth \add aught\add* of the carcass of them shall ash his clothes, and be unclean until the even.
Every beast hich parteth the hoof, and is not clovenfooted, nor cheeth the cud, is unclean unto you: every one that toucheth them shall be unclean.
And hatsoever goeth upon its pas, among all beasts that go on all fours, they are unclean unto you: hoso toucheth their carcass shall be unclean until the even.
And he that beareth the carcass of them shall ash his clothes, and be unclean until the even: they are unclean unto you.
And these are they hich are unclean unto you among the creeping things that creep upon the earth: the easel, and the mouse, and the great lizard after its kind,
and the gecko, and the land-crocodile, and the lizard, and the sand-lizard, and the chameleon.
These are they hich are unclean to you among all that creep: hosoever doth touch them, hen they are dead, shall be unclean until the even.

And upon hatsoever any of them, hen they are dead, doth fall, it shall be unclean; hether it be any vessel of ood, or raiment, or skin, or sack, hatsoever vessel it be, hereith any ork is done, it must be put into ater, and it shall be unclean until the even; then shall it be clean.
And every earthen vessel, hereinto any of them falleth, hatsoever is in it shall be unclean, and it ye shall break.
All food \add therein\add* hich may be eaten, that on hich ater cometh, shall be unclean; and all drink that may be drunk in every \add such\add* vessel shall be unclean.
And every thing hereupon \add any part\add* of their carcass falleth shall be unclean; hether oven, or range for pots, it shall be broken in pieces: they are unclean, and shall be unclean unto you.
Nevertheless a fountain or a pit herein is a gathering of ater shall be clean: but that hich toucheth their carcass shall be unclean.
And if \add aught\add* of their carcass fall upon any soing seed hich is to be son, it is clean.
But if ater be put upon the seed, and \add aught\add* of their carcass fall thereon, it is unclean unto you.
And if any beast, of hich ye may eat, die; he that toucheth the carcass thereof shall be unclean until the even.
And he that eateth of the carcass of it shall ash his clothes, and be unclean until the even: he also that beareth the carcass of it shall ash his clothes, and be unclean until the even.
And every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth is an abomination; it shall not be eaten.

Whatsoever goeth upon the belly, and hatsoever goeth upon all fours, or hatsoever hath many feet, even all creeping things that creep upon the earth, them ye shall not eat; for they are an abomination.
Ye shall not make yourselves abominable ith any creeping thing that creepeth, neither shall ye make yourselves unclean ith them, that ye should be defiled thereby.
For I am Jehovah your God: sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves ith any manner of creeping thing that moveth upon the earth.
For I am Jehovah that brought you up out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.
This is the la of the beast, and of the bird, and of every living creature that moveth in the aters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth;
to make a distinction beteen the unclean and the clean, and beteen the living thing that may be eaten and the living thing that may not be eaten.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a oman conceive seed, and bear a man-child, then she shall be unclean seven days; as in the days of the impurity of her sickness shall she be unclean.
And in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.
And she shall continue in the blood of \add her\add* purifying three and thirty days; she shall touch no halloed thing, nor come into the sanctuary, until the days of her purifying be fulfilled.
But if she bear a maid-child, then she shall be unclean to eeks, as in her impurity; and she shall continue in the blood of \add her\add* purifying threescore and six days.

And hen the days of her purifying are fulfilled, for a son, or for a daughter, she shall bring a lamb a year old for a burnt-offering, and a young pigeon, or a turtle-dove, for a sin-offering, unto the door of the tent of meeting, unto the priest:
and he shall offer it before Jehovah, and make atonement for her; and she shall be cleansed from the fountain of her blood. This is the la for her that beareth, hether a male or a female.

And if her means suffice not for a lamb, then she shall take to turtle-doves, or to young pigeons; the one for a burnt-offering, and the other for a sin-offering: and the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,

When a man shall have in the skin of his flesh a rising, or a scab, or a bright spot, and it become in the skin of his flesh the plague of leprosy, then he shall be brought unto Aaron the priest, or unto one of his sons the priests:

and the priest shall look on the plague in the skin of the flesh: and if the hair in the plague be turned hite, and the appearance of the plague be deeper than the skin of his flesh, it is the plague of leprosy; and the priest shall look on him, and pronounce him unclean.

And if the bright spot be hite in the skin of his flesh, and the appearance thereof be not deeper than the skin, and the hair thereof be not turned hite, then the priest shall shut up \add him that hath\add* the plague seven days:
and the priest shall look on him the seventh day: and, behold, if in his eyes the plague be at a stay, and the plague be not spread in the skin, then the priest shall shut him up seven days more:

and the priest shall look on him again the seventh day; and, behold, if the plague be dim, and the plague be not spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him clean: it is a scab: and he shall ash his clothes, and be clean.
But if the scab spread abroad in the skin, after that he hath shoed himself to the priest for his cleansing, he shall sho himself to the priest again:
and the priest shall look; and, behold, if the scab be spread in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is leprosy.
When the plague of leprosy is in a man, then he shall be brought unto the priest;
and the priest shall look; and, behold, if there be a hite rising in the skin, and it have turned the hair hite, and there be quick ra flesh in the rising,
it is an old leprosy in the skin of his flesh, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean: he shall not shut him up; for he is unclean.
And if the leprosy break out abroad in the skin, and the leprosy cover all the skin of \add him that hath\add* the plague from his head even to his feet, as far as appeareth to the priest;
then the priest shall look; and, behold, if the leprosy have covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce \add him\add* clean \add that hath\add* the plague: it is all turned hite: he is clean.
But hensoever ra flesh appeareth in him, he shall be unclean.
And the priest shall look on the ra flesh, and pronounce him unclean: the ra flesh is unclean: it is leprosy.
Or if the ra flesh turn again, and be changed unto hite, then he shall come unto the priest;
and the priest shall look on him; and, behold, if the plague be turned into hite, then the priest shall pronounce \add him\add* clean \add that hath\add* the plague: he is clean.
And hen the flesh hath in the skin thereof a boil, and it is healed,
and in the place of the boil there is a hite rising, or a bright spot, reddish-hite, then it shall be shoed to the priest;

and the priest shall look; and, behold, if the appearance thereof be loer than the skin, and the hair thereof be turned hite, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is the plague of leprosy, it hath broken out in the boil.
But if the priest look on it, and, behold, there be no hite hairs therein, and it be not loer than the skin, but be dim; then the priest shall shut him up seven days:
and if it spread abroad in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a plague.
But if the bright spot stay in its place, and be not spread, it is the scar of the boil; and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
Or hen the flesh hath in the skin thereof a burning by fire, and the quick \add flesh\add* of the burning become a bright spot, reddish-hite, or hite;

then the priest shall look upon it; and, behold, if the hair in the bright spot be turned hite, and the appearance thereof be deeper than the skin; it is leprosy, it hath broken out in the burning: and the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is the plague of leprosy.
But if the priest look on it, and, behold, there be no hite hair in the bright spot, and it be no loer than the skin, but be dim; then the priest shall shut him up seven days:
and the priest shall look upon him the seventh day: if it spread abroad in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is the plague of leprosy.
And if the bright spot stay in its place, and be not spread in the skin, but be dim; it is the rising of the burning, and the priest shall pronounce him clean: for it is the scar of the burning.
And hen a man or oman hath a plague upon the head or upon the beard,

then the priest shall look on the plague; and, behold, if the appearance thereof be deeper than the skin, and there be in it yello thin hair, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a scall, it is leprosy of the head or of the beard.

And if the priest look on the plague of the scall, and, behold, the appearance thereof be not deeper than the skin, and there be no black hair in it, then the priest shall shut up \add him that hath\add* the plague of the scall seven days:
and in the seventh day the priest shall look on the plague; and, behold, if the scall be not spread, and there be in it no yello hair, and the appearance of the scall be not deeper than the skin,
then he shall be shaven, but the scall shall he not shave; and the priest shall shut up \add him that hath\add* the scall seven days more:

and in the seventh day the priest shall look on the scall; and, behold, if the scall be not spread in the skin, and the appearance thereof be not deeper than the skin; then the priest shall pronounce him clean: and he shall ash his clothes, and be clean.
But if the scall spread abroad in the skin after his cleansing,
then the priest shall look on him; and, behold, if the scall be spread in the skin, the priest shall not seek for the yello hair; he is unclean.
But if in his eyes the scall be at a stay, and black hair be gron up therein; the scall is healed, he is clean: and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
And hen a man or a oman hath in the skin of the flesh bright spots, even hite bright spots;
then the priest shall look; and, behold, if the bright spots in the skin of their flesh be of a dull hite, it is a tetter, it hath broken out in the skin; he is clean.
And if a man’s hair be fallen off his head, he is bald; \add yet\add* is he clean.
And if his hair be fallen off from the front part of his head, he is forehead bald; \add yet\add* is he clean.
But if there be in the bald head, or the bald forehead, a reddish-hite plague; it is leprosy breaking out in his bald head, or his bald forehead.
Then the priest shall look upon him; and, behold, if the rising of the plague be reddish-hite in his bald head, or in his bald forehead, as the appearance of leprosy in the skin of the flesh;
he is a leprous man, he is unclean: the priest shall surely pronounce him unclean; his plague is in his head.
And the leper in hom the plague is, his clothes shall be rent, and the hair of his head shall go loose, and he shall cover his upper lip, and shall cry, Unclean, unclean.
All the days herein the plague is in him he shall be unclean; he is unclean: he shall dell alone; ithout the camp shall his delling be.
The garment also that the plague of leprosy is in, hether it be a oollen garment, or a linen garment;
hether it be in arp, or oof; of linen, or of oollen; hether in a skin, or in anything made of skin;
if the plague be greenish or reddish in the garment, or in the skin, or in the arp, or in the oof, or in anything of skin; it is the plague of leprosy, and shall be shoed unto the priest.
And the priest shall look upon the plague, and shut up \add that hich hath\add* the plague seven days:

and he shall look on the plague on the seventh day: if the plague be spread in the garment, either in the arp, or in the oof, or in the skin, hatever service skin is used for; the plague is a fretting leprosy; it is unclean.
And he shall burn the garment, hether the arp or the oof, in oollen or in linen, or anything of skin, herein the plague is: for it is a fretting leprosy; it shall be burnt in the fire.
And if the priest shall look, and, behold, the plague be not spread in the garment, either in the arp, or in the oof, or in anything of skin;
then the priest shall command that they ash the thing herein the plague is, and he shall shut it up seven days more:

and the priest shall look, after that the plague is ashed; and, behold, if the plague have not changed its color, and the plague be not spread, it is unclean; thou shalt burn it in the fire: it is a fret, hether the bareness be ithin or ithout.
And if the priest look, and, behold, the plague be dim after the ashing thereof, then he shall rend it out of the garment, or out of the skin, or out of the arp, or out of the oof:
and if it appear still in the garment, either in the arp, or in the oof, or in anything of skin, it is breaking out: thou shalt burn that herein the plague is ith fire.
And the garment, either the arp, or the oof, or hatsoever thing of skin it be, hich thou shalt ash, if the plague be departed from them, then it shall be ashed the second time, and shall be clean.
This is the la of the plague of leprosy in a garment of oollen or linen, either in the arp, or the oof, or anything of skin, to pronounce it clean, or to pronounce it unclean.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
This shall be the la of the leper in the day of his cleansing: he shall be brought unto the priest:
and the priest shall go forth out of the camp; and the priest shall look; and, behold, if the plague of leprosy be healed in the leper,
then shall the priest command to take for him that is to be cleansed to living clean birds, and cedar ood, and scarlet, and hyssop:
and the priest shall command to kill one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running ater.
As for the living bird, he shall take it, and the cedar ood, and the scarlet, and the hyssop, and shall dip them and the living bird in the blood of the bird that as killed over the running ater:
and he shall sprinkle upon him that is to be cleansed from the leprosy seven times, and shall pronounce him clean, and shall let go the living bird into the open field.

And he that is to be cleansed shall ash his clothes, and shave off all his hair, and bathe himself in ater; and he shall be clean: and after that he shall come into the camp, but shall dell outside his tent seven days.

And it shall be on the seventh day, that he shall shave all his hair off his head and his beard and his eyebros, even all his hair he shall shave off: and he shall ash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in ater, and he shall be clean.

And on the eighth day he shall take to he-lambs ithout blemish, and one ee-lamb a year old ithout blemish, and three tenth parts \add of an ephah\add* of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled ith oil, and one log of oil.
And the priest that cleanseth him shall set the man that is to be cleansed, and those things, before Jehovah, at the door of the tent of meeting.
And the priest shall take one of the he-lambs, and offer him for a trespass-offering, and the log of oil, and ave them for a ave-offering before Jehovah:

and he shall kill the he-lamb in the place here they kill the sin-offering and the burnt-offering, in the place of the sanctuary: for as the sin-offering is the priest’s, so is the trespass-offering: it is most holy.

And the priest shall take of the blood of the trespass-offering, and the priest shall put it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot.
And the priest shall take of the log of oil, and pour it into the palm of his on left hand;
and the priest shall dip his right finger in the oil that is in his left hand, and shall sprinkle of the oil ith his finger seven times before Jehovah.

And of the rest of the oil that is in his hand shall the priest put upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot, upon the blood of the trespass-offering:
and the rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he shall put upon the head of him that is to be cleansed: and the priest shall make atonement for him before Jehovah.
And the priest shall offer the sin-offering, and make atonement for him that is to be cleansed because of his uncleanness: and afterard he shall kill the burnt-offering;
and the priest shall offer the burnt-offering and the meal-offering upon the altar: and the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be clean.

And if he be poor, and cannot get so much, then he shall take one he-lamb for a trespass-offering to be aved, to make atonement for him, and one tenth part \add of an ephah\add* of fine flour mingled ith oil for a meal-offering, and a log of oil;
and to turtle-doves, or to young pigeons, such as he is able to get; and the one shall be a sin-offering, and the other a burnt-offering.
And on the eighth day he shall bring them for his cleansing unto the priest, unto the door of the tent of meeting, before Jehovah:
and the priest shall take the lamb of the trespass-offering, and the log of oil, and the priest shall ave them for a ave-offering before Jehovah.

And he shall kill the lamb of the trespass-offering; and the priest shall take of the blood of the trespass-offering, and put it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot.
And the priest shall pour of the oil into the palm of his on left hand;
and the priest shall sprinkle ith his right finger some of the oil that is in his left hand seven times before Jehovah:

and the priest shall put of the oil that is in his hand upon the tip of the right ear of him that is to be cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot, upon the place of the blood of the trespass-offering:
and the rest of the oil that is in the priest’s hand he shall put upon the head of him that is to be cleansed, to make atonement for him before Jehovah.
And he shall offer one of the turtle-doves, or of the young pigeons, such as he is able to get,

even such as he is able to get, the one for a sin-offering, and the other for a burnt-offering, ith the meal-offering: and the priest shall make atonement for him that is to be cleansed before Jehovah.
This is the la of him in hom is the plague of leprosy, ho is not able to get \add that hich pertaineth\add* to his cleansing.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,
When ye are come into the land of Canaan, hich I give to you for a possession, and I put the plague of leprosy in a house of the land of your possession;
then he that oneth the house shall come and tell the priest, saying, There seemeth to me to be as it ere a plague in the house.

And the priest shall command that they empty the house, before the priest goeth in to see the plague, that all that is in the house be not made unclean: and afterard the priest shall go in to see the house:
and he shall look on the plague; and, behold, if the plague be in the alls of the house ith hollo streaks, greenish or reddish, and the appearance thereof be loer than the all;
then the priest shall go out of the house to the door of the house, and shut up the house seven days.
And the priest shall come again the seventh day, and shall look; and, behold, if the plague be spread in the alls of the house;
then the priest shall command that they take out the stones in hich the plague is, and cast them into an unclean place ithout the city:
and he shall cause the house to be scraped ithin round about, and they shall pour out the mortar, that they scrape off, ithout the city into an unclean place:
and they shall take other stones, and put them in the place of those stones; and he shall take other mortar, and shall plaster the house.
And if the plague come again, and break out in the house, after that he hath taken out the stones, and after he hath scraped the house, and after it is plastered;
then the priest shall come in and look; and, behold, if the plague be spread in the house, it is a fretting leprosy in the house: it is unclean.
And he shall break don the house, the stones of it, and the timber thereof, and all the mortar of the house; and he shall carry them forth out of the city into an unclean place.
Moreover he that goeth into the house all the hile that it is shut up shall be unclean until the even.
And he that lieth in the house shall ash his clothes; and he that eateth in the house shall ash his clothes.

And if the priest shall come in, and look, and, behold, the plague hath not spread in the house, after the house as plastered; then the priest shall pronounce the house clean, because the plague is healed.
And he shall take to cleanse the house to birds, and cedar-ood, and scarlet, and hyssop:
and he shall kill one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running ater:
and he shall take the cedar-ood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet, and the living bird, and dip them in the blood of the slain bird, and in the running ater, and sprinkle the house seven times:
and he shall cleanse the house ith the blood of the bird, and ith the running ater, and ith the living bird, and ith the cedar-ood, and ith the hyssop, and ith the scarlet:
but he shall let go the living bird out of the city into the open field: so shall he make atonement for the house; and it shall be clean.
This is the la for all manner of plague of leprosy, and for a scall,
and for the leprosy of a garment, and for a house,
and for a rising, and for a scab, and for a bright spot;
to teach hen it is unclean, and hen it is clean: this is the la of leprosy.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses and to Aaron, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When any man hath an issue out of his flesh, because of his issue he is unclean.
And this shall be his uncleanness in his issue: hether his flesh run ith his issue, or his flesh be stopped from his issue, it is his uncleanness.
Every bed hereon he that hath the issue lieth shall be unclean; and everything hereon he sitteth shall be unclean.
And hosoever toucheth his bed shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the even.
And he that sitteth on anything hereon he that hath the issue sat shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the even.
And he that toucheth the flesh of him that hath the issue shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the even.
And if he that hath the issue spit upon him that is clean, then he shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the even.
And hat saddle soever he that hath the issue rideth upon shall be unclean.
And hosoever toucheth anything that as under him shall be unclean until the even: and he that beareth those things shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the even.
And homsoever he that hath the issue toucheth, ithout having rinsed his hands in ater, he shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the even.
And the earthen vessel, hich he that hath the issue toucheth, shall be broken; and every vessel of ood shall be rinsed in ater.

And hen he that hath an issue is cleansed of his issue, then he shall number to himself seven days for his cleansing, and ash his clothes; and he shall bathe his flesh in running ater, and shall be clean.
And on the eighth day he shall take to him to turtle-doves, or to young pigeons, and come before Jehovah unto the door of the tent of meeting, and give them unto the priest:
and the priest shall offer them, the one for a sin-offering, and the other for a burnt-offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him before Jehovah for his issue.
And if any man’s seed of copulation go out from him, then he shall bathe all his flesh in ater, and be unclean until the even.
And every garment, and every skin, hereon is the seed of copulation, shall be ashed ith ater, and be unclean until the even.
The oman also ith hom a man shall lie ith seed of copulation, they shall both bathe themselves in ater, and be unclean until the even.
And if a oman have an issue, \add and\add* her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be in her impurity seven days: and hosoever toucheth her shall be unclean until the even.
And everything that she lieth upon in her impurity shall be unclean: everything also that she sitteth upon shall be unclean.
And hosoever toucheth her bed shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the even.
And hosoever toucheth anything that she sitteth upon shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the even.
And if it be on the bed, or on anything hereon she sitteth, hen he toucheth it, he shall be unclean until the even.
And if any man lie ith her, and her impurity be upon him, he shall be unclean seven days; and every bed hereon he lieth shall be unclean.

And if a oman have an issue of her blood many days not in the time of her impurity, or if she have an issue beyond the time of her impurity; all the days of the issue of her uncleanness she shall be as in the days of her impurity: she is unclean.
Every bed hereon she lieth all the days of her issue shall be unto her as the bed of her impurity: and everything hereon she sitteth shall be unclean, as the uncleanness of her impurity.
And hosoever toucheth those things shall be unclean, and shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the even.
But if she be cleansed of her issue, then she shall number to herself seven days, and after that she shall be clean.
And on the eighth day she shall take unto her to turtle-doves, or to young pigeons, and bring them unto the priest, to the door of the tent of meeting.
And the priest shall offer the one for a sin-offering, and the other for a burnt-offering; and the priest shall make atonement for her before Jehovah for the issue of her uncleanness.
Thus shall ye separate the children of Israel from their uncleanness, that they die not in their uncleanness, hen they defile my tabernacle that is in the midst of them.
This is the la of him that hath an issue, and of him hose seed of copulation goeth from him, so that he is unclean thereby;
and of her that is sick ith her impurity, and of him that hath an issue, of the man, and of the oman, and of him that lieth ith her that is unclean.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, after the death of the to sons of Aaron, hen they dre near before Jehovah, and died;

and Jehovah said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place ithin the veil, before the mercy-seat hich is upon the ark; that he die not: for I ill appear in the cloud upon the mercy-seat.
Hereith shall Aaron come into the holy place: ith a young bullock for a sin-offering, and a ram for a burnt-offering.

He shall put on the holy linen coat, and he shall have the linen breeches upon his flesh, and shall be girded ith the linen girdle, and ith the linen mitre shall he be attired: they are the holy garments; and he shall bathe his flesh in ater, and put them on.
And he shall take of the congregation of the children of Israel to he-goats for a sin-offering, and one ram for a burnt-offering.
And Aaron shall present the bullock of the sin-offering, hich is for himself, and make atonement for himself, and for his house.
And he shall take the to goats, and set them before Jehovah at the door of the tent of meeting.
And Aaron shall cast lots upon the to goats; one lot for Jehovah, and the other lot for Azazel.
And Aaron shall present the goat upon hich the lot fell for Jehovah, and offer him for a sin-offering.
But the goat, on hich the lot fell for Azazel, shall be set alive before Jehovah, to make atonement for him, to send him aay for Azazel into the ilderness.

And Aaron shall present the bullock of the sin-offering, hich is for himself, and shall make atonement for himself, and for his house, and shall kill the bullock of the sin-offering hich is for himself.
And he shall take a censer full of coals of fire from off the altar before Jehovah, and his hands full of seet incense beaten small, and bring it ithin the veil:
and he shall put the incense upon the fire before Jehovah, that the cloud of the incense may cover the mercy-seat that is upon the testimony, that he die not:
and he shall take of the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it ith his finger upon the mercy-seat on the east; and before the mercy-seat shall he sprinkle of the blood ith his finger seven times.

Then shall he kill the goat of the sin-offering, that is for the people, and bring his blood ithin the veil, and do ith his blood as he did ith the blood of the bullock, and sprinkle it upon the mercy-seat, and before the mercy-seat:

and he shall make atonement for the holy place, because of the uncleannesses of the children of Israel, and because of their transgressions, even all their sins: and so shall he do for the tent of meeting, that delleth ith them in the midst of their uncleannesses.

And there shall be no man in the tent of meeting hen he goeth in to make atonement in the holy place, until he come out, and have made atonement for himself, and for his household, and for all the assembly of Israel.

And he shall go out unto the altar that is before Jehovah, and make atonement for it, and shall take of the blood of the bullock, and of the blood of the goat, and put it upon the horns of the altar round about.
And he shall sprinkle of the blood upon it ith his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and hallo it from the uncleannesses of the children of Israel.
