And hen he hath made an end of atoning for the holy place, and the tent of meeting, and the altar, he shall present the live goat:

and Aaron shall lay both his hands upon the head of the live goat, and confess over him all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their transgressions, even all their sins; and he shall put them upon the head of the goat, and shall send him aay by the hand of a man that is in readiness into the ilderness:
and the goat shall bear upon him all their iniquities unto a solitary land: and he shall let go the goat in the ilderness.
And Aaron shall come into the tent of meeting, and shall put off the linen garments, hich he put on hen he ent into the holy place, and shall leave them there:

and he shall bathe his flesh in ater in a holy place, and put on his garments, and come forth, and offer his burnt-offering and the burnt-offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people.
And the fat of the sin-offering shall he burn upon the altar.
And he that letteth go the goat for Azazel shall ash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in ater, and afterard he shall come into the camp.

And the bullock of the sin-offering, and the goat of the sin-offering, hose blood as brought in to make atonement in the holy place, shall be carried forth ithout the camp; and they shall burn in the fire their skins, and their flesh, and their dung.
And he that burneth them shall ash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in ater, and afterard he shall come into the camp.

And it shall be a statute for ever unto you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls, and shall do no manner of ork, the home-born, or the stranger that sojourneth among you:
for on this day shall atonement be made for you, to cleanse you; from all your sins shall ye be clean before Jehovah.
It is a sabbath of solemn rest unto you, and ye shall afflict your souls; it is a statute for ever.
And the priest, ho shall be anointed and ho shall be consecrated to be priest in his father’s stead, shall make the atonement, and shall put on the linen garments, even the holy garments:

and he shall make atonement for the holy sanctuary; and he shall make atonement for the tent of meeting and for the altar; and he shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you, to make atonement for the children of Israel because of all their sins once in the year. And he did as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto Aaron, and unto his sons, and unto all the children of Israel, and say unto them: This is the thing hich Jehovah hath commanded, saying,
What man soever there be of the house of Israel, that killeth an ox, or lamb, or goat, in the camp, or that killeth it ithout the camp,

and hath not brought it unto the door of the tent of meeting, to offer it as an oblation unto Jehovah before the tabernacle of Jehovah: blood shall be imputed unto that man; he hath shed blood; and that man shall be cut off from among his people:

to the end that the children of Israel may bring their sacrifices, hich they sacrifice in the open field, even that they may bring them unto Jehovah, unto the door of the tent of meeting, unto the priest, and sacrifice them for sacrifices of peace-offerings unto Jehovah.
And the priest shall sprinkle the blood upon the altar of Jehovah at the door of the tent of meeting, and burn the fat for a seet savor unto Jehovah.
And they shall no more sacrifice their sacrifices unto the he-goats, after hich they play the harlot. This shall be a statute forever unto them throughout their generations.
And thou shalt say unto them, Whatsoever man there be of the house of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn among them, that offereth a burnt-offering or sacrifice,
and bringeth it not unto the door of the tent of meeting, to sacrifice it unto Jehovah; that man shall be cut off from his people.

And hatsoever man there be of the house of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn among them, that eateth any manner of blood, I ill set my face against that soul that eateth blood, and ill cut him off from among his people.
For the life of the flesh is in the blood; and I have given it to you upon the altar to make atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that maketh atonement by reason of the life.
Therefore I said unto the children of Israel, No soul of you shall eat blood, neither shall any stranger that sojourneth among you eat blood.

And hatsoever man there be of the children of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn among them, ho taketh in hunting any beast or bird that may be eaten; he shall pour out the blood thereof, and cover it ith dust.

For as to the life of all flesh, the blood thereof is \add all one\add* ith the life thereof: therefore I said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall eat the blood of no manner of flesh; for the life of all flesh is the blood thereof: hosoever eateth it shall be cut off.

And every soul that eateth that hich dieth of itself, or that hich is torn of beasts, hether he be home-born or a sojourner, he shall ash his clothes, and bathe himself in ater, and be unclean until the even: then shall he be clean.
But if he ash them not, nor bathe his flesh, then he shall bear his iniquity.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, I am Jehovah your God.
After the doings of the land of Egypt, herein ye delt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, hither I bring you, shall ye not do; neither shall ye alk in their statutes.
Mine ordinances shall ye do, and my statutes shall ye keep, to alk therein: I am Jehovah your God.
Ye shall therefore keep my statutes, and mine ordinances; hich if a man do, he shall live in them: I am Jehovah.
None of you shall approach to any that are near of kin to him, to uncover \add their\add* nakedness: I am Jehovah.
The nakedness of thy father, even the nakedness of thy mother, shalt thou not uncover: she is thy mother; thou shalt not uncover her nakedness.
The nakedness of thy father’s ife shalt thou not uncover; it is thy father’s nakedness.
The nakedness of thy sister, the daughter of thy father, or the daughter of thy mother, hether born at home, or born abroad, even their nakedness thou shalt not uncover.
The nakedness of thy son’s daughter, or of thy daughter’s daughter, even their nakedness thou shalt not uncover: for theirs is thine on nakedness.
The nakedness of thy father’s ife’s daughter, begotten of thy father, she is thy sister, thou shalt not uncover her nakedness.
Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father’s sister: she is thy father’s near kinsoman.
Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy mother’s sister: for she is thy mother’s near kinsoman.
Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father’s brother, thou shalt not approach to his ife: she is thine aunt.
Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy daughter-in-la: she is thy son’s ife; thou shalt not uncover her nakedness.
Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy brother’s ife: it is thy brother’s nakedness.
Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of a oman and her daughter; thou shalt not take her son’s daughter, or her daughter’s daughter, to uncover her nakedness; they are near kinsomen: it is ickedness.
And thou shalt not take a ife to her sister, to be a rival \add to her\add*, to uncover her nakedness, besides the other in her life-time.
And thou shalt not approach unto a oman to uncover her nakedness, as long as she is impure by her uncleanness.
And thou shalt not lie carnally ith thy neighbor’s ife, to defile thyself ith her.
And thou shalt not give any of thy seed to make them pass through \add the fire\add* to Molech; neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am Jehovah.
Thou shalt not lie ith mankind, as ith omankind: it is abomination.
And thou shalt not lie ith any beast to defile thyself thereith; neither shall any oman stand before a beast, to lie don thereto: it is confusion.
Defile not ye yourselves in any of these things: for in all these the nations are defiled hich I cast out from before you;
and the land is defiled: therefore I do visit the iniquity thereof upon it, and the land vomiteth out her inhabitants.
Ye therefore shall keep my statutes and mine ordinances, and shall not do any of these abominations; neither the home-born, nor the stranger that sojourneth among you
( for all these abominations have the men of the land done, that ere before you, and the land is defiled);
that the land vomit not you out also, hen ye defile it, as it vomited out the nation that as before you.
For hosoever shall do any of these abominations, even the souls that do them shall be cut off from among their people.
Therefore shall ye keep my charge, that ye practise not any of these abominable customs, hich ere practised before you, and that ye defile not yourselves therein: I am Jehovah your God.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say unto them, Ye shall be holy; for I Jehovah your God am holy.
Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father; and ye shall keep my sabbaths: I am Jehovah your God.
Turn ye not unto idols, nor make to yourselves molten gods: I am Jehovah your God.
And hen ye offer a sacrifice of peace-offerings unto Jehovah, ye shall offer it that ye may be accepted.
It shall be eaten the same day ye offer it, and on the morro: and if aught remain until the third day, it shall be burnt ith fire.
And if it be eaten at all on the third day, it is an abomination; it shall not be accepted:
but every one that eateth it shall bear his iniquity, because he hath profaned the holy thing of Jehovah: and that soul shall be cut off from his people.
And hen ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not holly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleaning of thy harvest.
And thou shalt not glean thy vineyard, neither shalt thou gather the fallen fruit of thy vineyard; thou shalt leave them for the poor and for the sojourner: I am Jehovah your God.
Ye shall not steal; neither shall ye deal falsely, nor lie one to another.
And ye shall not sear by my name falsely, and profane the name of thy God: I am Jehovah.
Thou shalt not oppress thy neighbor, nor rob him: the ages of a hired servant shall not abide ith thee all night until the morning.
Thou shalt not curse the deaf, nor put a stumblingblock before the blind; but thou shalt fear thy God: I am Jehovah.
Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment: thou shalt not respect the person of the poor, nor honor the person of the mighty; but in righteousness shalt thou judge thy neighbor.
Thou shalt not go up and don as a talebearer among thy people: neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbor: I am Jehovah.
Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thy heart: thou shalt surely rebuke thy neighbor, and not bear sin because of him.
Thou shalt not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people; but thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself: I am Jehovah.

Ye shall keep my statutes. Thou shalt not let thy cattle gender ith a diverse kind: thou shalt not so thy field ith to kinds of seed: neither shall there come upon thee a garment of to kinds of stuff mingled together.

And hosoever lieth carnally ith a oman, that is a bondmaid, betrothed to a husband, and not at all redeemed, nor freedom given her; they shall be punished; they shall not be put to death, because she as not free.
And he shall bring his trespass-offering unto Jehovah, unto the door of the tent of meeting, even a ram for a trespass-offering.
And the priest shall make atonement for him ith the ram of the trespass-offering before Jehovah for his sin hich he hath sinned: and the sin hich he hath sinned shall be forgiven him.

And hen ye shall come into the land, and shall have planted all manner of trees for food, then ye shall count the fruit thereof as their uncircumcision: three years shall they be as uncircumcised unto you; it shall not be eaten.
But in the fourth year all the fruit thereof shall be holy, for giving praise unto Jehovah.
And in the fifth year shall ye eat of the fruit thereof, that it may yield unto you the increase thereof: I am Jehovah your God.
Ye shall not eat anything ith the blood: neither shall ye use enchantments, nor practise augury.
Ye shall not round the corners of your heads, neither shalt thou mar the corners of thy beard.
Ye shall not make any cuttings in your flesh for the dead, nor print any marks upon you: I am Jehovah.
Profane not thy daughter, to make her a harlot; lest the land fall to horedom, and the land become full of ickedness.
Ye shall keep my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary: I am Jehovah.
Turn ye not unto them that have familiar spirits, nor unto the izards; seek them not out, to be defiled by them: I am Jehovah your God.
Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honor the face of the old man, and thou shalt fear thy God: I am Jehovah.
And if a stranger sojourn ith thee in your land, ye shall not do him rong.
The stranger that sojourneth ith you shall be unto you as the home-born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself; for ye ere sojourners in the land of Egypt: I am Jehovah your God.
Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment, in measures of length, of eight, or of quantity.
Just balances, just eights, a just ephah, and a just hin, shall ye have: I am Jehovah your God, ho brought you out of the land of Egypt.
And ye shall observe all my statutes, and all mine ordinances, and do them: I am Jehovah.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

Moreover, thou shalt say to the children of Israel, Whosoever he be of the children of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn in Israel, that giveth of his seed unto Molech; he shall surely be put to death: the people of the land shall stone him ith stones.
I also ill set my face against that man, and ill cut him off from among his people; because he hath given of his seed unto Molech, to defile my sanctuary, and to profane my holy name.
And if the people of the land do at all hide their eyes from that man, hen he giveth of his seed unto Molech, and put him not to death;
then I ill set my face against that man, and against his family, and ill cut him off, and all that play the harlot after him, to play the harlot ith Molech, from among their people.

And the soul that turneth unto them that have familiar spirits, and unto the izards, to play the harlot after them, I ill even set my face against that soul, and ill cut him off from among his people.
Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy; for I am Jehovah your God.
And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I am Jehovah ho sanctifieth you.
For every one that curseth his father or his mother shall surely be put to death: he hath cursed his father or his mother; his blood shall be upon him.
And the man that committeth adultery ith another man’s ife, even he that committeth adultery ith his neighbor’s ife, the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely be put to death.
And the man that lieth ith his father’s ife hath uncovered his father’s nakedness: both of them shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.
And if a man lie ith his daughter-in-la, both of them shall surely be put to death: they have rought confusion; their blood shall be upon them.
And if a man lie ith mankind, as ith omankind, both of them have committed abomination: they shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.
And if a man take a ife and her mother, it is ickedness: they shall be burnt ith fire, both he and they; that there be no ickedness among you.
And if a man lie ith a beast, he shall surely be put to death: and ye shall slay the beast.
And if a oman approach unto any beast, and lie don thereto, thou shalt kill the oman, and the beast: they shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.

And if a man shall take his sister, his father’s daughter, or his mother’s daughter, and see her nakedness, and she see his nakedness; it is a shameful thing; and they shall be cut off in the sight of the children of their people: he hath uncovered his sister’s nakedness; he shall bear his iniquity.

And if a man shall lie ith a oman having her sickness, and shall uncover her nakedness; he hath made naked her fountain, and she hath uncovered the fountain of her blood: and both of them shall be cut off from among their people.
And thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy mother’s sister, nor of thy father’s sister; for he hath made naked his near kin: they shall bear their iniquity.
And if a man shall lie ith his uncle’s ife, he hath uncovered his uncle’s nakedness: they shall bear their sin; they shall die childless.
And if a man shall take his brother’s ife, it is impurity: he hath uncovered his brother’s nakedness; they shall be childless.
Ye shall therefore keep all my statutes, and all mine ordinances, and do them; that the land, hither I bring you to dell therein, vomit you not out.
And ye shall not alk in the customs of the nation, hich I cast out before you: for they did all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.
But I have said unto you, Ye shall inherit their land, and I ill give it unto you to possess it, a land floing ith milk and honey: I am Jehovah your God, ho hath separated you from the peoples.

Ye shall therefore make a distinction beteen the clean beast and the unclean, and beteen the unclean fol and the clean: and ye shall not make your souls abominable by beast, or by bird, or by anything hereith the ground teemeth, hich I have separated from you as unclean.
And ye shall be holy unto me: for I, Jehovah, am holy, and have set you apart from the peoples, that ye should be mine.
A man also or a oman that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a izard, shall surely be put to death: they shall stone them ith stones; their blood shall be upon them.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Speak unto the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say unto them, There shall none defile himself for the dead among his people;
except for his kin, that is near unto him, for his mother, and for his father, and for his son, and for his daughter, and for his brother,
and for his sister a virgin, that is near unto him, that hath had no husband; for her may he defile himself.
He shall not defile himself, \add being\add* a chief man among his people, to profane himself.
They shall not make baldness upon their head, neither shall they shave off the corner of their beard, nor make any cuttings in their flesh.
They shall be holy unto their God, and not profane the name of their God; for the offerings of Jehovah made by fire, the bread of their God, they do offer: therefore they shall be holy.
They shall not take a oman that is a harlot, or profane; neither shall they take a oman put aay from her husband: for he is holy unto his God.
Thou shalt sanctify him therefore; for he offereth the bread of thy God: he shall be holy unto thee; for I Jehovah, ho sanctify you, am holy.
And the daughter of any priest, if she profane herself by playing the harlot, she profaneth her father: she shall be burnt ith fire.

And he that is the high priest among his brethren, upon hose head the anointing oil is poured, and that is consecrated to put on the garments, shall not let the hair of his head go loose, nor rend his clothes;
neither shall he go in to any dead body, nor defile himself for his father, or for his mother;
neither shall he go out of the sanctuary, nor profane the sanctuary of his God; for the cron of the anointing oil of his God is upon him: I am Jehovah.
And he shall take a ife in her virginity.
A ido, or one divorced, or a profane oman, a harlot, these shall he not take: but a virgin of his on people shall he take to ife.
And he shall not profane his seed among his people: for I am Jehovah ho sanctifieth him.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto Aaron, saying, Whosoever he be of thy seed throughout their generations that hath a blemish, let him not approach to offer the bread of his God.
For hatsoever man he be that hath a blemish, he shall not approach: a blind man, or a lame, or he that hath a flat nose, or anything superfluous,
or a man that is broken-footed, or broken-handed,
or crook-backed, or a darf, or that hath a blemish in his eye, or is scurvy, or scabbed, or hath his stones broken;
no man of the seed of Aaron the priest, that hath a blemish, shall come nigh to offer the offerings of Jehovah made by fire: he hath a blemish; he shall not come nigh to offer the bread of his God.
He shall eat the bread of his God, both of the most holy, and of the holy:
only he shall not go in unto the veil, nor come nigh unto the altar, because he hath a blemish; that he profane not my sanctuaries: for I am Jehovah ho sanctifieth them.
So Moses spake unto Aaron, and to his sons, and unto all the children of Israel.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto Aaron and to his sons, that they separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Israel, hich they hallo unto me, and that they profane not my holy name: I am Jehovah.

Say unto them, Whosoever he be of all your seed throughout your generations, that approacheth unto the holy things, hich the children of Israel hallo unto Jehovah, having his uncleanness upon him, that soul shall be cut off from before me: I am Jehovah.

What man soever of the seed of Aaron is a leper, or hath an issue; he shall not eat of the holy things, until he be clean. And hoso toucheth anything that is unclean by the dead, or a man hose seed goeth from him;
or hosoever toucheth any creeping thing, hereby he may be made unclean, or a man of hom he may take uncleanness, hatsoever uncleanness he hath;
the soul that toucheth any such shall be unclean until the even, and shall not eat of the holy things, unless he bathe his flesh in ater.
And hen the sun is don, he shall be clean; and afterard he shall eat of the holy things, because it is his bread.
That hich dieth of itself, or is torn of beasts, he shall not eat, to defile himself thereith: I am Jehovah.
They shall therefore keep my charge, lest they bear sin for it, and die therein, if they profane it: I am Jehovah ho sanctifieth them.
There shall no stranger eat of the holy thing: a sojourner of the priest’s, or a hired servant, shall not eat of the holy thing.
But if a priest buy any soul, the purchase of his money, he shall eat of it; and such as are born in his house, they shall eat of his bread.
And if a priest’s daughter be married unto a stranger, she shall not eat of the heave-offering of the holy things.

But if a priest’s daughter be a ido, or divorced, and have no child, and be returned unto her father’s house, as in her youth, she shall eat of her father’s bread: but there shall no stranger eat thereof.
And if a man eat of the holy thing unittingly, then he shall put the fifth part thereof unto it, and shall give unto the priest the holy thing.
And they shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, hich they offer unto Jehovah,
and \add so\add* cause them to bear the iniquity that bringeth guilt, hen they eat their holy things: for I am Jehovah ho sanctifieth them.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

Speak unto Aaron, and to his sons, and unto all the children of Israel, and say unto them, Whosoever he be of the house of Israel, or of the sojourners in Israel, that offereth his oblation, hether it be any of their vos, or any of their freeill-offerings, hich they offer unto Jehovah for a burnt-offering;
that ye may be accepted, \add ye shall offer\add* a male ithout blemish, of the bullocks, of the sheep, or of the goats.
But hatsoever hath a blemish, that shall ye not offer: for it shall not be acceptable for you.

And hosoever offereth a sacrifice of peace-offerings unto Jehovah to accomplish a vo, or for a freeill-offering, of the herd or of the flock, it shall be perfect to be accepted; there shall be no blemish therein.
Blind, or broken, or maimed, or having a en, or scurvy, or scabbed, ye shall not offer these unto Jehovah, nor make an offering by fire of them upon the altar unto Jehovah.
Either a bullock or a lamb that hath anything superfluous or lacking in his parts, that mayest thou offer for a freeill-offering; but for a vo it shall not be accepted.
That hich hath its stones bruised, or crushed, or broken, or cut, ye shall not offer unto Jehovah; neither shall ye do \add thus\add* in your land.
Neither from the hand of a foreigner shall ye offer the bread of your God of any of these; because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them: they shall not be accepted for you.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

When a bullock, or a sheep, or a goat, is brought forth, then it shall be seven days under the dam; and from the eighth day and thenceforth it shall be accepted for the oblation of an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
And hether it be co or ee, ye shall not kill it and its young both in one day.
And hen ye sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving unto Jehovah, ye shall sacrifice it that ye may be accepted.
On the same day it shall be eaten; ye shall leave none of it until the morning: I am Jehovah.
Therefore shall ye keep my commandments, and do them: I am Jehovah.
And ye shall not profane my holy name; but I ill be halloed among the children of Israel: I am Jehovah ho halloeth you,
ho brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am Jehovah.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, The set feasts of Jehovah, hich ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my set feasts.
Six days shall ork be done: but on the seventh day is a sabbath of solemn rest, a holy convocation; ye shall do no manner of ork: it is a sabbath unto Jehovah in all your dellings.
These are the set feasts of Jehovah, even holy convocations, hich ye shall proclaim in their appointed season.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at even, is Jehovah’s passover.
And on the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread unto Jehovah: seven days ye shall eat unleavened bread.
In the first day ye shall have a holy convocation: ye shall do no servile ork.
But ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto Jehovah seven days: in the seventh day is a holy convocation; ye shall do no servile ork.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye are come into the land hich I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring the sheaf of the first-fruits of your harvest unto the priest:
and he shall ave the sheaf before Jehovah, to be accepted for you: on the morro after the sabbath the priest shall ave it.
And in the day hen ye ave the sheaf, ye shall offer a he-lamb ithout blemish a year old for a burnt-offering unto Jehovah.

And the meal-offering thereof shall be to tenth parts \add of an ephah\add* of fine flour mingled ith oil, an offering made by fire unto Jehovah for a seet savor; and the drink-offering thereof shall be of ine, the fourth part of a hin.

And ye shall eat neither bread, nor parched grain, nor fresh ears, until this selfsame day, until ye have brought the oblation of your God: it is a statute for ever throughout your generations in all your dellings.
And ye shall count unto you from the morro after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the ave-offering; seven sabbaths shall there be complete:
even unto the morro after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days; and ye shall offer a ne meal-offering unto Jehovah.
Ye shall bring out of your habitations to ave-loaves of to tenth parts \add of an ephah\add*: they shall be of fine flour, they shall be baken ith leaven, for first-fruits unto Jehovah.

And ye shall present ith the bread seven lambs ithout blemish a year old, and one young bullock, and to rams: they shall be a burnt-offering unto Jehovah, ith their meal-offering, and their drink-offerings, even an offering made by fire, of a seet savor unto Jehovah.
And ye shall offer one he-goat for a sin-offering, and to he-lambs a year old for a sacrifice of peace-offerings.
And the priest shall ave them ith the bread of the first-fruits for a ave-offering before Jehovah, ith the to lambs: they shall be holy to Jehovah for the priest.
And ye shall make proclamation on the selfsame day; there shall be a holy convocation unto you; ye shall do no servile ork: it is a statute for ever in all your dellings throughout your generations.

And hen ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not holly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleaning of thy harvest: thou shalt leave them for the poor, and for the sojourner: I am Jehovah your God.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, shall be a solemn rest unto you, a memorial of bloing of trumpets, a holy convocation.
Ye shall do no servile ork; and ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

Hobeit on the tenth day of this seventh month is the day of atonement: it shall be a holy convocation unto you, and ye shall afflict your souls; and ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
And ye shall do no manner of ork in that same day; for it is a day of atonement, to make atonement for you before Jehovah your God.
For hatsoever soul it be that shall not be afflicted in that same day; he shall be cut off from his people.
And hatsoever soul it be that doeth any manner of ork in that same day, that soul ill I destroy from among his people.
Ye shall do no manner of ork: it is a statute for ever throughout your generations in all your dellings.
It shall be unto you a sabbath of solemn rest, and ye shall afflict your souls: in the ninth day of the month at even, from even unto even, shall ye keep your sabbath.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto Jehovah.
On the first day shall be a holy convocation: ye shall do no servile ork.

Seven days ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto Jehovah: on the eighth day shall be a holy convocation unto you; and ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto Jehovah: it is a solemn assembly; ye shall do no servile ork.

These are the set feasts of Jehovah, hich ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, to offer an offering made by fire unto Jehovah, a burnt-offering, and a meal-offering, a sacrifice, and drink-offerings, each on its on day;
besides the sabbaths of Jehovah, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vos, and besides all your freeill-offerings, hich ye give unto Jehovah.

Hobeit on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, hen ye have gathered in the fruits of the land, ye shall keep the feast of Jehovah seven days: on the first day shall be a solemn rest, and on the eighth day shall be a solemn rest.
And ye shall take you on the first day the fruit of goodly trees, branches of palm-trees, and boughs of thick trees, and illos of the brook; and ye shall rejoice before Jehovah your God seven days.
And ye shall keep it a feast unto Jehovah seven days in the year: it is a statute for ever throughout your generations; ye shall keep it in the seventh month.
Ye shall dell in booths seven days; all that are home-born in Israel shall dell in booths;
that your generations may kno that I made the children of Israel to dell in booths, hen I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am Jehovah your God.
And Moses declared unto the children of Israel the set feasts of Jehovah.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.
Without the veil of the testimony, in the tent of meeting, shall Aaron keep it in order from evening to morning before Jehovah continually: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations.
He shall keep in order the lamps upon the pure candlestick before Jehovah continually.
And thou shalt take fine flour, and bake telve cakes thereof: to tenth parts \add of an ephah\add* shall be in one cake.
And thou shalt set them in to ros, six on a ro, upon the pure table before Jehovah.
And thou shalt put pure frankincense upon each ro, that it may be to the bread for a memorial, even an offering made by fire unto Jehovah.
Every sabbath day he shall set it in order before Jehovah continually; it is on the behalf of the children of Israel, an everlasting covenant.
And it shall be for Aaron and his sons; and they shall eat it in a holy place: for it is most holy unto him of the offerings of Jehovah made by fire by a perpetual statute.
And the son of an Israelitish oman, hose father as an Egyptian, ent out among the children of Israel; and the son of the Israelitish oman and a man of Israel strove together in the camp:
and the son of the Israelitish oman blasphemed the Name, and cursed; and they brought him unto Moses. And his mother’s name as Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
And they put him in ard, that it might be declared unto them at the mouth of Jehovah.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Bring forth him that hath cursed ithout the camp; and let all that heard him lay their hands upon his head, and let all the congregation stone him.
And thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, Whosoever curseth his God shall bear his sin.

And he that blasphemeth the name of Jehovah, he shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall certainly stone him: as ell the sojourner, as the home-born, hen he blasphemeth the name \add of Jehovah\add*, shall be put to death.
And he that smiteth any man mortally shall surely be put to death.
And he that smiteth a beast mortally shall make it good, life for life.
And if a man cause a blemish in his neighbor; as he hath done, so shall it be done to him:
breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he hath caused a blemish in a man, so shall it be rendered unto him.
And he that killeth a beast shall make it good: and he that killeth a man shall be put to death.
Ye shall have one manner of la, as ell for the sojourner, as for the home-born: for I am Jehovah your God.
And Moses spake to the children of Israel; and they brought forth him that had cursed out of the camp, and stoned him ith stones. And the children of Israel did as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses in mount Sinai, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye come into the land hich I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto Jehovah.
Six years thou shalt so thy field, and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and gather in the fruits thereof;
but in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of solemn rest for the land, a sabbath unto Jehovah: thou shalt neither so thy field, nor prune thy vineyard.
That hich groeth of itself of thy harvest thou shalt not reap, and the grapes of thy undressed vine thou shalt not gather: it shall be a year of solemn rest for the land.
And the sabbath of the land shall be for food for you; for thee, and for thy servant and for thy maid, and for thy hired servant and for thy stranger, ho sojourn ith thee.
And for thy cattle, and for the beasts that are in thy land, shall all the increase thereof be for food.
And thou shalt number seven sabbaths of years unto thee, seven times seven years; and there shall be unto thee the days of seven sabbaths of years, even forty and nine years.
Then shalt thou send abroad the loud trumpet on the tenth day of the seventh month; in the day of atonement shall ye send abroad the trumpet throughout all your land.

And ye shall hallo the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubilee unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and ye shall return every man unto his family.
A jubilee shall that fiftieth year be unto you: ye shall not so, neither reap that hich groeth of itself in it, nor gather \add the grapes\add* in it of the undressed vines.
For it is a jubilee; it shall be holy unto you: ye shall eat the increase thereof out of the field.
In this year of jubilee ye shall return every man unto his possession.
And if thou sell aught unto thy neighbor, or buy of thy neighbor’s hand, ye shall not rong one another.
According to the number of years after the jubilee thou shalt buy of thy neighbor, \add and\add* according unto the number of years of the crops he shall sell unto thee.

According to the multitude of the years thou shalt increase the price thereof, and according to the feness of the years thou shalt diminish the price of it; for the number of the crops doth he sell unto thee.
And ye shall not rong one another; but thou shalt fear thy God: for I am Jehovah your God.
Wherefore ye shall do my statutes, and keep mine ordinances and do them; and ye shall dell in the land in safety.
And the land shall yield its fruit, and ye shall eat your fill, and dell therein in safety.
And if ye shall say, What shall e eat the seventh year? behold, e shall not so, nor gather in our increase;
then I ill command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for the three years.
And ye shall so the eighth year, and eat of the fruits, the old store; until the ninth year, until its fruits come in, ye shall eat the old store.
And the land shall not be sold in perpetuity; for the land is mine: for ye are strangers and sojourners ith me.
And in all the land of your possession ye shall grant a redemption for the land.
If thy brother be axed poor, and sell some of his possession, then shall his kinsman that is next unto him come, and shall redeem that hich his brother hath sold.
And if a man have no one to redeem it, and he be axed rich and find sufficient to redeem it;
then let him reckon the years of the sale thereof, and restore the overplus unto the man to hom he sold it; and he shall return unto his possession.

But if he be not able to get it back for himself, then that hich he hath sold shall remain in the hand of him that hath bought it until the year of jubilee: and in the jubilee it shall go out, and he shall return unto his possession.
And if a man sell a delling-house in a alled city, then he may redeem it ithin a hole year after it is sold; for a full year shall he have the right of redemption.

And if it be not redeemed ithin the space of a full year, then the house that is in the alled city shall be made sure in perpetuity to him that bought it, throughout his generations: it shall not go out in the jubilee.
But the houses of the villages hich have no all round about them shall be reckoned ith the fields of the country: they may be redeemed, and they shall go out in the jubilee.
Nevertheless the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, may the Levites redeem at any time.

And if one of the Levites redeem, then the house that as sold, and the city of his possession, shall go out in the jubilee; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel.
But the field of the suburbs of their cities may not be sold; for it is their perpetual possession.
And if thy brother be axed poor, and his hand fail ith thee; then thou shalt uphold him: \add as\add* a stranger and a sojourner shall he live ith thee.
Take thou no interest of him or increase, but fear thy God; that thy brother may live ith thee.
Thou shalt not give him thy money upon interest, nor give him thy victuals for increase.
I am Jehovah your God, ho brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, \add and\add* to be your God.
And if thy brother be axed poor ith thee, and sell himself unto thee; thou shalt not make him to serve as a bondservant.
As a hired servant, and as a sojourner, he shall be ith thee; he shall serve ith thee unto the year of jubilee:
then shall he go out from thee, he and his children ith him, and shall return unto his on family, and unto the possession of his fathers shall he return.
For they are my servants, hom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as bondmen.
Thou shalt not rule over him ith rigor, but shalt fear thy God.
And as for thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, hom thou shalt have; of the nations that are round about you, of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.

Moreover of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are ith you, hich they have begotten in your land: and they shall be your possession.

And ye shall make them an inheritance for your children after you, to hold for a possession; of them shall ye take your bondmen for ever: but over your brethren the children of Israel ye shall not rule, one over another, ith rigor.

And if a stranger or sojourner ith thee be axed rich, and thy brother be axed poor beside him, and sell himself unto the stranger \add or\add* sojourner ith thee, or to the stock of the stranger’s family;
after that he is sold he may be redeemed: one of his brethren may redeem him;
or his uncle, or his uncle’s son, may redeem him, or any that is nigh of kin unto him of his family may redeem him; or if he be axed rich, he may redeem himself.

And he shall reckon ith him that bought him from the year that he sold himself to him unto the year of jubilee: and the price of his sale shall be according unto the number of years; according to the time of a hired servant shall he be ith him.
If there be yet many years, according unto them he shall give back the price of his redemption out of the money that he as bought for.
And if there remain but fe years unto the year of jubilee, then he shall reckon ith him; according unto his years shall he give back the price of his redemption.
As a servant hired year by year shall he be ith him: he shall not rule ith rigor over him in thy sight.
And if he be not redeemed by these \add means\add*, then he shall go out in the year of jubilee, he, and his children ith him.
For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants hom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am Jehovah your God.
Ye shall make you no idols, neither shall ye rear you up a graven image, or a pillar, neither shall ye place any figured stone in your land, to bo don unto it: for I am Jehovah your God.
Ye shall keep my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary: I am Jehovah.
If ye alk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them;
then I ill give your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit.
And your threshing shall reach unto the vintage, and the vintage shall reach unto the soing time; and ye shall eat your bread to the full, and dell in your land safely.
And I ill give peace in the land, and ye shall lie don, and none shall make you afraid: and I ill cause evil beasts to cease out of the land, neither shall the sord go through your land.
And ye shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sord.
And five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall chase ten thousand; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sord.
And I ill have respect unto you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, and ill establish my covenant ith you.
And ye shall eat old store long kept, and ye shall bring forth the old because of the ne.
And I ill set my tabernacle among you: and my soul shall not abhor you.
And I ill alk among you, and ill be your God, and ye shall be my people.
I am Jehovah your God, ho brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, that ye should not be their bondmen; and I have broken the bars of your yoke, and made you go upright.
But if ye ill not hearken unto me, and ill not do all these commandments;
and if ye shall reject my statutes, and if your soul abhor mine ordinances, so that ye ill not do all my commandments, but break my covenant;

I also ill do this unto you: I ill appoint terror over you, even consumption and fever, that shall consume the eyes, and make the soul to pine aay; and ye shall so your seed in vain, for your enemies shall eat it.
And I ill set my face against you, and ye shall be smitten before your enemies: they that hate you shall rule over you; and ye shall flee hen none pursueth you.
And if ye ill not yet for these things hearken unto me, then I ill chastise you seven times more for your sins.
And I ill break the pride of your poer: and I ill make your heaven as iron, and your earth as brass;
and your strength shall be spent in vain; for your land shall not yield its increase, neither shall the trees of the land yield their fruit.
And if ye alk contrary unto me, and ill not hearken unto me, I ill bring seven times more plagues upon you according to your sins.
And I ill send the beast of the field among you, hich shall rob you of your children, and destroy your cattle, and make you fe in number; and your ays shall become desolate.
And if by these things ye ill not be reformed unto me, but ill alk contrary unto me;
then ill I also alk contrary unto you; and I ill smite you, even I, seven times for your sins.

And I ill bring a sord upon you, that shall execute the vengeance of the covenant; and ye shall be gathered together ithin your cities: and I ill send the pestilence among you; and ye shall be delivered into the hand of the enemy.
When I break your staff of bread, ten omen shall bake your bread in one oven, and they shall deliver your bread again by eight: and ye shall eat, and not be satisfied.
And if ye ill not for all this hearken unto me, but alk contrary unto me;
then I ill alk contrary unto you in rath; and I also ill chastise you seven times for your sins.
And ye shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters shall ye eat.
And I ill destroy your high places, and cut don your sun-images, and cast your dead bodies upon the bodies of your idols; and my soul shall abhor you.
And I ill make your cities a aste, and ill bring your sanctuaries unto desolation, and I ill not smell the savor of your seet odors.
And I ill bring the land into desolation; and your enemies that dell therein shall be astonished at it.
And you ill I scatter among the nations, and I ill dra out the sord after you: and your land shall be a desolation, and your cities shall be a aste.
Then shall the land enjoy its sabbaths, as long as it lieth desolate, and ye are in your enemies’ land; even then shall the land rest, and enjoy its sabbaths.
As long as it lieth desolate it shall have rest, even the rest hich it had not in your sabbaths, hen ye delt upon it.

And as for them that are left of you, I ill send a faintness into their heart in the lands of their enemies: and the sound of a driven leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as one fleeth from the sord; and they shall fall hen none pursueth.
And they shall stumble one upon another, as it ere before the sord, hen none pursueth: and ye shall have no poer to stand before your enemies.
And ye shall perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies shall eat you up.
And they that are left of you shall pine aay in their iniquity in your enemies’ lands; and also in the iniquities of their fathers shall they pine aay ith them.
And they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers, in their trespass hich they trespassed against me, and also that, because they alked contrary unto me,
I also alked contrary unto them, and brought them into the land of their enemies: if then their uncircumcised heart be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity;
then ill I remember my covenant ith Jacob; and also my covenant ith Isaac, and also my covenant ith Abraham ill I remember; and I ill remember the land.

The land also shall be left by them, and shall enjoy its sabbaths, hile it lieth desolate ithout them: and they shall accept of the punishment of their iniquity; because, even because they rejected mine ordinances, and their soul abhorred my statutes.

And yet for all that, hen they are in the land of their enemies, I ill not reject them, neither ill I abhor them, to destroy them utterly, and to break my covenant ith them; for I am Jehovah their God;
but I ill for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors, hom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God: I am Jehovah.
These are the statutes and ordinances and las, hich Jehovah made beteen him and the children of Israel in mount Sinai by Moses.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When a man shall accomplish a vo, the persons shall be for Jehovah by thy estimation.
And thy estimation shall be of the male from tenty years old even unto sixty years old, even thy estimation shall be fifty shekels of silver, after the shekel of the sanctuary.
And if it be a female, then thy estimation shall be thirty shekels.
And if it be from five years old even unto tenty years old, then thy estimation shall be of the male tenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
And if it be from a month old even unto five years old, then thy estimation shall be of the male five shekels of silver, and for the female thy estimation shall be three shekels of silver.
And if it be from sixty years old and upard; if it be a male, then thy estimation shall be fifteen shekels, and for the female ten shekels.
But if he be poorer than thy estimation, then he shall be set before the priest, and the priest shall value him; according to the ability of him that voed shall the priest value him.
And if it be a beast, hereof men offer an oblation unto Jehovah, all that any man giveth of such unto Jehovah shall be holy.
He shall not alter it, nor change it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good: and if he shall at all change beast for beast, then both it and that for hich it is changed shall be holy.
And if it be any unclean beast, of hich they do not offer an oblation unto Jehovah, then he shall set the beast before the priest;
and the priest shall value it, hether it be good or bad: as thou the priest valuest it, so shall it be.
But if he ill indeed redeem it, then he shall add the fifth part thereof unto thy estimation.
And hen a man shall sanctify his house to be holy unto Jehovah, then the priest shall estimate it, hether it be good or bad: as the priest shall estimate it, so shall it stand.
And if he that sanctified it ill redeem his house, then he shall add the fifth part of the money of thy estimation unto it, and it shall be his.

And if a man shall sanctify unto Jehovah part of the field of his possession, then thy estimation shall be according to the soing thereof: the soing of a homer of barley \add shall be valued\add* at fifty shekels of silver.
If he sanctify his field from the year of jubilee, according to thy estimation it shall stand.

But if he sanctify his field after the jubilee, then the priest shall reckon unto him the money according to the years that remain unto the year of jubilee; and an abatement shall be made from thy estimation.
And if he that sanctified the field ill indeed redeem it, then he shall add the fifth part of the money of thy estimation unto it, and it shall be assured to him.
And if he ill not redeem the field, or if he have sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed any more:
but the field, hen it goeth out in the jubilee, shall be holy unto Jehovah, as a field devoted; the possession thereof shall be the priest’s.
And if he sanctify unto Jehovah a field hich he hath bought, hich is not of the field of his possession;
then the priest shall reckon unto him the orth of thy estimation unto the year of jubilee: and he shall give thine estimation in that day, as a holy thing unto Jehovah.
In the year of jubilee the field shall return unto him of hom it as bought, even to him to hom the possession of the land belongeth.
And all thy estimations shall be according to the shekel of the sanctuary: tenty gerahs shall be the shekel.
Only the firstling among beasts, hich is made a firstling to Jehovah, no man shall sanctify it; hether it be ox or sheep, it is Jehovah’s.

And if it be of an unclean beast, then he shall ransom it according to thine estimation, and shall add unto it the fifth part thereof: or if it be not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to thy estimation.

Notithstanding, no devoted thing, that a man shall devote unto Jehovah of all that he hath, hether of man or beast, or of the field of his possession, shall be sold or redeemed: every devoted thing is most holy unto Jehovah.
No one devoted, that shall be devoted from among men, shall be ransomed; he shall surely be put to death.
And all the tithe of the land, hether of the seed of the land, or of the fruit of the tree, is Jehovah’s: it is holy unto Jehovah.
And if a man ill redeem aught of his tithe, he shall add unto it the fifth part thereof.
And all the tithe of the herd or the flock, hatsoever passeth under the rod, the tenth shall be holy unto Jehovah.
He shall not search hether it be good or bad, neither shall he change it: and if he change it at all, then both it and that for hich it is changed shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed.
These are the commandments, hich Jehovah commanded Moses for the children of Israel in mount Sinai.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses in the ilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they ere come out of the land of Egypt, saying,
Take ye the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, every male, by their polls;
from tenty years old and upard, all that are able to go forth to ar in Israel, thou and Aaron shall number them by their hosts.
And ith you there shall be a man of every tribe; every one head of his fathers’ house.
And these are the names of the men that shall stand ith you. Of Reuben: Elizur the son of Shedeur.
Of Simeon: Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
Of Judah: Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
Of Issachar: Nethanel the son of Zuar.
Of Zebulun: Eliab the son of Helon.
Of the children of Joseph: Of Ephraim: Elishama the son of Ammihud. Of Manasseh: Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
Of Benjamin: Abidan the son of Gideoni.
Of Dan: Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
Of Asher: Pagiel the son of Ochran.
Of Gad: Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
Of Naphtali: Ahira the son of Enan.
These are they that ere called of the congregation, the princes of the tribes of their fathers; they ere the heads of the thousands of Israel.
And Moses and Aaron took these men that are mentioned by name:

and they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month; and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from tenty years old and upard, by their polls.
As Jehovah commanded Moses, so he numbered them in the ilderness of Sinai.

And the children of Reuben, Israel’s first-born, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, by their polls, every male from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Reuben, ere forty and six thousand and five hundred.

Of the children of Simeon, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, those that ere numbered thereof, according to the number of the names, by their polls, every male from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Simeon, ere fifty and nine thousand and three hundred.
Of the children of Gad, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Gad, ere forty and five thousand six hundred and fifty.
Of the children of Judah, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Judah, ere threescore and fourteen thousand and six hundred.
Of the children of Issachar, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Issachar, ere fifty and four thousand and four hundred.
Of the children of Zebulun, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Zebulun, ere fifty and seven thousand and four hundred.

Of the children of Joseph, \add namely\add*, of the children of Ephraim, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Ephraim, ere forty thousand and five hundred.
Of the children of Manasseh, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Manasseh, ere thirty and to thousand and to hundred.
Of the children of Benjamin, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Benjamin, ere thirty and five thousand and four hundred.
Of the children of Dan, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Dan, ere threescore and to thousand and seven hundred.
Of the children of Asher, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Asher, ere forty and one thousand and five hundred.
Of the children of Naphtali, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar;
those that ere numbered of them, of the tribe of Naphtali, ere fifty and three thousand and four hundred.
These are they that ere numbered, hom Moses and Aaron numbered, and the princes of Israel, being telve men: they ere each one for his fathers’ house.
So all they that ere numbered of the children of Israel by their fathers’ houses, from tenty years old and upard, all that ere able to go forth to ar in Israel;
even all they that ere numbered ere six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty.
But the Levites after the tribe of their fathers ere not numbered among them.
For Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Only the tribe of Levi thou shalt not number, neither shalt thou take the sum of them among the children of Israel;

but appoint thou the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony, and over all the furniture thereof, and over all that belongeth to it: they shall bear the tabernacle, and all the furniture thereof; and they shall minister unto it, and shall encamp round about the tabernacle.
And hen the tabernacle setteth forard, the Levites shall take it don; and hen the tabernacle is to be pitched, the Levites shall set it up: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.
And the children of Israel shall pitch their tents, every man by his on camp, and every man by his on standard, according to their hosts.

But the Levites shall encamp round about the tabernacle of the testimony, that there be no rath upon the congregation of the children of Israel: and the Levites shall keep the charge of the tabernacle of the testimony.
Thus did the children of Israel; according to all that Jehovah commanded Moses, so did they.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,
The children of Israel shall encamp every man by his on standard, ith the ensigns of their fathers’ houses: over against the tent of meeting shall they encamp round about.

And those that encamp on the east side toard the sunrising shall be they of the standard of the camp of Judah, according to their hosts: and the prince of the children of Judah shall be Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
And his host, and those that ere numbered of them, ere threescore and fourteen thousand and six hundred.
And those that encamp next unto him shall be the tribe of Issachar: and the prince of the children of Issachar shall be Nethanel the son of Zuar.
And his host, and those that ere numbered thereof, ere fifty and four thousand and four hundred.
\add And\add* the tribe of Zebulun: and the prince of the children of Zebulun shall be Eliab the son of Helon.
And his host, and those that ere numbered thereof, ere fifty and seven thousand and four hundred.
All that ere numbered of the camp of Judah ere a hundred thousand and fourscore thousand and six thousand and four hundred, according to their hosts. They shall set forth first.
On the south side shall be the standard of the camp of Reuben according to their hosts: and the prince of the children of Reuben shall be Elizur the son of Shedeur.
And his host, and those that ere numbered thereof, ere forty and six thousand and five hundred.
And those that encamp next unto him shall be the tribe of Simeon: and the prince of the children of Simeon shall be Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
And his host, and those that ere numbered of them, ere fifty and nine thousand and three hundred.
And the tribe of Gad: and the prince of the children of Gad shall be Eliasaph the son of Reuel.
And his host, and those that ere numbered of them, ere forty and five thousand and six hundred and fifty.
All that ere numbered of the camp of Reuben ere a hundred thousand and fifty and one thousand and four hundred and fifty, according to their hosts. And they shall set forth second.
Then the tent of meeting shall set forard, ith the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camps: as they encamp, so shall they set forard, every man in his place, by their standards.
On the est side shall be the standard of the camp of Ephraim according to their hosts: and the prince of the children of Ephraim shall be Elishama the son of Ammihud.
And his host, and those that ere numbered of them, ere forty thousand and five hundred.
And next unto him shall be the tribe of Manasseh: and the prince of the children of Manasseh shall be Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
And his host, and those that ere numbered of them, ere thirty and to thousand and to hundred.
And the tribe of Benjamin: and the prince of the children of Benjamin shall be Abidan the son of Gideoni.
And his host, and those that ere numbered of them, ere thirty and five thousand and four hundred.
All that ere numbered of the camp of Ephraim ere a hundred thousand and eight thousand and a hundred, according to their hosts. And they shall set forth third.
On the north side shall be the standard of the camp of Dan according to their hosts: and the prince of the children of Dan shall be Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
And his host, and those that ere numbered of them, ere threescore and to thousand and seven hundred.
And those that encamp next unto him shall be the tribe of Asher: and the prince of the children of Asher shall be Pagiel the son of Ochran.
And his hosts, and those that ere numbered of them, ere forty and one thousand and five hundred.
And the tribe of Naphtali: and the prince of the children of Naphtali shall be Ahira the son of Enan.
And his host, and those that ere numbered of them, ere fifty and three thousand and four hundred.
All that ere numbered of the camp of Dan ere a hundred thousand and fifty and seven thousand and six hundred. They shall set forth hindmost by their standards.

These are they that ere numbered of the children of Israel by their fathers’ houses: all that ere numbered of the camps according to their hosts ere six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty.
But the Levites ere not numbered among the children of Israel; as Jehovah commanded Moses.

Thus did the children of Israel; according to all that Jehovah commanded Moses, so they encamped by their standards, and so they set forard, every one by their families, according to their fathers’ houses.
No these are the generations of Aaron and Moses in the day that Jehovah spake ith Moses in mount Sinai.
And these are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the first-born, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the priests that ere anointed, hom he consecrated to minister in the priest’s office.

And Nadab and Abihu died before Jehovah, hen they offered strange fire before Jehovah, in the ilderness of Sinai, and they had no children; and Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest’s office in the presence of Aaron their father.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Bring the tribe of Levi near, and set them before Aaron the priest, that they may minister unto him.
And they shall keep his charge, and the charge of the hole congregation before the tent of meeting, to do the service of the tabernacle.
And they shall keep all the furniture of the tent of meeting, and the charge of the children of Israel, to do the service of the tabernacle.
And thou shalt give the Levites unto Aaron and to his sons: they are holly given unto him on the behalf of the children of Israel.
And thou shalt appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall keep their priesthood: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the first-born that openeth the omb among the children of Israel; and the Levites shall be mine:
for all the first-born are mine; on the day that I smote all the first-born in the land of Egypt I halloed unto me all the first-born in Israel, both man and beast; mine they shall be: I am Jehovah.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses in the ilderness of Sinai, saying,
Number the children of Levi by their fathers’ houses, by their families: every male from a month old and upard shalt thou number them.
And Moses numbered them according to the ord of Jehovah, as he as commanded.
And these ere the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari.
And these are the names of the sons of Gershon by their families: Libni and Shimei.
And the sons of Kohath by their families: Amram, and Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
And the sons of Merari by their families: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their fathers’ houses.
Of Gershon as the family of the Libnites, and the family of the Shimeites: these are the families of the Gershonites.
Those that ere numbered of them, according to the number of all the males, from a month old and upard, even those that ere numbered of them ere seven thousand and five hundred.
The families of the Gershonites shall encamp behind the tabernacle estard.
And the prince of the fathers’ house of the Gershonites shall be Eliasaph the son of Lael.
And the charge of the sons of Gershon in the tent of meeting shall be the tabernacle, and the Tent, the covering thereof, and the screen for the door of the tent of meeting,
and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the door of the court, hich is by the tabernacle, and by the altar round about, and the cords of it for all the service thereof.
And of Kohath as the family of the Amramites, and the family of the Izharites, and the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites: these are the families of the Kohathites.
According to the number of all the males, from a month old and upard, there ere eight thousand and six hundred, keeping the charge of the sanctuary.
The families of the sons of Kohath shall encamp on the side of the tabernacle southard.
And the prince of the fathers’ house of the families of the Kohathites shall be Elizaphan the son of Uzziel.
And their charge shall be the ark, and the table, and the candlestick, and the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary hereith they minister, and the screen, and all the service thereof.
And Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest shall be prince of the princes of the Levites, \add and have\add* the oversight of them that keep the charge of the sanctuary.
Of Merari as the family of the Mahlites, and the family of the Mushites: these are the families of Merari.
And those that ere numbered of them, according to the number of all the males, from a month old and upard, ere six thousand and to hundred.
And the prince of the fathers’ house of the families of Merari as Zuriel the son of Abihail: they shall encamp on the side of the tabernacle northard.

And the appointed charge of the sons of Merari shall be the boards of the tabernacle, and the bars thereof, and the pillars thereof, and the sockets thereof, and all the instruments thereof, and all the service thereof,
and the pillars of the court round about, and their sockets, and their pins, and their cords.

And those that encamp before the tabernacle eastard, before the tent of meeting toard the sunrising, shall be Moses, and Aaron and his sons, keeping the charge of the sanctuary for the charge of the children of Israel; and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.
All that ere numbered of the Levites, hom Moses and Aaron numbered at the commandment of Jehovah, by their families, all the males from a month old and upard, ere tenty and to thousand.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Number all the first-born males of the children of Israel from a month old and upard, and take the number of their names.

And thou shalt take the Levites for me ( I am Jehovah) instead of all the first-born among the children of Israel; and the cattle of the Levites instead of all the firstlings among the cattle of the children of Israel.
And Moses numbered, as Jehovah commanded him, all the first-born among the children of Israel.
And all the first-born males according to the number of names, from a month old and upard, of those that ere numbered of them, ere tenty and to thousand to hundred and threescore and thirteen.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Take the Levites instead of all the first-born among the children of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of their cattle; and the Levites shall be mine: I am Jehovah.
And for the redemption of the to hundred and threescore and thirteen of the first-born of the children of Israel, that are over and above \add the number of\add* the Levites,
thou shalt take five shekels apiece by the poll; after the shekel of the sanctuary shalt thou take them ( the shekel is tenty gerahs):
and thou shalt give the money, hereith the odd number of them is redeemed, unto Aaron and to his sons.
And Moses took the redemption-money from them that ere over and above them that ere redeemed by the Levites;
from the first-born of the children of Israel took he the money, a thousand three hundred and threescore and five \add shekels\add*, after the shekel of the sanctuary:
and Moses gave the redemption-money unto Aaron and to his sons, according to the ord of Jehovah, as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,
Take the sum of the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, by their families, by their fathers’ houses,
from thirty years old and upard even until fifty years old, all that enter upon the service, to do the ork in the tent of meeting.
This is the service of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting, \add about\add* the most holy things:
hen the camp setteth forard, Aaron shall go in, and his sons, and they shall take don the veil of the screen, and cover the ark of the testimony ith it,
and shall put thereon a covering of sealskin, and shall spread over it a cloth all of blue, and shall put in the staves thereof.
And upon the table of shobread they shall spread a cloth of blue, and put thereon the dishes, and the spoons, and the bols and the cups hereith to pour out; and the continual bread shall be thereon:
and they shall spread upon them a cloth of scarlet, and cover the same ith a covering of sealskin, and shall put in the staves thereof.
And they shall take a cloth of blue, and cover the candlestick of the light, and its lamps, and its snuffers, and its snuffdishes, and all the oil vessels thereof, hereith they minister unto it:
and they shall put it and all the vessels thereof ithin a covering of sealskin, and shall put it upon the frame.
And upon the golden altar they shall spread a cloth of blue, and cover it ith a covering of sealskin, and shall put in the staves thereof:
and they shall take all the vessels of ministry, hereith they minister in the sanctuary, and put them in a cloth of blue, and cover them ith a covering of sealskin, and shall put them on the frame.
And they shall take aay the ashes from the altar, and spread a purple cloth thereon:

and they shall put upon it all the vessels thereof, hereith they minister about it, the firepans, the flesh-hooks, and the shovels, and the basins, all the vessels of the altar; and they shall spread upon it a covering of sealskin, and put in the staves thereof.

And hen Aaron and his sons have made an end of covering the sanctuary, and all the furniture of the sanctuary, as the camp is set forard; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it: but they shall not touch the sanctuary, lest they die. These things are the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting.

And the charge of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest shall be the oil for the light, and the seet incense, and the continual meal-offering, and the anointing oil, the charge of all the tabernacle, and of all that therein is, the sanctuary, and the furniture thereof.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,
Cut ye not off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites from among the Levites;
but thus do unto them, that they may live, and not die, hen they approach unto the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in, and appoint them every one to his service and to his burden;
but they shall not go in to see the sanctuary even for a moment, lest they die.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Take the sum of the sons of Gershon also, by their fathers’ houses, by their families;
from thirty years old and upard until fifty years old shalt thou number them; all that enter in to ait upon the service, to do the ork in the tent of meeting.
This is the service of the families of the Gershonites, in serving and in bearing burdens:
they shall bear the curtains of the tabernacle, and the tent of meeting, its covering, and the covering of sealskin that is above upon it, and the screen for the door of the tent of meeting,

and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the door of the gate of the court, hich is by the tabernacle and by the altar round about, and their cords, and all the instruments of their service, and hatsoever shall be done ith them: therein shall they serve.

At the commandment of Aaron and his sons shall be all the service of the sons of the Gershonites, in all their burden, and in all their service; and ye shall appoint unto them in charge all their burden.
This is the service of the families of the sons of the Gershonites in the tent of meeting: and their charge shall be under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.
As for the sons of Merari, thou shalt number them by their families, by their fathers’ houses;
from thirty years old and upard even unto fifty years old shalt thou number them, every one that entereth upon the service, to do the ork of the tent of meeting.
And this is the charge of their burden, according to all their service in the tent of meeting: the boards of the tabernacle, and the bars thereof, and the pillars thereof, and the sockets thereof,

and the pillars of the court round about, and their sockets, and their pins, and their cords, ith all their instruments, and ith all their service: and by name ye shall appoint the instruments of the charge of their burden.

And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
