And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, When a man or oman shall commit any sin that men commit, so as to trespass against Jehovah, and that soul shall be guilty;

then he shall confess his sin hich he hath done: and he shall make restitution for his guilt in full, and add unto it the fifth part thereof, and give it unto him in respect of hom he hath been guilty.

But if the man have no kinsman to hom restitution may be made for the guilt, the restitution for guilt hich is made unto Jehovah shall be the priest’s; besides the ram of the atonement, hereby atonement shall be made for him.
And every heave-offering of all the holy things of the children of Israel, hich they present unto the priest, shall be his.
And every man’s halloed things shall be his: hatsoever any man giveth the priest, it shall be his.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, If any man’s ife go aside, and commit a trespass against him,
and a man lie ith her carnally, and it be hid from the eyes of her husband, and be kept close, and she be defiled, and there be no itness against her, and she be not taken in the act;
and the spirit of jealousy come upon him, and he be jealous of his ife, and she be defiled: or if the spirit of jealousy come upon him, and he be jealous of his ife, and she be not defiled:

then shall the man bring his ife unto the priest, and shall bring her oblation for her, the tenth part of an ephah of barley meal; he shall pour no oil upon it, nor put frankincense thereon; for it is a meal-offering of jealousy, a meal-offering of memorial, bringing iniquity to remembrance.
And the priest shall bring her near, and set her before Jehovah:
and the priest shall take holy ater in an earthen vessel; and of the dust that is on the floor of the tabernacle the priest shall take, and put it into the ater.

And the priest shall set the oman before Jehovah, and let the hair of the oman’s head go loose, and put the meal-offering of memorial in her hands, hich is the meal-offering of jealousy: and the priest shall have in his hand the ater of bitterness that causeth the curse.

And the priest shall cause her to sear, and shall say unto the oman, If no man have lain ith thee, and if thou have not gone aside to uncleanness, being under thy husband, be thou free from this ater of bitterness that causeth the curse.
But if thou have gone aside, being under thy husband, and if thou be defiled, and some man have lain ith thee besides thy husband:

then the priest shall cause the oman to sear ith the oath of cursing, and the priest shall say unto the oman, Jehovah make thee a curse and an oath among thy people, hen Jehovah doth make thy thigh to fall aay, and thy body to sell;
and this ater that causeth the curse shall go into thy boels, and make thy body to sell, and thy thigh to fall aay. And the oman shall say, Amen, Amen.
And the priest shall rite these curses in a book, and he shall blot them out into the ater of bitterness:
and he shall make the oman drink the ater of bitterness that causeth the curse; and the ater that causeth the curse shall enter into her \add and become\add* bitter.
And the priest shall take the meal-offering of jealousy out of the oman’s hand, and shall ave the meal-offering before Jehovah, and bring it unto the altar:
and the priest shall take a handful of the meal-offering, as the memorial thereof, and burn it upon the altar, and afterard shall make the oman drink the ater.

And hen he hath made her drink the ater, then it shall come to pass, if she be defiled, and have committed a trespass against her husband, that the ater that causeth the curse shall enter into her \add and become\add* bitter, and her body shall sell, and her thigh shall fall aay: and the oman shall be a curse among her people.
And if the oman be not defiled, but be clean; then she shall be free, and shall conceive seed.
This is the la of jealousy, hen a ife, being under her husband, goeth aside, and is defiled;
or hen the spirit of jealousy cometh upon a man, and he is jealous of his ife; then shall he set the oman before Jehovah, and the priest shall execute upon her all this la.
And the man shall be free from iniquity, and that oman shall bear her iniquity.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When either man or oman shall make a special vo, the vo of a Nazirite, to separate himself unto Jehovah,
he shall separate himself from ine and strong drink; he shall drink no vinegar of ine, or vinegar of strong drink, neither shall he drink any juice of grapes, nor eat fresh grapes or dried.
All the days of his separation shall he eat nothing that is made of the grape-vine, from the kernels even to the husk.

All the days of his vo of separation there shall no razor come upon his head: until the days be fulfilled, in hich he separateth himself unto Jehovah, he shall be holy; he shall let the locks of the hair of his head gro long.
All the days that he separateth himself unto Jehovah he shall not come near to a dead body.
He shall not make himself unclean for his father, or for his mother, for his brother, or for his sister, hen they die; because his separation unto God is upon his head.
All the days of his separation he is holy unto Jehovah.
And if any man die very suddenly beside him, and he defile the head of his separation; then he shall shave his head in the day of his cleansing, on the seventh day shall he shave it.
And on the eighth day he shall bring to turtle-doves, or to young pigeons, to the priest, to the door of the tent of meeting:
and the priest shall offer one for a sin-offering, and the other for a burnt-offering, and make atonement for him, for that he sinned by reason of the dead, and shall hallo his head that same day.
And he shall separate unto Jehovah the days of his separation, and shall bring a he-lamb a year old for a trespass-offering; but the former days shall be void, because his separation as defiled.
And this is the la of the Nazirite, hen the days of his separation are fulfilled: he shall be brought unto the door of the tent of meeting:

and he shall offer his oblation unto Jehovah, one he-lamb a year old ithout blemish for a burnt-offering, and one ee-lamb a year old ithout blemish for a sin-offering, and one ram ithout blemish for peace-offerings,
and a basket of unleavened bread, cakes of fine flour mingled ith oil, and unleavened afers anointed ith oil, and their meal-offering, and their drink-offerings.
And the priest shall present them before Jehovah, and shall offer his sin-offering, and his burnt-offering:
and he shall offer the ram for a sacrifice of peace-offerings unto Jehovah, ith the basket of unleavened bread: the priest shall offer also the meal-offering thereof, and the drink-offering thereof.

And the Nazirite shall shave the head of his separation at the door of the tent of meeting, and shall take the hair of the head of his separation, and put it on the fire hich is under the sacrifice of peace-offerings.

And the priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, and one unleavened cake out of the basket, and one unleavened afer, and shall put them upon the hands of the Nazirite, after he hath shaven \add the head of\add* his separation;
and the priest shall ave them for a ave-offering before Jehovah; this is holy for the priest, together ith the ave-breast and heave-thigh: and after that the Nazirite may drink ine.

This is the la of the Nazirite ho voeth, \add and of\add* his oblation unto Jehovah for his separation, besides that hich he is able to get: according to his vo hich he voeth, so he must do after the la of his separation.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying, On this ise ye shall bless the children of Israel: ye shall say unto them,
Jehovah bless thee, and keep thee:
Jehovah make his face to shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee:
Jehovah lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.

This as the dedication of the altar, in the day hen it as anointed, by the princes of Israel: telve silver platters, telve silver bols, telve golden spoons;

The ell, hich the princes digged, Which the nobles of the people delved, With the sceptre, \add and\add* ith their staves.
and from Mattanah to Nahaliel; and from Nahaliel to Bamoth;
and from Bamoth to the valley that is in the field of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, hich looketh don upon the desert.
And Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,
Let me pass through thy land: e ill not turn aside into field, or into vineyard; e ill not drink of the ater of the ells: e ill go by the king’s highay, until e have passed thy border.

And Sihon ould not suffer Israel to pass through his border: but Sihon gathered all his people together, and ent out against Israel into the ilderness, and came to Jahaz; and he fought against Israel.
And Israel smote him ith the edge of the sord, and possessed his land from the Arnon unto the Jabbok, even unto the children of Ammon; for the border of the children of Ammon as strong.
And Israel took all these cities: and Israel delt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all the tons thereof.
For Heshbon as the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites, ho had fought against the former king of Moab, and taken all his land out of his hand, even unto the Arnon.
Wherefore they that speak in proverbs say, Come ye to Heshbon; Let the city of Sihon be built and established:
For a fire is gone out of Heshbon, A flame from the city of Sihon: It hath devoured Ar of Moab, The lords of the high places of the Arnon.
Woe to thee, Moab! Thou art undone, O people of Chemosh: He hath given his sons as fugitives, And his daughters into captivity, Unto Sihon king of the Amorites.
We have shot at them; Heshbon is perished even unto Dibon, And e have laid aste even unto Nophah, Which \add reacheth\add* unto Medeba.
Thus Israel delt in the land of the Amorites.
And Moses sent to spy out Jazer; and they took the tons thereof, and drove out the Amorites that ere there.
And they turned and ent up by the ay of Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan ent out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.

And Jehovah said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand, and all his people, and his land; and thou shalt do to him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, ho delt at Heshbon.
So they smote him, and his sons and all his people, until there as none left him remaining: and they possessed his land.
And the children of Israel journeyed, and encamped in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho.
And Balak the son of Zippor sa all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
And Moab as sore afraid of the people, because they ere many: and Moab as distressed because of the children of Israel.

And Moab said unto the elders of Midian, No ill this multitude lick up all that is round about us, as the ox licketh up the grass of the field. And Balak the son of Zippor as king of Moab at that time.

And he sent messengers unto Balaam the son of Beor, to Pethor, hich is by the River, to the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me.

Come no therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me: peradventure I shall prevail, that e may smite them, and that I may drive them out of the land; for I kno that he hom thou blessest is blessed, and he hom thou cursest is cursed.
And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed ith the reards of divination in their hand; and they came unto Balaam, and spake unto him the ords of Balak.
And he said unto them, Lodge here this night, and I ill bring you ord again, as Jehovah shall speak unto me: and the princes of Moab abode ith Balaam.
And God came unto Balaam, and said, What men are these ith thee?
And Balaam said unto God, Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, hath sent unto me, \add saying\add*,
Behold, the people that is come out of Egypt, it covereth the face of the earth: no, come curse me them; peradventure I shall be able to fight against them, and shall drive them out.
And God said unto Balaam, Thou shalt not go ith them; thou shalt not curse the people; for they are blessed.
And Balaam rose up in the morning, and said unto the princes of Balak, Get you into your land; for Jehovah refuseth to give me leave to go ith you.
And the princes of Moab rose up, and they ent unto Balak, and said, Balaam refuseth to come ith us.
And Balak sent yet again princes, more, and more honorable than they.
And they came to Balaam, and said to him, Thus saith Balak the son of Zippor, Let nothing, I pray thee, hinder thee from coming unto me:
for I ill promote thee unto very great honor, and hatsoever thou sayest unto me I ill do: come therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people.
And Balaam ansered and said unto the servants of Balak, If Balak ould give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the ord of Jehovah my God, to do less or more.
No therefore, I pray you, tarry ye also here this night, that I may kno hat Jehovah ill speak unto me more.
And God came unto Balaam at night, and said unto him, If the men are come to call thee, rise up, go ith them; but only the ord hich I speak unto thee, that shalt thou do.
And Balaam rose up in the morning, and saddled his ass, and ent ith the princes of Moab.
And God’s anger as kindled because he ent; and the angel of Jehovah placed himself in the ay for an adversary against him. No he as riding upon his ass, and his to servants ere ith him.

And the ass sa the angel of Jehovah standing in the ay, ith his sord dran in his hand; and the ass turned aside out of the ay, and ent into the field: and Balaam smote the ass, to turn her into the ay.
Then the angel of Jehovah stood in a narro path beteen the vineyards, a all being on this side, and a all on that side.
And the ass sa the angel of Jehovah, and she thrust herself unto the all, and crushed Balaam’s foot against the all: and he smote her again.
And the angel of Jehovah ent further, and stood in a narro place, here as no ay to turn either to the right hand or to the left.
And the ass sa the angel of Jehovah, and she lay don under Balaam: and Balaam’s anger as kindled, and he smote the ass ith his staff.
And Jehovah opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?
And Balaam said unto the ass, Because thou hast mocked me: I ould there ere a sord in my hand, for no I had killed thee.
And the ass said unto Balaam, Am not I thine ass, upon hich thou hast ridden all thy life long unto this day? as I ever ont to do so unto thee? and he said, Nay.
Then Jehovah opened the eyes of Balaam, and he sa the angel of Jehovah standing in the ay, ith his sord dran in his hand; and he boed his head, and fell on his face.
And the angel of Jehovah said unto him, Wherefore hast thou smitten thine ass these three times? behold, I am come forth for an adversary, because thy ay is perverse before me:
and the ass sa me, and turned aside before me these three times: unless she had turned aside from me, surely no I had even slain thee, and saved her alive.
And Balaam said unto the angel of Jehovah, I have sinned; for I kne not that thou stoodest in the ay against me: no therefore, if it displease thee, I ill get me back again.
And the angel of Jehovah said unto Balaam, Go ith the men; but only the ord that I shall speak unto thee, that thou shalt speak. So Balaam ent ith the princes of Balak.
And hen Balak heard that Balaam as come, he ent out to meet him unto the City of Moab, hich is on the border of the Arnon, hich is in the utmost part of the border.
And Balak said unto Balaam, Did I not earnestly send unto thee to call thee? herefore camest thou not unto me? am I not able indeed to promote thee to honor?
And Balaam said unto Balak, Lo, I am come unto thee: have I no any poer at all to speak anything? the ord that God putteth in my mouth, that shall I speak.
And Balaam ent ith Balak, and they came unto Kiriath-huzoth.
And Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep, and sent to Balaam, and to the princes that ere ith him.
And it came to pass in the morning, that Balak took Balaam, and brought him up into the high places of Baal; and he sa from thence the utmost part of the people.
And Balaam said unto Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bullocks and seven rams.
And Balak did as Balaam had spoken; and Balak and Balaam offered on every altar a bullock and a ram.
And Balaam said unto Balak, Stand by thy burnt-offering, and I ill go: peradventure Jehovah ill come to meet me; and hatsoever he shoeth me I ill tell thee. And he ent to a bare height.
And God met Balaam: and he said unto him, I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered up a bullock and a ram on every altar.
And Jehovah put a ord in Balaam’s mouth, and said, Return unto Balak, and thus thou shalt speak.
And he returned unto him, and, lo, he as standing by his burnt-offering, he, and all the princes of Moab.
And he took up his parable, and said, From Aram hath Balak brought me, The king of Moab from the mountains of the East: Come, curse me Jacob, And come, defy Israel.
Ho shall I curse, hom God hath not cursed? And ho shall I defy, hom Jehovah hath not defied?
For from the top of the rocks I see him, And from the hills I behold him: Lo, it is a people that delleth alone, And shall not be reckoned among the nations.
Who can count the dust of Jacob, Or number the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous, And let my last end be like his!
And Balak said unto Balaam, What hast thou done unto me? I took thee to curse mine enemies, and, behold, thou hast blessed them altogether.
And he ansered and said, Must I not take heed to speak that hich Jehovah putteth in my mouth?

And Balak said unto him, Come, I pray thee, ith me unto another place, from hence thou mayest see them; thou shalt see but the utmost part of them, and shalt not see them all: and curse me them from thence.
And he took him into the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offered up a bullock and a ram on every altar.
And he said unto Balak, Stand here by thy burnt-offering, hile I meet \add Jehovah\add* yonder.
And Jehovah met Balaam, and put a ord in his mouth, and said, Return unto Balak, and thus shalt thou speak.
And he came to him, and, lo, he as standing by his burnt-offering, and the princes of Moab ith him. And Balak said unto him, What hath Jehovah spoken?
And he took up his parable, and said, Rise up, Balak, and hear; Hearken unto me, thou son of Zippor:
God is not a man, that he should lie, Neither the son of man, that he should repent: Hath he said, and ill he not do it? Or hath he spoken, and ill he not make it good?
Behold, I have received \add commandment\add* to bless: And he hath blessed, and I cannot reverse it.
He hath not beheld iniquity in Jacob; Neither hath he seen perverseness in Israel: Jehovah his God is ith him, And the shout of a king is among them.
God bringeth them forth out of Egypt; He hath as it ere the strength of the ild-ox.
Surely there is no enchantment ith Jacob; Neither is there any divination ith Israel: No shall it be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God rought!
Behold, the people riseth up as a lioness, And as a lion doth he lift himself up: He shall not lie don until he eat of the prey, And drink the blood of the slain.
And Balak said unto Balaam, Neither curse them at all, nor bless them at all.
But Balaam ansered and said unto Balak, Told not I thee, saying, All that Jehovah speaketh, that I must do?
And Balak said unto Balaam, Come no, I ill take thee unto another place; peradventure it ill please God that thou mayest curse me them from thence.
And Balak took Balaam unto the top of Peor, that looketh don upon the desert.
And Balaam said unto Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bullocks and seven rams.
And Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered up a bullock and a ram on every altar.
And hen Balaam sa that it pleased Jehovah to bless Israel, he ent not, as at the other times, to meet ith enchantments, but he set his face toard the ilderness.
And Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he sa Israel delling according to their tribes; and the Spirit of God came upon him.
And he took up his parable, and said, Balaam the son of Beor saith, And the man hose eye as closed saith;
He saith, ho heareth the ords of God, Who seeth the vision of the Almighty, Falling don, and having his eyes open:
Ho goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, Thy tabernacles, O Israel!
As valleys are they spread forth, As gardens by the river-side, As lign-aloes hich Jehovah hath planted, As cedar-trees beside the aters.
Water shall flo from his buckets, And his seed shall be in many aters, And his king shall be higher than Agag, And his kingdom shall be exalted.

God bringeth him forth out of Egypt; He hath as it ere the strength of the ild-ox: He shall eat up the nations his adversaries, And shall break their bones in pieces, And smite \add them\add* through ith his arros.
He couched, he lay don as a lion, And as a lioness; ho shall rouse him up? Blessed be every one that blesseth thee, And cursed be every one that curseth thee.

And Balak’s anger as kindled against Balaam, and he smote his hands together; and Balak said unto Balaam, I called thee to curse mine enemies, and, behold, thou hast altogether blessed them these three times.
Therefore no flee thou to thy place: I thought to promote thee unto great honor; but, lo, Jehovah hath kept thee back from honor.
And Balaam said unto Balak, Spake I not also to thy messengers that thou sentest unto me, saying,
If Balak ould give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the ord of Jehovah, to do either good or bad of mine on mind; hat Jehovah speaketh, that ill I speak?
And no, behold, I go unto my people: come, \add and\add* I ill advertise thee hat this people shall do to thy people in the latter days.
And he took up his parable, and said, Balaam the son of Beor saith, And the man hose eye as closed saith;
He saith, ho heareth the ords of God, And knoeth the knoledge of the Most High, Who seeth the vision of the Almighty, Falling don, and having his eyes open:

I see him, but not no; I behold him, but not nigh: There shall come forth a star out of Jacob, And a sceptre shall rise out of Israel, And shall smite through the corners of Moab, And break don all the sons of tumult.
And Edom shall be a possession, Seir also shall be a possession, \add ho ere\add* his enemies; While Israel doeth valiantly.
And out of Jacob shall one have dominion, And shall destroy the remnant from the city.
And he looked on Amalek, and took up his parable, and said, Amalek as the first of the nations; But his latter end shall come to destruction.
And he looked on the Kenite, and took up his parable, and said, Strong is thy delling-place, And thy nest is set in the rock.
Nevertheless Kain shall be asted, Until Asshur shall carry thee aay captive.
And he took up his parable, and said, Alas, ho shall live hen God doeth this?
But ships \add shall come\add* from the coast of Kittim, And they shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber; And he also shall come to destruction.
And Balaam rose up, and ent and returned to his place; and Balak also ent his ay.
And Israel abode in Shittim; and the people began to play the harlot ith the daughters of Moab:
for they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods; and the people did eat, and boed don to their gods.
And Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor: and the anger of Jehovah as kindled against Israel.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Take all the chiefs of the people, and hang them up unto Jehovah before the sun, that the fierce anger of Jehovah may turn aay from Israel.
And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that have joined themselves unto Baal-peor.

And, behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought unto his brethren a Midianitish oman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, hile they ere eeping at the door of the tent of meeting.
And hen Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, sa it, he rose up from the midst of the congregation, and took a spear in his hand;
and he ent after the man of Israel into the pavilion, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the oman through her body. So the plague as stayed from the children of Israel.
And those that died by the plague ere tenty and four thousand.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my rath aay from the children of Israel, in that he as jealous ith my jealousy among them, so that I consumed not the children of Israel in my jealousy.
Wherefore say, Behold, I give unto him my covenant of peace:
and it shall be unto him, and to his seed after him, the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he as jealous for his God, and made atonement for the children of Israel.
No the name of the man of Israel that as slain, ho as slain ith the Midianitish oman, as Zimri, the son of Salu, a prince of a fathers’ house among the Simeonites.
And the name of the Midianitish oman that as slain as Cozbi, the daughter of Zur; he as head of the people of a fathers’ house in Midian.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Vex the Midianites, and smite them;

for they vex you ith their iles, hereith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of the prince of Midian, their sister, ho as slain on the day of the plague in the matter of Peor.
And it came to pass after the plague, that Jehovah spake unto Moses and unto Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, saying,
Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, from tenty years old and upard, by their fathers’ houses, all that are able to go forth to ar in Israel.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest spake ith them in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
\add Take the sum of the people\add*, from tenty years old and upard; as Jehovah commanded Moses and the children of Israel, that came forth out of the land of Egypt.
Reuben, the first-born of Israel; the sons of Reuben: \add of\add* Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the family of the Palluites;
of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Carmi, the family of the Carmites.
These are the families of the Reubenites; and they that ere numbered of them ere forty and three thousand and seven hundred and thirty.
And the sons of Pallu: Eliab.

And the sons of Eliab: Nemuel, and Dathan, and Abiram. These are that Dathan and Abiram, ho ere called of the congregation, ho strove against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, hen they strove against Jehovah,
and the earth opened its mouth, and salloed them up together ith Korah, hen that company died; hat time the fire devoured to hundred and fifty men, and they became a sign.
Notithstanding, the sons of Korah died not.
The sons of Simeon after their families: of Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites; of Jamin, the family of the Jaminites; of Jachin, the family of the Jachinites;
of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites; of Shaul, the family of the Shaulites.
These are the families of the Simeonites, tenty and to thousand and to hundred.
The sons of Gad after their families: of Zephon, the family of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the family of the Haggites; of Shuni, the family of the Shunites;
of Ozni, the family of the Oznites; of Eri, the family of the Erites;
of Arod, the family of the Arodites; of Areli, the family of the Arelites.
These are the families of the sons of Gad according to those that ere numbered of them, forty thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Judah: Er and Onan; and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
And the sons of Judah after their families ere: of Shelah, the family of the Shelanites; of Perez, the family of the Perezites; of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites.
And the sons of Perez ere: of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Hamul, the family of the Hamulites.
These are the families of Judah according to those that ere numbered of them, threescore and sixteen thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Issachar after their families: \add of\add* Tola, the family of the Tolaites; of Puvah, the family of the Punites;
of Jashub, the family of the Jashubites; of Shimron, the family of the Shimronites.
These are the families of Issachar according to those that ere numbered of them, threescore and four thousand and three hundred.
The sons of Zebulun after their families: of Sered, the family of the Seredites; of Elon, the family of the Elonites; of Jahleel, the family of the Jahleelites.
These are the families of the Zebulunites according to those that ere numbered of them, threescore thousand and five hundred.
The sons of Joseph after their families: Manasseh and Ephraim.
The sons of Manasseh: of Machir, the family of the Machirites; and Machir begat Gilead: of Gilead, the family of the Gileadites.
These are the sons of Gilead: \add of\add* Iezer, the family of the Iezerites; of Helek, the family of the Helekites;
and \add of\add* Asriel, the family of the Asrielites; and \add of\add* Shechem, the family of the Shechemites;
and \add of\add* Shemida, the family of the Shemidaites; and \add of\add* Hepher, the family of the Hepherites.
And Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters: and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad ere Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the families of Manasseh; and they that ere numbered of them ere fifty and to thousand and seven hundred.
These are the sons of Ephraim after their families: of Shuthelah, the family of the Shuthelahites; of Becher, the family of the Becherites; of Tahan, the family of the Tahanites.
And these are the sons of Shuthelah: of Eran, the family of the Eranites.
These are the families of the sons of Ephraim according to those that ere numbered of them, thirty and to thousand and five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph after their families.
The sons of Benjamin after their families: of Bela, the family of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the family of the Ahiramites;
of Shephupham, the family of the Shuphamites; of Hupham, the family of the Huphamites.
And the sons of Bela ere Ard and Naaman: \add of Ard\add*, the family of the Ardites; of Naaman, the family of the Naamites.
These are the sons of Benjamin after their families; and they that ere numbered of them ere forty and five thousand and six hundred.
These are the sons of Dan after their families: of Shuham, the family of the Shuhamites. These are the families of Dan after their families.
All the families of the Shuhamites, according to those that ere numbered of them, ere threescore and four thousand and four hundred.
The sons of Asher after their families: of Imnah, the family of the Imnites; of Ishvi, the family of the Ishvites; of Beriah, the family of the Berites.
Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the family of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the family of the Malchielites.
And the name of the daughter of Asher as Serah.
These are the families of the sons of Asher according to those that ere numbered of them, fifty and three thousand and four hundred.
The sons of Naphtali after their families: of Jahzeel, the family of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the family of the Gunites;
of Jezer, the family of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the family of the Shillemites.
These are the families of Naphtali according to their families; and they that ere numbered of them ere forty and five thousand and four hundred.
These are they that ere numbered of the children of Israel, six hundred thousand and a thousand seven hundred and thirty.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Unto these the land shall be divided for an inheritance according to the number of names.
To the more thou shalt give the more inheritance, and to the feer thou shalt give the less inheritance: to every one according to those that ere numbered of him shall his inheritance be given.
Notithstanding, the land shall be divided by lot: according to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit.
According to the lot shall their inheritance be divided beteen the more and the feer.
And these are they that ere numbered of the Levites after their families: of Gershon, the family of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the family of the Kohathites; of Merari, the family of the Merarites.
These are the families of Levi: the family of the Libnites, the family of the Hebronites, the family of the Mahlites, the family of the Mushites, the family of the Korahites. And Kohath begat Amram.
And the name of Amram’s ife as Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, ho as born to Levi in Egypt: and she bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister.
And unto Aaron ere born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
And Nadab and Abihu died, hen they offered strange fire before Jehovah.

And they that ere numbered of them ere tenty and three thousand, every male from a month old and upard: for they ere not numbered among the children of Israel, because there as no inheritance given them among the children of Israel.
These are they that ere numbered by Moses and Eleazar the priest, ho numbered the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
But among these there as not a man of them that ere numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest, ho numbered the children of Israel in the ilderness of Sinai.
For Jehovah had said of them, They shall surely die in the ilderness. And there as not left a man of them, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.

Then dre near the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of Manasseh the son of Joseph; and these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.
And they stood before Moses, and before Eleazar the priest, and before the princes and all the congregation, at the door of the tent of meeting, saying,
Our father died in the ilderness, and he as not among the company of them that gathered themselves together against Jehovah in the company of Korah: but he died in his on sin; and he had no sons.
Why should the name of our father be taken aay from among his family, because he had no son? Give unto us a possession among the brethren of our father.
And Moses brought their cause before Jehovah.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

The daughters of Zelophehad speak right: thou shalt surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father’s brethren; and thou shalt cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them.
And thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter.
And if he have no daughter, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his brethren.
And if he have no brethren, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his father’s brethren.

And if his father have no brethren, then ye shall give his inheritance unto his kinsman that is next to him of his family, and he shall possess it: and it shall be unto the children of Israel a statute \add and\add* ordinance, as Jehovah commanded Moses.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Get thee up into this mountain of Abarim, and behold the land hich I have given unto the children of Israel.
And hen thou hast seen it, thou also shalt be gathered unto thy people, as Aaron thy brother as gathered;

because ye rebelled against my ord in the ilderness of Zin, in the strife of the congregation, to sanctify me at the aters before their eyes. ( These are the aters of Meribah of Kadesh in the ilderness of Zin.)
And Moses spake unto Jehovah, saying,
Let Jehovah, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation,
ho may go out before them, and ho may come in before them, and ho may lead them out, and ho may bring them in; that the congregation of Jehovah be not as sheep hich have no shepherd.
And Jehovah said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in hom is the Spirit, and lay thy hand upon him;
and set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; and give him a charge in their sight.
And thou shalt put of thine honor upon him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may obey.

Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye pass over the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
then ye shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their figured \add stones\add*, and destroy all their molten images, and demolish all their high places:
and ye shall take possession of the land, and dell therein; for unto you have I given the land to possess it.

And ye shall inherit the land by lot according to your families; to the more ye shall give the more inheritance, and to the feer thou shalt give the less inheritance: heresoever the lot falleth to any man, that shall be his; according to the tribes of your fathers shall ye inherit.

But if ye ill not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you, then shall those that ye let remain of them be as pricks in your eyes, and as thorns in your sides, and they shall vex you in the land herein ye dell.
And it shall come to pass, that, as I thought to do unto them, so ill I do unto you.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,

Command the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye come into the land of Canaan ( this is the land that shall fall unto you for an inheritance, even the land of Canaan according to the borders thereof),
then your south quarter shall be from the ilderness of Zin along by the side of Edom, and your south border shall be from the end of the Salt Sea eastard;

and your border shall turn about southard of the ascent of Akrabbim, and pass along to Zin; and the goings out thereof shall be southard of Kadesh-barnea; and it shall go forth to Hazar-addar, and pass along to Azmon;
and the border shall turn about from Azmon unto the brook of Egypt, and the goings out thereof shall be at the sea.
And for the estern border, ye shall have the great sea and the border \add thereof\add*: this shall be your est border.
And this shall be your north border: from the great sea ye shall mark out for you mount Hor;
from mount Hor ye shall mark out unto the entrance of Hamath; and the goings out of the border shall be at Zedad;
and the border shall go forth to Ziphron, and the goings out thereof shall be at Hazar-enan: this shall be your north border.
And ye shall mark out your east border from Hazar-enan to Shepham;
and the border shall go don from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain; and the border shall go don, and shall reach unto the side of the sea of Chinnereth eastard;
and the border shall go don to the Jordan, and the goings out thereof shall be at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land according to the borders thereof round about.
And Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying, This is the land hich ye shall inherit by lot, hich Jehovah hath commanded to give unto the nine tribes, and to the half-tribe;

for the tribe of the children of Reuben according to their fathers’ houses, and the tribe of the children of Gad according to their fathers’ houses, have received, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received, their inheritance:
the to tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan at Jericho eastard, toard the sunrising.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
These are the names of the men that shall divide the land unto you for inheritance: Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun.
And ye shall take one prince of every tribe, to divide the land for inheritance.
And these are the names of the men: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
And of the tribe of the children of Simeon, Shemuel the son of Ammihud.
Of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad the son of Chislon.
And of the tribe of the children of Dan a prince, Bukki the son of Jogli.
Of the children of Joseph: of the tribe of the children of Manasseh a prince, Hanniel the son of Ephod.
And of the tribe of the children of Ephraim a prince, Kemuel the son of Shiphtan.
And of the tribe of the children of Zebulun a prince, Elizaphan the son of Parnach.
And of the tribe of the children of Issachar a prince, Paltiel the son of Azzan.
And of the tribe of the children of Asher a prince, Ahihud the son of Shelomi.
And of the tribe of the children of Naphtali a prince, Pedahel the son of Ammihud.
These are they hom Jehovah commanded to divide the inheritance unto the children of Israel in the land of Canaan.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
Command the children of Israel, that they give unto the Levites of the inheritance of their possession cities to dell in; and suburbs for the cities round about them shall ye give unto the Levites.
And the cities shall they have to dell in; and their suburbs shall be for their cattle, and for their substance, and for all their beasts.
And the suburbs of the cities, hich ye shall give unto the Levites, shall be from the all of the city and outard a thousand cubits round about.

And ye shall measure ithout the city for the east side to thousand cubits, and for the south side to thousand cubits, and for the est side to thousand cubits, and for the north side to thousand cubits, the city being in the midst. This shall be to them the suburbs of the cities.
And the cities hich ye shall give unto the Levites, they shall be the six cities of refuge, hich ye shall give for the manslayer to flee unto: and besides them ye shall give forty and to cities.
All the cities hich ye shall give to the Levites shall be forty and eight cities; them \add shall ye give\add* ith their suburbs.

And concerning the cities hich ye shall give of the possession of the children of Israel, from the many ye shall take many; and from the fe ye shall take fe: every one according to his inheritance hich he inheriteth shall give of his cities unto the Levites.
And Jehovah spake unto Moses, saying,
Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye pass over the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
then ye shall appoint you cities to be cities of refuge for you, that the manslayer that killeth any person unittingly may flee thither.
And the cities shall be unto you for refuge from the avenger, that the manslayer die not, until he stand before the congregation for judgment.
And the cities hich ye shall give shall be for you six cities of refuge.
Ye shall give three cities beyond the Jordan, and three cities shall ye give in the land of Canaan; they shall be cities of refuge.
For the children of Israel, and for the stranger and for the sojourner among them, shall these six cities be for refuge; that every one that killeth any person unittingly may flee thither.
But if he smote him ith an instrument of iron, so that he died, he is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death.
And if he smote him ith a stone in the hand, hereby a man may die, and he died, he is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death.
Or if he smote him ith a eapon of ood in the hand, hereby a man may die, and he died, he is a murderer: the murderer shall surely be put to death.
The avenger of blood shall himself put the murderer to death: hen he meeteth him, he shall put him to death.
And if he thrust him of hatred, or hurled at him, lying in ait, so that he died,
or in enmity smote him ith his hand, so that he died; he that smote him shall surely be put to death; he is a murderer: the avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death, hen he meeteth him.
But if he thrust him suddenly ithout enmity, or hurled upon him anything ithout lying in ait,
or ith any stone, hereby a man may die, seeing him not, and cast it upon him, so that he died, and he as not his enemy, neither sought his harm;
then the congregation shall judge beteen the smiter and the avenger of blood according to these ordinances;

and the congregation shall deliver the manslayer out of the hand of the avenger of blood, and the congregation shall restore him to his city of refuge, hither he as fled: and he shall dell therein until the death of the high priest, ho as anointed ith the holy oil.
But if the manslayer shall at any time go beyond the border of his city of refuge, hither he fleeth,
and the avenger of blood find him ithout the border of his city of refuge, and the avenger of blood slay the manslayer; he shall not be guilty of blood,
because he should have remained in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest: but after the death of the high priest the manslayer shall return into the land of his possession.
And these things shall be for a statute \add and\add* ordinance unto you throughout your generations in all your dellings.
Whoso killeth any person, the murderer shall be slain at the mouth of itnesses: but one itness shall not testify against any person that he die.
Moreover ye shall take no ransom for the life of a murderer, that is guilty of death; but he shall surely be put to death.
And ye shall take no ransom for him that is fled to his city of refuge, that he may come again to dell in the land, until the death of the priest.
So ye shall not pollute the land herein ye are: for blood, it polluteth the land; and no expiation can be made for the land for the blood that is shed therein, but by the blood of him that shed it.
And thou shalt not defile the land hich ye inhabit, in the midst of hich I dell: for I, Jehovah, dell in the midst of the children of Israel.

And the heads of the fathers’ \add houses\add* of the family of the children of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of the sons of Joseph, came near, and spake before Moses, and before the princes, the heads of the fathers’ \add houses\add* of the children of Israel:

and they said, Jehovah commanded my lord to give the land for inheritance by lot to the children of Israel: and my lord as commanded by Jehovah to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother unto his daughters.

And if they be married to any of the sons of the \add other\add* tribes of the children of Israel, then ill their inheritance be taken aay from the inheritance of our fathers, and ill be added to the inheritance of the tribe hereunto they shall belong: so ill it be taken aay from the lot of our inheritance.

And hen the jubilee of the children of Israel shall be, then ill their inheritance be added unto the inheritance of the tribe hereunto they shall belong: so ill their inheritance be taken aay from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers.
And Moses commanded the children of Israel according to the ord of Jehovah, saying, The tribe of the sons of Joseph speaketh right.

This is the thing hich Jehovah doth command concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, Let them be married to hom they think best; only into the family of the tribe of their father shall they be married.
So shall no inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe; for the children of Israel shall cleave every one to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.

And every daughter, that possesseth an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Israel, shall be ife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that the children of Israel may possess every man the inheritance of his fathers.
So shall no inheritance remove from one tribe to another tribe; for the tribes of the children of Israel shall cleave every one to his on inheritance.
Even as Jehovah commanded Moses, so did the daughters of Zelophehad:
for Mahlah, Tirzah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, ere married unto their father’s brothers’ sons.
They ere married into the families of the sons of Manasseh the son of Joseph; and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father.
These are the commandments and the ordinances hich Jehovah commanded by Moses unto the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
These are the ords hich Moses spake unto all Israel beyond the Jordan in the ilderness, in the Arabah over against Suph, beteen Paran, and Tophel, and Laban, and Hazeroth, and Di-zahab.
It is eleven days’ \add journey\add* from Horeb by the ay of mount Seir unto Kadesh-barnea.

And it came to pass in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses spake unto the children of Israel, according unto all that Jehovah had given him in commandment unto them;
after he had smitten Sihon the king of the Amorites, ho delt in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, ho delt in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.
Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, began Moses to declare this la, saying,
Jehovah our God spake unto us in Horeb, saying, Ye have delt long enough in this mountain:

turn you, and take your journey, and go to the hill-country of the Amorites, and unto all \add the places\add* nigh thereunto, in the Arabah, in the hill-country, and in the loland, and in the South, and by the sea-shore, the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates.
Behold, I have set the land before you: go in and possess the land hich Jehovah sare unto your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give unto them and to their seed after them.
And I spake unto you at that time, saying, I am not able to bear you myself alone:
Jehovah your God hath multiplied you, and, behold, ye are this day as the stars of heaven for multitude.
Jehovah, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times as many as ye are, and bless you, as he hath promised you!
Ho can I myself alone bear your cumbrance, and your burden, and your strife?
Take you ise men, and understanding, and knon, according to your tribes, and I ill make them heads over you.
And ye ansered me, and said, The thing hich thou hast spoken is good \add for us\add* to do.

So I took the heads of your tribes, ise men, and knon, and made them heads over you, captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, and captains of fifties, and captains of tens, and officers, according to your tribes.
And I charged your judges at that time, saying, Hear \add the causes\add* beteen your brethren, and judge righteously beteen a man and his brother, and the sojourner that is ith him.

Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; ye shall hear the small and the great alike; ye shall not be afraid of the face of man; for the judgment is God’s: and the cause that is too hard for you ye shall bring unto me, and I ill hear it.
And I commanded you at that time all the things hich ye should do.

And e journeyed from Horeb, and ent through all that great and terrible ilderness hich ye sa, by the ay to the hill-country of the Amorites, as Jehovah our God commanded us; and e came to Kadesh-barnea.
And I said unto you, Ye are come unto the hill-country of the Amorites, hich Jehovah our God giveth unto us.
Behold, Jehovah thy God hath set the land before thee: go up, take possession, as Jehovah, the God of thy fathers, hath spoken unto thee; fear not, neither be dismayed.

And ye came near unto me every one of you, and said, Let us send men before us, that they may search the land for us, and bring us ord again of the ay by hich e must go up, and the cities unto hich e shall come.
And the thing pleased me ell; and I took telve men of you, one man for every tribe:
and they turned and ent up into the hill-country, and came unto the valley of Eshcol, and spied it out.
And they took of the fruit of the land in their hands, and brought it don unto us, and brought us ord again, and said, It is a good land hich Jehovah our God giveth unto us.
Yet ye ould not go up, but rebelled against the commandment of Jehovah your God:
and ye murmured in your tents, and said, Because Jehovah hated us, he hath brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us.

Whither are e going up? our brethren have made our heart to melt, saying, The people are greater and taller than e; the cities are great and fortified up to heaven; and moreover e have seen the sons of the Anakim there.
Then I said unto you, Dread not, neither be afraid of them.
Jehovah your God ho goeth before you, he ill fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
and in the ilderness, here thou hast seen ho that Jehovah thy God bare thee, as a man doth bear his son, in all the ay that ye ent, until ye came unto this place.
Yet in this thing ye did not believe Jehovah your God,
ho ent before you in the ay, to seek you out a place to pitch your tents in, in fire by night, to sho you by hat ay ye should go, and in the cloud by day.
And Jehovah heard the voice of your ords, and as roth, and sare, saying,
Surely there shall not one of these men of this evil generation see the good land, hich I sare to give unto your fathers,
save Caleb the son of Jephunneh; he shall see it; and to him ill I give the land that he hath trodden upon, and to his children, because he hath holly folloed Jehovah.
Also Jehovah as angry ith me for your sakes, saying, Thou also shalt not go in thither:
Joshua the son of Nun, ho standeth before thee, he shall go in thither: encourage thou him; for he shall cause Israel to inherit it.

Moreover your little ones, that ye said should be a prey, and your children, that this day have no knoledge of good or evil, they shall go in thither, and unto them ill I give it, and they shall possess it.
But as for you, turn you, and take your journey into the ilderness by the ay to the Red Sea.

Then ye ansered and said unto me, We have sinned against Jehovah, e ill go up and fight, according to all that Jehovah our God commanded us. And ye girded on every man his eapons of ar, and ere forard to go up into the hill-country.
And Jehovah said unto me, Say unto them, Go not up, neither fight; for I am not among you; lest ye be smitten before your enemies.
So I spake unto you, and ye hearkened not; but ye rebelled against the commandment of Jehovah, and ere presumptuous, and ent up into the hill-country.
And the Amorites, that delt in that hill-country, came out against you, and chased you, as bees do, and beat you don in Seir, even unto Hormah.
And ye returned and ept before Jehovah; but Jehovah hearkened not to your voice, nor gave ear unto you.
So ye abode in Kadesh many days, according unto the days that ye abode \add there\add*.
Then e turned, and took our journey into the ilderness by the ay to the Red Sea, as Jehovah spake unto me; and e compassed mount Seir many days.
And Jehovah spake unto me, saying,
Ye have compassed this mountain long enough: turn you northard.

And command thou the people, saying, Ye are to pass through the border of your brethren the children of Esau, that dell in Seir; and they ill be afraid of you. Take ye good heed unto yourselves therefore;
contend not ith them; for I ill not give you of their land, no, not so much as for the sole of the foot to tread on; because I have given mount Seir unto Esau for a possession.
Ye shall purchase food of them for money, that ye may eat; and ye shall also buy ater of them for money, that ye may drink.
For Jehovah thy God hath blessed thee in all the ork of thy hand; he hath knon thy alking through this great ilderness: these forty years Jehovah thy God hath been ith thee; thou hast lacked nothing.
So e passed by from our brethren the children of Esau, that dell in Seir, from the ay of the Arabah from Elath and from Ezion-geber. And e turned and passed by the ay of the ilderness of Moab.
And Jehovah said unto me, Vex not Moab, neither contend ith them in battle; for I ill not give thee of his land for a possession; because I have given Ar unto the children of Lot for a possession.
( The Emim delt therein aforetime, a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakim:
these also are accounted Rephaim, as the Anakim; but the Moabites call them Emim.

The Horites also delt in Seir aforetime, but the children of Esau succeeded them; and they destroyed them from before them, and delt in their stead; as Israel did unto the land of his possession, hich Jehovah gave unto them).
No rise up, and get you over the brook Zered. And e ent over the brook Zered.

And the days in hich e came from Kadesh-barnea, until e ere come over the brook Zered, ere thirty and eight years; until all the generation of the men of ar ere consumed from the midst of the camp, as Jehovah sare unto them.
Moreover the hand of Jehovah as against them, to destroy them from the midst of the camp, until they ere consumed.
So it came to pass, hen all the men of ar ere consumed and dead from among the people,
that Jehovah spake unto me, saying,
Thou art this day to pass over Ar, the border of Moab:

and hen thou comest nigh over against the children of Ammon, vex them not, nor contend ith them; for I ill not give thee of the land of the children of Ammon for a possession; because I have given it unto the children of Lot for a possession.
( That also is accounted a land of Rephaim: Rephaim delt therein aforetime; but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakim; but Jehovah destroyed them before them; and they succeeded them, and delt in their stead;
as he did for the children of Esau, that dell in Seir, hen he destroyed the Horites from before them; and they succeeded them, and delt in their stead even unto this day.
And the Avvim, that delt in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim, that came forth out of Caphtor, destroyed them, and delt in their stead.)

Rise ye up, take your journey, and pass over the valley of the Arnon: behold, I have given into thy hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land; begin to possess it, and contend ith him in battle.

This day ill I begin to put the dread of thee and the fear of thee upon the peoples that are under the hole heaven, ho shall hear the report of thee, and shall tremble, and be in anguish because of thee.
And I sent messengers out of the ilderness of Kedemoth unto Sihon king of Heshbon ith ords of peace, saying,
Let me pass through thy land: I ill go along by the highay, I ill turn neither unto the right hand nor to the left.
Thou shalt sell me food for money, that I may eat; and give me ater for money, that I may drink: only let me pass through on my feet;
as the children of Esau that dell in Seir, and the Moabites that dell in Ar, did unto me; until I shall pass over the Jordan into the land hich Jehovah our God giveth us.
But Sihon king of Heshbon ould not let us pass by him; for Jehovah thy God hardened his spirit, and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand, as at this day.
And Jehovah said unto me, Behold, I have begun to deliver up Sihon and his land before thee: begin to possess, that thou mayest inherit his land.
Then Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, unto battle at Jahaz.
And Jehovah our God delivered him up before us; and e smote him, and his sons, and all his people.
And e took all his cities at that time, and utterly destroyed every inhabited city, ith the omen and the little ones; e left none remaining:
only the cattle e took for a prey unto ourselves, ith the spoil of the cities hich e had taken.

From Aroer, hich is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and \add from\add* the city that is in the valley, even unto Gilead, there as not a city too high for us; Jehovah our God delivered up all before us:
only to the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not near; all the side of the river Jabbok, and the cities of the hill-country, and heresoever Jehovah our God forbade us.
Then e turned, and ent up the ay to Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, unto battle at Edrei.

And Jehovah said unto me, Fear him not; for I have delivered him, and all his people, and his land, into thy hand; and thou shalt do unto him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, ho delt at Heshbon.
So Jehovah our God delivered into our hand Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and e smote him until none as left to him remaining.
And e took all his cities at that time; there as not a city hich e took not from them; threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these ere cities fortified ith high alls, gates, and bars; besides the unalled tons a great many.
And e utterly destroyed them, as e did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying every inhabited city, ith the omen and the little ones.
But all the cattle, and the spoil of the cities, e took for a prey unto ourselves.
And e took the land at that time out of the hand of the to kings of the Amorites that ere beyond the Jordan, from the valley of the Arnon unto mount Hermon
(\add hich\add* Hermon the Sidonians call Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir);
all the cities of the plain, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, unto Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

( For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the Rephaim; behold, his bedstead as a bedstead of iron; is it not in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? nine cubits as the length thereof, and four cubits the breadth of it, after the cubit of a man.)

And this land e took in possession at that time: from Aroer, hich is by the valley of the Arnon, and half the hill-country of Gilead, and the cities thereof, gave I unto the Reubenites and to the Gadites:
and the rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, gave I unto the half-tribe of Manasseh; all the region of Argob, even all Bashan. ( The same is called the land of Rephaim.
Jair the son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob, unto the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and called them, even Bashan, after his on name, Havvoth-jair, unto this day.)
And I gave Gilead unto Machir.

And unto the Reubenites and unto the Gadites I gave from Gilead even unto the valley of the Arnon, the middle of the valley, and the border \add thereof\add*, even unto the river Jabbok, hich is the border of the children of Ammon;
the Arabah also, and the Jordan and the border \add thereof\add*, from Chinnereth even unto the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah eastard.
And I commanded you at that time, saying, Jehovah your God hath given you this land to possess it: ye shall pass over armed before your brethren the children of Israel, all the men of valor.
But your ives, and your little ones, and your cattle ( I kno that ye have much cattle), shall abide in your cities hich I have given you,

until Jehovah give rest unto your brethren, as unto you, and they also possess the land hich Jehovah your God giveth them beyond the Jordan: then shall ye return every man unto his possession, hich I have given you.
And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, Thine eyes have seen all that Jehovah your God hath done unto these to kings: so shall Jehovah do unto all the kingdoms hither thou goest over.
Ye shall not fear them; for Jehovah your God, he it is that fighteth for you.
And I besought Jehovah at that time, saying,
O Lord Jehovah, thou hast begun to sho thy servant thy greatness, and thy strong hand: for hat god is there in heaven or in earth, that can do according to thy orks, and according to thy mighty acts?
Let me go over, I pray thee, and see the good land that is beyond the Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon.
But Jehovah as roth ith me for your sakes, and hearkened not unto me; and Jehovah said unto me, Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter.
Get thee up unto the top of Pisgah, and lift up thine eyes estard, and northard, and southard, and eastard, and behold ith thine eyes: for thou shalt not go over this Jordan.
But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him; for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land hich thou shalt see.
So e abode in the valley over against Beth-peor.
And no, O Israel, hearken unto the statutes and unto the ordinances, hich I teach you, to do them; that ye may live, and go in and possess the land hich Jehovah, the God of your fathers, giveth you.
Ye shall not add unto the ord hich I command you, neither shall ye diminish from it, that ye may keep the commandments of Jehovah your God hich I command you.
Your eyes have seen hat Jehovah did because of Baal-peor; for all the men that folloed Baal-peor, Jehovah thy God hath destroyed them from the midst of thee.
But ye that did cleave unto Jehovah your God are alive every one of you this day.
Behold, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, even as Jehovah my God commanded me, that ye should do so in the midst of the land hither ye go in to possess it.

Keep therefore and do them; for this is your isdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples, that shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a ise and understanding people.
For hat great nation is there, that hath a god so nigh unto them, as Jehovah our God is hensoever e call upon him?
And hat great nation is there, that hath statutes and ordinances so righteous as all this la, hich I set before you this day?

Only take heed to thyself, and keep thy soul diligently, lest thou forget the things hich thine eyes sa, and lest they depart from thy heart all the days of thy life; but make them knon unto thy children and thy children’s children;

the day that thou stoodest before Jehovah thy God in Horeb, hen Jehovah said unto me, Assemble me the people, and I ill make them hear my ords, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children.
And ye came near and stood under the mountain; and the mountain burned ith fire unto the heart of heaven, ith darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.
And Jehovah spake unto you out of the midst of the fire: ye heard the voice of ords, but ye sa no form; only \add ye heard\add* a voice.
And he declared unto you his covenant, hich he commanded you to perform, even the ten commandments; and he rote them upon to tables of stone.
And Jehovah commanded me at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, that ye might do them in the land hither ye go over to possess it.
Take ye therefore good heed unto yourselves; for ye sa no manner of form on the day that Jehovah spake unto you in Horeb out of the midst of the fire;
lest ye corrupt yourselves, and make you a graven image in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female,
the likeness of any beast that is on the earth, the likeness of any inged bird that flieth in the heavens,
the likeness of anything that creepeth on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the ater under the earth;

and lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and hen thou seest the sun and the moon and the stars, even all the host of heaven, thou be dran aay and orship them, and serve them, hich Jehovah thy God hath allotted unto all the peoples under the hole heaven.
But Jehovah hath taken you, and brought you forth out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be unto him a people of inheritance, as at this day.

Furthermore Jehovah as angry ith me for your sakes, and sare that I should not go over the Jordan, and that I should not go in unto that good land, hich Jehovah thy God giveth thee for an inheritance:
but I must die in this land, I must not go over the Jordan; but ye shall go over, and possess that good land.
Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant of Jehovah your God, hich he made ith you, and make you a graven image in the form of anything hich Jehovah thy God hath forbidden thee.
For Jehovah thy God is a devouring fire, a jealous God.

When thou shalt beget children, and children’s children, and ye shall have been long in the land, and shall corrupt yourselves, and make a graven image in the form of anything, and shall do that hich is evil in the sight of Jehovah thy God, to provoke him to anger;

I call heaven and earth to itness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land hereunto ye go over the Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed.
And Jehovah ill scatter you among the peoples, and ye shall be left fe in number among the nations, hither Jehovah shall lead you aay.
And there ye shall serve gods, the ork of men’s hands, ood and stone, hich neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.
But from thence ye shall seek Jehovah thy God, and thou shalt find him, hen thou searchest after him ith all thy heart and ith all thy soul.
When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, in the latter days thou shalt return to Jehovah thy God, and hearken unto his voice:
for Jehovah thy God is a merciful God; he ill not fail thee, neither destroy thee, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers hich he sare unto them.

For ask no of the days that are past, hich ere before thee, since the day that God created man upon the earth, and from the one end of heaven unto the other, hether there hath been \add any such thing\add* as this great thing is, or hath been heard like it?
Did ever a people hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as thou hast heard, and live?

Or hath God assayed to go and take him a nation from the midst of \add another\add* nation, by trials, by signs, and by onders, and by ar, and by a mighty hand, and by an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, according to all that Jehovah your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
Unto thee it as shoed, that thou mightest kno that Jehovah he is God; there is none else besides him.
Out of heaven he made thee to hear his voice, that he might instruct thee: and upon earth he made thee to see his great fire; and thou heardest his ords out of the midst of the fire.
And because he loved thy fathers, therefore he chose their seed after them, and brought thee out ith his presence, ith his great poer, out of Egypt;
to drive out nations from before thee greater and mightier than thou, to bring thee in, to give thee their land for an inheritance, as at this day.
Kno therefore this day, and lay it to thy heart, that Jehovah he is God in heaven above and upon the earth beneath; there is none else.

And thou shalt keep his statutes, and his commandments, hich I command thee this day, that it may go ell ith thee, and ith thy children after thee, and that thou mayest prolong thy days in the land, hich Jehovah thy God giveth thee, for ever.
Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan toard the sunrising;
that the manslayer might flee thither, that slayeth his neighbor unaares, and hated him not in time past; and that fleeing unto one of these cities he might live:
\add namely\add*, Bezer in the ilderness, in the plain country, for the Reubenites; and Ramoth in Gilead, for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan, for the Manassites.
And this is the la hich Moses set before the children of Israel:
these are the testimonies, and the statutes, and the ordinances, hich Moses spake unto the children of Israel, hen they came forth out of Egypt,
beyond the Jordan, in the valley over against Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, ho delt at Heshbon, hom Moses and the children of Israel smote, hen they came forth out of Egypt.
And they took his land in possession, and the land of Og king of Bashan, the to kings of the Amorites, ho ere beyond the Jordan toard the sunrising;
from Aroer, hich is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, even unto mount Sion ( the same is Hermon),
and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan eastard, even unto the sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.
And Moses called unto all Israel, and said unto them, Hear, O Israel, the statutes and the ordinances hich I speak in your ears this day, that ye may learn them, and observe to do them.
Jehovah our God made a covenant ith us in Horeb.
Jehovah made not this covenant ith our fathers, but ith us, even us, ho are all of us here alive this day.
Jehovah spake ith you face to face in the mount out of the midst of the fire
( I stood beteen Jehovah and you at that time, to sho you the ord of Jehovah: for ye ere afraid because of the fire, and ent not up into the mount), saying,
I am Jehovah thy God, ho brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
Thou shalt not make unto thee a graven image, \add nor\add* any likeness \add of anything\add* that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the ater under the earth:

thou shalt not bo don thyself unto them, nor serve them; for I, Jehovah, thy God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the third and upon the fourth generation of them that hate me;
and shoing lovingkindness unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.
Thou shalt not take the name of Jehovah thy God in vain: for Jehovah ill not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.
Observe the sabbath day, to keep it holy, as Jehovah thy God commanded thee.
Six days shalt thou labor, and do all thy ork;

but the seventh day is a sabbath unto Jehovah thy God: \add in it\add* thou shalt not do any ork, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, nor thy man-servant, nor thy maid-servant, nor thine ox, nor thine ass, nor any of thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is ithin thy gates; that thy man-servant and thy maid-servant may rest as ell as thou.

And thou shalt remember that thou ast a servant in the land of Egypt, and Jehovah thy God brought thee out thence by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm: therefore Jehovah thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day.
Honor thy father and thy mother, as Jehovah thy God commanded thee; that thy days may be long, and that it may go ell ith thee, in the land hich Jehovah thy God giveth thee.
Thou shalt not kill.
Neither shalt thou commit adultery.
Neither shalt thou steal.
Neither shalt thou bear false itness against thy neighbor.

Neither shalt thou covet thy neighbor’s ife; neither shalt thou desire thy neighbor’s house, his field, or his man-servant, or his maid-servant, his ox, or his ass, or anything that is thy neighbor’s.

These ords Jehovah spake unto all your assembly in the mount out of the midst of the fire, of the cloud, and of the thick darkness, ith a great voice: and he added no more. And he rote them upon to tables of stone, and gave them unto me.
And it came to pass, hen ye heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness, hile the mountain as burning ith fire, that ye came near unto me, even all the heads of your tribes, and your elders;

and ye said, Behold, Jehovah our God hath shoed us his glory and his greatness, and e have heard his voice out of the midst of the fire: e have seen this day that God doth speak ith man, and he liveth.
No therefore hy should e die? for this great fire ill consume us: if e hear the voice of Jehovah our God any more, then e shall die.
For ho is there of all flesh, that hath heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as e have, and lived?
Go thou near, and hear all that Jehovah our God shall say: and speak thou unto us all that Jehovah our God shall speak unto thee; and e ill hear it, and do it.

And Jehovah heard the voice of your ords, hen ye spake unto me; and Jehovah said unto me, I have heard the voice of the ords of this people, hich they have spoken unto thee: they have ell said all that they have spoken.
Oh that there ere such a heart in them, that they ould fear me, and keep all my commandments alays, that it might be ell ith them, and ith their children for ever!
Go say to them, Return ye to your tents.

But as for thee, stand thou here by me, and I ill speak unto thee all the commandment, and the statutes, and the ordinances, hich thou shalt teach them, that they may do them in the land hich I give them to possess it.
Ye shall observe to do therefore as Jehovah your God hath commanded you: ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.
Ye shall alk in all the ay hich Jehovah your God hath commanded you, that ye may live, and that it may be ell ith you, and that ye may prolong your days in the land hich ye shall possess.
No this is the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances, hich Jehovah your God commanded to teach you, that ye might do them in the land hither ye go over to possess it;

that thou mightest fear Jehovah thy God, to keep all his statutes and his commandments, hich I command thee, thou, and thy son, and thy son’s son, all the days of thy life; and that thy days may be prolonged.

Hear therefore, O Israel, and observe to do it; that it may be ell ith thee, and that ye may increase mightily, as Jehovah, the God of thy fathers, hath promised unto thee, in a land floing ith milk and honey.
Hear, O Israel: Jehovah our God is one Jehovah:
and thou shalt love Jehovah thy God ith all thy heart, and ith all thy soul, and ith all thy might.
And these ords, hich I command thee this day, shall be upon thy heart;
and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them hen thou sittest in thy house, and hen thou alkest by the ay, and hen thou liest don, and hen thou risest up.
And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thy hand, and they shall be for frontlets beteen thine eyes.
And thou shalt rite them upon the door-posts of thy house, and upon thy gates.
And it shall be, hen Jehovah thy God shall bring thee into the land hich he sare unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give thee, great and goodly cities, hich thou buildest not,
and houses full of all good things, hich thou filledst not, and cisterns hen out, hich thou heedst not, vineyards and olive-trees, hich thou plantedst not, and thou shalt eat and be full;
then beare lest thou forget Jehovah, ho brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
Thou shalt fear Jehovah thy God; and him shalt thou serve, and shalt sear by his name.
Ye shall not go after other gods, of the gods of the peoples that are round about you;
for Jehovah thy God in the midst of thee is a jealous God; lest the anger of Jehovah thy God be kindled against thee, and he destroy thee from off the face of the earth.
Ye shall not tempt Jehovah your God, as ye tempted him in Massah.
Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of Jehovah your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes, hich he hath commanded thee.
And thou shalt do that hich is right and good in the sight of Jehovah; that it may be ell ith thee, and that thou mayest go in and possess the good land hich Jehovah sare unto thy fathers,
to thrust out all thine enemies from before thee, as Jehovah hath spoken.
When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the ordinances, hich Jehovah our God hath commanded you?
then thou shalt say unto thy son, We ere Pharaoh’s bondmen in Egypt: and Jehovah brought us out of Egypt ith a mighty hand;
and Jehovah shoed signs and onders, great and sore, upon Egypt, upon Pharaoh, and upon all his house, before our eyes;
and he brought us out from thence, that he might bring us in, to give us the land hich he sare unto our fathers.
And Jehovah commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear Jehovah our God, for our good alays, that he might preserve us alive, as at this day.
