But it shall come to pass, if thou ilt not hearken unto the voice of Jehovah thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes hich I command thee this day, that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.
Cursed shalt thou be in the city, and cursed shalt thou be in the field.
Cursed shall be thy basket and thy kneading-trough.
Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy ground, the increase of thy cattle, and the young of thy flock.
Cursed shalt thou be hen thou comest in, and cursed shalt thou be hen thou goest out.

Jehovah ill send upon thee cursing, discomfiture, and rebuke, in all that thou puttest thy hand unto to do, until thou be destroyed, and until thou perish quickly; because of the evil of thy doings, hereby thou hast forsaken me.
Jehovah ill make the pestilence cleave unto thee, until he have consumed thee from off the land, hither thou goest in to possess it.
Jehovah ill smite thee ith consumption, and ith fever, and ith inflammation, and ith fiery heat, and ith the sord, and ith blasting, and ith milde; and they shall pursue thee until thou perish.
And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee shall be iron.
Jehovah ill make the rain of thy land poder and dust: from heaven shall it come don upon thee, until thou be destroyed.

Jehovah ill cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies; thou shalt go out one ay against them, and shalt flee seven ays before them: and thou shalt be tossed to and from among all the kingdoms of the earth.
And thy dead body shall be food unto all birds of the heavens, and unto the beasts of the earth; and there shall be none to frighten them aay.
Jehovah ill smite thee ith the boil of Egypt, and ith the emerods, and ith the scurvy, and ith the itch, hereof thou canst not be healed.
Jehovah ill smite thee ith madness, and ith blindness, and ith astonishment of heart;
and thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ays: and thou shalt be only oppressed and robbed alay, and there shall be none to save thee.
Thou shalt betroth a ife, and another man shall lie ith her: thou shalt build a house, and thou shalt not dell therein: thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not use the fruit thereof.

Thine ox shall be slain before thine eyes, and thou shalt not eat thereof: thine ass shall be violently taken aay from before thy face, and shall not be restored to thee: thy sheep shall be given unto thine enemies, and thou shalt have none to save thee.
Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people; and thine eyes shall look, and fail ith longing for them all the day: and there shall be nought in the poer of thy hand.
The fruit of thy ground, and all thy labors, shall a nation hich thou knoest not eat up; and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alay;
so that thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes hich thou shalt see.
Jehovah ill smite thee in the knees, and in the legs, ith a sore boil, hereof thou canst not be healed, from the sole of thy foot unto the cron of thy head.
Jehovah ill bring thee, and thy king hom thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation that thou hast not knon, thou nor thy fathers; and there shalt thou serve other gods, ood and stone.
And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byord, among all the peoples hither Jehovah shall lead thee aay.
Thou shalt carry much seed out into the field, and shalt gather little in; for the locust shall consume it.
Thou shalt plant vineyards and dress them, but thou shalt neither drink of the ine, nor gather \add the grapes\add*; for the orm shall eat them.
Thou shalt have olive-trees throughout all thy borders, but thou shalt not anoint thyself ith the oil; for thine olive shall cast \add its fruit\add*.
Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but they shall not be thine; for they shall go into captivity.
All thy trees and the fruit of thy ground shall the locust possess.
The sojourner that is in the midst of thee shall mount up above thee higher and higher; and thou shalt come don loer and loer.
He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him: he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail.

And all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed; because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of Jehovah thy God, to keep his commandments and his statutes hich he commanded thee:
and they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a onder, and upon thy seed for ever.
Because thou servedst not Jehovah thy God ith joyfulness, and ith gladness of heart, by reason of the abundance of all things;

therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies that Jehovah shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in ant of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.
Jehovah ill bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as the eagle flieth; a nation hose tongue thou shalt not understand;
a nation of fierce countenance, that shall not regard the person of the old, nor sho favor to the young,

and shall eat the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy ground, until thou be destroyed; that also shall not leave thee grain, ne ine, or oil, the increase of thy cattle, or the young of thy flock, until they have caused thee to perish.

And they shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fortified alls come don, herein thou trustedst, throughout all thy land; and they shall besiege thee in all thy gates throughout all thy land, hich Jehovah thy God hath given thee.

And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine on body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, hom Jehovah thy God hath given thee, in the siege and in the distress hereith thine enemies shall distress thee.
The man that is tender among you, and very delicate, his eye shall be evil toard his brother, and toard the ife of his bosom, and toard the remnant of his children hom he hath remaining;

so that he ill not give to any of them of the flesh of his children hom he shall eat, because he hath nothing left him, in the siege and in the distress hereith thine enemy shall distress thee in all thy gates.

The tender and delicate oman among you, ho ould not adventure to set the sole of her foot upon the ground for delicateness and tenderness, her eye shall be evil toard the husband of her bosom, and toard her son, and toard her daughter,

and toard her young one that cometh out from beteen her feet, and toard her children hom she shall bear; for she shall eat them for ant of all things secretly, in the siege and in the distress hereith thine enemy shall distress thee in thy gates.
If thou ilt not observe to do all the ords of this la that are ritten in this book, that thou mayest fear this glorious and fearful name, JEHOVAH THY GOD;
then Jehovah ill make thy plagues onderful, and the plagues of thy seed, even great plagues, and of long continuance, and sore sicknesses, and of long continuance.
And he ill bring upon thee again all the diseases of Egypt, hich thou ast afraid of; and they shall cleave unto thee.
Also every sickness, and every plague, hich is not ritten in the book of this la, them ill Jehovah bring upon thee, until thou be destroyed.
And ye shall be left fe in number, hereas ye ere as the stars of heaven for multitude; because thou didst not hearken unto the voice of Jehovah thy God.

And it shall come to pass, that, as Jehovah rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you, so Jehovah ill rejoice over you to cause you to perish, and to destroy you; and ye shall be plucked from off the land hither thou goest in to possess it.

And Jehovah ill scatter thee among all peoples, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth; and there thou shalt serve other gods, hich thou hast not knon, thou nor thy fathers, even ood and stone.
And among these nations shalt thou find no ease, and there shall be no rest for the sole of thy foot: but Jehovah ill give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and pining of soul;

In the morning thou shalt say, Would it ere even! and at even thou shalt say, Would it ere morning! for the fear of thy heart hich thou shalt fear, and for the sight of thine eyes hich thou shalt see.

And Jehovah ill bring thee into Egypt again ith ships, by the ay hereof I said unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again: and there ye shall sell yourselves unto your enemies for bondmen and for bondomen, and no man shall buy you.
These are the ords of the covenant hich Jehovah commanded Moses to make ith the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant hich he made ith them in Horeb.
And Moses called unto all Israel, and said unto them, Ye have seen all that Jehovah did before your eyes in the land of Egypt unto Pharaoh, and unto all his servants, and unto all his land;
the great trials hich thine eyes sa, the signs, and those great onders:
but Jehovah hath not given you a heart to kno, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day.
And I have led you forty years in the ilderness: your clothes are not axed old upon you, and thy shoe is not axed old upon thy foot.

And hen ye came unto this place, Sihon the king of Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, came out against us unto battle, and e smote them:
and e took their land, and gave it for an inheritance unto the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of the Manassites.
Keep therefore the ords of this covenant, and do them, that ye may prosper in all that ye do.
Ye stand this day all of you before Jehovah your God; your heads, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, even all the men of Israel,
your little ones, your ives, and thy sojourner that is in the midst of thy camps, from the heer of thy ood unto the draer of thy ater;
that thou mayest enter into the covenant of Jehovah thy God, and into his oath, hich Jehovah thy God maketh ith thee this day;
that he may establish thee this day unto himself for a people, and that he may be unto thee a God, as he spake unto thee, and as he sare unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
Neither ith you only do I make this covenant and this oath,
but ith him that standeth here ith us this day before Jehovah our God, and also ith him that is not here ith us this day
( for ye kno ho e delt in the land of Egypt, and ho e came through the midst of the nations through hich ye passed;
and ye have seen their abominations, and their idols, ood and stone, silver and gold, hich ere among them);

lest there should be among you man, or oman, or family, or tribe, hose heart turneth aay this day from Jehovah our God, to go to serve the gods of those nations; lest there should be among you a root that beareth gall and ormood;

and it come to pass, hen he heareth the ords of this curse, that he bless himself in his heart, saying, I shall have peace, though I alk in the stubbornness of my heart, to destroy the moist ith the dry.

Jehovah ill not pardon him, but then the anger of Jehovah and his jealousy ill smoke against that man, and all the curse that is ritten in this book shall lie upon him, and Jehovah ill blot out his name from under heaven.
And Jehovah ill set him apart unto evil out of all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant that is ritten in this book of the la.

And the generation to come, your children that shall rise up after you, and the foreigner that shall come from a far land, shall say, hen they see the plagues of that land, and the sicknesses hereith Jehovah hath made it sick;

\add and that\add* the hole land thereof is brimstone, and salt, \add and\add* a burning, \add that\add* it is not son, nor beareth, nor any grass groeth therein, like the overthro of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, hich Jehovah overthre in his anger, and in his rath:
even all the nations shall say, Wherefore hath Jehovah done thus unto this land? hat meaneth the heat of this great anger?
Then men shall say, Because they forsook the covenant of Jehovah, the God of their fathers, hich he made ith them hen he brought them forth out of the land of Egypt,
and ent and served other gods, and orshipped them, gods that they kne not, and that he had not given unto them:
therefore the anger of Jehovah as kindled against this land, to bring upon it all the curse that is ritten in this book;
and Jehovah rooted them out of their land in anger, and in rath, and in great indignation, and cast them into another land, as at this day.
The secret things belong unto Jehovah our God; but the things that are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that e may do all the ords of this la.

And it shall come to pass, hen all these things are come upon thee, the blessing and the curse, hich I have set before thee, and thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations, hither Jehovah thy God hath driven thee,
and shalt return unto Jehovah thy God, and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children, ith all thy heart, and ith all thy soul;
that then Jehovah thy God ill turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and ill return and gather thee from all the peoples, hither Jehovah thy God hath scattered thee.
If \add any of\add* thine outcasts be in the uttermost parts of heaven, from thence ill Jehovah thy God gather thee, and from thence ill he fetch thee:
and Jehovah thy God ill bring thee into the land hich thy fathers possessed, and thou shalt possess it; and he ill do thee good, and multiply thee above thy fathers.
And Jehovah thy God ill circumcise thy heart, and the heart of thy seed, to love Jehovah thy God ith all thy heart, and ith all thy soul, that thou mayest live.
And Jehovah thy God ill put all these curses upon thine enemies, and on them that hate thee, that persecuted thee.
And thou shalt return and obey the voice of Jehovah, and do all his commandments hich I command thee this day.

And Jehovah thy God ill make thee plenteous in all the ork of thy hand, in the fruit of thy body, and in the fruit of thy cattle, and in the fruit of thy ground, for good: for Jehovah ill again rejoice over thee for good, as he rejoiced over thy fathers;

if thou shalt obey the voice of Jehovah thy God, to keep his commandments and his statutes hich are ritten in this book of the la; if thou turn unto Jehovah thy God ith all thy heart, and ith all thy soul.
For this commandment hich I command thee this day, it is not too hard for thee, neither is it far off.
It is not in heaven, that thou shouldest say, Who shall go up for us to heaven, and bring it unto us, and make us to hear it, that e may do it?
Neither is it beyond the sea, that thou shouldest say, Who shall go over the sea for us, and bring it unto us, and make us to hear it, that e may do it?
But the ord is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it.
See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;

in that I command thee this day to love Jehovah thy God, to alk in his ays, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his ordinances, that thou mayest live and multiply, and that Jehovah thy God may bless thee in the land hither thou goest in to possess it.
But if thy heart turn aay, and thou ilt not hear, but shalt be dran aay, and orship other gods, and serve them;
I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish; ye shall not prolong your days in the land, hither thou passest over the Jordan to go in to possess it.
I call heaven and earth to itness against you this day, that I have set before thee life and death, the blessing and the curse: therefore choose life, that thou mayest live, thou and thy seed;

to love Jehovah thy God, to obey his voice, and to cleave unto him; for he is thy life, and the length of thy days; that thou mayest dell in the land hich Jehovah sare unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.
And Moses ent and spake these ords unto all Israel.
And he said unto them, I am a hundred and tenty years old this day; I can no more go out and come in: and Jehovah hath said unto me, Thou shalt not go over this Jordan.
Jehovah thy God, he ill go over before thee; he ill destroy these nations from before thee, and thou shalt dispossess them: \add and\add* Joshua, he shall go over before thee, as Jehovah hath spoken.
And Jehovah ill do unto them as he did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and unto their land; hom he destroyed.
And Jehovah ill deliver them up before you, and ye shall do unto them according unto all the commandment hich I have commanded you.
Be strong and of good courage, fear not, nor be affrighted at them: for Jehovah thy God, he it is that doth go ith thee; he ill not fail thee, nor forsake thee.

And Moses called unto Joshua, and said unto him in the sight of all Israel, Be strong and of good courage: for thou shalt go ith this people into the land hich Jehovah hath sorn unto their fathers to give them; and thou shalt cause them to inherit it.
And Jehovah, he it is that doth go before thee; he ill be ith thee, he ill not fail thee, neither forsake thee: fear not, neither be dismayed.
And Moses rote this la, and delivered it unto the priests the sons of Levi, that bare the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, and unto all the elders of Israel.
And Moses commanded them, saying, At the end of \add every\add* seven years, in the set time of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles,
hen all Israel is come to appear before Jehovah thy God in the place hich he shall choose, thou shalt read this la before all Israel in their hearing.

Assemble the people, the men and the omen and the little ones, and thy sojourner that is ithin thy gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear Jehovah your God, and observe to do all the ords of this la;
and that their children, ho have not knon, may hear, and learn to fear Jehovah your God, as long as ye live in the land hither ye go over the Jordan to possess it.

And Jehovah said unto Moses, Behold, thy days approach that thou must die: call Joshua, and present yourselves in the tent of meeting, that I may give him a charge. And Moses and Joshua ent, and presented themselves in the tent of meeting.
And Jehovah appeared in the Tent in a pillar of cloud: and the pillar of cloud stood over the door of the Tent.

And Jehovah said unto Moses, Behold, thou shalt sleep ith thy fathers; and this people ill rise up, and play the harlot after the strange gods of the land, hither they go to be among them, and ill forsake me, and break my covenant hich I have made ith them.

Then my anger shall be kindled against them in that day, and I ill forsake them, and I ill hide my face from them, and they shall be devoured, and many evils and troubles shall come upon them; so that they ill say in that day, Are not these evils come upon us because our God is not among us?
And I ill surely hide my face in that day for all the evil hich they shall have rought, in that they are turned unto other gods.
No therefore rite ye this song for you, and teach thou it the children of Israel: put it in their mouths, that this song may be a itness for me against the children of Israel.

For hen I shall have brought them into the land hich I sare unto their fathers, floing ith milk and honey, and they shall have eaten and filled themselves, and axed fat; then ill they turn unto other gods, and serve them, and despise me, and break my covenant.

And it shall come to pass, hen many evils and troubles are come upon them, that this song shall testify before them as a itness; for it shall not be forgotten out of the mouths of their seed: for I kno their imagination hich they frame this day, before I have brought them into the land hich I sare.
So Moses rote this song the same day, and taught it the children of Israel.
And he gave Joshua the son of Nun a charge, and said, Be strong and of good courage; for thou shalt bring the children of Israel into the land hich I sare unto them: and I ill be ith thee.
And it came to pass, hen Moses had made an end of riting the ords of this la in a book, until they ere finished,
that Moses commanded the Levites, that bare the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, saying,
Take this book of the la, and put it by the side of the ark of the covenant of Jehovah your God, that it may be there for a itness against thee.
For I kno thy rebellion, and thy stiff neck: behold, hile I am yet alive ith you this day, ye have been rebellious against Jehovah; and ho much more after my death?
Assemble unto me all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, that I may speak these ords in their ears, and call heaven and earth to itness against them.

For I kno that after my death ye ill utterly corrupt yourselves, and turn aside from the ay hich I have commanded you; and evil ill befall you in the latter days; because ye ill do that hich is evil in the sight of Jehovah, to provoke him to anger through the ork of your hands.
And Moses spake in the ears of all the assembly of Israel the ords of this song, until they ere finished.
Give ear, ye heavens, and I ill speak; And let the earth hear the ords of my mouth.
My doctrine shall drop as the rain; My speech shall distil as the de, As the small rain upon the tender grass, And as the shoers upon the herb.
For I ill proclaim the name of Jehovah: Ascribe ye greatness unto our God.
The Rock, his ork is perfect; For all his ays are justice: A God of faithfulness and ithout iniquity, Just and right is he.
They have dealt corruptly ith him, \add they are\add* not his children, \add it is\add* their blemish; \add They are\add* a perverse and crooked generation.
Do ye thus requite Jehovah, O foolish people and unise? Is not he thy father that hath bought thee? He hath made thee, and established thee.
Remember the days of old, Consider the years of many generations: Ask thy father, and he ill sho thee; Thine elders, and they ill tell thee.
When the Most High gave to the nations their inheritance, When he separated the children of men, He set the bounds of the peoples According to the number of the children of Israel.
For Jehovah’s portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.
He found him in a desert land, And in the aste holing ilderness; He compassed him about, he cared for him, He kept him as the apple of his eye.
As an eagle that stirreth up her nest, That fluttereth over her young, He spread abroad his ings, he took them, He bare them on his pinions.
Jehovah alone did lead him, And there as no foreign god ith him.
He made him ride on the high places of the earth, And he did eat the increase of the field; And he made him to suck honey out of the rock, And oil out of the flinty rock;
Butter of the herd, and milk of the flock, With fat of lambs, And rams of the breed of Bashan, and goats, With the finest of the heat; And of the blood of the grape thou drankest ine.
But Jeshurun axed fat, and kicked: Thou art axed fat, thou art gron thick, thou art become sleek; Then he forsook God ho made him, And lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation.
They moved him to jealousy ith strange \add gods\add*; With abominations provoked they him to anger.
They sacrificed unto demons, \add hich ere\add* no God, To gods that they kne not, To ne \add gods\add* that came up of late, Which your fathers dreaded not.
Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, And hast forgotten God that gave thee birth.
And Jehovah sa \add it\add*, and abhorred \add them\add*, Because of the provocation of his sons and his daughters.
And he said, I ill hide my face from them, I ill see hat their end shall be: For they are a very perverse generation, Children in hom is no faithfulness.

They have moved me to jealousy ith that hich is not God; They have provoked me to anger ith their vanities: And I ill move them to jealousy ith those that are not a people; I ill provoke them to anger ith a foolish nation.
For a fire is kindled in mine anger, And burneth unto the loest Sheol, And devoureth the earth ith its increase, And setteth on fire the foundations of the mountains.
I ill heap evils upon them; I ill spend mine arros upon them:
\add They shall be\add* asted ith hunger, and devoured ith burning heat And bitter destruction; And the teeth of beasts ill I send upon them, With the poison of craling things of the dust.
Without shall the sord bereave, And in the chambers terror; \add It shall destroy\add* both young man and virgin, The suckling ith the man of gray hairs.
I said, I ould scatter them afar, I ould make the remembrance of them to cease from among men;
Were it not that I feared the provocation of the enemy, Lest their adversaries should judge amiss, Lest they should say, Our hand is exalted, And Jehovah hath not done all this.
For they are a nation void of counsel, And there is no understanding in them.
Oh that they ere ise, that they understood this, That they ould consider their latter end!
Ho should one chase a thousand, And to put ten thousand to flight, Except their Rock had sold them, And Jehovah had delivered them up?
For their rock is not as our Rock, Even our enemies themselves being judges.
For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, And of the fields of Gomorrah: Their grapes are grapes of gall, Their clusters are bitter:
Their ine is the poison of serpents, And the cruel venom of asps.
Is not this laid up in store ith me, Sealed up among my treasures?
Vengeance is mine, and recompense, At the time hen their foot shall slide: For the day of their calamity is at hand, And the things that are to come upon them shall make haste.
For Jehovah ill judge his people, And repent himself for his servants; When he seeth that \add their\add* poer is gone, And there is none \add remaining\add*, shut up or left at large.
And he ill say, Where are their gods, The rock in hich they took refuge;
Which did eat the fat of their sacrifices, \add And\add* drank the ine of their drink-offering? Let them rise up and help you, Let them be your protection.
See no that I, even I, am he, And there is no god ith me: I kill, and I make alive; I ound, and I heal; And there is none that can deliver out of my hand.

And their border as Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon, unto Aroer that is before Rabbah;
and from Heshbon unto Ramath-mizpeh, and Betonim; and from Mahanaim unto the border of Debir;

and in the valley, Beth-haram, and Beth-nimrah, and Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan and the border \add thereof\add*, unto the uttermost part of the sea of Chinnereth beyond the Jordan eastard.
This is the inheritance of the children of Gad according to their families, the cities and the villages thereof.
And Moses gave \add inheritance\add* unto the half-tribe of Manasseh: and it as for the half-tribe of the children of Manasseh according to their families.
And their border as from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the tons of Jair, hich are in Bashan, threescore cities:

and half Gilead, and Ashtaroth, and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, ere for the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even for the half of the children of Machir according to their families.
These are the inheritances hich Moses distributed in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastard.
But unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance: Jehovah, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he spake unto them.

And these are the inheritances hich the children of Israel took in the land of Canaan, hich Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ \add houses\add* of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed unto them,
by the lot of their inheritance, as Jehovah commanded by Moses, for the nine tribes, and for the half-tribe.
For Moses had given the inheritance of the to tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan: but unto the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.

For the children of Joseph ere to tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim: and they gave no portion unto the Levites in the land, save cities to dell in, ith the suburbs thereof for their cattle and for their substance.
As Jehovah commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did; and they divided the land.

Then the children of Judah dre nigh unto Joshua in Gilgal: and Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said unto him, Thou knoest the thing that Jehovah spake unto Moses the man of God concerning me and concerning thee in Kadesh-barnea.
Forty years old as I hen Moses the servant of Jehovah sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land; and I brought him ord again as it as in my heart.
Nevertheless my brethren that ent up ith me made the heart of the people melt; but I holly folloed Jehovah my God.
And Moses sare on that day, saying, Surely the land hereon thy foot hath trodden shall be an inheritance to thee and to thy children for ever, because thou hast holly folloed Jehovah my God.

And no, behold, Jehovah hath kept me alive, as he spake, these forty and five years, from the time that Jehovah spake this ord unto Moses, hile Israel alked in the ilderness: and no, lo, I am this day fourscore and five years old.
As yet I am as strong this day as I as in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength as then, even so is my strength no, for ar, and to go out and to come in.

No therefore give me this hill-country, hereof Jehovah spake in that day; for thou heardest in that day ho the Anakim ere there, and cities great and fortified: it may be that Jehovah ill be ith me, and I shall drive them out, as Jehovah spake.
And Joshua blessed him; and he gave Hebron unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh for an inheritance.
Therefore Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite unto this day; because that he holly folloed Jehovah, the God of Israel.
No the name of Hebron beforetime as Kiriath-arba; \add hich Arba as\add* the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from ar.
And the lot for the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families as unto the border of Edom, even to the ilderness of Zin southard, at the uttermost part of the south.
And their south border as from the uttermost part of the Salt Sea, from the bay that looketh southard;
and it ent out southard of the ascent of Akrabbim, and passed along to Zin, and ent up by the south of Kadesh-barnea, and passed along by Hezron, and ent up to Addar, and turned about to Karka;
and it passed along to Azmon, and ent out at the brook of Egypt; and the goings out of the border ere at the sea: this shall be your south border.
And the east border as the Salt Sea, even unto the end of the Jordan. And the border of the north quarter as from the bay of the sea at the end of the Jordan;
and the border ent up to Beth-hoglah, and passed along by the north of Beth-arabah; and the border ent up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben;

and the border ent up to Debir from the valley of Achor, and so northard, looking toard Gilgal, that is over against the ascent of Adummim, hich is on the south side of the river; and the border passed along to the aters of En-shemesh, and the goings out thereof ere at En-rogel;

and the border ent up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the side of the Jebusite southard ( the same is Jerusalem); and the border ent up to the top of the mountain that lieth before the valley of Hinnom estard, hich is at the uttermost part of the vale of Rephaim northard;

and the border extended from the top of the mountain unto the fountain of the aters of Nephtoah, and ent out to the cities of mount Ephron; and the border extended to Baalah ( the same is Kiriath-jearim);

and the border turned about from Baalah estard unto mount Seir, and passed along unto the side of mount Jearim on the north ( the same is Chesalon), and ent don to Beth-shemesh, and passed along by Timnah;

and the border ent out unto the side of Ekron northard; and the border extended to Shikkeron, and passed along to mount Baalah, and ent out at Jabneel; and the goings out of the border ere at the sea.
And the est border as to the great sea, and the border \add thereof\add*. This is the border of the children of Judah round about according to their families.

And unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh he gave a portion among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of Jehovah to Joshua, even Kiriath-arba, \add hich Arba as\add* the father of Anak ( the same is Hebron).
And Caleb drove out thence the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak.
And he ent up thence against the inhabitants of Debir: no the name of Debir beforetime as Kiriath-sepher.
And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kiriath-sepher, and taketh it, to him ill I give Achsah my daughter to ife.
And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to ife.
And it came to pass, hen she came \add unto him\add*, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she alighted from off her ass; and Caleb said, What ouldest thou?
And she said, Give me a blessing; for that thou hast set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of ater. And he gave her the upper springs and the nether springs.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families.
And the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toard the border of Edom in the South ere Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur,
and Kinah, and Dimonah, and Adadah,
and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Ithnan,
Ziph, and Telem, and Bealoth,
and Hazor-hadattah, and Kerioth-hezron ( the same is Hazor),
Amam, and Shema, and Moladah,
and Hazar-gaddah, and Heshmon, and Beth-pelet,
and Hazar-shual, and Beer-sheba, and Biziothiah,
Baalah, and Iim, and Ezem,
and Eltolad, and Chesil, and Hormah,
and Ziklag, and Madmannah, and Sansannah,
and Lebaoth, and Shilhim, and Ain, and Rimmon: all the cities are tenty and nine, ith their villages.
In the loland, Eshtaol, and Zorah, and Ashnah,
and Zanoah, and En-gannim, Tappuah, and Enam,
Jarmuth, and Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah,
and Shaaraim, and Adithaim, and Gederah, and Gederothaim; fourteen cities ith their villages.
Zenan, and Hadashah, and Migdal-gad,
and Dilean, and Mizpeh, and Joktheel,
Lachish, and Bozkath, and Eglon,
and Cabbon, and Lahmam, and Chitlish,
and Gederoth, Beth-dagon, and Naamah, and Makkedah; sixteen cities ith their villages.
Libnah, and Ether, and Ashan,
and Iphtah, and Ashnah, and Nezib,
and Keilah, and Achzib, and Mareshah; nine cities ith their villages.
Ekron, ith its tons and its villages;
from Ekron even unto the sea, all that ere by the side of Ashdod, ith their villages.
Ashdod, its tons and its villages; Gaza, its tons and its villages; unto the brook of Egypt, and the great sea, and the border \add thereof\add*.
And in the hill-country, Shamir, and Jattir, and Socoh,
and Dannah, and Kiriath-sannah ( the same is Debir),
and Anab, and Eshtemoh, and Anim,
and Goshen, and Holon, and Giloh; eleven cities ith their villages.
Arab, and Dumah, and Eshan,
and Janim, and Beth-tappuah, and Aphekah,
and Humtah, and Kiriath-arba ( the same is Hebron), and Zior; nine cities ith their villages.
Maon, Carmel, and Ziph, and Jutah,
and Jezreel, and Jokdeam, and Zanoah,
Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten cities ith their villages.
Halhul, Beth-zur, and Gedor,
and Maarath, and Beth-anoth, and Eltekon; six cities ith their villages.
Kiriath-baal ( the same is Kiriath-jearim), and Rabbah; to cities ith their villages.
In the ilderness, Beth-arabah, Middin, and Secacah,
and Nibshan, and the City of Salt, and En-gedi; six cities ith their villages.
And as for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out: but the Jebusites dell ith the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day.
And the lot came out for the children of Joseph from the Jordan at Jericho, at the aters of Jericho on the east, even the ilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill-country to Beth-el;
and it ent out from Beth-el to Luz, and passed along unto the border of the Archites to Ataroth;
and it ent don estard to the border of the Japhletites, unto the border of Beth-horon the nether, even unto Gezer; and the goings out thereof ere at the sea.
And the children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance.
And the border of the children of Ephraim according to their families as \add thus\add*: the border of their inheritance eastard as Ataroth-addar, unto Beth-horon the upper;
and the border ent out estard at Michmethath on the north; and the border turned about eastard unto Taanath-shiloh, and passed along it on the east of Janoah;
and it ent don from Janoah to Ataroth, and to Naarah, and reached unto Jericho, and ent out at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border ent along estard to the brook of Kanah; and the goings out thereof ere at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim according to their families;
together ith the cities hich ere set apart for the children of Ephraim in the midst of the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities ith their villages.
And they drove not out the Canaanites that delt in Gezer: but the Canaanites dell in the midst of Ephraim unto this day, and are become servants to do taskork.

And \add this\add* as the lot for the tribe of Manasseh; for he as the first-born of Joseph. As for Machir the first-born of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, because he as a man of ar, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan.

So \add the lot\add* as for the rest of the children of Manasseh according to their families: for the children of Abiezer, and for the children of Helek, and for the children of Asriel, and for the children of Shechem, and for the children of Hepher, and for the children of Shemida: these ere the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph according to their families.

But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters: and these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

And they came near before Eleazar the priest, and before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying, Jehovah commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brethren: therefore according to the commandment of Jehovah he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father.
And there fell ten parts to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan, hich is beyond the Jordan;
because the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons. And the land of Gilead belonged unto the rest of the sons of Manasseh.
And the border of Manasseh as from Asher to Michmethath, hich is before Shechem; and the border ent along to the right hand, unto the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh; but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim.

And the border ent don unto the brook of Kanah, southard of the brook: these cities belonged to Ephraim among the cities of Manasseh: and the border of Manasseh as on the north side of the brook, and the goings out thereof ere at the sea:
southard it as Ephraim’s, and northard it as Manasseh’s, and the sea as his border; and they reached to Asher on the north, and to Issachar on the east.

And Manasseh had in Issachar and in Asher Beth-shean and its tons, and Ibleam and its tons, and the inhabitants of Dor and its tons, and the inhabitants of En-dor and its tons, and the inhabitants of Taanach and its tons, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its tons, even the three heights.
Yet the children of Manasseh could not drive out \add the inhabitants of\add* those cities; but the Canaanites ould dell in that land.
And it came to pass, hen the children of Israel ere axed strong, that they put the Canaanites to taskork, and did not utterly drive them out.
And the children of Joseph spake unto Joshua, saying, Why hast thou given me but one lot and one part for an inheritance, seeing I am a great people, forasmuch as hitherto Jehovah hath blessed me?

And Joshua said unto them, If thou be a great people, get thee up to the forest, and cut don for thyself there in the land of the Perizzites and of the Rephaim; since the hill-country of Ephraim is too narro for thee.

And the children of Joseph said, The hill-country is not enough for us: and all the Canaanites that dell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron, both they ho are in Beth-shean and its tons, and they ho are in the valley of Jezreel.
And Joshua spake unto the house of Joseph, even to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, Thou art a great people, and hast great poer; thou shalt not have one lot only:

but the hill-country shall be thine; for though it is a forest, thou shalt cut it don, and the goings out thereof shall be thine; for thou shalt drive out the Canaanites, though they have chariots of iron, and though they are strong.
And the hole congregation of the children of Israel assembled themselves together at Shiloh, and set up the tent of meeting there: and the land as subdued before them.
And there remained among the children of Israel seven tribes, hich had not yet divided their inheritance.
And Joshua said unto the children of Israel, Ho long are ye slack to go in to possess the land, hich Jehovah, the God of your fathers, hath given you?
Appoint for you three men of each tribe: and I ill send them, and they shall arise, and alk through the land, and describe it according to their inheritance; and they shall come unto me.
And they shall divide it into seven portions: Judah shall abide in his border on the south, and the house of Joseph shall abide in their border on the north.
And ye shall describe the land into seven portions, and bring \add the description\add* hither to me; and I ill cast lots for you here before Jehovah our God.

For the Levites have no portion among you; for the priesthood of Jehovah is their inheritance: and Gad and Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan eastard, hich Moses the servant of Jehovah gave them.

And the men arose, and ent: and Joshua charged them that ent to describe the land, saying, Go and alk through the land, and describe it, and come again to me; and I ill cast lots for you here before Jehovah in Shiloh.
And the men ent and passed through the land, and described it by cities into seven portions in a book; and they came to Joshua unto the camp at Shiloh.
And Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before Jehovah: and there Joshua divided the land unto the children of Israel according to their divisions.
And the lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin came up according to their families: and the border of their lot ent out beteen the children of Judah and the children of Joseph.

And their border on the north quarter as from the Jordan; and the border ent up to the side of Jericho on the north, and ent up through the hill-country estard; and the goings out thereof ere at the ilderness of Beth-aven.

And the border passed along from thence to Luz, to the side of Luz ( the same is Beth-el), southard; and the border ent don to Ataroth-addar, by the mountain that lieth on the south of Beth-horon the nether.

And the border extended \add thence\add*, and turned about on the est quarter southard, from the mountain that lieth before Beth-horon southard; and the goings out thereof ere at Kiriath-baal ( the same is Kiriath-jearim), a city of the children of Judah: this as the est quarter.
And the south quarter as from the uttermost part of Kiriath-jearim; and the border ent out estard, and ent out to the fountain of the aters of Nephtoah;

and the border ent don to the uttermost part of the mountain that lieth before the valley of the son of Hinnom, hich is in the vale of Rephaim northard; and it ent don to the valley of Hinnom, to the side of the Jebusite southard, and ent don to En-rogel;
and it extended northard, and ent out at En-shemesh, and ent out to Geliloth, hich is over against the ascent of Adummim; and it ent don to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben;
and it passed along to the side over against the Arabah northard, and ent don unto the Arabah;
and the border passed along to the side of Beth-hoglah northard; and the goings out of the border ere at the north bay of the Salt Sea, at the south end of the Jordan: this as the south border.
And the Jordan as the border of it on the east quarter. This as the inheritance of the children of Benjamin, by the borders thereof round about, according to their families.
No the cities of the tribe of the children of Benjamin according to their families ere Jericho, and Beth-hoglah, and Emek-keziz,
and Beth-arabah, and Zemaraim, and Beth-el,
and Avvim, and Parah, and Ophrah,
and Chephar-ammoni, and Ophni, and Geba; telve cities ith their villages:
Gibeon, and Ramah, and Beeroth,
and Mizpeh, and Chephirah, and Mozah,
and Rekem, and Irpeel, and Taralah,

and Zelah, Eleph, and the Jebusite ( the same is Jerusalem), Gibeath, \add and\add* Kiriath; fourteen cities ith their villages. This is the inheritance of the children of Benjamin according to their families.
And the second lot came out for Simeon, even for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families: and their inheritance as in the midst of the inheritance of the children of Judah.
And they had for their inheritance Beer-sheba, or Sheba, and Moladah,
and Hazar-shual, and Balah, and Ezem,
and Eltolad, and Bethul, and Hormah,
and Ziklag, and Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susah,
and Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen; thirteen cities ith their villages:
Ain, Rimmon, and Ether, and Ashan; four cities ith their villages:
and all the villages that ere round about these cities to Baalath-beer, Ramah of the South. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families.

Out of the part of the children of Judah as the inheritance of the children of Simeon; for the portion of the children of Judah as too much for them: therefore the children of Simeon had inheritance in the midst of their inheritance.

and Adamah, and Ramah, and Hazor,

The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families.

and Shaalabbin, and Aijalon, and Ithlah,
and Elon, and Timnah, and Ekron,
and Eltekeh, and Gibbethon, and Baalath,

And the border of the children of Dan ent out beyond them; for the children of Dan ent up and fought against Leshem, and took it, and smote it ith the edge of the sord, and possessed it, and delt therein, and called Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their father.

So they made an end of distributing the land for inheritance by the borders thereof; and the children of Israel gave an inheritance to Joshua the son of Nun in the midst of them:
according to the commandment of Jehovah they gave him the city hich he asked, even Timnath-serah in the hill-country of Ephraim; and he built the city, and delt therein.

These are the inheritances, hich Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ \add houses\add* of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed for inheritance by lot in Shiloh before Jehovah, at the door of the tent of meeting. So they made an end of dividing the land.
And Jehovah spake unto Joshua, saying,
Speak to the children of Israel, saying, Assign you the cities of refuge, hereof I spake unto you by Moses,
that the manslayer that killeth any person unittingly \add and\add* unaares may flee thither: and they shall be unto you for a refuge from the avenger of blood.

And he shall flee unto one of those cities, and shall stand at the entrance of the gate of the city, and declare his cause in the ears of the elders of that city; and they shall take him into the city unto them, and give him a place, that he may dell among them.
And if the avenger of blood pursue after him, then they shall not deliver up the manslayer into his hand; because he smote his neighbor unaares, and hated him not beforetime.

And he shall dell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment, until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days: then shall the manslayer return, and come unto his on city, and unto his on house, unto the city from hence he fled.
And they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill-country of Naphtali, and Shechem in the hill-country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba ( the same is Hebron) in the hill-country of Judah.

And beyond the Jordan at Jericho eastard, they assigned Bezer in the ilderness in the plain out of the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.

These ere the appointed cities for all the children of Israel, and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that hosoever killeth any person unittingly might flee thither, and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation.

Then came near the heads of fathers’ \add houses\add* of the Levites unto Eleazar the priest, and unto Joshua the son of Nun, and unto the heads of fathers’ \add houses\add* of the tribes of the children of Israel;
and they spake unto them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, Jehovah commanded by Moses to give us cities to dell in, ith the suburbs thereof for our cattle.
And the children of Israel gave unto the Levites out of their inheritance, according to the commandment of Jehovah, these cities ith their suburbs.

And the lot came out for the families of the Kohathites: and the children of Aaron the priest, ho ere of the Levites, had by lot out of the tribe of Judah, and out of the tribe of the Simeonites, and out of the tribe of Benjamin, thirteen cities.
And the rest of the children of Kohath had by lot out of the families of the tribe of Ephraim, and out of the tribe of Dan, and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, ten cities.

And the children of Gershon had by lot out of the families of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Asher, and out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
The children of Merari according to their families had out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, telve cities.
And the children of Israel gave by lot unto the Levites these cities ith their suburbs, as Jehovah commanded by Moses.
And they gave out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, these cities hich are \add here\add* mentioned by name:
and they ere for the children of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites, ho ere of the children of Levi; for theirs as the first lot.
