But hen the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah, Jehovah raised them up a saviour, Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a man left-handed. And the children of Israel sent tribute by him unto Eglon the king of Moab.
And Ehud made him a sord hich had to edges, a cubit in length; and he girded it under his raiment upon his right thigh.
And he offered the tribute unto Eglon king of Moab: no Eglon as a very fat man.
And hen he had made an end of offering the tribute, he sent aay the people that bare the tribute.
But he himself turned back from the quarries that ere by Gilgal, and said, I have a secret errand unto thee, O king. And he said, Keep silence. And all that stood by him ent out from him.
And Ehud came unto him; and he as sitting by himself alone in the cool upper room. And Ehud said, I have a message from God unto thee. And he arose out of his seat.
And Ehud put forth his left hand, and took the sord from his right thigh, and thrust it into his body:
and the haft also ent in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, for he dre not the sord out of his body; and it came out behind.
Then Ehud ent forth into the porch, and shut the doors of the upper room upon him, and locked them.
No hen he as gone out, his servants came; and they sa, and, behold, the doors of the upper room ere locked; and they said, Surely he is covering his feet in the upper chamber.

And they tarried till they ere ashamed; and, behold, he opened not the doors of the upper room: therefore they took the key, and opened \add them\add*; and, behold, their lord as fallen don dead on the earth.
And Ehud escaped hile they tarried, and passed beyond the quarries, and escaped unto Seirah.
And it came to pass, hen he as come, that he ble a trumpet in the hill-country of Ephraim; and the children of Israel ent don ith him from the hill-country, and he before them.

And he said unto them, Follo after me; for Jehovah hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand. And they ent don after him, and took the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, and suffered not a man to pass over.
And they smote of Moab at that time about ten thousand men, every lusty man, and every man of valor; and there escaped not a man.
So Moab as subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land had rest fourscore years.
And after him as Shamgar the son of Anath, ho smote of the Philistines six hundred men ith an ox-goad: and he also saved Israel.
And the children of Israel again did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, hen Ehud as dead.
And Jehovah sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor; the captain of hose host as Sisera, ho delt in Harosheth of the Gentiles.
And the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah: for he had nine hundred chariots of iron; and tenty years he mightily oppressed the children of Israel.
No Deborah, a prophetess, the ife of Lappidoth, she judged Israel at that time.
And she delt under the palm-tree of Deborah beteen Ramah and Beth-el in the hill-country of Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.

And she sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh-naphtali, and said unto him, Hath not Jehovah, the God of Israel, commanded, \add saying\add*, Go and dra unto mount Tabor, and take ith thee ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun?
And I ill dra unto thee, to the river Kishon, Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, ith his chariots and his multitude; and I ill deliver him into thy hand.
And Barak said unto her, If thou ilt go ith me, then I ill go; but if thou ilt not go ith me, I ill not go.

And she said, I ill surely go ith thee: notithstanding, the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honor; for Jehovah ill sell Sisera into the hand of a oman. And Deborah arose, and ent ith Barak to Kedesh.
And Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali together to Kedesh; and there ent up ten thousand men at his feet: and Deborah ent up ith him.
No Heber the Kenite had separated himself from the Kenites, even from the children of Hobab the brother-in-la of Moses, and had pitched his tent as far as the oak in Zaanannim, hich is by Kedesh.
And they told Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam as gone up to mount Tabor.
And Sisera gathered together all his chariots, even nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people that ere ith him, from Harosheth of the Gentiles, unto the river Kishon.

And Deborah said unto Barak, Up; for this is the day in hich Jehovah hath delivered Sisera into thy hand; is not Jehovah gone out before thee? So Barak ent don from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.
And Jehovah discomfited Sisera, and all his chariots, and all his host, ith the edge of the sord before Barak; and Sisera alighted from his chariot, and fled aay on his feet.
But Barak pursued after the chariots, and after the host, unto Harosheth of the Gentiles: and all the host of Sisera fell by the edge of the sord; there as not a man left.
Hobeit Sisera fled aay on his feet to the tent of Jael the ife of Heber the Kenite; for there as peace beteen Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
And Jael ent out to meet Sisera, and said unto him, Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; fear not. And he turned in unto her into the tent, and she covered him ith a rug.
And he said unto her, Give me, I pray thee, a little ater to drink; for I am thirsty. And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him.
And he said unto her, Stand in the door of the tent, and it shall be, hen any man doth come and inquire of thee, and say, Is there any man here? that thou shalt say, No.

Then Jael Heber’s ife took a tent-pin, and took a hammer in her hand, and ent softly unto him, and smote the pin into his temples, and it pierced through into the ground; for he as in a deep sleep; so he sooned and died.

And, behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said unto him, Come, and I ill sho thee the man hom thou seekest. And he came unto her; and, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the tent-pin as in his temples.
So God subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel.
And the hand of the children of Israel prevailed more and more against Jabin the king of Canaan, until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.
Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day, saying,
For that the leaders took the lead in Israel, For that the people offered themselves illingly, Bless ye Jehovah.
Hear, O ye kings; give ear, O ye princes; I, \add even\add* I, ill sing unto Jehovah; I ill sing praise to Jehovah, the God of Israel.
Jehovah, hen thou entest forth out of Seir, When thou marchedst out of the field of Edom, The earth trembled, the heavens also dropped, Yea, the clouds dropped ater.
The mountains quaked at the presence of Jehovah, Even yon Sinai at the presence of Jehovah, the God of Israel. \b
In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, In the days of Jael, the highays ere unoccupied, And the travellers alked through byays.
The rulers ceased in Israel, they ceased, Until that I Deborah arose, That I arose a mother in Israel.
They chose ne gods; Then as ar in the gates: Was there a shield or spear seen Among forty thousand in Israel?
My heart is toard the governors of Israel, That offered themselves illingly among the people: Bless ye Jehovah.
Tell \add of it\add*, ye that ride on hite asses, Ye that sit on rich carpets, And ye that alk by the ay.

Far from the noise of archers, in the places of draing ater, There shall they rehearse the righteous acts of Jehovah, \add Even\add* the righteous acts of his rule in Israel. Then the people of Jehovah ent don to the gates. \b
Aake, aake, Deborah; Aake, aake, utter a song: Arise, Barak, and lead aay thy captives, thou son of Abinoam.
Then came don a remnant of the nobles \add and\add* the people; Jehovah came don for me against the mighty.
Out of Ephraim \add came don\add* they hose root is in Amalek; After thee, Benjamin, among thy peoples; Out of Machir came don governors, And out of Zebulun they that handle the marshal’s staff.
And the princes of Issachar ere ith Deborah; As as Issachar, so as Barak; Into the valley they rushed forth at his feet. By the atercourses of Reuben There ere great resolves of heart.
Why sattest thou among the sheepfolds, To hear the pipings for the flocks? At the atercourses of Reuben There ere great searchings of heart.
Gilead abode beyond the Jordan: And Dan, hy did he remain in ships? Asher sat still at the haven of the sea, And abode by his creeks.
Zebulun as a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death, And Naphtali, upon the high places of the field. \b
The kings came and fought; Then fought the kings of Canaan, In Taanach by the aters of Megiddo: They took no gain of money.
From heaven fought the stars, From their courses they fought against Sisera.
The river Kishon sept them aay, That ancient river, the river Kishon. O my soul, march on ith strength.
Then did the horsehoofs stamp By reason of the prancings, the prancings of their strong ones.
Curse ye Meroz, said the angel of Jehovah. Curse ye bitterly the inhabitants thereof, Because they came not to the help of Jehovah, To the help of Jehovah against the mighty. \b
Blessed above omen shall Jael be, The ife of Heber the Kenite; Blessed shall she be above omen in the tent.
He asked ater, \add and\add* she gave him milk; She brought him butter in a lordly dish.
She put her hand to the tent-pin, And her right hand to the orkmen’s hammer; And ith the hammer she smote Sisera, she smote through his head; Yea, she pierced and struck through his temples.
At her feet he boed, he fell, he lay; At her feet he boed, he fell: Where he boed, there he fell don dead. \b
Through the indo she looked forth, and cried, The mother of Sisera \add cried\add* through the lattice, Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why tarry the heels of his chariots?
Her ise ladies ansered her, Yea, she returned anser to herself,

Have they not found, have they not divided the spoil? A damsel, to damsels to every man; To Sisera a spoil of dyed garments, A spoil of dyed garments embroidered, Of dyed garments embroidered on both sides, on the necks of the spoil?
So let all thine enemies perish, O Jehovah: But let them that love him be as the sun hen he goeth forth in his might.
And the children of Israel did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah: and Jehovah delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years.
And the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel; and because of Midian the children of Israel made them the dens hich are in the mountains, and the caves, and the strongholds.
And so it as, hen Israel had son, that the Midianites came up, and the Amalekites, and the children of the east; they came up against them;
and they encamped against them, and destroyed the increase of the earth, till thou come unto Gaza, and left no sustenance in Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass.
For they came up ith their cattle and their tents; they came in as locusts for multitude; both they and their camels ere ithout number: and they came into the land to destroy it.
And Israel as brought very lo because of Midian; and the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah.
And it came to pass, hen the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah because of Midian,
that Jehovah sent a prophet unto the children of Israel: and he said unto them, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, I brought you up from Egypt, and brought you forth out of the house of bondage;
and I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all that oppressed you, and drove them out from before you, and gave you their land;
and I said unto you, I am Jehovah your God; ye shall not fear the gods of the Amorites, in hose land ye dell. But ye have not hearkened unto my voice.

And the angel of Jehovah came, and sat under the oak hich as in Ophrah, that pertained unto Joash the Abiezrite: and his son Gideon as beating out heat in the inepress, to hide it from the Midianites.
And the angel of Jehovah appeared unto him, and said unto him, Jehovah is ith thee, thou mighty man of valor.

And Gideon said unto him, Oh, my lord, if Jehovah is ith us, hy then is all this befallen us? and here are all his ondrous orks hich our fathers told us of, saying, Did not Jehovah bring us up from Egypt? but no Jehovah hath cast us off, and delivered us into the hand of Midian.
And Jehovah looked upon him, and said, Go in this thy might, and save Israel from the hand of Midian: have not I sent thee?
And he said unto him, Oh, Lord, hereith shall I save Israel? behold, my family is the poorest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.
And Jehovah said unto him, Surely I ill be ith thee, and thou shalt smite the Midianites as one man.
And he said unto him, If no I have found favor in thy sight, then sho me a sign that it is thou that talkest ith me.
Depart not hence, I pray thee, until I come unto thee, and bring forth my present, and lay it before thee. And he said, I ill tarry until thou come again.

And Gideon ent in, and made ready a kid, and unleavened cakes of an ephah of meal: the flesh he put in a basket, and he put the broth in a pot, and brought it out unto him under the oak, and presented it.
And the angel of God said unto him, Take the flesh and the unleavened cakes, and lay them upon this rock, and pour out the broth. And he did so.

Then the angel of Jehovah put forth the end of the staff that as in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and there ent up fire out of the rock, and consumed the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and the angel of Jehovah departed out of his sight.
And Gideon sa that he as the angel of Jehovah; and Gideon said, Alas, O Lord Jehovah! forasmuch as I have seen the angel of Jehovah face to face.
And Jehovah said unto him, Peace be unto thee; fear not: thou shalt not die.
Then Gideon built an altar there unto Jehovah, and called it Jehovah-shalom: unto this day it is yet in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

And it came to pass the same night, that Jehovah said unto him, Take thy father’s bullock, even the second bullock seven years old, and thro don the altar of Baal that thy father hath, and cut don the Asherah that is by it;

and build an altar unto Jehovah thy God upon the top of this stronghold, in the orderly manner, and take the second bullock, and offer a burnt-offering ith the ood of the Asherah hich thou shalt cut don.

Then Gideon took ten men of his servants, and did as Jehovah had spoken unto him: and it came to pass, because he feared his father’s household and the men of the city, so that he could not do it by day, that he did it by night.

And hen the men of the city arose early in the morning, behold, the altar of Baal as broken don, and the Asherah as cut don that as by it, and the second bullock as offered upon the altar that as built.
And they said one to another, Who hath done this thing? And hen they inquired and asked, they said, Gideon the son of Joash hath done this thing.
Then the men of the city said unto Joash, Bring out thy son, that he may die, because he hath broken don the altar of Baal, and because he hath cut don the Asherah that as by it.

And Joash said unto all that stood against him, Will ye contend for Baal? or ill ye save him? he that ill contend for him, let him be put to death hilst \add it is yet\add* morning: if he be a god, let him contend for himself, because one hath broken don his altar.
Therefore on that day he called him Jerubbaal, saying, Let Baal contend against him, because he hath broken don his altar.
Then all the Midianites and the Amalekites and the children of the east assembled themselves together; and they passed over, and encamped in the valley of Jezreel.
But the Spirit of Jehovah came upon Gideon; and he ble a trumpet; and Abiezer as gathered together after him.
And he sent messengers throughout all Manasseh; and they also ere gathered together after him: and he sent messengers unto Asher, and unto Zebulun, and unto Naphtali; and they came up to meet them.
And Gideon said unto God, If thou ilt save Israel by my hand, as thou hast spoken,

behold, I ill put a fleece of ool on the threshing-floor; if there be de on the fleece only, and it be dry upon all the ground, then shall I kno that thou ilt save Israel by my hand, as thou hast spoken.
And it as so; for he rose up early on the morro, and pressed the fleece together, and rung the de out of the fleece, a bolful of ater.

And Gideon said unto God, Let not thine anger be kindled against me, and I ill speak but this once: let me make trial, I pray thee, but this once ith the fleece; let it no be dry only upon the fleece, and upon all the ground let there be de.
And God did so that night: for it as dry upon the fleece only, and there as de on all the ground.

Then Jerubbaal, ho is Gideon, and all the people that ere ith him, rose up early, and encamped beside the spring of Harod: and the camp of Midian as on the north side of them, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.
And Jehovah said unto Gideon, The people that are ith thee are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hand, lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine on hand hath saved me.

No therefore proclaim in the ears of the people, saying, Whosoever is fearful and trembling, let him return and depart from mount Gilead. And there returned of the people tenty and to thousand; and there remained ten thousand.

And Jehovah said unto Gideon, The people are yet too many; bring them don unto the ater, and I ill try them for thee there: and it shall be, that of hom I say unto thee, This shall go ith thee, the same shall go ith thee; and of homsoever I say unto thee, This shall not go ith thee, the same shall not go.

So he brought don the people unto the ater: and Jehovah said unto Gideon, Every one that lappeth of the ater ith his tongue, as a dog lappeth, him shalt thou set by himself; likeise every one that boeth don upon his knees to drink.
And the number of them that lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, as three hundred men: but all the rest of the people boed don upon their knees to drink ater.
And Jehovah said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped ill I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thy hand; and let all the people go every man unto his place.

So the people took victuals in their hand, and their trumpets; and he sent all the men of Israel every man unto his tent, but retained the three hundred men: and the camp of Midian as beneath him in the valley.
And it came to pass the same night, that Jehovah said unto him, Arise, get thee don into the camp; for I have delivered it into thy hand.
But if thou fear to go don, go thou ith Purah thy servant don to the camp:

and thou shalt hear hat they say; and afterard shall thy hands be strengthened to go don into the camp. Then ent he don ith Purah his servant unto the outermost part of the armed men that ere in the camp.

And the Midianites and the Amalekites and all the children of the east lay along in the valley like locusts for multitude; and their camels ere ithout number, as the sand hich is upon the sea-shore for multitude.

And hen Gideon as come, behold, there as a man telling a dream unto his fello; and he said, Behold, I dreamed a dream; and, lo, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the camp of Midian, and came unto the tent, and smote it so that it fell, and turned it upside don, so that the tent lay flat.
And his fello ansered and said, This is nothing else save the sord of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel: into his hand God hath delivered Midian, and all the host.

And it as so, hen Gideon heard the telling of the dream, and the interpretation thereof, that he orshipped; and he returned into the camp of Israel, and said, Arise; for Jehovah hath delivered into your hand the host of Midian.
And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put into the hands of all of them trumpets, and empty pitchers, ith torches ithin the pitchers.
And he said unto them, Look on me, and do likeise: and, behold, hen I come to the outermost part of the camp, it shall be that, as I do, so shall ye do.
When I blo the trumpet, I and all that are ith me, then blo ye the trumpets also on every side of all the camp, and say, For Jehovah and for Gideon.

So Gideon, and the hundred men that ere ith him, came unto the outermost part of the camp in the beginning of the middle atch, hen they had but nely set the atch: and they ble the trumpets, and brake in pieces the pitchers that ere in their hands.

And the three companies ble the trumpets, and brake the pitchers, and held the torches in their left hands, and the trumpets in their right hands hereith to blo; and they cried, The sord of Jehovah and of Gideon.
And they stood every man in his place round about the camp; and all the host ran; and they shouted, and put \add them\add* to flight.

And they ble the three hundred trumpets, and Jehovah set every man’s sord against his fello, and against all the host; and the host fled as far as Beth-shittah toard Zererah, as far as the border of Abel-meholah, by Tabbath.
And the men of Israel ere gathered together out of Naphtali, and out of Asher, and out of all Manasseh, and pursued after Midian.

And Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill-country of Ephraim, saying, Come don against Midian, and take before them the aters, as far as Beth-barah, even the Jordan. So all the men of Ephraim ere gathered together, and took the aters as far as Beth-barah, even the Jordan.

And they took the to princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and they sle Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they sle at the inepress of Zeeb, and pursued Midian: and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon beyond the Jordan.
And the men of Ephraim said unto him, Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not, hen thou entest to fight ith Midian? And they did chide ith him sharply.
And he said unto them, What have I no done in comparison ith you? Is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer?
God hath delivered into your hand the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb: and hat as I able to do in comparison ith you? Then their anger as abated toard him, hen he had said that.
And Gideon came to the Jordan, \add and\add* passed over, he, and the three hundred men that ere ith him, faint, yet pursuing.
And he said unto the men of Succoth, Give, I pray you, loaves of bread unto the people that follo me; for they are faint, and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.
And the princes of Succoth said, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna no in thy hand, that e should give bread unto thine army?
And Gideon said, Therefore hen Jehovah hath delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, then I ill tear your flesh ith the thorns of the ilderness and ith briers.
And he ent up thence to Penuel, and spake unto them in like manner; and the men of Penuel ansered him as the men of Succoth had ansered.
And he spake also unto the men of Penuel, saying, When I come again in peace, I ill break don this toer.

No Zebah and Zalmunna ere in Karkor, and their hosts ith them, about fifteen thousand men, all that ere left of all the host of the children of the east; for there fell a hundred and tenty thousand men that dre sord.
And Gideon ent up by the ay of them that delt in tents on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and smote the host; for the host as secure.
And Zebah and Zalmunna fled; and he pursued after them; and he took the to kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and discomfited all the host.
And Gideon the son of Joash returned from the battle from the ascent of Heres.
And he caught a young man of the men of Succoth, and inquired of him: and he described for him the princes of Succoth, and the elders thereof, seventy and seven men.

And he came unto the men of Succoth, and said, Behold Zebah and Zalmunna, concerning hom ye did taunt me, saying, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna no in thy hand, that e should give bread unto thy men that are eary?
And he took the elders of the city, and thorns of the ilderness and briers, and ith them he taught the men of Succoth.
And he brake don the toer of Penuel, and sle the men of the city.
Then said he unto Zebah and Zalmunna, What manner of men ere they hom ye sle at Tabor? And they ansered, As thou art, so ere they; each one resembled the children of a king.
And he said, They ere my brethren, the sons of my mother: as Jehovah liveth, if ye had saved them alive, I ould not slay you.
And he said unto Jether his first-born, Up, and slay them. But the youth dre not his sord; for he feared, because he as yet a youth.
Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, Rise thou, and fall upon us; for as the man is, so is his strength. And Gideon arose, and sle Zebah and Zalmunna, and took the crescents that ere on their camels’ necks.
Then the men of Israel said unto Gideon, Rule thou over us, both thou, and thy son, and thy son’s son also; for thou hast saved us out of the hand of Midian.
And Gideon said unto them, I ill not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: Jehovah shall rule over you.
And Gideon said unto them, I ould make a request of you, that ye ould give me every man the ear-rings of his spoil. ( For they had golden ear-rings, because they ere Ishmaelites.)
And they ansered, We ill illingly give them. And they spread a garment, and did cast therein every man the ear-rings of his spoil.

And the eight of the golden ear-rings that he requested as a thousand and seven hundred \add shekels\add* of gold; besides the crescents, and the pendants, and the purple raiment that as on the kings of Midian, and besides the chains that ere about their camels’ necks.
And Gideon made an ephod thereof, and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and all Israel played the harlot after it there; and it became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house.
So Midian as subdued before the children of Israel, and they lifted up their heads no more. And the land had rest forty years in the days of Gideon.
And Jerubbaal the son of Joash ent and delt in his on house.
And Gideon had threescore and ten sons of his body begotten; for he had many ives.
And his concubine that as in Shechem, she also bare him a son, and he called his name Abimelech.
And Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age, and as buried in the sepulchre of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
And it came to pass, as soon as Gideon as dead, that the children of Israel turned again, and played the harlot after the Baalim, and made Baal-berith their god.
And the children of Israel remembered not Jehovah their God, ho had delivered them out of the hand of all their enemies on every side;
neither shoed they kindness to the house of Jerubbaal, \add ho is\add* Gideon, according to all the goodness hich he had shoed unto Israel.
And Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal ent to Shechem unto his mother’s brethren, and spake ith them, and ith all the family of the house of his mother’s father, saying,

Speak, I pray you, in the ears of all the men of Shechem, Whether is better for you, that all the sons of Jerubbaal, ho are threescore and ten persons, rule over you, or that one rule over you? remember also that I am your bone and your flesh.
And his mother’s brethren spake of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem all these ords: and their hearts inclined to follo Abimelech; for they said, He is our brother.
And they gave him threescore and ten \add pieces\add* of silver out of the house of Baal-berith, hereith Abimelech hired vain and light fellos, ho folloed him.

And he ent unto his father’s house at Ophrah, and sle his brethren the sons of Jerubbaal, being threescore and ten persons, upon one stone: but Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal as left; for he hid himself.
And all the men of Shechem assembled themselves together, and all the house of Millo, and ent and made Abimelech king, by the oak of the pillar that as in Shechem.

And hen they told it to Jotham, he ent and stood on the top of mount Gerizim, and lifted up his voice, and cried, and said unto them, Hearken unto me, ye men of Shechem, that God may hearken unto you.
The trees ent forth on a time to anoint a king over them; and they said unto the olive-tree, Reign thou over us.
But the olive-tree said unto them, Should I leave my fatness, hereith by me they honor God and man, and go to ave to and fro over the trees?
And the trees said to the fig-tree, Come thou, and reign over us.
But the fig-tree said unto them, Should I leave my seetness, and my good fruit, and go to ave to and fro over the trees?
And the trees said unto the vine, Come thou, and reign over us.
And the vine said unto them, Should I leave my ne ine, hich cheereth God and man, and go to ave to and fro over the trees?
Then said all the trees unto the bramble, Come thou, and reign over us.
And the bramble said unto the trees, If in truth ye anoint me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shade; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.

No therefore, if ye have dealt truly and uprightly, in that ye have made Abimelech king, and if ye have dealt ell ith Jerubbaal and his house, and have done unto him according to the deserving of his hands
( for my father fought for you, and adventured his life, and delivered you out of the hand of Midian:

and ye are risen up against my father’s house this day, and have slain his sons, threescore and ten persons, upon one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his maid-servant, king over the men of Shechem, because he is your brother);
if ye then have dealt truly and uprightly ith Jerubbaal and ith his house this day, then rejoice ye in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you:
but if not, let fire come out from Abimelech, and devour the men of Shechem, and the house of Millo; and let fire come out from the men of Shechem, and from the house of Millo, and devour Abimelech.
And Jotham ran aay, and fled, and ent to Beer, and delt there, for fear of Abimelech his brother.
And Abimelech as prince over Israel three years.
And God sent an evil spirit beteen Abimelech and the men of Shechem; and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously ith Abimelech:

that the violence done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal might come, and that their blood might be laid upon Abimelech their brother, ho sle them, and upon the men of Shechem, ho strengthened his hands to slay his brethren.
And the men of Shechem set liers-in-ait for him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed all that came along that ay by them: and it as told Abimelech.
And Gaal the son of Ebed came ith his brethren, and ent over to Shechem; and the men of Shechem put their trust in him.
And they ent out into the field, and gathered their vineyards, and trod \add the grapes\add*, and held festival, and ent into the house of their god, and did eat and drink, and cursed Abimelech.

And Gaal the son of Ebed said, Who is Abimelech, and ho is Shechem, that e should serve him? is not he the son of Jerubbaal? and Zebul his officer? serve ye the men of Hamor the father of Shechem: but hy should e serve him?
And ould that this people ere under my hand! then ould I remove Abimelech. And he said to Abimelech, Increase thine army, and come out.
And hen Zebul the ruler of the city heard the ords of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger as kindled.
And he sent messengers unto Abimelech craftily, saying, Behold, Gaal the son of Ebed and his brethren are come to Shechem; and, behold, they constrain the city \add to take part\add* against thee.
No therefore, up by night, thou and the people that are ith thee, and lie in ait in the field:

and it shall be, that in the morning, as soon as the sun is up, thou shalt rise early, and rush upon the city; and, behold, hen he and the people that are ith him come out against thee, then mayest thou do to them as thou shalt find occasion.
And Abimelech rose up, and all the people that ere ith him, by night, and they laid ait against Shechem in four companies.
And Gaal the son of Ebed ent out, and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city: and Abimelech rose up, and the people that ere ith him, from the ambushment.
And hen Gaal sa the people, he said to Zebul, Behold, there come people don from the tops of the mountains. And Zebul said unto him, Thou seest the shado of the mountains as if they ere men.
And Gaal spake again and said, See, there come people don by the middle of the land, and one company cometh by the ay of the oak of Meonenim.
Then said Zebul unto him, Where is no thy mouth, that thou saidst, Who is Abimelech, that e should serve him? is not this the people that thou hast despised? go out no, I pray, and fight ith them.
And Gaal ent out before the men of Shechem, and fought ith Abimelech.
And Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him, and there fell many ounded, even unto the entrance of the gate.
And Abimelech delt at Arumah: and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brethren, that they should not dell in Shechem.
And it came to pass on the morro, that the people ent out into the field; and they told Abimelech.

And he took the people, and divided them into three companies, and laid ait in the field; and he looked, and, behold, the people came forth out of the city; and he rose up against them, and smote them.
And Abimelech, and the companies that ere ith him, rushed forard, and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city: and the to companies rushed upon all that ere in the field, and smote them.
And Abimelech fought against the city all that day; and he took the city, and sle the people that ere therein: and he beat don the city, and soed it ith salt.
And hen all the men of the toer of Shechem heard thereof, they entered into the stronghold of the house of Elberith.
And it as told Abimelech that all the men of the toer of Shechem ere gathered together.

And Abimelech gat him up to mount Zalmon, he and all the people that ere ith him; and Abimelech took an axe in his hand, and cut don a bough from the trees, and took it up, and laid it on his shoulder: and he said unto the people that ere ith him, What ye have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done.

And all the people likeise cut don every man his bough, and folloed Abimelech, and put them to the stronghold, and set the stronghold on fire upon them; so that all the men of the toer of Shechem died also, about a thousand men and omen.
Then ent Abimelech to Thebez, and encamped against Thebez, and took it.
But there as a strong toer ithin the city, and thither fled all the men and omen, and all they of the city, and shut themselves in, and gat them up to the roof of the toer.
And Abimelech came unto the toer, and fought against it, and dre near unto the door of the toer to burn it ith fire.
And a certain oman cast an upper millstone upon Abimelech’s head, and brake his skull.
Then he called hastily unto the young man his armorbearer, and said unto him, Dra thy sord, and kill me, that men say not of me, A oman sle him. And his young man thrust him through, and he died.
And hen the men of Israel sa that Abimelech as dead, they departed every man unto his place.
Thus God requited the ickedness of Abimelech, hich he did unto his father, in slaying his seventy brethren;
and all the ickedness of the men of Shechem did God requite upon their heads: and upon them came the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal.
And after Abimelech there arose to save Israel Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar; and he delt in Shamir in the hill-country of Ephraim.
And he judged Israel tenty and three years, and died, and as buried in Shamir.
And after him arose Jair, the Gileadite; and he judged Israel tenty and to years.
And he had thirty sons that rode on thirty ass colts, and they had thirty cities, hich are called Havvoth-jair unto this day, hich are in the land of Gilead.
And Jair died, and as buried in Kamon.

And the children of Israel again did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, and served the Baalim, and the Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria, and the gods of Sidon, and the gods of Moab, and the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines; and they forsook Jehovah, and served him not.
And the anger of Jehovah as kindled against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the children of Ammon.

And they vexed and oppressed the children of Israel that year: eighteen years \add oppressed they\add* all the children of Israel that ere beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, hich is in Gilead.
And the children of Ammon passed over the Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim; so that Israel as sore distressed.
And the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah, saying, We have sinned against thee, even because e have forsaken our God, and have served the Baalim.
And Jehovah said unto the children of Israel, \add Did\add* not \add I save you\add* from the Egyptians, and from the Amorites, from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines?
The Sidonians also, and the Amalekites, and the Maonites, did oppress you; and ye cried unto me, and I saved you out of their hand.
Yet ye have forsaken me, and served other gods: herefore I ill save you no more.
Go and cry unto the gods hich ye have chosen; let them save you in the time of your distress.
And the children of Israel said unto Jehovah, We have sinned: do thou unto us hatsoever seemeth good unto thee; only deliver us, e pray thee, this day.
And they put aay the foreign gods from among them, and served Jehovah; and his soul as grieved for the misery of Israel.
Then the children of Ammon ere gathered together, and encamped in Gilead. And the children of Israel assembled themselves together, and encamped in Mizpah.
And the people, the princes of Gilead, said one to another, What man is he that ill begin to fight against the children of Ammon? he shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.
No Jephthah the Gileadite as a mighty man of valor, and he as the son of a harlot: and Gilead begat Jephthah.
And Gilead’s ife bare him sons; and hen his ife’s sons gre up, they drove out Jephthah, and said unto him, Thou shalt not inherit in our father’s house; for thou art the son of another oman.
Then Jephthah fled from his brethren, and delt in the land of Tob: and there ere gathered vain fellos to Jephthah, and they ent out ith him.
And it came to pass after a hile, that the children of Ammon made ar against Israel.
And it as so, that, hen the children of Ammon made ar against Israel, the elders of Gilead ent to fetch Jephthah out of the land of Tob;
and they said unto Jephthah, Come and be our chief, that e may fight ith the children of Ammon.
And Jephthah said unto the elders of Gilead, Did not ye hate me, and drive me out of my father’s house? and hy are ye come unto me no hen ye are in distress?

And the elders of Gilead said unto Jephthah, Therefore are e turned again to thee no, that thou mayest go ith us, and fight ith the children of Ammon; and thou shalt be our head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.
And Jephthah said unto the elders of Gilead, If ye bring me home again to fight ith the children of Ammon, and Jehovah deliver them before me, shall I be your head?
And the elders of Gilead said unto Jephthah, Jehovah shall be itness beteen us; surely according to thy ord so ill e do.
Then Jephthah ent ith the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and chief over them: and Jephthah spake all his ords before Jehovah in Mizpah.
And Jephthah sent messengers unto the king of the children of Ammon, saying, What hast thou to do ith me, that thou art come unto me to fight against my land?

And the king of the children of Ammon ansered unto the messengers of Jephthah, Because Israel took aay my land, hen he came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon even unto the Jabbok, and unto the Jordan: no therefore restore those \add lands\add* again peaceably.
And Jephthah sent messengers again unto the king of the children of Ammon;
and he said unto him, Thus saith Jephthah: Israel took not aay the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon;
but hen they came up from Egypt, and Israel ent through the ilderness unto the Red Sea, and came to Kadesh;

then Israel sent messengers unto the king of Edom, saying, Let me, I pray thee, pass through thy land; but the king of Edom hearkened not. And in like manner he sent unto the king of Moab; but he ould not: and Israel abode in Kadesh.

Then they ent through the ilderness, and ent around the land of Edom, and the land of Moab, and came by the east side of the land of Moab, and they encamped on the other side of the Arnon; but they came not ithin the border of Moab, for the Arnon as the border of Moab.
And Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon; and Israel said unto him, Let us pass, e pray thee, through thy land unto my place.
But Sihon trusted not Israel to pass through his border; but Sihon gathered all his people together, and encamped in Jahaz, and fought against Israel.
And Jehovah, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that country.
And they possessed all the border of the Amorites, from the Arnon even unto the Jabbok, and from the ilderness even unto the Jordan.
So no Jehovah, the God of Israel, hath dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and shouldest thou possess them?
Wilt not thou possess that hich Chemosh thy god giveth thee to possess? So homsoever Jehovah our God hath dispossessed from before us, them ill e possess.
And no art thou anything better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? did he ever strive against Israel, or did he ever fight against them?

While Israel delt in Heshbon and its tons, and in Aroer and its tons, and in all the cities that are along by the side of the Arnon, three hundred years; herefore did ye not recover them ithin that time?
I therefore have not sinned against thee, but thou doest me rong to ar against me: Jehovah, the Judge, be judge this day beteen the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.
Hobeit the king of the children of Ammon hearkened not unto the ords of Jephthah hich he sent him.
Then the Spirit of Jehovah came upon Jephthah, and he passed over Gilead and Manasseh, and passed over Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he passed over unto the children of Ammon.
And Jephthah voed a vo unto Jehovah, and said, If thou ilt indeed deliver the children of Ammon into my hand,

then it shall be, that hatsoever cometh forth from the doors of my house to meet me, hen I return in peace from the children of Ammon, it shall be Jehovah’s, and I ill offer it up for a burnt-offering.
So Jephthah passed over unto the children of Ammon to fight against them; and Jehovah delivered them into his hand.
And he smote them from Aroer until thou come to Minnith, even tenty cities, and unto Abel-cheramim, ith a very great slaughter. So the children of Ammon ere subdued before the children of Israel.
And Jephthah came to Mizpah unto his house; and, behold, his daughter came out to meet him ith timbrels and ith dances: and she as his only child; besides her he had neither son nor daughter.

And it came to pass, hen he sa her, that he rent his clothes, and said, Alas, my daughter! thou hast brought me very lo, and thou art one of them that trouble me; for I have opened my mouth unto Jehovah, and I cannot go back.

And she said unto him, My father, thou hast opened thy mouth unto Jehovah; do unto me according to that hich hath proceeded out of thy mouth, forasmuch as Jehovah hath taken vengeance for thee on thine enemies, even on the children of Ammon.
And she said unto her father, Let this thing be done for me: let me alone to months, that I may depart and go don upon the mountains, and beail my virginity, I and my companions.
And he said, Go. And he sent her aay for to months: and she departed, she and her companions, and beailed her virginity upon the mountains.
And it came to pass at the end of to months, that she returned unto her father, ho did ith her according to his vo hich he had voed: and she kne not man. And it as a custom in Israel,
that the daughters of Israel ent yearly to celebrate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

And the men of Ephraim ere gathered together, and passed northard; and they said unto Jephthah, Wherefore passedst thou over to fight against the children of Ammon, and didst not call us to go ith thee? e ill burn thy house upon thee ith fire.
And Jephthah said unto them, I and my people ere at great strife ith the children of Ammon; and hen I called you, ye saved me not out of their hand.

And hen I sa that ye saved me not, I put my life in my hand, and passed over against the children of Ammon, and Jehovah delivered them into my hand: herefore then are ye come up unto me this day, to fight against me?

Then Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead, and fought ith Ephraim; and the men of Gilead smote Ephraim, because they said, Ye are fugitives of Ephraim, ye Gileadites, in the midst of Ephraim, \add and\add* in the midst of Manasseh.

And the Gileadites took the fords of the Jordan against the Ephraimites. And it as so, that, hen \add any of\add* the fugitives of Ephraim said, Let me go over, the men of Gilead said unto him, Art thou an Ephraimite? If he said, Nay;

then said they unto him, Say no Shibboleth; and he said Sibboleth; for he could not frame to pronounce it right: then they laid hold on him, and sle him at the fords of the Jordan. And there fell at that time of Ephraim forty and to thousand.
And Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then died Jephthah the Gileadite, and as buried in \add one of\add* the cities of Gilead.
And after him Ibzan of Beth-lehem judged Israel.
And he had thirty sons; and thirty daughters he sent abroad, and thirty daughters he brought in from abroad for his sons. And he judged Israel seven years.
And Ibzan died, and as buried at Beth-lehem.
And after him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel; and he judged Israel ten years.
And Elon the Zebulunite died, and as buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
And after him Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.
And he had forty sons and thirty sons’ sons, that rode on threescore and ten ass colts: and he judged Israel eight years.
And Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died, and as buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill-country of the Amalekites.
And the children of Israel again did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah; and Jehovah delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
And there as a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, hose name as Manoah; and his ife as barren, and bare not.
And the angel of Jehovah appeared unto the oman, and said unto her, Behold no, thou art barren, and bearest not; but thou shalt conceive, and bear a son.
No therefore beare, I pray thee, and drink no ine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing:

for, lo, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come upon his head; for the child shall be a Nazirite unto God from the omb: and he shall begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.

Then the oman came and told her husband, saying, A man of God came unto me, and his countenance as like the countenance of the angel of God, very terrible; and I asked him not hence he as, neither told he me his name:

but he said unto me, Behold, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no drink no ine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing; for the child shall be a Nazirite unto God from the omb to the day of his death.
Then Manoah entreated Jehovah, and said, Oh, Lord, I pray thee, let the man of God hom thou didst send come again unto us, and teach us hat e shall do unto the child that shall be born.
And God hearkened to the voice of Manoah; and the angel of God came again unto the oman as she sat in the field: but Manoah her husband as not ith her.
And the oman made haste, and ran, and told her husband, and said unto him, Behold, the man hath appeared unto me, that came unto me the \add other\add* day.
And Manoah arose, and ent after his ife, and came to the man, and said unto him, Art thou the man that spakest unto the oman? And he said, I am.
And Manoah said, No let thy ords come to pass: hat shall be the ordering of the child, and \add ho\add* shall e do unto him?
And the angel of Jehovah said unto Manoah, Of all that I said unto the oman let her beare.
She may not eat of anything that cometh of the vine, neither let her drink ine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing; all that I commanded her let her observe.
And Manoah said unto the angel of Jehovah, I pray thee, let us detain thee, that e may make ready a kid for thee.

And the angel of Jehovah said unto Manoah, Though thou detain me, I ill not eat of thy bread; and if thou ilt make ready a burnt-offering, thou must offer it unto Jehovah. For Manoah kne not that he as the angel of Jehovah.
And Manoah said unto the angel of Jehovah, What is thy name, that, hen thy ords come to pass, e may do thee honor?
And the angel of Jehovah said unto him, Wherefore askest thou after my name, seeing it is onderful?
So Manoah took the kid ith the meal-offering, and offered it upon the rock unto Jehovah: and \add the angel\add* did ondrously, and Manoah and his ife looked on.

For it came to pass, hen the flame ent up toard heaven from off the altar, that the angel of Jehovah ascended in the flame of the altar: and Manoah and his ife looked on; and they fell on their faces to the ground.
But the angel of Jehovah did no more appear to Manoah or to his ife. Then Manoah kne that he as the angel of Jehovah.
And Manoah said unto his ife, We shall surely die, because e have seen God.

But his ife said unto him, If Jehovah ere pleased to kill us, he ould not have received a burnt-offering and a meal-offering at our hand, neither ould he have shoed us all these things, nor ould at this time have told such things as these.
And the oman bare a son, and called his name Samson: and the child gre, and Jehovah blessed him.
And the Spirit of Jehovah began to move him in Mahaneh-dan, beteen Zorah and Eshtaol.
And Samson ent don to Timnah, and sa a oman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines.
And he came up, and told his father and his mother, and said, I have seen a oman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines: no therefore get her for me to ife.

Then his father and his mother said unto him, Is there never a oman among the daughters of thy brethren, or among all my people, that thou goest to take a ife of the uncircumcised Philistines? And Samson said unto his father, Get her for me; for she pleaseth me ell.
But his father and his mother kne not that it as of Jehovah; for he sought an occasion against the Philistines. No at that time the Philistines had rule over Israel.
Then ent Samson don, and his father and his mother, to Timnah, and came to the vineyards of Timnah: and, behold, a young lion roared against him.
And the Spirit of Jehovah came mightily upon him, and he rent him as he ould have rent a kid; and he had nothing in his hand: but he told not his father or his mother hat he had done.
And he ent don, and talked ith the oman, and she pleased Samson ell.
And after a hile he returned to take her; and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion: and, behold, there as a sarm of bees in the body of the lion, and honey.

And he took it into his hands, and ent on, eating as he ent; and he came to his father and mother, and gave unto them, and they did eat: but he told them not that he had taken the honey out of the body of the lion.
And his father ent don unto the oman: and Samson made there a feast; for so used the young men to do.
And it came to pass, hen they sa him, that they brought thirty companions to be ith him.

And Samson said unto them, Let me no put forth a riddle unto you: if ye can declare it unto me ithin the seven days of the feast, and find it out, then I ill give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of raiment;
but if ye cannot declare it unto me, then shall ye give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of raiment. And they said unto him, Put forth thy riddle, that e may hear it.
And he said unto them, Out of the eater came forth food, And out of the strong came forth seetness.

And it came to pass on the seventh day, that they said unto Samson’s ife, Entice thy husband, that he may declare unto us the riddle, lest e burn thee and thy father’s house ith fire: have ye called us to impoverish us? is it not \add so\add*?

And Samson’s ife ept before him, and said, Thou dost but hate me, and lovest me not: thou hast put forth a riddle unto the children of my people, and hast not told it me. And he said unto her, Behold, I have not told it my father nor my mother, and shall I tell thee?

And she ept before him the seven days, hile their feast lasted: and it came to pass on the seventh day, that he told her, because she pressed him sore; and she told the riddle to the children of her people.

And the men of the city said unto him on the seventh day before the sun ent don, What is seeter than honey? and hat is stronger than a lion? And he said unto them, If ye had not ploed ith my heifer, Ye had not found out my riddle.

And the Spirit of Jehovah came mightily upon him, and he ent don to Ashkelon, and smote thirty men of them, and took their spoil, and gave the changes \add of raiment\add* unto them that declared the riddle. And his anger as kindled, and he ent up to his father’s house.
But Samson’s ife as \add given\add* to his companion, hom he had used as his friend.
But it came to pass after a hile, in the time of heat harvest, that Samson visited his ife ith a kid; and he said, I ill go in to my ife into the chamber. But her father ould not suffer him to go in.
And her father said, I verily thought that thou hadst utterly hated her; therefore I gave her to thy companion: is not her younger sister fairer than she? take her, I pray thee, instead of her.
And Samson said unto them, This time shall I be blameless in regard of the Philistines, hen I do them a mischief.
And Samson ent and caught three hundred foxes, and took firebrands, and turned tail to tail, and put a firebrand in the midst beteen every to tails.
And hen he had set the brands on fire, he let them go into the standing grain of the Philistines, and burnt up both the shocks and the standing grain, and also the oliveyards.

Then the Philistines said, Who hath done this? And they said, Samson, the son-in-la of the Timnite, because he hath taken his ife, and given her to his companion. And the Philistines came up, and burnt her and her father ith fire.
And Samson said unto them, If ye do after this manner, surely I ill be avenged of you, and after that I ill cease.
And he smote them hip and thigh ith a great slaughter: and he ent don and delt in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
Then the Philistines ent up, and encamped in Judah, and spread themselves in Lehi.
And the men of Judah said, Why are ye come up against us? And they said, To bind Samson are e come up, to do to him as he hath done to us.

Then three thousand men of Judah ent don to the cleft of the rock of Etam, and said to Samson, Knoest thou not that the Philistines are rulers over us? hat then is this that thou hast done unto us? And he said unto them, As they did unto me, so have I done unto them.
And they said unto him, We are come don to bind thee, that e may deliver thee into the hand of the Philistines. And Samson said unto them, Sear unto me, that ye ill not fall upon me yourselves.
And they spake unto him, saying, No; but e ill bind thee fast, and deliver thee into their hand: but surely e ill not kill thee. And they bound him ith to ne ropes, and brought him up from the rock.

When he came unto Lehi, the Philistines shouted as they met him: and the Spirit of Jehovah came mightily upon him, and the ropes that ere upon his arms became as flax that as burnt ith fire, and his bands dropped from off his hands.
And he found a fresh jabone of an ass, and put forth his hand, and took it, and smote a thousand men thereith.
And Samson said, With the jabone of an ass, heaps upon heaps, With the jabone of an ass have I smitten a thousand men.
And it came to pass, hen he had made an end of speaking, that he cast aay the jabone out of his hand; and that place as called Ramath-lehi.
And he as sore athirst, and called on Jehovah, and said, Thou hast given this great deliverance by the hand of thy servant; and no shall I die for thirst, and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised.

But God clave the hollo place that is in Lehi, and there came ater thereout; and hen he had drunk, his spirit came again, and he revived: herefore the name thereof as called En-hakkore, hich is in Lehi, unto this day.
And he judged Israel in the days of the Philistines tenty years.
And Samson ent to Gaza, and sa there a harlot, and ent in unto her.

And these are the golden tumors hich the Philistines returned for a trespass-offering unto Jehovah: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;

and the golden mice, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, both of fortified cities and of country villages, even unto the great stone, hereon they set don the ark of Jehovah, \add hich stone remaineth\add* unto this day in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite.

And Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel, saying, If ye do return unto Jehovah ith all your heart, then put aay the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct your hearts unto Jehovah, and serve him only; and he ill deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.

And the cities hich the Philistines had taken from Israel ere restored to Israel, from Ekron even unto Gath; and the border thereof did Israel deliver out of the hand of the Philistines. And there as peace beteen Israel and the Amorites.

And he ent from year to year in circuit to Beth-el, and Gilgal, and Mizpah; and he judged Israel in all those places.

and they said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons alk not in thy ays: no make us a king to judge us like all the nations.

No there as a man of Benjamin, hose name as Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, the son of a Benjamite, a mighty man of valor.

Saul as \add forty\add* years old hen he began to reign; and hen he had reigned to years over Israel,

Saul chose him three thousand men of Israel, hereof to thousand ere ith Saul in Michmash and in the mount of Beth-el, and a thousand ere ith Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin: and the rest of the people he sent every man to his tent.
And Jonathan smote the garrison of the Philistines that as in Geba; and the Philistines heard of it. And Saul ble the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, Let the Hebres hear.

When the men of Israel sa that they ere in a strait ( for the people ere distressed), then the people did hide themselves in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in coverts, and in pits.

And hen Saul sa that he behaved himself very isely, he stood in ae of him.
But all Israel and Judah loved David; for he ent out and came in before them.

And Saul said to David, Behold, my elder daughter Merab, her ill I give thee to ife: only be thou valiant for me, and fight Jehovah’s battles. For Saul said, Let not my hand be upon him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him.
And David said unto Saul, Who am I, and hat is my life, \add or\add* my father’s family in Israel, that I should be son-in-la to the king?
But it came to pass at the time hen Merab, Saul’s daughter, should have been given to David, that she as given unto Adriel the Meholathite to ife.
And Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved David: and they told Saul, and the thing pleased him.

And Saul said, I ill give him her, that she may be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him. Wherefore Saul said to David, Thou shalt this day be my son-in-la a second time.
And Saul commanded his servants, \add saying\add*, Commune ith David secretly, and say, Behold, the king hath delight in thee, and all his servants love thee: no therefore be the king’s son-in-la.
And Saul’s servants spake those ords in the ears of David. And David said, Seemeth it to you a light thing to be the king’s son-in-la, seeing that I am a poor man, and lightly esteemed?
And the servants of Saul told him, saying, On this manner spake David.

And Saul said, Thus shall ye say to David, The king desireth not any dory, but a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to be avenged of the king’s enemies. No Saul thought to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.
And hen his servants told David these ords, it pleased David ell to be the king’s son-in-la. And the days ere not expired;

and David arose and ent, he and his men, and sle of the Philistines to hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full number to the king, that he might be the king’s son-in-la. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter to ife.
And Saul sa and kne that Jehovah as ith David; and Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved him.
And Saul as yet the more afraid of David; and Saul as David’s enemy continually.
Then the princes of the Philistines ent forth: and it came to pass, as often as they ent forth, that David behaved himself more isely than all the servants of Saul; so that his name as much set by.
And Saul spake to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should slay David. But Jonathan, Saul’s son, delighted much in David.
And Jonathan told David, saying, Saul my father seeketh to slay thee: no therefore, I pray thee, take heed to thyself in the morning, and abide in a secret place, and hide thyself:
and I ill go out and stand beside my father in the field here thou art, and I ill commune ith my father of thee; and if I see aught, I ill tell thee.

And Jonathan spake good of David unto Saul his father, and said unto him, Let not the king sin against his servant, against David; because he hath not sinned against thee, and because his orks have been to thee-ard very good:

for he put his life in his hand, and smote the Philistine, and Jehovah rought a great victory for all Israel: thou saest it, and didst rejoice; herefore then ilt thou sin against innocent blood, to slay David ithout a cause?
And Saul hearkened unto the voice of Jonathan: and Saul sare, As Jehovah liveth, he shall not be put to death.
And Jonathan called David, and Jonathan shoed him all those things. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he as in his presence, as beforetime.
And there as ar again: and David ent out, and fought ith the Philistines, and sle them ith a great slaughter; and they fled before him.
And an evil spirit from Jehovah as upon Saul, as he sat in his house ith his spear in his hand; and David as playing ith his hand.
And Saul sought to smite David even to the all ith the spear; but he slipped aay out of Saul’s presence, and he smote the spear into the all: and David fled, and escaped that night.
And Saul sent messengers unto David’s house, to atch him, and to slay him in the morning: and Michal, David’s ife, told him, saying, If thou save not thy life to-night, to-morro thou ilt be slain.
So Michal let David don through the indo: and he ent, and fled, and escaped.
And Michal took the teraphim, and laid it in the bed, and put a pillo of goats’ \add hair\add* at the head thereof, and covered it ith the clothes.
And hen Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, He is sick.
And Saul sent the messengers to see David, saying, Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him.
And hen the messengers came in, behold, the teraphim as in the bed, ith the pillo of goats’ \add hair\add* at the head thereof.
And Saul said unto Michal, Why hast thou deceived me thus, and let mine enemy go, so that he is escaped? And Michal ansered Saul, He said unto me, Let me go; hy should I kill thee?
No David fled, and escaped, and came to Samuel to Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel ent and delt in Naioth.
And it as told Saul, saying, Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah.

And Saul sent messengers to take David: and hen they sa the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing as head over them, the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied.
And hen it as told Saul, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And Saul sent messengers again the third time, and they also prophesied.
Then ent he also to Ramah, and came to the great ell that is in Secu: and he asked and said, Where are Samuel and David? And one said, Behold, they are at Naioth in Ramah.
And he ent thither to Naioth in Ramah: and the Spirit of God came upon him also, and he ent on, and prophesied, until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
And he also stripped off his clothes, and he also prophesied before Samuel, and lay don naked all that day and all that night. Wherefore they say, Is Saul also among the prophets?
And David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and came and said before Jonathan, What have I done? hat is mine iniquity? and hat is my sin before thy father, that he seeketh my life?

And he said unto him, Far from it; thou shalt not die: behold, my father doeth nothing either great or small, but that he discloseth it unto me; and hy should my father hide this thing from me? it is not so.

And David sare moreover, and said, Thy father knoeth ell that I have found favor in thine eyes; and he saith, Let not Jonathan kno this, lest he be grieved: but truly as Jehovah liveth, and as thy soul liveth, there is but a step beteen me and death.
Then said Jonathan unto David, Whatsoever thy soul desireth, I ill even do it for thee.
And David said unto Jonathan, Behold, to-morro is the ne moon, and I should not fail to sit ith the king at meat: but let me go, that I may hide myself in the field unto the third day at even.
If thy father miss me at all, then say, David earnestly asked leave of me that he might run to Beth-lehem his city; for it is the yearly sacrifice there for all the family.
If he say thus, It is ell; thy servant shall have peace: but if he be roth, then kno that evil is determined by him.

Therefore deal kindly ith thy servant; for thou hast brought thy servant into a covenant of Jehovah ith thee: but if there be in me iniquity, slay me thyself; for hy shouldest thou bring me to thy father?
And Jonathan said, Far be it from thee; for if I should at all kno that evil ere determined by my father to come upon thee, then ould not I tell it thee?
Then said David to Jonathan, Who shall tell me if perchance thy father anser thee roughly?
And Jonathan said unto David, Come, and let us go out into the field. And they ent out both of them into the field.

And Jonathan said unto David, Jehovah, the God of Israel, \add be itness\add*: hen I have sounded my father about this time to-morro, \add or\add* the third day, behold, if there be good toard David, shall I not then send unto thee, and disclose it unto thee?

Jehovah do so to Jonathan, and more also, should it please my father to do thee evil, if I disclose it not unto thee, and send thee aay, that thou mayest go in peace: and Jehovah be ith thee, as he hath been ith my father.
And thou shalt not only hile yet I live sho me the lovingkindness of Jehovah, that I die not;
but also thou shalt not cut off thy kindness from my house for ever; no, not hen Jehovah hath cut off the enemies of David every one from the face of the earth.
So Jonathan made a covenant ith the house of David, \add saying\add*, And Jehovah ill require it at the hand of David’s enemies.
And Jonathan caused David to sear again, for the love that he had to him; for he loved him as he loved his on soul.
Then Jonathan said unto him, To-morro is the ne moon: and thou ilt be missed, because thy seat ill be empty.
And hen thou hast stayed three days, thou shalt go don quickly, and come to the place here thou didst hide thyself hen the business as in hand, and shalt remain by the stone Ezel.
And I ill shoot three arros on the side thereof, as though I shot at a mark.

And, behold, I ill send the lad, \add saying\add*, Go, find the arros. If I say unto the lad, Behold, the arros are on this side of thee; take them, and come; for there is peace to thee and no hurt, as Jehovah liveth.
But if I say thus unto the boy, Behold, the arros are beyond thee; go thy ay; for Jehovah hath sent thee aay.
And as touching the matter hich thou and I have spoken of, behold, Jehovah is beteen thee and me for ever.
So David hid himself in the field: and hen the ne moon as come, the king sat him don to eat food.
And the king sat upon his seat, as at other times, even upon the seat by the all; and Jonathan stood up, and Abner sat by Saul’s side: but David’s place as empty.
Nevertheless Saul spake not anything that day: for he thought, Something hath befallen him, he is not clean; surely he is not clean.

And it came to pass on the morro after the ne moon, \add hich as\add* the second \add day\add*, that David’s place as empty: and Saul said unto Jonathan his son, Wherefore cometh not the son of Jesse to meat, neither yesterday, nor to-day?
And Jonathan ansered Saul, David earnestly asked leave of me to go to Beth-lehem:

and he said, Let me go, I pray thee; for our family hath a sacrifice in the city; and my brother, he hath commanded me \add to be there\add*: and no, if I have found favor in thine eyes, let me get aay, I pray thee, and see my brethren. Therefore he is not come unto the king’s table.

Then Saul’s anger as kindled against Jonathan, and he said unto him, Thou son of a perverse rebellious oman, do not I kno that thou hast chosen the son of Jesse to thine on shame, and unto the shame of thy mother’s nakedness?
For as long as the son of Jesse liveth upon the ground, thou shalt not be established, nor thy kingdom. Wherefore no send and fetch him unto me, for he shall surely die.
And Jonathan ansered Saul his father, and said unto him, Wherefore should he be put to death? hat hath he done?
And Saul cast his spear at him to smite him; hereby Jonathan kne that it as determined of his father to put David to death.
So Jonathan arose from the table in fierce anger, and did eat no food the second day of the month; for he as grieved for David, because his father had done him shame.
And it came to pass in the morning, that Jonathan ent out into the field at the time appointed ith David, and a little lad ith him.
And he said unto his lad, Run, find no the arros hich I shoot. And as the lad ran, he shot an arro beyond him.
And hen the lad as come to the place of the arro hich Jonathan had shot, Jonathan cried after the lad, and said, Is not the arro beyond thee?
And Jonathan cried after the lad, Make speed, haste, stay not. And Jonathan’s lad gathered up the arros, and came to his master.
But the lad kne not anything: only Jonathan and David kne the matter.
And Jonathan gave his eapons unto his lad, and said unto him, Go, carry them to the city.

And as soon as the lad as gone, David arose out of \add a place\add* toard the South, and fell on his face to the ground, and boed himself three times: and they kissed one another, and ept one ith another, until David exceeded.

And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, forasmuch as e have sorn both of us in the name of Jehovah, saying, Jehovah shall be beteen me and thee, and beteen my seed and thy seed, for ever. And he arose and departed: and Jonathan ent into the city.
Then came David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest: and Ahimelech came to meet David trembling, and said unto him, Why art thou alone, and no man ith thee?

And David said unto Ahimelech the priest, The king hath commanded me a business, and hath said unto me, Let no man kno anything of the business hereabout I send thee, and hat I have commanded thee: and I have appointed the young men to such and such a place.
No therefore hat is under thy hand? give me five loaves of bread in my hand, or hatsoever there is present.
And the priest ansered David, and said, There is no common bread under my hand, but there is holy bread; if only the young men have kept themselves from omen.

And David ansered the priest, and said unto him, Of a truth omen have been kept from us about these three days; hen I came out, the vessels of the young men ere holy, though it as but a common journey; ho much more then to-day shall their vessels be holy?
So the priest gave him holy \add bread\add*; for there as no bread there but the shobread, that as taken from before Jehovah, to put hot bread in the day hen it as taken aay.
No a certain man of the servants of Saul as there that day, detained before Jehovah; and his name as Doeg the Edomite, the chiefest of the herdsmen that belonged to Saul.
And David said unto Ahimelech, And is there not here under thy hand spear or sord? for I have neither brought my sord nor my eapons ith me, because the king’s business required haste.

And the priest said, The sord of Goliath the Philistine, hom thou sleest in the vale of Elah, behold, it is here rapped in a cloth behind the ephod: if thou ilt take that, take it; for there is no other save that here. And David said, There is none like that; give it me.
And David arose, and fled that day for fear of Saul, and ent to Achish the king of Gath.

And the servants of Achish said unto him, Is not this David the king of the land? did they not sing one to another of him in dances, saying, Saul hath slain his thousands, And David his ten thousands?
And David laid up these ords in his heart, and as sore afraid of Achish the king of Gath.
And he changed his behavior before them, and feigned himself mad in their hands, and scrabbled on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle fall don upon his beard.
Then said Achish unto his servants, Lo, ye see the man is mad; herefore then have ye brought him to me?
Do I lack madmen, that ye have brought this fello to play the madman in my presence? shall this fello come into my house?
David therefore departed thence, and escaped to the cave of Adullam: and hen his brethren and all his father’s house heard it, they ent don thither to him.

And every one that as in distress, and every one that as in debt, and every one that as discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became captain over them: and there ere ith him about four hundred men.
And David ent thence to Mizpeh of Moab: and he said unto the king of Moab, Let my father and my mother, I pray thee, come forth, \add and be\add* ith you, till I kno hat God ill do for me.
And he brought them before the king of Moab: and they delt ith him all the hile that David as in the stronghold.
And the prophet Gad said unto David, Abide not in the stronghold; depart, and get thee into the land of Judah. Then David departed, and came into the forest of Hereth.

And Saul heard that David as discovered, and the men that ere ith him: no Saul as sitting in Gibeah, under the tamarisk-tree in Ramah, ith his spear in his hand, and all his servants ere standing about him.

And Saul said unto his servants that stood about him, Hear no, ye Benjamites; ill the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards, ill he make you all captains of thousands and captains of hundreds,

that all of you have conspired against me, and there is none that discloseth to me hen my son maketh a league ith the son of Jesse, and there is none of you that is sorry for me, or discloseth unto me that my son hath stirred up my servant against me, to lie in ait, as at this day?
Then ansered Doeg the Edomite, ho stood by the servants of Saul, and said, I sa the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
And he inquired of Jehovah for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sord of Goliath the Philistine.
Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests that ere in Nob: and they came all of them to the king.
And Saul said, Hear no, thou son of Ahitub. And he ansered, Here I am, my lord.

And Saul said unto him, Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, in that thou hast given him bread, and a sord, and hast inquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in ait, as at this day?
Then Ahimelech ansered the king, and said, And ho among all thy servants is so faithful as David, ho is the king’s son-in-la, and is taken into thy council, and is honorable in thy house?

Have I to-day begun to inquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute anything unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father; for thy servant knoeth nothing of all this, less or more.
And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father’s house.

And the king said unto the guard that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of Jehovah; because their hand also is ith David, and because they kne that he fled, and did not disclose it to me. But the servants of the king ould not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of Jehovah.

And the king said to Doeg, Turn thou, and fall upon the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and he sle on that day fourscore and five persons that did ear a linen ephod.
And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he ith the edge of the sord, both men and omen, children and sucklings, and oxen and asses and sheep, ith the edge of the sord.
And one of the sons of Ahimelech, the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.
And Abiathar told David that Saul had slain Jehovah’s priests.
And David said unto Abiathar, I kne on that day, hen Doeg the Edomite as there, that he ould surely tell Saul: I have occasioned \add the death\add* of all the persons of thy father’s house.
Abide thou ith me, fear not; for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life: for ith me thou shalt be in safeguard.
And they told David, saying, Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and are robbing the threshing-floors.
Therefore David inquired of Jehovah, saying, Shall I go and smite these Philistines? And Jehovah said unto David, Go, and smite the Philistines, and save Keilah.
And David’s men said unto him, Behold, e are afraid here in Judah: ho much more then if e go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?
Then David inquired of Jehovah yet again. And Jehovah ansered him, and said, Arise, go don to Keilah; for I ill deliver the Philistines into thy hand.
And David and his men ent to Keilah, and fought ith the Philistines, and brought aay their cattle, and sle them ith a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
And it came to pass, hen Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David to Keilah, that he came don ith an ephod in his hand.
And it as told Saul that David as come to Keilah. And Saul said, God hath delivered him into my hand; for he is shut in, by entering into a ton that hath gates and bars.
And Saul summoned all the people to ar, to go don to Keilah, to besiege David and his men.
And David kne that Saul as devising mischief against him; and he said to Abiathar the priest, Bring hither the ephod.
Then said David, O Jehovah, the God of Israel, thy servant hath surely heard that Saul seeketh to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.
