Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? ill Saul come don, as thy servant hath heard? O Jehovah, the God of Israel, I beseech thee, tell thy servant. And Jehovah said, He ill come don.
Then said David, Will the men of Keilah deliver up me and my men into the hand of Saul? And Jehovah said, They ill deliver thee up.

Then David and his men, ho ere about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah, and ent hithersoever they could go. And it as told Saul that David as escaped from Keilah; and he forbare to go forth.
And David abode in the ilderness in the strongholds, and remained in the hill-country in the ilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but God delivered him not into his hand.
And David sa that Saul as come out to seek his life: and David as in the ilderness of Ziph in the ood.
And Jonathan, Saul’s son, arose, and ent to David into the ood, and strengthened his hand in God.
And he said unto him, Fear not; for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Israel, and I shall be next unto thee; and that also Saul my father knoeth.
And they to made a covenant before Jehovah: and David abode in the ood, and Jonathan ent to his house.
Then came up the Ziphites to Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself ith us in the strongholds in the ood, in the hill of Hachilah, hich is on the south of the desert?
No therefore, O king, come don, according to all the desire of thy soul to come don; and our part shall be to deliver him up into the king’s hand.
And Saul said, Blessed be ye of Jehovah; for ye have had compassion on me.
Go, I pray you, make yet more sure, and kno and see his place here his haunt is, \add and\add* ho hath seen him there; for it is told me that he dealeth very subtly.

See therefore, and take knoledge of all the lurking-places here he hideth himself, and come ye again to me of a certainty, and I ill go ith you: and it shall come to pass, if he be in the land, that I ill search him out among all the thousands of Judah.
And they arose, and ent to Ziph before Saul: but David and his men ere in the ilderness of Maon, in the Arabah on the south of the desert.

And Saul and his men ent to seek him. And they told David: herefore he came don to the rock, and abode in the ilderness of Maon. And hen Saul heard \add that\add*, he pursued after David in the ilderness of Maon.

And Saul ent on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain: and David made haste to get aay for fear of Saul; for Saul and his men compassed David and his men round about to take them.
But there came a messenger unto Saul, saying, Haste thee, and come; for the Philistines have made a raid upon the land.
So Saul returned from pursuing after David, and ent against the Philistines: therefore they called that place Sela-hammahlekoth.
And David ent up from thence, and delt in the strongholds of En-gedi.
And it came to pass, hen Saul as returned from folloing the Philistines, that it as told him, saying, Behold, David is in the ilderness of En-gedi.
Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and ent to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the ild goats.
And he came to the sheepcotes by the ay, here as a cave; and Saul ent in to cover his feet. No David and his men ere abiding in the innermost parts of the cave.

And the men of David said unto him, Behold, the day of hich Jehovah said unto thee, Behold, I ill deliver thine enemy into thy hand, and thou shalt do to him as it shall seem good unto thee. Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe privily.
And it came to pass afterard, that David’s heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul’s skirt.
And he said unto his men, Jehovah forbid that I should do this thing unto my lord, Jehovah’s anointed, to put forth my hand against him, seeing he is Jehovah’s anointed.
So David checked his men ith these ords, and suffered them not to rise against Saul. And Saul rose up out of the cave, and ent on his ay.
David also arose afterard, and ent out of the cave, and cried after Saul, saying, My lord the king. And hen Saul looked behind him, David boed ith his face to the earth, and did obeisance.
And David said to Saul, Wherefore hearkenest thou to men’s ords, saying, Behold, David seeketh thy hurt?

Behold, this day thine eyes have seen ho that Jehovah had delivered thee to-day into my hand in the cave: and some bade me kill thee; but \add mine eye\add* spared thee; and I said, I ill not put forth my hand against my lord; for he is Jehovah’s anointed.

Moreover, my father, see, yea, see the skirt of thy robe in my hand; for in that I cut off the skirt of thy robe, and killed thee not, kno thou and see that there is neither evil nor transgression in my hand, and I have not sinned against thee, though thou huntest after my life to take it.
Jehovah judge beteen me and thee, and Jehovah avenge me of thee; but my hand shall not be upon thee.
As saith the proverb of the ancients, Out of the icked cometh forth ickedness; but my hand shall not be upon thee.
After hom is the king of Israel come out? after hom dost thou pursue? after a dead dog, after a flea.
Jehovah therefore be judge, and give sentence beteen me and thee, and see, and plead my cause, and deliver me out of thy hand.
And it came to pass, hen David had made an end of speaking these ords unto Saul, that Saul said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and ept.
And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I; for thou hast rendered unto me good, hereas I have rendered unto thee evil.
And thou hast declared this day ho that thou hast dealt ell ith me, forasmuch as hen Jehovah had delivered me up into thy hand, thou killedst me not.
For if a man find his enemy, ill he let him go ell aay? herefore Jehovah reard thee good for that hich thou hast done unto me this day.
And no, behold, I kno that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thy hand.
Sear no therefore unto me by Jehovah, that thou ilt not cut off my seed after me, and that thou ilt not destroy my name out of my father’s house.
And David sare unto Saul. And Saul ent home; but David and his men gat them up unto the stronghold.
And Samuel died; and all Israel gathered themselves together, and lamented him, and buried him in his house at Ramah. And David arose, and ent don to the ilderness of Paran.
And there as a man in Maon, hose possessions ere in Carmel; and the man as very great, and he had three thousand sheep, and a thousand goats: and he as shearing his sheep in Carmel.

No the name of the man as Nabal; and the name of his ife Abigail; and the oman as of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man as churlish and evil in his doings; and he as of the house of Caleb.
And David heard in the ilderness that Nabal as shearing his sheep.
And David sent ten young men, and David said unto the young men, Get you up to Carmel, and go to Nabal, and greet him in my name:
and thus shall ye say to him that liveth \add in prosperity\add*, Peace be unto thee, and peace be to thy house, and peace be unto all that thou hast.
And no I have heard that thou hast shearers: thy shepherds have no been ith us, and e did them no hurt, neither as there aught missing unto them, all the hile they ere in Carmel.

Ask thy young men, and they ill tell thee: herefore let the young men find favor in thine eyes; for e come in a good day: give, I pray thee, hatsoever cometh to thy hand, unto thy servants, and to thy son David.
And hen David’s young men came, they spake to Nabal according to all those ords in the name of David, and ceased.
And Nabal ansered David’s servants, and said, Who is David? and ho is the son of Jesse? there are many servants no-a-days that break aay every man from his master.
Shall I then take my bread, and my ater, and my flesh that I have killed for my shearers, and give it unto men of hom I kno not hence they are?
So David’s young men turned on their ay, and ent back, and came and told him according to all these ords.

And David said unto his men, Gird ye on every man his sord. And they girded on every man his sord; and David also girded on his sord: and there ent up after David about four hundred men; and to hundred abode by the baggage.
But one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s ife, saying, Behold, David sent messengers out of the ilderness to salute our master; and he railed at them.
But the men ere very good unto us, and e ere not hurt, neither missed e anything, as long as e ent ith them, hen e ere in the fields:
they ere a all unto us both by night and by day, all the hile e ere ith them keeping the sheep.
No therefore kno and consider hat thou ilt do; for evil is determined against our master, and against all his house: for he is such a orthless fello, that one cannot speak to him.

Then Abigail made haste, and took to hundred loaves, and to bottles of ine, and five sheep ready dressed, and five measures of parched grain, and a hundred clusters of raisins, and to hundred cakes of figs, and laid them on asses.
And she said unto her young men, Go on before me; behold, I come after you. But she told not her husband Nabal.
And it as so, as she rode on her ass, and came don by the covert of the mountain, that, behold, David and his men came don toard her; and she met them.
No David had said, Surely in vain have I kept all that this fello hath in the ilderness, so that nothing as missed of all that pertained unto him: and he hath returned me evil for good.
God do so unto the enemies of David, and more also, if I leave of all that pertain to him by the morning light so much as one man-child.
And hen Abigail sa David, she hasted, and alighted from her ass, and fell before David on her face, and boed herself to the ground.
And she fell at his feet, and said, Upon me, my lord, upon me be the iniquity; and let thy handmaid, I pray thee, speak in thine ears, and hear thou the ords of thy handmaid.

Let not my lord, I pray thee, regard this orthless fello, even Nabal; for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is ith him: but I thy handmaid sa not the young men of my lord, hom thou didst send.

No therefore, my lord, as Jehovah liveth, and as thy soul liveth, seeing Jehovah hath ithholden thee from bloodguiltiness, and from avenging thyself ith thine on hand, no therefore let thine enemies, and them that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.
And no this present hich thy servant hath brought unto my lord, let it be given unto the young men that follo my lord.

Forgive, I pray thee, the trespass of thy handmaid: for Jehovah ill certainly make my lord a sure house, because my lord fighteth the battles of Jehovah; and evil shall not be found in thee all thy days.

And though men be risen up to pursue thee, and to seek thy soul, yet the soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life ith Jehovah thy God; and the souls of thine enemies, them shall he sling out, as from the hollo of a sling.
And it shall come to pass, hen Jehovah shall have done to my lord according to all the good that he hath spoken concerning thee, and shall have appointed thee prince over Israel,

that this shall be no grief unto thee, nor offence of heart unto my lord, either that thou hast shed blood ithout cause, or that my lord hath avenged himself. And hen Jehovah shall have dealt ell ith my lord, then remember thy handmaid.
And David said to Abigail, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, ho sent thee this day to meet me:
and blessed be thy discretion, and blessed be thou, that hast kept me this day from bloodguiltiness, and from avenging myself ith mine on hand.

For in very deed, as Jehovah, the God of Israel, liveth, ho hath ithholden me from hurting thee, except thou hadst hasted and come to meet me, surely there had not been left unto Nabal by the morning light so much as one man-child.
So David received of her hand that hich she had brought him: and he said unto her, Go up in peace to thy house; see, I have hearkened to thy voice, and have accepted thy person.

And Abigail came to Nabal; and, behold, he held a feast in his house, like the feast of a king; and Nabal’s heart as merry ithin him, for he as very drunken: herefore she told him nothing, less or more, until the morning light.
And it came to pass in the morning, hen the ine as gone out of Nabal, that his ife told him these things, and his heart died ithin him, and he became as a stone.
And it came to pass about ten days after, that Jehovah smote Nabal, so that he died.

And hen David heard that Nabal as dead, he said, Blessed be Jehovah, that hath pleaded the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and hath kept back his servant from evil: and the evil-doing of Nabal hath Jehovah returned upon his on head. And David sent and spake concerning Abigail, to take her to him to ife.
And hen the servants of David ere come to Abigail to Carmel, they spake unto her, saying, David hath sent us unto thee, to take thee to him to ife.
And she arose, and boed herself ith her face to the earth, and said, Behold, thy handmaid is a servant to ash the feet of the servants of my lord.
And Abigail hasted, and arose, and rode upon an ass, ith five damsels of hers that folloed her; and she ent after the messengers of David, and became his ife.
David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel; and they became both of them his ives.
No Saul had given Michal his daughter, David’s ife, to Palti the son of Laish, ho as of Gallim.
And the Ziphites came unto Saul to Gibeah, saying, Doth not David hide himself in the hill of Hachilah, hich is before the desert?
Then Saul arose, and ent don to the ilderness of Ziph, having three thousand chosen men of Israel ith him, to seek David in the ilderness of Ziph.
And Saul encamped in the hill of Hachilah, hich is before the desert, by the ay. But David abode in the ilderness, and he sa that Saul came after him into the ilderness.
David therefore sent out spies, and understood that Saul as come of a certainty.

And David arose, and came to the place here Saul had encamped; and David beheld the place here Saul lay, and Abner the son of Ner, the captain of his host: and Saul lay ithin the place of the agons, and the people ere encamped round about him.
Then ansered David and said to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, brother to Joab, saying, Who ill go don ith me to Saul to the camp? And Abishai said, I ill go don ith thee.

So David and Abishai came to the people by night: and, behold, Saul lay sleeping ithin the place of the agons, ith his spear stuck in the ground at his head; and Abner and the people lay round about him.

Then said Abishai to David, God hath delivered up thine enemy into thy hand this day: no therefore let me smite him, I pray thee, ith the spear to the earth at one stroke, and I ill not smite him the second time.
And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not; for ho can put forth his hand against Jehovah’s anointed, and be guiltless?
And David said, As Jehovah liveth, Jehovah ill smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall go don into battle and perish.
Jehovah forbid that I should put forth my hand against Jehovah’s anointed: but no take, I pray thee, the spear that is at his head, and the cruse of ater, and let us go.

So David took the spear and the cruse of ater from Saul’s head; and they gat them aay: and no man sa it, nor kne it, neither did any aake; for they ere all asleep, because a deep sleep from Jehovah as fallen upon them.
Then David ent over to the other side, and stood on the top of the mountain afar off; a great space being beteen them;
and David cried to the people, and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, Anserest thou not, Abner? Then Abner ansered and said, Who art thou that criest to the king?

And David said to Abner, Art not thou a \add valiant\add* man? and ho is like to thee in Israel? herefore then hast thou not kept atch over thy lord the king? for there came one of the people in to destroy the king thy lord.

This thing is not good that thou hast done. As Jehovah liveth, ye are orthy to die, because ye have not kept atch over your lord, Jehovah’s anointed. And no see here the king’s spear is, and the cruse of ater that as at his head.
And Saul kne David’s voice, and said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And David said, It is my voice, my lord, O king.
And he said, Wherefore doth my lord pursue after his servant? for hat have I done? or hat evil is in my hand?

No therefore, I pray thee, let my lord the king hear the ords of his servant. If it be Jehovah that hath stirred thee up against me, let him accept an offering: but if it be the children of men, cursed be they before Jehovah; for they have driven me out this day that I should not cleave unto the inheritance of Jehovah, saying, Go, serve other gods.
No therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth aay from the presence of Jehovah: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as hen one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.
Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David; for I ill no more do thee harm, because my life as precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.
And David ansered and said, Behold the spear, O king! let then one of the young men come over and fetch it.
And Jehovah ill render to every man his righteousness and his faithfulness; forasmuch as Jehovah delivered thee into my hand to-day, and I ould not put forth my hand against Jehovah’s anointed.
And, behold, as thy life as much set by this day in mine eyes, so let my life be much set by in the eyes of Jehovah, and let him deliver me out of all tribulation.
Then Saul said to David, Blessed be thou, my son David: thou shalt both do mightily, and shalt surely prevail. So David ent his ay, and Saul returned to his place.

And David said in his heart, I shall no perish one day by the hand of Saul: there is nothing better for me than that I should escape into the land of the Philistines; and Saul ill despair of me, to seek me any more in all the borders of Israel: so shall I escape out of his hand.
And David arose, and passed over, he and the six hundred men that ere ith him, unto Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
And David delt ith Achish at Gath, he and his men, every man ith his household, even David ith his to ives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal’s ife.
And it as told Saul that David as fled to Gath: and he sought no more again for him.

And David said unto Achish, If no I have found favor in thine eyes, let them give me a place in one of the cities in the country, that I may dell there: for hy should thy servant dell in the royal city ith thee?
Then Achish gave him Ziklag that day: herefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day.
And the number of the days that David delt in the country of the Philistines as a full year and four months.

And David and his men ent up, and made a raid upon the Geshurites, and the Girzites, and the Amalekites; for those \add nations\add* ere the inhabitants of the land, ho ere of old, as thou goest to Shur, even unto the land of Egypt.
And David smote the land, and saved neither man nor oman alive, and took aay the sheep, and the oxen, and the asses, and the camels, and the apparel; and he returned, and came to Achish.
And Achish said, Against hom have ye made a raid to-day? And David said, Against the South of Judah, and against the South of the Jerahmeelites, and against the South of the Kenites.

And David saved neither man nor oman alive, to bring them to Gath, saying, Lest they should tell of us, saying, So did David, and so hath been his manner all the hile he hath delt in the country of the Philistines.
And Achish believed David, saying, He hath made his people Israel utterly to abhor him; therefore he shall be my servant for ever.

And it came to pass in those days, that the Philistines gathered their hosts together for arfare, to fight ith Israel. And Achish said unto David, Kno thou assuredly, that thou shalt go out ith me in the host, thou and thy men.
And David said to Achish, Therefore thou shalt kno hat thy servant ill do. And Achish said to David, Therefore ill I make thee keeper of my head for ever.
No Samuel as dead, and all Israel had lamented him, and buried him in Ramah, even in his on city. And Saul had put aay those that had familiar spirits, and the izards, out of the land.
And the Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and encamped in Shunem: and Saul gathered all Israel together, and they encamped in Gilboa.
And hen Saul sa the host of the Philistines, he as afraid, and his heart trembled greatly.
And hen Saul inquired of Jehovah, Jehovah ansered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.

Then said Saul unto his servants, Seek me a oman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and inquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, there is a oman that hath a familiar spirit at En-dor.

And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and ent, he and to men ith him, and they came to the oman by night: and he said, Divine unto me, I pray thee, by the familiar spirit, and bring me up homsoever I shall name unto thee.

And the oman said unto him, Behold, thou knoest hat Saul hath done, ho he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the izards, out of the land: herefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?
And Saul sare to her by Jehovah, saying, As Jehovah liveth, there shall no punishment happen to thee for this thing.
Then said the oman, Whom shall I bring up unto thee? And he said, Bring me up Samuel.
And hen the oman sa Samuel, she cried ith a loud voice; and the oman spake to Saul, saying, Why hast thou deceived me? for thou art Saul.
And the king said unto her, Be not afraid: for hat seest thou? And the oman said unto Saul, I see a god coming up out of the earth.

And he said unto her, What form is he of? And she said, An old man cometh up; and he is covered ith a robe. And Saul perceived that it as Samuel, and he boed ith his face to the ground, and did obeisance.

And Samuel said to Saul, Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up? And Saul ansered, I am sore distressed; for the Philistines make ar against me, and God is departed from me, and ansereth me no more, neither by prophets, nor by dreams: therefore I have called thee, that thou mayest make knon unto me hat I shall do.
And Samuel said, Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing Jehovah is departed from thee, and is become thine adversary?
And Jehovah hath done unto thee, as he spake by me: and Jehovah hath rent the kingdom out of thy hand, and given it to thy neighbor, even to David.
Because thou obeyedst not the voice of Jehovah, and didst not execute his fierce rath upon Amalek, therefore hath Jehovah done this thing unto thee this day.

Moreover Jehovah ill deliver Israel also ith thee into the hand of the Philistines; and to-morro shalt thou and thy sons be ith me: Jehovah ill deliver the host of Israel also into the hand of the Philistines.
Then Saul fell straightay his full length upon the earth, and as sore afraid, because of the ords of Samuel: and there as no strength in him; for he had eaten no bread all the day, nor all the night.

And the oman came unto Saul, and sa that he as sore troubled, and said unto him, Behold, thy handmaid hath hearkened unto thy voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have hearkened unto thy ords hich thou spakest unto me.
No therefore, I pray thee, hearken thou also unto the voice of thy handmaid, and let me set a morsel of bread before thee; and eat, that thou mayest have strength, hen thou goest on thy ay.
But he refused, and said, I ill not eat. But his servants, together ith the oman, constrained him; and he hearkened unto their voice. So he arose from the earth, and sat upon the bed.
And the oman had a fatted calf in the house; and she hasted, and killed it; and she took flour, and kneaded it, and did bake unleavened bread thereof:
and she brought it before Saul, and before his servants; and they did eat. Then they rose up, and ent aay that night.
No the Philistines gathered together all their hosts to Aphek: and the Israelites encamped by the fountain hich is in Jezreel.
And the lords of the Philistines passed on by hundreds, and by thousands; and David and his men passed on in the rearard ith Achish.

Then said the princes of the Philistines, What \add do\add* these Hebres \add here\add*? And Achish said unto the princes of the Philistines, Is not this David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, ho hath been ith me these days, or \add rather\add* these years, and I have found no fault in him since he fell aay \add unto me\add* unto this day?

But the princes of the Philistines ere roth ith him; and the princes of the Philistines said unto him, Make the man return, that he may go back to his place here thou hast appointed him, and let him not go don ith us to battle, lest in the battle he become an adversary to us: for hereith should this \add fello\add* reconcile himself unto his lord? should it not be ith the heads of these men?
Is not this David, of hom they sang one to another in dances, saying, Saul hath slain his thousands, And David his ten thousands?

Then Achish called David, and said unto him, As Jehovah liveth, thou hast been upright, and thy going out and thy coming in ith me in the host is good in my sight; for I have not found evil in thee since the day of thy coming unto me unto this day: nevertheless the lords favor thee not.
Wherefore no return, and go in peace, that thou displease not the lords of the Philistines.

And David said unto Achish, But hat have I done? and hat hast thou found in thy servant so long as I have been before thee unto this day, that I may not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?
And Achish ansered and said to David, I kno that thou art good in my sight, as an angel of God: notithstanding the princes of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up ith us to the battle.
Wherefore no rise up early in the morning ith the servants of thy lord that are come ith thee; and as soon as ye are up early in the morning, and have light, depart.
So David rose up early, he and his men, to depart in the morning, to return into the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines ent up to Jezreel.
And it came to pass, hen David and his men ere come to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had made a raid upon the South, and upon Ziklag, and had smitten Ziklag, and burned it ith fire,
and had taken captive the omen \add and all\add* that ere therein, both small and great: they sle not any, but carried them off, and ent their ay.
And hen David and his men came to the city, behold, it as burned ith fire; and their ives, and their sons, and their daughters, ere taken captive.
Then David and the people that ere ith him lifted up their voice and ept, until they had no more poer to eep.
And David’s to ives ere taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the ife of Nabal the Carmelite.

And David as greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning him, because the soul of all the people as grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters: but David strengthened himself in Jehovah his God.
And David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, I pray thee, bring me hither the ephod. And Abiathar brought thither the ephod to David.

And David inquired of Jehovah, saying, If I pursue after this troop, shall I overtake them? And he ansered him, Pursue; for thou shalt surely overtake \add them\add*, and shalt ithout fail recover \add all\add*.
So David ent, he and the six hundred men that ere ith him, and came to the brook Besor, here those that ere left behind stayed.
But David pursued, he and four hundred men; for to hundred stayed behind, ho ere so faint that they could not go over the brook Besor.
And they found an Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David, and gave him bread, and he did eat; and they gave him ater to drink;

and they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and to clusters of raisins: and hen he had eaten, his spirit came again to him; for he had eaten no bread, nor drunk any ater, three days and three nights.
And David said unto him, To hom belongest thou? and hence art thou? And he said, I am a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days ago I fell sick.
We made a raid upon the South of the Cherethites, and upon that hich belongeth to Judah, and upon the South of Caleb; and e burned Ziklag ith fire.

And David said to him, Wilt thou bring me don to this troop? And he said, Sear unto me by God, that thou ilt neither kill me, nor deliver me up into the hands of my master, and I ill bring thee don to this troop.

And hen he had brought him don, behold, they ere spread abroad over all the ground, eating and drinking, and dancing, because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.
And David smote them from the tilight even unto the evening of the next day: and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred young men, ho rode upon camels and fled.
And David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken; and David rescued his to ives.
And there as nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil, nor anything that they had taken to them: David brought back all.
And David took all the flocks and the herds, \add hich\add* they drove before those \add other\add* cattle, and said, This is David’s spoil.

And David came to the to hundred men, ho ere so faint that they could not follo David, hom also they had made to abide at the brook Besor; and they ent forth to meet David, and to meet the people that ere ith him: and hen David came near to the people, he saluted them.

Then ansered all the icked men and base fellos, of those that ent ith David, and said, Because they ent not ith us, e ill not give them aught of the spoil that e have recovered, save to every man his ife and his children, that he may lead them aay, and depart.
Then said David, Ye shall not do so, my brethren, ith that hich Jehovah hath given unto us, ho hath preserved us, and delivered the troop that came against us into our hand.
And ho ill hearken unto you in this matter? for as his share is that goeth don to the battle, so shall his share be that tarrieth by the baggage: they shall share alike.
And it as so from that day forard, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day.
And hen David came to Ziklag, he sent of the spoil unto the elders of Judah, even to his friends, saying, Behold, a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of Jehovah:
to them that ere in Beth-el, and to them that ere in Ramoth of the South, and to them that ere in Jattir,
and to them that ere in Aroer, and to them that ere in Siphmoth, and to them that ere in Eshtemoa,
and to them that ere in Racal, and to them that ere in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to them that ere in the cities of the Kenites,
and to them that ere in Hormah, and to them that ere in Bor-ashan, and to them that ere in Athach,
and to them that ere in Hebron, and to all the places here David himself and his men ere ont to haunt.
No the Philistines fought against Israel: and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell don slain in mount Gilboa.
And the Philistines folloed hard upon Saul and upon his sons; and the Philistines sle Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.
And the battle ent sore against Saul, and the archers overtook him; and he as greatly distressed by reason of the archers.

Then said Saul to his armorbearer, Dra thy sord, and thrust me through thereith, lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armorbearer ould not; for he as sore afraid. Therefore Saul took his sord, and fell upon it.
And hen his armorbearer sa that Saul as dead, he likeise fell upon his sord, and died ith him.
So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armorbearer, and all his men, that same day together.

And hen the men of Israel that ere on the other side of the valley, and they that ere beyond the Jordan, sa that the men of Israel fled, and that Saul and his sons ere dead, they forsook the cities, and fled; and the Philistines came and delt in them.
And it came to pass on the morro, hen the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen in mount Gilboa.
And they cut off his head, and stripped off his armor, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to carry the tidings unto the house of their idols, and to the people.
And they put his armor in the house of the Ashtaroth; and they fastened his body to the all of Beth-shan.
And hen the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard concerning him that hich the Philistines had done to Saul,
all the valiant men arose, and ent all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the all of Beth-shan; and they came to Jabesh, and burnt them there.
And they took their bones, and buried them under the tamarisk-tree in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
And it came to pass after the death of Saul, hen David as returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode to days in Ziklag;

it came to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul, ith his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it as, hen he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.
And David said unto him, From hence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.

And David said unto him, Ho ent the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he ansered, The people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.
And David said unto the young man that told him, Ho knoest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?
And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul as leaning upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and the horsemen folloed hard after him.
And hen he looked behind him, he sa me, and called unto me. And I ansered, Here am I.
And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I ansered him, I am an Amalekite.
And he said unto me, Stand, I pray thee, beside me, and slay me; for anguish hath taken hold of me, because my life is yet hole in me.

So I stood beside him, and sle him, because I as sure that he could not live after that he as fallen: and I took the cron that as upon his head, and the bracelet that as on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.
Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likeise all the men that ere ith him:
and they mourned, and ept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Jehovah, and for the house of Israel; because they ere fallen by the sord.
And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence art thou? And he ansered, I am the son of a sojourner, an Amalekite.
And David said unto him, Ho ast thou not afraid to put forth thy hand to destroy Jehovah’s anointed?
And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him, so that he died.
And David said unto him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain Jehovah’s anointed.
And David lamented ith this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son
( and he bade them teach the children of Judah \add the song of\add* the bo: behold, it is ritten in the book of Jashar):
Thy glory, O Israel, is slain upon thy high places! Ho are the mighty fallen!
Tell it not in Gath, Publish it not in the streets of Ashkelon; Lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, Lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
Ye mountains of Gilboa, Let there be no de nor rain upon you, neither fields of offerings: For there the shield of the mighty as vilely cast aay, The shield of Saul, not anointed ith oil.
From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, The bo of Jonathan turned not back, And the sord of Saul returned not empty.
Saul and Jonathan ere lovely and pleasant in their lives, And in their death they ere not divided: They ere sifter than eagles, They ere stronger than lions.
Ye daughters of Israel, eep over Saul, Who clothed you in scarlet delicately, Who put ornaments of gold upon your apparel.
Ho are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan is slain upon thy high places.
I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: Very pleasant hast thou been unto me: Thy love to me as onderful, Passing the love of omen.
Ho are the mighty fallen, And the eapons of ar perished!

And it came to pass after this, that David inquired of Jehovah, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And Jehovah said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron.
So David ent up thither, and his to ives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the ife of Nabal the Carmelite.
And his men that ere ith him did David bring up, every man ith his household: and they delt in the cities of Hebron.
And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, The men of Jabesh-gilead ere they that buried Saul.
And David sent messengers unto the men of Jabesh-gilead, and said unto them, Blessed be ye of Jehovah, that ye have shoed this kindness unto your lord, even unto Saul, and have buried him.
And no Jehovah sho lovingkindness and truth unto you: and I also ill requite you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.
No therefore let your hands be strong, and be ye valiant; for Saul your lord is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them.
No Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul’s host, had taken Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim;
and he made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, as forty years old hen he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned to years. But the house of Judah folloed David.
And the time that David as king in Hebron over the house of Judah as seven years and six months.
And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, ent out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, ent out, and met them by the pool of Gibeon; and they sat don, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.
And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men, I pray thee, arise and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.
Then they arose and ent over by number: telve for Benjamin, and for Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and telve of the servants of David.
And they caught every one his fello by the head, and \add thrust\add* his sord in his fello’s side; so they fell don together: herefore that place as called Helkath-hazzurim, hich is in Gibeon.
And the battle as very sore that day; and Abner as beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.
And the three sons of Zeruiah ere there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel as as light of foot as a ild roe.
And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from folloing Abner.
Then Abner looked behind him, and said, Is it thou, Asahel? And he ansered, It is I.
And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his armor. But Asahel ould not turn aside from folloing him.
And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from folloing me: herefore should I smite thee to the ground? ho then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?

Hobeit he refused to turn aside: herefore Abner ith the hinder end of the spear smote him in the body, so that the spear came out behind him; and he fell don there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that as many as came to the place here Asahel fell don and died stood still.
But Joab and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun ent don hen they ere come to the hill of Ammah, that lieth before Giah by the ay of the ilderness of Gibeon.
And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one band, and stood on the top of a hill.

Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sord devour for ever? knoest thou not that it ill be bitterness in the latter end? ho long shall it be then, ere thou bid the people return from folloing their brethren?
And Joab said, As God liveth, if thou hadst not spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone aay, nor folloed every one his brother.
So Joab ble the trumpet; and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.
And Abner and his men ent all that night through the Arabah; and they passed over the Jordan, and ent through all Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.
And Joab returned from folloing Abner: and hen he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of David’s servants nineteen men and Asahel.
But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner’s men, \add so that\add* three hundred and threescore men died.
And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulchre of his father, hich as in Beth-lehem. And Joab and his men ent all night, and the day brake upon them at Hebron.
No there as long ar beteen the house of Saul and the house of David: and David axed stronger and stronger, but the house of Saul axed eaker and eaker.
And unto David ere sons born in Hebron: and his first-born as Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
and his second, Chileab, of Abigail the ife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
and the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;
and the sixth, Ithream, of Eglah, David’s ife. These ere born to David in Hebron.
And it came to pass, hile there as ar beteen the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong in the house of Saul.
No Saul had a concubine, hose name as Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and \add Ish-bosheth\add* said to Abner, Wherefore hast thou gone in unto my father’s concubine?

Then as Abner very roth for the ords of Ish-bosheth, and said, Am I a dog’s head that belongeth to Judah? This day do I sho kindness unto the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David; and yet thou chargest me this day ith a fault concerning this oman.
God do so to Abner, and more also, if, as Jehovah hath sorn to David, I do not even so to him;
to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beer-sheba.
And he could not anser Abner another ord, because he feared him.

And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose is the land? saying \add also\add*, Make thy league ith me, and, behold, my hand shall be ith thee, to bring about all Israel unto thee.
And he said, Well; I ill make a league ith thee; but one thing I require of thee: that is, thou shalt not see my face, except thou first bring Michal, Saul’s daughter, hen thou comest to see my face.
And David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, saying, Deliver me my ife Michal, hom I betrothed to me for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.
And Ish-bosheth sent, and took her from her husband, even from Paltiel the son of Laish.
And her husband ent ith her, eeping as he ent, and folloed her to Bahurim. Then said Abner unto him, Go, return: and he returned.
And Abner had communication ith the elders of Israel, saying, In times past ye sought for David to be king over you:
no then do it; for Jehovah hath spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I ill save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.
And Abner also spake in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner ent also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and to the hole house of Benjamin.
So Abner came to David to Hebron, and tenty men ith him. And David made Abner and the men that ere ith him a feast.

And Abner said unto David, I ill arise and go, and ill gather all Israel unto my lord the king, that they may make a covenant ith thee, and that thou mayest reign over all that thy soul desireth. And David sent Abner aay; and he ent in peace.
And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from a foray, and brought in a great spoil ith them: but Abner as not ith David in Hebron; for he had sent him aay, and he as gone in peace.
When Joab and all the host that as ith him ere come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he hath sent him aay, and he is gone in peace.
Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done? behold, Abner came unto thee; hy is it that thou hast sent him aay, and he is quite gone?
Thou knoest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee, and to kno thy going out and thy coming in, and to kno all that thou doest.
And hen Joab as come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the ell of Sirah: but David kne it not.
And hen Abner as returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the midst of the gate to speak ith him quietly, and smote him there in the body, so that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
And afterard, hen David heard it, he said, I and my kingdom are guiltless before Jehovah for ever of the blood of Abner the son of Ner:

let it fall upon the head of Joab, and upon all his father’s house; and let there not fail from the house of Joab one that hath an issue, or that is a leper, or that leaneth on a staff, or that falleth by the sord, or that lacketh bread.
So Joab and Abishai his brother sle Abner, because he had killed their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.
And David said to Joab, and to all the people that ere ith him, Rend your clothes, and gird you ith sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David folloed the bier.
And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his voice, and ept at the grave of Abner; and all the people ept.
And the king lamented for Abner, and said, Should Abner die as a fool dieth?
Thy hands ere not bound, nor thy feet put into fetters: As a man falleth before the children of iniquity, so didst thou fall.
And all the people came to cause David to eat bread hile it as yet day; but David sare, saying, God do so to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or aught else, till the sun be don.
And all the people took notice of it, and it pleased them; as hatsoever the king did pleased all the people.
So all the people and all Israel understood that day that it as not of the king to slay Abner the son of Ner.
And the king said unto his servants, Kno ye not that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?
And I am this day eak, though anointed king; and these men the sons of Zeruiah are too hard for me: Jehovah reard the evil-doer according to his ickedness.
And hen \add Ish-bosheth\add*, Saul’s son, heard that Abner as dead in Hebron, his hands became feeble, and all the Israelites ere troubled.

And \add Ish-bosheth\add*, Saul’s son, \add had\add* to men that ere captains of bands: the name of the one as Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin ( for Beeroth also is reckoned to Benjamin:
and the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and have been sojourners there until this day).

No Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son that as lame of his feet. He as five years old hen the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel; and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name as Mephibosheth.
And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, ent, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, as he took his rest at noon.
And they came thither into the midst of the house, as though they ould have fetched heat; and they smote him in the body: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
No hen they came into the house, as he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, they smote him, and sle him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and ent by the ay of the Arabah all night.

And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold, the head of Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul, thine enemy, ho sought thy life; and Jehovah hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.
And David ansered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, As Jehovah liveth, ho hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
hen one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and sle him in Ziklag, hich as the reard I gave him for his tidings.
Ho much more, hen icked men have slain a righteous person in his on house upon his bed, shall I not no require his blood of your hand, and take you aay from the earth?

And David commanded his young men, and they sle them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up beside the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth, and buried it in the grave of Abner in Hebron.
Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, e are thy bone and thy flesh.

In times past, hen Saul as king over us, it as thou that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and Jehovah said to thee, Thou shalt be shepherd of my people Israel, and thou shalt be prince over Israel.
So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a covenant ith them in Hebron before Jehovah: and they anointed David king over Israel.
David as thirty years old hen he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.
In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months; and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.

And the king and his men ent to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, ho spake unto David, saying, Except thou take aay the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither; thinking, David cannot come in hither.
Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion; the same is the city of David.

And David said on that day, Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites, let him get up to the atercourse, and \add smite\add* the lame and the blind, that are hated of David’s soul. Wherefore they say, There are the blind and the lame; he cannot come into the house.
And David delt in the stronghold, and called it the city of David. And David built round about from Millo and inard.
And David axed greater and greater; for Jehovah, the God of hosts, as ith him.
And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar-trees, and carpenters, and masons; and they built David a house.
And David perceived that Jehovah had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel’s sake.
And David took him more concubines and ives out of Jerusalem, after he as come from Hebron; and there ere yet sons and daughters born to David.
And these are the names of those that ere born unto him in Jerusalem: Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
and Ibhar, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
and Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet.
And hen the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines ent up to seek David; and David heard of it, and ent don to the stronghold.
No the Philistines had come and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

And David inquired of Jehovah, saying, Shall I go up against the Philistines? ilt thou deliver them into my hand? And Jehovah said unto David, Go up; for I ill certainly deliver the Philistines into thy hand.
And David came to Baal-perazim, and David smote them there; and he said, Jehovah hath broken mine enemies before me, like the breach of aters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
And they left their images there; and David and his men took them aay.
And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
And hen David inquired of Jehovah, he said, Thou shalt not go up: make a circuit behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry-trees.

And it shall be, hen thou hearest the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry-trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself; for then is Jehovah gone out before thee to smite the host of the Philistines.
And David did so, as Jehovah commanded him, and smote the Philistines from Geba until thou come to Gezer.
And David again gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

And David arose, and ent ith all the people that ere ith him, from Baale-judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God, hich is called by the Name, even the name of Jehovah of hosts that sitteth \add above\add* the cherubim.
And they set the ark of God upon a ne cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that as in the hill: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the ne cart.
And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab, hich as in the hill, ith the ark of God: and Ahio ent before the ark.

And David and all the house of Israel played before Jehovah ith all manner of \add instruments made of\add* fir-ood, and ith harps, and ith psalteries, and ith timbrels, and ith castanets, and ith cymbals.
And hen they came to the threshing-floor of Nacon, Uzzah put forth \add his hand\add* to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen stumbled.
And the anger of Jehovah as kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.
And David as displeased, because Jehovah had broken forth upon Uzzah; and he called that place Perez-uzzah, unto this day.
And David as afraid of Jehovah that day; and he said, Ho shall the ark of Jehovah come unto me?
So David ould not remove the ark of Jehovah unto him into the city of David; but David carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
And the ark of Jehovah remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months: and Jehovah blessed Obed-edom, and all his house.

And it as told king David, saying, Jehovah hath blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that pertaineth unto him, because of the ark of God. And David ent and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the city of David ith joy.
And it as so, that, hen they that bare the ark of Jehovah had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
And David danced before Jehovah ith all his might; and David as girded ith a linen ephod.
So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of Jehovah ith shouting, and ith the sound of the trumpet.

And it as so, as the ark of Jehovah came into the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the indo, and sa king David leaping and dancing before Jehovah; and she despised him in her heart.
And they brought in the ark of Jehovah, and set it in its place, in the midst of the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings before Jehovah.
And hen David had made an end of offering the burnt-offering and the peace-offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Jehovah of hosts.

And he dealt among all the people, even among the hole multitude of Israel, both to men and omen, to every one a cake of bread, and a portion \add of flesh\add*, and a cake of raisins. So all the people departed every one to his house.

Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, Ho glorious as the king of Israel to-day, ho uncovered himself to-day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellos shamelessly uncovereth himself!

And David said unto Michal, \add It as\add* before Jehovah, ho chose me above thy father, and above all his house, to appoint me prince over the people of Jehovah, over Israel: therefore ill I play before Jehovah.
And I ill be yet more vile than this, and ill be base in mine on sight: but of the handmaids of hom thou hast spoken, of them shall I be had in honor.
And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.
And it came to pass, hen the king delt in his house, and Jehovah had given him rest from all his enemies round about,
that the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See no, I dell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God delleth ithin curtains.
And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that is in thy heart; for Jehovah is ith thee.
And it came to pass the same night, that the ord of Jehovah came unto Nathan, saying,
Go and tell my servant David, Thus saith Jehovah, Shalt thou build me a house for me to dell in?
for I have not delt in a house since the day that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have alked in a tent and in a tabernacle.

In all places herein I have alked ith all the children of Israel, spake I a ord ith any of the tribes of Israel, hom I commanded to be shepherd of my people Israel, saying, Why have ye not built me a house of cedar?

No therefore thus shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from folloing the sheep, that thou shouldest be prince over my people, over Israel;
and I have been ith thee hithersoever thou entest, and have cut off all thine enemies from before thee; and I ill make thee a great name, like unto the name of the great ones that are in the earth.

And I ill appoint a place for my people Israel, and ill plant them, that they may dell in their on place, and be moved no more; neither shall the children of ickedness afflict them any more, as at the first,

and \add as\add* from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel; and I ill cause thee to rest from all thine enemies. Moreover Jehovah telleth thee that Jehovah ill make thee a house.
When thy days are fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep ith thy fathers, I ill set up thy seed after thee, that shall proceed out of thy boels, and I ill establish his kingdom.
He shall build a house for my name, and I ill establish the throne of his kingdom for ever.
I ill be his father, and he shall be my son: if he commit iniquity, I ill chasten him ith the rod of men, and ith the stripes of the children of men;
but my lovingkindness shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul, hom I put aay before thee.
And thy house and thy kingdom shall be made sure for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.
According to all these ords, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak unto David.
Then David the king ent in, and sat before Jehovah; and he said, Who am I, O Lord Jehovah, and hat is my house, that thou hast brought me thus far?
And this as yet a small thing in thine eyes, O Lord Jehovah; but thou hast spoken also of thy servant’s house for a great hile to come; and this \add too\add* after the manner of men, O Lord Jehovah!
And hat can David say more unto thee? for thou knoest thy servant, O Lord Jehovah.
For thy ord’s sake, and according to thine on heart, hast thou rought all this greatness, to make thy servant kno it.
Wherefore thou art great, O Jehovah God: for there is none like thee, neither is there any God besides thee, according to all that e have heard ith our ears.

And hat one nation in the earth is like thy people, even like Israel, hom God ent to redeem unto himself for a people, and to make him a name, and to do great things for you, and terrible things for thy land, before thy people, hom thou redeemedst to thee out of Egypt, \add from\add* the nations and their gods?
And thou didst establish to thyself thy people Israel to be a people unto thee for ever; and thou, Jehovah, becamest their God.
And no, O Jehovah God, the ord that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, confirm thou it for ever, and do as thou hast spoken.
And let thy name be magnified for ever, saying, Jehovah of hosts is God over Israel; and the house of thy servant David shall be established before thee.
For thou, O Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, hast revealed to thy servant, saying, I ill build thee a house: therefore hath thy servant found in his heart to pray this prayer unto thee.
And no, O Lord Jehovah, thou art God, and thy ords are truth, and thou hast promised this good thing unto thy servant:

no therefore let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee; for thou, O Lord Jehovah, hast spoken it: and ith thy blessing let the house of thy servant be blessed for ever.
And after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took the bridle of the mother city out of the hand of the Philistines.

And he smote Moab, and measured them ith the line, making them to lie don on the ground; and he measured to lines to put to death, and one full line to keep alive. And the Moabites became servants to David, and brought tribute.
David smote also Hadadezer the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he ent to recover his dominion at the River.
And David took from him a thousand and seven hundred horsemen, and tenty thousand footmen: and David hocked all the chariot horses, but reserved of them for a hundred chariots.
And hen the Syrians of Damascus came to succor Hadadezer king of Zobah, David smote of the Syrians to and tenty thousand men.
Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought tribute. And Jehovah gave victory to David hithersoever he ent.
And David took the shields of gold that ere on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
And from Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took exceeding much brass.
And hen Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer,

then Toi sent Joram his son unto king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and smitten him: for Hadadezer had ars ith Toi. And \add Joram\add* brought ith him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:
these also did king David dedicate unto Jehovah, ith the silver and gold that he dedicated of all the nations hich he subdued;
of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
And David gat him a name hen he returned from smiting the Syrians in the Valley of Salt, even eighteen thousand men.
And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all the Edomites became servants to David. And Jehovah gave victory to David hithersoever he ent.
And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed justice and righteousness unto all his people.
And Joab the son of Zeruiah as over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud as recorder;
and Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, ere priests; and Seraiah as scribe;
and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada \add as over\add* the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons ere chief ministers.
And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may sho him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?
And there as of the house of Saul a servant hose name as Ziba, and they called him unto David; and the king said unto him, Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant is he.
And the king said, Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may sho the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son, ho is lame of his feet.
And the king said unto him, Where is he? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.
Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
And Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came unto David, and fell on his face, and did obeisance. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he ansered, Behold, thy servant!

And David said unto him, Fear not; for I ill surely sho thee kindness for Jonathan thy father’s sake, and ill restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
And he did obeisance, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I am?
Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said unto him, All that pertained to Saul and to all his house have I given unto thy master’s son.

And thou shalt till the land for him, thou, and thy sons, and thy servants; and thou shalt bring in \add the fruits\add*, that thy master’s son may have bread to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master’s son shall eat bread alay at my table. No Ziba had fifteen sons and tenty servants.

Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king commandeth his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth, \add said the king\add*, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king’s sons.
And Mephibosheth had a young son, hose name as Mica. And all that delt in the house of Ziba ere servants unto Mephibosheth.
So Mephibosheth delt in Jerusalem; for he did eat continually at the king’s table. And he as lame in both his feet.
And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.

And David said, I ill sho kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father shoed kindness unto me. So David sent by his servants to comfort him concerning his father. And David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.

But the princes of the children of Ammon said unto Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David doth honor thy father, in that he hath sent comforters unto thee? hath not David sent his servants unto thee to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthro it?
So Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them aay.
When they told it unto David, he sent to meet them; for the men ere greatly ashamed. And the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards be gron, and then return.

And hen the children of Ammon sa that they ere become odious to David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob, and the Syrians of Zobah, tenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah ith a thousand men, and the men of Tob telve thousand men.
And hen David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.
And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate: and the Syrians of Zobah and of Rehob, and the men of Tob and Maacah, ere by themselves in the field.
No hen Joab sa that the battle as set against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians:
and the rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and he put them in array against the children of Ammon.
And he said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me; but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I ill come and help thee.
Be of good courage, and let us play the man for our people, and for the cities of our God: and Jehovah do that hich seemeth him good.
So Joab and the people that ere ith him dre nigh unto the battle against the Syrians: and they fled before him.
And hen the children of Ammon sa that the Syrians ere fled, they likeise fled before Abishai, and entered into the city. Then Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem.
And hen the Syrians sa that they ere put to the orse before Israel, they gathered themselves together.
And Hadarezer sent, and brought out the Syrians that ere beyond the River: and they came to Helam, ith Shobach the captain of the host of Hadarezer at their head.
And it as told David; and he gathered all Israel together, and passed over the Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Syrians set themselves in array against David, and fought ith him.

And the Syrians fled before Israel; and David sle of the Syrians \add the men of\add* seven hundred chariots, and forty thousand horsemen, and smote Shobach the captain of their host, so that he died there.

And hen all the kings that ere servants to Hadarezer sa that they ere put to the orse before Israel, they made peace ith Israel, and served them. So the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more.

And it came to pass, at the return of the year, at the time hen kings go out \add to battle\add*, that David sent Joab, and his servants ith him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried at Jerusalem.
And it came to pass at eventide, that David arose from off his bed, and alked upon the roof of the king’s house: and from the roof he sa a oman bathing; and the oman as very beautiful to look upon.
And David sent and inquired after the oman. And one said, Is not this Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam, the ife of Uriah the Hittite?
And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay ith her ( for she as purified from her uncleanness); and she returned unto her house.
And the oman conceived; and she sent and told David, and said, I am ith child.
And David sent to Joab, \add saying\add*, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.
And hen Uriah as come unto him, David asked of him ho Joab did, and ho the people fared, and ho the ar prospered.
And David said to Uriah, Go don to thy house, and ash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and there folloed him a mess \add of food\add* from the king.
But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house ith all the servants of his lord, and ent not don to his house.
And hen they had told David, saying, Uriah ent not don unto his house, David said unto Uriah, Art thou not come from a journey? herefore didst thou not go don unto thy house?

And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in booths; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open field; shall I then go into my house, to eat and to drink, and to lie ith my ife? as thou livest, and as thy soul liveth, I ill not do this thing.
And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to-day also, and to-morro I ill let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the morro.
And hen David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he ent out to lie on his bed ith the servants of his lord, but ent not don to his house.
And it came to pass in the morning, that David rote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
And he rote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.
And it came to pass, hen Joab kept atch upon the city, that he assigned Uriah unto the place here he kne that valiant men ere.
And the men of the city ent out, and fought ith Joab: and there fell some of the people, even of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the ar;
and he charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling all the things concerning the ar unto the king,
it shall be that, if the king’s rath arise, and he say unto thee, Wherefore ent ye so nigh unto the city to fight? kne ye not that they ould shoot from the all?

ho smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a oman cast an upper millstone upon him from the all, so that he died at Thebez? hy ent ye so nigh the all? then shalt thou say, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
So the messenger ent, and came and shoed David all that Joab had sent him for.
And the messenger said unto David, The men prevailed against us, and came out unto us into the field, and e ere upon them even unto the entrance of the gate.
And the shooters shot at thy servants from off the all; and some of the king’s servants are dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

Then David said unto the messenger, Thus shalt thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sord devoureth one as ell as another; make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthro it: and encourage thou him.
And hen the ife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband as dead, she made lamentation for her husband.
And hen the mourning as past, David sent and took her home to his house, and she became his ife, and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased Jehovah.
And Jehovah sent Nathan unto David. And he came unto him, and said unto him, There ere to men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds;

but the poor man had nothing, save one little ee lamb, hich he had bought and nourished up: and it gre up together ith him, and ith his children; it did eat of his on morsel, and drank of his on cup, and lay in his bosom, and as unto him as a daughter.

And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his on flock and of his on herd, to dress for the ayfaring man that as come unto him, but took the poor man’s lamb, and dressed it for the man that as come to him.
And David’s anger as greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As Jehovah liveth, the man that hath done this is orthy to die:
and he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;

and I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s ives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that had been too little, I ould have added unto thee such and such things.

Wherefore hast thou despised the ord of Jehovah, to do that hich is evil in his sight? thou hast smitten Uriah the Hittite ith the sord, and hast taken his ife to be thy ife, and hast slain him ith the sord of the children of Ammon.
No therefore the sord shall never depart from thy house, because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the ife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy ife.

Thus saith Jehovah, Behold, I ill raise up evil against thee out of thine on house; and I ill take thy ives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbor, and he shall lie ith thy ives in the sight of this sun.
For thou didst it secretly: but I ill do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.
And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against Jehovah. And Nathan said unto David, Jehovah also hath put aay thy sin; thou shalt not die.
Hobeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of Jehovah to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.
And Nathan departed unto his house. And Jehovah struck the child that Uriah’s ife bare unto David, and it as very sick.
David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and ent in, and lay all night upon the earth.
And the elders of his house arose, \add and stood\add* beside him, to raise him up from the earth: but he ould not, neither did he eat bread ith them.

And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child as dead; for they said, Behold, hile the child as yet alive, e spake unto him, and he hearkened not unto our voice: ho ill he then vex himself, if e tell him that the child is dead!
But hen David sa that his servants ere hispering together, David perceived that the child as dead; and David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.

Then David arose from the earth, and ashed, and anointed himself, and changed his apparel; and he came into the house of Jehovah, and orshipped: then he came to his on house; and hen he required, they set bread before him, and he did eat.
Then said his servants unto him, What thing is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and eep for the child, hile it as alive; but hen the child as dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.
And he said, While the child as yet alive, I fasted and ept: for I said, Who knoeth hether Jehovah ill not be gracious to me, that the child may live?
But no he is dead, herefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he ill not return to me.
And David comforted Bath-sheba his ife, and ent in unto her, and lay ith her: and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon. And Jehovah loved him;
and he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, for Jehovah’s sake.
No Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah; yea, I have taken the city of aters.
No therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it; lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.
And David gathered all the people together, and ent to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.

And he took the cron of their king from off his head; and the eight thereof as a talent of gold, and \add in it ere\add* precious stones; and it as set on David’s head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city, exceeding much.

And he brought forth the people that ere therein, and put them under sas, and under harros of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. And David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.
And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, hose name as Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.
And Amnon as so vexed that he fell sick because of his sister Tamar; for she as a virgin; and it seemed hard to Amnon to do anything unto her.
But Amnon had a friend, hose name as Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David’s brother: and Jonadab as a very subtle man.
And he said unto him, Why, O son of the king, art thou thus lean from day to day? ilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said unto him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.

And Jonadab said unto him, Lay thee don on thy bed, and feign thyself sick: and hen thy father cometh to see thee, say unto him, Let my sister Tamar come, I pray thee, and give me bread to eat, and dress the food in my sight, that I may see it, and eat it from her hand.

So Amnon lay don, and feigned himself sick: and hen the king as come to see him, Amnon said unto the king, Let my sister Tamar come, I pray thee, and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand.
Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go no to thy brother Amnon’s house, and dress him food.
So Tamar ent to her brother Amnon’s house; and he as laid don. And she took dough, and kneaded it, and made cakes in his sight, and did bake the cakes.
And she took the pan, and poured them out before him; but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Have out all men from me. And they ent out every man from him.
And Amnon said unto Tamar, Bring the food into the chamber, that I may eat from thy hand. And Tamar took the cakes hich she had made, and brought them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.
And hen she had brought them near unto him to eat, he took hold of her, and said unto her, Come, lie ith me, my sister.
And she ansered him, Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.
