And I, hither shall I carry my shame? and as for thee, thou ilt be as one of the fools in Israel. No therefore, I pray thee, speak unto the king; for he ill not ithhold me from thee.
Hobeit he ould not hearken unto her voice; but being stronger than she, he forced her, and lay ith her.
Then Amnon hated her ith exceeding great hatred; for the hatred hereith he hated her as greater than the love hereith he had loved her. And Amnon said unto her, Arise, be gone.
And she said unto him, Not so, because this great rong in putting me forth is \add orse\add* than the other that thou didst unto me. But he ould not hearken unto her.
Then he called his servant that ministered unto him, and said, Put no this oman out from me, and bolt the door after her.
And she had a garment of divers colors upon her; for ith such robes ere the king’s daughters that ere virgins apparelled. Then his servant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.
And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of divers colors that as on her; and she laid her hand on her head, and ent her ay, crying aloud as she ent.

And Absalom her brother said unto her, Hath Amnon thy brother been ith thee? but no hold thy peace, my sister: he is thy brother; take not this thing to heart. So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.
But hen king David heard of all these things, he as very roth.
And Absalom spake unto Amnon neither good nor bad; for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.
And it came to pass after to full years, that Absalom had sheep-shearers in Baal-hazor, hich is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.
And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold no, thy servant hath sheep-shearers; let the king, I pray thee, and his servants go ith thy servant.
And the king said to Absalom, Nay, my son, let us not all go, lest e be burdensome unto thee. And he pressed him: hobeit he ould not go, but blessed him.
Then said Absalom, If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go ith us. And the king said unto him, Why should he go ith thee?
But Absalom pressed him, and he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go ith him.

And Absalom commanded his servants, saying, Mark ye no, hen Amnon’s heart is merry ith ine; and hen I say unto you, Smite Amnon, then kill him; fear not; have not I commanded you? be courageous, and be valiant.
And the servants of Absalom did unto Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king’s sons arose, and every man gat him up upon his mule, and fled.
And it came to pass, hile they ere in the ay, that the tidings came to David, saying, Absalom hath slain all the king’s sons, and there is not one of them left.
Then the king arose, and rent his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by ith their clothes rent.

And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David’s brother, ansered and said, Let not my lord suppose that they have killed all the young men the king’s sons; for Amnon only is dead: for by the appointment of Absalom this hath been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.
No therefore let not my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king’s sons are dead; for Amnon only is dead.
But Absalom fled. And the young man that kept the atch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came much people by the ay of the hill-side behind him.
And Jonadab said unto the king, Behold, the king’s sons are come: as thy servant said, so it is.
And it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of speaking, that, behold, the king’s sons came, and lifted up their voice, and ept: and the king also and all his servants ept very sore.
But Absalom fled, and ent to Talmai the son of Ammihur, king of Geshur. And \add David\add* mourned for his son every day.
So Absalom fled, and ent to Geshur, and as there three years.
And \add the soul of\add* king David longed to go forth unto Absalom: for he as comforted concerning Amnon, seeing he as dead.
No Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart as toard Absalom.

And Joab sent to Tekoa, and fetched thence a ise oman, and said unto her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on mourning apparel, I pray thee, and anoint not thyself ith oil, but be as a oman that hath a long time mourned for the dead:
and go in to the king, and speak on this manner unto him. So Joab put the ords in her mouth.
And hen the oman of Tekoa spake to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, Help, O king.
And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she ansered, Of a truth I am a ido, and my husband is dead.
And thy handmaid had to sons, and they to strove together in the field, and there as none to part them, but the one smote the other, and killed him.

And, behold, the hole family is risen against thy handmaid, and they say, Deliver him that smote his brother, that e may kill him for the life of his brother hom he sle, and so destroy the heir also. Thus ill they quench my coal hich is left, and ill leave to my husband neither name nor remainder upon the face of the earth.
And the king said unto the oman, Go to thy house, and I ill give charge concerning thee.
And the oman of Tekoa said unto the king, My lord, O king, the iniquity be on me, and on my father’s house; and the king and his throne be guiltless.
And the king said, Whosoever saith aught unto thee, bring him to me, and he shall not touch thee any more.

Then said she, I pray thee, let the king remember Jehovah thy God, that the avenger of blood destroy not any more, lest they destroy my son. And he said, As Jehovah liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.
Then the oman said, Let thy handmaid, I pray thee, speak a ord unto my lord the king. And he said, Say on.

And the oman said, Wherefore then hast thou devised such a thing against the people of God? for in speaking this ord the king is as one that is guilty, in that the king doth not fetch home again his banished one.
For e must needs die, and are as ater spilt on the ground, hich cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God take aay life, but deviseth means, that he that is banished be not an outcast from him.

No therefore seeing that I am come to speak this ord unto my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid: and thy handmaid said, I ill no speak unto the king; it may be that the king ill perform the request of his servant.
For the king ill hear, to deliver his servant out of the hand of the man that ould destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.
Then thy handmaid said, Let, I pray thee, the ord of my lord the king be comfortable; for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad: and Jehovah thy God be ith thee.
Then the king ansered and said unto the oman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, aught that I shall ask thee. And the oman said, Let my lord the king no speak.

And the king said, Is the hand of Joab ith thee in all this? And the oman ansered and said, As thy soul liveth, my lord the king, none can turn to the right hand or to the left from aught that my lord the king hath spoken; for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these ords in the mouth of thy handmaid;
to change the face of the matter hath thy servant Joab done this thing: and my lord is ise, according to the isdom of an angel of God, to kno all things that are in the earth.
And the king said unto Joab, Behold no, I have done this thing: go therefore, bring the young man Absalom back.

And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and did obeisance, and blessed the king; and Joab said, To-day thy servant knoeth that I have found favor in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath performed the request of his servant.
So Joab arose and ent to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
And the king said, Let him turn to his on house, but let him not see my face. So Absalom turned to his on house, and sa not the king’s face.
No in all Israel there as none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the cron of his head there as no blemish in him.

And hen he cut the hair of his head ( no it as at every year’s end that he cut it; because it as heavy on him, therefore he cut it); he eighed the hair of his head at to hundred shekels, after the king’s eight.
And unto Absalom there ere born three sons, and one daughter, hose name as Tamar: she as a oman of a fair countenance.
And Absalom delt to full years in Jerusalem; and he sa not the king’s face.
Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king; but he ould not come to him: and he sent again a second time, but he ould not come.
Therefore he said unto his servants, See, Joab’s field is near mine, and he hath barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom unto his house, and said unto him, Wherefore have thy servants set my field on fire?

And Absalom ansered Joab, Behold, I sent unto thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Wherefore am I come from Geshur? it ere better for me to be there still. No therefore let me see the king’s face; and if there be iniquity in me, let him kill me.
So Joab came to the king, and told him; and hen he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and boed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.
And it came to pass after this, that Absalom prepared him a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the ay of the gate: and it as so, that, hen any man had a suit hich should come to the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him, and said, Of hat city art thou? And he said, Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.
And Absalom said unto him, See, thy matters are good and right; but there is no man deputed of the king to hear thee.
Absalom said moreover, Oh that I ere made judge in the land, that every man ho hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I ould do him justice!
And it as so, that, hen any man came nigh to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took hold of him, and kissed him.
And on this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
And it came to pass at the end of forty years, that Absalom said unto the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay my vo, hich I have voed unto Jehovah, in Hebron.
For thy servant voed a vo hile I abode at Geshur in Syria, saying, If Jehovah shall indeed bring me again to Jerusalem, then I ill serve Jehovah.
And the king said unto him, Go in peace. So he arose, and ent to Hebron.
But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as ye hear the sound of the trumpet, then ye shall say, Absalom is king in Hebron.
And ith Absalom ent to hundred men out of Jerusalem, that ere invited, and ent in their simplicity; and they kne not anything.

And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counsellor, from his city, even from Giloh, hile he as offering the sacrifices. And the conspiracy as strong; for the people increased continually ith Absalom.
And there came a messenger to David, saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.

And David said unto all his servants that ere ith him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for else none of us shall escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he overtake us quickly, and bring don evil upon us, and smite the city ith the edge of the sord.
And the king’s servants said unto the king, Behold, thy servants are ready to do hatsoever my lord the king shall choose.
And the king ent forth, and all his household after him. And the king left ten omen, that ere concubines, to keep the house.
And the king ent forth, and all the people after him; and they tarried in Beth-merhak.
And all his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men that came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
Then said the king to Ittai the Gittite, Wherefore goest thou also ith us? return, and abide ith the king: for thou art a foreigner, and also an exile; \add return\add* to thine on place.
Whereas thou camest but yesterday, should I this day make thee go up and don ith us, seeing I go hither I may? return thou, and take back thy brethren; mercy and truth be ith thee.

And Ittai ansered the king, and said, As Jehovah liveth, and as my lord the king liveth, surely in hat place my lord the king shall be, hether for death or for life, even there also ill thy servant be.
And David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones that ere ith him.
And all the country ept ith a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toard the ay of the ilderness.

And, lo, Zadok also \add came\add*, and all the Levites ith him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God; and they set don the ark of God; and Abiathar ent up, until all the people had done passing out of the city.
And the king said unto Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favor in the eyes of Jehovah, he ill bring me again, and sho me both it, and his habitation:
but if he say thus, I have no delight in thee; behold, here am I, let him do to me as seemeth good unto him.
The king said also unto Zadok the priest, Art thou \add not\add* a seer? return into the city in peace, and your to sons ith you, Ahimaaz thy son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
See, I ill tarry at the fords of the ilderness, until there come ord from you to certify me.
Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem: and they abode there.

And David ent up by the ascent of the \add mount of\add* Olives, and ept as he ent up; and he had his head covered, and ent barefoot: and all the people that ere ith him covered every man his head, and they ent up, eeping as they ent up.
And one told David, saying, Ahithophel is among the conspirators ith Absalom. And David said, O Jehovah, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.
And it came to pass, that, hen David as come to the top \add of the ascent\add*, here God as orshipped, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him ith his coat rent, and earth upon his head.
And David said unto him, If thou passest on ith me, then thou ilt be a burden unto me:

but if thou return to the city, and say unto Absalom, I ill be thy servant, O king; as I have been thy father’s servant in time past, so ill I no be thy servant; then ilt thou defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.

And hast thou not there ith thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be, that hat thing soever thou shalt hear out of the king’s house, thou shalt tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
Behold, they have there ith them their to sons, Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son, and Jonathan, Abiathar’s son; and by them ye shall send unto me everything that ye shall hear.
So Hushai, David’s friend, came into the city; and Absalom came into Jerusalem.

And hen David as a little past the top \add of the ascent\add*, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, ith a couple of asses saddled, and upon them to hundred loaves of bread, and a hundred clusters of raisins, and a hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of ine.

And the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses are for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the ine, that such as are faint in the ilderness may drink.
And the king said, And here is thy master’s son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem; for he said, To-day ill the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.
Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine is all that pertaineth unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I do obeisance; let me find favor in thy sight, my lord, O king.
And hen king David came to Bahurim, behold, there came out thence a man of the family of the house of Saul, hose name as Shimei, the son of Gera; he came out, and cursed still as he came.
And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men ere on his right hand and on his left.
And thus said Shimei hen he cursed, Begone, begone, thou man of blood, and base fello:

Jehovah hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in hose stead thou hast reigned; and Jehovah hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son; and, behold, thou art \add taken\add* in thine on mischief, because thou art a man of blood.
Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.
And the king said, What have I to do ith you, ye sons of Zeruiah? Because he curseth, and because Jehovah hath said unto him, Curse David; ho then shall say, Wherefore hast thou done so?

And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, ho came forth from my boels, seeketh my life: ho much more \add may\add* this Benjamite no \add do it\add*? let him alone, and let him curse; for Jehovah hath bidden him.
It may be that Jehovah ill look on the rong done unto me, and that Jehovah ill requite me good for \add his\add* cursing of me this day.
So David and his men ent by the ay; and Shimei ent along on the hill-side over against him, and cursed as he ent, and thre stones at him, and cast dust.
And the king, and all the people that ere ith him, came eary; and he refreshed himself there.
And Absalom, and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel ith him.
And it came to pass, hen Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, as come unto Absalom, that Hushai said unto Absalom, \add Long\add* live the king, \add Long\add* live the king.
And Absalom said to Hushai, Is this thy kindness to thy friend? hy entest thou not ith thy friend?
And Hushai said unto Absalom, Nay; but hom Jehovah, and this people, and all the men of Israel have chosen, his ill I be, and ith him ill I abide.
And again, hom should I serve? \add should I\add* not \add serve\add* in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father’s presence, so ill I be in thy presence.
Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give your counsel hat e shall do.

And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, that he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel ill hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then ill the hands of all that are ith thee be strong.
So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom ent in unto his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
And the counsel of Ahithophel, hich he gave in those days, as as if a man inquired at the oracle of God: so as all the counsel of Ahithophel both ith David and ith Absalom.
Moreover Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me no choose out telve thousand men, and I ill arise and pursue after David this night:
and I ill come upon him hile he is eary and eak-handed, and ill make him afraid; and all the people that are ith him shall flee; and I ill smite the king only;
and I ill bring back all the people unto thee: the man hom thou seekest is as if all returned: \add so\add* all the people shall be in peace.
And the saying pleased Absalom ell, and all the elders of Israel.
Then said Absalom, Call no Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likeise hat he saith.
And hen Hushai as come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: shall e do \add after\add* his saying? if not, speak thou.
And Hushai said unto Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel hath given this time is not good.

Hushai said moreover, Thou knoest thy father and his men, that they are mighty men, and they are chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her helps in the field; and thy father is a man of ar, and ill not lodge ith the people.

Behold, he is hid no in some pit, or in some \add other\add* place: and it ill come to pass, hen some of them are fallen at the first, that hosoever heareth it ill say, There is a slaughter among the people that follo Absalom.
And even he that is valiant, hose heart is as the heart of a lion, ill utterly melt; for all Israel knoeth that thy father is a mighty man, and they that are ith him are valiant men.
But I counsel that all Israel be gathered together unto thee, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, as the sand that is by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine on person.
So shall e come upon him in some place here he shall be found, and e ill light upon him as the de falleth on the ground; and of him and of all the men that are ith him e ill not leave so much as one.
Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and e ill dra it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.

And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For Jehovah had ordained to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that Jehovah might bring evil upon Absalom.
Then said Hushai unto Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.
No therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night at the fords of the ilderness, but by all means pass over; lest the king be salloed up, and all the people that are ith him.
No Jonathan and Ahimaaz ere staying by En-rogel; and a maid-servant used to go and tell them; and they ent and told king David: for they might not be seen to come into the city.
But a lad sa them, and told Absalom: and they ent both of them aay quickly, and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, ho had a ell in his court; and they ent don thither.
And the oman took and spread the covering over the ell’s mouth, and streed bruised grain thereon; and nothing as knon.

And Absalom’s servants came to the oman to the house; and they said, Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the oman said unto them, They are gone over the brook of ater. And hen they had sought and could not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.

And it came to pass, after they ere departed, that they came up out of the ell, and ent and told king David; and they said unto David, Arise ye, and pass quickly over the ater; for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.
Then David arose, and all the people that ere ith him, and they passed over the Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that as not gone over the Jordan.

And hen Ahithophel sa that his counsel as not folloed, he saddled his ass, and arose, and gat him home, unto his city, and set his house in order, and hanged himself; and he died, and as buried in the sepulchre of his father.
Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel ith him.
And Absalom set Amasa over the host instead of Joab. No Amasa as the son of a man, hose name as Ithra the Israelite, that ent in to Abigal the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.
And Israel and Absalom encamped in the land of Gilead.
And it came to pass, hen David as come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
brought beds, and basins, and earthen vessels, and heat, and barley, and meal, and parched \add grain\add*, and beans, and lentils, and parched \add pulse\add*,
and honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of the herd, for David, and for the people that ere ith him, to eat: for they said, The people are hungry, and eary, and thirsty, in the ilderness.
And David numbered the people that ere ith him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.

And David sent forth the people, a third part under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I ill surely go forth ith you myself also.

But the people said, Thou shalt not go forth: for if e flee aay, they ill not care for us; neither if half of us die, ill they care for us: but thou art orth ten thousand of us; therefore no it is better that thou be ready to succor us out of the city.
And the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I ill do. And the king stood by the gate-side, and all the people ent out by hundreds and by thousands.

And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Deal gently for my sake ith the young man, even ith Absalom. And all the people heard hen the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.
So the people ent out into the field against Israel: and the battle as in the forest of Ephraim.
And the people of Israel ere smitten there before the servants of David, and there as a great slaughter there that day of tenty thousand men.
For the battle as there spread over the face of all the country; and the forest devoured more people that day than the sord devoured.

And Absalom chanced to meet the servants of David. And Absalom as riding upon his mule, and the mule ent under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he as taken up beteen heaven and earth; and the mule that as under him ent on.
And a certain man sa it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I sa Absalom hanging in an oak.
And Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou saest it, and hy didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I ould have given thee ten \add pieces of\add* silver, and a girdle.

And the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand \add pieces of\add* silver in my hand, yet ould I not put forth my hand against the king’s son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beare that none touch the young man Absalom.
Otherise if I had dealt falsely against his life ( and there is no matter hid from the king), then thou thyself ouldest have set thyself against \add me\add*.
Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus ith thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, hile he as yet alive in the midst of the oak.
And ten young men that bare Joab’s armor compassed about and smote Absalom, and sle him.
And Joab ble the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel; for Joab held back the people.
And they took Absalom, and cast him into the great pit in the forest, and raised over him a very great heap of stones: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.

No Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself the pillar, hich is in the king’s dale; for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his on name; and it is called Absalom’s monument, unto this day.
Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me no run, and bear the king tidings, ho that Jehovah hath avenged him of his enemies.
And Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not be the bearer of tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day; but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king’s son is dead.
Then said Joab to the Cushite, Go, tell the king hat thou hast seen. And the Cushite boed himself unto Joab, and ran.

Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But come hat may, let me, I pray thee, also run after the Cushite. And Joab said, Wherefore ilt thou run, my son, seeing that thou ilt have no reard for the tidings?
But come hat may, \add said he\add*, I ill run. And he said unto him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the ay of the Plain, and outran the Cushite.
No David as sitting beteen the to gates: and the atchman ent up to the roof of the gate unto the all, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, a man running alone.
And the atchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he be alone, there is tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and dre near.
And the atchman sa another man running; and the atchman called unto the porter, and said, Behold, \add another\add* man running alone. And the king said, He also bringeth tidings.
And the atchman said, I think the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He is a good man, and cometh ith good tidings.

And Ahimaaz called, and said unto the king, All is ell. And he boed himself before the king ith his face to the earth, and said, Blessed be Jehovah thy God, ho hath delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king.
And the king said, Is it ell ith the young man Absalom? And Ahimaaz ansered, When Joab sent the king’s servant, even me thy servant, I sa a great tumult, but I kne not hat it as.
And the king said, Turn aside, and stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.
And, behold, the Cushite came; and the Cushite said, Tidings for my lord the king; for Jehovah hath avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee.

And the king said unto the Cushite, Is it ell ith the young man Absalom? And the Cushite ansered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise up against thee to do thee hurt, be as that young man is.

And the king as much moved, and ent up to the chamber over the gate, and ept: and as he ent, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! ould I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!
And it as told Joab, Behold, the king eepeth and mourneth for Absalom.
And the victory that day as turned into mourning unto all the people; for the people heard say that day, The king grieveth for his son.
And the people gat them by stealth that day into the city, as people that are ashamed steal aay hen they flee in battle.
And the king covered his face, and the king cried ith a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!

And Joab came into the house to the king, and said, Thou hast shamed this day the faces of all thy servants, ho this day have saved thy life, and the lives of thy sons and of thy daughters, and the lives of thy ives, and the lives of thy concubines;

in that thou lovest them that hate thee, and hatest them that love thee. For thou hast declared this day, that princes and servants are nought unto thee: for this day I perceive, that if Absalom had lived, and all e had died this day, then it had pleased thee ell.

No therefore arise, go forth, and speak comfortably unto thy servants; for I sear by Jehovah, if thou go not forth, there ill not tarry a man ith thee this night: and that ill be orse unto thee than all the evil that hath befallen thee from thy youth until no.

Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. And they told unto all the people, saying, Behold, the king is sitting in the gate: and all the people came before the king. No Israel had fled every man to his tent.

And all the people ere at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The king delivered us out of the hand of our enemies, and he saved us out of the hand of the Philistines; and no he is fled out of the land from Absalom.
And Absalom, hom e anointed over us, is dead in battle. No therefore hy speak ye not a ord of bringing the king back?

And king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak unto the elders of Judah, saying, Why are ye the last to bring the king back to his house? seeing the speech of all Israel is come to the king, \add to bring him\add* to his house.
Ye are my brethren, ye are my bone and my flesh: herefore then are ye the last to bring back the king?
And say ye to Amasa, Art thou not my bone and my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.
And he boed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as \add the heart of\add* one man; so that they sent unto the king, \add saying\add*, Return thou, and all thy servants.
So the king returned, and came to the Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to bring the king over the Jordan.
And Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite, ho as of Bahurim, hasted and came don ith the men of Judah to meet king David.

And there ere a thousand men of Benjamin ith him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his tenty servants ith him; and they ent through the Jordan in the presence of the king.
And there ent over a ferry-boat to bring over the king’s household, and to do hat he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell don before the king, hen he as come over the Jordan.

And he said unto the king, Let not my lord impute iniquity unto me, neither do thou remember that hich thy servant did perversely the day that my lord the king ent out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.
For thy servant doth kno that I have sinned: therefore, behold, I am come this day the first of all the house of Joseph to go don to meet my lord the king.
But Abishai the son of Zeruiah ansered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed Jehovah’s anointed?

And David said, What have I to do ith you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I kno that I am this day king over Israel?
And the king said unto Shimei, Thou shalt not die. And the king sare unto him.

And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came don to meet the king; and he had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor ashed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came home in peace.
And it came to pass, hen he as come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said unto him, Wherefore entest not thou ith me, Mephibosheth?
And he ansered, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me: for thy servant said, I ill saddle me an ass, that I may ride thereon, and go ith the king; because thy servant is lame.
And he hath slandered thy servant unto my lord the king; but my lord the king is as an angel of God: do therefore hat is good in thine eyes.

For all my father’s house ere but dead men before my lord the king; yet didst thou set thy servant among them that did eat at thine on table. What right therefore have I yet that I should cry any more unto the king?
And the king said unto him, Why speakest thou any more of thy matters? I say, Thou and Ziba divide the land.
And Mephibosheth said unto the king, yea, let him take all, forasmuch as my lord the king is come in peace unto his on house.
And Barzillai the Gileadite came don from Rogelim; and he ent over the Jordan ith the king, to conduct him over the Jordan.
No Barzillai as a very aged man, even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king ith sustenance hile he lay at Mahanaim; for he as a very great man.
And the king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over ith me, and I ill sustain thee ith me in Jerusalem.
And Barzillai said unto the king, Ho many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up ith the king unto Jerusalem?

I am this day fourscore years old: can I discern beteen good and bad? can thy servant taste hat I eat or hat I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing omen? herefore then should thy servant be yet a burden unto my lord the king?
Thy servant ould but just go over the Jordan ith the king: and hy should the king recompense it me ith such a reard?

Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine on city, by the grave of my father and my mother. But behold, thy servant Chimham; let him go over ith my lord the king; and do to him hat shall seem good unto thee.
And the king ansered, Chimham shall go over ith me, and I ill do to him that hich shall seem good unto thee: and hatsoever thou shalt require of me, that ill I do for thee.
And all the people ent over the Jordan, and the king ent over: and the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his on place.
So the king ent over to Gilgal, and Chimham ent over ith him: and all the people of Judah brought the king over, and also half the people of Israel.

And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said unto the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee aay, and brought the king, and his household, over the Jordan, and all David’s men ith him?

And all the men of Judah ansered the men of Israel, Because the king is near of kin to us: herefore then are ye angry for this matter? have e eaten at all at the king’s cost? or hath he given us any gift?

And the men of Israel ansered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and e have also more \add right\add* in David than ye: hy then did ye despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the ords of the men of Judah ere fiercer than the ords of the men of Israel.

And there happened to be there a base fello, hose name as Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he ble the trumpet, and said, We have no portion in David, neither have e inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.
So all the men of Israel ent up from folloing David, and folloed Sheba the son of Bichri; but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from the Jordan even to Jerusalem.

And David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten omen his concubines, hom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ard, and provided them ith sustenance, but ent not in unto them. So they ere shut up unto the day of their death, living in idohood.
Then said the king to Amasa, Call me the men of Judah together ithin three days, and be thou here present.
So Amasa ent to call \add the men of\add* Judah together; but he tarried longer than the set time hich he had appointed him.

And David said to Abishai, No ill Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than did Absalom: take thou thy lord’s servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fortified cities, and escape out of our sight.
And there ent out after him Joab’s men, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men; and they ent out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.

When they ere at the great stone hich is in Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. And Joab as girded ith his apparel of ar that he had put on, and thereon as a girdle ith a sord fastened upon his loins in the sheath thereof; and as he ent forth it fell out.
And Joab said to Amasa, Is it ell ith thee, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard ith his right hand to kiss him.

But Amasa took no heed to the sord that as in Joab’s hand: so he smote him thereith in the body, and shed out his boels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. And Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.
And there stood by him one of Joab’s young men, and said, He that favoreth Joab, and he that is for David, let him follo Joab.

And Amasa lay alloing in his blood in the midst of the highay. And hen the man sa that all the people stood still, he carried Amasa out of the highay into the field, and cast a garment over him, hen he sa that every one that came by him stood still.
When he as removed out of the highay, all the people ent on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
And he ent through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and to Beth-maacah, and all the Berites: and they ere gathered together, and ent also after him.

And they came and besieged him in Abel of Beth-maacah, and they cast up a mound against the city, and it stood against the rampart; and all the people that ere ith Joab battered the all, to thro it don.
Then cried a ise oman out of the city, Hear, hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak ith thee.
And he came near unto her; and the oman said, Art thou Joab? And he ansered, I am. Then she said unto him, Hear the ords of thy handmaid. And he ansered, I do hear.
Then she spake, saying, They ere ont to speak in old time, saying, They shall surely ask \add counsel\add* at Abel: and so they ended \add the matter\add*.
I am of them that are peaceable and faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel: hy ilt thou sallo up the inheritance of Jehovah?
And Joab ansered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should sallo up or destroy.

The matter is not so: but a man of the hill-country of Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David; deliver him only, and I ill depart from the city. And the oman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thron to thee over the all.

Then the oman ent unto all the people in her isdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and thre it out to Joab. And he ble the trumpet, and they ere dispersed from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king.
No Joab as over all the host of Israel; and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada as over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites;
and Adoram as over the men subject to taskork; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud as the recorder;
and Sheva as scribe; and Zadok and Abiathar ere priests;
and also Ira the Jairite as chief minister unto David.

And there as a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David sought the face of Jehovah. And Jehovah said, It is for Saul, and for his bloody house, because he put to death the Gibeonites.

And the king called the Gibeonites, and said unto them ( no the Gibeonites ere not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sorn unto them: and Saul sought to slay them in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah);
and David said unto the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? and hereith shall I make atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of Jehovah?

And the Gibeonites said unto him, It is no matter of silver or gold beteen us and Saul, or his house; neither is it for us to put any man to death in Israel. And he said, What ye shall say, that ill I do for you.
And they said unto the king, The man that consumed us, and that devised against us, \add that\add* e should be destroyed from remaining in any of the borders of Israel,
let seven men of his sons be delivered unto us, and e ill hang them up unto Jehovah in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of Jehovah. And the king said, I ill give them.
But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of Jehovah’s oath that as beteen them, beteen David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

But the king took the to sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, hom she bare unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, hom she bare to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite:

and he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the mountain before Jehovah, and they fell \add all\add* seven together. And they ere put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of barley harvest.

And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until ater as poured upon them from heaven; and she suffered neither the birds of the heavens to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
And it as told David hat Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

And David ent and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh-gilead, ho had stolen them from the street of Beth-shan, here the Philistines had hanged them, in the day that the Philistines sle Saul in Gilboa;
and he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son: and they gathered the bones of them that ere hanged.

And they buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the country of Benjamin in Zela, in the sepulchre of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. And after that God as entreated for the land.
And the Philistines had ar again ith Israel; and David ent don, and his servants ith him, and fought against the Philistines. And David axed faint;
and Ishbi-benob, ho as of the sons of the giant, the eight of hose spear as three hundred \add shekels\add* of brass in eight, he being girded ith a ne \add sord\add*, thought to have slain David.

But Abishai the son of Zeruiah succored him, and smote the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David sare unto him, saying, Thou shalt go no more out ith us to battle, that thou quench not the lamp of Israel.
And it came to pass after this, that there as again ar ith the Philistines at Gob: then Sibbecai the Hushathite sle Saph, ho as of the sons of the giant.
And there as again ar ith the Philistines at Gob; and Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim the Beth-lehemite sle Goliath the Gittite, the staff of hose spear as like a eaver’s beam.
And there as again ar at Gath, here as a man of great stature, that had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, four and tenty in number; and he also as born to the giant.
And hen he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimei, David’s brother, sle him.
These four ere born to the giant in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
And David spake unto Jehovah the ords of this song in the day that Jehovah delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul:
and he said, Jehovah is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer, even mine;
God, my rock, in him ill I take refuge; My shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high toer, and my refuge; My saviour, thou savest me from violence.
I ill call upon Jehovah, ho is orthy to be praised: So shall I be saved from mine enemies.
For the aves of death compassed me; The floods of ungodliness made me afraid:
The cords of Sheol ere round about me; The snares of death came upon me.
In my distress I called upon Jehovah; Yea, I called unto my God: And he heard my voice out of his temple, And my cry \add came\add* into his ears.
Then the earth shook and trembled, The foundations of heaven quaked And ere shaken, because he as roth.
There ent up a smoke out of his nostrils, And fire out of his mouth devoured: Coals ere kindled by it.
He boed the heavens also, and came don; And thick darkness as under his feet.
And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly; Yea, he as seen upon the ings of the ind.
And he made darkness pavilions round about him, Gathering of aters, thick clouds of the skies.
At the brightness before him Coals of fire ere kindled.
Jehovah thundered from heaven, And the Most High uttered his voice.
And he sent out arros, and scattered them; Lightning, and discomfited them.
Then the channels of the sea appeared, The foundations of the orld ere laid bare, By the rebuke of Jehovah, At the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
He sent from on high, he took me; He dre me out of many aters;
He delivered me from my strong enemy, From them that hated me; for they ere too mighty for me.
They came upon me in the day of my calamity; But Jehovah as my stay.
He brought me forth also into a large place; He delivered me, because he delighted in me.
Jehovah rearded me according to my righteousness; According to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me.
For I have kept the ays of Jehovah, And have not ickedly departed from my God.
For all his ordinances ere before me; And as for his statutes, I did not depart from them.
I as also perfect toard him; And I kept myself from mine iniquity.
Therefore hath Jehovah recompensed me according to my righteousness, According to my cleanness in his eyesight.
With the merciful thou ilt sho thyself merciful; With the perfect man thou ilt sho thyself perfect;
With the pure thou ilt sho thyself pure; And ith the perverse thou ilt sho thyself froard.
And the afflicted people thou ilt save; But thine eyes are upon the haughty, that thou mayest bring them don.
For thou art my lamp, O Jehovah; And Jehovah ill lighten my darkness.
For by thee I run upon a troop; By my God do I leap over a all.
As for God, his ay is perfect: The ord of Jehovah is tried; He is a shield unto all them that take refuge in him.
For ho is God, save Jehovah? And ho is a rock, save our God?
God is my strong fortress; And he guideth the perfect in his ay.
He maketh his feet like hinds’ \add feet\add*, And setteth me upon my high places.
He teacheth my hands to ar, So that mine arms do bend a bo of brass.
Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation; And thy gentleness hath made me great.
Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; And my feet have not slipped.
I have pursued mine enemies, and destroyed them; Neither did I turn again till they ere consumed.
And I have consumed them, and smitten them through, so that they cannot arise: Yea, they are fallen under my feet.
For thou hast girded me ith strength unto the battle; Thou hast subdued under me those that rose up against me.
Thou hast also made mine enemies turn their backs unto me, That I might cut off them that hate me.
They looked, but there as none to save; Even unto Jehovah, but he ansered them not.
Then did I beat them small as the dust of the earth, I did crush them as the mire of the streets, and did spread them abroad.
Thou also hast delivered me from the strivings of my people; Thou hast kept me to be the head of the nations: A people hom I have not knon shall serve me.
The foreigners shall submit themselves unto me: As soon as they hear of me, they shall obey me.
The foreigners shall fade aay, And shall come trembling out of their close places.
Jehovah liveth; And blessed be my rock; And exalted be God, the rock of my salvation,
Even the God that executeth vengeance for me, And that bringeth don peoples under me,
And that bringeth me forth from mine enemies: Yea, thou liftest me up above them that rise up against me; Thou deliverest me from the violent man.
Therefore I ill give thanks unto thee, O Jehovah, among the nations, And ill sing praises unto thy name.
Great deliverance giveth he to his king, And shoeth lovingkindness to his anointed, To David and to his seed, for evermore.
No these are the last ords of David. David the son of Jesse saith, And the man ho as raised on high saith, The anointed of the God of Jacob, And the seet psalmist of Israel:
The Spirit of Jehovah spake by me, And his ord as upon my tongue.
The God of Israel said, The Rock of Israel spake to me: One that ruleth over men righteously, That ruleth in the fear of God,
\add He shall be\add* as the light of the morning, hen the sun riseth, A morning ithout clouds, \add When\add* the tender grass \add springeth\add* out of the earth, Through clear shining after rain.

Verily my house is not so ith God; Yet he hath made ith me an everlasting covenant, Ordered in all things, and sure: For it is all my salvation, and all \add my\add* desire, Although he maketh it not to gro.
But the ungodly shall be all of them as thorns to be thrust aay, Because they cannot be taken ith the hand;
But the man that toucheth them Must be armed ith iron and the staff of a spear: And they shall be utterly burned ith fire in \add their\add* place.
These are the names of the mighty men hom David had: Josheb-basshebeth a Tahchemonite, chief of the captains; the same as Adino the Eznite, against eight hundred slain at one time.

And after him as Eleazar the son of Dodai the son of an Ahohite, one of the three mighty men ith David, hen they defied the Philistines that ere there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel ere gone aay.
He arose, and smote the Philistines until his hand as eary, and his hand clave unto the sord; and Jehovah rought a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to take spoil.
And after him as Shammah the son of Agee a Hararite. And the Philistines ere gathered together into a troop, here as a plot of ground full of lentils; and the people fled from the Philistines.
But he stood in the midst of the plot, and defended it, and sle the Philistines; and Jehovah rought a great victory.
And three of the thirty chief men ent don, and came to David in the harvest time unto the cave of Adullam; and the troop of the Philistines as encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
And David as then in the stronghold; and the garrison of the Philistines as then in Beth-lehem.
And David longed, and said, Oh that one ould give me ater to drink of the ell of Beth-lehem, hich is by the gate!

And the three mighty men brake through the host of the Philistines, and dre ater out of the ell of Beth-lehem, that as by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: but he ould not drink thereof, but poured it out unto Jehovah.

And he said, Be it far from me, O Jehovah, that I should do this: \add shall I drink\add* the blood of the men that ent in jeopardy of their lives? therefore he ould not drink it. These things did the three mighty men.
And Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, as chief of the three. And he lifted up his spear against three hundred and sle them, and had a name among the three.
Was he not most honorable of the three? therefore he as made their captain: hobeit he attained not unto the \add first\add* three.

And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, ho had done mighty deeds, he sle the to \add sons of\add* Ariel of Moab: he ent don also and sle a lion in the midst of a pit in time of sno.
And he sle an Egyptian, a goodly man: and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; but he ent don to him ith a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and sle him ith his on spear.
These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had a name among the three mighty men.
He as more honorable than the thirty, but he attained not to the \add first\add* three. And David set him over his guard.
Asahel the brother of Joab as one of the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Beth-lehem,
Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite,
Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
Heleb the son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,
Benaiah a Pirathonite, Hiddai of the brooks of Gaash.
Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite,
Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan,
Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Ararite,
Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maacathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
Hezro the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite,
Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, armorbearers to Joab the son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite: thirty and seven in all.
And again the anger of Jehovah as kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them, saying, Go, number Israel and Judah.

And the king said to Joab the captain of the host, ho as ith him, Go no to and fro through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, and number ye the people, that I may kno the sum of the people.

And Joab said unto the king, No Jehovah thy God add unto the people, ho many soever they may be, a hundredfold; and may the eyes of my lord the king see it: but hy doth my lord the king delight in this thing?

Notithstanding, the king’s ord prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the host. And Joab and the captains of the host ent out from the presence of the king, to number the people of Israel.
And they passed over the Jordan, and encamped in Aroer, on the right side of the city that is in the middle of the valley of Gad, and unto Jazer:
then they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi; and they came to Dan-jaan, and round about to Sidon,
and came to the stronghold of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites, and of the Canaanites; and they ent out to the south of Judah, at Beer-sheba.
So hen they had gone to and fro through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and tenty days.

And Joab gave up the sum of the numbering of the people unto the king: and there ere in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that dre the sord; and the men of Judah ere five hundred thousand men.

And David’s heart smote him after that he had numbered the people. And David said unto Jehovah, I have sinned greatly in that hich I have done: but no, O Jehovah, put aay, I beseech thee, the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.
And hen David rose up in the morning, the ord of Jehovah came unto the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying,
Go and speak unto David, Thus saith Jehovah, I offer thee three things: choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.

So Gad came to David, and told him, and said unto him, Shall seven years of famine come unto thee in thy land? or ilt thou flee three months before thy foes hile they pursue thee? or shall there be three days’ pestilence in thy land? no advise thee, and consider hat anser I shall return to him that sent me.
And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall no into the hand of Jehovah; for his mercies are great; and let me not fall into the hand of man.
So Jehovah sent a pestilence upon Israel from the morning even to the time appointed; and there died of the people from Dan even to Beer-sheba seventy thousand men.

And hen the angel stretched out his hand toard Jerusalem to destroy it, Jehovah repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed the people, It is enough; no stay thy hand. And the angel of Jehovah as by the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

And David spake unto Jehovah hen he sa the angel that smote the people, and said, Lo, I have sinned, and I have done perversely; but these sheep, hat have they done? let thy hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against my father’s house.
And Gad came that day to David, and said unto him, Go up, rear an altar unto Jehovah in the threshing-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
And David ent up according to the saying of Gad, as Jehovah commanded.
And Araunah looked forth, and sa the king and his servants coming on toard him: and Araunah ent out, and boed himself before the king ith his face to the ground.
And Araunah said, Wherefore is my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshing-floor of thee, to build an altar unto Jehovah, that the plague may be stayed from the people.

And Araunah said unto David, Let my lord the king take and offer up hat seemeth good unto him: behold, the oxen for the burnt-offering, and the threshing instruments and the yokes of the oxen for the ood:
all this, O king, doth Araunah give unto the king. And Araunah said unto the king, Jehovah thy God accept thee.

And the king said unto Araunah, Nay; but I ill verily buy it of thee at a price; neither ill I offer burnt-offerings unto Jehovah my God hich cost me nothing. So David bought the threshing-floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
And David built there an altar unto Jehovah, and offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings. So Jehovah as entreated for the land, and the plague as stayed from Israel.
No king David as old and stricken in years; and they covered him ith clothes, but he gat no heat.

Wherefore his servants said unto him, Let there be sought for my lord the king a young virgin: and let her stand before the king, and cherish him; and let her lie in thy bosom, that my lord the king may get heat.
So they sought for a fair damsel throughout all the borders of Israel, and found Abishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
And the damsel as very fair; and she cherished the king, and ministered to him; but the king kne her not.
Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I ill be king: and he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
And his father had not displeased him at any time in saying, Why hast thou done so? and he as also a very goodly man; and he as born after Absalom.
And he conferred ith Joab the son of Zeruiah, and ith Abiathar the priest: and they folloing Adonijah helped him.
But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei, and Rei, and the mighty men that belonged to David, ere not ith Adonijah.
And Adonijah sle sheep and oxen and fatlings by the stone of Zoheleth, hich is beside En-rogel; and he called all his brethren, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah, the king’s servants:
but Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother, he called not.
Then Nathan spake unto Bath-sheba the mother of Solomon, saying, Hast thou not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith doth reign, and David our lord knoeth it not?
No therefore come, let me, I pray thee, give thee counsel, that thou mayest save thine on life, and the life of thy son Solomon.

Go and get thee in unto king David, and say unto him, Didst not thou, my lord, O king, sear unto thy handmaid, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne? hy then doth Adonijah reign?
Behold, hile thou yet talkest there ith the king, I also ill come in after thee, and confirm thy ords.
And Bath-sheba ent in unto the king into the chamber: and the king as very old; and Abishag the Shunammite as ministering unto the king.
And Bath-sheba boed, and did obeisance unto the king. And the king said, What ouldest thou?
And she said unto him, My lord, thou sarest by Jehovah thy God unto thy handmaid, \add saying\add*, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne.
And no, behold, Adonijah reigneth; and thou, my lord the king, knoest it not:

and he hath slain oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and hath called all the sons of the king, and Abiathar the priest, and Joab the captain of the host; but Solomon thy servant hath he not called.
And thou, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are upon thee, that thou shouldest tell them ho shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
Otherise it ill come to pass, hen my lord the king shall sleep ith his fathers, that I and my son Solomon shall be counted offenders.
And, lo, hile she yet talked ith the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
And they told the king, saying, Behold, Nathan the prophet. And hen he as come in before the king, he boed himself before the king ith his face to the ground.
And Nathan said, My lord, O king, hast thou said, Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne?

For he is gone don this day, and hath slain oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and hath called all the king’s sons, and the captains of the host, and Abiathar the priest; and, behold, they are eating and drinking before him, and say, \add Long\add* live king Adonijah.
But me, even me thy servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and thy servant Solomon, hath he not called.
Is this thing done by my lord the king, and thou hast not shoed unto thy servants ho should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?
Then king David ansered and said, Call to me Bath-sheba. And she came into the king’s presence, and stood before the king.
And the king sare, and said, As Jehovah liveth, ho hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
verily as I sare unto thee by Jehovah, the God of Israel, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne in my stead; verily so ill I do this day.
Then Bath-sheba boed ith her face to the earth, and did obeisance to the king, and said, Let my lord king David live for ever.
And king David said, Call to me Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada. And they came before the king.
And the king said unto them, Take ith you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride upon mine on mule, and bring him don to Gihon:
and let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there king over Israel; and blo ye the trumpet, and say, \add Long\add* live king Solomon.
Then ye shall come up after him, and he shall come and sit upon my throne; for he shall be king in my stead; and I have appointed him to be prince over Israel and over Judah.
And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada ansered the king, and said, Amen: Jehovah, the God of my lord the king, say so \add too\add*.
As Jehovah hath been ith my lord the king, even so be he ith Solomon, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord king David.

So Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, ent don, and caused Solomon to ride upon king David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.
And Zadok the priest took the horn of oil out of the Tent, and anointed Solomon. And they ble the trumpet; and all the people said, \add Long\add* live king Solomon.
And all the people came up after him, and the people piped ith pipes, and rejoiced ith great joy, so that the earth rent ith the sound of them.

And Adonijah and all the guests that ere ith him heard it as they had made an end of eating. And hen Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, Wherefore is this noise of the city being in an uproar?
While he yet spake, behold, Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest came: and Adonijah said, Come in; for thou art a orthy man, and bringest good tidings.
And Jonathan ansered and said to Adonijah, Verily our lord king David hath made Solomon king:

and the king hath sent ith him Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and they have caused him to ride upon the king’s mule;
and Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king in Gihon; and they are come up from thence rejoicing, so that the city rang again. This is the noise that ye have heard.
And also Solomon sitteth on the throne of the kingdom.

And moreover the king’s servants came to bless our lord king David, saying, Thy God make the name of Solomon better than thy name, and make his throne greater than thy throne: and the king boed himself upon the bed.
And also thus said the king, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, ho hath given one to sit on my throne this day, mine eyes even seeing it.
And all the guests of Adonijah ere afraid, and rose up, and ent every man his ay.
And Adonijah feared because of Solomon; and he arose, and ent, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.

And it as told Solomon, saying, Behold, Adonijah feareth king Solomon; for, lo, he hath laid hold on the horns of the altar, saying, Let king Solomon sear unto me first that he ill not slay his servant ith the sord.
And Solomon said, If he shall sho himself a orthy man, there shall not a hair of him fall to the earth; but if ickedness be found in him, he shall die.
So king Solomon sent, and they brought him don from the altar. And he came and did obeisance to king Solomon; and Solomon said unto him, Go to thy house.
No the days of David dre nigh that he should die; and he charged Solomon his son, saying,
I am going the ay of all the earth: be thou strong therefore, and sho thyself a man;

and keep the charge of Jehovah thy God, to alk in his ays, to keep his statutes, \add and\add* his commandments, and his ordinances, and his testimonies, according to that hich is ritten in the la of Moses, that thou mayest prosper in all that thou doest, and hithersoever thou turnest thyself;

that Jehovah may establish his ord hich he spake concerning me, saying, If thy children take heed to their ay, to alk before me in truth ith all their heart and ith all their soul, there shall not fail thee ( said he) a man on the throne of Israel.

Moreover thou knoest also hat Joab the son of Zeruiah did unto me, even hat he did to the to captains of the hosts of Israel, unto Abner the son of Ner, and unto Amasa the son of Jether, hom he sle, and shed the blood of ar in peace, and put the blood of ar upon his girdle that as about his loins, and in his shoes that ere on his feet.
Do therefore according to thy isdom, and let not his hoar head go don to Sheol in peace.
But sho kindness unto the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be of those that eat at thy table; for so they came to me hen I fled from Absalom thy brother.

And, behold, there is ith thee Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjamite, of Bahurim, ho cursed me ith a grievous curse in the day hen I ent to Mahanaim; but he came don to meet me at the Jordan, and I sare to him by Jehovah, saying, I ill not put thee to death ith the sord.
No therefore hold him not guiltless, for thou art a ise man; and thou ilt kno hat thou oughtest to do unto him, and thou shalt bring his hoar head don to Sheol ith blood.
And David slept ith his fathers, and as buried in the city of David.
And the days that David reigned over Israel ere forty years: seven years reigned he in Hebron, and thirty and three years reigned he in Jerusalem.
And Solomon sat upon the throne of David his father; and his kingdom as established greatly.
Then Adonijah the son of Haggith came to Bath-sheba the mother of Solomon. And she said, Comest thou peaceably? And he said, Peaceably.
He said moreover, I have somehat to say unto thee. And she said, Say on.

And he said, Thou knoest that the kingdom as mine, and that all Israel set their faces on me, that I should reign: hobeit the kingdom is turned about, and is become my brother’s; for it as his from Jehovah.
And no I ask one petition of thee; deny me not. And she said unto him, Say on.
And he said, Speak, I pray thee, unto Solomon the king ( for he ill not say thee nay), that he give me Abishag the Shunammite to ife.
And Bath-sheba said, Well; I ill speak for thee unto the king.

Bath-sheba therefore ent unto king Solomon, to speak unto him for Adonijah. And the king rose up to meet her, and boed himself unto her, and sat don on his throne, and caused a throne to be set for the king’s mother; and she sat on his right hand.
Then she said, I ask one small petition of thee; deny me not. And the king said unto her, Ask on, my mother; for I ill not deny thee.
And she said, Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah thy brother to ife.

And king Solomon ansered and said unto his mother, And hy dost thou ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? ask for him the kingdom also; for he is mine elder brother; even for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab the son of Zeruiah.
Then king Solomon sare by Jehovah, saying, God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah hath not spoken this ord against his on life.
No therefore as Jehovah liveth, ho hath established me, and set me on the throne of David my father, and ho hath made me a house, as he promised, surely Adonijah shall be put to death this day.
And king Solomon sent by Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he fell upon him, so that he died.

And unto Abiathar the priest said the king, Get thee to Anathoth, unto thine on fields; for thou art orthy of death: but I ill not at this time put thee to death, because thou barest the ark of the Lord Jehovah before David my father, and because thou ast afflicted in all herein my father as afflicted.
So Solomon thrust out Abiathar from being priest unto Jehovah, that he might fulfil the ord of Jehovah, hich he spake concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.
And the tidings came to Joab; for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he turned not after Absalom. And Joab fled unto the Tent of Jehovah, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.
And it as told king Solomon, Joab is fled unto the Tent of Jehovah, and, behold, he is by the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, saying, Go, fall upon him.

And Benaiah came to the Tent of Jehovah, and said unto him, Thus saith the king, Come forth. And he said, Nay; but I ill die here. And Benaiah brought the king ord again, saying, Thus said Joab, and thus he ansered me.
And the king said unto him, Do as he hath said, and fall upon him, and bury him; that thou mayest take aay the blood, hich Joab shed ithout cause, from me and from my father’s house.

And Jehovah ill return his blood upon his on head, because he fell upon to men more righteous and better than he, and sle them ith the sord, and my father David kne it not, \add to it\add*, Abner the son of Ner, captain of the host of Israel, and Amasa the son of Jether, captain of the host of Judah.

So shall their blood return upon the head of Joab, and upon the head of his seed for ever: but unto David, and unto his seed, and unto his house, and unto his throne, shall there be peace for ever from Jehovah.
Then Benaiah the son of Jehoiada ent up, and fell upon him, and sle him; and he as buried in his on house in the ilderness.
And the king put Benaiah the son of Jehoiada in his room over the host; and Zadok the priest did the king put in the room of Abiathar.
And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said unto him, Build thee a house in Jerusalem, and dell there, and go not forth thence any hither.
For on the day thou goest out, and passest over the brook Kidron, kno thou for certain that thou shalt surely die: thy blood shall be upon thine on head.
And Shimei said unto the king, The saying is good: as my lord the king hath said, so ill thy servant do. And Shimei delt in Jerusalem many days.
And it came to pass at the end of three years, that to of the servants of Shimei ran aay unto Achish, son of Maacah, king of Gath. And they told Shimei, saying, Behold, thy servants are in Gath.
And Shimei arose, and saddled his ass, and ent to Gath to Achish, to seek his servants; and Shimei ent, and brought his servants from Gath.
And it as told Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath, and as come again.

And the king sent and called for Shimei, and said unto him, Did I not adjure thee by Jehovah, and protest unto thee, saying, Kno for certain, that on the day thou goest out, and alkest abroad any hither, thou shalt surely die? and thou saidst unto me, The saying that I have heard is good.
Why then hast thou not kept the oath of Jehovah, and the commandment that I have charged thee ith?
The king said moreover to Shimei, Thou knoest all the ickedness hich thy heart is privy to, that thou didst to David my father: therefore Jehovah shall return thy ickedness upon thine on head.
But king Solomon shall be blessed, and the throne of David shall be established before Jehovah for ever.
So the king commanded Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he ent out, and fell upon him, so that he died. And the kingdom as established in the hand of Solomon.

And Solomon made affinity ith Pharaoh king of Egypt, and took Pharaoh’s daughter, and brought her into the city of David, until he had made an end of building his on house, and the house of Jehovah, and the all of Jerusalem round about.
Only the people sacrificed in the high places, because there as no house built for the name of Jehovah until those days.
And Solomon loved Jehovah, alking in the statutes of David his father: only he sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.
And the king ent to Gibeon to sacrifice there; for that as the great high place: a thousand burnt-offerings did Solomon offer upon that altar.
In Gibeon Jehovah appeared to Solomon in a dream by night; and God said, Ask hat I shall give thee.

And Solomon said, Thou hast shoed unto thy servant David my father great lovingkindness, according as he alked before thee in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart ith thee; and thou hast kept for him this great lovingkindness, that thou hast given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day.
And no, O Jehovah my God, thou hast made thy servant king instead of David my father: and I am but a little child; I kno not ho to go out or come in.
And thy servant is in the midst of thy people hich thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.
Give thy servant therefore an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern beteen good and evil; for ho is able to judge this thy great people?
And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.

And God said unto him, Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life, neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies, but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern justice;

behold, I have done according to thy ord: lo, I have given thee a ise and an understanding heart; so that there hath been none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.
And I have also given thee that hich thou hast not asked, both riches and honor, so that there shall not be any among the kings like unto thee, all thy days.
And if thou ilt alk in my ays, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as thy father David did alk, then I ill lengthen thy days.

And Solomon aoke; and, behold, it as a dream: and he came to Jerusalem, and stood before the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, and offered up burnt-offerings, and offered peace-offerings, and made a feast to all his servants.
Then there came to omen that ere harlots, unto the king, and stood before him.
And the one oman said, Oh, my lord, I and this oman dell in one house; and I as delivered of a child ith her in the house.
And it came to pass the third day after I as delivered, that this oman as delivered also; and e ere together; there as no stranger ith us in the house, save e to in the house.
And this oman’s child died in the night, because she lay upon it.
And she arose at midnight, and took my son from beside me, hile thy handmaid slept, and laid it in her bosom, and laid her dead child in my bosom.
And hen I rose in the morning to give my child suck, behold, it as dead; but hen I had looked at it in the morning, behold, it as not my son, hom I did bear.
And the other oman said, Nay; but the living is my son, and the dead is thy son. And this said, No; but the dead is thy son, and the living is my son. Thus they spake before the king.
Then said the king, The one saith, This is my son that liveth, and thy son is the dead: and the other saith, Nay; but thy son is the dead, and my son is the living.
And the king said, Fetch me a sord. And they brought a sord before the king.
And the king said, Divide the living child in to, and give half to the one, and half to the other.

Then spake the oman hose the living child as unto the king, for her heart yearned over her son, and she said, Oh, my lord, give her the living child, and in no ise slay it. But the other said, It shall be neither mine nor thine; divide it.
Then the king ansered and said, Give her the living child, and in no ise slay it: she is the mother thereof.
And all Israel heard of the judgment hich the king had judged; and they feared the king: for they sa that the isdom of God as in him, to do justice.
And king Solomon as king over all Israel.
And these ere the princes hom he had: Azariah the son of Zadok, the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud, the recorder;
and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada as over the host; and Zadok and Abiathar ere priests;
and Azariah the son of Nathan as over the officers; and Zabud the son of Nathan as chief minister, \add and\add* the king’s friend;
and Ahishar as over the household; and Adoniram the son of Abda as over the men subject to taskork.
And Solomon had telve officers over all Israel, ho provided victuals for the king and his household: each man had to make provision for a month in the year.
And these are their names: Ben-hur, in the hill-country of Ephraim;
Ben-deker, in Makaz, and in Shaalbim, and Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan;
