Ben-hesed, in Arubboth ( to him \add pertained\add* Socoh, and all the land of Hepher);
Ben-abinadab, in all the height of Dor ( he had Taphath the daughter of Solomon to ife);
Baana the son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth-shean hich is beside Zarethan, beneath Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;

Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead ( to him \add pertained\add* the tons of Jair the son of Manasseh, hich are in Gilead; \add even\add* to him \add pertained\add* the region of Argob, hich is in Bashan, threescore great cities ith alls and brazen bars);
Ahinadab the son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
Ahimaaz, in Naphtali ( he also took Basemath the daughter of Solomon to ife);
Baana the son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
Jehoshaphat the son of Paruah, in Issachar;
Shimei the son of Ela, in Benjamin;
Geber the son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan; and \add he as\add* the only officer that as in the land.
Judah and Israel ere many as the sand hich is by the sea in multitude, eating and drinking and making merry.
And Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River unto the land of the Philistines, and unto the border of Egypt: they brought tribute, and served Solomon all the days of his life.
And Solomon’s provision for one day as thirty measures of fine flour, and threescore measures of meal,
ten fat oxen, and tenty oxen out of the pastures, and a hundred sheep, besides harts, and gazelles, and roebucks, and fatted fol.
For he had dominion over all \add the region\add* on this side the River, from Tiphsah even to Gaza, over all the kings on this side the River: and he had peace on all sides round about him.
And Judah and Israel delt safely, every man under his vine and under his fig-tree, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, all the days of Solomon.
And Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and telve thousand horsemen.
And those officers provided victuals for king Solomon, and for all that came unto king Solomon’s table, every man in his month; they let nothing be lacking.
Barley also and stra for the horses and sift steeds brought they unto the place here \add the officers\add* ere, every man according to his charge.
And God gave Solomon isdom and understanding exceeding much, and largeness of heart, even as the sand that is on the sea-shore.
And Solomon’s isdom excelled the isdom of all the children of the east, and all the isdom of Egypt.
For he as iser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame as in all the nations round about.
And he spake three thousand proverbs; and his songs ere a thousand and five.
And he spake of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon even unto the hyssop that springeth out of the all; he spake also of beasts, and of birds, and of creeping things, and of fishes.
And there came of all peoples to hear the isdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth, ho had heard of his isdom.
And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants unto Solomon; for he had heard that they had anointed him king in the room of his father: for Hiram as ever a lover of David.
And Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,
Thou knoest ho that David my father could not build a house for the name of Jehovah his God for the ars hich ere about him on every side, until Jehovah put them under the soles of his feet.
But no Jehovah my God hath given me rest on every side; there is neither adversary, nor evil occurrence.

And, behold, I purpose to build a house for the name of Jehovah my God, as Jehovah spake unto David my father, saying, Thy son, hom I ill set upon thy throne in thy room, he shall build the house for my name.

No therefore command thou that they cut me cedar-trees out of Lebanon; and my servants shall be ith thy servants; and I ill give thee hire for thy servants according to all that thou shalt say: for thou knoest that there is not among us any that knoeth ho to cut timber like unto the Sidonians.
And it came to pass, hen Hiram heard the ords of Solomon, that he rejoiced greatly, and said, Blessed be Jehovah this day, ho hath given unto David a ise son over this great people.
And Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, I have heard \add the message\add* hich thou hast sent unto me: I ill do all thy desire concerning timber of cedar, and concerning timber of fir.

My servants shall bring them don from Lebanon unto the sea; and I ill make them into rafts to go by sea unto the place that thou shalt appoint me, and ill cause them to be broken up there, and thou shalt receive them; and thou shalt accomplish my desire, in giving food for my household.
So Hiram gave Solomon timber of cedar and timber of fir according to all his desire.
And Solomon gave Hiram tenty thousand measures of heat for food to his household, and tenty measures of pure oil: thus gave Solomon to Hiram year by year.
And Jehovah gave Solomon isdom, as he promised him; and there as peace beteen Hiram and Solomon; and they to made a league together.
And king Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel; and the levy as thirty thousand men.
And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month by courses; a month they ere in Lebanon, and to months at home: and Adoniram as over the men subject to taskork.
And Solomon had threescore and ten thousand that bare burdens, and fourscore thousand that ere heers in the mountains;
besides Solomon’s chief officers that ere over the ork, three thousand and three hundred, ho bare rule over the people that rought in the ork.
And the king commanded, and they heed out great stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house ith rought stone.
And Solomon’s builders and Hiram’s builders and the Gebalites did fashion them, and prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.

And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel ere come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Ziv, hich is the second month, that he began to build the house of Jehovah.
And the house hich king Solomon built for Jehovah, the length thereof as threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof tenty \add cubits\add*, and the height thereof thirty cubits.
And the porch before the temple of the house, tenty cubits as the length thereof, according to the breadth of the house; \add and\add* ten cubits as the breadth thereof before the house.
And for the house he made indos of fixed lattice-ork.
And against the all of the house he built stories round about, against the alls of the house round about, both of the temple and of the oracle; and he made side-chambers round about.

The nethermost story as five cubits broad, and the middle as six cubits broad, and the third as seven cubits broad; for on the outside he made offsets \add in the all\add* of the house round about, that \add the beams\add* should not have hold in the alls of the house.
And the house, hen it as in building, as built of stone made ready at the quarry; and there as neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron heard in the house, hile it as in building.
The door for the middle side-chambers as in the right side of the house: and they ent up by inding stairs into the middle \add story\add*, and out of the middle into the third.
So he built the house, and finished it; and he covered the house ith beams and planks of cedar.
And he built the stories against all the house, each five cubits high: and they rested on the house ith timber of cedar.
And the ord of Jehovah came to Solomon, saying,

Concerning this house hich thou art building, if thou ilt alk in my statutes, and execute mine ordinances, and keep all my commandments to alk in them; then ill I establish my ord ith thee, hich I spake unto David thy father.
And I ill dell among the children of Israel, and ill not forsake my people Israel.
So Solomon built the house, and finished it.

And he built the alls of the house ithin ith boards of cedar: from the floor of the house unto the alls of the ceiling, he covered them on the inside ith ood; and he covered the floor of the house ith boards of fir.

And he built tenty cubits on the hinder part of the house ith boards of cedar from the floor unto the alls \add of the ceiling\add*: he built \add them\add* for it ithin, for an oracle, even for the most holy place.
And the house, that is, the temple before \add the oracle\add*, as forty cubits \add long\add*.
And there as cedar on the house ithin, carved ith knops and open floers: all as cedar; there as no stone seen.
And he prepared an oracle in the midst of the house ithin, to set there the ark of the covenant of Jehovah.

And ithin the oracle as \add a space of\add* tenty cubits in length, and tenty cubits in breadth, and tenty cubits in the height thereof; and he overlaid it ith pure gold: and he covered the altar ith cedar.
So Solomon overlaid the house ithin ith pure gold: and he dre chains of gold across before the oracle; and he overlaid it ith gold.
And the hole house he overlaid ith gold, until all the house as finished: also the hole altar that belonged to the oracle he overlaid ith gold.
And in the oracle he made to cherubim of olive-ood, each ten cubits high.
And five cubits as the one ing of the cherub, and five cubits the other ing of the cherub: from the uttermost part of the one ing unto the uttermost part of the other ere ten cubits.
And the other cherub as ten cubits: both the cherubim ere of one measure and one form.
The height of the one cherub as ten cubits, and so as it of the other cherub.

And he set the cherubim ithin the inner house; and the ings of the cherubim ere stretched forth, so that the ing of the one touched the one all, and the ing of the other cherub touched the other all; and their ings touched one another in the midst of the house.
And he overlaid the cherubim ith gold.
And he carved all the alls of the house round about ith carved figures of cherubim and palm-trees and open floers, ithin and ithout.
And the floor of the house he overlaid ith gold, ithin and ithout.
And for the entrance of the oracle he made doors of olive-ood: the lintel \add and\add* door-posts ere a fifth part \add of the all\add*.

So \add he made\add* to doors of olive-ood; and he carved upon them carvings of cherubim and palm-trees and open floers, and overlaid them ith gold; and he spread the gold upon the cherubim, and upon the palm-trees.
So also made he for the entrance of the temple door-posts of olive-ood, out of a fourth part \add of the all\add*;
and to doors of fir-ood: the to leaves of the one door ere folding, and the to leaves of the other door ere folding.
And he carved \add thereon\add* cherubim and palm-trees and open floers; and he overlaid them ith gold fitted upon the graven ork.
And he built the inner court ith three courses of hen stone, and a course of cedar beams.
In the fourth year as the foundation of the house of Jehovah laid, in the month Ziv.

And in the eleventh year, in the month Bul, hich is the eighth month, as the house finished throughout all the parts thereof, and according to all the fashion of it. So as he seven years in building it.
And Solomon as building his on house thirteen years, and he finished all his house.

For he built the house of the forest of Lebanon; the length thereof as a hundred cubits, and the breadth thereof fifty cubits, and the height thereof thirty cubits, upon four ros of cedar pillars, ith cedar beams upon the pillars.
And it as covered ith cedar above over the forty and five beams, that ere upon the pillars; fifteen in a ro.
And there ere beams in three ros, and indo as over against indo in three ranks.
And all the doors and posts ere made square ith beams: and indo as over against indo in three ranks.
And he made the porch of pillars; the length thereof as fifty cubits, and the breadth thereof thirty cubits; and a porch before them; and pillars and a threshold before them.
And he made the porch of the throne here he as to judge, even the porch of judgment: and it as covered ith cedar from floor to floor.
And his house here he as to dell, the other court ithin the porch, as of the like ork. He made also a house for Pharaoh’s daughter (hom Solomon had taken to ife), like unto this porch.
All these ere of costly stones, even of hen stone, according to measure, saed ith sas, ithin and ithout, even from the foundation unto the coping, and so on the outside unto the great court.
And the foundation as of costly stones, even great stones, stones of ten cubits, and stones of eight cubits.
And above ere costly stones, even hen stone, according to measure, and cedar-ood.
And the great court round about had three courses of hen stone, and a course of cedar beams; like as the inner court of the house of Jehovah, and the porch of the house.
And king Solomon sent and fetched Hiram out of Tyre.

He as the son of a ido of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father as a man of Tyre, a orker in brass; and he as filled ith isdom and understanding and skill, to ork all orks in brass. And he came to king Solomon, and rought all his ork.
For he fashioned the to pillars of brass, eighteen cubits high apiece: and a line of telve cubits compassed either of them about.
And he made to capitals of molten brass, to set upon the tops of the pillars: the height of the one capital as five cubits, and the height of the other capital as five cubits.
There ere nets of checker-ork, and reaths of chain-ork, for the capitals hich ere upon the top of the pillars; seven for the one capital, and seven for the other capital.
So he made the pillars; and there ere to ros round about upon the one netork, to cover the capitals that ere upon the top of the pillars: and so did he for the other capital.
And the capitals that ere upon the top of the pillars in the porch ere of lily-ork, four cubits.
And there ere capitals above also upon the to pillars, close by the belly hich as beside the netork: and the pomegranates ere to hundred, in ros round about upon the other capital.
And he set up the pillars at the porch of the temple: and he set up the right pillar, and called the name thereof Jachin; and he set up the left pillar, and called the name thereof Boaz.
And upon the top of the pillars as lily-ork: so as the ork of the pillars finished.
And he made the molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim, round in compass, and the height thereof as five cubits; and a line of thirty cubits compassed it round about.
And under the brim of it round about there ere knops hich did compass it, for ten cubits, compassing the sea round about: the knops ere in to ros, cast hen it as cast.

It stood upon telve oxen, three looking toard the north, and three looking toard the est, and three looking toard the south, and three looking toard the east; and the sea as set upon them above, and all their hinder parts ere inard.
And it as a handbreadth thick: and the brim thereof as rought like the brim of a cup, like the floer of a lily: it held to thousand baths.
And he made the ten bases of brass; four cubits as the length of one base, and four cubits the breadth thereof, and three cubits the height of it.
And the ork of the bases as on this manner: they had panels; and there ere panels beteen the ledges;
and on the panels that ere beteen the ledges ere lions, oxen, and cherubim; and upon the ledges there as a pedestal above; and beneath the lions and oxen ere reaths of hanging ork.
And every base had four brazen heels, and axles of brass; and the four feet thereof had undersetters: beneath the laver ere the undersetters molten, ith reaths at the side of each.

And the mouth of it ithin the capital and above as a cubit: and the mouth thereof as round after the ork of a pedestal, a cubit and a half; and also upon the mouth of it ere gravings, and their panels ere foursquare, not round.
And the four heels ere underneath the panels; and the axletrees of the heels ere in the base: and the height of a heel as a cubit and half a cubit.
And the ork of the heels as like the ork of a chariot heel: their axletrees, and their felloes, and their spokes, and their naves, ere all molten.
And there ere four undersetters at the four corners of each base: the undersetters thereof ere of the base itself.
And in the top of the base as there a round compass half a cubit high; and on the top of the base the stays thereof and the panels thereof ere of the same.
And on the plates of the stays thereof, and on the panels thereof, he graved cherubim, lions, and palm-trees, according to the space of each, ith reaths round about.
After this manner he made the ten bases: all of them had one casting, one measure, and one form.
And he made ten lavers of brass: one laver contained forty baths; and every laver as four cubits; and upon every one of the ten bases one laver.
And he set the bases, five on the right side of the house, and five on the left side of the house: and he set the sea on the right side of the house eastard, toard the south.
And Hiram made the lavers, and the shovels, and the basins. So Hiram made an end of doing all the ork that he rought for king Solomon in the house of Jehovah:
the to pillars, and the to bols of the capitals that ere on the top of the pillars; and the to netorks to cover the to bols of the capitals that ere on the top of the pillars;
and the four hundred pomegranates for the to netorks; to ros of pomegranates for each netork, to cover the to bols of the capitals that ere upon the pillars;
and the ten bases, and the ten lavers on the bases;
and the one sea, and the telve oxen under the sea;
and the pots, and the shovels, and the basins: even all these vessels, hich Hiram made for king Solomon, in the house of Jehovah, ere of burnished brass.
In the plain of the Jordan did the king cast them, in the clay ground beteen Succoth and Zarethan.
And Solomon left all the vessels \add uneighed\add*, because they ere exceeding many: the eight of the brass could not be found out.
And Solomon made all the vessels that ere in the house of Jehovah: the golden altar, and the table hereupon the shobread as, of gold;
and the candlesticks, five on the right side, and five on the left, before the oracle, of pure gold; and the floers, and the lamps, and the tongs, of gold;

and the cups, and the snuffers, and the basins, and the spoons, and the firepans, of pure gold; and the hinges, both for the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and for the doors of the house, \add to it\add*, of the temple, of gold.

Thus all the ork that king Solomon rought in the house of Jehovah as finished. And Solomon brought in the things hich David his father had dedicated, \add even\add* the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, and put them in the treasuries of the house of Jehovah.

Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the princes of the fathers’ \add houses\add* of the children of Israel, unto king Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of Jehovah out of the city of David, hich is Zion.
And all the men of Israel assembled themselves unto king Solomon at the feast, in the month Ethanim, hich is the seventh month.
And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark.
And they brought up the ark of Jehovah, and the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that ere in the Tent; even these did the priests and the Levites bring up.
And king Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, that ere assembled unto him, ere ith him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen, that could not be counted nor numbered for multitude.
And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of Jehovah unto its place, into the oracle of the house, to the most holy place, even under the ings of the cherubim.
For the cherubim spread forth their ings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and the staves thereof above.
And the staves ere so long that the ends of the staves ere seen from the holy place before the oracle; but they ere not seen ithout: and there they are unto this day.
There as nothing in the ark save the to tables of stone hich Moses put there at Horeb, hen Jehovah made a covenant ith the children of Israel, hen they came out of the land of Egypt.
And it came to pass, hen the priests ere come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of Jehovah,
so that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud; for the glory of Jehovah filled the house of Jehovah.
Then spake Solomon, Jehovah hath said that he ould dell in the thick darkness.
I have surely built thee a house of habitation, a place for thee to dell in for ever.
And the king turned his face about, and blessed all the assembly of Israel: and all the assembly of Israel stood.
And he said, Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, ho spake ith his mouth unto David my father, and hath ith his hand fulfilled it, saying,

Since the day that I brought forth my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house, that my name might be there; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.
No it as in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of Jehovah, the God of Israel.
But Jehovah said unto David my father, Whereas it as in thy heart to build a house for my name, thou didst ell that it as in thy heart:
nevertheless thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house for my name.

And Jehovah hath established his ord that he spake; for I am risen up in the room of David my father, and sit on the throne of Israel, as Jehovah promised, and have built the house for the name of Jehovah, the God of Israel.
And there have I set a place for the ark, herein is the covenant of Jehovah, hich he made ith our fathers, hen he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
And Solomon stood before the altar of Jehovah in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and spread forth his hands toard heaven;

and he said, O Jehovah, the God of Israel, there is no God like thee, in heaven above, or on earth beneath; ho keepest covenant and lovingkindness ith thy servants, that alk before thee ith all their heart;
ho hast kept ith thy servant David my father that hich thou didst promise him: yea, thou spakest ith thy mouth, and hast fulfilled it ith thy hand, as it is this day.

No therefore, O Jehovah, the God of Israel, keep ith thy servant David my father that hich thou hast promised him, saying, There shall not fail thee a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel, if only thy children take heed to their ay, to alk before me as thou hast alked before me.
No therefore, O God of Israel, let thy ord, I pray thee, be verified, hich thou spakest unto thy servant David my father.
But ill God in very deed dell on the earth? behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; ho much less this house that I have builded!
Yet have thou respect unto the prayer of thy servant, and to his supplication, O Jehovah my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer hich thy servant prayeth before thee this day;

that thine eyes may be open toard this house night and day, even toard the place hereof thou hast said, My name shall be there; to hearken unto the prayer hich thy servant shall pray toard this place.
And hearken thou to the supplication of thy servant, and of thy people Israel, hen they shall pray toard this place: yea, hear thou in heaven thy delling-place; and hen thou hearest, forgive.
If a man sin against his neighbor, and an oath be laid upon him to cause him to sear, and he come \add and\add* sear before thine altar in this house;
then hear thou in heaven, and do, and judge thy servants, condemning the icked, to bring his ay upon his on head, and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.

When thy people Israel are smitten don before the enemy, because they have sinned against thee; if they turn again to thee, and confess thy name, and pray and make supplication unto thee in this house:
then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy people Israel, and bring them again unto the land hich thou gavest unto their fathers.
When heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against thee; if they pray toard this place, and confess thy name, and turn from their sin, hen thou dost afflict them:

then hear thou in heaven, and forgive the sin of thy servants, and of thy people Israel, hen thou teachest them the good ay herein they should alk; and send rain upon thy land, hich thou hast given to thy people for an inheritance.

If there be in the land famine, if there be pestilence, if there be blasting \add or\add* milde, locust \add or\add* caterpillar; if their enemy besiege them in the land of their cities; hatsoever plague, hatsoever sickness there be;
hat prayer and supplication soever be made by any man, \add or\add* by all thy people Israel, ho shall kno every man the plague of his on heart, and spread forth his hands toard this house:

then hear thou in heaven thy delling-place, and forgive, and do, and render unto every man according to all his ays, hose heart thou knoest; ( for thou, even thou only, knoest the hearts of all the children of men;)
that they may fear thee all the days that they live in the land hich thou gavest unto our fathers.
Moreover concerning the foreigner, that is not of thy people Israel, hen he shall come out of a far country for thy name’s sake
( for they shall hear of thy great name, and of thy mighty hand, and of thine outstretched arm); hen he shall come and pray toard this house;

hear thou in heaven thy delling-place, and do according to all that the foreigner calleth to thee for; that all the peoples of the earth may kno thy name, to fear thee, as doth thy people Israel, and that they may kno that this house hich I have built is called by thy name.

If thy people go out to battle against their enemy, by hatsoever ay thou shalt send them, and they pray unto Jehovah toard the city hich thou hast chosen, and toard the house hich I have built for thy name;
then hear thou in heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.

If they sin against thee ( for there is no man that sinneth not), and thou be angry ith them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them aay captive unto the land of the enemy, far off or near;

yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land hither they are carried captive, and turn again, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captive, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, e have dealt ickedly;

if they return unto thee ith all their heart and ith all their soul in the land of their enemies, ho carried them captive, and pray unto thee toard their land, hich thou gavest unto their fathers, the city hich thou hast chosen, and the house hich I have built for thy name:
then hear thou their prayer and their supplication in heaven thy delling-place, and maintain their cause;

and forgive thy people ho have sinned against thee, and all their transgressions herein they have transgressed against thee; and give them compassion before those ho carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them
( for they are thy people, and thine inheritance, hich thou broughtest forth out of Egypt, from the midst of the furnace of iron);
that thine eyes may be open unto the supplication of thy servant, and unto the supplication of thy people Israel, to hearken unto them hensoever they cry unto thee.
For thou didst separate them from among all the peoples of the earth, to be thine inheritance, as thou spakest by Moses thy servant, hen thou broughtest our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord Jehovah.

And it as so, that, hen Solomon had made an end of praying all this prayer and supplication unto Jehovah, he arose from before the altar of Jehovah, from kneeling on his knees ith his hands spread forth toard heaven.
And he stood, and blessed all the assembly of Israel ith a loud voice, saying,
Blessed be Jehovah, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one ord of all his good promise, hich he promised by Moses his servant.
Jehovah our God be ith us, as he as ith our fathers: let him not leave us, nor forsake us;
that he may incline our hearts unto him, to alk in all his ays, and to keep his commandments, and his statutes, and his ordinances, hich he commanded our fathers.

And let these my ords, hereith I have made supplication before Jehovah, be nigh unto Jehovah our God day and night, that he maintain the cause of his servant, and the cause of his people Israel, as every day shall require;
that all the peoples of the earth may kno that Jehovah, he is God; there is none else.
Let your heart therefore be perfect ith Jehovah our God, to alk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as at this day.
And the king, and all Israel ith him, offered sacrifice before Jehovah.

And Solomon offered for the sacrifice of peace-offerings, hich he offered unto Jehovah, to and tenty thousand oxen, and a hundred and tenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Israel dedicated the house of Jehovah.

The same day did the king hallo the middle of the court that as before the house of Jehovah; for there he offered the burnt-offering, and the meal-offering, and the fat of the peace-offerings, because the brazen altar that as before Jehovah as too little to receive the burnt-offering, and the meal-offering, and the fat of the peace-offerings.

So Solomon held the feast at that time, and all Israel ith him, a great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath unto the brook of Egypt, before Jehovah our God, seven days and seven days, even fourteen days.

On the eighth day he sent the people aay; and they blessed the king, and ent unto their tents joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that Jehovah had shoed unto David his servant, and to Israel his people.
And it came to pass, hen Solomon had finished the building of the house of Jehovah, and the king’s house, and all Solomon’s desire hich he as pleased to do,
that Jehovah appeared to Solomon the second time, as he had appeared unto him at Gibeon.

And Jehovah said unto him, I have heard thy prayer and thy supplication, that thou hast made before me: I have halloed this house, hich thou hast built, to put my name there for ever; and mine eyes and my heart shall be there perpetually.

And as for thee, if thou ilt alk before me, as David thy father alked, in integrity of heart, and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded thee, and ilt keep my statutes and mine ordinances;
then I ill establish the throne of thy kingdom over Israel for ever, according as I promised to David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man upon the throne of Israel.
But if ye shall turn aay from folloing me, ye or your children, and not keep my commandments and my statutes hich I have set before you, but shall go and serve other gods, and orship them;

then ill I cut off Israel out of the land hich I have given them; and this house, hich I have halloed for my name, ill I cast out of my sight; and Israel shall be a proverb and a byord among all peoples.
And though this house is so high, yet shall every one that passeth by it be astonished, and shall hiss; and they shall say, Why hath Jehovah done thus unto this land, and to this house?

and they shall anser, Because they forsook Jehovah their God, ho brought forth their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold on other gods, and orshipped them, and served them: therefore hath Jehovah brought all this evil upon them.
And it came to pass at the end of tenty years, herein Solomon had built the to houses, the house of Jehovah and the king’s house
( no Hiram the king of Tyre had furnished Solomon ith cedar-trees and fir-trees, and ith gold, according to all his desire), that then king Solomon gave Hiram tenty cities in the land of Galilee.
And Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities hich Solomon had given him; and they pleased him not.
And he said, What cities are these hich thou hast given me, my brother? And he called them the land of Cabul unto this day.
And Hiram sent to the king sixscore talents of gold.
And this is the reason of the levy hich king Solomon raised, to build the house of Jehovah, and his on house, and Millo, and the all of Jerusalem, and Hazor, and Megiddo, and Gezer.
Pharaoh king of Egypt had gone up, and taken Gezer, and burnt it ith fire, and slain the Canaanites that delt in the city, and given it for a portion unto his daughter, Solomon’s ife.
And Solomon built Gezer, and Beth-horon the nether,
and Baalath, and Tamar in the ilderness, in the land,

and all the store-cities that Solomon had, and the cities for his chariots, and the cities for his horsemen, and that hich Solomon desired to build for his pleasure in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
As for all the people that ere left of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, ho ere not of the children of Israel;
their children that ere left after them in the land, hom the children of Israel ere not able utterly to destroy, of them did Solomon raise a levy of bondservants unto this day.
But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondservants; but they ere the men of ar, and his servants, and his princes, and his captains, and rulers of his chariots and of his horsemen.
These ere the chief officers that ere over Solomon’s ork, five hundred and fifty, ho bare rule over the people that rought in the ork.
But Pharaoh’s daughter came up out of the city of David unto her house hich \add Solomon\add* had built for her: then did he build Millo.

And three times in a year did Solomon offer burnt-offerings and peace-offerings upon the altar hich he built unto Jehovah, burning incense thereith, \add upon the altar\add* that as before Jehovah. So he finished the house.
And king Solomon made a navy of ships in Ezion-geber, hich is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom.
And Hiram sent in the navy his servants, shipmen that had knoledge of the sea, ith the servants of Solomon.
And they came to Ophir, and fetched from thence gold, four hundred and tenty talents, and brought it to king Solomon.
And hen the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of Jehovah, she came to prove him ith hard questions.

And she came to Jerusalem ith a very great train, ith camels that bare spices, and very much gold, and precious stones; and hen she as come to Solomon, she communed ith him of all that as in her heart.
And Solomon told her all her questions: there as not anything hid from the king hich he told her not.
And hen the queen of Sheba had seen all the isdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,

and the food of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel, and his cupbearers, and his ascent by hich he ent up unto the house of Jehovah; there as no more spirit in her.
And she said to the king, It as a true report that I heard in mine on land of thine acts, and of thy isdom.
Hobeit I believed not the ords, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the half as not told me; thy isdom and prosperity exceed the fame hich I heard.
Happy are thy men, happy are these thy servants, that stand continually before thee, \add and\add* that hear thy isdom.
Blessed be Jehovah thy God, ho delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because Jehovah loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king, to do justice and righteousness.

And she gave the king a hundred and tenty talents of gold, and of spices very great store, and precious stones: there came no more such abundance of spices as these hich the queen of Sheba gave to king Solomon.
And the navy also of Hiram, that brought gold from Ophir, brought in from Ophir great plenty of almug-trees and precious stones.

And the king made of the almug-trees pillars for the house of Jehovah, and for the king’s house, harps also and psalteries for the singers: there came no such almug-trees, nor ere seen, unto this day.
And king Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, hatsoever she asked, besides that hich Solomon gave her of his royal bounty. So she turned, and ent to her on land, she and her servants.
No the eight of gold that came to Solomon in one year as six hundred threescore and six talents of gold,
besides \add that hich\add* the traders \add brought\add*, and the traffic of the merchants, and of all the kings of the mingled people, and of the governors of the country.
And king Solomon made to hundred bucklers of beaten gold; six hundred \add shekels\add* of gold ent to one buckler.
And \add he made\add* three hundred shields of beaten gold; three pounds of gold ent to one shield: and the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it ith the finest gold.
There ere six steps to the throne, and the top of the throne as round behind; and there ere stays on either side by the place of the seat, and to lions standing beside the stays.
And telve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps: there as not the like made in any kingdom.
And all king Solomon’s drinking vessels ere of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon ere of pure gold: none ere of silver; it as nothing accounted of in the days of Solomon.
For the king had at sea a navy of Tarshish ith the navy of Hiram: once every three years came the navy of Tarshish, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and in isdom.
And all the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his isdom, hich God had put in his heart.
And they brought every man his tribute, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and raiment, and armor, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year.

And Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand and four hundred chariots, and telve thousand horsemen, that he bestoed in the chariot cities, and ith the king at Jerusalem.
And the king made silver to be in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars made he to be as the sycomore-trees that are in the loland, for abundance.
And the horses hich Solomon had ere brought out of Egypt; and the king’s merchants received them in droves, each drove at a price.

And a chariot came up and ent out of Egypt for six hundred \add shekels\add* of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty; and so for all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, did they bring them out by their means.
No king Solomon loved many foreign omen, together ith the daughter of Pharaoh, omen of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites;

of the nations concerning hich Jehovah said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go among them, neither shall they come among you; for surely they ill turn aay your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.
And he had seven hundred ives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; and his ives turned aay his heart.
For it came to pass, hen Solomon as old, that his ives turned aay his heart after other gods; and his heart as not perfect ith Jehovah his God, as as the heart of David his father.
For Solomon ent after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
And Solomon did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, and ent not fully after Jehovah, as did David his father.
Then did Solomon build a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, in the mount that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech the abomination of the children of Ammon.
And so did he for all his foreign ives, ho burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.
And Jehovah as angry ith Solomon, because his heart as turned aay from Jehovah, the God of Israel, ho had appeared unto him tice,
and had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods: but he kept not that hich Jehovah commanded.

Wherefore Jehovah said unto Solomon, Forasmuch as this is done of thee, and thou hast not kept my covenant and my statutes, hich I have commanded thee, I ill surely rend the kingdom from thee, and ill give it to thy servant.
Notithstanding in thy days I ill not do it, for David thy father’s sake: but I ill rend it out of the hand of thy son.
Hobeit I ill not rend aay all the kingdom; but I ill give one tribe to thy son, for David my servant’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake hich I have chosen.
And Jehovah raised up an adversary unto Solomon, Hadad the Edomite: he as of the king’s seed in Edom.
For it came to pass, hen David as in Edom, and Joab the captain of the host as gone up to bury the slain, and had smitten every male in Edom
( for Joab and all Israel remained there six months, until he had cut off every male in Edom);
that Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites of his father’s servants ith him, to go into Egypt, Hadad being yet a little child.

And they arose out of Midian, and came to Paran; and they took men ith them out of Paran, and they came to Egypt, unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, ho gave him a house, and appointed him victuals, and gave him land.
And Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him to ife the sister of his on ife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
And the sister of Tahpenes bare him Genubath his son, hom Tahpenes eaned in Pharaoh’s house; and Genubath as in Pharaoh’s house among the sons of Pharaoh.
And hen Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept ith his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the host as dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, Let me depart, that I may go to mine on country.
Then Pharaoh said unto him, But hat hast thou lacked ith me, that, behold, thou seekest to go to thine on country? And he ansered, Nothing: hobeit only let me depart.
And God raised up \add another\add* adversary unto him, Rezon the son of Eliada, ho had fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah.
And he gathered men unto him, and became captain over a troop, hen David sle them \add of Zobah\add*: and they ent to Damascus, and delt therein, and reigned in Damascus.
And he as an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, besides the mischief that Hadad \add did\add*: and he abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria.
And Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, a servant of Solomon, hose mother’s name as Zeruah, a ido, he also lifted up his hand against the king.
And this as the reason hy he lifted up his hand against the king: Solomon built Millo, and repaired the breach of the city of David his father.
And the man Jeroboam as a mighty man of valor; and Solomon sa the young man that he as industrious, and he gave him charge over all the labor of the house of Joseph.

And it came to pass at that time, hen Jeroboam ent out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the ay; no \add Ahijah\add* had clad himself ith a ne garment; and they to ere alone in the field.
And Ahijah laid hold of the ne garment that as on him, and rent it in telve pieces.
And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces; for thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, Behold, I ill rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and ill give ten tribes to thee
( but he shall have one tribe, for my servant David’s sake and for Jerusalem’s sake, the city hich I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel);

because that they have forsaken me, and have orshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon; and they have not alked in my ays, to do that hich is right in mine eyes, and \add to keep\add* my statutes and mine ordinances, as did David his father.
Hobeit I ill not take the hole kingdom out of his hand; but I ill make him prince all the days of his life, for David my servant’s sake hom I chose, ho kept my commandments and my statutes;
but I ill take the kingdom out of his son’s hand, and ill give it unto thee, even ten tribes.
And unto his son ill I give one tribe, that David my servant may have a lamp alay before me in Jerusalem, the city hich I have chosen me to put my name there.
And I ill take thee, and thou shalt reign according to all that thy soul desireth, and shalt be king over Israel.

And it shall be, if thou ilt hearken unto all that I command thee, and ilt alk in my ays, and do that hich is right in mine eyes, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I ill be ith thee, and ill build thee a sure house, as I built for David, and ill give Israel unto thee.
And I ill for this afflict the seed of David, but not for ever.
Solomon sought therefore to kill Jeroboam; but Jeroboam arose, and fled into Egypt, unto Shishak king of Egypt, and as in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
No the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his isdom, are they not ritten in the book of the acts of Solomon?
And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel as forty years.
And Solomon slept ith his fathers, and as buried in the city of David his father: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.
And Rehoboam ent to Shechem: for all Israel ere come to Shechem to make him king.
And it came to pass, hen Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it ( for he as yet in Egypt, hither he had fled from the presence of king Solomon, and Jeroboam delt in Egypt,
and they sent and called him), that Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel came, and spake unto Rehoboam, saying,
Thy father made our yoke grievous: no therefore make thou the grievous service of thy father, and his heavy yoke hich he put upon us, lighter, and e ill serve thee.
And he said unto them, Depart yet for three days, then come again to me. And the people departed.
And king Rehoboam took counsel ith the old men, that had stood before Solomon his father hile he yet lived, saying, What counsel give ye me to return anser to this people?
And they spake unto him, saying, If thou ilt be a servant unto this people this day, and ilt serve them, and anser them, and speak good ords to them, then they ill be thy servants for ever.
But he forsook the counsel of the old men hich they had given him, and took counsel ith the young men that ere gron up ith him, that stood before him.
And he said unto them, What counsel give ye, that e may return anser to this people, ho have spoken to me, saying, Make the yoke that thy father did put upon us lighter?

And the young men that ere gron up ith him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou say unto this people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it lighter unto us; thus shalt thou speak unto them, My little finger is thicker than my father’s loins.
And no hereas my father did lade you ith a heavy yoke, I ill add to your yoke: my father chastised you ith hips, but I ill chastise you ith scorpions.
So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king bade, saying, Come to me again the third day.
And the king ansered the people roughly, and forsook the counsel of the old men hich they had given him,
and spake to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, but I ill add to your yoke: my father chastised you ith hips, but I ill chastise you ith scorpions.
So the king hearkened not unto the people; for it as a thing brought about of Jehovah, that he might establish his ord, hich Jehovah spake by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

And hen all Israel sa that the king hearkened not unto them, the people ansered the king, saying, What portion have e in David? neither have e inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: no see to thine on house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.
But as for the children of Israel that delt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
Then king Rehoboam sent Adoram, ho as over the men subject to taskork; and all Israel stoned him to death ith stones. And king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

And it came to pass, hen all Israel heard that Jeroboam as returned, that they sent and called him unto the congregation, and made him king over all Israel: there as none that folloed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.

And hen Rehoboam as come to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah, and the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, that ere arriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
But the ord of God came unto Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
Speak unto Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and unto all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people, saying,

Thus saith Jehovah, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is of me. So they hearkened unto the ord of Jehovah, and returned and ent their ay, according to the ord of Jehovah.
Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill-country of Ephraim, and delt therein; and he ent out from thence, and built Penuel.
And Jeroboam said in his heart, No ill the kingdom return to the house of David:

if this people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of Jehovah at Jerusalem, then ill the heart of this people turn again unto their lord, even unto Rehoboam king of Judah; and they ill kill me, and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.

Whereupon the king took counsel, and made to calves of gold; and he said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, hich brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
And he set the one in Beth-el, and the other put he in Dan.
And this thing became a sin; for the people ent \add to orship\add* before the one, even unto Dan.
And he made houses of high places, and made priests from among all the people, that ere not of the sons of Levi.

And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that is in Judah, and he ent up unto the altar; so did he in Beth-el, sacrificing unto the calves that he had made: and he placed in Beth-el the priests of the high places that he had made.

And he ent up unto the altar hich he had made in Beth-el on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, even in the month hich he had devised of his on heart: and he ordained a feast for the children of Israel, and ent up unto the altar, to burn incense.
And, behold, there came a man of God out of Judah by the ord of Jehovah unto Beth-el: and Jeroboam as standing by the altar to burn incense.

And he cried against the altar by the ord of Jehovah, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith Jehovah: Behold, a son shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he sacrifice the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men’s bones shall they burn upon thee.
And he gave a sign the same day, saying, This is the sign hich Jehovah hath spoken: Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that are upon it shall be poured out.

And it came to pass, hen the king heard the saying of the man of God, hich he cried against the altar in Beth-el, that Jeroboam put forth his hand from the altar, saying, Lay hold on him. And his hand, hich he put forth against him, dried up, so that he could not dra it back again to him.
The altar also as rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign hich the man of God had given by the ord of Jehovah.

And the king ansered and said unto the man of God, Entreat no the favor of Jehovah thy God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored me again. And the man of God entreated Jehovah, and the king’s hand as restored him again, and became as it as before.
And the king said unto the man of God, Come home ith me, and refresh thyself, and I ill give thee a reard.
And the man of God said unto the king, If thou ilt give me half thy house, I ill not go in ith thee, neither ill I eat bread nor drink ater in this place;
for so as it charged me by the ord of Jehovah, saying, Thou shalt eat no bread, nor drink ater, neither return by the ay that thou camest.
So he ent another ay, and returned not by the ay that he came to Beth-el.

No there delt an old prophet in Beth-el; and one of his sons came and told him all the orks that the man of God had done that day in Beth-el: the ords hich he had spoken unto the king, them also they told unto their father.
And their father said unto them, What ay ent he? No his sons had seen hat ay the man of God ent, that came from Judah.
And he said unto his sons, Saddle me the ass. So they saddled him the ass; and he rode thereon.
And he ent after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak; and he said unto him, Art thou the man of God that camest from Judah? And he said, I am.
Then he said unto him, Come home ith me, and eat bread.
And he said, I may not return ith thee, nor go in ith thee; neither ill I eat bread nor drink ater ith thee in this place:
for it as said to me by the ord of Jehovah, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink ater there, nor turn again to go by the ay that thou camest.

And he said unto him, I also am a prophet as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the ord of Jehovah, saying, Bring him back ith thee into thy house, that he may eat bread and drink ater. \add But\add* he lied unto him.
So he ent back ith him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank ater.
And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the ord of Jehovah came unto the prophet that brought him back;

and he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith Jehovah, Forasmuch as thou hast been disobedient unto the mouth of Jehovah, and hast not kept the commandment hich Jehovah thy God commanded thee,
but camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk ater in the place of hich he said to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no ater; thy body shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.
And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled for him the ass, \add to it\add*, for the prophet hom he had brought back.
And hen he as gone, a lion met him by the ay, and sle him: and his body as cast in the ay, and the ass stood by it; the lion also stood by the body.
And, behold, men passed by, and sa the body cast in the ay, and the lion standing by the body; and they came and told it in the city here the old prophet delt.

And hen the prophet that brought him back from the ay heard thereof, he said, It is the man of God, ho as disobedient unto the mouth of Jehovah: therefore Jehovah hath delivered him unto the lion, hich hath torn him, and slain him, according to the ord of Jehovah, hich he spake unto him.
And he spake to his sons, saying, Saddle me the ass. And they saddled it.
And he ent and found his body cast in the ay, and the ass and the lion standing by the body: the lion had not eaten the body, nor torn the ass.
And the prophet took up the body of the man of God, and laid it upon the ass, and brought it back; and he came to the city of the old prophet, to mourn, and to bury him.
And he laid his body in his on grave; and they mourned over him, \add saying\add*, Alas, my brother!
And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spake to his sons, saying, When I am dead, then bury me in the sepulchre herein the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.
For the saying hich he cried by the ord of Jehovah against the altar in Beth-el, and against all the houses of the high places hich are in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass.

After this thing Jeroboam returned not from his evil ay, but made again from among all the people priests of the high places: hosoever ould, he consecrated him, that there might be priests of the high places.
And this thing became sin unto the house of Jeroboam, even to cut it off, and to destroy it from off the face of the earth.
At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.

And Jeroboam said to his ife, Arise, I pray thee, and disguise thyself, that thou be not knon to be the ife of Jeroboam; and get thee to Shiloh: behold, there is Ahijah the prophet, ho spake concerning me that I should be king over this people.
And take ith thee ten loaves, and cakes, and a cruse of honey, and go to him: he ill tell thee hat shall become of the child.
And Jeroboam’s ife did so, and arose, and ent to Shiloh, and came to the house of Ahijah. No Ahijah could not see; for his eyes ere set by reason of his age.

And Jehovah said unto Ahijah, Behold, the ife of Jeroboam cometh to inquire of thee concerning her son; for he is sick: thus and thus shalt thou say unto her; for it ill be, hen she cometh in, that she ill feign herself to be another oman.

And it as so, hen Ahijah heard the sound of her feet, as she came in at the door, that he said, Come in, thou ife of Jeroboam; hy feignest thou thyself to be another? for I am sent to thee ith heavy tidings.
Go, tell Jeroboam, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel: Forasmuch as I exalted thee from among the people, and made thee prince over my people Israel,

and rent the kingdom aay from the house of David, and gave it thee; and yet thou hast not been as my servant David, ho kept my commandments, and ho folloed me ith all his heart, to do that only hich as right in mine eyes,
but hast done evil above all that ere before thee, and hast gone and made thee other gods, and molten images, to provoke me to anger, and hast cast me behind thy back:

therefore, behold, I ill bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and ill cut off from Jeroboam every man-child, him that is shut up and him that is left at large in Israel, and ill utterly seep aay the house of Jeroboam, as a man seepeth aay dung, till it be all gone.
Him that dieth of Jeroboam in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the birds of the heavens eat: for Jehovah hath spoken it.
Arise thou therefore, get thee to thy house: \add and\add* hen thy feet enter into the city, the child shall die.

And all Israel shall mourn for him, and bury him; for he only of Jeroboam shall come to the grave, because in him there is found some good thing toard Jehovah, the God of Israel, in the house of Jeroboam.
Moreover Jehovah ill raise him up a king over Israel, ho shall cut off the house of Jeroboam that day: but hat? even no.

For Jehovah ill smite Israel, as a reed is shaken in the ater; and he ill root up Israel out of this good land hich he gave to their fathers, and ill scatter them beyond the River, because they have made their Asherim, provoking Jehovah to anger.
And he ill give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, hich he hath sinned, and hereith he hath made Israel to sin.
And Jeroboam’s ife arose, and departed, and came to Tirzah: \add and\add* as she came to the threshold of the house, the child died.
And all Israel buried him, and mourned for him, according to the ord of Jehovah, hich he spake by his servant Ahijah the prophet.
And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, ho he arred, and ho he reigned, behold, they are ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
And the days hich Jeroboam reigned ere to and tenty years: and he slept ith his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his stead.

And Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam as forty and one years old hen he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city hich Jehovah had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there: and his mother’s name as Naamah the Ammonitess.
And Judah did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, and they provoked him to jealousy ith their sins hich they committed, above all that their fathers had done.
For they also built them high places, and pillars, and Asherim, on every high hill, and under every green tree;
and there ere also sodomites in the land: they did according to all the abominations of the nations hich Jehovah drove out before the children of Israel.
And it came to pass in the fifth year of king Rehoboam, that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem;
and he took aay the treasures of the house of Jehovah, and the treasures of the king’s house; he even took aay all: and he took aay all the shields of gold hich Solomon had made.
And king Rehoboam made in their stead shields of brass, and committed them to the hands of the captains of the guard, ho kept the door of the king’s house.
And it as so, that, as oft as the king ent into the house of Jehovah, the guard bare them, and brought them back into the guard-chamber.
No the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And there as ar beteen Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
And Rehoboam slept ith his fathers, and as buried ith his fathers in the city of David: and his mother’s name as Naamah the Ammonitess. And Abijam his son reigned in his stead.
No in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam the son of Nebat began Abijam to reign over Judah.
Three years reigned he in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name as Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
And he alked in all the sins of his father, hich he had done before him; and his heart as not perfect ith Jehovah his God, as the heart of David his father.
Nevertheless for David’s sake did Jehovah his God give him a lamp in Jerusalem, to set up his son after him, and to establish Jerusalem;
because David did that hich as right in the eyes of Jehovah, and turned not aside from anything that he commanded him all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
No there as ar beteen Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.
And the rest of the acts of Abijam, and all that he did, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And there as ar beteen Abijam and Jeroboam.
And Abijam slept ith his fathers; and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead.
And in the tentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel began Asa to reign over Judah.
And forty and one years reigned he in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name as Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
And Asa did that hich as right in the eyes of Jehovah, as did David his father.
And he put aay the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.
And also Maacah his mother he removed from being queen, because she had made an abominable image for an Asherah; and Asa cut don her image, and burnt it at the brook Kidron.
But the high places ere not taken aay: nevertheless the heart of Asa as perfect ith Jehovah all his days.
And he brought into the house of Jehovah the things that his father had dedicated, and the things that himself had dedicated, silver, and gold, and vessels.
And there as ar beteen Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
And Baasha king of Israel ent up against Judah, and built Ramah, that he might not suffer any one to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

Then Asa took all the silver and the gold that ere left in the treasures of the house of Jehovah, and the treasures of the king’s house, and delivered them into the hand of his servants; and king Asa sent them to Ben-hadad, the son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, that delt at Damascus, saying,

\add There is\add* a league beteen me and thee, beteen my father and thy father: behold, I have sent unto thee a present of silver and gold; go, break thy league ith Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.

And Ben-hadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel, and smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-beth-maacah, and all Chinneroth, ith all the land of Naphtali.
And it came to pass, hen Baasha heard thereof, that he left off building Ramah, and delt in Tirzah.

Then king Asa made a proclamation unto all Judah; none as exempted: and they carried aay the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, hereith Baasha had builded; and king Asa built thereith Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah.

No the rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities hich he built, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? But in the time of his old age he as diseased in his feet.
And Asa slept ith his fathers, and as buried ith his fathers in the city of David his father; and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead.
And Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah; and he reigned over Israel to years.
And he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, and alked in the ay of his father, and in his sin hereith he made Israel to sin.

And Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha smote him at Gibbethon, hich belonged to the Philistines; for Nadab and all Israel ere laying siege to Gibbethon.
Even in the third year of Asa king of Judah did Baasha slay him, and reigned in his stead.

And it came to pass that, as soon as he as king, he smote all the house of Jeroboam: he left not to Jeroboam any that breathed, until he had destroyed him; according unto the saying of Jehovah, hich he spake by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite;
for the sins of Jeroboam hich he sinned, and hereith he made Israel to sin, because of his provocation hereith he provoked Jehovah, the God of Israel, to anger.
No the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And there as ar beteen Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
In the third year of Asa king of Judah began Baasha the son of Ahijah to reign over all Israel in Tirzah, \add and reigned\add* tenty and four years.
And he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, and alked in the ay of Jeroboam, and in his sin hereith he made Israel to sin.
And the ord of Jehovah came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,

Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust, and made thee prince over my people Israel, and thou hast alked in the ay of Jeroboam, and hast made my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger ith their sins;
behold, I ill utterly seep aay Baasha and his house; and I ill make thy house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
Him that dieth of Baasha in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth of his in the field shall the birds of the heavens eat.
No the rest of the acts of Baasha, and hat he did, and his might, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Baasha slept ith his fathers, and as buried in Tirzah; and Elah his son reigned in his stead.

And moreover by the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani came the ord of Jehovah against Baasha, and against his house, both because of all the evil that he did in the sight of Jehovah, to provoke him to anger ith the ork of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam, and because he smote him.
In the tenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, \add and reigned\add* to years.
And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him. No he as in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, ho as over the household in Tirzah:
and Zimri ent in and smote him, and killed him, in the tenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.
And it came to pass, hen he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he smote all the house of Baasha: he left him not a single man-child, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.
Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the ord of Jehovah, hich he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,
for all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, hich they sinned, and hereith they made Israel to sin, to provoke Jehovah, the God of Israel, to anger ith their vanities.
No the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
In the tenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah did Zimri reign seven days in Tirzah. No the people ere encamped against Gibbethon, hich belonged to the Philistines.
And the people that ere encamped heard say, Zimri hath conspired, and hath also smitten the king: herefore all Israel made Omri, the captain of the host, king over Israel that day in the camp.
And Omri ent up from Gibbethon, and all Israel ith him, and they besieged Tirzah.
And it came to pass, hen Zimri sa that the city as taken, that he ent into the castle of the king’s house, and burnt the king’s house over him ith fire, and died,
for his sins hich he sinned in doing that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, in alking in the ay of Jeroboam, and in his sin hich he did, to make Israel to sin.
No the rest of the acts of Zimri, and his treason that he rought, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Then ere the people of Israel divided into to parts: half of the people folloed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king; and half folloed Omri.
But the people that folloed Omri prevailed against the people that folloed Tibni the son of Ginath: so Tibni died, and Omri reigned.
In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah began Omri to reign over Israel, \add and reigned\add* telve years: six years reigned he in Tirzah.
And he bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for to talents of silver; and he built on the hill, and called the name of the city hich he built, after the name of Shemer, the oner of the hill, Samaria.
And Omri did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, and dealt ickedly above all that ere before him.
For he alked in all the ay of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and in his sins hereith he made Israel to sin, to provoke Jehovah, the God of Israel, to anger ith their vanities.
No the rest of the acts of Omri hich he did, and his might that he shoed, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
So Omri slept ith his fathers, and as buried in Samaria; and Ahab his son reigned in his stead.
And in the thirty and eighth year of Asa king of Judah began Ahab the son of Omri to reign over Israel: and Ahab the son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria tenty and to years.
And Ahab the son of Omri did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah above all that ere before him.

And it came to pass, as if it had been a light thing for him to alk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, that he took to ife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and ent and served Baal, and orshipped him.
And he reared up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, hich he had built in Samaria.
And Ahab made the Asherah; and Ahab did yet more to provoke Jehovah, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel that ere before him.

In his days did Hiel the Beth-elite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof ith the loss of Abiram his first-born, and set up the gates thereof ith the loss of his youngest son Segub, according to the ord of Jehovah, hich he spake by Joshua the son of Nun.

And Elijah the Tishbite, ho as of the sojourners of Gilead, said unto Ahab, As Jehovah, the God of Israel, liveth, before hom I stand, there shall not be de nor rain these years, but according to my ord.
And the ord of Jehovah came unto him, saying,
Get thee hence, and turn thee eastard, and hide thyself by the brook Cherith, that is before the Jordan.
And it shall be, that thou shalt drink of the brook; and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.
So he ent and did according unto the ord of Jehovah; for he ent and delt by the brook Cherith, that is before the Jordan.
And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.
And it came to pass after a hile, that the brook dried up, because there as no rain in the land.
And the ord of Jehovah came unto him, saying,
Arise, get thee to Zarephath, hich belongeth to Sidon, and dell there: behold, I have commanded a ido there to sustain thee.

So he arose and ent to Zarephath; and hen he came to the gate of the city, behold, a ido as there gathering sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little ater in a vessel, that I may drink.
And as she as going to fetch it, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thy hand.

And she said, As Jehovah thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but a handful of meal in the jar, and a little oil in the cruse: and, behold, I am gathering to sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that e may eat it, and die.
And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said; but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it forth unto me, and afterard make for thee and for thy son.
For thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, The jar of meal shall not aste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that Jehovah sendeth rain upon the earth.
And she ent and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat \add many\add* days.
The jar of meal asted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the ord of Jehovah, hich he spake by Elijah.
And it came to pass after these things, that the son of the oman, the mistress of the house, fell sick; and his sickness as so sore, that there as no breath left in him.
And she said unto Elijah, What have I to do ith thee, O thou man of God? thou art come unto me to bring my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son!
And he said unto her, Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into the chamber, here he abode, and laid him upon his on bed.
And he cried unto Jehovah, and said, O Jehovah my God, hast thou also brought evil upon the ido ith hom I sojourn, by slaying her son?
And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto Jehovah, and said, O Jehovah my God, I pray thee, let this child’s soul come into him again.
And Jehovah hearkened unto the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
And Elijah took the child, and brought him don out of the chamber into the house, and delivered him unto his mother; and Elijah said, See, thy son liveth.
And the oman said to Elijah, No I kno that thou art a man of God, and that the ord of Jehovah in thy mouth is truth.
And it came to pass after many days, that the ord of Jehovah came to Elijah, in the third year, saying, Go, sho thyself unto Ahab; and I ill send rain upon the earth.
And Elijah ent to sho himself unto Ahab. And the famine as sore in Samaria.
And Ahab called Obadiah, ho as over the household. ( No Obadiah feared Jehovah greatly:
for it as so, hen Jezebel cut off the prophets of Jehovah, that Obadiah took a hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them ith bread and ater.)

And Ahab said unto Obadiah, Go through the land, unto all the fountains of ater, and unto all the brooks: peradventure e may find grass and save the horses and mules alive, that e lose not all the beasts.
So they divided the land beteen them to pass throughout it: Ahab ent one ay by himself, and Obadiah ent another ay by himself.
And as Obadiah as in the ay, behold, Elijah met him: and he kne him, and fell on his face, and said, Is it thou, my lord Elijah?
And he ansered him, It is I: go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah \add is here\add*.
And he said, Wherein have I sinned, that thou ouldest deliver thy servant into the hand of Ahab, to slay me?

As Jehovah thy God liveth, there is no nation or kingdom, hither my lord hath not sent to seek thee: and hen they said, He is not here, he took an oath of the kingdom and nation, that they found thee not.
And no thou sayest, Go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah \add is here\add*.

And it ill come to pass, as soon as I am gone from thee, that the Spirit of Jehovah ill carry thee hither I kno not; and so hen I come and tell Ahab, and he cannot find thee, he ill slay me: but I thy servant fear Jehovah from my youth.
Was it not told my lord hat I did hen Jezebel sle the prophets of Jehovah, ho I hid a hundred men of Jehovah’s prophets by fifty in a cave, and fed them ith bread and ater?
And no thou sayest, Go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah \add is here\add*; and he ill slay me.
And Elijah said, As Jehovah of hosts liveth, before hom I stand, I ill surely sho myself unto him to-day.
So Obadiah ent to meet Ahab, and told him; and Ahab ent to meet Elijah.
And it came to pass, hen Ahab sa Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Is it thou, thou troubler of Israel?
And he ansered, I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father’s house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of Jehovah, and thou hast folloed the Baalim.
No therefore send, and gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the Asherah four hundred, that eat at Jezebel’s table.
So Ahab sent unto all the children of Israel, and gathered the prophets together unto mount Carmel.
And Elijah came near unto all the people, and said, Ho long go ye limping beteen the to sides? if Jehovah be God, follo him; but if Baal, then follo him. And the people ansered him not a ord.
Then said Elijah unto the people, I, even I only, am left a prophet of Jehovah; but Baal’s prophets are four hundred and fifty men.

Let them therefore give us to bullocks; and let them choose one bullock for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay it on the ood, and put no fire under; and I ill dress the other bullock, and lay it on the ood, and put no fire under.
And call ye on the name of your god, and I ill call on the name of Jehovah; and the God that ansereth by fire, let him be God. And all the people ansered and said, It is ell spoken.
And Elijah said unto the prophets of Baal, Choose you one bullock for yourselves, and dress it first; for ye are many; and call on the name of your god, but put no fire under.

And they took the bullock hich as given them, and they dressed it, and called on the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us. But there as no voice, nor any that ansered. And they leaped about the altar hich as made.

And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud; for he is a god: either he is musing, or he is gone aside, or he is on a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth and must be aaked.
And they cried aloud, and cut themselves after their manner ith knives and lances, till the blood gushed out upon them.
And it as so, hen midday as past, that they prophesied until the time of the offering of the \add evening\add* oblation; but there as neither voice, nor any to anser, nor any that regarded.
And Elijah said unto all the people, Come near unto me; and all the people came near unto him. And he repaired the altar of Jehovah that as thron don.
And Elijah took telve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, unto hom the ord of Jehovah came, saying, Israel shall be thy name.
And ith the stones he built an altar in the name of Jehovah; and he made a trench about the altar, as great as ould contain to measures of seed.
And he put the ood in order, and cut the bullock in pieces, and laid it on the ood. And he said, Fill four jars ith ater, and pour it on the burnt-offering, and on the ood.
And he said, Do it the second time; and they did it the second time. And he said, Do it the third time; and they did it the third time.
And the ater ran round about the altar; and he filled the trench also ith ater.
