And it came to pass at the time of the offering of the \add evening\add* oblation, that Elijah the prophet came near, and said, O Jehovah, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, let it be knon this day that thou art God in Israel, and that I am thy servant, and that I have done all these things at thy ord.
Hear me, O Jehovah, hear me, that this people may kno that thou, Jehovah, art God, and \add that\add* thou hast turned their heart back again.
Then the fire of Jehovah fell, and consumed the burnt-offering, and the ood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the ater that as in the trench.
And hen all the people sa it, they fell on their faces: and they said, Jehovah, he is God; Jehovah, he is God.
And Elijah said unto them, Take the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape. And they took them; and Elijah brought them don to the brook Kishon, and sle them there.
And Elijah said unto Ahab, Get thee up, eat and drink; for there is the sound of abundance of rain.
So Ahab ent up to eat and to drink. And Elijah ent up to the top of Carmel; and he boed himself don upon the earth, and put his face beteen his knees.
And he said to his servant, Go up no, look toard the sea. And he ent up, and looked, and said, There is nothing. And he said, Go again seven times.

And it came to pass at the seventh time, that he said, Behold, there ariseth a cloud out of the sea, as small as a man’s hand. And he said, Go up, say unto Ahab, Make ready \add thy chariot\add*, and get thee don, that the rain stop thee not.
And it came to pass in a little hile, that the heavens gre black ith clouds and ind, and there as a great rain. And Ahab rode, and ent to Jezreel:
and the hand of Jehovah as on Elijah; and he girded up his loins, and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.
And Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and ithal ho he had slain all the prophets ith the sord.
Then Jezebel sent a messenger unto Elijah, saying, So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I make not thy life as the life of one of them by to-morro about this time.
And hen he sa that, he arose, and ent for his life, and came to Beer-sheba, hich belongeth to Judah, and left his servant there.

But he himself ent a day’s journey into the ilderness, and came and sat don under a juniper-tree: and he requested for himself that he might die, and said, It is enough; no, O Jehovah, take aay my life; for I am not better than my fathers.
And he lay don and slept under a juniper-tree; and, behold, an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat.
And he looked, and, behold, there as at his head a cake baken on the coals, and a cruse of ater. And he did eat and drink, and laid him don again.
And the angel of Jehovah came again the second time, and touched him, and said, Arise and eat, because the journey is too great for thee.
And he arose, and did eat and drink, and ent in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights unto Horeb the mount of God.
And he came thither unto a cave, and lodged there; and, behold, the ord of Jehovah came to him, and he said unto him, What doest thou here, Elijah?

And he said, I have been very jealous for Jehovah, the God of hosts; for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thron don thine altars, and slain thy prophets ith the sord: and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it aay.

And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before Jehovah. And, behold, Jehovah passed by, and a great and strong ind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before Jehovah; but Jehovah as not in the ind: and after the ind an earthquake; but Jehovah as not in the earthquake:
and after the earthquake a fire; but Jehovah as not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.

And it as so, hen Elijah heard it, that he rapped his face in his mantle, and ent out, and stood in the entrance of the cave. And, behold, there came a voice unto him, and said, What doest thou here, Elijah?

And he said, I have been very jealous for Jehovah, the God of hosts; for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thron don thine altars, and slain thy prophets ith the sord; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it aay.
And Jehovah said unto him, Go, return on thy ay to the ilderness of Damascus: and hen thou comest, thou shalt anoint Hazael to be king over Syria;
and Jehu the son of Nimshi shalt thou anoint to be king over Israel; and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah shalt thou anoint to be prophet in thy room.
And it shall come to pass, that him that escapeth from the sord of Hazael shall Jehu slay; and him that escapeth from the sord of Jehu shall Elisha slay.
Yet ill I leave \add me\add* seven thousand in Israel, all the knees hich have not boed unto Baal, and every mouth hich hath not kissed him.

So he departed thence, and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, ho as ploing, ith telve yoke \add of oxen\add* before him, and he ith the telfth: and Elijah passed over unto him, and cast his mantle upon him.
And he left the oxen, and ran after Elijah, and said, Let me, I pray thee, kiss my father and my mother, and then I ill follo thee. And he said unto him, Go back again; for hat have I done to thee?

And he returned from folloing him, and took the yoke of oxen, and sle them, and boiled their flesh ith the instruments of the oxen, and gave unto the people, and they did eat. Then he arose, and ent after Elijah, and ministered unto him.
And Ben-hadad the king of Syria gathered all his host together; and there ere thirty and to kings ith him, and horses and chariots: and he ent up and besieged Samaria, and fought against it.
And he sent messengers to Ahab king of Israel, into the city, and said unto him, Thus saith Ben-hadad,
Thy silver and thy gold is mine; thy ives also and thy children, even the goodliest, are mine.
And the king of Israel ansered and said, It is according to thy saying, my lord, O king; I am thine, and all that I have.
And the messengers came again, and said, Thus speaketh Ben-hadad, saying, I sent indeed unto thee, saying, Thou shalt deliver me thy silver, and thy gold, and thy ives, and thy children;

but I ill send my servants unto thee to-morro about this time, and they shall search thy house, and the houses of thy servants; and it shall be, that hatsoever is pleasant in thine eyes, they shall put it in their hand, and take it aay.

Then the king of Israel called all the elders of the land, and said, Mark, I pray you, and see ho this man seeketh mischief: for he sent unto me for my ives, and for my children, and for my silver, and for my gold; and I denied him not.
And all the elders and all the people said unto him, Hearken thou not, neither consent.

Wherefore he said unto the messengers of Ben-hadad, Tell my lord the king, All that thou didst send for to thy servant at the first I ill do; but this thing I may not do. And the messengers departed, and brought him ord again.
And Ben-hadad sent unto him, and said, The gods do so unto me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for handfuls for all the people that follo me.
And the king of Israel ansered and said, Tell him, Let not him that girdeth on \add his armor\add* boast himself as he that putteth it off.

And it came to pass, hen \add Ben-hadad\add* heard this message, as he as drinking, he and the kings, in the pavilions, that he said unto his servants, Set \add yourselves in array\add*. And they set \add themselves in array\add* against the city.

And, behold, a prophet came near unto Ahab king of Israel, and said, Thus saith Jehovah, Hast thou seen all this great multitude? behold, I ill deliver it into thy hand this day; and thou shalt kno that I am Jehovah.
And Ahab said, By hom? And he said, Thus saith Jehovah, By the young men of the princes of the provinces. Then he said, Who shall begin the battle? And he ansered, Thou.

Then he mustered the young men of the princes of the provinces, and they ere to hundred and thirty-to: and after them he mustered all the people, even all the children of Israel, being seven thousand.
And they ent out at noon. But Ben-hadad as drinking himself drunk in the pavilions, he and the kings, the thirty and to kings that helped him.
And the young men of the princes of the provinces ent out first; and Ben-hadad sent out, and they told him, saying, There are men come out from Samaria.
And he said, Whether they are come out for peace, take them alive; or hether they are come out for ar, take them alive.
So these ent out of the city, the young men of the princes of the provinces, and the army hich folloed them.
And they sle every one his man; and the Syrians fled, and Israel pursued them: and Ben-hadad the king of Syria escaped on a horse ith horsemen.
And the king of Israel ent out, and smote the horses and chariots, and sle the Syrians ith a great slaughter.
And the prophet came near to the king of Israel, and said unto him, Go, strengthen thyself, and mark, and see hat thou doest; for at the return of the year the king of Syria ill come up against thee.

And the servants of the king of Syria said unto him, Their god is a god of the hills; therefore they ere stronger than e: but let us fight against them in the plain, and surely e shall be stronger than they.
And do this thing: take the kings aay, every man out of his place, and put captains in their room;

and number thee an army, like the army that thou hast lost, horse for horse, and chariot for chariot; and e ill fight against them in the plain, and surely e shall be stronger than they. And he hearkened unto their voice, and did so.
And it came to pass at the return of the year, that Ben-hadad mustered the Syrians, and ent up to Aphek, to fight against Israel.
And the children of Israel ere mustered, and ere victualled, and ent against them: and the children of Israel encamped before them like to little flocks of kids; but the Syrians filled the country.

And a man of God came near and spake unto the king of Israel, and said, Thus saith Jehovah, Because the Syrians have said, Jehovah is a god of the hills, but he is not a god of the valleys; therefore ill I deliver all this great multitude into thy hand, and ye shall kno that I am Jehovah.

And they encamped one over against the other seven days. And so it as, that in the seventh day the battle as joined; and the children of Israel sle of the Syrians a hundred thousand footmen in one day.
But the rest fled to Aphek, into the city; and the all fell upon tenty and seven thousand men that ere left. And Ben-hadad fled, and came into the city, into an inner chamber.

And his servants said unto him, Behold no, e have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful kings: let us, e pray thee, put sackcloth on our loins, and ropes upon our heads, and go out to the king of Israel: peradventure he ill save thy life.

So they girded sackcloth on their loins, and \add put\add* ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel, and said, Thy servant Ben-hadad saith, I pray thee, let me live. And he said, Is he yet alive? he is my brother.

No the men observed diligently, and hasted to catch hether it ere his mind; and they said, Thy brother Ben-hadad. Then he said, Go ye, bring him. Then Ben-hadad came forth to him; and he caused him to come up into the chariot.

And \add Ben-hadad\add* said unto him, The cities hich my father took from thy father I ill restore; and thou shalt make streets for thee in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria. And I, \add said Ahab\add*, ill let thee go ith this covenant. So he made a covenant ith him, and let him go.
And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said unto his fello by the ord of Jehovah, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man refused to smite him.

Then said he unto him, Because thou hast not obeyed the voice of Jehovah, behold, as soon as thou art departed from me, a lion shall slay thee. And as soon as he as departed from him, a lion found him, and sle him.
Then he found another man, and said, Smite me, I pray thee. And the man smote him, smiting and ounding him.
So the prophet departed, and aited for the king by the ay, and disguised himself ith his headband over his eyes.

And as the king passed by, he cried unto the king; and he said, Thy servant ent out into the midst of the battle; and, behold, a man turned aside, and brought a man unto me, and said, Keep this man: if by any means he be missing, then shall thy life be for his life, or else thou shalt pay a talent of silver.
And as thy servant as busy here and there, he as gone. And the king of Israel said unto him, So shall thy judgment be; thyself hast decided it.
And he hasted, and took the headband aay from his eyes; and the king of Israel discerned him that he as of the prophets.
And he said unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Because thou hast let go out of thy hand the man hom I had devoted to destruction, therefore thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people.
And the king of Israel ent to his house heavy and displeased, and came to Samaria.
And it came to pass after these things, that Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard, hich as in Jezreel, hard by the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

And Ahab spake unto Naboth, saying, Give me thy vineyard, that I may have it for a garden of herbs, because it is near unto my house; and I ill give thee for it a better vineyard than it: or, if it seem good to thee, I ill give thee the orth of it in money.
And Naboth said to Ahab, Jehovah forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.

And Ahab came into his house heavy and displeased because of the ord hich Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him; for he had said, I ill not give thee the inheritance of my fathers. And he laid him don upon his bed, and turned aay his face, and ould eat no bread.
But Jezebel his ife came to him, and said unto him, Why is thy spirit so sad, that thou eatest no bread?

And he said unto her, Because I spake unto Naboth the Jezreelite, and said unto him, Give me thy vineyard for money; or else, if it please thee, I ill give thee \add another\add* vineyard for it: and he ansered, I ill not give thee my vineyard.
And Jezebel his ife said unto him, Dost thou no govern the kingdom of Israel? arise, and eat bread, and let thy heart be merry: I ill give thee the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.
So she rote letters in Ahab’s name, and sealed them ith his seal, and sent the letters unto the elders and to the nobles that ere in his city, \add and\add* that delt ith Naboth.
And she rote in the letters, saying, Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people:
and set to men, base fellos, before him, and let them bear itness against him, saying, Thou didst curse God and the king. And then carry him out, and stone him to death.
And the men of his city, even the elders and the nobles ho delt in his city, did as Jezebel had sent unto them, according as it as ritten in the letters hich she had sent unto them.
They proclaimed a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people.

And the to men, the base fellos, came in and sat before him: and the base fellos bare itness against him, even against Naboth, in the presence of the people, saying, Naboth did curse God and the king. Then they carried him forth out of the city, and stoned him to death ith stones.
Then they sent to Jezebel, saying, Naboth is stoned, and is dead.

And it came to pass, hen Jezebel heard that Naboth as stoned, and as dead, that Jezebel said to Ahab, Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, hich he refused to give thee for money; for Naboth is not alive, but dead.
And it came to pass, hen Ahab heard that Naboth as dead, that Ahab rose up to go don to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.
And the ord of Jehovah came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
Arise, go don to meet Ahab king of Israel, ho delleth in Samaria: behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, hither he is gone don to take possession of it.

And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith Jehovah, Hast thou killed, and also taken possession? And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith Jehovah, In the place here dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.
And Ahab said to Elijah, Hast thou found me, O mine enemy? And he ansered, I have found thee, because thou hast sold thyself to do that hich is evil in the sight of Jehovah.
Behold, I ill bring evil upon thee, and ill utterly seep thee aay and ill cut off from Ahab every man-child, and him that is shut up and him that is left at large in Israel:

and I ill make thy house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah for the provocation hereith thou hast provoked me to anger, and hast made Israel to sin.
And of Jezebel also spake Jehovah, saying, The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the rampart of Jezreel.
Him that dieth of Ahab in the city the dogs shall eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the birds of the heavens eat.
( But there as none like unto Ahab, ho did sell himself to do that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, hom Jezebel his ife stirred up.
And he did very abominably in folloing idols, according to all that the Amorites did, hom Jehovah cast out before the children of Israel.)
And it came to pass, hen Ahab heard those ords, that he rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his flesh, and fasted, and lay in sackcloth, and ent softly.
And the ord of Jehovah came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
Seest thou ho Ahab humbleth himself before me? because he humbleth himself before me, I ill not bring the evil in his days; but in his son’s day ill I bring the evil upon his house.
And they continued three years ithout ar beteen Syria and Israel.
And it came to pass in the third year, that Jehoshaphat the king of Judah came don to the king of Israel.
And the king of Israel said unto his servants, Kno ye that Ramoth-gilead is ours, and e are still, and take it not out of the hand of the king of Syria?
And he said unto Jehoshaphat, Wilt thou go ith me to battle to Ramoth-gilead? And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, I am as thou art, my people as thy people, my horses as thy horses.
And Jehoshaphat said unto the king of Israel, Inquire first, I pray thee, for the ord of Jehovah.

Then the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, about four hundred men, and said unto them, Shall I go against Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I forbear? And they said, Go up; for the Lord ill deliver it into the hand of the king.
But Jehoshaphat said, Is there not here a prophet of Jehovah besides, that e may inquire of him?

And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, There is yet one man by hom e may inquire of Jehovah, Micaiah the son of Imlah: but I hate him; for he doth not prophesy good concerning me, but evil. And Jehoshaphat said, Let not the king say so.
Then the king of Israel called an officer, and said, Fetch quickly Micaiah the son of Imlah.

No the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah ere sitting each on his throne, arrayed in their robes, in an open place at the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets ere prophesying before them.
And Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made him horns of iron, and said, Thus saith Jehovah, With these shalt thou push the Syrians, until they be consumed.
And all the prophets prophesied so, saying, Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and prosper; for Jehovah ill deliver it into the hand of the king.

And the messenger that ent to call Micaiah spake unto him, saying, Behold no, the ords of the prophets \add declare\add* good unto the king ith one mouth: let thy ord, I pray thee, be like the ord of one of them, and speak thou good.
And Micaiah said, As Jehovah liveth, hat Jehovah saith unto me, that ill I speak.

And hen he as come to the king, the king said unto him, Micaiah, shall e go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall e forbear? And he ansered him, Go up and prosper; and Jehovah ill deliver it into the hand of the king.
And the king said unto him, Ho many times shall I adjure thee that thou speak unto me nothing but the truth in the name of Jehovah?
And he said, I sa all Israel scattered upon the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd: and Jehovah said, These have no master; let them return every man to his house in peace.
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell thee that he ould not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?
And \add Micaiah\add* said, Therefore hear thou the ord of Jehovah: I sa Jehovah sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.
And Jehovah said, Who shall entice Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead? And one said on this manner; and another said on that manner.
And there came forth a spirit, and stood before Jehovah, and said, I ill entice him.

And Jehovah said unto him, Whereith? And he said, I ill go forth, and ill be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt entice him, and shalt prevail also: go forth, and do so.
No therefore, behold, Jehovah hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets; and Jehovah hath spoken evil concerning thee.
Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah came near, and smote Micaiah on the cheek, and said, Which ay ent the Spirit of Jehovah from me to speak unto thee?
And Micaiah said, Behold, thou shalt see on that day, hen thou shalt go into an inner chamber to hide thyself.
And the king of Israel said, Take Micaiah, and carry him back unto Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son;
and say, Thus saith the king, Put this fello in the prison, and feed him ith bread of affliction and ith ater of affliction, until I come in peace.
And Micaiah said, If thou return at all in peace, Jehovah hath not spoken by me. And he said, Hear, ye peoples, all of you.
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah ent up to Ramoth-gilead.
And the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, I ill disguise myself, and go into the battle; but put thou on thy robes. And the king of Israel disguised himself, and ent into the battle.
No the king of Syria had commanded the thirty and to captains of his chariots, saying, Fight neither ith small nor great, save only ith the king of Israel.
And it came to pass, hen the captains of the chariots sa Jehoshaphat, that they said, Surely it is the king of Israel; and they turned aside to fight against him: and Jehoshaphat cried out.
And it came to pass, hen the captains of the chariots sa that it as not the king of Israel, that they turned back from pursuing him.

And a certain man dre his bo at a venture, and smote the king of Israel beteen the joints of the armor: herefore he said unto the driver of his chariot, Turn thy hand, and carry me out of the host; for I am sore ounded.
And the battle increased that day: and the king as stayed up in his chariot against the Syrians, and died at even; and the blood ran out of the ound into the bottom of the chariot.
And there ent a cry throughout the host about the going don of the sun, saying, Every man to his city, and every man to his country.
So the king died, and as brought to Samaria; and they buried the king in Samaria.
And they ashed the chariot by the pool of Samaria; and the dogs licked up his blood ( no the harlots ashed themselves \add there\add*); according unto the ord of Jehovah hich he spake.
No the rest of the acts of Ahab, and all that he did, and the ivory house hich he built, and all the cities that he built, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
So Ahab slept ith his fathers; and Ahaziah his son reigned in his stead.
And Jehoshaphat the son of Asa began to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat as thirty and five years old hen he began to reign; and he reigned tenty and five years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name as Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.

And he alked in all the ay of Asa his father; he turned not aside from it, doing that hich as right in the eyes of Jehovah: hobeit the high places ere not taken aay; the people still sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.
And Jehoshaphat made peace ith the king of Israel.
No the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he shoed, and ho he arred, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And the remnant of the sodomites, that remained in the days of his father Asa, he put aay out of the land.
And there as no king in Edom: a deputy as king.
Jehoshaphat made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold: but they ent not; for the ships ere broken at Ezion-geber.
Then said Ahaziah the son of Ahab unto Jehoshaphat, Let my servants go ith thy servants in the ships. But Jehoshaphat ould not.
And Jehoshaphat slept ith his fathers, and as buried ith his fathers in the city of David his father; And Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.
Ahaziah the son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned to years over Israel.
And he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, and alked in the ay of his father, and in the ay of his mother, and in the ay of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, herein he made Israel to sin.
And he served Baal, and orshipped him, and provoked to anger Jehovah, the God of Israel, according to all that his father had done.
And Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.

And Ahaziah fell don through the lattice in his upper chamber that as in Samaria, and as sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, hether I shall recover of this sickness.

But the angel of Jehovah said to Elijah the Tishbite, Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say unto them, Is it because there is no God in Israel, that ye go to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?
No therefore thus saith Jehovah, Thou shalt not come don from the bed hither thou art gone up, but shalt surely die. And Elijah departed.
And the messengers returned unto him, and he said unto them, Why is it that ye are returned?

And they said unto him, There came up a man to meet us, and said unto us, Go, turn again unto the king that sent you, and say unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Is it because there is no God in Israel, that thou sendest to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? therefore thou shalt not come don from the bed hither thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.
And he said unto them, What manner of man as he that came up to meet you, and told you these ords?
And they ansered him, He as a hairy man, and girt ith a girdle of leather about his loins. And he said, It is Elijah the Tishbite.

Then \add the king\add* sent unto him a captain of fifty ith his fifty. And he ent up to him: and, behold, he as sitting on the top of the hill. And he spake unto him, O man of God, the king hath said, Come don.

And Elijah ansered and said to the captain of fifty, If I be a man of God, let fire come don from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And there came don fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
And again he sent unto him another captain of fifty ith his fifty. And he ansered and said unto him, O man of God, thus hath the king said, Come don quickly.
And Elijah ansered and said unto them, If I be a man of God, let fire come don from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And the fire of God came don from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.

And again he sent the captain of a third fifty ith his fifty. And the third captain of fifty ent up, and came and fell on his knees before Elijah, and besought him, and said unto him, O man of God, I pray thee, let my life, and the life of these fifty thy servants, be precious in thy sight.
Behold, there came fire don from heaven, and consumed the to former captains of fifty ith their fifties; but no let my life be precious in thy sight.
And the angel of Jehovah said unto Elijah, Go don ith him: be not afraid of him. And he arose, and ent don ith him unto the king.

And he said unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Forasmuch as thou hast sent messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, is it because there is no God in Israel to inquire of his ord? therefore thou shalt not come don from the bed hither thou art gone up, but shalt surely die.
So he died according to the ord of Jehovah hich Elijah had spoken. And Jehoram began to reign in his stead in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah; because he had no son.
No the rest of the acts of Ahaziah hich he did, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And it came to pass, hen Jehovah ould take up Elijah by a hirlind into heaven, that Elijah ent ith Elisha from Gilgal.
