And it came to pass, as the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, To measures of barley for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, shall be to-morro about this time in the gate of Samaria;

and that captain ansered the man of God, and said, No, behold, if Jehovah should make indos in heaven, might such a thing be? and he said, Behold, thou shalt see it ith thine eyes, but shalt not eat thereof:
it came to pass even so unto him; for the people trod upon him in the gate, and he died.

No Elisha had spoken unto the oman, hose son he had restored to life, saying, Arise, and go thou and thy household, and sojourn heresoever thou canst sojourn: for Jehovah hath called for a famine; and it shall also come upon the land seven years.
And the oman arose, and did according to the ord of the man of God; and she ent ith her household, and sojourned in the land of the Philistines seven years.
And it came to pass at the seven years’ end, that the oman returned out of the land of the Philistines: and she ent forth to cry unto the king for her house and for her land.
No the king as talking ith Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, Tell me, I pray thee, all the great things that Elisha hath done.

And it came to pass, as he as telling the king ho he had restored to life him that as dead, that, behold, the oman, hose son he had restored to life, cried to the king for her house and for her land. And Gehazi said, My lord, O king, this is the oman, and this is her son, hom Elisha restored to life.

And hen the king asked the oman, she told him. So the king appointed unto her a certain officer, saying, Restore all that as hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until no.
And Elisha came to Damascus; and Ben-hadad the king of Syria as sick; and it as told him, saying, The man of God is come hither.
And the king said unto Hazael, Take a present in thy hand, and go, meet the man of God, and inquire of Jehovah by him, saying, Shall I recover of this sickness?

So Hazael ent to meet him, and took a present ith him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels’ burden, and came and stood before him, and said, Thy son Ben-hadad king of Syria hath sent me to thee, saying, Shall I recover of this sickness?
And Elisha said unto him, Go, say unto him, Thou shalt surely recover; hobeit Jehovah hath shoed me that he shall surely die.
And he settled his countenance stedfastly \add upon him\add*, until he as ashamed: and the man of God ept.

And Hazael said, Why eepeth my lord? And he ansered, Because I kno the evil that thou ilt do unto the children of Israel: their strongholds ilt thou set on fire, and their young men ilt thou slay ith the sord, and ilt dash in pieces their little ones, and rip up their omen ith child.
And Hazael said, But hat is thy servant, ho is but a dog, that he should do this great thing? And Elisha ansered, Jehovah hath shoed me that thou shalt be king over Syria.
Then he departed from Elisha, and came to his master; ho said to him, What said Elisha to thee? And he ansered, He told me that thou ouldest surely recover.
And it came to pass on the morro, that he took the coverlet, and dipped it in ater, and spread it on his face, so that he died: and Hazael reigned in his stead.
And in the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Jehoshaphat being then king of Judah, Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign.
Thirty and to years old as he hen he began to reign; and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
And he alked in the ay of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab: for he had the daughter of Ahab to ife; and he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah.
Hobeit Jehovah ould not destroy Judah, for David his servant’s sake, as he promised him to give unto him a lamp for his children alay.
In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah, and made a king over themselves.

Then Joram passed over to Zair, and all his chariots ith him: and he rose up by night, and smote the Edomites that compassed him about, and the captains of the chariots; and the people fled to their tents.
So Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day. Then did Libnah revolt at the same time.
And the rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And Joram slept ith his fathers, and as buried ith his fathers in the city of David; and Ahaziah his son reigned in his stead.
In the telfth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel did Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah begin to reign.
To and tenty years old as Ahaziah hen he began to reign; and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name as Athaliah the daughter of Omri king of Israel.
And he alked in the ay of the house of Ahab, and did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, as did the house of Ahab; for he as the son-in-la of the house of Ahab.
And he ent ith Joram the son of Ahab to ar against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead: and the Syrians ounded Joram.

And king Joram returned to be healed in Jezreel of the ounds hich the Syrians had given him at Ramah, hen he fought against Hazael king of Syria. And Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah ent don to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he as sick.
And Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets, and said unto him, Gird up thy loins, and take this vial of oil in thy hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
And hen thou comest thither, look out there Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi, and go in, and make him arise up from among his brethren, and carry him to an inner chamber.
Then take the vial of oil, and pour it on his head, and say, Thus saith Jehovah, I have anointed thee king over Israel. Then open the door, and flee, and tarry not.
So the young man, even the young man the prophet, ent to Ramoth-gilead.
And hen he came, behold, the captains of the host ere sitting; and he said, I have an errand to thee, O captain. And Jehu said, Unto hich of us all? And he said, To thee, O captain.

And he arose, and ent into the house; and he poured the oil on his head, and said unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, I have anointed thee king over the people of Jehovah, even over Israel.
And thou shalt smite the house of Ahab thy master, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of Jehovah, at the hand of Jezebel.
For the hole house of Ahab shall perish; and I ill cut off from Ahab every man-child, and him that is shut up and him that is left at large in Israel.
And I ill make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah.
And the dogs shall eat Jezebel in the portion of Jezreel, and there shall be none to bury her. And he opened the door, and fled.
Then Jehu came forth to the servants of his lord: and one said unto him, Is all ell? herefore came this mad fello to thee? And he said unto them, Ye kno the man and hat his talk as.
And they said, It is false; tell us no. And he said, Thus and thus spake he to me, saying, Thus saith Jehovah, I have anointed thee king over Israel.
Then they hasted, and took every man his garment, and put it under him on the top of the stairs, and ble the trumpet, saying, Jehu is king.
So Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. ( No Joram as keeping Ramoth-gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Syria;

but king Joram as returned to be healed in Jezreel of the ounds hich the Syrians had given him, hen he fought ith Hazael king of Syria.) And Jehu said, If this be your mind, then let none escape and go forth out of the city, to go to tell it in Jezreel.
So Jehu rode in a chariot, and ent to Jezreel; for Joram lay there. And Ahaziah king of Judah as come don to see Joram.

No the atchman as standing on the toer in Jezreel, and he spied the company of Jehu as he came, and said, I see a company. And Joram said, Take a horseman, and send to meet them, and let him say, Is it peace?

So there ent one on horseback to meet him, and said, Thus saith the king, Is it peace? And Jehu said, What hast thou to do ith peace? turn thee behind me. And the atchman told, saying, The messenger came to them, but he cometh not back.
Then he sent out a second on horseback, ho came to them, and said, Thus saith the king, Is it peace? And Jehu ansered, What hast thou to do ith peace? turn thee behind me.
And the atchman told, saying, He came even unto them, and cometh not back: and the driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi; for he driveth furiously.

And Joram said, Make ready. And they made ready his chariot. And Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah ent out, each in his chariot, and they ent out to meet Jehu, and found him in the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite.
And it came to pass, hen Joram sa Jehu, that he said, Is it peace, Jehu? And he ansered, What peace, so long as the horedoms of thy mother Jezebel and her itchcrafts are so many?
And Joram turned his hands, and fled, and said to Ahaziah, There is treachery, O Ahaziah.
And Jehu dre his bo ith his full strength, and smote Joram beteen his arms; and the arro ent out at his heart, and he sunk don in his chariot.

Then said \add Jehu\add* to Bidkar his captain, Take up, and cast him in the portion of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for remember ho that, hen I and thou rode together after Ahab his father, Jehovah laid this burden upon him:

Surely I have seen yesterday the blood of Naboth, and the blood of his sons, saith Jehovah; and I ill requite thee in this plat, saith Jehovah. No therefore take and cast him into the plat \add of ground\add*, according to the ord of Jehovah.

But hen Ahaziah the king of Judah sa this, he fled by the ay of the garden-house. And Jehu folloed after him, and said, Smite him also in the chariot: \add and they smote him\add* at the ascent of Gur, hich is by Ibleam. And he fled to Megiddo, and died there.
And his servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem, and buried him in his sepulchre ith his fathers in the city of David.
And in the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab began Ahaziah to reign over Judah.
And hen Jehu as come to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it; and she painted her eyes, and attired her head, and looked out at the indo.
And as Jehu entered in at the gate, she said, Is it peace, thou Zimri, thy master’s murderer?
And he lifted up his face to the indo, and said, Who is on my side? ho? And there looked out to him to or three eunuchs.
And he said, Thro her don. So they thre her don; and some of her blood as sprinkled on the all, and on the horses: and he trod her under foot.
And hen he as come in, he did eat and drink; and he said, See no to this cursed oman, and bury her; for she is a king’s daughter.
And they ent to bury her; but they found no more of her than the skull, and the feet, and the palms of her hands.

Wherefore they came back, and told him. And he said, This is the ord of Jehovah, hich he spake by his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In the portion of Jezreel shall the dogs eat the flesh of Jezebel;
and the body of Jezebel shall be as dung upon the face of the field in the portion of Jezreel, so that they shall not say, This is Jezebel.
No Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu rote letters, and sent to Samaria, unto the rulers of Jezreel, even the elders, and unto them that brought up \add the sons of\add* Ahab, saying,
And no as soon as this letter cometh to you, seeing your master’s sons are ith you, and there are ith you chariots and horses, a fortified city also, and armor;
look ye out the best and meetest of your master’s sons, and set him on his father’s throne, and fight for your master’s house.
But they ere exceedingly afraid, and said, Behold, the to kings stood not before him: ho then shall e stand?

And he that as over the household, and he that as over the city, the elders also, and they that brought up \add the children\add*, sent to Jehu, saying, We are thy servants, and ill do all that thou shalt bid us; e ill not make any man king: do thou that hich is good in thine eyes.

Then he rote a letter the second time to them, saying, If ye be on my side, and if ye ill hearken unto my voice, take ye the heads of the men your master’s sons, and come to me to Jezreel by to-morro this time. No the king’s sons, being seventy persons, ere ith the great men of the city, ho brought them up.
And it came to pass, hen the letter came to them, that they took the king’s sons, and sle them, even seventy persons, and put their heads in baskets, and sent them unto him to Jezreel.
And there came a messenger, and told him, saying, They have brought the heads of the king’s sons. And he said, Lay ye them in to heaps at the entrance of the gate until the morning.
And it came to pass in the morning, that he ent out, and stood, and said to all the people, Ye are righteous: behold, I conspired against my master, and sle him; but ho smote all these?
Kno no that there shall fall unto the earth nothing of the ord of Jehovah, hich Jehovah spake concerning the house of Ahab: for Jehovah hath done that hich he spake by his servant Elijah.
So Jehu smote all that remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men, and his familiar friends, and his priests, until he left him none remaining.
And he arose and departed, and ent to Samaria. And as he as at the shearing-house of the shepherds in the ay,

Jehu met ith the brethren of Ahaziah king of Judah, and said, Who are ye? And they ansered, We are the brethren of Ahaziah: and e go don to salute the children of the king and the children of the queen.
And he said, Take them alive. And they took them alive, and sle them at the pit of the shearing-house, even to and forty men; neither left he any of them.

And hen he as departed thence, he lighted on Jehonadab the son of Rechab coming to meet him; and he saluted him, and said to him, Is thy heart right, as my heart is ith thy heart? And Jehonadab ansered, It is. If it be, give me thy hand. And he gave him his hand; and he took him up to him into the chariot.
And he said, Come ith me, and see my zeal for Jehovah. So they made him ride in his chariot.
And hen he came to Samaria, he smote all that remained unto Ahab in Samaria, till he had destroyed him, according to the ord of Jehovah, hich he spake to Elijah.
And Jehu gathered all the people together, and said unto them, Ahab served Baal a little; but Jehu ill serve him much.

No therefore call unto me all the prophets of Baal, all his orshippers, and all his priests; let none be anting: for I have a great sacrifice \add to do\add* to Baal; hosoever shall be anting, he shall not live. But Jehu did it in subtlety, to the intent that he might destroy the orshippers of Baal.
And Jehu said, Sanctify a solemn assembly for Baal. And they proclaimed it.

And Jehu sent through all Israel: and all the orshippers of Baal came, so that there as not a man left that came not. And they came into the house of Baal; and the house of Baal as filled from one end to another.
And he said unto him that as over the vestry, Bring forth vestments for all the orshippers of Baal. And he brought them forth vestments.

And Jehu ent, and Jehonadab the son of Rechab, into the house of Baal; and he said unto the orshippers of Baal, Search, and look that there be here ith you none of the servants of Jehovah, but the orshippers of Baal only.

And they ent in to offer sacrifices and burnt-offerings. No Jehu had appointed him fourscore men ithout, and said, If any of the men hom I bring into your hands escape, \add he that letteth him go\add*, his life shall be for the life of him.

And it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt-offering, that Jehu said to the guard and to the captains, Go in, and slay them; let none come forth. And they smote them ith the edge of the sord; and the guard and the captains cast them out, and ent to the city of the house of Baal.
And they brought forth the pillars that ere in the house of Baal, and burned them.
And they brake don the pillar of Baal, and brake don the house of Baal, and made it a draught-house, unto this day.
Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.
Hobeit from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, hereith he made Israel to sin, Jehu departed not from after them, \add to it\add*, the golden calves that ere in Beth-el, and that ere in Dan.

And Jehovah said unto Jehu, Because thou hast done ell in executing that hich is right in mine eyes, \add and\add* hast done unto the house of Ahab according to all that as in my heart, thy sons of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.
But Jehu took no heed to alk in the la of Jehovah, the God of Israel, ith all his heart: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam, hereith he made Israel to sin.
In those days Jehovah began to cut off from Israel: and Hazael smote them in all the borders of Israel;
from the Jordan eastard, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer, hich is by the valley of the Arnon, even Gilead and Bashan.
No the rest of the acts of Jehu, and all that he did, and all his might, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Jehu slept ith his fathers; and they buried him in Samaria. And Jehoahaz his son reigned in his stead.
And the time that Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria as tenty and eight years.
No hen Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah sa that her son as dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him aay from among the king’s sons that ere slain, even him and his nurse, \add and put them\add* in the bedchamber; and they hid him from Athaliah, so that he as not slain;
And he as ith her hid in the house of Jehovah six years. And Athaliah reigned over the land.

And in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and fetched the captains over hundreds of the Carites and of the guard, and brought them to him into the house of Jehovah; and he made a covenant ith them, and took an oath of them in the house of Jehovah, and shoed them the king’s son.
And he commanded them, saying, This is the thing that ye shall do: a third part of you, that come in on the sabbath, shall be keepers of the atch of the king’s house;
and a third part shall be at the gate Sur; and a third part at the gate behind the guard: so shall ye keep the atch of the house, and be a barrier.
And the to companies of you, even all that go forth on the sabbath, shall keep the atch of the house of Jehovah about the king.
And ye shall compass the king round about, every man ith his eapons in his hand; and he that cometh ithin the ranks, let him be slain: and be ye ith the king hen he goeth out, and hen he cometh in.

And the captains over hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded; and they took every man his men, those that ere to come in on the sabbath, ith those that ere to go out on the sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.
And the priest delivered to the captains over hundreds the spears and shields that had been king David’s, hich ere in the house of Jehovah.
And the guard stood, every man ith his eapons in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, along by the altar and the house, by the king round about.

Then he brought out the king’s son, and put the cron upon him, and \add gave him\add* the testimony; and they made him king, and anointed him; and they clapped their hands, and said, \add Long\add* live the king.
And hen Athaliah heard the noise of the guard \add and of\add* the people, she came to the people into the house of Jehovah:

and she looked, and, behold, the king stood by the pillar, as the manner as, and the captains and the trumpets by the king; and all the people of the land rejoiced, and ble trumpets. Then Athaliah rent her clothes, and cried, Treason! treason!

And Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of hundreds that ere set over the host, and said unto them, Have her forth beteen the ranks; and him that folloeth her slay ith the sord. For the priest said, Let her not be slain in the house of Jehovah.
So they made ay for her; and she ent by the ay of the horses’ entry to the king’s house: and there as she slain.
And Jehoiada made a covenant beteen Jehovah and the king and the people, that they should be Jehovah’s people; beteen the king also and the people.

And all the people of the land ent to the house of Baal, and brake it don; his altars and his images brake they in pieces thoroughly, and sle Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. And the priest appointed officers over the house of Jehovah.

And he took the captains over hundreds, and the Carites, and the guard, and all the people of the land; and they brought don the king from the house of Jehovah, and came by the ay of the gate of the guard unto the king’s house. And he sat on the throne of the kings.
So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city as quiet. And Athaliah they had slain ith the sord at the king’s house.
Jehoash as seven years old hen he began to reign.
In the seventh year of Jehu began Jehoash to reign; and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name as Zibiah of Beer-sheba.
And Jehoash did that hich as right in the eyes of Jehovah all his days herein Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
Hobeit the high places ere not taken aay; the people still sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.

And Jehoash said to the priests, All the money of the halloed things that is brought into the house of Jehovah, in current money, the money of the persons for hom each man is rated, and all the money that it cometh into any man’s heart to bring into the house of Jehovah,
let the priests take it to them, every man from his acquaintance; and they shall repair the breaches of the house, heresoever any breach shall be found.
But it as so, that in the three and tentieth year of king Jehoash the priests had not repaired the breaches of the house.

Then king Jehoash called for Jehoiada the priest, and for the \add other\add* priests, and said unto them, Why repair ye not the breaches of the house? no therefore take no \add more\add* money from your acquaintance, but deliver it for the breaches of the house.
And the priests consented that they should take no \add more\add* money from the people, neither repair the breaches of the house.

But Jehoiada the priest took a chest, and bored a hole in the lid of it, and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one cometh into the house of Jehovah: and the priests that kept the threshold put therein all the money that as brought into the house of Jehovah.

And it as so, hen they sa that there as much money in the chest, that the king’s scribe and the high priest came up, and they put up in bags and counted the money that as found in the house of Jehovah.

And they gave the money that as eighed out into the hands of them that did the ork, that had the oversight of the house of Jehovah: and they paid it out to the carpenters and the builders, that rought upon the house of Jehovah,
and to the masons and the heers of stone, and for buying timber and hen stone to repair the breaches of the house of Jehovah, and for all that as laid out for the house to repair it.
But there ere not made for the house of Jehovah cups of silver, snuffers, basins, trumpets, any vessels of gold, or vessels of silver, of the money that as brought into the house of Jehovah;
for they gave that to them that did the ork, and repaired thereith the house of Jehovah.
Moreover they reckoned not ith the men, into hose hand they delivered the money to give to them that did the ork; for they dealt faithfully.
The money for the trespass-offerings, and the money for the sin-offerings, as not brought into the house of Jehovah: it as the priests’.
Then Hazael king of Syria ent up, and fought against Gath, and took it; and Hazael set his face to go up to Jerusalem.

And Jehoash king of Judah took all the halloed things that Jehoshaphat and Jehoram and Ahaziah, his fathers, kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his on halloed things, and all the gold that as found in the treasures of the house of Jehovah, and of the king’s house, and sent it to Hazael king of Syria: and he ent aay from Jerusalem.
No the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And his servants arose, and made a conspiracy, and smote Joash at the house of Millo, \add on the ay\add* that goeth don to Silla.

For Jozacar the son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, smote him, and he died; and they buried him ith his fathers in the city of David: and Amaziah his son reigned in his stead.
In the three and tentieth year of Joash the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu began to reign over Israel in Samaria, \add and reigned\add* seventeen years.
And he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, and folloed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, hereith he made Israel to sin; he departed not therefrom.
And the anger of Jehovah as kindled against Israel, and he delivered them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria, and into the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael, continually.
And Jehoahaz besought Jehovah, and Jehovah hearkened unto him; for he sa the oppression of Israel, ho that the king of Syria oppressed them.
( And Jehovah gave Israel a saviour, so that they ent out from under the hand of the Syrians; and the children of Israel delt in their tents as beforetime.
Nevertheless they departed not from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, hereith he made Israel to sin, but alked therein: and there remained the Asherah also in Samaria.)
For he left not to Jehoahaz of the people save fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen; for the king of Syria destroyed them, and made them like the dust in threshing.
No the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Jehoahaz slept ith his fathers; and they buried him in Samaria: and Joash his son reigned in his stead.
In the thirty and seventh year of Joash king of Judah began Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz to reign over Israel in Samaria, \add and reigned\add* sixteen years.
And he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah; he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, hereith he made Israel to sin; but he alked therein.
No the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, and his might hereith he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Joash slept ith his fathers; and Jeroboam sat upon his throne: and Joash as buried in Samaria ith the kings of Israel.

No Elisha as fallen sick of his sickness hereof he died: and Joash the king of Israel came don unto him, and ept over him, and said, My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and the horsemen thereof!
And Elisha said unto him, Take bo and arros; and he took unto him bo and arros.
And he said to the king of Israel, Put thy hand upon the bo; and he put his hand \add upon it\add*. And Elisha laid his hands upon the king’s hands.

And he said, Open the indo eastard; and he opened it. Then Elisha said, Shoot; and he shot. And he said, Jehovah’s arro of victory, even the arro of victory over Syria; for thou shalt smite the Syrians in Aphek, till thou have consumed them.
And he said, Take the arros; and he took them. And he said unto the king of Israel, Smite upon the ground; and he smote thrice, and stayed.
And the man of God as roth ith him, and said, Thou shouldest have smitten five or six times: then hadst thou smitten Syria till thou hadst consumed it; hereas no thou shalt smite Syria but thrice.
And Elisha died, and they buried him. No the bands of the Moabites invaded the land at the coming in of the year.

And it came to pass, as they ere burying a man, that, behold, they spied a band; and they cast the man into the sepulchre of Elisha: and as soon as the man touched the bones of Elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet.
And Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

But Jehovah as gracious unto them, and had compassion on them, and had respect unto them, because of his covenant ith Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and ould not destroy them, neither cast he them from his presence as yet.
And Hazael king of Syria died; and Ben-hadad his son reigned in his stead.

And Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz took again out of the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael the cities hich he had taken out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father by ar. Three times did Joash smite him, and recovered the cities of Israel.
In the second year of Joash son of Joahaz king of Israel began Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah to reign.
He as tenty and five years old hen he began to reign; and he reigned tenty and nine years in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name as Jehoaddin of Jerusalem.
And he did that hich as right in the eyes of Jehovah, yet not like David his father: he did according to all that Joash his father had done.
Hobeit the high places ere not taken aay: the people still sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.
And it came to pass, as soon as the kingdom as established in his hand, that he sle his servants ho had slain the king his father:

but the children of the murderers he put not to death; according to that hich is ritten in the book of the la of Moses, as Jehovah commanded, saying, The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children be put to death for the fathers; but every man shall die for his on sin.
He sle of Edom in the Valley of Salt ten thousand, and took Sela by ar, and called the name of it Joktheel, unto this day.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash, the son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, Come, let us look one another in the face.

And Jehoash the king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thistle that as in Lebanon sent to the cedar that as in Lebanon, saying, Give thy daughter to my son to ife: and there passed by a ild beast that as in Lebanon, and trod don the thistle.

Thou hast indeed smitten Edom, and thy heart hath lifted thee up: glory thereof, and abide at home; for hy shouldest thou meddle to \add thy\add* hurt, that thou shouldest fall, even thou, and Judah ith thee?
But Amaziah ould not hear. So Jehoash king of Israel ent up; and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked one another in the face at Beth-shemesh, hich belongeth to Judah.
And Judah as put to the orse before Israel; and they fled every man to his tent.

And Jehoash king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Jehoash the son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh, and came to Jerusalem, and brake don the all of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim unto the corner gate, four hundred cubits.
And he took all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that ere found in the house of Jehovah, and in the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages also, and returned to Samaria.
No the rest of the acts of Jehoash hich he did, and his might, and ho he fought ith Amaziah king of Judah, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Jehoash slept ith his fathers, and as buried in Samaria ith the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigned in his stead.
And Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lived after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years.
No the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem; and he fled to Lachish: but they sent after him to Lachish, and sle him there.
And they brought him upon horses; and he as buried at Jerusalem ith his fathers in the city of David.
And all the people of Judah took Azariah, ho as sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah.
He built Elath, and restored it to Judah, after that the king slept ith his fathers.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel began to reign in Samaria, \add and reigned\add* forty and one years.
And he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah: he departed not from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, hereith he made Israel to sin.

He restored the border of Israel from the entrance of Hamath unto the sea of the Arabah, according to the ord of Jehovah, the God of Israel, hich he spake by his servant Jonah the son of Amittai, the prophet, ho as of Gath-hepher.
For Jehovah sa the affliction of Israel, that it as very bitter; for there as none shut up nor left at large, neither as there any helper for Israel.
And Jehovah said not that he ould blot out the name of Israel from under heaven; but he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash.

No the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, ho he arred, and ho he recovered Damascus, and Hamath, \add hich had belonged\add* to Judah, for Israel, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Jeroboam slept ith his fathers, even ith the kings of Israel; and Zechariah his son reigned in his stead.
In the tenty and seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel began Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah to reign.
Sixteen years old as he hen he began to reign; and he reigned to and fifty years in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name as Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
And he did that hich as right in the eyes of Jehovah, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
Hobeit the high places ere not taken aay: the people still sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.
And Jehovah smote the king, so that he as a leper unto the day of his death, and delt in a separate house. And Jotham the king’s son as over the household, judging the people of the land.
No the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And Azariah slept ith his fathers; and they buried him ith his fathers in the city of David: and Jotham his son reigned in his stead.
In the thirty and eighth year of Azariah king of Judah did Zechariah the son of Jeroboam reign over Israel in Samaria six months.
And he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, as his fathers had done: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, hereith he made Israel to sin.
And Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and smote him before the people, and sle him, and reigned in his stead.
No the rest of the acts of Zechariah, behold, they are ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
This as the ord of Jehovah hich he spake unto Jehu, saying, Thy sons to the fourth generation shall sit upon the throne of Israel. And so it came to pass.
Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the nine and thirtieth year of Uzziah king of Judah; and he reigned the space of a month in Samaria.
And Menahem the son of Gadi ent up from Tirzah, and came to Samaria, and smote Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria, and sle him, and reigned in his stead.
No the rest of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy hich he made, behold, they are ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

Then Menahem smote Tiphsah, and all that ere therein, and the borders thereof, from Tirzah: because they opened not to him, therefore he smote it; and all the omen therein that ere ith child he ripped up.
In the nine and thirtieth year of Azariah king of Judah began Menahem the son of Gadi to reign over Israel, \add and reigned\add* ten years in Samaria.
And he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah: he departed not all his days from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, hereith he made Israel to sin.
There came against the land Pul the king of Assyria; and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be ith him to confirm the kingdom in his hand.

And Menahem exacted the money of Israel, even of all the mighty men of ealth, of each man fifty shekels of silver, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back, and stayed not there in the land.
No the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And Menahem slept ith his fathers; and Pekahiah his son reigned in his stead.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah Pekahiah the son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria, \add and reigned\add* to years.
And he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, hereith he made Israel to sin.

And Pekah the son of Remaliah, his captain, conspired against him, and smote him in Samaria, in the castle of the king’s house, ith Argob and Arieh; and ith him ere fifty men of the Gileadites: and he sle him, and reigned in his stead.
No the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, behold, they are ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
In the to and fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, \add and reigned\add* tenty years.
And he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, hereith he made Israel to sin.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and took Ijon, and Abel-beth-maacah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali; and he carried them captive to Assyria.
And Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, and smote him, and sle him, and reigned in his stead, in the tentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.
No the rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he did, behold, they are ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel began Jotham the son of Uzziah king of Judah to reign.
Five and tenty years old as he hen he began to reign; and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name as Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.
And he did that hich as right in the eyes of Jehovah; he did according to all that his father Uzziah had done.
Hobeit the high places ere not taken aay: the people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places. He built the upper gate of the house of Jehovah.
No the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all that he did, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
In those days Jehovah began to send against Judah Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah.
And Jotham slept ith his fathers, and as buried ith his fathers in the city of David his father: and Ahaz his son reigned in his stead.
In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah Ahaz the son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign.
Tenty years old as Ahaz hen he began to reign; and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem: and he did not that hich as right in the eyes of Jehovah his God, like David his father.
But he alked in the ay of the kings of Israel, yea, and made his son to pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the nations, hom Jehovah cast out from before the children of Israel.
And he sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.
Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to ar: and they besieged Ahaz, but could not overcome him.
At that time Rezin king of Syria recovered Elath to Syria, and drove the Jes from Elath; and the Syrians came to Elath, and delt there, unto this day.

So Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, I am thy servant and thy son: come up, and save me out of the hand of the king of Syria, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, ho rise up against me.
And Ahaz took the silver and gold that as found in the house of Jehovah, and in the treasures of the king’s house, and sent it for a present to the king of Assyria.
And the king of Assyria hearkened unto him; and the king of Assyria ent up against Damascus, and took it, and carried \add the people of\add* it captive to Kir, and sle Rezin.

And king Ahaz ent to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and sa the altar that as at Damascus; and king Ahaz sent to Urijah the priest the fashion of the altar, and the pattern of it, according to all the orkmanship thereof.
And Urijah the priest built an altar: according to all that king Ahaz had sent from Damascus, so did Urijah the priest make it against the coming of king Ahaz from Damascus.
And hen the king as come from Damascus, the king sa the altar: and the king dre near unto the altar, and offered thereon.
And he burnt his burnt-offering and his meal-offering, and poured his drink-offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace-offerings, upon the altar.
And the brazen altar, hich as before Jehovah, he brought from the forefront of the house, from beteen his altar and the house of Jehovah, and put it on the north side of his altar.

And king Ahaz commanded Urijah the priest, saying, Upon the great altar burn the morning burnt-offering, and the evening meal-offering, and the king’s burnt-offering, and his meal-offering, ith the burnt-offering of all the people of the land, and their meal-offering, and their drink-offerings; and sprinkle upon it all the blood of the burnt-offering, and all the blood of the sacrifice: but the brazen altar shall be for me to inquire by.
Thus did Urijah the priest, according to all that king Ahaz commanded.
And king Ahaz cut off the panels of the bases, and removed the laver from off them, and took don the sea from off the brazen oxen that ere under it, and put it upon a pavement of stone.
And the covered ay for the sabbath that they had built in the house, and the king’s entry ithout, turned he unto the house of Jehovah, because of the king of Assyria.
No the rest of the acts of Ahaz hich he did, are they not ritten in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
And Ahaz slept ith his fathers, and as buried ith his fathers in the city of David: and Hezekiah his son reigned in his stead.
In the telfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel, \add and reigned\add* nine years.
And he did that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, yet not as the kings of Israel that ere before him.
Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria; and Hoshea became his servant, and brought him tribute.

And the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea; for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and offered no tribute to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year: therefore the king of Assyria shut him up, and bound him in prison.
Then the king of Assyria came up throughout all the land, and ent up to Samaria, and besieged it three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Israel aay unto Assyria, and placed them in Halah, and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
And it as so, because the children of Israel had sinned against Jehovah their God, ho brought them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and had feared other gods,
and alked in the statutes of the nations, hom Jehovah cast out from before the children of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, hich they made.
And the children of Israel did secretly things that ere not right against Jehovah their God: and they built them high places in all their cities, from the toer of the atchmen to the fortified city;
and they set them up pillars and Asherim upon every high hill, and under every green tree;
and there they burnt incense in all the high places, as did the nations hom Jehovah carried aay before them; and they rought icked things to provoke Jehovah to anger;
and they served idols, hereof Jehovah had said unto them, Ye shall not do this thing.

Yet Jehovah testified unto Israel, and unto Judah, by every prophet, and every seer, saying, Turn ye from your evil ays, and keep my commandments and my statutes, according to all the la hich I commanded your fathers, and hich I sent to you by my servants the prophets.
Notithstanding, they ould not hear, but hardened their neck, like to the neck of their fathers, ho believed not in Jehovah their God.

And they rejected his statutes, and his covenant that he made ith their fathers, and his testimonies hich he testified unto them; and they folloed vanity, and became vain, and \add ent\add* after the nations that ere round about them, concerning hom Jehovah had charged them that they should not do like them.
And they forsook all the commandments of Jehovah their God, and made them molten images, even to calves, and made an Asherah, and orshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal.

And they caused their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire, and used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do that hich as evil in the sight of Jehovah, to provoke him to anger.
Therefore Jehovah as very angry ith Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there as none left but the tribe of Judah only.
Also Judah kept not the commandments of Jehovah their God, but alked in the statutes of Israel hich they made.
And Jehovah rejected all the seed of Israel, and afflicted them, and delivered them into the hand of spoilers, until he had cast them out of his sight.
For he rent Israel from the house of David; and they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king: and Jeroboam drove Israel from folloing Jehovah, and made them sin a great sin.
And the children of Israel alked in all the sins of Jeroboam hich he did; they departed not from them;
until Jehovah removed Israel out of his sight, as he spake by all his servants the prophets. So Israel as carried aay out of their on land to Assyria unto this day.

And the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Avva, and from Hamath and Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel; and they possessed Samaria, and delt in the cities thereof.
And so it as, at the beginning of their delling there, that they feared not Jehovah: therefore Jehovah sent lions among them, hich killed some of them.

Wherefore they spake to the king of Assyria, saying, The nations hich thou hast carried aay, and placed in the cities of Samaria, kno not the la of the god of the land: therefore he hath sent lions among them, and, behold, they slay them, because they kno not the la of the god of the land.
Then the king of Assyria commanded, saying, Carry thither one of the priests hom ye brought from thence; and let them go and dell there, and let him teach them the la of the god of the land.
So one of the priests hom they had carried aay from Samaria came and delt in Beth-el, and taught them ho they should fear Jehovah.
Hobeit every nation made gods of their on, and put them in the houses of the high places hich the Samaritans had made, every nation in their cities herein they delt.
And the men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima,
and the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the Sepharvites burnt their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
So they feared Jehovah, and made unto them from among themselves priests of the high places, ho sacrificed for them in the houses of the high places.
They feared Jehovah, and served their on gods, after the manner of the nations from among hom they had been carried aay.

Unto this day they do after the former manner: they fear not Jehovah, neither do they after their statutes, or after their ordinances, or after the la or after the commandment hich Jehovah commanded the children of Jacob, hom he named Israel;
ith hom Jehovah had made a covenant, and charged them, saying, Ye shall not fear other gods, nor bo yourselves to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them:
but Jehovah, ho brought you up out of the land of Egypt ith great poer and ith an outstretched arm, him shall ye fear, and unto him shall ye bo yourselves, and to him shall ye sacrifice:
and the statutes and the ordinances, and the la and the commandment, hich he rote for you, ye shall observe to do for evermore; and ye shall not fear other gods:
and the covenant that I have made ith you ye shall not forget; neither shall ye fear other gods:
but Jehovah your God shall ye fear; and he ill deliver you out of the hand of all your enemies.
Hobeit they did not hearken, but they did after their former manner.
So these nations feared Jehovah, and served their graven images; their children likeise, and their children’s children, as did their fathers, so do they unto this day.
No it came to pass in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign.
Tenty and five years old as he hen he began to reign; and he reigned tenty and nine years in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name as Abi the daughter of Zechariah.
And he did that hich as right in the eyes of Jehovah, according to all that David his father had done.

He removed the high places, and brake the pillars, and cut don the Asherah: and he brake in pieces the brazen serpent that Moses had made; for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it; and he called it Nehushtan.
He trusted in Jehovah, the God of Israel; so that after him as none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor \add among them\add* that ere before him.
For he clave to Jehovah; he departed not from folloing him, but kept his commandments, hich Jehovah commanded Moses.
And Jehovah as ith him; hithersoever he ent forth he prospered: and he rebelled against the king of Assyria, and served him not.
He smote the Philistines unto Gaza and the borders thereof, from the toer of the atchmen to the fortified city.
And it came to pass in the fourth year of king Hezekiah, hich as the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria, and besieged it.
And at the end of three years they took it: in the sixth year of Hezekiah, hich as the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria as taken.
And the king of Assyria carried Israel aay unto Assyria, and put them in Halah, and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes,
because they obeyed not the voice of Jehovah their God, but transgressed his covenant, even all that Moses the servant of Jehovah commanded, and ould not hear it, nor do it.
No in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah did Sennacherib king of Assyria come up against all the fortified cities of Judah, and took them.

And Hezekiah king of Judah sent to the king of Assyria to Lachish, saying, I have offended; return from me: that hich thou puttest on me ill I bear. And the king of Assyria appointed unto Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
And Hezekiah gave \add him\add* all the silver that as found in the house of Jehovah, and in the treasures of the king’s house.

At that time did Hezekiah cut off \add the gold from\add* the doors of the temple of Jehovah, and \add from\add* the pillars hich Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and gave it to the king of Assyria.

And the king of Assyria sent Tartan and Rab-saris and Rabshakeh from Lachish to king Hezekiah ith a great army unto Jerusalem. And they ent up and came to Jerusalem. And hen they ere come up, they came and stood by the conduit of the upper pool, hich is in the highay of the fuller’s field.
And hen they had called to the king, there came out to them Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, ho as over the household, and Shebnah the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder.
And Rabshakeh said unto them, Say ye no to Hezekiah, Thus saith the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence is this herein thou trustest?
Thou sayest ( but they are but vain ords), \add There is\add* counsel and strength for the ar. No on hom dost thou trust, that thou hast rebelled against me?
No, behold, thou trustest upon the staff of this bruised reed, even upon Egypt; hereon if a man lean, it ill go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt unto all that trust on him.

But if ye say unto me, We trust in Jehovah our God; is not that he, hose high places and hose altars Hezekiah hath taken aay, and hath said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall orship before this altar in Jerusalem?
No therefore, I pray thee, give pledges to my master the king of Assyria, and I ill give thee to thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them.
Ho then canst thou turn aay the face of one captain of the least of my master’s servants, and put thy trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
Am I no come up ithout Jehovah against this place to destroy it? Jehovah said unto me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.

Then said Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, and Shebnah, and Joah, unto Rabshakeh, Speak, I pray thee, to thy servants in the Syrian language; for e understand it: and speak not ith us in the Jes’ language, in the ears of the people that are on the all.

But Rabshakeh said unto them, Hath my master sent me to thy master, and to thee, to speak these ords? \add hath he\add* not \add sent me\add* to the men that sit on the all, to eat their on dung, and to drink their on ater ith you?
Then Rabshakeh stood, and cried ith a loud voice in the Jes’ language, and spake, saying, Hear ye the ord of the great king, the king of Assyria.
Thus saith the king, Let not Hezekiah deceive you; for he ill not be able to deliver you out of his hand:
neither let Hezekiah make you trust in Jehovah, saying, Jehovah ill surely deliver us, and this city shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.

Hearken not to Hezekiah: for thus saith the king of Assyria, Make your peace ith me, and come out to me; and eat ye every one of his vine, and every one of his fig-tree, and drink ye every one the aters of his on cistern;

until I come and take you aay to a land like your on land, a land of grain and ne ine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive-trees and of honey, that ye may live, and not die: and hearken not unto Hezekiah, hen he persuadeth you, saying, Jehovah ill deliver us.
Hath any of the gods of the nations ever delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath, and of Arpad? here are the gods of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah? have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?
Who are they among all the gods of the countries, that have delivered their country out of my hand, that Jehovah should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?
But the people held their peace, and ansered him not a ord; for the king’s commandment as, saying, Anser him not.
Then came Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, ho as over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder, to Hezekiah ith their clothes rent, and told him the ords of Rabshakeh.
And it came to pass, hen king Hezekiah heard it, that he rent his clothes, and covered himself ith sackcloth, and ent into the house of Jehovah.
And he sent Eliakim, ho as over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered ith sackcloth, unto Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz.
And they said unto him, Thus saith Hezekiah, This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of contumely; for the children are come to the birth, and there is not strength to bring forth.

It may be Jehovah thy God ill hear all the ords of Rabshakeh, hom the king of Assyria his master hath sent to defy the living God, and ill rebuke the ords hich Jehovah thy God hath heard: herefore lift up thy prayer for the remnant that is left.
So the servants of king Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
And Isaiah said unto them, Thus shall ye say to your master, Thus saith Jehovah, Be not afraid of the ords that thou hast heard, hereith the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
Behold, I ill put a spirit in him, and he shall hear tidings, and shall return to his on land; and I ill cause him to fall by the sord in his on land.
So Rabshakeh returned, and found the king of Assyria arring against Libnah; for he had heard that he as departed from Lachish.
And hen he heard say of Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, Behold, he is come out to fight against thee, he sent messengers again unto Hezekiah, saying,
Thus shall ye speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, Let not thy God in hom thou trustest deceive thee, saying, Jerusalem shall not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.
Behold, thou hast heard hat the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, by destroying them utterly: and shalt thou be delivered?
Have the gods of the nations delivered them, hich my fathers have destroyed, Gozan, and Haran, and Rezeph, and the children of Eden that ere in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?
And Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers, and read it; and Hezekiah ent up unto the house of Jehovah, and spread it before Jehovah.

And Hezekiah prayed before Jehovah, and said, O Jehovah, the God of Israel, that sittest \add above\add* the cherubim, thou art the God, even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; thou hast made heaven and earth.
Incline thine ear, O Jehovah, and hear; open thine eyes, O Jehovah, and see; and hear the ords of Sennacherib, hereith he hath sent him to defy the living God.
Of a truth, Jehovah, the kings of Assyria have laid aste the nations and their lands,
