And all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the forces, arose, and came to Egypt; for they ere afraid of the Chaldeans.

And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the telfth month, on the seven and tentieth day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison;
and he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that ere ith him in Babylon,
and changed his prison garments. And \add Jehoiachin\add* did eat bread before him continually all the days of his life:
and for his alloance, there as a continual alloance given him of the king, every day a portion, all the days of his life.
Adam, Seth, Enosh,
Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,
Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.
And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, and Diphath, and Togarmah.
And the sons of Javan: Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
The sons of Ham: Cush, and Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
And the sons of Cush: Seba, and Havilah, and Sabta, and Raama, and Sabteca. And the sons of Raamah: Sheba, and Dedan.
And Cush begat Nimrod; he began to be a mighty one in the earth.
And Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,
and Pathrusim, and Casluhim ( from hence came the Philistines), and Caphtorim.
And Canaan begat Sidon his first-born, and Heth,
and the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgashite,
and the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,
and the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite.
The sons of Shem: Elam, and Asshur, and Arpachshad, and Lud, and Aram, and Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Meshech.
And Arpachshad begat Shelah, and Shelah begat Eber.
And unto Eber ere born to sons: the name of the one as Peleg; for in his days the earth as divided; and his brother’s name as Joktan.
And Joktan begat Almodad, and Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth, and Jerah,
and Hadoram, and Uzal, and Diklah,
and Ebal, and Abimael, and Sheba,
and Ophir, and Havilah, and Jobab. All these ere the sons of Joktan.
Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah,
Eber, Peleg, Reu,
Serug, Nahor, Terah,
Abram ( the same is Abraham).
The sons of Abraham: Isaac, and Ishmael.
These are their generations: the first-born of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
Mishma, and Dumah, Massa, Hadad, and Tema,
Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael.
And the sons of Keturah, Abraham’s concubine: she bare Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah. And the sons of Jokshan: Sheba, and Dedan.
And the sons of Midian: Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these ere the sons of Keturah.
And Abraham begat Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau, and Israel.
The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, and Jeush, and Jalam, and Korah.
The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, and Omar, Zephi, and Gatam, Kenaz, and Timna, and Amalek.
The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
And the sons of Seir: Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah, and Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan.
And the sons of Lotan: Hori, and Homam; and Timna as Lotan’s sister.
The sons of Shobal: Alian, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. And the sons of Zibeon: Aiah, and Anah.
The sons of Anah: Dishon. And the sons of Dishon: Hamran, and Eshban, and Ithran, and Cheran.
The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, and Zaavan, Jaakan. The sons of Dishan: Uz, and Aran.
No these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Israel: Bela the son of Beor; and the name of his city as Dinhabah.
And Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead.
And Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his stead.
And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, ho smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead; and the name of his city as Avith.
And Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his stead.
And Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the River reigned in his stead.
And Shaul died, and Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.
And Baal-hanan died, and Hadad reigned in his stead; and the name of his city as Pai: and his ife’s name as Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-zahab.
And Hadad died. And the chiefs of Edom ere: chief Timna, chief Aliah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom.
These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, and Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
The sons of Judah: Er, and Onan, and Shelah; hich three ere born unto him of Shua’s daughter the Canaanitess. And Er, Judah’s first-born, as icked in the sight of Jehovah; and he sle him.
And Tamar his daughter-in-la bare him Perez and Zerah. All the sons of Judah ere five.
The sons of Perez: Hezron, and Hamul.
And the sons of Zerah: Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara; five of them in all.
And the sons of Carmi: Achar, the troubler of Israel, ho committed a trespass in the devoted thing.
And the sons of Ethan: Azariah.
The sons also of Hezron, that ere born unto him: Jerahmeel, and Ram, and Chelubai.
And Ram begat Amminadab, and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah;
and Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz,
and Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse;
and Jesse begat his first-born Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimea the third,
Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
Ozem the sixth, David the seventh;
and their sisters ere Zeruiah and Abigail. And the sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, and Joab, and Asahel, three.
And Abigail bare Amasa; and the father of Amasa as Jether the Ishmaelite.
And Caleb the son of Hezron begat \add children\add* of Azubah \add his\add* ife, and of Jerioth; and these ere her sons: Jesher, and Shobab, and Ardon.
And Azubah died, and Caleb took unto him Ephrath, ho bare him Hur.
And Hur begat Uri, and Uri begat Bezalel.
And afterard Hezron ent in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, hom he took \add to ife\add* hen he as threescore years old; and she bare him Segub.
And Segub begat Jair, ho had three and tenty cities in the land of Gilead.
And Geshur and Aram took the tons of Jair from them, ith Kenath, and the villages thereof, even threescore cities. All these ere the sons of Machir the father of Gilead.
And after that Hezron as dead in Caleb-ephrathah, then Abijah Hezron’s ife bare him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.
And the sons of Jerahmeel the first-born of Hezron ere Ram the first-born, and Bunah, and Oren, and Ozem, Ahijah.
And Jerahmeel had another ife, hose name as Atarah; she as the mother of Onam.
And the sons of Ram the first-born of Jerahmeel ere Maaz, and Jamin, and Eker.
And the sons of Onam ere Shammai, and Jada. And the sons of Shammai: Nadab, and Abishur.
And the name of the ife of Abishur as Abihail; and she bare him Ahban, and Molid.
And the sons of Nadab: Seled, and Appaim; but Seled died ithout children.
And the sons of Appaim: Ishi. And the sons of Ishi: Sheshan. And the sons of Sheshan: Ahlai.
And the sons of Jada the brother of Shammai: Jether, and Jonathan; and Jether died ithout children.
And the sons of Jonathan: Peleth, and Zaza. These ere the sons of Jerahmeel.
No Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, hose name as Jarha.
And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to ife; and she bare him Attai.
And Attai begat Nathan, and Nathan begat Zabad,
and Zabad begat Ephlal, and Ephlal begat Obed,
and Obed begat Jehu, and Jehu begat Azariah,
and Azariah begat Helez, and Helez begat Eleasah,
and Eleasah begat Sismai, and Sismai begat Shallum,
and Shallum begat Jekamiah, and Jekamiah begat Elishama.
And the sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel ere Mesha his first-born, ho as the father of Ziph; and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron.
And the sons of Hebron: Korah, and Tappuah, and Rekem, and Shema.
And Shema begat Raham, the father of Jorkeam; and Rekem begat Shammai.
And the son of Shammai as Maon; and Maon as the father of Beth-zur.
And Ephah, Caleb’s concubine, bare Haran, and Moza, and Gazez; and Haran begat Gazez.
And the sons of Jahdai: Regem, and Jothan, and Geshan, and Pelet, and Ephah, and Shaaph.
Maacah, Caleb’s concubine, bare Sheber and Tirhanah.
She bare also Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Machbena, and the father of Gibea; and the daughter of Caleb as Achsah.
These ere the sons of Caleb, the son of Hur, the first-born of Ephrathah: Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim,
Salma the father of Beth-lehem, Hareph the father of Beth-gader.
And Shobal the father of Kiriath-jearim had sons: Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth.
And the families of Kiriath-jearim: The Ithrites, and the Puthites, and the Shumathites, and the Mishraites; of them came the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.
The sons of Salma: Beth-lehem, and the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, and half of the Manahathites, the Zorites.
And the families of scribes that delt at Jabez: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, the Sucathites. These are the Kenites that came of Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.
No these ere the sons of David, that ere born unto him in Hebron: the first-born, Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; the second, Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelitess;
the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith;
the fifth, Shephatiah of Abital; the sixth, Ithream by Eglah his ife:
six ere born unto him in Hebron; and there he reigned seven years and six months. And in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years;
and these ere born unto him in Jerusalem: Shimea, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon, four, of Bath-shua the daughter of Ammiel;
and Ibhar, and Elishama, and Eliphelet,
and Nogah, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
and Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine.
All these ere the sons of David, besides the sons of the concubines; and Tamar as their sister.
And Solomon’s son as Rehoboam, Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son,
Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son,
Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son,
Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son,
Amon his son, Josiah his son.
And the sons of Josiah: the first-born Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum.
And the sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, Zedekiah his son.
And the sons of Jeconiah, the captive: Shealtiel his son,
and Malchiram, and Pedaiah, and Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
And the sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel, and Shimei. And the sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam, and Hananiah; and Shelomith as their sister;
and Hashubah, and Ohel, and Berechiah, and Hasadiah, Jushab-hesed, five.
And the sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah, and Jeshaiah; the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shecaniah.
And the sons of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. And the sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, and Igal, and Bariah, and Neariah, and Shaphat, six.
And the sons of Neariah: Elioenai, and Hizkiah, and Azrikam, three.
And the sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, and Eliashib, and Pelaiah, and Akkub, and Johanan, and Delaiah, and Anani, seven.
The sons of Judah: Perez, Hezron, and Carmi, and Hur, and Shobal.
And Reaiah the son of Shobal begat Jahath; and Jahath begat Ahumai and Lahad. These are the families of the Zorathites.
And these ere \add the sons of\add* the father of Etam: Jezreel, and Ishma, and Idbash; and the name of their sister as Hazzelelponi;
and Penuel the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah. These are the sons of Hur, the first-born of Ephrathah, the father of Beth-lehem.
And Ashhur the father of Tekoa had to ives, Helah and Naarah.
And Naarah bare him Ahuzzam, and Hepher, and Temeni, and Haahashtari. These ere the sons of Naarah.
And the sons of Helah ere Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
And Hakkoz begat Anub, and Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum.
And Jabez as more honorable than his brethren: and his mother called his name Jabez, saying, Because I bare him ith sorro.

And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou ouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my border, and that thy hand might be ith me, and that thou ouldest keep me from evil, that it be not to my sorro! And God granted him that hich he requested.
And Chelub the brother of Shuhah begat Mehir, ho as the father of Eshton.
And Eshton begat Beth-rapha, and Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Ir-nahash. These are the men of Recah.
And the sons of Kenaz: Othniel, and Seraiah. And the sons of Othniel: Hathath.
And Meonothai begat Ophrah: and Seraiah begat Joab the father of Ge-harashim; for they ere craftsmen.
And the sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah, and Naam; and the sons of Elah; and Kenaz.
And the sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, and Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
And the sons of Ezrah: Jether, and Mered, and Epher, and Jalon; and she bare Miriam, and Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa.
And his ife the Jeess bare Jered the father of Gedor, and Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. And these are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, hom Mered took.
And the sons of the ife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham, ere the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
And the sons of Shimon: Amnon, and Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon. And the sons of Ishi: Zoheth, and Ben-zoheth.
The sons of Shelah the son of Judah: Er the father of Lecah, and Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the house of them that rought fine linen, of the house of Ashbea;
and Jokim, and the men of Cozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, ho had dominion in Moab, and Jashubi-lehem. And the records are ancient.
These ere the potters, and the inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah: there they delt ith the king for his ork.
The sons of Simeon: Nemuel, and Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, Shaul;
Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son.
And the sons of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son.
And Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brethren had not many children, neither did all their family multiply like to the children of Judah.
And they delt at Beer-sheba, and Moladah, and Hazar-shual,
and at Bilhah, and at Ezem, and at Tolad,
and at Bethuel, and at Hormah, and at Ziklag,
and at Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susim, and at Beth-biri, and at Shaaraim. These ere their cities unto the reign of David.
And their villages ere Etam, and Ain, Rimmon, and Tochen, and Ashan, five cities;
and all their villages that ere round about the same cities, unto Baal. These ere their habitations, and they have their genealogy.
And Meshobab, and Jamlech, and Joshah the son of Amaziah,
and Joel, and Jehu the son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel,
and Elioenai, and Jaakobah, and Jeshohaiah, and Asaiah, and Adiel, and Jesimiel, and Benaiah,
and Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah—
these mentioned by name ere princes in their families: and their fathers’ houses increased greatly.
And they ent to the entrance of Gedor, even unto the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks.
And they found fat pasture and good, and the land as ide, and quiet, and peaceable; for they that delt there aforetime ere of Ham.

And these ritten by name came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and smote their tents, and the Meunim that ere found there, and destroyed them utterly unto this day, and delt in their stead; because there as pasture there for their flocks.
And some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, ent to mount Seir, having for their captains Pelatiah, and Neariah, and Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
And they smote the remnant of the Amalekites that escaped, and have delt there unto this day.

And the sons of Reuben the first-born of Israel ( for he as the first-born; but, forasmuch as he defiled his father’s couch, his birthright as given unto the sons of Joseph the son of Israel; and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.
For Judah prevailed above his brethren, and of him came the prince; but the birthright as Joseph’s),
the sons of Reuben the first-born of Israel: Hanoch, and Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,
Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,
Beerah his son, hom Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria carried aay captive: he as prince of the Reubenites.
And his brethren by their families, hen the genealogy of their generations as reckoned: the chief, Jeiel, and Zechariah,
and Bela the son of Azaz, the son of Shema, the son of Joel, ho delt in Aroer, even unto Nebo and Baal-meon:
and eastard he delt even unto the entrance of the ilderness from the river Euphrates, because their cattle ere multiplied in the land of Gilead.
And in the days of Saul, they made ar ith the Hagrites, ho fell by their hand; and they delt in their tents throughout all the \add land\add* east of Gilead.
And the sons of Gad delt over against them, in the land of Bashan unto Salecah:
Joel the chief, and Shapham the second, and Janai, and Shaphat in Bashan.
And their brethren of their fathers’ houses: Michael, and Meshullam, and Sheba, and Jorai, and Jacan, and Zia, and Eber, seven.
These ere the sons of Abihail, the son of Huri, the son of Jaroah, the son of Gilead, the son of Michael, the son of Jeshishai, the son of Jahdo, the son of Buz;
Ahi the son of Abdiel, the son of Guni, chief of their fathers’ houses.
And they delt in Gilead in Bashan, and in its tons, and in all the suburbs of Sharon, as far as their borders.
All these ere reckoned by genealogies in the days of Jotham king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.

The sons of Reuben, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men, men able to bear buckler and sord, and to shoot ith bo, and skilful in ar, ere forty and four thousand seven hundred and threescore, that ere able to go forth to ar.
And they made ar ith the Hagrites, ith Jetur, and Naphish, and Nodab.

And they ere helped against them, and the Hagrites ere delivered into their hand, and all that ere ith them; for they cried to God in the battle, and he as entreated of them, because they put their trust in him.
And they took aay their cattle; of their camels fifty thousand, and of sheep to hundred and fifty thousand, and of asses to thousand, and of men a hundred thousand.
For there fell many slain, because the ar as of God. And they delt in their stead until the captivity.
And the children of the half-tribe of Manasseh delt in the land: they increased from Bashan unto Baal-hermon and Senir and mount Hermon.

And these ere the heads of their fathers’ houses: even Epher, and Ishi, and Eliel, and Azriel, and Jeremiah, and Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, mighty men of valor, famous men, heads of their fathers’ houses.
And they trespassed against the God of their fathers, and played the harlot after the gods of the peoples of the land, hom God destroyed before them.

And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried them aay, even the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them unto Halah, and Habor, and Hara, and to the river of Gozan, unto this day.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
And the sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel.
And the children of Amram: Aaron, and Moses, and Miriam. And the sons of Aaron: Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar begat Phinehas, Phinehas begat Abishua,
and Abishua begat Bukki, and Bukki begat Uzzi,
and Uzzi begat Zerahiah, and Zerahiah begat Meraioth,
Meraioth begat Amariah, and Amariah begat Ahitub,
and Ahitub begat Zadok, and Zadok begat Ahimaaz,
and Ahimaaz begat Azariah, and Azariah begat Johanan,
and Johanan begat Azariah ( he it is that executed the priest’s office in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem),
and Azariah begat Amariah, and Amariah begat Ahitub,
and Ahitub begat Zadok, and Zadok begat Shallum,
and Shallum begat Hilkiah, and Hilkiah begat Azariah,
and Azariah begat Seraiah, and Seraiah begat Jehozadak;
And Jehozadak ent \add into captivity\add*, hen Jehovah carried aay Judah and Jerusalem by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
And these are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.
And the sons of Kohath ere Amram, and Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. And these are the families of the Levites according to their fathers’ \add houses\add*.
Of Gershom: Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son,
Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, Jeatherai his son.
The sons of Kohath: Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son,
Elkanah his son, and Ebiasaph his son, and Assir his son,
Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Shaul his son.
And the sons of Elkanah: Amasai, and Ahimoth.
As for Elkanah, the sons of Elkanah: Zophai his son, and Nahath his son,
Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, Elkanah his son.
And the sons of Samuel: the first-born, \add Joel\add*, and the second Abijah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,
Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son.
And these are they hom David set over the service of song in the house of Jehovah, after that the ark had rest.
And they ministered ith song before the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, until Solomon had built the house of Jehovah in Jerusalem: and they aited on their office according to their order.
And these are they that aited, and their sons. Of the sons of the Kohathites: Heman the singer, the son of Joel, the son of Samuel,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah,
the son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai,
the son of Elkanah, the son of Joel, the son of Azariah, the son of Zephaniah,
the son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah,
the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel.
And his brother Asaph, ho stood on his right hand, even Asaph the son of Berechiah, the son of Shimea,
the son of Michael, the son of Baaseiah, the son of Malchijah,
the son of Ethni, the son of Zerah, the son of Adaiah,
the son of Ethan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimei,
the son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi.
And on the left hand their brethren the sons of Merari: Ethan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,
the son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah,
the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shemer,
the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi.
And their brethren the Levites ere appointed for all the service of the tabernacle of the house of God.

But Aaron and his sons offered upon the altar of burnt-offering, and upon the altar of incense, for all the ork of the most holy place, and to make atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.
And these are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son.
No these are their delling-places according to their encampments in their borders: to the sons of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites (for theirs as the \add first\add* lot),
to them they gave Hebron in the land of Judah, and the suburbs thereof round about it;
but the fields of the city, and the villages thereof, they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
And to the sons of Aaron they gave the cities of refuge, Hebron; Libnah also ith its suburbs, and Jattir, and Eshtemoa ith its suburbs,
and Hilen ith its suburbs, Debir ith its suburbs,
and Ashan ith its suburbs, and Beth-shemesh ith its suburbs;
and out of the tribe of Benjamin, Geba ith its suburbs, and Allemeth ith its suburbs, and Anathoth ith its suburbs. All their cities throughout their families ere thirteen cities.
And unto the rest of the sons of Kohath \add ere given\add* by lot, out of the family of the tribe, out of the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh, ten cities.

And to the sons of Gershom, according to their families, out of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Asher, and out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities.
Unto the sons of Merari \add ere given\add* by lot, according to their families, out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, telve cities.
And the children of Israel gave to the Levites the cities ith their suburbs.

And they gave by lot out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, and out of the tribe of the children of Benjamin, these cities hich are mentioned by name.
And some of the families of the sons of Kohath had cities of their borders out of the tribe of Ephraim.
And they gave unto them the cities of refuge, Shechem in the hill-country of Ephraim ith its suburbs; Gezer also ith its suburbs,
and Jokmeam ith its suburbs, and Beth-horon ith its suburbs,
and Aijalon ith its suburbs, and Gath-rimmon ith its suburbs;
and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Aner ith its suburbs, and Bileam ith its suburbs, for the rest of the family of the sons of Kohath.
Unto the sons of Gershom \add ere given\add*, out of the family of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan ith its suburbs, and Ashtaroth ith its suburbs;
and out of the tribe of Issachar, Kedesh ith its suburbs, Daberath ith its suburbs,
and Ramoth ith its suburbs, and Anem ith its suburbs;
and out of the tribe of Asher, Mashal ith its suburbs, and Abdon ith its suburbs,
and Hukok ith its suburbs, and Rehob ith its suburbs;
and out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee ith its suburbs, and Hammon ith its suburbs, and Kiriathaim ith its suburbs.
Unto the rest of \add the Levites\add*, the sons of Merari, \add ere given\add*, out of the tribe of Zebulun, Rimmono ith its suburbs, Tabor ith its suburbs;
and beyond the Jordan at Jericho, on the east side of the Jordan, \add ere given them\add*, out of the tribe of Reuben, Bezer in the ilderness ith its suburbs, and Jahzah ith its suburbs,
and Kedemoth ith its suburbs, and Mephaath ith its suburbs;
and out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead ith its suburbs, and Mahanaim ith its suburbs,
and Heshbon ith its suburbs, and Jazer ith its suburbs.
And of the sons of Issachar: Tola, and Puah, Jashub, and Shimron, four.

And the sons of Tola: Uzzi, and Rephaiah, and Jeriel, and Jahmai, and Ibsam, and Shemuel, heads of their fathers’ houses, \add to it\add*, of Tola; mighty men of valor in their generations: their number in the days of David as to and tenty thousand and six hundred.
And the sons of Uzzi: Izrahiah. And the sons of Izrahiah: Michael, and Obadiah, and Joel, Isshiah, five; all of them chief men.
And ith them, by their generations, after their fathers’ houses, ere bands of the host for ar, six and thirty thousand; for they had many ives and sons.
And their brethren among all the families of Issachar, mighty men of valor, reckoned in all by genealogy, ere fourscore and seven thousand.
\add The sons of\add* Benjamin: Bela, and Becher, and Jediael, three.

And the sons of Bela: Ezbon, and Uzzi, and Uzziel, and Jerimoth, and Iri, five; heads of fathers’ houses, mighty men of valor; and they ere reckoned by genealogy tenty and to thousand and thirty and four.
And the sons of Becher: Zemirah, and Joash, and Eliezer, and Elioenai, and Omri, and Jeremoth, and Abijah, and Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these ere the sons of Becher.
And they ere reckoned by genealogy, after their generations, heads of their fathers’ houses, mighty men of valor, tenty thousand and to hundred.
And the sons of Jediael: Bilhan. And the sons of Bilhan: Jeush, and Benjamin, and Ehud, and Chenaanah, and Zethan, and Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these ere sons of Jediael, according to the heads of their fathers’ \add houses\add*, mighty men of valor, seventeen thousand and to hundred, that ere able to go forth in the host for ar.
Shuppim also, and Huppim, the sons of Ir, Hushim, the sons of Aher.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shallum, the sons of Bilhah.
The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, hom his concubine the Aramitess bare; she bare Machir the father of Gilead.
And Machir took a ife of Huppim and Shuppim, hose sister’s name as Maacah; and the name of the second as Zelophehad: and Zelophehad had daughters.
And Maacah the ife of Machir bare a son, and she called his name Peresh; and the name of his brother as Sheresh; and his sons ere Ulam and Rakem.
And the sons of Ulam: Bedan. These ere the sons of Gilead the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.
And his sister Hammolecheth bare Ishhod, and Abiezer, and Mahlah.
And the sons of Shemida ere Ahian, and Shechem, and Likhi, and Aniam.
And the sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah, and Bered his son, and Tahath his son, and Eleadah his son, and Tahath his son,
and Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer, and Elead, hom the men of Gath that ere born in the land sle, because they came don to take aay their cattle.
And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him.
And he ent in to his ife, and she conceived, and bare a son, and he called his name Beriah, because it ent evil ith his house.
And his daughter as Sheerah, ho built Beth-horon the nether and the upper, and Uzzen-sheerah.
And Rephah as his son, and Resheph, and Telah his son, and Tahan his son,
Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
Nun his son, Joshua his son.
And their possessions and habitations ere Beth-el and the tons thereof, and eastard Naaran, and estard Gezer, ith the tons thereof; Shechem also and the tons thereof, unto Azzah and the tons thereof;
and by the borders of the children of Manasseh, Beth-shean and its tons, Taanach and its tons, Megiddo and its tons, Dor and its tons. In these delt the children of Joseph the son of Israel.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, and Ishvah, and Ishvi, and Beriah, and Serah their sister.
And the sons of Beriah: Heber, and Malchiel, ho as the father of Birzaith.
And Heber begat Japhlet, and Shomer, and Hotham, and Shua their sister.
And the sons of Japhlet: Pasach, and Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the children of Japhlet.
And the sons of Shemer: Ahi, and Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
And the sons of Helem his brother: Zophah, and Imna, and Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Zophah: Suah, and Harnepher, and Shual, and Beri, and Imrah,
Bezer, and Hod, and Shamma, and Shilshah, and Ithran, and Beera.
And the sons of Jether: Jephunneh, and Pispa, and Ara.
And the sons of Ulla: Arah, and Hanniel, and Rizia.

All these ere the children of Asher, heads of the fathers’ houses, choice and mighty men of valor, chief of the princes. And the number of them reckoned by genealogy for service in ar as tenty and six thousand men.
And Benjamin begat Bela his first-born, Ashbel the second, and Aharah the third,
Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth.
And Bela had sons: Addar, and Gera, and Abihud,
and Abishua, and Naaman, and Ahoah,
and Gera, and Shephuphan, and Huram.
And these are the sons of Ehud: these are the heads of fathers’ \add houses\add* of the inhabitants of Geba, and they carried them captive to Manahath:
and Naaman, and Ahijah, and Gera, he carried them captive; and he begat Uzza and Ahihud.
And Shaharaim begat children in the field of Moab, after he had sent them aay; Hushim and Baara ere his ives.
And he begat of Hodesh his ife, Jobab, and Zibia, and Mesha, and Malcam,
and Jeuz, and Shachia, and Mirmah. These ere his sons, heads of fathers’ \add houses\add*.
And of Hushim he begat Abitub and Elpaal.
And the sons of Elpaal: Eber, and Misham, and Shemed, ho built Ono and Lod, ith the tons thereof;
and Beriah, and Shema, ho ere heads of fathers’ \add houses\add* of the inhabitants of Aijalon, ho put to flight the inhabitants of Gath;
and Ahio, Shashak, and Jeremoth,
and Zebadiah, and Arad, and Eder,
and Michael, and Ishpah, and Joha, the sons of Beriah,
and Zebadiah, and Meshullam, and Hizki, and Heber,
and Ishmerai, and Izliah, and Jobab, the sons of Elpaal,
and Jakim, and Zichri, and Zabdi,
and Elienai, and Zillethai, and Eliel,
and Adaiah, and Beraiah, and Shimrath, the sons of Shimei,
and Ishpan, and Eber, and Eliel,
and Abdon, and Zichri, and Hanan,
and Hananiah, and Elam, and Anthothijah,
and Iphdeiah, and Penuel, the sons of Shashak,
and Shamsherai, and Shehariah, and Athaliah,
and Jaareshiah, and Elijah, and Zichri, the sons of Jeroham.
These ere heads of fathers’ \add houses\add* throughout their generations, chief men: these delt in Jerusalem.
And in Gibeon there delt the father of Gibeon, \add Jeiel\add*, hose ife’s name as Maacah;
and his first-born son Abdon, and Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Nadab,
and Gedor, and Ahio, and Zecher.
And Mikloth begat Shimeah. And they also delt ith their brethren in Jerusalem, over against their brethren.
And Ner begat Kish; and Kish begat Saul; and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchi-shua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
And the son of Jonathan as Merib-baal; and Merib-baal begat Micah.
And the sons of Micah: Pithon, and Melech, and Tarea, and Ahaz.
And Ahaz begat Jehoaddah; and Jehoaddah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri begat Moza.
And Moza begat Binea; Raphah as his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
And Azel had six sons, hose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, and Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan. All these ere the sons of Azel.
And the sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his first-born, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
And the sons of Ulam ere mighty men of valor, archers, and had many sons, and sons’ sons, a hundred and fifty. All these ere of the sons of Benjamin.
So all Israel ere reckoned by genealogies; and, behold, they are ritten in the book of the kings of Israel. And Judah as carried aay captive to Babylon for their transgression.
No the first inhabitants that delt in their possessions in their cities ere Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the Nethinim.
And in Jerusalem delt of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin, and of the children of Ephraim and Manasseh:
Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, of the children of Perez the son of Judah.
And of the Shilonites: Asaiah the first-born, and his sons.
And of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel, and their brethren, six hundred and ninety.
And of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Hodaviah, the son of Hassenuah,
and Ibneiah the son of Jeroham, and Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri, and Meshullam the son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel, the son of Ibnijah;
and their brethren, according to their generations, nine hundred and fifty and six. All these men ere heads of fathers’ \add houses\add* by their fathers’ houses.
And of the priests: Jedaiah, and Jehoiarib, Jachin,
and Azariah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of the house of God;
and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah, and Maasai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer;
and their brethren, heads of their fathers’ houses, a thousand and seven hundred and threescore; very able men for the ork of the service of the house of God.
And of the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari;
and Bakbakkar, Heresh, and Galal, and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of Zichri, the son of Asaph,
and Obadiah the son of Shemaiah, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun, and Berechiah the son of Asa, the son of Elkanah, that delt in the villages of the Netophathites.
And the porters: Shallum, and Akkub, and Talmon, and Ahiman, and their brethren ( Shallum as the chief),
ho hitherto \add aited\add* in the king’s gate eastard: they ere the porters for the camp of the children of Levi.

And Shallum the son of Kore, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah, and his brethren, of his father’s house, the Korahites, ere over the ork of the service, keepers of the thresholds of the tent: and their fathers had been over the camp of Jehovah, keepers of the entry.
And Phinehas the son of Eleazar as ruler over them in time past, \add and\add* Jehovah as ith him.
Zechariah the son of Meshelemiah as porter of the door of the tent of meeting.

All these that ere chosen to be porters in the thresholds ere to hundred and telve. These ere reckoned by genealogy in their villages, hom David and Samuel the seer did ordain in their office of trust.
So they and their children had the oversight of the gates of the house of Jehovah, even the house of the tent, by ards.
On the four sides ere the porters, toard the east, est, north, and south.
And their brethren, in their villages, ere to come in every seven days from time to time to be ith them:
for the four chief porters, ho ere Levites, ere in an office of trust, and ere over the chambers and over the treasuries in the house of God.
And they lodged round about the house of God, because the charge \add thereof\add* as upon them; and to them pertained the opening thereof morning by morning.
And certain of them had charge of the vessels of service; for by count ere these brought in and by count ere these taken out.
Some of them also ere appointed over the furniture, and over all the vessels of the sanctuary, and over the fine flour, and the ine, and the oil, and the frankincense, and the spices.
And some of the sons of the priests prepared the confection of the spices.
And Mattithiah, one of the Levites, ho as the first-born of Shallum the Korahite, had the office of trust over the things that ere baked in pans.
And some of their brethren, of the sons of the Kohathites, ere over the shobread, to prepare it every sabbath.

And these are the singers, heads of fathers’ \add houses\add* of the Levites, \add ho delt\add* in the chambers \add and ere\add* free \add from other service\add*; for they ere employed in their ork day and night.
These ere heads of fathers’ \add houses\add* of the Levites, throughout their generations, chief men: these delt at Jerusalem.
And in Gibeon there delt the father of Gibeon, Jeiel, hose ife’s name as Maacah;
and his first-born son Abdon, and Zur, and Kish, and Baal, and Ner, and Nadab,
and Gedor, and Ahio, and Zechariah, and Mikloth.
And Mikloth begat Shimeam. And they also delt ith their brethren in Jerusalem, over against their brethren.
And Ner begat Kish; and Kish begat Saul; and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
And the son of Jonathan as Merib-baal; and Merib-baal begat Micah.
And the sons of Micah: Pithon, and Melech, and Tahrea, \add and Ahaz\add*.
And Ahaz begat Jarah; and Jarah begat Alemeth, and Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri begat Moza;
and Moza begat Binea; and Rephaiah his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
And Azel had six sons, hose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, and Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan: these ere the sons of Azel.
No the Philistines fought against Israel: and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell don slain in mount Gilboa.
And the Philistines folloed hard after Saul and after his sons; and the Philistines sle Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.
And the battle ent sore against Saul, and the archers overtook him; and he as distressed by reason of the archers.

Then said Saul unto his armor-bearer, Dra thy sord, and thrust me through thereith, lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me. But his armor-bearer ould not; for he as sore afraid. Therefore Saul took his sord, and fell upon it.
And hen his armor-bearer sa that Saul as dead, he likeise fell upon his sord, and died.
So Saul died, and his three sons; and all his house died together.
And hen all the men of Israel that ere in the valley sa that they fled, and that Saul and his sons ere dead, they forsook their cities, and fled; and the Philistines came and delt in them.
And it came to pass on the morro, hen the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his sons fallen in mount Gilboa.
And they stripped him, and took his head, and his armor, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to carry the tidings unto their idols, and to the people.
And they put his armor in the house of their gods, and fastened his head in the house of Dagon.
And hen all Jabesh-gilead heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul,
all the valiant men arose, and took aay the body of Saul, and the bodies of his sons, and brought them to Jabesh, and buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.

So Saul died for his trespass hich he committed against Jehovah, because of the ord of Jehovah, hich he kept not; and also for that he asked counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to inquire \add thereby\add*,
and inquired not of Jehovah: therefore he sle him, and turned the kingdom unto David the son of Jesse.
Then all Israel gathered themselves to David unto Hebron, saying, Behold, e are thy bone and thy flesh.

In times past, even hen Saul as king, it as thou that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and Jehovah thy God said unto thee, Thou shalt be shepherd of my people Israel, and thou shalt be prince over my people Israel.

So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and David made a covenant ith them in Hebron before Jehovah; and they anointed David king over Israel, according to the ord of Jehovah by Samuel.
And David and all Israel ent to Jerusalem ( the same is Jebus); and the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, ere there.
And the inhabitants of Jebus said to David, Thou shalt not come in hither. Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion; the same is the city of David.
And David said, Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites first shall be chief and captain. And Joab the son of Zeruiah ent up first, and as made chief.
And David delt in the stronghold; therefore they called it the city of David.
And he built the city round about, from Millo even round about; and Joab repaired the rest of the city.
And David axed greater and greater; for Jehovah of hosts as ith him.

No these are the chief of the mighty men hom David had, ho shoed themselves strong ith him in his kingdom, together ith all Israel, to make him king, according to the ord of Jehovah concerning Israel.
And this is the number of the mighty men hom David had: Jashobeam, the son of a Hachmonite, the chief of the thirty; he lifted up his spear against three hundred and sle them at one time.
And after him as Eleazar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite, ho as one of the three mighty men.
He as ith David at Pasdammim, and there the Philistines ere gathered together to battle, here as a plot of ground full of barley; and the people fled from before the Philistines.
And they stood in the midst of the plot, and defended it, and sle the Philistines; and Jehovah saved them by a great victory.
And three of the thirty chief men ent don to the rock to David, into the cave of Adullam; and the host of the Philistines ere encamped in the valley of Rephaim.
And David as then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines as then in Beth-lehem.
And David longed, and said, Oh that one ould give me ater to drink of the ell of Beth-lehem, hich is by the gate!

And the three brake through the host of the Philistines, and dre ater out of the ell of Beth-lehem, that as by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: but David ould not drink thereof, but poured it out unto Jehovah,

and said, My God forbid it me, that I should do this: shall I drink the blood of these men that have put their lives in jeopardy? for ith \add the jeopardy of\add* their lives they brought it. Therefore he ould not drink it. These things did the three mighty men.
And Abishai, the brother of Joab, he as chief of the three; for he lifted up his spear against three hundred and sle them, and had a name among the three.
Of the three, he as more honorable than the to, and as made their captain: hobeit he attained not to the \add first\add* three.

Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, ho had done mighty deeds, he sle the to \add sons of\add* Ariel of Moab: he ent don also and sle a lion in the midst of a pit in time of sno.

And he sle an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits high; and in the Egyptian’s hand as a spear like a eaver’s beam; and he ent don to him ith a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and sle him ith his on spear.
These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and had a name among the three mighty men.
Behold, he as more honorable than the thirty, but he attained not to the \add first\add* three: and David set him over his guard.
Also the mighty men of the armies: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan the son of Dodo of Beth-lehem,
Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,
Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite,
Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
Maharai the Netophathite, Heled the son of Baanah the Netophathite,
Ithai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite,
Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,
Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan the son of Shagee the Hararite,
Ahiam the son of Sacar the Hararite, Eliphal the son of Ur,
Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,
Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai the son of Ezbai,
Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the son of Hagri,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, the armorbearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite, Zabad the son of Ahlai,
Adina the son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, and thirty ith him,
Hanan the son of Maacah, and Joshaphat the Mithnite,
Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite,
Jediael the son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite,
Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai, and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite,
Eliel, and Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
No these are they that came to David to Ziklag, hile he yet kept himself close because of Saul the son of Kish; and they ere among the mighty men, his helpers in ar.
They ere armed ith bos, and could use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and in shooting arros from the bo: they ere of Saul’s brethren of Benjamin.
The chief as Ahiezer; then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite, and Jeziel, and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth, and Beracah, and Jehu the Anathothite,
and Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty, and over the thirty, and Jeremiah, and Jahaziel, and Johanan, and Jozabad the Gederathite,
Eluzai, and Jerimoth, and Bealiah, and Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite,
Elkanah, and Isshiah, and Azarel, and Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites,
and Joelah, and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.

And of the Gadites there separated themselves unto David to the stronghold in the ilderness, mighty men of valor, men trained for ar, that could handle shield and spear; hose faces ere like the faces of lions, and they ere as sift as the roes upon the mountains:
Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,
Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,
Jeremiah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh.
These of the sons of Gad ere captains of the host: he that as least as equal to a hundred, and the greatest to a thousand.
These are they that ent over the Jordan in the first month, hen it had overfloed all its banks; and they put to flight all them of the valleys, both toard the east and toard the est.
And there came of the children of Benjamin and Judah to the stronghold unto David.

And David ent out to meet them, and ansered and said unto them, If ye be come peaceably unto me to help me, my heart shall be knit unto you; but if \add ye be come\add* to betray me to mine adversaries, seeing there is no rong in my hands, the God of our fathers look thereon, and rebuke it.

Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, ho as chief of the thirty, \add and he said\add*, Thine are e, David, and on thy side, thou son of Jesse: peace, peace be unto thee, and peace be to thy helpers; for thy God helpeth thee. Then David received them, and made them captains of the band.

Of Manasseh also there fell aay some to David, hen he came ith the Philistines against Saul to battle: but they helped them not; for the lords of the Philistines upon advisement sent him aay, saying, He ill fall aay to his master Saul to the jeopardy of our heads.
As he ent to Ziklag, there fell to him of Manasseh, Adnah, and Jozabad, and Jediael, and Michael, and Jozabad, and Elihu, and Zillethai, captains of thousands that ere of Manasseh.
And they helped David against the band of rovers: for they ere all mighty men of valor, and ere captains in the host.
For from day to day men came to David to help him, until there as a great host, like the host of God.
And these are the numbers of the heads of them that ere armed for ar, ho came to David to Hebron, to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the ord of Jehovah.
The children of Judah that bare shield and spear ere six thousand and eight hundred, armed for ar.
Of the children of Simeon, mighty men of valor for the ar, seven thousand and one hundred.
Of the children of Levi four thousand and six hundred.
And Jehoiada as the leader of \add the house of\add* Aaron; and ith him ere three thousand and seven hundred,
and Zadok, a young man mighty of valor, and of his father’s house tenty and to captains.
And of the children of Benjamin, the brethren of Saul, three thousand: for hitherto the greatest part of them had kept their allegiance to the house of Saul.
And of the children of Ephraim tenty thousand and eight hundred, mighty men of valor, famous men in their fathers’ houses.
And of the half-tribe of Manasseh eighteen thousand, ho ere mentioned by name, to come and make David king.
And of the children of Issachar, men that had understanding of the times, to kno hat Israel ought to do, the heads of them ere to hundred; and all their brethren ere at their commandment.

Of Zebulun, such as ere able to go out in the host, that could set the battle in array, ith all manner of instruments of ar, fifty thousand, and that could order \add the battle array, and ere\add* not of double heart.
And of Naphtali a thousand captains, and ith them ith shield and spear thirty and seven thousand.
And of the Danites that could set the battle in array, tenty and eight thousand and six hundred.
And of Asher, such as ere able to go out in the host, that could set the battle in array, forty thousand.
And on the other side of the Jordan, of the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and of the half-tribe of Manasseh, ith all manner of instruments of ar for the battle, a hundred and tenty thousand.

All these, being men of ar, that could order the battle array, came ith a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel: and all the rest also of Israel ere of one heart to make David king.
And they ere there ith David three days, eating and drinking; for their brethren had made preparation for them.

Moreover they that ere nigh unto them, \add even\add* as far as Issachar and Zebulun and Naphtali, brought bread on asses, and on camels, and on mules, and on oxen, victuals of meal, cakes of figs, and clusters of raisins, and ine, and oil, and oxen, and sheep in abundance: for there as joy in Israel.
And David consulted ith the captains of thousands and of hundreds, even ith every leader.

And David said unto all the assembly of Israel, If it seem good unto you, and if it be of Jehovah our God, let us send abroad every here unto our brethren that are left in all the land of Israel, ith hom the priests and Levites are in their cities that have suburbs, that they may gather themselves unto us;
and let us bring again the ark of our God to us: for e sought not unto it in the days of Saul.
And all the assembly said that they ould do so; for the thing as right in the eyes of all the people.
So David assembled all Israel together, from the Shihor \add the brook\add* of Egypt even unto the entrance of Hamath, to bring the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim.

And David ent up, and all Israel, to Baalah, \add that is\add*, to Kiriath-jearim, hich belonged to Judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God Jehovah that sitteth \add above\add* the cherubim, that is called by the Name.
And they carried the ark of God upon a ne cart, \add and brought it\add* out of the house of Abinadab: and Uzza and Ahio drove the cart.
And David and all Israel played before God ith all their might, even ith songs, and ith harps, and ith psalteries, and ith timbrels, and ith cymbals, and ith trumpets.
And hen they came unto the threshing-floor of Chidon, Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen stumbled.
And the anger of Jehovah as kindled against Uzza, and he smote him, because he put forth his hand to the ark; and there he died before God.
And David as displeased, because Jehovah had broken forth upon Uzza: and he called that place Perez-uzza, unto this day.
And David as afraid of God that day, saying, Ho shall I bring the ark of God home to me?
So David removed not the ark unto him into the city of David, but carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
And the ark of God remained ith the family of Obed-edom in his house three months: and Jehovah blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that he had.
And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar-trees, and masons, and carpenters, to build him a house.
And David perceived that Jehovah had established him king over Israel; for his kingdom as exalted on high, for his people Israel’s sake.
And David took more ives at Jerusalem; and David begat more sons and daughters.
And these are the names of the children hom he had in Jerusalem: Shammua, and Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon,
and Ibhar, and Elishua, and Elpelet,
and Nogah, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
and Elishama, and Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
And hen the Philistines heard that David as anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines ent up to seek David: and David heard of it, and ent out against them.
No the Philistines had come and made a raid in the valley of Rephaim.
And David inquired of God, saying, Shall I go up against the Philistines? and ilt thou deliver them into my hand? And Jehovah said unto him, Go up; for I ill deliver them into thy hand.

So they came up to Baal-perazim, and David smote them there; and David said, God hath broken mine enemies by my hand, like the breach of aters. Therefore they called the name of that place Baal-perazim.
And they left their gods there; and David gave commandment, and they ere burned ith fire.
And the Philistines yet again made a raid in the valley.
And David inquired again of God; and God said unto him, Thou shalt not go up after them: turn aay from them, and come upon them over against the mulberry-trees.
And it shall be, hen thou hearest the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry-trees, that then thou shalt go out to battle; for God is gone out before thee to smite the host of the Philistines.
And David did as God commanded him: and they smote the host of the Philistines from Gibeon even to Gezer.
And the fame of David ent out into all lands; and Jehovah brought the fear of him upon all nations.
And \add David\add* made him houses in the city of David; and he prepared a place for the ark of God, and pitched for it a tent.
Then David said, None ought to carry the ark of God but the Levites: for them hath Jehovah chosen to carry the ark of God, and to minister unto him for ever.
And David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of Jehovah unto its place, hich he had prepared for it.
And David gathered together the sons of Aaron, and the Levites:
of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief, and his brethren a hundred and tenty;
of the sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief, and his brethren to hundred and tenty;
of the sons of Gershom, Joel the chief, and his brethren a hundred and thirty;
of the sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, and his brethren to hundred;
of the sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief, and his brethren fourscore;
of the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, and his brethren a hundred and telve.
And David called for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites, for Uriel, Asaiah, and Joel, Shemaiah, and Eliel, and Amminadab,

and said unto them, Ye are the heads of the fathers’ \add houses\add* of the Levites: sanctify yourselves, both ye and your brethren, that ye may bring up the ark of Jehovah, the God of Israel, unto \add the place\add* that I have prepared for it.
For because ye \add bare it\add* not at the first, Jehovah our God made a breach upon us, for that e sought him not according to the ordinance.
So the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of Jehovah, the God of Israel.
And the children of the Levites bare the ark of God upon their shoulders ith the staves thereon, as Moses commanded according to the ord of Jehovah.
And David spake to the chief of the Levites to appoint their brethren the singers, ith instruments of music, psalteries and harps and cymbals, sounding aloud and lifting up the voice ith joy.
So the Levites appointed Heman the son of Joel; and of his brethren, Asaph the son of Berechiah; and of the sons of Merari their brethren, Ethan the son of Kushaiah;

and ith them their brethren of the second degree, Zechariah, Ben, and Jaaziel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Unni, Eliab, and Benaiah, and Maaseiah, and Mattithiah, and Eliphelehu, and Mikneiah, and Obed-edom, and Jeiel, the doorkeepers.
So the singers, Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, \add ere appointed\add*, ith cymbals of brass to sound aloud;
and Zechariah, and Aziel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Unni, and Eliab, and Maaseiah, and Benaiah, ith psalteries set to Alamoth;
and Mattithiah, and Eliphelehu, and Mikneiah, and Obed-edom, and Jeiel, and Azaziah, ith harps set to the Sheminith, to lead.
And Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, as over the song: he instructed about the song, because he as skilful.
And Berechiah and Elkanah ere doorkeepers for the ark.

And Shebaniah, and Joshaphat, and Nethanel, and Amasai, and Zechariah, and Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, did blo the trumpets before the ark of God; and Obed-edom and Jehiah ere doorkeepers for the ark.
So David, and the elders of Israel, and the captains over thousands, ent to bring up the ark of the covenant of Jehovah out of the house of Obed-edom ith joy.
And it came to pass, hen God helped the Levites that bare the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, that they sacrificed seven bullocks and seven rams.

And David as clothed ith a robe of fine linen, and all the Levites that bare the ark, and the singers, and Chenaniah the master of the song \add ith\add* the singers: and David had upon him an ephod of linen.
Thus all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of Jehovah ith shouting, and ith sound of the cornet, and ith trumpets, and ith cymbals, sounding aloud ith psalteries and harps.

And it came to pass, as the ark of the covenant of Jehovah came to the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the indo, and sa king David dancing and playing; and she despised him in her heart.
And they brought in the ark of God, and set it in the midst of the tent that David had pitched for it: and they offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings before God.
And hen David had made an end of offering the burnt-offering and the peace-offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Jehovah.
And he dealt to every one of Israel, both man and oman, to every one a loaf of bread, and a portion \add of flesh\add*, and a cake of raisins.
And he appointed certain of the Levites to minister before the ark of Jehovah, and to celebrate and to thank and praise Jehovah, the God of Israel:

Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, Jeiel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehiel, and Mattithiah, and Eliab, and Benaiah, and Obed-edom, and Jeiel, ith psalteries and ith harps; and Asaph ith cymbals, sounding aloud;
and Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests ith trumpets continually, before the ark of the covenant of God.
Then on that day did David first ordain to give thanks unto Jehovah, by the hand of Asaph and his brethren.
O give thanks unto Jehovah, call upon his name; Make knon his doings among the peoples.
Sing unto him, sing praises unto him; Talk ye of all his marvellous orks.
Glory ye in his holy name; Let the heart of them rejoice that seek Jehovah.
Seek ye Jehovah and his strength; Seek his face evermore.
Remember his marvellous orks that he hath done, His onders, and the judgments of his mouth,
O ye seed of Israel his servant, Ye children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is Jehovah our God; His judgments are in all the earth.
Remember his covenant for ever, The ord hich he commanded to a thousand generations,
\add The covenant\add* hich he made ith Abraham, And his oath unto Isaac,
And confirmed the same unto Jacob for a statute, To Israel for an everlasting covenant,
Saying, Unto thee ill I give the land of Canaan, The lot of your inheritance;
When ye ere but a fe men in number, Yea, very fe, and sojourners in it;
And they ent about from nation to nation, And from one kingdom to another people.
He suffered no man to do them rong; Yea, he reproved kings for their sakes,
\add Saying\add*, Touch not mine anointed ones, And do my prophets no harm.
Sing unto Jehovah, all the earth; Sho forth his salvation from day to day.
Declare his glory among the nations, His marvellous orks among all the peoples.
For great is Jehovah, and greatly to be praised: He also is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols: But Jehovah made the heavens.
Honor and majesty are before him: Strength and gladness are in his place.
Ascribe unto Jehovah, ye kindreds of the peoples, Ascribe unto Jehovah glory and strength;
Ascribe unto Jehovah the glory due unto his name: Bring an offering, and come before him; Worship Jehovah in holy array.
Tremble before him, all the earth: The orld also is established that it cannot be moved.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice; And let them say among the nations, Jehovah reigneth.
Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof; Let the field exult, and all that is therein;
Then shall the trees of the ood sing for joy before Jehovah; For he cometh to judge the earth.
O give thanks unto Jehovah; for he is good; For his lovingkindness \add endureth\add* for ever.
And say ye, Save us, O God of our salvation, And gather us together and deliver us from the nations, To give thanks unto thy holy name, And to triumph in thy praise.
Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, From everlasting even to everlasting.
So he left there, before the ark of the covenant of Jehovah, Asaph and his brethren, to minister before the ark continually, as every day’s ork required;
and Obed-edom ith their brethren, threescore and eight; Obed-edom also the son of Jeduthun and Hosah to be doorkeepers;
and Zadok the priest, and his brethren the priests, before the tabernacle of Jehovah in the high place that as at Gibeon,
to offer burnt-offerings unto Jehovah upon the altar of burnt-offering continually morning and evening, even according to all that is ritten in the la of Jehovah, hich he commanded unto Israel;
and ith them Heman and Jeduthun, and the rest that ere chosen, ho ere mentioned by name, to give thanks to Jehovah, because his lovingkindness \add endureth\add* for ever;
and ith them Heman and Jeduthun \add ith\add* trumpets and cymbals for those that should sound aloud, and \add ith\add* instruments for the songs of God; and the sons of Jeduthun to be at the gate.
And all the people departed every man to his house: and David returned to bless his house.
And it came to pass, hen David delt in his house, that David said to Nathan the prophet, Lo, I dell in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of Jehovah \add delleth\add* under curtains.
And Nathan said unto David, Do all that is in thy heart; for God is ith thee.
And it came to pass the same night, that the ord of God came to Nathan, saying,
Go and tell David my servant, Thus saith Jehovah, Thou shalt not build me a house to dell in:
for I have not delt in a house since the day that I brought up Israel, unto this day, but have gone from tent to tent, and from \add one\add* tabernacle \add to another\add*.
In all places herein I have alked ith all Israel, spake I a ord ith any of the judges of Israel, hom I commanded to be shepherd of my people, saying, Why have ye not built me a house of cedar?
No therefore thus shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from folloing the sheep, that thou shouldest be prince over my people Israel:
and I have been ith thee hithersoever thou hast gone, and have cut off all thine enemies from before thee; and I ill make thee a name, like unto the name of the great ones that are in the earth.

And I ill appoint a place for my people Israel, and ill plant them, that they may dell in their on place, and be moved no more; neither shall the children of ickedness aste them any more, as at the first,
and \add as\add* from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel; and I ill subdue all thine enemies. Moreover I tell thee that Jehovah ill build thee a house.
And it shall come to pass, hen thy days are fulfilled that thou must go to be ith thy fathers, that I ill set up thy seed after thee, ho shall be of thy sons; and I ill establish his kingdom.
He shall build me a house, and I ill establish his throne for ever.
I ill be his father, and he shall be my son: and I ill not take my lovingkindness aay from him, as I took it from him that as before thee;
but I ill settle him in my house and in my kingdom for ever; and his throne shall be established for ever.
According to all these ords, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak unto David.
Then David the king ent in, and sat before Jehovah; and he said, Who am I, O Jehovah God, and hat is my house, that thou hast brought me thus far?

And this as a small thing in thine eyes, O God; but thou hast spoken of thy servant’s house for a great hile to come, and hast regarded me according to the estate of a man of high degree, O Jehovah God.
What can David \add say\add* yet more unto thee concerning the honor hich is done to thy servant? for thou knoest thy servant.
O Jehovah, for thy servant’s sake, and according to thine on heart, hast thou rought all this greatness, to make knon all \add these\add* great things.
O Jehovah, there is none like thee, neither is there any God besides thee, according to all that e have heard ith our ears.

And hat one nation in the earth is like thy people Israel, hom God ent to redeem unto himself for a people, to make thee a name by great and terrible things, in driving out nations from before thy people, hom thou redeemedst out of Egypt?
For thy people Israel didst thou make thine on people for ever; and thou, Jehovah, becamest their God.
And no, O Jehovah, let the ord that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, be established for ever, and do as thou hast spoken.
And let thy name be established and magnified for ever, saying, Jehovah of hosts is the God of Israel, even a God to Israel: and the house of David thy servant is established before thee.
For thou, O my God, hast revealed to thy servant that thou ilt build him a house: therefore hath thy servant found \add in his heart\add* to pray before thee.
And no, O Jehovah, thou art God, and hast promised this good thing unto thy servant:
and no it hath pleased thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee: for thou, O Jehovah, hast blessed, and it is blessed for ever.
And after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them, and took Gath and its tons out of the hand of the Philistines.
And he smote Moab; and the Moabites became servants to David, and brought tribute.
And David smote Hadarezer king of Zobah unto Hamath, as he ent to establish his dominion by the river Euphrates.
And David took from him a thousand chariots, and seven thousand horsemen, and tenty thousand footmen; and David hocked all the chariot horses, but reserved of them for a hundred chariots.
And hen the Syrians of Damascus came to succor Hadarezer king of Zobah, David smote of the Syrians to and tenty thousand men.
Then David put \add garrisons\add* in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians became servants to David, and brought tribute. And Jehovah gave victory to David hithersoever he ent.
And David took the shields of gold that ere on the servants of Hadarezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
And from Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadarezer, David took very much brass, hereith Solomon made the brazen sea, and the pillars, and the vessels of brass.
And hen Tou king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadarezer king of Zobah,

he sent Hadoram his son to king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadarezer and smitten him ( for Hadarezer had ars ith Tou); and \add he had ith him\add* all manner of vessels of gold and silver and brass.

These also did king David dedicate unto Jehovah, ith the silver and the gold that he carried aay from all the nations; from Edom, and from Moab, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines, and from Amalek.
Moreover Abishai the son of Zeruiah smote of the Edomites in the Valley of Salt eighteen thousand.
And he put garrisons in Edom; and all the Edomites became servants to David. And Jehovah gave victory to David hithersoever he ent.
And David reigned over all Israel; and he executed justice and righteousness unto all his people.
And Joab the son of Zeruiah as over the host; and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud as recorder;
and Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abimelech the son of Abiathar, ere priests; and Shavsha as scribe;
and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada as over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David ere chief about the king.
And it came to pass after this, that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon died, and his son reigned in his stead.

And David said, I ill sho kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, because his father shoed kindness to me. So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. And David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon to Hanun, to comfort him.

But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun, Thinkest thou that David doth honor thy father, in that he hath sent comforters unto thee? are not his servants come unto thee to search, and to overthro, and to spy out the land?
So Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved them, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them aay.

Then there ent certain persons, and told David ho the men ere served. And he sent to meet them; for the men ere greatly ashamed. And the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards be gron, and then return.

And hen the children of Ammon sa that they had made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the children of Ammon sent a thousand talents of silver to hire them chariots and horsemen out of Mesopotamia, and out of Aram-maacah, and out of Zobah.

So they hired them thirty and to thousand chariots, and the king of Maacah and his people, ho came and encamped before Medeba. And the children of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities, and came to battle.
And hen David heard of it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.
And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the gate of the city: and the kings that ere come ere by themselves in the field.
No hen Joab sa that the battle as set against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel, and put them in array against the Syrians.
And the rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and they put themselves in array against the children of Ammon.
And he said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me; but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I ill help thee.
Be of good courage, and let us play the man for our people, and for the cities of our God: and Jehovah do that hich seemeth him good.
So Joab and the people that ere ith him dre nigh before the Syrians unto the battle; and they fled before him.
And hen the children of Ammon sa that the Syrians ere fled, they likeise fled before Abishai his brother, and entered into the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.

And hen the Syrians sa that they ere put to the orse before Israel, they sent messengers, and dre forth the Syrians that ere beyond the River, ith Shophach the captain of the host of Hadarezer at their head.

And it as told David; and he gathered all Israel together, and passed over the Jordan, and came upon them, and set the battle in array against them. So hen David had put the battle in array against the Syrians, they fought ith him.
And the Syrians fled before Israel; and David sle of the Syrians \add the men of\add* seven thousand chariots, and forty thousand footmen, and killed Shophach the captain of the host.
And hen the servants of Hadarezer sa that they ere put to the orse before Israel, they made peace ith David, and served him: neither ould the Syrians help the children of Ammon any more.

And it came to pass, at the time of the return of the year, at the time hen kings go out \add to battle\add*, that Joab led forth the army, and asted the country of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried at Jerusalem. And Joab smote Rabbah, and overthre it.

And David took the cron of their king from off his head, and found it to eigh a talent of gold, and there ere precious stones in it; and it as set upon David’s head: and he brought forth the spoil of the city, exceeding much.

And he brought forth the people that ere therein, and cut \add them\add* ith sas, and ith harros of iron, and ith axes. And thus did David unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. And David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
And it came to pass after this, that there arose ar at Gezer ith the Philistines: then Sibbecai the Hushathite sle Sippai, of the sons of the giant; and they ere subdued.
And there as again ar ith the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Jair sle Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of hose spear as like a eaver’s beam.

And there as again ar at Gath, here as a man of great stature, hose fingers and toes ere four and tenty, six \add on each hand\add*, and six \add on each foot\add*; and he also as born unto the giant.
And hen he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea David’s brother sle him.
These ere born unto the giant in Gath; and they fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
And Satan stood up against Israel, and moved David to number Israel.
And David said to Joab and to the princes of the people, Go, number Israel from Beer-sheba even to Dan; and bring me ord, that I may kno the sum of them.

And Joab said, Jehovah make his people a hundred times as many as they are: but, my lord the king, are they not all my lord’s servants? hy doth my lord require this thing? hy ill he be a cause of guilt unto Israel?
Nevertheless the king’s ord prevailed against Joab. Wherefore Joab departed, and ent throughout all Israel, and came to Jerusalem.

And Joab gave up the sum of the numbering of the people unto David. And all they of Israel ere a thousand thousand and a hundred thousand men that dre sord: and Judah as four hundred threescore and ten thousand men that dre sord.
But Levi and Benjamin counted he not among them; for the king’s ord as abominable to Joab.
And God as displeased ith this thing; therefore he smote Israel.
And David said unto God, I have sinned greatly, in that I have done this thing: but no, put aay, I beseech thee, the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.
And Jehovah spake unto Gad, David’s seer, saying,
Go and speak unto David, saying, Thus saith Jehovah, I offer thee three things: choose thee one of them, that I may do it unto thee.
So Gad came to David, and said unto him, Thus saith Jehovah, Take hich thou ilt:

either three years of famine; or three months to be consumed before thy foes, hile the sord of thine enemies overtaketh thee; or else three days the sord of Jehovah, even pestilence in the land, and the angel of Jehovah destroying throughout all the borders of Israel. No therefore consider hat anser I shall return to him that sent me.
And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let me fall, I pray, into the hand of Jehovah; for very great are his mercies: and let me not fall into the hand of man.
So Jehovah sent a pestilence upon Israel; and there fell of Israel seventy thousand men.

And God sent an angel unto Jerusalem to destroy it: and as he as about to destroy, Jehovah beheld, and he repented him of the evil, and said to the destroying angel, It is enough; no stay thy hand. And the angel of Jehovah as standing by the threshing-floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

And David lifted up his eyes, and sa the angel of Jehovah standing beteen earth and heaven, having a dran sord in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell upon their faces.

And David said unto God, Is it not I that commanded the people to be numbered? even I it is that have sinned and done very ickedly; but these sheep, hat have they done? let thy hand, I pray thee, O Jehovah my God, be against me, and against my father’s house; but not against thy people, that they should be plagued.
Then the angel of Jehovah commanded Gad to say to David, that David should go up, and rear an altar unto Jehovah in the threshing-floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
And David ent up at the saying of Gad, hich he spake in the name of Jehovah.
And Ornan turned back, and sa the angel; and his four sons that ere ith him hid themselves. No Ornan as threshing heat.
And as David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and sa David, and ent out of the threshing-floor, and boed himself to David ith his face to the ground.

Then David said to Ornan, Give me the place of this threshing-floor, that I may build thereon an altar unto Jehovah: for the full price shalt thou give it me, that the plague may be stayed from the people.

And Ornan said unto David, Take it to thee, and let my lord the king do that hich is good in his eyes: lo, I give \add thee\add* the oxen for burnt-offerings, and the threshing instruments for ood, and the heat for the meal-offering; I give it all.
And king David said to Ornan, Nay; but I ill verily buy it for the full price: for I ill not take that hich is thine for Jehovah, nor offer a burnt-offering ithout cost.

In those days also sa I the Jes that had married omen of Ashdod, of Ammon, \add and\add* of Moab:
