Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations as there no king like him, and he as beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did foreign omen cause to sin.
Shall e then hearken unto you to do all this great evil, to trespass against our God in marrying foreign omen?
And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, as son-in-la to Sanballat the Horonite: therefore I chased him from me.
Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites.
Thus cleansed I them from all foreigners, and appointed charges for the priests and for the Levites, every one in his ork;
and for the ood-offering, at times appointed, and for the first-fruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.
No it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus ( this is Ahasuerus ho reigned from India even unto Ethiopia, over a hundred and seven and tenty provinces),
that in those days, hen the king Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom, hich as in Shushan the palace,

What shall e do unto the queen Vashti according to la, because she hath not done the bidding of the king Ahasuerus by the chamberlains?

And Memucan ansered before the king and the princes, Vashti the queen hath not done rong to the king only, but also to all the princes, and to all the peoples that are in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus.

For this deed of the queen ill come abroad unto all omen, to make their husbands contemptible in their eyes, hen it shall be reported, The king Ahasuerus commanded Vashti the queen to be brought in before him, but she came not.
And this day ill the princesses of Persia and Media ho have heard of the deed of the queen say \add the like\add* unto all the king’s princes. So \add ill there arise\add* much contempt and rath.

If it please the king, let there go forth a royal commandment from him, and let it be ritten among the las of the Persians and the Medes, that it be not altered, that Vashti come no more before king Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal estate unto another that is better than she.
And hen the king’s decree hich he shall make shall be published throughout all his kingdom ( for it is great), all the ives ill give to their husbands honor, both to great and small.
And the saying pleased the king and the princes; and the king did according to the ord of Memucan:

for he sent letters into all the king’s provinces, into every province according to the riting thereof, and to every people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his on house, and should speak according to the language of his people.

Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king:

and let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the omen, unto the custody of Hegai the king’s chamberlain, keeper of the omen; and let their things for purification be given them;
and let the maiden that pleaseth the king be queen instead of Vashti. And the thing pleased the king; and he did so.
There as a certain Je in Shushan the palace, hose name as Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite,
ho had been carried aay from Jerusalem ith the captives that had been carried aay ith Jeconiah king of Judah, hom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried aay.

And he brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maiden as fair and beautiful; and hen her father and mother ere dead, Mordecai took her for his on daughter.

So it came to pass, hen the king’s commandment and his decree as heard, and hen many maidens ere gathered together unto Shushan the palace, to the custody of Hegai, that Esther as taken into the king’s house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the omen.

And the maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindness of him; and he speedily gave her her things for purification, ith her portions, and the seven maidens ho ere meet to be given her out of the king’s house: and he removed her and her maidens to the best place of the house of the omen.
Esther had not made knon her people nor her kindred; for Mordecai had charged her that she should not make it knon.
And Mordecai alked every day before the court of the omen’s house, to kno ho Esther did, and hat ould become of her.

No hen the turn of every maiden as come to go in to king Ahasuerus, after that it had been done to her according to the la for the omen telve months ( for so ere the days of their purifications accomplished, \add to it\add*, six months ith oil of myrrh, and six months ith seet odors and ith the things for the purifying of the omen),
then in this ise came the maiden unto the king: Whatsoever she desired as given her to go ith her out of the house of the omen unto the king’s house.

In the evening she ent, and on the morro she returned into the second house of the omen, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s chamberlain, ho kept the concubines: she came in unto the king no more, except the king delighted in her, and she ere called by name.

And the king loved Esther above all the omen, and she obtained favor and kindness in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal cron upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.
Then the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his servants, even Esther’s feast; and he made a release to the provinces, and gave gifts, according to the bounty of the king.
And hen the virgins ere gathered together the second time, then Mordecai as sitting in the king’s gate.
Esther had not yet made knon her kindred nor her people; as Mordecai had charged her: for Esther did the commandment of Mordecai, like as hen she as brought up ith him.

In those days, hile Mordecai as sitting in the king’s gate, to of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those that kept the threshold, ere roth, and sought to lay hands on the king Ahasuerus.
And the thing became knon to Mordecai, ho shoed it unto Esther the queen; and Esther told the king \add thereof\add* in Mordecai’s name.
And hen inquisition as made of the matter, and it as found to be so, they ere both hanged on a tree: and it as ritten in the book of the chronicles before the king.
After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that ere ith him.
And all the king’s servants, that ere in the king’s gate, boed don, and did reverence to Haman; for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai boed not don, nor did him reverence.
Then the king’s servants, that ere in the king’s gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king’s commandment?
No it came to pass, hen they spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see hether Mordecai’s matters ould stand: for he had told them that he as a Je.
And hen Haman sa that Mordecai boed not don, nor did him reverence, then as Haman full of rath.

But he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had made knon to him the people of Mordecai: herefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jes that ere throughout the hole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even the people of Mordecai.

In the first month, hich is the month Nisan, in the telfth year of king Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, \add to\add* the telfth \add month\add*, hich is the month Adar.

And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their las are diverse from \add those of\add* every people; neither keep they the king’s las: therefore it is not for the king’s profit to suffer them.

If it please the king, let it be ritten that they be destroyed: and I ill pay ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those that have the charge of the \add king’s\add* business, to bring it into the king’s treasuries.
And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it unto Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jes’ enemy.
And the king said unto Haman, The silver is given to thee, the people also, to do ith them as it seemeth good to thee.

Then ere the king’s scribes called in the first month, on the thirteenth day thereof; and there as ritten according to all that Haman commanded unto the king’s satraps, and to the governors that ere over every province, and to the princes of every people, to every province according to the riting thereof, and to every people after their language; in the name of king Ahasuerus as it ritten, and it as sealed ith the king’s ring.

A copy of the riting, that the decree should be given out in every province, as published unto all the peoples, that they should be ready against that day.
The posts ent forth in haste by the king’s commandment, and the decree as given out in Shushan the palace. And the king and Haman sat don to drink; but the city of Shushan as perplexed.
No hen Mordecai kne all that as done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth ith ashes, and ent out into the midst of the city, and cried ith a loud and a bitter cry;
and he came even before the king’s gate: for none might enter ithin the king’s gate clothed ith sackcloth.

And Esther’s maidens and her chamberlains came and told it her; and the queen as exceedingly grieved: and she sent raiment to clothe Mordecai, and to take his sackcloth from off him; but he received it not.

Then Esther bade them return anser unto Mordecai,

\add This as done\add* on the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of the same they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

But the Jes that ere in Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth \add day\add* thereof, and on the fourteenth thereof; and on the fifteenth \add day\add* of the same they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

And Mordecai rote these things, and sent letters unto all the Jes that ere in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, both nigh and far,
to enjoin them that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly,

as the days herein the Jes had rest from their enemies, and the month hich as turned unto them from sorro to gladness, and from mourning into a good day; that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.

He uncovereth deep things out of darkness, And bringeth out to light the shado of death.
He increaseth the nations, and he destroyeth them: He enlargeth the nations, and he leadeth them captive.
He taketh aay understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth, And causeth them to ander in a ilderness here there is no ay.
They grope in the dark ithout light; And he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man. \b
Lo, mine eye hath seen all \add this\add*, Mine ear hath heard and understood it.
What ye kno, \add the same\add* do I kno also: I am not inferior unto you. \b
Surely I ould speak to the Almighty, And I desire to reason ith God.
But ye are forgers of lies; Ye are all physicians of no value.
Oh that ye ould altogether hold your peace! And it ould be your isdom.
Hear no my reasoning, And hearken to the pleadings of my lips.
Will ye speak unrighteously for God, And talk deceitfully for him?
Will ye sho partiality to him? Will ye contend for God?
Is it good that he should search you out? Or as one deceiveth a man, ill ye deceive him?
He ill surely reprove you, If ye do secretly sho partiality.
Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his dread fall upon you?
Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defences are defences of clay. \b
Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak; And let come on me hat ill.
Wherefore should I take my flesh in my teeth, And put my life in my hand?
Behold, he ill slay me; I have no hope: Nevertheless I ill maintain my ays before him.
This also shall be my salvation, That a godless man shall not come before him.
Hear diligently my speech, And let my declaration be in your ears.
Behold no, I have set my cause in order; I kno that I am righteous.
Who is he that ill contend ith me? For then ould I hold my peace and give up the ghost. \b
Only do not to things unto me; Then ill I not hide myself from thy face:
Withdra thy hand far from me; And let not thy terror make me afraid.
Then call thou, and I ill anser; Or let me speak, and anser thou me.
Ho many are mine iniquities and sins? Make me to kno my transgression and my sin.
Wherefore hidest thou thy face, And holdest me for thine enemy?
Wilt thou harass a driven leaf? And ilt thou pursue the dry stubble?
For thou ritest bitter things against me, And makest me to inherit the iniquities of my youth:
Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, And markest all my paths; Thou settest a bound to the soles of my feet:
Though I am like a rotten thing that consumeth, Like a garment that is moth-eaten. \b
Man, that is born of a oman, Is of fe days, and full of trouble.
He cometh forth like a floer, and is cut don: He fleeth also as a shado, and continueth not.
And dost thou open thine eyes upon such a one, And bringest me into judgment ith thee?
Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean? not one.
Seeing his days are determined, The number of his months is ith thee, And thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;
Look aay from him, that he may rest, Till he shall accomplish, as a hireling, his day. \b
For there is hope of a tree, If it be cut don, that it ill sprout again, And that the tender branch thereof ill not cease.
Though the root thereof ax old in the earth, And the stock thereof die in the ground;
Yet through the scent of ater it ill bud, And put forth boughs like a plant.
But man dieth, and is laid lo: Yea, man giveth up the ghost, and here is he?
\add As\add* the aters fail from the sea, And the river asteth and drieth up;
So man lieth don and riseth not: Till the heavens be no more, they shall not aake, Nor be roused out of their sleep. \b
Oh that thou ouldest hide me in Sheol, That thou ouldest keep me secret, until thy rath be past, That thou ouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!
If a man die, shall he live \add again\add*? All the days of my arfare ould I ait, Till my release should come.
Thou ouldest call, and I ould anser thee: Thou ouldest have a desire to the ork of thy hands.
But no thou numberest my steps: Dost thou not atch over my sin?
My transgression is sealed up in a bag, And thou fastenest up mine iniquity. \b
But the mountain falling cometh to nought; And the rock is removed out of its place;
The aters ear the stones; The overfloings thereof ash aay the dust of the earth: So thou destroyest the hope of man.
Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth; Thou changest his countenance, and sendest him aay.
His sons come to honor, and he knoeth it not; And they are brought lo, but he perceiveth it not of them.
But his flesh upon him hath pain, And his soul ithin him mourneth. \b
Then ansered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
Should a ise man make anser ith vain knoledge, And fill himself ith the east ind?
Should he reason ith unprofitable talk, Or ith speeches hereith he can do no good?
Yea, thou doest aay ith fear, And hinderest devotion before God.
For thine iniquity teacheth thy mouth, And thou choosest the tongue of the crafty.
Thine on mouth condemneth thee, and not I; Yea, thine on lips testify against thee. \b
Art thou the first man that as born? Or ast thou brought forth before the hills?
Hast thou heard the secret counsel of God? And dost thou limit isdom to thyself?
What knoest thou, that e kno not? What understandest thou, hich is not in us?
With us are both the gray-headed and the very aged men, Much elder than thy father.
Are the consolations of God too small for thee, Even the ord that is gentle toard thee?
Why doth thy heart carry thee aay? And hy do thine eyes flash,
That against God thou turnest thy spirit, And lettest ords go out of thy mouth?
What is man, that he should be clean? And he that is born of a oman, that he should be righteous?
Behold, he putteth no trust in his holy ones; Yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight:
Ho much less one that is abominable and corrupt, A man that drinketh iniquity like ater! \b
I ill sho thee, hear thou me; And that hich I have seen I ill declare
(Which ise men have told From their fathers, and have not hid it;
Unto hom alone the land as given, And no stranger passed among them):
The icked man travaileth ith pain all his days, Even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor.
A sound of terrors is in his ears; In prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him.
He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, And he is aited for of the sord.
He andereth abroad for bread, \add saying\add*, Where is it? He knoeth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
Distress and anguish make him afraid; They prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
Because he hath stretched out his hand against God, And behaveth himself proudly against the Almighty;
He runneth upon him ith a \add stiff\add* neck, With the thick bosses of his bucklers;
Because he hath covered his face ith his fatness, And gathered fat upon his loins;
And he hath delt in desolate cities, In houses hich no man inhabited, Which ere ready to become heaps;
He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, Neither shall their possessions be extended on the earth.
He shall not depart out of darkness; The flame shall dry up his branches, And by the breath of \add God’s\add* mouth shall he go aay.
Let him not trust in vanity, deceiving himself; For vanity shall be his recompense.
It shall be accomplished before his time, And his branch shall not be green.
He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, And shall cast off his floer as the olive-tree.
For the company of the godless shall be barren, And fire shall consume the tents of bribery.
They conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity, And their heart prepareth deceit. \b
Then Job ansered and said,
I have heard many such things: Miserable comforters are ye all.
Shall vain ords have an end? Or hat provoketh thee that thou anserest?
I also could speak as ye do; If your soul ere in my soul’s stead, I could join ords together against you, And shake my head at you.
\add But\add* I ould strengthen you ith my mouth, And the solace of my lips ould assuage \add your grief\add*. \b
Though I speak, my grief is not assuaged; And though I forbear, hat am I eased?
But no he hath made me eary: Thou hast made desolate all my company.
And thou hast laid fast hold on me, \add hich\add* is a itness \add against me\add*: And my leanness riseth up against me, It testifieth to my face.
He hath torn me in his rath, and persecuted me; He hath gnashed upon me ith his teeth: Mine adversary sharpeneth his eyes upon me.
They have gaped upon me ith their mouth; They have smitten me upon the cheek reproachfully: They gather themselves together against me.
God delivereth me to the ungodly, And casteth me into the hands of the icked.
I as at ease, and he brake me asunder; Yea, he hath taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces: He hath also set me up for his mark.
His archers compass me round about; He cleaveth my reins asunder, and doth not spare; He poureth out my gall upon the ground.
He breaketh me ith breach upon breach; He runneth upon me like a giant.
I have seed sackcloth upon my skin, And have laid my horn in the dust.
My face is red ith eeping, And on my eyelids is the shado of death;
Although there is no violence in my hands, And my prayer is pure. \b
O earth, cover not thou my blood, And let my cry have no \add resting\add*-place.
Even no, behold, my itness is in heaven, And he that voucheth for me is on high.
My friends scoff at me: \add But\add* mine eye poureth out tears unto God,
That he ould maintain the right of a man ith God, And of a son of man ith his neighbor!
For hen a fe years are come, I shall go the ay hence I shall not return.
My spirit is consumed, my days are extinct, The grave is \add ready\add* for me.
Surely there are mockers ith me, And mine eye delleth upon their provocation. \b
Give no a pledge, be surety for me ith thyself; Who is there that ill strike hands ith me?
For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: Therefore shalt thou not exalt \add them\add*.
He that denounceth his friends for a prey, Even the eyes of his children shall fail. \b
But he hath made me a byord of the people; And they spit in my face.
Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorro, And all my members are as a shado.
Upright men shall be astonished at this, And the innocent shall stir up himself against the godless.
Yet shall the righteous hold on his ay, And he that hath clean hands shall ax stronger and stronger.
But as for you all, come on no again; And I shall not find a ise man among you.
My days are past, my purposes are broken off, Even the thoughts of my heart.
They change the night into day: The light, \add say they\add*, is near unto the darkness.
If I look for Sheol as my house; If I have spread my couch in the darkness;
If I have said to corruption, Thou art my father; To the orm, \add Thou art\add* my mother, and my sister;
Where then is my hope? And as for my hope, ho shall see it?
It shall go don to the bars of Sheol, When once there is rest in the dust. \b
Then ansered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
Ho long ill ye hunt for ords? Consider, and afterards e ill speak.
Wherefore are e counted as beasts, \add And\add* are become unclean in your sight?
Thou that tearest thyself in thine anger, Shall the earth be forsaken for thee? Or shall the rock be removed out of its place? \b
Yea, the light of the icked shall be put out, And the spark of his fire shall not shine.
The light shall be dark in his tent, And his lamp above him shall be put out.
The steps of his strength shall be straitened, And his on counsel shall cast him don.
For he is cast into a net by his on feet, And he alketh upon the toils.
A gin shall take \add him\add* by the heel, \add And\add* a snare shall lay hold on him.
A noose is hid for him in the ground, And a trap for him in the ay.
Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, And shall chase him at his heels.
His strength shall be hunger-bitten, And calamity shall be ready at his side.
The members of his body shall be devoured, \add Yea\add*, the first-born of death shall devour his members.
He shall be rooted out of his tent herein he trusteth; And he shall be brought to the king of terrors.
There shall dell in his tent that hich is none of his: Brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.
His roots shall be dried up beneath, And above shall his branch be cut off.
His remembrance shall perish from the earth, And he shall have no name in the street.
He shall be driven from light into darkness, And chased out of the orld.
He shall have neither son nor son’s son among his people, Nor any remaining here he sojourned.
They that come after shall be astonished at his day, As they that ent before ere affrighted.
Surely such are the dellings of the unrighteous, And this is the place of him that knoeth not God. \b
Then Job ansered and said,
Ho long ill ye vex my soul, And break me in pieces ith ords?
These ten times have ye reproached me: Ye are not ashamed that ye deal hardly ith me.
And be it indeed that I have erred, Mine error remaineth ith myself.
If indeed ye ill magnify yourselves against me, And plead against me my reproach;
Kno no that God hath subverted me \add in my cause\add*, And hath compassed me ith his net. \b
Behold, I cry out of rong, but I am not heard: I cry for help, but there is no justice.
He hath alled up my ay that I cannot pass, And hath set darkness in my paths.
He hath stripped me of my glory, And taken the cron from my head.
He hath broken me don on every side, and I am gone; And my hope hath he plucked up like a tree.
He hath also kindled his rath against me, And he counteth me unto him as \add one of\add* his adversaries.
His troops come on together, And cast up their ay against me, And encamp round about my tent. \b
He hath put my brethren far from me, And mine acquaintance are holly estranged from me.
My kinsfolk have failed, And my familiar friends have forgotten me.
They that dell in my house, and my maids, count me for a stranger: I am an alien in their sight.
I call unto my servant, and he giveth me no anser, \add Though\add* I entreat him ith my mouth.
My breath is strange to my ife, And my supplication to the children of mine on mother.
Even young children despise me; If I arise, they speak against me.
All my familiar friends abhor me, And they hom I loved are turned against me.
My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, And I am escaped ith the skin of my teeth.
Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends; For the hand of God hath touched me.
Why do ye persecute me as God, And are not satisfied ith my flesh? \b
Oh that my ords ere no ritten! Oh that they ere inscribed in a book!
That ith an iron pen and lead They ere graven in the rock for ever!
But as for me I kno that my Redeemer liveth, And at last he ill stand up upon the earth:
And after my skin, \add even\add* this \add body\add*, is destroyed, Then ithout my flesh shall I see God;
Whom I, even I, shall see, on my side, And mine eyes shall behold, and not as a stranger. My heart is consumed ithin me.
If ye say, Ho e ill persecute him! And that the root of the matter is found in me;
Be ye afraid of the sord: For rath \add bringeth\add* the punishments of the sord, That ye may kno there is a judgment. \b
Then ansered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,
Therefore do my thoughts give anser to me, Even by reason of my haste that is in me.
I have heard the reproof hich putteth me to shame; And the spirit of my understanding ansereth me.
Knoest thou \add not\add* this of old time, Since man as placed upon earth,
That the triumphing of the icked is short, And the joy of the godless but for a moment?
Though his height mount up to the heavens, And his head reach unto the clouds;
Yet he shall perish for ever like his on dung: They that have seen him shall say, Where is he?
He shall fly aay as a dream, and shall not be found: Yea, he shall be chased aay as a vision of the night.
The eye hich sa him shall see him no more; Neither shall his place any more behold him.
His children shall seek the favor of the poor, And his hands shall give back his ealth.
His bones are full of his youth, But it shall lie don ith him in the dust. \b
Though ickedness be seet in his mouth, Though he hide it under his tongue,
Though he spare it, and ill not let it go, But keep it still ithin his mouth;
Yet his food in his boels is turned, It is the gall of asps ithin him.
He hath salloed don riches, and he shall vomit them up again; God ill cast them out of his belly.
He shall suck the poison of asps: The viper’s tongue shall slay him.
He shall not look upon the rivers, The floing streams of honey and butter.
That hich he labored for shall he restore, and shall not sallo it don; According to the substance that he hath gotten, he shall not rejoice.
For he hath oppressed and forsaken the poor; He hath violently taken aay a house, and he shall not build it up. \b
Because he kne no quietness ithin him, He shall not save aught of that herein he delighteth.
There as nothing left that he devoured not; Therefore his prosperity shall not endure.
In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: The hand of every one that is in misery shall come upon him.
When he is about to fill his belly, \add God\add* ill cast the fierceness of his rath upon him, And ill rain it upon him hile he is eating.
He shall flee from the iron eapon, And the bo of brass shall strike him through.
He draeth it forth, and it cometh out of his body; Yea, the glittering point cometh out of his gall: Terrors are upon him.
All darkness is laid up for his treasures: A fire not blon \add by man\add* shall devour him; It shall consume that hich is left in his tent.
The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, And the earth shall rise up against him.
The increase of his house shall depart; \add His goods\add* shall flo aay in the day of his rath.
This is the portion of a icked man from God, And the heritage appointed unto him by God. \b
Then Job ansered and said,
Hear diligently my speech; And let this be your consolations.
Suffer me, and I also ill speak; And after that I have spoken, mock on.
As for me, is my complaint to man? And hy should I not be impatient?
Mark me, and be astonished, And lay your hand upon your mouth.
Even hen I remember I am troubled, And horror taketh hold on my flesh.
Wherefore do the icked live, Become old, yea, ax mighty in poer?
Their seed is established ith them in their sight, And their offspring before their eyes.
Their houses are safe from fear, Neither is the rod of God upon them.
Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; Their co calveth, and casteth not her calf.
They send forth their little ones like a flock, And their children dance.
They sing to the timbrel and harp, And rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
They spend their days in prosperity, And in a moment they go don to Sheol.
And they say unto God, Depart from us; For e desire not the knoledge of thy ays.
What is the Almighty, that e should serve him? And hat profit should e have, if e pray unto him?
Lo, their prosperity is not in their hand: The counsel of the icked is far from me. \b
Ho oft is it that the lamp of the icked is put out? That their calamity cometh upon them? That \add God\add* distributeth sorros in his anger?
That they are as stubble before the ind, And as chaff that the storm carrieth aay?
\add Ye say\add*, God layeth up his iniquity for his children. Let him recompense it unto himself, that he may kno it:
Let his on eyes see his destruction, And let him drink of the rath of the Almighty.
For hat careth he for his house after him, When the number of his months is cut off?
Shall any teach God knoledge, Seeing he judgeth those that are high?
One dieth in his full strength, Being holly at ease and quiet:
His pails are full of milk, And the marro of his bones is moistened.
And another dieth in bitterness of soul, And never tasteth of good.
They lie don alike in the dust, And the orm covereth them. \b
Behold, I kno your thoughts, And the devices hereith ye ould rong me.
For ye say, Where is the house of the prince? And here is the tent herein the icked delt?
Have ye not asked ayfaring men? And do ye not kno their evidences,
That the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity? That they are led forth to the day of rath?
Who shall declare his ay to his face? And ho shall repay him hat he hath done?
Yet shall he be borne to the grave, And men shall keep atch over the tomb.
The clods of the valley shall be seet unto him, And all men shall dra after him, As there ere innumerable before him.
Ho then comfort ye me in vain, Seeing in your ansers there remaineth \add only\add* falsehood? \b
Then ansered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
Can a man be profitable unto God? Surely he that is ise is profitable unto himself.
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? Or is it gain \add to him\add*, that thou makest thy ays perfect?
Is it for thy fear \add of him\add* that he reproveth thee, That he entereth ith thee into judgment?
Is not thy ickedness great? Neither is there any end to thine iniquities.
For thou hast taken pledges of thy brother for nought, And stripped the naked of their clothing.
Thou hast not given ater to the eary to drink, And thou hast ithholden bread from the hungry.
But as for the mighty man, he had the earth; And the honorable man, he delt in it.
Thou hast sent idos aay empty, And the arms of the fatherless have been broken.
Therefore snares are round about thee, And sudden fear troubleth thee,
Or darkness, so that thou canst not see, And abundance of aters cover thee. \b
Is not God in the height of heaven? And behold the height of the stars, ho high they are!
And thou sayest, What doth God kno? Can he judge through the thick darkness?
Thick clouds are a covering to him, so that he seeth not; And he alketh on the vault of heaven.
Wilt thou keep the old ay Which icked men have trodden?
Who ere snatched aay before their time, Whose foundation as poured out as a stream,
Who said unto God, Depart from us; And, What can the Almighty do for us?
Yet he filled their houses ith good things: But the counsel of the icked is far from me.
The righteous see it, and are glad; And the innocent laugh them to scorn,
\add Saying\add*, Surely they that did rise up against us are cut off, And the remnant of them the fire hath consumed. \b
Acquaint no thyself ith him, and be at peace: Thereby good shall come unto thee.
Receive, I pray thee, the la from his mouth, And lay up his ords in thy heart.
If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, If thou put aay unrighteousness far from thy tents.
And lay thou \add thy\add* treasure in the dust, And \add the gold of\add* Ophir among the stones of the brooks;
And the Almighty ill be thy treasure, And precious silver unto thee.
For then shalt thou delight thyself in the Almighty, And shalt lift up thy face unto God.
Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he ill hear thee; And thou shalt pay thy vos.
Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee; And light shall shine upon thy ays.
When they cast \add thee\add* don, thou shalt say, \add There is\add* lifting up; And the humble person he ill save.
He ill deliver \add even\add* him that is not innocent: Yea, he shall be delivered through the cleanness of thy hands. \b
Then Job ansered and said,
Even to-day is my complaint rebellious: My stroke is heavier than my groaning.
Oh that I kne here I might find him! That I might come even to his seat!
I ould set my cause in order before him, And fill my mouth ith arguments.
I ould kno the ords hich he ould anser me, And understand hat he ould say unto me.
Would he contend ith me in the greatness of his poer? Nay; but he ould give heed unto me.
There the upright might reason ith him; So should I be delivered for ever from my judge.
Behold, I go forard, but he is not \add there\add*; And backard, but I cannot perceive him;
On the left hand, hen he doth ork, but I cannot behold him; He hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see him. \b
But he knoeth the ay that I take; When he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.
My foot hath held fast to his steps; His ay have I kept, and turned not aside.
I have not gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have treasured up the ords of his mouth more than my necessary food.
But he is in one \add mind\add*, and ho can turn him? And hat his soul desireth, even that he doeth.
For he performeth that hich is appointed for me: And many such things are ith him.
Therefore am I terrified at his presence; When I consider, I am afraid of him.
For God hath made my heart faint, And the Almighty hath terrified me;
Because I as not cut off before the darkness, Neither did he cover the thick darkness from my face. \b
Why are times not laid up by the Almighty? And hy do not they that kno him see his days?
There are that remove the landmarks; They violently take aay flocks, and feed them.
They drive aay the ass of the fatherless; They take the ido’s ox for a pledge.
They turn the needy out of the ay: The poor of the earth all hide themselves.
Behold, as ild asses in the desert They go forth to their ork, seeking diligently for food; The ilderness \add yieldeth\add* them bread for their children.
They cut their provender in the field; And they glean the vintage of the icked.
They lie all night naked ithout clothing, And have no covering in the cold.
They are et ith the shoers of the mountains, And embrace the rock for ant of a shelter.
There are that pluck the fatherless from the breast, And take a pledge of the poor;
\add So that\add* they go about naked ithout clothing, And being hungry they carry the sheaves.
They make oil ithin the alls of these men; They tread \add their\add* inepresses, and suffer thirst.
From out of the populous city men groan, And the soul of the ounded crieth out: Yet God regardeth not the folly. \b
These are of them that rebel against the light; They kno not the ays thereof, Nor abide in the paths thereof.
The murderer riseth ith the light; He killeth the poor and needy; And in the night he is as a thief.
The eye also of the adulterer aiteth for the tilight, Saying, No eye shall see me: And he disguiseth his face.
In the dark they dig through houses: They shut themselves up in the day-time; They kno not the light.
For the morning is to all of them as thick darkness; For they kno the terrors of the thick darkness. \b
Siftly they \add pass aay\add* upon the face of the aters; Their portion is cursed in the earth: They turn not into the ay of the vineyards.
Drought and heat consume the sno aters: \add So doth\add* Sheol \add those that\add* have sinned.
The omb shall forget him; The orm shall feed seetly on him; He shall be no more remembered; And unrighteousness shall be broken as a tree.
He devoureth the barren that beareth not, And doeth not good to the ido.
Yet \add God\add* preserveth the mighty by his poer: He riseth up that hath no assurance of life.
\add God\add* giveth them to be in security, and they rest thereon; And his eyes are upon their ays.
They are exalted; yet a little hile, and they are gone; Yea, they are brought lo, they are taken out of the ay as all others, And are cut off as the tops of the ears of grain.
And if it be not so no, ho ill prove me a liar, And make my speech nothing orth? \b
Then ansered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
Dominion and fear are ith him; He maketh peace in his high places.
Is there any number of his armies? And upon hom doth not his light arise?
Ho then can man be just ith God? Or ho can he be clean that is born of a oman?
Behold, even the moon hath no brightness, And the stars are not pure in his sight:
Ho much less man, that is a orm! And the son of man, that is a orm! \b
Then Job ansered and said,
Ho hast thou helped him that is ithout poer! Ho hast thou saved the arm that hath no strength!
Ho hast thou counselled him that hath no isdom, And plentifully declared sound knoledge!
To hom hast thou uttered ords? And hose spirit came forth from thee? \b
