And unto this people thou shalt say, Thus saith Jehovah: Behold, I set before you the ay of life and the ay of death.

He that abideth in this city shall die by the sord, and by the famine, and by the pestilence; but he that goeth out, and passeth over to the Chaldeans that besiege you, he shall live, and his life shall be unto him for a prey.
For I have set my face upon this city for evil, and not for good, saith Jehovah: it shall be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it ith fire.
And touching the house of the king of Judah, hear ye the ord of Jehovah:

O house of David, thus saith Jehovah, Execute justice in the morning, and deliver him that is robbed out of the hand of the oppressor, lest my rath go forth like fire, and burn so that none can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.
Behold, I am against thee, O inhabitant of the valley, \add and\add* of the rock of the plain, saith Jehovah; you that say, Who shall come don against us? or ho shall enter into our habitations?
And I ill punish you according to the fruit of your doings, saith Jehovah; and I ill kindle a fire in her forest, and it shall devour all that is round about her. \b
Thus said Jehovah: Go don to the house of the king of Judah, and speak there this ord,
and say, Hear the ord of Jehovah, O king of Judah, that sittest upon the throne of David, thou, and thy servants, and thy people that enter in by these gates.

Thus saith Jehovah: Execute ye justice and righteousness, and deliver him that is robbed out of the hand of the oppressor: and do no rong, do no violence, to the sojourner, the fatherless, nor the ido; neither shed innocent blood in this place.
For if ye do this thing indeed, then shall there enter in by the gates of this house kings sitting upon the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses, he, and his servants, and his people.
But if ye ill not hear these ords, I sear by myself, saith Jehovah, that this house shall become a desolation.

For thus saith Jehovah concerning the house of the king of Judah: Thou art Gilead unto me, \add and\add* the head of Lebanon; \add yet\add* surely I ill make thee a ilderness, \add and\add* cities hich are not inhabited.
And I ill prepare destroyers against thee, every one ith his eapons; and they shall cut don thy choice cedars, and cast them into the fire.
And many nations shall pass by this city, and they shall say every man to his neighbor, Wherefore hath Jehovah done thus unto this great city?
Then they shall anser, Because they forsook the covenant of Jehovah their God, and orshipped other gods, and served them.
Weep ye not for the dead, neither bemoan him; but eep sore for him that goeth aay; for he shall return no more, nor see his native country.
For thus saith Jehovah touching Shallum the son of Josiah, king of Judah, ho reigned instead of Josiah his father, \add and\add* ho ent forth out of this place: He shall not return thither any more;
but in the place hither they have led him captive, there shall he die, and he shall see this land no more.
Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness, and his chambers by injustice; that useth his neighbor’s service ithout ages, and giveth him not his hire;
that saith, I ill build me a ide house and spacious chambers, and cutteth him out indos; and it is ceiled ith cedar, and painted ith vermilion.
Shalt thou reign, because thou strivest to excel in cedar? Did not thy father eat and drink, and do justice and righteousness? then it as ell ith him.
He judged the cause of the poor and needy; then it as ell. Was not this to kno me? saith Jehovah.
But thine eyes and thy heart are not but for thy covetousness, and for shedding innocent blood, and for oppression, and for violence, to do it.

Therefore thus saith Jehovah concerning Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah: they shall not lament for him, \add saying\add*, Ah my brother! or, Ah sister! They shall not lament for him, \add saying\add* Ah lord! or, Ah his glory!
He shall be buried ith the burial of an ass, dran and cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
Go up to Lebanon, and cry; and lift up thy voice in Bashan, and cry from Abarim; for all thy lovers are destroyed.
I spake unto thee in thy prosperity; but thou saidst, I ill not hear. This hath been thy manner from thy youth, that thou obeyedst not my voice.
The ind shall feed all thy shepherds, and thy lovers shall go into captivity: surely then shalt thou be ashamed and confounded for all thy ickedness.
O inhabitant of Lebanon, that makest thy nest in the cedars, ho greatly to be pitied shalt thou be hen pangs come upon thee, the pain as of a oman in travail!
As I live, saith Jehovah, though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah ere the signet upon my right hand, yet ould I pluck thee thence;

and I ill give thee into the hand of them that seek thy life, and into the hand of them of hom thou art afraid, even into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of the Chaldeans.
And I ill cast thee out, and thy mother that bare thee, into another country, here ye ere not born; and there shall ye die.
But to the land hereunto their soul longeth to return, thither shall they not return.
Is this man Coniah a despised broken vessel? is he a vessel herein none delighteth? herefore are they cast out, he and his seed, and are cast into the land hich they kno not?
O earth, earth, earth, hear the ord of Jehovah.
Thus saith Jehovah, Write ye this man childless, a man that shall not prosper in his days; for no more shall a man of his seed prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling in Judah.
Woe unto the shepherds that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith Jehovah.

Therefore thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, against the shepherds that feed my people: Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them aay, and have not visited them; behold, I ill visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith Jehovah.
And I ill gather the remnant of my flock out of all the countries hither I have driven them, and ill bring them again to their folds; and they shall be fruitful and multiply.
And I ill set up shepherds over them, ho shall feed them; and they shall fear no more, nor be dismayed, neither shall any be lacking, saith Jehovah.
Behold, the days come, saith Jehovah, that I ill raise unto David a righteous Branch, and he shall reign as king and deal isely, and shall execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dell safely; and this is his name hereby he shall be called: Jehovah our righteousness.
Therefore, behold, the days come, saith Jehovah, that they shall no more say, As Jehovah liveth, ho brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt;
but, As Jehovah liveth, ho brought up and ho led the seed of the house of Israel out of the north country, and from all the countries hither I had driven them. And they shall dell in their on land.
Concerning the prophets. My heart ithin me is broken, all my bones shake; I am like a drunken man, and like a man hom ine hath overcome, because of Jehovah, and because of his holy ords.
For the land is full of adulterers; for because of searing the land mourneth; the pastures of the ilderness are dried up. And their course is evil, and their might is not right;
for both prophet and priest are profane; yea, in my house have I found their ickedness, saith Jehovah.
Wherefore their ay shall be unto them as slippery places in the darkness: they shall be driven on, and fall therein; for I ill bring evil upon them, even the year of their visitation, saith Jehovah.
And I have seen folly in the prophets of Samaria; they prophesied by Baal, and caused my people Israel to err.

In the prophets of Jerusalem also I have seen a horrible thing: they commit adultery, and alk in lies; and they strengthen the hands of evil-doers, so that none doth return from his ickedness: they are all of them become unto me as Sodom, and the inhabitants thereof as Gomorrah.

Therefore thus saith Jehovah of hosts concerning the prophets: Behold, I ill feed them ith ormood, and make them drink the ater of gall; for from the prophets of Jerusalem is ungodliness gone forth into all the land.
Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, Hearken not unto the ords of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they teach you vanity; they speak a vision of their on heart, and not out of the mouth of Jehovah.
They say continually unto them that despise me, Jehovah hath said, Ye shall have peace; and unto every one that alketh in the stubbornness of his on heart they say, No evil shall come upon you.
For ho hath stood in the council of Jehovah, that he should perceive and hear his ord? ho hath marked my ord, and heard it?
Behold, the tempest of Jehovah, \add even his\add* rath, is gone forth, yea, a hirling tempest: it shall burst upon the head of the icked.
The anger of Jehovah shall not return, until he have executed, and till he have performed the intents of his heart: in the latter days ye shall understand it perfectly.
I sent not these prophets, yet they ran: I spake not unto them, yet they prophesied.
But if they had stood in my council, then had they caused my people to hear my ords, and had turned them from their evil ay, and from the evil of their doings.
Am I a God at hand, saith Jehovah, and not a God afar off?
Can any hide himself in secret places so that I shall not see him? saith Jehovah. Do not I fill heaven and earth? saith Jehovah.
I have heard hat the prophets have said, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.
Ho long shall this be in the heart of the prophets that prophesy lies, even the prophets of the deceit of their on heart?
that think to cause my people to forget my name by their dreams hich they tell every man to his neighbor, as their fathers forgat my name for Baal.
The prophet that hath a dream, let him tell a dream; and he that hath my ord, let him speak my ord faithfully. What is the stra to the heat? saith Jehovah.
Is not my ord like fire? saith Jehovah; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?
Therefore, behold, I am against the prophets, saith Jehovah, that steal my ords every one from his neighbor.
Behold, I am against the prophets, saith Jehovah, that use their tongues, and say, He saith.

Behold, I am against them that prophesy lying dreams, saith Jehovah, and do tell them, and cause my people to err by their lies, and by their vain boasting: yet I sent them not, nor commanded them; neither do they profit this people at all, saith Jehovah.
And hen this people, or the prophet, or a priest, shall ask thee, saying, What is the burden of Jehovah? then shalt thou say unto them, What burden! I ill cast you off, saith Jehovah.
And as for the prophet, and the priest, and the people, that shall say, The burden of Jehovah, I ill even punish that man and his house.
Thus shall ye say every one to his neighbor, and every one to his brother, What hath Jehovah ansered? and, What hath Jehovah spoken?
And the burden of Jehovah shall ye mention no more: for every man’s on ord shall be his burden; for ye have perverted the ords of the living God, of Jehovah of hosts our God.
Thus shalt thou say to the prophet, What hath Jehovah ansered thee? and, What hath Jehovah spoken?
But if ye say, The burden of Jehovah; therefore thus saith Jehovah: Because ye say this ord, The burden of Jehovah, and I have sent unto you, saying, Ye shall not say, The burden of Jehovah;
therefore, behold, I ill utterly forget you, and I ill cast you off, and the city that I gave unto you and to your fathers, aay from my presence:
and I ill bring an everlasting reproach upon you, and a perpetual shame, hich shall not be forgotten. \b

Jehovah shoed me, and, behold, to baskets of figs set before the temple of Jehovah, after that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had carried aay captive Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and the princes of Judah, ith the craftsmen and smiths, from Jerusalem, and had brought them to Babylon.
One basket had very good figs, like the figs that are first-ripe; and the other basket had very bad figs, hich could not be eaten, they ere so bad.
Then said Jehovah unto me, What seest thou, Jeremiah? And I said, Figs; the good figs, very good; and the bad, very bad, that cannot be eaten, they are so bad.
And the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,
Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel: Like these good figs, so ill I regard the captives of Judah, hom I have sent out of this place into the land of the Chaldeans, for good.
For I ill set mine eyes upon them for good, and I ill bring them again to this land: and I ill build them, and not pull them don; and I ill plant them, and not pluck them up.
And I ill give them a heart to kno me, that I am Jehovah: and they shall be my people, and I ill be their God; for they shall return unto me ith their hole heart.

And as the bad figs, hich cannot be eaten, they are so bad, surely thus saith Jehovah, So ill I give up Zedekiah the king of Judah, and his princes, and the residue of Jerusalem, that remain in this land, and them that dell in the land of Egypt,
I ill even give them up to be tossed to and fro among all the kingdoms of the earth for evil; to be a reproach and a proverb, a taunt and a curse, in all places hither I shall drive them.
And I ill send the sord, the famine, and the pestilence, among them, till they be consumed from off the land that I gave unto them and to their fathers. \b
The ord that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah ( the same as the first year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon),
hich Jeremiah the prophet spake unto all the people of Judah, and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, saying:

From the thirteenth year of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah, even unto this day, these three and tenty years, the ord of Jehovah hath come unto me, and I have spoken unto you, rising up early and speaking; but ye have not hearkened.
And Jehovah hath sent unto you all his servants the prophets, rising up early and sending them, ( but ye have not hearkened, nor inclined your ear to hear),
saying, Return ye no every one from his evil ay, and from the evil of your doings, and dell in the land that Jehovah hath given unto you and to your fathers, from of old and even for evermore;
and go not after other gods to serve them, and to orship them, and provoke me not to anger ith the ork of your hands; and I ill do you no hurt.
Yet ye have not hearkened unto me, saith Jehovah; that ye may provoke me to anger ith the ork of your hands to your on hurt.
Therefore thus saith Jehovah of hosts: Because ye have not heard my ords,

behold, I ill send and take all the families of the north, saith Jehovah, and \add I ill send\add* unto Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon, my servant, and ill bring them against this land, and against the inhabitants thereof, and against all these nations round about; and I ill utterly destroy them, and make them an astonishment, and a hissing, and perpetual desolations.
Moreover I ill take from them the voice of mirth and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp.
And this hole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

And it shall come to pass, hen seventy years are accomplished, that I ill punish the king of Babylon, and that nation, saith Jehovah, for their iniquity, and the land of the Chaldeans; and I ill make it desolate for ever.
And I ill bring upon that land all my ords hich I have pronounced against it, even all that is ritten in this book, hich Jeremiah hath prophesied against all the nations.
For many nations and great kings shall make bondmen of them, even of them; and I ill recompense them according to their deeds, and according to the ork of their hands.
For thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, unto me: Take this cup of the ine of rath at my hand, and cause all the nations, to hom I send thee, to drink it.
And they shall drink, and reel to and fro, and be mad, because of the sord that I ill send among them.
Then took I the cup at Jehovah’s hand, and made all the nations to drink, unto hom Jehovah had sent me:
\add to it\add*, Jerusalem, and the cities of Judah, and the kings thereof, and the princes thereof, to make them a desolation, an astonishment, a hissing, and a curse, as it is this day;
Pharaoh king of Egypt, and his servants, and his princes, and all his people;
and all the mingled people, and all the kings of the land of Uz, and all the kings of the Philistines, and Ashkelon, and Gaza, and Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
Edom, and Moab, and the children of Ammon;
and all the kings of Tyre, and all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the isle hich is beyond the sea;
Dedan, and Tema, and Buz, and all that have the corners \add of their hair\add* cut off;
and all the kings of Arabia, and all the kings of the mingled people that dell in the ilderness;
and all the kings of Zimri, and all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of the Medes;
and all the kings of the north, far and near, one ith another; and all the kingdoms of the orld, hich are upon the face of the earth: and the king of Sheshach shall drink after them.
And thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel: Drink ye, and be drunken, and spe, and fall, and rise no more, because of the sord hich I ill send among you.
And it shall be, if they refuse to take the cup at thy hand to drink, then shalt thou say unto them, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: Ye shall surely drink.

For, lo, I begin to ork evil at the city hich is called by my name; and should ye be utterly unpunished? Ye shall not be unpunished; for I ill call for a sord upon all the inhabitants of the earth, saith Jehovah of hosts.

Therefore prophesy thou against them all these ords, and say unto them, Jehovah ill roar from on high, and utter his voice from his holy habitation; he ill mightily roar against his fold; he ill give a shout, as they that tread \add the grapes\add*, against all the inhabitants of the earth.

A noise shall come even to the end of the earth; for Jehovah hath a controversy ith the nations; he ill enter into judgment ith all flesh: as for the icked, he ill give them to the sord, saith Jehovah.
Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, Behold, evil shall go forth from nation to nation, and a great tempest shall be raised up from the uttermost parts of the earth.

And the slain of Jehovah shall be at that day from one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth: they shall not be lamented, neither gathered, nor buried; they shall be dung upon the face of the ground.
Wail, ye shepherds, and cry; and allo \add in ashes\add*, ye principal of the flock; for the days of your slaughter and of your dispersions are fully come, and ye shall fall like a goodly vessel.
And the shepherds shall have no ay to flee, nor the principal of the flock to escape.
A voice of the cry of the shepherds, and the ailing of the principal of the flock! for Jehovah layeth aste their pasture.
And the peaceable folds are brought to silence because of the fierce anger of Jehovah.
He hath left his covert, as the lion; for their land is become an astonishment because of the fierceness of the oppressing \add sord\add*, and because of his fierce anger. \b
In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, came this ord from Jehovah, saying,

Thus saith Jehovah: Stand in the court of Jehovah’s house, and speak unto all the cities of Judah, hich come to orship in Jehovah’s house, all the ords that I command thee to speak unto them; diminish not a ord.
It may be they ill hearken, and turn every man from his evil ay; that I may repent me of the evil hich I purpose to do unto them because of the evil of their doings.
And thou shalt say unto them, Thus saith Jehovah: If ye ill not hearken to me, to alk in my la, hich I have set before you,
to hearken to the ords of my servants the prophets, hom I send unto you, even rising up early and sending them, but ye have not hearkened;
then ill I make this house like Shiloh, and ill make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.
And the priests and the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these ords in the house of Jehovah.

And it came to pass, hen Jeremiah had made an end of speaking all that Jehovah had commanded him to speak unto all the people, that the priests and the prophets and all the people laid hold on him, saying, Thou shalt surely die.

Why hast thou prophesied in the name of Jehovah, saying, This house shall be like Shiloh, and this city shall be desolate, ithout inhabitant? And all the people ere gathered unto Jeremiah in the house of Jehovah.
And hen the princes of Judah heard these things, they came up from the king’s house unto the house of Jehovah; and they sat in the entry of the ne gate of Jehovah’s \add house\add*.
Then spake the priests and the prophets unto the princes and to all the people, saying, This man is orthy of death; for he hath prophesied against this city, as ye have heard ith your ears.
Then spake Jeremiah unto all the princes and to all the people, saying, Jehovah sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the ords that ye have heard.
No therefore amend your ays and your doings, and obey the voice of Jehovah your God; and Jehovah ill repent him of the evil that he hath pronounced against you.
But as for me, behold, I am in your hand: do ith me as is good and right in your eyes.

Only kno ye for certain that, if ye put me to death, ye ill bring innocent blood upon yourselves, and upon this city, and upon the inhabitants thereof; for of a truth Jehovah hath sent me unto you to speak all these ords in your ears.
Then said the princes and all the people unto the priests and to the prophets: This man is not orthy of death; for he hath spoken to us in the name of Jehovah our God.
Then rose up certain of the elders of the land, and spake to all the assembly of the people, saying,

Micah the Morashtite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah; and he spake to all the people of Judah, saying, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: Zion shall be ploed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest.

Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? did he not fear Jehovah, and entreat the favor of Jehovah, and Jehovah repented him of the evil hich he had pronounced against them? Thus should e commit great evil against our on souls.

And there as also a man that prophesied in the name of Jehovah, Uriah the son of Shemaiah of Kiriath-jearim; and he prophesied against this city and against this land according to all the ords of Jeremiah.
And hen Jehoiakim the king, ith all his mighty men, and all the princes, heard his ords, the king sought to put him to death; but hen Uriah heard it, he as afraid, and fled, and ent into Egypt.
And Jehoiakim the king sent men into Egypt, \add namely\add*, Elnathan the son of Achbor, and certain men ith him, into Egypt;
and they fetched forth Uriah out of Egypt, and brought him unto Jehoiakim the king, ho sle him ith the sord, and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people.
But the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan as ith Jeremiah, that they should not give him into the hand of the people to put him to death. \b
In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, came this ord unto Jeremiah from Jehovah, saying,
Thus saith Jehovah to me: Make thee bonds and bars, and put them upon thy neck;

and send them to the king of Edom, and to the king of Moab, and to the king of the children of Ammon, and to the king of Tyre, and to the king of Sidon, by the hand of the messengers that come to Jerusalem unto Zedekiah king of Judah:
and give them a charge unto their masters, saying, Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, Thus shall ye say unto your masters:
I have made the earth, the men and the beasts that are upon the face of the earth, by my great poer and by my outstretched arm; and I give it unto hom it seemeth right unto me.
And no have I given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, my servant; and the beasts of the field also have I given him to serve him.
And all the nations shall serve him, and his son, and his son’s son, until the time of his on land come: and then many nations and great kings shall make him their bondman.

And it shall come to pass, that the nation and the kingdom hich ill not serve the same Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and that ill not put their neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, that nation ill I punish, saith Jehovah, ith the sord, and ith the famine, and ith the pestilence, until I have consumed them by his hand.

But as for you, hearken ye not to your prophets, nor to your diviners, nor to your dreams, nor to your soothsayers, nor to your sorcerers, that speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon:
for they prophesy a lie unto you, to remove you far from your land, and that I should drive you out, and ye should perish.

But the nation that shall bring their neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him, that \add nation\add* ill I let remain in their on land, saith Jehovah; and they shall till it, and dell therein.
And I spake to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these ords, saying, Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.
Why ill ye die, thou and thy people, by the sord, by the famine, and by the pestilence, as Jehovah hath spoken concerning the nation that ill not serve the king of Babylon?
And hearken not unto the ords of the prophets that speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon; for they prophesy a lie unto you.
For I have not sent them, saith Jehovah, but they prophesy falsely in my name; that I may drive you out, and that ye may perish, ye, and the prophets that prophesy unto you.

Also I spake to the priests and to all this people, saying, Thus saith Jehovah: Hearken not to the ords of your prophets that prophesy unto you, saying, Behold, the vessels of Jehovah’s house shall no shortly be brought again from Babylon; for they prophesy a lie unto you.
Hearken not unto them; serve the king of Babylon, and live: herefore should this city become a desolation?

But if they be prophets, and if the ord of Jehovah be ith them, let them no make intercession to Jehovah of hosts, that the vessels hich are left in the house of Jehovah, and in the house of the king of Judah, and at Jerusalem, go not to Babylon.
For thus saith Jehovah of hosts concerning the pillars, and concerning the sea, and concerning the bases, and concerning the residue of the vessels that are left in this city,
hich Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took not, hen he carried aay captive Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, from Jerusalem to Babylon, and all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem;
yea, thus saith Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the vessels that are left in the house of Jehovah, and in the house of the king of Judah, and at Jerusalem:
They shall be carried to Babylon, and there shall they be, until the day that I visit them, saith Jehovah; then ill I bring them up, and restore them to this place.

And it came to pass the same year, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, that Hananiah the son of Azzur, the prophet, ho as of Gibeon, spake unto me in the house of Jehovah, in the presence of the priests and of all the people, saying,
Thus speaketh Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, saying, I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within to full years ill I bring again into this place all the vessels of Jehovah’s house, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took aay from this place, and carried to Babylon:
and I ill bring again to this place Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, ith all the captives of Judah, that ent to Babylon, saith Jehovah; for I ill break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Then the prophet Jeremiah said unto the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests, and in the presence of all the people that stood in the house of Jehovah,

even the prophet Jeremiah said, Amen: Jehovah do so; Jehovah perform thy ords hich thou hast prophesied, to bring again the vessels of Jehovah’s house, and all them of the captivity, from Babylon unto this place.
Nevertheless hear thou no this ord that I speak in thine ears, and in the ears of all the people:
The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of ar, and of evil, and of pestilence.
The prophet that prophesieth of peace, hen the ord of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be knon, that Jehovah hath truly sent him.

Or if I send a pestilence into that land, and pour out my rath upon it in blood, to cut off from it man and beast;
though Noah, Daniel, and Job, ere in it, as I live, saith the Lord Jehovah, they should deliver neither son nor daughter; they should but deliver their on souls by their righteousness.
For thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Ho much more hen I send my four sore judgments upon Jerusalem, the sord, and the famine, and the evil beasts, and the pestilence, to cut off from it man and beast!

Yet, behold, therein shall be left a remnant that shall be carried forth, both sons and daughters: behold, they shall come forth unto you, and ye shall see their ay and their doings; and ye shall be comforted concerning the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem, even concerning all that I have brought upon it.
And they shall comfort you, hen ye see their ay and their doings; and ye shall kno that I have not done ithout cause all that I have done in it, saith the Lord Jehovah.
And the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,
Son of man, hat is the vine-tree more than any tree, the vine-branch hich is among the trees of the forest?
Shall ood be taken thereof to make any ork? or ill men take a pin of it to hang any vessel thereon?
Behold, it is cast into the fire for fuel; the fire hath devoured both the ends of it, and the midst of it is burned: is it profitable for any ork?
Behold, hen it as hole, it as meet for no ork: ho much less, hen the fire hath devoured it, and it is burned, shall it yet be meet for any ork!
Therefore thus saith the Lord Jehovah: As the vine-tree among the trees of the forest, hich I have given to the fire for fuel, so ill I give the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And I ill set my face against them; they shall go forth from the fire, but the fire shall devour them; and ye shall kno that I am Jehovah, hen I set my face against them.
And I ill make the land desolate, because they have committed a trespass, saith the Lord Jehovah.
Again the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,
Son of man, cause Jerusalem to kno her abominations;
and say, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah unto Jerusalem: Thy birth and thy nativity is of the land of the Canaanite; the Amorite as thy father, and thy mother as a Hittite.
And as for thy nativity, in the day thou ast born thy navel as not cut, neither ast thou ashed in ater to cleanse thee; thou ast not salted at all, nor saddled at all.
No eye pitied thee, to do any of these things unto thee, to have compassion upon thee; but thou ast cast out in the open field, for that thy person as abhorred, in the day that thou ast born.
And hen I passed by thee, and sa thee eltering in thy blood, I said unto thee, \add Though thou art\add* in thy blood, live; yea, I said unto thee, \add Though thou art\add* in thy blood, live.

I caused thee to multiply as that hich groeth in the field, and thou didst increase and ax great, and thou attainedst to excellent ornament; thy breasts ere fashioned, and thy hair as gron; yet thou ast naked and bare.

No hen I passed by thee, and looked upon thee, behold, thy time as the time of love; and I spread my skirt over thee, and covered thy nakedness: yea, I sare unto thee, and entered into a covenant ith thee, saith the Lord Jehovah, and thou becamest mine.
Then ashed I thee ith ater; yea, I thoroughly ashed aay thy blood from thee, and I anointed thee ith oil.
I clothed thee also ith broidered ork, and shod thee ith sealskin, and I girded thee about ith fine linen, and covered thee ith silk.
And I decked thee ith ornaments, and I put bracelets upon thy hands, and a chain on thy neck.
And I put a ring upon thy nose, and ear-rings in thine ears, and a beautiful cron upon thy head.

Thus ast thou decked ith gold and silver; and thy raiment as of fine linen, and silk, and broidered ork; thou didst eat fine flour, and honey, and oil; and thou ast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper unto royal estate.
And thy renon ent forth among the nations for thy beauty; for it as perfect, through my majesty hich I had put upon thee, saith the Lord Jehovah.
But thou didst trust in thy beauty, and playedst the harlot because of thy renon, and pouredst out thy horedoms on every one that passed by; his it as.

And thou didst take of thy garments, and madest for thee high places decked ith divers colors, and playedst the harlot upon them: \add the like things\add* shall not come, neither shall it be \add so\add*.
Thou didst also take thy fair jeels of my gold and of my silver, hich I had given thee, and madest for thee images of men, and didst play the harlot ith them;
and thou tookest thy broidered garments, and coveredst them, and didst set mine oil and mine incense before them.
My bread also hich I gave thee, fine flour, and oil, and honey, hereith I fed thee, thou didst even set it before them for a seet savor; and \add thus\add* it as, saith the Lord Jehovah.
Moreover thou hast taken thy sons and thy daughters, hom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured. Were thy horedoms a small matter,
that thou hast slain my children, and delivered them up, in causing them to pass through \add the fire\add* unto them?
And in all thine abominations and thy horedoms thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, hen thou ast naked and bare, and ast eltering in thy blood.
And it is come to pass after all thy ickedness (oe, oe unto thee! saith the Lord Jehovah),
that thou hast built unto thee a vaulted place, and hast made thee a lofty place in every street.
Thou hast built thy lofty place at the head of every ay, and hast made thy beauty an abomination, and hast opened thy feet to every one that passed by, and multiplied thy horedom.
Thou hast also committed fornication ith the Egyptians, thy neighbors, great of flesh; and hast multiplied thy horedom, to provoke me to anger.

Behold therefore, I have stretched out my hand over thee, and have diminished thine ordinary \add food\add*, and delivered thee unto the ill of them that hate thee, the daughters of the Philistines, that are ashamed of thy led ay.
Thou hast played the harlot also ith the Assyrians, because thou ast insatiable; yea, thou hast played the harlot ith them, and yet thou ast not satisfied.
Thou hast moreover multiplied thy horedom unto the land of traffic, unto Chaldea; and yet thou ast not satisfied hereith.
Ho eak is thy heart, saith the Lord Jehovah, seeing thou doest all these things, the ork of an impudent harlot;
in that thou buildest thy vaulted place at the head of every ay, and makest thy lofty place in every street, and hast not been as a harlot, in that thou scornest hire.
A ife that committeth adultery! that taketh strangers instead of her husband!
They give gifts to all harlots; but thou givest thy gifts to all thy lovers, and bribest them, that they may come unto thee on every side for thy horedoms.

And thou art different from \add other\add* omen in thy horedoms, in that none folloeth thee to play the harlot; and hereas thou givest hire, and no hire is given unto thee, therefore thou art different.
Wherefore, O harlot, hear the ord of Jehovah:

Thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Because thy filthiness as poured out, and thy nakedness uncovered through thy horedoms ith thy lovers; and because of all the idols of thy abominations, and for the blood of thy children, that thou didst give unto them;

therefore behold, I ill gather all thy lovers, ith hom thou hast taken pleasure, and all them that thou hast loved, ith all them that thou hast hated; I ill even gather them against thee on every side, and ill uncover thy nakedness unto them, that they may see all thy nakedness.
And I ill judge thee, as omen that break edlock and shed blood are judged; and I ill bring upon thee the blood of rath and jealousy.

I ill also give thee into their hand, and they shall thro don thy vaulted place, and break don thy lofty places; and they shall strip thee of thy clothes, and take thy fair jeels; and they shall leave thee naked and bare.
They shall also bring up a company against thee, and they shall stone thee ith stones, and thrust thee through ith their sords.
And they shall burn thy houses ith fire, and execute judgments upon thee in the sight of many omen; and I ill cause thee to cease from playing the harlot, and thou shalt also give no hire any more.
So ill I cause my rath toard thee to rest, and my jealousy shall depart from thee, and I ill be quiet, and ill be no more angry.

Because thou hast not remembered the days of thy youth, but hast raged against me in all these things; therefore, behold, I also ill bring thy ay upon thy head, saith the Lord Jehovah: and thou shalt not commit this ledness ith all thine abominations.
Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use \add this\add* proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter.

Thou art the daughter of thy mother, that loatheth her husband and her children; and thou art the sister of thy sisters, ho loathed their husbands and their children: your mother as a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
And thine elder sister is Samaria, that delleth at thy left hand, she and her daughters; and thy younger sister, that delleth at thy right hand, is Sodom and her daughters.
Yet hast thou not alked in their ays, nor done after their abominations; but, as \add if that ere\add* a very little \add thing\add*, thou ast more corrupt than they in all thy ays.
As I live, saith the Lord Jehovah, Sodom thy sister hath not done, she nor her daughters, as thou hast done, thou and thy daughters.
Behold, this as the iniquity of thy sister Sodom: pride, fulness of bread, and prosperous ease as in her and in her daughters; neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
And they ere haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them aay as I sa \add good\add*.
Neither hath Samaria committed half of thy sins; but thou hast multiplied thine abominations more than they, and hast justified thy sisters by all thine abominations hich thou hast done.

Thou also, bear thou thine on shame, in that thou hast given judgment for thy sisters; through thy sins that thou hast committed more abominable than they, they are more righteous than thou: yea, be thou also confounded, and bear thy shame, in that thou hast justified thy sisters.
And I ill turn again their captivity, the captivity of Sodom and her daughters, and the captivity of Samaria and her daughters, and the captivity of thy captives in the midst of them;
that thou mayest bear thine on shame, and mayest be ashamed because of all that thou hast done, in that thou art a comfort unto them.

And thy sisters, Sodom and her daughters, shall return to their former estate; and Samaria and her daughters shall return to their former estate; and thou and thy daughters shall return to your former estate.
For thy sister Sodom as not mentioned by thy mouth in the day of thy pride,

before thy ickedness as uncovered, as at the time of the reproach of the daughters of Syria, and of all that are round about her, the daughters of the Philistines, that do despite unto thee round about.
Thou hast borne thy ledness and thine abominations, saith Jehovah.
For thus saith the Lord Jehovah: I ill also deal ith thee as thou hast done, ho hast despised the oath in breaking the covenant.
Nevertheless I ill remember my covenant ith thee in the days of thy youth, and I ill establish unto thee an everlasting covenant.

Then shalt thou remember thy ays, and be ashamed, hen thou shalt receive thy sisters, thine elder \add sisters\add* and thy younger; and I ill give them unto thee for daughters, but not by thy covenant.
And I ill establish my covenant ith thee; and thou shalt kno that I am Jehovah;
that thou mayest remember, and be confounded, and never open thy mouth any more, because of thy shame, hen I have forgiven thee all that thou hast done, saith the Lord Jehovah.
And the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,
Son of man, put forth a riddle, and speak a parable unto the house of Israel;
and say, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: A great eagle ith great ings and long pinions, full of feathers, hich had divers colors, came unto Lebanon, and took the top of the cedar:
he cropped off the topmost of the young tigs thereof, and carried it unto a land of traffic; he set it in a city of merchants.
He took also of the seed of the land, and planted it in a fruitful soil; he placed it beside many aters; he set it as a illo-tree.
And it gre, and became a spreading vine of lo stature, hose branches turned toard him, and the roots thereof ere under him: so it became a vine, and brought forth branches, and shot forth sprigs.

There as also another great eagle ith great ings and many feathers: and, behold, this vine did bend its roots toard him, and shot forth its branches toard him, from the beds of its plantation, that he might ater it.
It as planted in a good soil by many aters, that it might bring forth branches, and that it might bear fruit, that it might be a goodly vine.

Say thou, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Shall it prosper? shall he not pull up the roots thereof, and cut off the fruit thereof, that it may ither; that all its fresh springing leaves may ither? and not by a strong arm or much people can it be raised from the roots thereof.
Yea, behold, being planted, shall it prosper? shall it not utterly ither, hen the east ind toucheth it? it shall ither in the beds here it gre.
Moreover the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,

Say no to the rebellious house, Kno ye not hat these things mean? tell them, Behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, and took the king thereof, and the princes thereof, and brought them to him to Babylon.
And he took of the seed royal, and made a covenant ith him; he also brought him under an oath, and took aay the mighty of the land;
that the kingdom might be base, that it might not lift itself up, but that by keeping his covenant it might stand.

But he rebelled against him in sending his ambassadors into Egypt, that they might give him horses and much people. Shall he prosper? shall he escape that doeth such things? shall he break the covenant, and yet escape?
As I live, saith the Lord Jehovah, surely in the place here the king delleth that made him king, hose oath he despised, and hose covenant he brake, even ith him in the midst of Babylon he shall die.
Neither shall Pharaoh ith his mighty army and great company help him in the ar, hen they cast up mounds and build forts, to cut off many persons.
For he hath despised the oath by breaking the covenant; and behold, he had given his hand, and yet hath done all these things; he shall not escape.
Therefore thus saith the Lord Jehovah: As I live, surely mine oath that he hath despised, and my covenant that he hath broken, I ill even bring it upon his on head.
And I ill spread my net upon him, and he shall be taken in my snare, and I ill bring him to Babylon, and ill enter into judgment ith him there for his trespass that he hath trespassed against me.
And all his fugitives in all his bands shall fall by the sord, and they that remain shall be scattered toard every ind: and ye shall kno that I, Jehovah, have spoken it.

Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: I ill also take of the lofty top of the cedar, and ill set it; I ill crop off from the topmost of its young tigs a tender one, and I ill plant it upon a high and lofty mountain:

in the mountain of the height of Israel ill I plant it; and it shall bring forth boughs, and bear fruit, and be a goodly cedar: and under it shall dell all birds of every ing; in the shade of the branches thereof shall they dell.

And all the trees of the field shall kno that I, Jehovah, have brought don the high tree, have exalted the lo tree, have dried up the green tree, and have made the dry tree to flourish: I, Jehovah, have spoken and have done it.
The ord of Jehovah came unto me again, saying,
What mean ye, that ye use this proverb concerning the land of Israel, saying, The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge?
As I live, saith the Lord Jehovah, ye shall not have \add occasion\add* any more to use this proverb in Israel.
Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.
But if a man be just, and do that hich is laful and right,
and hath not eaten upon the mountains, neither hath lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, neither hath defiled his neighbor’s ife, neither hath come near to a oman in her impurity,
and hath not ronged any, but hath restored to the debtor his pledge, hath taken nought by robbery, hath given his bread to the hungry, and hath covered the naked ith a garment;
he that hath not given forth upon interest, neither hath taken any increase, that hath ithdran his hand from iniquity, hath executed true justice beteen man and man,
hath alked in my statutes, and hath kept mine ordinances, to deal truly; he is just, he shall surely live, saith the Lord Jehovah.
If he beget a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood, and that doeth any one of these things,
and that doeth not any of those \add duties\add*, but even hath eaten upon the mountains, and defiled his neighbor’s ife,
hath ronged the poor and needy, hath taken by robbery, hath not restored the pledge, and hath lifted up his eyes to the idols, hath committed abomination,
hath given forth upon interest, and hath taken increase; shall he then live? he shall not live: he hath done all these abominations; he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him.
No, lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father’s sins, hich he hath done, and feareth, and doeth not such like;
that hath not eaten upon the mountains, neither hath lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, hath not defiled his neighbor’s ife,
neither hath ronged any, hath not taken aught to pledge, neither hath taken by robbery, but hath given his bread to the hungry, and hath covered the naked ith a garment;

that hath ithdran his hand from the poor, that hath not received interest nor increase, hath executed mine ordinances, hath alked in my statutes; he shall not die for the iniquity of his father, he shall surely live.
As for his father, because he cruelly oppressed, robbed his brother, and did that hich is not good among his people, behold, he shall die in his iniquity.
Yet say ye, Wherefore doth not the son bear the iniquity of the father? When the son hath done that hich is laful and right, and hath kept all my statutes, and hath done them, he shall surely live.

The soul that sinneth, it shall die: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son; the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the ickedness of the icked shall be upon him.
But if the icked turn from all his sins that he hath committed, and keep all my statutes, and do that hich is laful and right, he shall surely live, he shall not die.
None of his transgressions that he hath committed shall be remembered against him: in his righteousness that he hath done he shall live.
Have I any pleasure in the death of the icked? saith the Lord Jehovah; and not rather that he should return from his ay, and live?

But hen the righteous turneth aay from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, and doeth according to all the abominations that the icked man doeth, shall he live? None of his righteous deeds that he hath done shall be remembered: in his trespass that he hath trespassed, and in his sin that he hath sinned, in them shall he die.
Yet ye say, The ay of the Lord is not equal. Hear no, O house of Israel: Is not my ay equal? are not your ays unequal?
When the righteous man turneth aay from his righteousness, and committeth iniquity, and dieth therein; in his iniquity that he hath done shall he die.
Again, hen the icked man turneth aay from his ickedness that he hath committed, and doeth that hich is laful and right, he shall save his soul alive.
Because he considereth, and turneth aay from all his transgressions that he hath committed, he shall surely live, he shall not die.
Yet saith the house of Israel, The ay of the Lord is not equal. O house of Israel, are not my ays equal? are not your ays unequal?
Therefore I ill judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ays, saith the Lord Jehovah. Return ye, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin.
Cast aay from you all your transgressions, herein ye have transgressed; and make you a ne heart and a ne spirit: for hy ill ye die, O house of Israel?
For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith the Lord Jehovah: herefore turn yourselves, and live.
Moreover, take thou up a lamentation for the princes of Israel,
and say, What as thy mother? A lioness: she couched among lions, in the midst of the young lions she nourished her helps.
And she brought up one of her helps: he became a young lion, and he learned to catch the prey; he devoured men.
The nations also heard of him; he as taken in their pit; and they brought him ith hooks unto the land of Egypt.
No hen she sa that she had aited, and her hope as lost, then she took another of her helps, and made him a young lion.
And he ent up and don among the lions; he became a young lion, and he learned to catch the prey; he devoured men.
And he kne their palaces, and laid aste their cities; and the land as desolate, and the fulness thereof, because of the noise of his roaring.
Then the nations set against him on every side from the provinces; and they spread their net over him; he as taken in their pit.
And they put him in a cage ith hooks, and brought him to the king of Babylon; they brought him into strongholds, that his voice should no more be heard upon the mountains of Israel.
Thy mother as like a vine, in thy blood, planted by the aters: it as fruitful and full of branches by reason of many aters.
And it had strong rods for the sceptres of them that bare rule, and their stature as exalted among the thick boughs, and they ere seen in their height ith the multitude of their branches.
But it as plucked up in fury, it as cast don to the ground, and the east ind dried up its fruit: its strong rods ere broken off and ithered; the fire consumed them.
And no it is planted in the ilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.
And fire is gone out of the rods of its branches, it hath devoured its fruit, so that there is in it no strong rod to be a sceptre to rule. This is a lamentation, and shall be for a lamentation.
And it came to pass in the seventh year, in the fifth \add month\add*, the tenth \add day\add* of the month, that certain of the elders of Israel came to inquire of Jehovah, and sat before me.
And the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,

Son of man, speak unto the elders of Israel, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Is it to inquire of me that ye are come? As I live, saith the Lord Jehovah, I ill not be inquired of by you.
Wilt thou judge them, son of man, ilt thou judge them? Cause them to kno the abominations of their fathers;

and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: In the day hen I chose Israel, and sare unto the seed of the house of Jacob, and made myself knon unto them in the land of Egypt, hen I sare unto them, saying, I am Jehovah your God;
in that day I sare unto them, to bring them forth out of the land of Egypt into a land that I had searched out for them, floing ith milk and honey, hich is the glory of all lands.
And I said unto them, Cast ye aay every man the abominations of his eyes, and defile not yourselves ith the idols of Egypt; I am Jehovah your God.

But they rebelled against me, and ould not hearken unto me; they did not every man cast aay the abominations of their eyes, neither did they forsake the idols of Egypt. Then I said I ould pour out my rath upon them, to accomplish my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt.

But I rought for my name’s sake, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations, among hich they ere, in hose sight I made myself knon unto them, in bringing them forth out of the land of Egypt.
So I caused them to go forth out of the land of Egypt, and brought them into the ilderness.
And I gave them my statutes, and shoed them mine ordinances, hich if a man do, he shall live in them.
Moreover also I gave them my sabbaths, to be a sign beteen me and them, that they might kno that I am Jehovah that sanctifieth them.

But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the ilderness: they alked not in my statutes, and they rejected mine ordinances, hich if a man keep, he shall live in them; and my sabbaths they greatly profaned. Then I said I ould pour out my rath upon them in the ilderness, to consume them.
But I rought for my name’s sake, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations, in hose sight I brought them out.
Moreover also I sare unto them in the ilderness, that I ould not bring them into the land hich I had given them, floing ith milk and honey, hich is the glory of all lands;
because they rejected mine ordinances, and alked not in my statutes, and profaned my sabbaths: for their heart ent after their idols.
Nevertheless mine eye spared them, and I destroyed them not, neither did I make a full end of them in the ilderness.
And I said unto their children in the ilderness, Walk ye not in the statutes of your fathers, neither observe their ordinances, nor defile yourselves ith their idols.
I am Jehovah your God: alk in my statutes, and keep mine ordinances, and do them;
and hallo my sabbaths; and they shall be a sign beteen me and you, that ye may kno that I am Jehovah your God.

But the children rebelled against me; they alked not in my statutes, neither kept mine ordinances to do them, hich if a man do, he shall live in them; they profaned my sabbaths. Then I said I ould pour out my rath upon them, to accomplish my anger against them in the ilderness.
Nevertheless I ithdre my hand, and rought for my name’s sake, that it should not be profaned in the sight of the nations, in hose sight I brought them forth.
Moreover I sare unto them in the ilderness, that I ould scatter them among the nations, and disperse them through the countries;
because they had not executed mine ordinances, but had rejected my statutes, and had profaned my sabbaths, and their eyes ere after their fathers’ idols.
Moreover also I gave them statutes that ere not good, and ordinances herein they should not live;

and I polluted them in their on gifts, in that they caused to pass through \add the fire\add* all that openeth the omb, that I might make them desolate, to the end that they might kno that I am Jehovah.

Therefore, son of man, speak unto the house of Israel, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: In this moreover have your fathers blasphemed me, in that they have committed a trespass against me.

For hen I had brought them into the land, hich I sare to give unto them, then they sa every high hill, and every thick tree, and they offered there their sacrifices, and there they presented the provocation of their offering; there also they made their seet savor, and they poured out there their drink-offerings.
Then I said unto them, What meaneth the high place hereunto ye go? So the name thereof is called Bamah unto this day.
Wherefore say unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Do ye pollute yourselves after the manner of your fathers? and play ye the harlot after their abominations?

and hen ye offer your gifts, hen ye make your sons to pass through the fire, do ye pollute yourselves ith all your idols unto this day? and shall I be inquired of by you, O house of Israel? As I live, saith the Lord Jehovah, I ill not be inquired of by you;
and that hich cometh into your mind shall not be at all, in that ye say, We ill be as the nations, as the families of the countries, to serve ood and stone.
As I live, saith the Lord Jehovah, surely ith a mighty hand, and ith an outstretched arm, and ith rath poured out, ill I be king over you.
And I ill bring you out from the peoples, and ill gather you out of the countries herein ye are scattered, ith a mighty hand, and ith an outstretched arm, and ith rath poured out;
and I ill bring you into the ilderness of the peoples, and there ill I enter into judgment ith you face to face.
Like as I entered into judgment ith your fathers in the ilderness of the land of Egypt, so ill I enter into judgment ith you, saith the Lord Jehovah.
And I ill cause you to pass under the rod, and I ill bring you into the bond of the covenant;

and I ill purge out from among you the rebels, and them that transgress against me; I ill bring them forth out of the land here they sojourn, but they shall not enter into the land of Israel: and ye shall kno that I am Jehovah.

As for you, O house of Israel, thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Go ye, serve every one his idols, and hereafter also, if ye ill not hearken unto me; but my holy name shall ye no more profane ith your gifts, and ith your idols.

For in my holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel, saith the Lord Jehovah, there shall all the house of Israel, all of them, serve me in the land: there ill I accept them, and there ill I require your offerings, and the first-fruits of your oblations, ith all your holy things.
As a seet savor ill I accept you, hen I bring you out from the peoples, and gather you out of the countries herein ye have been scattered; and I ill be sanctified in you in the sight of the nations.
And ye shall kno that I am Jehovah, hen I shall bring you into the land of Israel, into the country hich I sare to give unto your fathers.
And there shall ye remember your ays, and all your doings, herein ye have polluted yourselves; and ye shall loathe yourselves in your on sight for all your evils that ye have committed.
And ye shall kno that I am Jehovah, hen I have dealt ith you for my name’s sake, not according to your evil ays, nor according to your corrupt doings, O ye house of Israel, saith the Lord Jehovah.
And the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,
Son of man, set thy face toard the south, and drop \add thy ord\add* toard the south, and prophesy against the forest of the field in the South;

and say to the forest of the South, Hear the ord of Jehovah: Thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Behold, I ill kindle a fire in thee, and it shall devour every green tree in thee, and every dry tree: the flaming flame shall not be quenched, and all faces from the south to the north shall be burnt thereby.

And the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,

and say to the land of Israel, Thus saith Jehovah: Behold, I am against thee, and ill dra forth my sord out of its sheath, and ill cut off from thee the righteous and the icked.

and all flesh shall kno that I, Jehovah, have dran forth my sord out of its sheath; it shall not return any more.

it is sharpened that it may make a slaughter; it is furbished that it may be as lightning: shall e then make mirth? the rod of my son, it contemneth every tree.
And it is given to be furbished, that it may be handled: the sord, it is sharpened, yea, it is furbished, to give it into the hand of the slayer.
Cry and ail, son of man; for it is upon my people, it is upon all the princes of Israel: they are delivered over to the sord ith my people; smite therefore upon thy thigh.
For there is a trial; and hat if even the rod that contemneth shall be no more? saith the Lord Jehovah.

Thou therefore, son of man, prophesy, and smite thy hands together; and let the sord be doubled the third time, the sord of the deadly ounded: it is the sord of the great one that is deadly ounded, hich entereth into their chambers.

hile they see for thee false visions, hile they divine lies unto thee, to lay thee upon the necks of the icked that are deadly ounded, hose day is come in the time of the iniquity of the end.
Cause it to return into its sheath. In the place here thou ast created, in the land of thy birth, ill I judge thee.

Moreover the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,
And thou, son of man, ilt thou judge, ilt thou judge the bloody city? then cause her to kno all her abominations.
And thou shalt say, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: A city that sheddeth blood in the midst of her, that her time may come, and that maketh idols against herself to defile her!

Thou art become guilty in thy blood that thou hast shed, and art defiled in thine idols hich thou hast made; and thou hast caused thy days to dra near, and art come even unto thy years: therefore have I made thee a reproach unto the nations, and a mocking to all the countries.
Those that are near, and those that are far from thee, shall mock thee, thou infamous one \add and\add* full of tumult.
Behold, the princes of Israel, every one according to his poer, have been in thee to shed blood.
In thee have they set light by father and mother; in the midst of thee have they dealt by oppression ith the sojourner; in thee have they ronged the fatherless and the ido.
Thou hast despised my holy things, and hast profaned my sabbaths.
Slanderous men have been in thee to shed blood; and in thee they have eaten upon the mountains: in the midst of thee they have committed ledness.
In thee have they uncovered their fathers’ nakedness; in thee have they humbled her that as unclean in her impurity.
And one hath committed abomination ith his neighbor’s ife; and another hath ledly defiled his daughter-in-la; and another in thee hath humbled his sister, his father’s daughter.
In thee have they taken bribes to shed blood; thou hast taken interest and increase, and thou hast greedily gained of thy neighbors by oppression, and hast forgotten me, saith the Lord Jehovah.
Behold, therefore, I have smitten my hand at thy dishonest gain hich thou hast made, and at thy blood hich hath been in the midst of thee.
Can thy heart endure, or can thy hands be strong, in the days that I shall deal ith thee? I, Jehovah, have spoken it, and ill do it.
And I ill scatter thee among the nations, and disperse thee through the countries; and I ill consume thy filthiness out of thee.
And thou shalt be profaned in thyself, in the sight of the nations; and thou shalt kno that I am Jehovah.
And the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,
Son of man, the house of Israel is become dross unto me: all of them are brass and tin and iron and lead, in the midst of the furnace; they are the dross of silver.
Therefore thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Because ye are all become dross, therefore, behold, I ill gather you into the midst of Jerusalem.

As they gather silver and brass and iron and lead and tin into the midst of the furnace, to blo the fire upon it, to melt it; so ill I gather you in mine anger and in my rath, and I ill lay you there, and melt you.
Yea, I ill gather you, and blo upon you ith the fire of my rath, and ye shall be melted in the midst thereof.

And the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,
Son of man, say unto her, Thou art a land that is not cleansed, nor rained upon in the day of indignation.

There is a conspiracy of her prophets in the midst thereof, like a roaring lion ravening the prey: they have devoured souls; they take treasure and precious things; they have made her idos many in the midst thereof.

Her priests have done violence to my la, and have profaned my holy things: they have made no distinction beteen the holy and the common, neither have they caused men to discern beteen the unclean and the clean, and have hid their eyes from my sabbaths, and I am profaned among them.
Her princes in the midst thereof are like olves ravening the prey, to shed blood, \add and\add* to destroy souls, that they may get dishonest gain.
And her prophets have daubed for them ith untempered \add mortar\add*, seeing false visions, and divining lies unto them, saying, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah, hen Jehovah hath not spoken.
The people of the land have used oppression, and exercised robbery; yea, they have vexed the poor and needy, and have oppressed the sojourner rongfully.
And I sought for a man among them, that should build up the all, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it; but I found none.
Therefore have I poured out mine indignation upon them; I have consumed them ith the fire of my rath: their on ay have I brought upon their heads, saith the Lord Jehovah.
The ord of Jehovah came again unto me, saying,
Son of man, there ere to omen, the daughters of one mother:
and they played the harlot in Egypt; they played the harlot in their youth; there ere their breasts pressed, and there as handled the bosom of their virginity.
And the names of them ere Oholah the elder, and Oholibah her sister: and they became mine, and they bare sons and daughters. And as for their names, Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem Oholibah.
And Oholah played the harlot hen she as mine; and she doted on her lovers, on the Assyrians \add her\add* neighbors,
ho ere clothed ith blue, governors and rulers, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding upon horses.
And she bestoed her horedoms upon them, the choicest men of Assyria all of them; and on homsoever she doted, ith all their idols she defiled herself.
Neither hath she left her horedoms since \add the days of\add* Egypt; for in her youth they lay ith her, and they handled the bosom of her virginity; and they poured out their horedom upon her.
Wherefore I delivered her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the Assyrians, upon hom she doted.
These uncovered her nakedness; they took her sons and her daughters; and her they sle ith the sord: and she became a byord among omen; for they executed judgments upon her.
And her sister Oholibah sa this, yet as she more corrupt in her doting than she, and in her horedoms hich ere more than the horedoms of her sister.
She doted upon the Assyrians, governors and rulers, \add her\add* neighbors, clothed most gorgeously, horsemen riding upon horses, all of them desirable young men.
And I sa that she as defiled; they both took one ay.
And she increased her horedoms; for she sa men portrayed upon the all, the images of the Chaldeans portrayed ith vermilion,
girded ith girdles upon their loins, ith floing turbans upon their heads, all of them princes to look upon, after the likeness of the Babylonians in Chaldea, the land of their nativity.
And as soon as she sa them she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea.
And the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love, and they defiled her ith their horedom, and she as polluted ith them, and her soul as alienated from them.
So she uncovered her horedoms, and uncovered her nakedness: then my soul as alienated from her, like as my soul as alienated from her sister.
Yet she multiplied her horedoms, remembering the days of her youth, herein she had played the harlot in the land of Egypt.
And she doted upon their paramours, hose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and hose issue is like the issue of horses.
Thus thou calledst to remembrance the ledness of thy youth, in the handling of thy bosom by the Egyptians for the breasts of thy youth.
Therefore, O Oholibah, thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I ill raise up thy lovers against thee, from hom thy soul is alienated, and I ill bring them against thee on every side:

the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod and Shoa and Koa, \add and\add* all the Assyrians ith them; desirable young men, governors and rulers all of them, princes and men of renon, all of them riding upon horses.

And they shall come against thee ith eapons, chariots, and agons, and ith a company of peoples; they shall set themselves against thee ith buckler and shield and helmet round about: and I ill commit the judgment unto them, and they shall judge thee according to their judgments.

And I ill set my jealousy against thee, and they shall deal ith thee in fury; they shall take aay thy nose and thine ears; and thy residue shall fall by the sord: they shall take thy sons and thy daughters; and thy residue shall be devoured by the fire.

Thus ill I make thy ledness to cease from thee, and thy horedom \add brought\add* from the land of Egypt; so that thou shalt not lift up thine eyes unto them, nor remember Egypt any more.
For thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I ill deliver thee into the hand of them hom thou hatest, into the hand of them from hom thy soul is alienated;
and they shall deal ith thee in hatred, and shall take aay all thy labor, and shall leave thee naked and bare; and the nakedness of thy horedoms shall be uncovered, both thy ledness and thy horedoms.

Thou hast alked in the ay of thy sister; therefore ill I give her cup into thy hand.

For they have committed adultery, and blood is in their hands; and ith their idols have they committed adultery; and they have also caused their sons, hom they bare unto me, to pass through \add the fire\add* unto them to be devoured.

Again, in the ninth year, in the tenth month, in the tenth \add day\add* of the month, the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,

She hath earied \add herself\add* ith toil; yet her great rust goeth not forth out of her; her rust \add goeth not forth\add* by fire.

I, Jehovah, have spoken it: it shall come to pass, and I ill do it: I ill not go back, neither ill I spare, neither ill I repent; according to thy ays, and according to thy doings, shall they judge thee, saith the Lord Jehovah.

and say unto the children of Ammon, Hear the ord of the Lord Jehovah: Thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary, hen it as profaned; and against the land of Israel, hen it as made desolate; and against the house of Judah, hen they ent into captivity:

And it came to pass in the eleventh year, in the first \add day\add* of the month, that the ord of Jehovah came unto me, saying,

For thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Behold, I ill bring upon Tyre Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, from the north, ith horses, and ith chariots, and ith horsemen, and a company, and much people.

then ill I bring thee don ith them that descend into the pit, to the people of old time, and ill make thee to dell in the nether parts of the earth, in the places that are desolate of old, ith them that go don to the pit, that thou be not inhabited; and I ill set glory in the land of the living.

The ord of Jehovah came again unto me, saying,
And thou, son of man, take up a lamentation over Tyre;
and say unto Tyre, O thou that dellest at the entry of the sea, that art the merchant of the peoples unto many isles, thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Thou, O Tyre, hast said, I am perfect in beauty.
Thy borders are in the heart of the seas; thy builders have perfected thy beauty.
They have made all thy planks of fir-trees from Senir; they have taken a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for thee.
Of the oaks of Bashan have they made thine oars; they have made thy benches of ivory inlaid in boxood, from the isles of Kittim.
Of fine linen ith broidered ork from Egypt as thy sail, that it might be to thee for an ensign; blue and purple from the isles of Elishah as thine aning.
The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad ere thy roers: thy ise men, O Tyre, ere in thee, they ere thy pilots.
The old men of Gebal and the ise men thereof ere in thee thy calkers: all the ships of the sea ith their mariners ere in thee to deal in thy merchandise.
Persia and Lud and Put ere in thine army, thy men of ar: they hanged the shield and helmet in thee; they set forth thy comeliness.
The men of Arvad ith thine army ere upon thy alls round about, and valorous men ere in thy toers; they hanged their shields upon thy alls round about; they have perfected thy beauty.
Tarshish as thy merchant by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches; ith silver, iron, tin, and lead, they traded for thy ares.
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech, they ere thy traffickers; they traded the persons of men and vessels of brass for thy merchandise.
They of the house of Togarmah traded for thy ares ith horses and ar-horses and mules.
