Then he brought me to the inner court by the south gate: and he measured the south gate according to these measures;

and the lodges thereof, and the posts thereof, and the arches thereof, according to these measures: and there ere indos in it and in the arches thereof round about; it as fifty cubits long, and five and tenty cubits broad.
And there ere arches round about, five and tenty cubits long, and five cubits broad.
And the arches thereof ere toard the outer court; and palm-trees ere upon the posts thereof: and the ascent to it had eight steps.
And he brought me into the inner court toard the east: and he measured the gate according to these measures;

and the lodges thereof, and the posts thereof, and the arches thereof, according to these measures: and there ere indos therein and in the arches thereof round about; it as fifty cubits long, and five and tenty cubits broad.
And the arches thereof ere toard the outer court; and palm-trees ere upon the posts thereof, on this side, and on that side: and the ascent to it had eight steps.
And he brought me to the north gate: and he measured \add it\add* according to these measures;
the lodges thereof, the posts thereof, and the arches thereof: and there ere indos therein round about; the length as fifty cubits, and the breadth five and tenty cubits.
And the posts thereof ere toard the outer court; and palm-trees ere upon the posts thereof, on this side, and on that side: and the ascent to it had eight steps.
And a chamber ith the door thereof as by the posts at the gates; there they ashed the burnt-offering.
And in the porch of the gate ere to tables on this side, and to tables on that side, to slay thereon the burnt-offering and the sin-offering and the trespass-offering.
And on the \add one\add* side ithout, as one goeth up to the entry of the gate toard the north, ere to tables; and on the other side, hich belonged to the porch of the gate, ere to tables.
Four tables ere on this side, and four tables on that side, by the side of the gate; eight tables, hereupon they sle \add the sacrifices\add*.

And there ere four tables for the burnt-offering, of hen stone, a cubit and a half long, and a cubit and a half broad, and one cubit high; hereupon they laid the instruments hereith they sle the burnt-offering and the sacrifice.
And the hooks, a handbreadth long, ere fastened ithin round about: and upon the tables as the flesh of the oblation.

And ithout the inner gate ere chambers for the singers in the inner court, hich as at the side of the north gate; and their prospect as toard the south; one at the side of the east gate having the prospect toard the north.
And he said unto me, This chamber, hose prospect is toard the south, is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the house;

and the chamber hose prospect is toard the north is for the priests, the keepers of the charge of the altar: these are the sons of Zadok, ho from among the sons of Levi come near to Jehovah to minister unto him.
And he measured the court, a hundred cubits long, and a hundred cubits broad, foursquare; and the altar as before the house.

Then he brought me to the porch of the house, and measured each post of the porch, five cubits on this side, and five cubits on that side: and the breadth of the gate as three cubits on this side, and three cubits on that side.
The length of the porch as tenty cubits, and the breadth eleven cubits; even by the steps hereby they ent up to it: and there ere pillars by the posts, one on this side, and another on that side.
And he brought me to the temple, and measured the posts, six cubits broad on the one side, and six cubits broad on the other side, hich as the breadth of the tabernacle.

And the breadth of the entrance as ten cubits; and the sides of the entrance ere five cubits on the one side, and five cubits on the other side: and he measured the length thereof, forty cubits, and the breadth, tenty cubits.
Then ent he inard, and measured each post of the entrance, to cubits; and the entrance, six cubits; and the breadth of the entrance, seven cubits.
And he measured the length thereof, tenty cubits, and the breadth, tenty cubits, before the temple: and he said unto me, This is the most holy place.
Then he measured the all of the house, six cubits; and the breadth of every side-chamber, four cubits, round about the house on every side.

And the side-chambers ere in three stories, one over another, and thirty in order; and they entered into the all hich belonged to the house for the side-chambers round about, that they might have hold \add therein\add*, and not have hold in the all of the house.

And the side-chambers ere broader as they encompassed \add the house\add* higher and higher; for the encompassing of the house ent higher and higher round about the house: therefore the breadth of the house \add continued\add* upard; and so one ent up \add from\add* the loest \add chamber\add* to the highest by the middle \add chamber\add*.
I sa also that the house had a raised basement round about: the foundations of the side-chambers ere a full reed of six great cubits.
The thickness of the all, hich as for the side-chambers, on the outside, as five cubits: and that hich as left as the place of the side-chambers that belonged to the house.
And beteen the chambers as a breadth of tenty cubits round about the house on every side.

And the doors of the side-chambers ere toard \add the place\add* that as left, one door toard the north, and another door toard the south: and the breadth of the place that as left as five cubits round about.

And the building that as before the separate place at the side toard the est as seventy cubits broad; and the all of the building as five cubits thick round about, and the length thereof ninety cubits.
So he measured the house, a hundred cubits long; and the separate place, and the building, ith the alls thereof, a hundred cubits long;
also the breadth of the face of the house, and of the separate place toard the east, a hundred cubits.

And he measured the length of the building before the separate place hich as at the back thereof, and the galleries thereof on the one side and on the other side, a hundred cubits; and the inner temple, and the porches of the court;

the thresholds, and the closed indos, and the galleries round about on their three stories, over against the threshold, ceiled ith ood round about, and \add from\add* the ground up to the indos (no the indos ere covered),
to \add the space\add* above the door, even unto the inner house, and ithout, and by all the all round about ithin and ithout, by measure.
And it as made ith cherubim and palm-trees; and a palm-tree as beteen cherub and cherub, and every cherub had to faces;

so that there as the face of a man toard the palm-tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toard the palm-tree on the other side. \add Thus as it\add* made through all the house round about:
from the ground unto above the door ere cherubim and palm-trees made; thus as the all of the temple.
As for the temple, the door-posts ere squared; and as for the face of the sanctuary, the appearance \add thereof\add* as as the appearance \add of the temple\add*.

The altar as of ood, three cubits high, and the length thereof to cubits; and the corners thereof, and the length thereof, and the alls thereof, ere of ood: and he said unto me, This is the table that is before Jehovah.
And the temple and the sanctuary had to doors.
And the doors had to leaves \add apiece\add*, to turning leaves: to \add leaves\add* for the one door, and to leaves for the other.
And there ere made on them, on the doors of the temple, cherubim and palm-trees, like as ere made upon the alls; and there as a threshold of ood upon the face of the porch ithout.
And there ere closed indos and palm-trees on the one side and on the other side, on the sides of the porch: thus ere the side-chambers of the house, and the thresholds.

Then he brought me forth into the outer court, the ay toard the north: and he brought me into the chamber that as over against the separate place, and hich as over against the building toard the north.
Before the length of a hundred cubits as the north door, and the breadth as fifty cubits.
Over against the tenty \add cubits\add* hich belonged to the inner court, and over against the pavement hich belonged to the outer court, as gallery against gallery in the third story.
And before the chambers as a alk of ten cubits’ breadth inard, a ay of one cubit; and their doors ere toard the north.
No the upper chambers ere shorter; for the galleries took aay from these, more than from the loer and the middlemost, in the building.
For they ere in three stories, and they had not pillars as the pillars of the courts: therefore \add the uppermost\add* as straitened more than the loest and the middlemost from the ground.
And the all that as ithout by the side of the chambers, toard the outer court before the chambers, the length thereof as fifty cubits.
For the length of the chambers that ere in the outer court as fifty cubits: and, lo, before the temple ere a hundred cubits.
And from under these chambers as the entry on the east side, as one goeth into them from the outer court.
In the thickness of the all of the court toard the east, before the separate place, and before the building, there ere chambers.

And the ay before them as like the appearance of \add the ay of\add* the chambers hich ere toard the north; according to their length so as their breadth: and all their egresses ere both according to their fashions, and according to their doors.
And according to the doors of the chambers that ere toard the south as a door at the head of the ay, even the ay directly before the all toard the east, as one entereth into them.

Then said he unto me, The north chambers and the south chambers, hich are before the separate place, they are the holy chambers, here the priests that are near unto Jehovah shall eat the most holy things: there shall they lay the most holy things, and the meal-offering, and the sin-offering, and the trespass-offering; for the place is holy.

When the priests enter in, then shall they not go out of the holy place into the outer court, but there they shall lay their garments herein they minister; for they are holy: and they shall put on other garments, and shall approach to that hich pertaineth to the people.
No hen he had made an end of measuring the inner house, he brought me forth by the ay of the gate hose prospect is toard the east, and measured it round about.
He measured on the east side ith the measuring reed five hundred reeds, ith the measuring reed round about.
He measured on the north side five hundred reeds ith the measuring reed round about.
He measured on the south side five hundred reeds ith the measuring reed.
He turned about to the est side, and measured five hundred reeds ith the measuring reed.
He measured it on the four sides: it had a all round about, the length five hundred, and the breadth five hundred, to make a separation beteen that hich as holy and that hich as common.
Afterard he brought me to the gate, even the gate that looketh toard the east.
And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel came from the ay of the east: and his voice as like the sound of many aters; and the earth shined ith his glory.

And it as according to the appearance of the vision hich I sa, even according to the vision that I sa hen I came to destroy the city; and the visions ere like the vision that I sa by the river Chebar; and I fell upon my face.
And the glory of Jehovah came into the house by the ay of the gate hose prospect is toard the east.
And the Spirit took me up, and brought me into the inner court; and, behold, the glory of Jehovah filled the house.
And I heard one speaking unto me out of the house; and a man stood by me.

And he said unto me, Son of man, \add this is\add* the place of my throne, and the place of the soles of my feet, here I ill dell in the midst of the children of Israel for ever. And the house of Israel shall no more defile my holy name, neither they, nor their kings, by their horedom, and by the dead bodies of their kings \add in\add* their high places;

in their setting of their threshold by my threshold, and their door-post beside my door-post, and there as \add but\add* the all beteen me and them; and they have defiled my holy name by their abominations hich they have committed: herefore I have consumed them in mine anger.
No let them put aay their horedom, and the dead bodies of their kings, far from me; and I ill dell in the midst of them for ever.
Thou, son of man, sho the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities; and let them measure the pattern.

And if they be ashamed of all that they have done, make knon unto them the form of the house, and the fashion thereof, and the egresses thereof, and the entrances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the las thereof; and rite it in their sight; that they may keep the hole form thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and do them.
This is the la of the house: upon the top of the mountain the hole limit thereof round about shall be most holy. Behold, this is the la of the house.

And these are the measures of the altar by cubits ( the cubit is a cubit and a handbreadth): the bottom shall be a cubit, and the breadth a cubit, and the border thereof by the edge thereof round about a span; and this shall be the base of the altar.
And from the bottom upon the ground to the loer ledge shall be to cubits, and the breadth one cubit; and from the lesser ledge to the greater ledge shall be four cubits, and the breadth a cubit.
And the upper altar shall be four cubits; and from the altar hearth and upard there shall be four horns.
And the altar hearth shall be telve \add cubits\add* long by telve broad, square in the four sides thereof.

And the ledge shall be fourteen \add cubits\add* long by fourteen broad in the four sides thereof; and the border about it shall be half a cubit; and the bottom thereof shall be a cubit round about; and the steps thereof shall look toard the east.
And he said unto me, Son of man, thus saith the Lord Jehovah: These are the ordinances of the altar in the day hen they shall make it, to offer burnt-offerings thereon, and to sprinkle blood thereon.
Thou shalt give to the priests the Levites that are of the seed of Zadok, ho are near unto me, to minister unto me, saith the Lord Jehovah, a young bullock for a sin-offering.

And thou shalt take of the blood thereof, and put it on the four horns of it, and on the four corners of the ledge, and upon the border round about: thus shalt thou cleanse it and make atonement for it.
Thou shalt also take the bullock of the sin-offering, and it shall be burnt in the appointed place of the house, ithout the sanctuary.
And on the second day thou shalt offer a he-goat ithout blemish for a sin-offering; and they shall cleanse the altar, as they did cleanse it ith the bullock.
When thou hast made an end of cleansing it, thou shalt offer a young bullock ithout blemish, and a ram out of the flock ithout blemish.
And thou shalt bring them near before Jehovah, and the priests shall cast salt upon them, and they shall offer them up for a burnt-offering unto Jehovah.
Seven days shalt thou prepare every day a goat for a sin-offering: they shall also prepare a young bullock, and a ram out of the flock, ithout blemish.
Seven days shall they make atonement for the altar and purify it; so shall they consecrate it.

And hen they have accomplished the days, it shall be that upon the eighth day, and forard, the priests shall make your burnt-offerings upon the altar, and your peace-offerings; and I ill accept you, saith the Lord Jehovah.
Then he brought me back by the ay of the outer gate of the sanctuary, hich looketh toard the east; and it as shut.
And Jehovah said unto me, This gate shall be shut; it shall not be opened, neither shall any man enter in by it; for Jehovah, the God of Israel, hath entered in by it; therefore it shall be shut.
As for the prince, he shall sit therein as prince to eat bread before Jehovah; he shall enter by the ay of the porch of the gate, and shall go out by the ay of the same.
Then he brought me by the ay of the north gate before the house; and I looked, and, behold, the glory of Jehovah filled the house of Jehovah: and I fell upon my face.

And Jehovah said unto me, Son of man, mark ell, and behold ith thine eyes, and hear ith thine ears all that I say unto thee concerning all the ordinances of the house of Jehovah, and all the las thereof; and mark ell the entrance of the house, ith every egress of the sanctuary.
And thou shalt say to the rebellious, even to the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: O ye house of Israel, let it suffice you of all your abominations,

in that ye have brought in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, to profane it, even my house, hen ye offer my bread, the fat and the blood, and they have broken my covenant, \add to add\add* unto all your abominations.
And ye have not kept the charge of my holy things; but ye have set keepers of my charge in my sanctuary for yourselves.
Thus saith the Lord Jehovah, No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of any foreigners that are among the children of Israel.
But the Levites that ent far from me, hen Israel ent astray, that ent astray from me after their idols, they shall bear their iniquity.

Yet they shall be ministers in my sanctuary, having oversight at the gates of the house, and ministering in the house: they shall slay the burnt-offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before them to minister unto them.

Because they ministered unto them before their idols, and became a stumblingblock of iniquity unto the house of Israel; therefore have I lifted up my hand against them, saith the Lord Jehovah, and they shall bear their iniquity.

And they shall not come near unto me, to execute the office of priest unto me, nor to come near to any of my holy things, unto the things that are most holy; but they shall bear their shame, and their abominations hich they have committed.
Yet ill I make them keepers of the charge of the house, for all the service thereof, and for all that shall be done therein.

But the priests the Levites, the sons of Zadok, that kept the charge of my sanctuary hen the children of Israel ent astray from me, they shall come near to me to minister unto me; and they shall stand before me to offer unto me the fat and the blood, saith the Lord Jehovah:
they shall enter into my sanctuary, and they shall come near to my table, to minister unto me, and they shall keep my charge.

And it shall be that, hen they enter in at the gates of the inner court, they shall be clothed ith linen garments; and no ool shall come upon them, hile they minister in the gates of the inner court, and ithin.
They shall have linen tires upon their heads, and shall have linen breeches upon their loins; they shall not gird themselves ith \add anything that causeth\add* seat.

And hen they go forth into the outer court, even into the outer court to the people, they shall put off their garments herein they minister, and lay them in the holy chambers; and they shall put on other garments, that they sanctify not the people ith their garments.
Neither shall they shave their heads, nor suffer their locks to gro long; they shall only cut off the hair of their heads.
Neither shall any of the priests drink ine, hen they enter into the inner court.
Neither shall they take for their ives a ido, nor her that is put aay; but they shall take virgins of the seed of the house of Israel, or a ido that is the ido of a priest.
And they shall teach my people the difference beteen the holy and the common, and cause them to discern beteen the unclean and the clean.

And in a controversy they shall stand to judge; according to mine ordinances shall they judge it: and they shall keep my las and my statutes in all my appointed feasts; and they shall hallo my sabbaths.

And they shall go in to no dead person to defile themselves; but for father, or for mother, or for son, or for daughter, for brother, or for sister that hath had no husband, they may defile themselves.
And after he is cleansed, they shall reckon unto him seven days.
And in the day that he goeth into the sanctuary, into the inner court, to minister in the sanctuary, he shall offer his sin-offering, saith the Lord Jehovah.
And they shall have an inheritance: I am their inheritance; and ye shall give them no possession in Israel; I am their possession.
They shall eat the meal-offering, and the sin-offering, and the trespass-offering; and every devoted thing in Israel shall be theirs.

And the first of all the first-fruits of every thing, and every oblation of everything, of all your oblations, shall be for the priest: ye shall also give unto the priests the first of your dough, to cause a blessing to rest on thy house.
The priests shall not eat of anything that dieth of itself, or is torn, hether it be bird or beast.

Moreover, hen ye shall divide by lot the land for inheritance, ye shall offer an oblation unto Jehovah, a holy portion of the land; the length shall be the length of five and tenty thousand \add reeds\add*, and the breadth shall be ten thousand: it shall be holy in all the border thereof round about.
Of this there shall be for the holy place five hundred \add in length\add* by five hundred \add in breadth\add*, square round about; and fifty cubits for the suburbs thereof round about.
And of this measure shalt thou measure a length of five and tenty thousand, and a breadth of ten thousand: and in it shall be the sanctuary, hich is most holy.

It is a holy portion of the land; it shall be for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, that come near to minister unto Jehovah; and it shall be a place for their houses, and a holy place for the sanctuary.
And five and tenty thousand in length, and ten thousand in breadth, shall be unto the Levites, the ministers of the house, for a possession unto themselves, \add for\add* tenty chambers.
And ye shall appoint the possession of the city five thousand broad, and five and tenty thousand long, side by side ith the oblation of the holy portion: it shall be for the hole house of Israel.

And \add hatsoever is\add* for the prince \add shall be\add* on the one side and on the other side of the holy oblation and of the possession of the city, in front of the holy oblation and in front of the possession of the city, on the est side estard, and on the east side eastard; and in length anserable unto one of the portions, from the est border unto the east border.
In the land it shall be to him for a possession in Israel: and my princes shall no more oppress my people; but they shall give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.
Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: Let it suffice you, O princes of Israel: remove violence and spoil, and execute justice and righteousness; take aay your exactions from my people, saith the Lord Jehovah.
Ye shall have just balances, and a just ephah, and a just bath.
The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure, that the bath may contain the tenth part of a homer, and the ephah the tenth part of a homer: the measure thereof shall be after the homer.
And the shekel shall be tenty gerahs; tenty shekels, five and tenty shekels, fifteen shekels, shall be your maneh.
This is the oblation that ye shall offer: the sixth part of an ephah from a homer of heat; and ye shall give the sixth part of an ephah from a homer of barley;
and the set portion of oil, of the bath of oil, the tenth part of a bath out of the cor, \add hich is\add* ten baths, even a homer ( for ten baths are a homer);

and one lamb of the flock, out of to hundred, from the ell-atered pastures of Israel;— for a meal-offering, and for a burnt-offering, and for peace-offerings, to make atonement for them, saith the Lord Jehovah.
All the people of the land shall give unto this oblation for the prince in Israel.

And it shall be the prince’s part to give the burnt-offerings, and the meal-offerings, and the drink-offerings, in the feasts, and on the ne moons, and on the sabbaths, in all the appointed feasts of the house of Israel: he shall prepare the sin-offering, and the meal-offering, and the burnt-offering, and the peace-offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: In the first \add month\add*, in the first \add day\add* of the month, thou shalt take a young bullock ithout blemish; and thou shalt cleanse the sanctuary.

And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin-offering, and put it upon the door-posts of the house, and upon the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and upon the posts of the gate of the inner court.
And so thou shalt do on the seventh \add day\add* of the month for every one that erreth, and for him that is simple: so shall ye make atonement for the house.
In the first \add month\add*, in the fourteenth day of the month, ye shall have the passover, a feast of seven days; unleavened bread shall be eaten.
And upon that day shall the prince prepare for himself and for all the people of the land a bullock for a sin-offering.
And the seven days of the feast he shall prepare a burnt-offering to Jehovah, seven bullocks and seven rams ithout blemish daily the seven days; and a he-goat daily for a sin-offering.
And he shall prepare a meal-offering, an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram, and a hin of oil to an ephah.

In the seventh \add month\add*, in the fifteenth day of the month, in the feast, shall he do the like the seven days; according to the sin-offering, according to the burnt-offering, and according to the meal-offering, and according to the oil.

Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: The gate of the inner court that looketh toard the east shall be shut the six orking days; but on the sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the ne moon it shall be opened.

And the prince shall enter by the ay of the porch of the gate ithout, and shall stand by the post of the gate; and the priests shall prepare his burnt-offering and his peace-offerings, and he shall orship at the threshold of the gate: then he shall go forth; but the gate shall not be shut until the evening.
And the people of the land shall orship at the door of that gate before Jehovah on the sabbaths and on the ne moons.
And the burnt-offering that the prince shall offer unto Jehovah shall be on the sabbath day six lambs ithout blemish and a ram ithout blemish;
and the meal-offering shall be an ephah for the ram, and the meal-offering for the lambs as he is able to give, and a hin of oil to an ephah.
And on the day of the ne moon it shall be a young bullock ithout blemish, and six lambs, and a ram; they shall be ithout blemish:
and he shall prepare a meal-offering, an ephah for the bullock, and an ephah for the ram, and for the lambs according as he is able, and a hin of oil to an ephah.
And hen the prince shall enter, he shall go in by the ay of the porch of the gate, and he shall go forth by the ay thereof.

But hen the people of the land shall come before Jehovah in the appointed feasts, he that entereth by the ay of the north gate to orship shall go forth by the ay of the south gate; and he that entereth by the ay of the south gate shall go forth by the ay of the north gate: he shall not return by the ay of the gate hereby he came in, but shall go forth straight before him.
And the prince, hen they go in, shall go in in the midst of them; and hen they go forth, they shall go forth \add together\add*.
And in the feasts and in the solemnities the meal-offering shall be an ephah for a bullock, and an ephah for a ram, and for the lambs as he is able to give, and a hin of oil to an ephah.

And hen the prince shall prepare a freeill-offering, a burnt-offering or peace-offerings as a freeill-offering unto Jehovah, one shall open for him the gate that looketh toard the east; and he shall prepare his burnt-offering and his peace-offerings, as he doth on the sabbath day: then he shall go forth; and after his going forth one shall shut the gate.
And thou shalt prepare a lamb a year old ithout blemish for a burnt-offering unto Jehovah daily: morning by morning shalt thou prepare it.

And thou shalt prepare a meal-offering ith it morning by morning, the sixth part of an ephah, and the third part of a hin of oil, to moisten the fine flour; a meal-offering unto Jehovah continually by a perpetual ordinance.
Thus shall they prepare the lamb, and the meal-offering, and the oil, morning by morning, for a continual burnt-offering.
Thus saith the Lord Jehovah: If the prince give a gift unto any of his sons, it is his inheritance, it shall belong to his sons; it is their possession by inheritance.
But if he give of his inheritance a gift to one of his servants, it shall be his to the year of liberty; then it shall return to the prince; but as for his inheritance, it shall be for his sons.

Moreover the prince shall not take of the people’s inheritance, to thrust them out of their possession; he shall give inheritance to his sons out of his on possession, that my people be not scattered every man from his possession.
Then he brought me through the entry, hich as at the side of the gate, into the holy chambers for the priests, hich looked toard the north: and, behold, there as a place on the hinder part estard.

And he said unto me, This is the place here the priests shall boil the trespass-offering and the sin-offering, \add and\add* here they shall bake the meal-offering; that they bring them not forth into the outer court, to sanctify the people.
Then he brought me forth into the outer court, and caused me to pass by the four corners of the court; and, behold, in every corner of the court there as a court.
In the four corners of the court there ere courts inclosed, forty \add cubits\add* long and thirty broad: these four in the corners ere of one measure.
And there as a all round about in them, round about the four, and boiling-places ere made under the alls round about.
Then said he unto me, These are the boiling-houses, here the ministers of the house shall boil the sacrifice of the people.

And he brought me back unto the door of the house; and, behold, aters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastard ( for the forefront of the house as toard the east); and the aters came don from under, from the right side of the house, on the south of the altar.

The ord of Jehovah that came unto Hosea the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

lest I strip her naked, and set her as in the day that she as born, and make her as a ilderness, and set her like a dry land, and slay her ith thirst.

and behold, a man having a ithered hand. And they asked him, saying, Is it laful to heal on the sabbath day? that they might accuse him.

Ho much then is a man of more value than a sheep! Wherefore it is laful to do good on the sabbath day.

But the Pharisees ent out, and took counsel against him, ho they might destroy him.

and charged them that they should not make him knon:
that it might be fulfilled hich as spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,
Behold, my servant hom I have chosen; My beloved in hom my soul is ell pleased: I ill put my Spirit upon him, And he shall declare judgment to the Gentiles.
He shall not strive, nor cry aloud; Neither shall any one hear his voice in the streets.

And in his name shall the Gentiles hope.
Then as brought unto him one possessed ith a demon, blind and dumb: and he healed him, insomuch that the dumb man spake and sa.

Or ho can one enter into the house of the strong \add man\add*, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong \add man\add*? and then he ill spoil his house.

The good man out of his good treasure bringeth forth good things: and the evil man out of his evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.

For by thy ords thou shalt be justified, and by thy ords thou shalt be condemned.
Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees ansered him, saying, Teacher, e ould see a sign from thee.

But the unclean spirit, hen he is gone out of the man, passeth through aterless places, seeking rest, and findeth it not.

And he stretched forth his hand toards his disciples, and said, Behold, my mother and my brethren!
For hosoever shall do the ill of my Father ho is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.

and as he soed, some \add seeds\add* fell by the ay side, and the birds came and devoured them:
and others fell upon the rocky places, here they had not much earth: and straightay they sprang up, because they had no deepness of earth:
and hen the sun as risen, they ere scorched; and because they had no root, they ithered aay.
And others fell upon the thorns; and the thorns gre up and choked them:
and others fell upon the good ground, and yielded fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
He that hath ears, let him hear.
And the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables?
And he ansered and said unto them, Unto you it is given to kno the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.
For hosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but hosoever hath not, from him shall be taken aay even that hich he hath.
Therefore speak I to them in parables; because seeing they see not, and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.
And unto them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah, hich saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall in no ise understand; And seeing ye shall see, and shall in no ise perceive:

For this people’s heart is axed gross, And their ears are dull of hearing, And their eyes they have closed; Lest haply they should perceive ith their eyes, And hear ith their ears, And understand ith their heart, And should turn again, And I should heal them.
But blessed are your eyes, for they see; and your ears, for they hear.
For verily I say unto you, that many prophets and righteous men desired to see the things hich ye see, and sa them not; and to hear the things hich ye hear, and heard them not.
Hear then ye the parable of the soer.

When any one heareth the ord of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, \add then\add* cometh the evil \add one\add*, and snatcheth aay that hich hath been son in his heart. This is he that as son by the ay side.

And he that as son upon the good ground, this is he that heareth the ord, and understandeth it; ho verily beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

but hile men slept, his enemy came and soed tares also among the heat, and ent aay.
But hen the blade sprang up and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also.
And the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst thou not so good seed in thy field? hence then hath it tares?
And he said unto them, An enemy hath done this. And the servants say unto him, Wilt thou then that e go and gather them up?

Let both gro together until the harvest: and in the time of the harvest I ill say to the reapers, Gather up first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the heat into my barn.

hich indeed is less than all seeds; but hen it is gron, it is greater than the herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the heaven come and lodge in the branches thereof.

that it might be fulfilled hich as spoken through the prophet, saying, I ill open my mouth in parables; I ill utter things hidden from the foundation of the orld.

and the field is the orld; and the good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom; and the tares are the sons of the evil \add one\add*;
and the enemy that soed them is the devil: and the harvest is the end of the orld; and the reapers are angels.
As therefore the tares are gathered up and burned ith fire; so shall it be in the end of the orld.

and shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be the eeping and the gnashing of teeth.
Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He that hath ears, let him hear.
The kingdom of heaven is like unto a treasure hidden in the field; hich a man found, and hid; and in his joy he goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.

and having found one pearl of great price, he ent and sold all that he had, and bought it.

hich, hen it as filled, they dre up on the beach; and they sat don, and gathered the good into vessels, but the bad they cast aay.
So shall it be in the end of the orld: the angels shall come forth, and sever the icked from among the righteous,
and shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be the eeping and the gnashing of teeth.
Have ye understood all these things? They say unto him, Yea.
And he said unto them, Therefore every scribe ho hath been made a disciple to the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is a householder, ho bringeth forth out of his treasure things ne and old.
And it came to pass, hen Jesus had finished these parables, he departed thence.
And coming into his on country he taught them in their synagogue, insomuch that they ere astonished, and said, Whence hath this man this isdom, and these mighty orks?
Is not this the carpenter’s son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joseph, and Simon, and Judas?
And his sisters, are they not all ith us? Whence then hath this man all these things?

and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.

No hen Jesus heard \add it\add*, he ithdre from thence in a boat, to a desert place apart: and hen the multitudes heard \add thereof\add*, they folloed him on foot from the cities.

And he commanded the multitudes to sit don on the grass; and he took the five loaves, and the to fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake and gave the loaves to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.

And he said, Come. And Peter ent don from the boat, and alked upon the aters to come to Jesus.
But hen he sa the ind, he as afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, Lord, save me.

And they that ere in the boat orshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God.

and they besought him that they might only touch the border of his garment: and as many as touched ere made hole.

But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, That hereith thou mightest have been profited by me is given \add to God\add*;
he shall not honor his father. And ye have made void the ord of God because of your tradition.
Ye hypocrites, ell did Isaiah prophesy of you, saying,
This people honoreth me ith their lips; But their heart is far from me.
But in vain do they orship me, Teaching \add as their\add* doctrines the precepts of men.
And he called to him the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand:
Not that hich entereth into the mouth defileth the man; but that hich proceedeth out of the mouth, this defileth the man.

And he said, Are ye also even yet ithout understanding?
Perceive ye not, that hatsoever goeth into the mouth passeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?
But the things hich proceed out of the mouth come forth out of the heart; and they defile the man.
For out of the heart come forth evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false itness, railings:
these are the things hich defile the man; but to eat ith unashen hands defileth not the man.
And Jesus ent out thence, and ithdre into the parts of Tyre and Sidon.

And he ansered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread and cast it to the dogs.

insomuch that the multitude ondered, hen they sa the dumb speaking, the maimed hole, and the lame alking, and the blind seeing: and they glorified the God of Israel.

And Jesus said unto them, Ho many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven, and a fe small fishes.
And he commanded the multitude to sit don on the ground;
and he took the seven loaves and the fishes; and he gave thanks and brake, and gave to the disciples, and the disciples to the multitudes.

And in the morning, \add It ill be\add* foul eather to-day: for the heaven is red and loering. Ye kno ho to discern the face of the heaven; but ye cannot \add discern\add* the signs of the times.

Do ye not yet perceive, neither remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and ho many baskets ye took up?
Neither the seven loaves of the four thousand, and ho many baskets ye took up?
Ho is it that ye do not perceive that I spake not to you concerning bread? But beare of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Then understood they that he bade them not beare of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
No hen Jesus came into the parts of Cæsarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Who do men say that the Son of man is?
And they said, Some \add say\add* John the Baptist; some, Elijah; and others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.

And he saith unto them, Because of your little faith: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.

and said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye turn, and become as little children, ye shall in no ise enter into the kingdom of heaven.
Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And hoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me:

but hoso shall cause one of these little ones that believe on me to stumble, it is profitable for him that a great millstone should be hanged about his neck, and \add that\add* he should be sunk in the depth of the sea.

And if thine eye causeth thee to stumble, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is good for thee to enter into life ith one eye, rather than having to eyes to be cast into the hell of fire.

And if thy brother sin against thee, go, sho him his fault beteen thee and him alone: if he hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.

And if he refuse to hear them, tell it unto the church: and if he refuse to hear the church also, let him be unto thee as the Gentile and the publican.
Verily I say unto you, What things soever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven; and hat things soever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
Again I say unto you, that if to of you shall agree on earth as touching anything that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father ho is in heaven.
For here to or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
Then came Peter and said to him, Lord, ho oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? until seven times?

Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, ho ould make a reckoning ith his servants.
And hen he had begun to reckon, one as brought unto him, that oed him ten thousand talents.
But forasmuch as he had not \add hereith\add* to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his ife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.

And the lord of that servant, being moved ith compassion, released him, and forgave him the debt.
But that servant ent out, and found one of his fello-servants, ho oed him a hundred shillings: and he laid hold on him, and took \add him\add* by the throat, saying, Pay hat thou oest.

And it came to pass hen Jesus had finished these ords, he departed from Galilee, and came into the borders of Judæa beyond the Jordan;

Honor thy father and thy mother; and, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.

And hen the disciples heard it, they ere astonished exceedingly, saying, Who then can be saved?
And Jesus looking upon \add them\add* said to them, With men this is impossible; but ith God all things are possible.

And hen they heard it, they marvelled, and left him, and ent aay.

and say, If e had been in the days of our fathers, e should not have been partakers ith them in the blood of the prophets.

And Jesus ent out from the temple, and as going on his ay; and his disciples came to him to sho him the buildings of the temple.

And as he sat on the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, hen shall these things be? and hat \add shall be\add* the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the orld?
And Jesus ansered and said unto them, Take heed that no man lead you astray.

And then shall many stumble, and shall deliver up one another, and shall hate one another.
And many false prophets shall arise, and shall lead many astray.
And because iniquity shall be multiplied, the love of the many shall ax cold.
But he that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved.
And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in the hole orld for a testimony unto all the nations; and then shall the end come.
When therefore ye see the abomination of desolation, hich as spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place ( let him that readeth understand),
then let them that are in Judæa flee unto the mountains:
let him that is on the housetop not go don to take out the things that are in his house:
and let him that is in the field not return back to take his cloak.
But oe unto them that are ith child and to them that give suck in those days!
And pray ye that your flight be not in the inter, neither on a sabbath:
for then shall be great tribulation, such as hath not been from the beginning of the orld until no, no, nor ever shall be.
And except those days had been shortened, no flesh ould have been saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.
Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is the Christ, or, Here; believe \add it\add* not.
For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall sho great signs and onders; so as to lead astray, if possible, even the elect.
Behold, I have told you beforehand.
If therefore they shall say unto you, Behold, he is in the ilderness; go not forth: Behold, he is in the inner chambers; believe \add it\add* not.
For as the lightning cometh forth from the east, and is seen even unto the est; so shall be the coming of the Son of man.
Wheresoever the carcase is, there ill the eagles be gathered together.

No from the fig tree learn her parable: hen her branch is no become tender, and putteth forth its leaves, ye kno that the summer is nigh;
even so ye also, hen ye see all these things, kno ye that he is nigh, \add even\add* at the doors.

Heaven and earth shall pass aay, but my ords shall not pass aay.
But of that day and hour knoeth no one, not even the angels of heaven, neither the Son, but the Father only.

and they kne not until the flood came, and took them all aay; so shall be the coming of the Son of man.
Then shall to men be in the field; one is taken, and one is left:
to omen \add shall be\add* grinding at the mill; one is taken, and one is left.
Watch therefore: for ye kno not on hat day your Lord cometh.
But kno this, that if the master of the house had knon in hat atch the thief as coming, he ould have atched, and ould not have suffered his house to be broken through.

Who then is the faithful and ise servant, hom his lord hath set over his household, to give them their food in due season?
Blessed is that servant, hom his lord hen he cometh shall find so doing.

And the scribes of the Pharisees, hen they sa that he as eating ith the sinners and publicans, said unto his disciples, \add Ho is it\add* that he eateth and drinketh ith publicans and sinners?

And Jesus said unto them, Can the sons of the bridechamber fast, hile the bridegroom is ith them? as long as they have the bridegroom ith them, they cannot fast.
But the days ill come, hen the bridegroom shall be taken aay from them, and then ill they fast in that day.
No man seeth a piece of undressed cloth on an old garment: else that hich should fill it up taketh from it, the ne from the old, and a orse rent is made.
And no man putteth ne ine into old ine-skins; else the ine ill burst the skins, and the ine perisheth, and the skins: but \add they put\add* ne ine into fresh ine-skins.
And it came to pass, that he as going on the sabbath day through the grainfields; and his disciples began, as they ent, to pluck the ears.
And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, hy do they on the sabbath day that hich is not laful?
And he said unto them, Did ye never read hat David did, hen he had need, and as hungry, he, and they that ere ith him?
Ho he entered into the house of God hen Abiathar as high priest, and ate the shobread, hich it is not laful to eat save for the priests, and gave also to them that ere ith him?
And he said unto them, The sabbath as made for man, and not man for the sabbath:
so that the Son of man is lord even of the sabbath.
And he entered again into the synagogue; and there as a man there ho had his hand ithered.
And they atched him, hether he ould heal him on the sabbath day; that they might accuse him.
And he saith unto the man that had his hand ithered, Stand forth.
And he saith unto them, Is it laful on the sabbath day to do good, or to do harm? to save a life, or to kill? But they held their peace.
And hen he had looked round about on them ith anger, being grieved at the hardening of their heart, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he stretched it forth; and his hand as restored.
And the Pharisees ent out, and straightay ith the Herodians took counsel against him, ho they might destroy him.
And Jesus ith his disciples ithdre to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee folloed; and from Judæa,
and from Jerusalem, and from Idumæa, and beyond the Jordan, and about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing hat great things he did, came unto him.
And he spake to his disciples, that a little boat should ait on him because of the crod, lest they should throng him:
for he had healed many; insomuch that as many as had plagues pressed upon him that they might touch him.
And the unclean spirits, hensoever they beheld him, fell don before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God.
And he charged them much that they should not make him knon.
And he goeth up into the mountain, and calleth unto him hom he himself ould; and they ent unto him.
And he appointed telve, that they might be ith him, and that he might send them forth to preach,
and to have authority to cast out demons:
and Simon he surnamed Peter;
and James the \add son\add* of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and them he surnamed Boanerges, hich is, Sons of thunder:
and Andre, and Philip, and Bartholome, and Matthe, and Thomas, and James the \add son\add* of Alphæus, and Thaddæus, and Simon the Cananæan,
and Judas Iscariot, ho also betrayed him. And he cometh into a house.
And the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
And hen his friends heard it, they ent out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself.
And the scribes that came don from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and, By the prince of the demons casteth he out the demons.
And he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, Ho can Satan cast out Satan?
And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a house be divided against itself, that house ill not be able to stand.
And if Satan hath risen up against himself, and is divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.
But no one can enter into the house of the strong \add man\add*, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong \add man\add*; and then he ill spoil his house.
Verily I say unto you, All their sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and their blasphemies hereith soever they shall blaspheme:
but hosoever shall blaspheme against the Holy Spirit hath never forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin:
because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.
And there come his mother and his brethren; and, standing ithout, they sent unto him, calling him.
And a multitude as sitting about him; and they say unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren ithout seek for thee.
And he ansereth them, and saith, Who is my mother and my brethren?
And looking round on them that sat round about him, he saith, Behold, my mother and my brethren!
For hosoever shall do the ill of God, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.

And again he began to teach by the sea side. And there is gathered unto him a very great multitude, so that he entered into a boat, and sat in the sea; and all the multitude ere by the sea on the land.
And he taught them many things in parables, and said unto them in his teaching,
Hearken: Behold, the soer ent forth to so:
and it came to pass, as he soed, some \add seed\add* fell by the ay side, and the birds came and devoured it.
And other fell on the rocky \add ground\add*, here it had not much earth; and straightay it sprang up, because it had no deepness of earth:
and hen the sun as risen, it as scorched; and because it had no root, it ithered aay.
And other fell among the thorns, and the thorns gre up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
And others fell into the good ground, and yielded fruit, groing up and increasing; and brought forth, thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.
And he said, Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.
And hen he as alone, they that ere about him ith the telve asked of him the parables.
And he said unto them, Unto you is given the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are ithout, all things are done in parables:
that seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest haply they should turn again, and it should be forgiven them.
And he saith unto them, Kno ye not this parable? and ho shall ye kno all the parables?
The soer soeth the ord.
And these are they by the ay side, here the ord is son; and hen they have heard, straightay cometh Satan, and taketh aay the ord hich hath been son in them.
And these in like manner are they that are son upon the rocky \add places\add*, ho, hen they have heard the ord, straightay receive it ith joy;
and they have no root in themselves, but endure for a hile; then, hen tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the ord, straightay they stumble.
And others are they that are son among the thorns; these are they that have heard the ord,
and the cares of the orld, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the ord, and it becometh unfruitful.
And those are they that ere son upon the good ground; such as hear the ord, and accept it, and bear fruit, thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.
And he said unto them, Is the lamp brought to be put under the bushel, or under the bed, \add and\add* not to be put on the stand?
For there is nothing hid, save that it should be manifested; neither as \add anything\add* made secret, but that it should come to light.
If any man hath ears to hear, let him hear.
And he said unto them, Take heed hat ye hear: ith hat measure ye mete it shall be measured unto you; and more shall be given unto you.
For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken aay even that hich he hath.
And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed upon the earth;
and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and gro, he knoeth not ho.
The earth beareth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
But hen the fruit is ripe, straightay he putteth forth the sickle, because the harvest is come.
And he said, Ho shall e liken the kingdom of God? or in hat parable shall e set it forth?
It is like a grain of mustard seed, hich, hen it is son upon the earth, though it be less than all the seeds that are upon the earth,
yet hen it is son, groeth up, and becometh greater than all the herbs, and putteth out great branches; so that the birds of the heaven can lodge under the shado thereof.
And ith many such parables spake he the ord unto them, as they ere able to hear it;
and ithout a parable spake he not unto them: but privately to his on disciples he expounded all things.
And on that day, hen even as come, he saith unto them, Let us go over unto the other side.
And leaving the multitude, they take him ith them, even as he as, in the boat. And other boats ere ith him.
And there ariseth a great storm of ind, and the aves beat into the boat, insomuch that the boat as no filling.
And he himself as in the stern, asleep on the cushion: and they aake him, and say unto him, Teacher, carest thou not that e perish?
And he aoke, and rebuked the ind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the ind ceased, and there as a great calm.
And he said unto them, Why are ye fearful? have ye not yet faith?
And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, Who then is this, that even the ind and the sea obey him?
And they came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gerasenes.
And hen he as come out of the boat, straightay there met him out of the tombs a man ith an unclean spirit,
ho had his delling in the tombs: and no man could any more bind him, no, not ith a chain;
because that he had been often bound ith fetters and chains, and the chains had been rent asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: and no man had strength to tame him.
And alays, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he as crying out, and cutting himself ith stones.
And hen he sa Jesus from afar, he ran and orshipped him;
and crying out ith a loud voice, he saith, What have I to do ith thee, Jesus, thou Son of the Most High God? I adjure thee by God, torment me not.
For he said unto him, Come forth, thou unclean spirit, out of the man.
And he asked him, What is thy name? And he saith unto him, My name is Legion; for e are many.
And he besought him much that he ould not send them aay out of the country.
No there as there on the mountain side a great herd of sine feeding.
And they besought him, saying, Send us into the sine, that e may enter into them.

And he gave them leave. And the unclean spirits came out, and entered into the sine: and the herd rushed don the steep into the sea, \add in number\add* about to thousand; and they ere droned in the sea.
And they that fed them fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they came to see hat it as that had come to pass.
And they come to Jesus, and behold him that as possessed ith demons sitting, clothed and in his right mind, \add even\add* him that had the legion: and they ere afraid.
And they that sa it declared unto them ho it befell him that as possessed ith demons, and concerning the sine.
And they began to beseech him to depart from their borders.
And as he as entering into the boat, he that had been possessed ith demons besought him that he might be ith him.
And he suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go to thy house unto thy friends, and tell them ho great things the Lord hath done for thee, and \add ho\add* he had mercy on thee.
And he ent his ay, and began to publish in Decapolis ho great things Jesus had done for him: and all men marvelled.
And hen Jesus had crossed over again in the boat unto the other side, a great multitude as gathered unto him; and he as by the sea.
And there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jaïrus by name; and seeing him, he falleth at his feet,
and beseecheth him much, saying, My little daughter is at the point of death: \add I pray thee\add*, that thou come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be made hole, and live.
And he ent ith him; and a great multitude folloed him, and they thronged him.
And a oman, ho had an issue of blood telve years,
and had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and as nothing bettered, but rather gre orse,

For she said, If I touch but his garments, I shall be made hole.
And straightay the fountain of her blood as dried up; and she felt in her body that she as healed of her plague.
And straightay Jesus, perceiving in himself that the poer \add proceeding\add* from him had gone forth, turned him about in the crod, and said, Who touched my garments?

And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.
But the oman fearing and trembling, knoing hat had been done to her, came and fell don before him, and told him all the truth.

While he yet spake, they come from the ruler of the synagogue’s \add house\add*, saying, Thy daughter is dead: hy troublest thou the Teacher any further?
But Jesus, not heeding the ord spoken, saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Fear not, only believe.

And they come to the house of the ruler of the synagogue; and he beholdeth a tumult, and \add many\add* eeping and ailing greatly.

For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s ife; for he had married her.
For John said unto Herod, It is not laful for thee to have thy brother’ s ife.

And hen a convenient day as come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, and the high captains, and the chief men of Galilee;

and hen the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and them that sat at meat ith him; and the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me hatsoever thou ilt, and I ill give it thee.
And he sare unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I ill give it thee, unto the half of my kingdom.
And she ent out, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptizer.
And she came in straightay ith haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I ill that thou forthith give me on a platter the head of John the Baptist.
And the king as exceeding sorry; but for the sake of his oaths, and of them that sat at meat, he ould not reject her.
And straightay the king sent forth a soldier of his guard, and commanded to bring his head: and he ent and beheaded him in the prison,

And hen his disciples heard \add thereof\add*, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.
And the apostles gather themselves together unto Jesus; and they told him all things, hatsoever they had done, and hatsoever they had taught.
And he saith unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a hile. For there ere many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
And they ent aay in the boat to a desert place apart.
And \add the people\add* sa them going, and many kne \add them\add*, and they ran together there on foot from all the cities, and outent them.

And hen the day as no far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, The place is desert, and the day is no far spent;
send them aay, that they may go into the country and villages round about, and buy themselves somehat to eat.
But he ansered and said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall e go and buy to hundred shillings’ orth of bread, and give them to eat?
And he saith unto them, Ho many loaves have ye? go \add and\add* see. And hen they kne, they say, Five, and to fishes.

And they sat don in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties.

And hen even as come, the boat as in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land.

but they, hen they sa him alking on the sea, supposed that it as a ghost, and cried out;

And hen they had crossed over, they came to the land unto Gennesaret, and moored to the shore.
And hen they ere come out of the boat, straightay \add the people\add* kne him,
and ran round about that hole region, and began to carry about on their beds those that ere sick, here they heard he as.

and had seen that some of his disciples ate their bread ith defiled, that is, unashen, hands.
( For the Pharisees, and all the Jes, except they ash their hands diligently, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders;

and \add hen they come\add* from the marketplace, except they bathe themselves, they eat not; and many other things there are, hich they have received to hold, ashings of cups, and pots, and brasen vessels.)
And the Pharisees and the scribes ask him, Why alk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread ith defiled hands?
And he said unto them, Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is ritten, This people honoreth me ith their lips, But their heart is far from me.
But in vain do they orship me, Teaching \add as their\add* doctrines the precepts of men.
Ye leave the commandment of God, and hold fast the tradition of men.
And he said unto them, Full ell do ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your tradition.
For Moses said, Honor thy father and thy mother; and, He that speaketh evil of father or mother, let him die the death:
but ye say, If a man shall say to his father or his mother, That hereith thou mightest have been profited by me is Corban, that is to say, Given \add to God\add*;
ye no longer suffer him to do aught for his father or his mother;
making void the ord of God by your tradition, hich ye have delivered: and many such like things ye do.
And he called to him the multitude again, and said unto them, Hear me all of you, and understand:
there is nothing from ithout the man, that going into him can defile him; but the things hich proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.
And hen he as entered into the house from the multitude, his disciples asked of him the parable.
And he saith unto them, Are ye so ithout understanding also? Perceive ye not, that hatsoever from ithout goeth into the man, \add it\add* cannot defile him;
because it goeth not into his heart, but into his belly, and goeth out into the draught? \add This he said\add*, making all meats clean.
And he said, That hich proceedeth out of the man, that defileth the man.
For from ithin, out of the heart of men, evil thoughts proceed, fornications, thefts, murders, adulteries,
covetings, ickednesses, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, railing, pride, foolishness:
all these evil things proceed from ithin, and defile the man.
And from thence he arose, and ent aay into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. And he entered into a house, and ould have no man kno it; and he could not be hid.
But straightay a oman, hose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell don at his feet.
No the oman as a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. And she besought him that he ould cast forth the demon out of her daughter.
And he said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread and cast it to the dogs.
But she ansered and saith unto him, Yea, Lord; even the dogs under the table eat of the children’ s crumbs.
And he said unto her, For this saying go thy ay; the demon is gone out of thy daughter.
And she ent aay unto her house, and found the child laid upon the bed, and the demon gone out.
And again he ent out from the borders of Tyre, and came through Sidon unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the borders of Decapolis.
And they bring unto him one that as deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to lay his hand upon him.
And he took him aside from the multitude privately, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spat, and touched his tongue;
and looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.
And his ears ere opened, and the bond of his tongue as loosed, and he spake plain.
And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it.
And they ere beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things ell; he maketh even the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.
In those days, hen there as again a great multitude, and they had nothing to eat, he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them,
I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue ith me no three days, and have nothing to eat:
and if I send them aay fasting to their home, they ill faint on the ay; and some of them are come from far.
And his disciples ansered him, Whence shall one be able to fill these men ith bread here in a desert place?
And he asked them, Ho many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.

And he commandeth the multitude to sit don on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and having given thanks, he brake, and gave to his disciples, to set before them; and they set them before the multitude.
And they had a fe small fishes: and having blessed them, he commanded to set these also before them.
And they ate, and ere filled: and they took up, of broken pieces that remained over, seven baskets.
And they ere about four thousand: and he sent them aay.
And straightay he entered into the boat ith his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question ith him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, trying him.
And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.
And he left them, and again entering into \add the boat\add* departed to the other side.
And they forgot to take bread; and they had not in the boat ith them more than one loaf.
And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beare of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.
And they reasoned one ith another, saying, We have no bread.
And Jesus perceiving it saith unto them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? do ye not yet perceive, neither understand? have ye your heart hardened?
Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?
When I brake the five loaves among the five thousand, ho many baskets full of broken pieces took ye up? They say unto him, Telve.
And hen the seven among the four thousand, ho many basketfuls of broken pieces took ye up? And they say unto him, Seven.
And he said unto them, Do ye not yet understand?
And they come unto Bethsaida. And they bring to him a blind man, and beseech him to touch him.
And he took hold of the blind man by the hand, and brought him out of the village; and hen he had spit on his eyes, and laid his hands upon him, he asked him, Seest thou aught?
And he looked up, and said, I see men; for I behold \add them\add* as trees, alking.
Then again he laid his hands upon his eyes; and he looked stedfastly, and as restored, and sa all things clearly.
And he sent him aay to his home, saying, Do not even enter into the village.
And Jesus ent forth, and his disciples, into the villages of Cæsarea Philippi: and on the ay he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Who do men say that I am?
And they told him, saying, John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; but others, One of the prophets.
And he asked them, But ho say ye that I am? Peter ansereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.
And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.
And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, and the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
And he spake the saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.
But he turning about, and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, and saith, Get thee behind me, Satan; for thou mindest not the things of God, but the things of men.
And he called unto him the multitude ith his disciples, and said unto them, If any man ould come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follo me.
For hosoever ould save his life shall lose it; and hosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s shall save it.
For hat doth it profit a man, to gain the hole orld, and forfeit his life?
For hat should a man give in exchange for his life?
For hosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my ords in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of man also shall be ashamed of him, hen he cometh in the glory of his Father ith the holy angels.
And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, There are some here of them that stand \add by\add*, ho shall in no ise taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God come ith poer.
And after six days Jesus taketh ith him Peter, and James, and John, and bringeth them up into a high mountain apart by themselves: and he as transfigured before them;
and his garments became glistering, exceeding hite, so as no fuller on earth can hiten them.
And there appeared unto them Elijah ith Moses: and they ere talking ith Jesus.
And Peter ansereth and saith to Jesus, Rabbi, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
For he kne not hat to anser; for they became sore afraid.
And there came a cloud overshadoing them: and there came a voice out of the cloud, This is my beloved Son: hear ye him.
And suddenly looking round about, they sa no one any more, save Jesus only ith themselves.
And as they ere coming don from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man hat things they had seen, save hen the Son of man should have risen again from the dead.
And they kept the saying, questioning among themselves hat the rising again from the dead should mean.
And they asked him, saying, \add Ho is it\add* that the scribes say that Elijah must first come?
And he said unto them, Elijah indeed cometh first, and restoreth all things: and ho is it ritten of the Son of man, that he should suffer many things and be set at nought?
But I say unto you, that Elijah is come, and they have also done unto him hatsoever they ould, even as it is ritten of him.
And hen they came to the disciples, they sa a great multitude about them, and scribes questioning ith them.
And straightay all the multitude, hen they sa him, ere greatly amazed, and running to him saluted him.
And he asked them, What question ye ith them?
And one of the multitude ansered him, Teacher, I brought unto thee my son, ho hath a dumb spirit;
and heresoever it taketh him, it dasheth him don: and he foameth, and grindeth his teeth, and pineth aay: and I spake to thy disciples that they should cast it out; and they ere not able.
And he ansereth them and saith, O faithless generation, ho long shall I be ith you? ho long shall I bear ith you? bring him unto me.
And they brought him unto him: and hen he sa him, straightay the spirit tare him grievously; and he fell on the ground, and alloed foaming.
And he asked his father, Ho long time is it since this hath come unto him? And he said, From a child.
And oft-times it hath cast him both into the fire and into the aters, to destroy him: but if thou canst do anything, have compassion on us, and help us.
And Jesus said unto him, If thou canst! All things are possible to him that believeth.
Straightay the father of the child cried out, and said, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
And hen Jesus sa that a multitude came running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying unto him, Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I command thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.
And having cried out, and torn him much, he came out: and \add the boy\add* became as one dead; insomuch that the more part said, He is dead.
But Jesus took him by the hand, and raised him up; and he arose.
And hen he as come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, \add Ho is it\add* that e could not cast it out?
And he said unto them, This kind can come out by nothing, save by prayer.
And they ent forth from thence, and passed through Galilee; and he ould not that any man should kno it.

But they held their peace: for they had disputed one ith another on the ay, ho \add as\add* the greatest.

Whosoever shall receive one of such little children in my name, receiveth me: and hosoever receiveth me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.
John said unto him, Teacher, e sa one casting out demons in thy name; and e forbade him, because he folloed not us.

For he that is not against us is for us.
For hosoever shall give you a cup of ater to drink, because ye are Christ’s, verily I say unto you, he shall in no ise lose his reard.

And if thy foot cause thee to stumble, cut it off: it is good for thee to enter into life halt, rather than having thy to feet to be cast into hell.

And Jesus looking upon him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go, sell hatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follo me.

While ye have the light, believe on the light, that ye may become sons of light. These things spake Jesus, and he departed and hid himself from them.
But though he had done so many signs before them, yet they believed not on him:
that the ord of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, hich he spake, Lord, ho hath believed our report? And to hom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?
For this cause they could not believe, for that Isaiah said again,
He hath blinded their eyes, and he hardened their heart; Lest they should see ith their eyes, and perceive ith their heart, And should turn, And I should heal them.
These things said Isaiah, because he sa his glory; and he spake of him.
Nevertheless even of the rulers many believed on him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess \add it\add*, lest they should be put out of the synagogue:
for they loved the glory \add that is\add* of men more than the glory \add that is\add* of God.
And Jesus cried and said, He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me.
And he that beholdeth me beholdeth him that sent me.
I am come a light into the orld, that hosoever believeth on me may not abide in the darkness.
And if any man hear my sayings, and keep them not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the orld, but to save the orld.
He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my sayings, hath one that judgeth him: the ord that I spake, the same shall judge him in the last day.
For I spake not from myself; but the Father that sent me, he hath given me a commandment, hat I should say, and hat I should speak.
And I kno that his commandment is life eternal; the things therefore hich I speak, even as the Father hath said unto me, so I speak.
No before the feast of the passover, Jesus knoing that his hour as come that he should depart out of this orld unto the Father, having loved his on that ere in the orld, he loved them unto the end.
And during supper, the devil having already put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s \add son\add*, to betray him,
\add Jesus\add*, knoing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he came forth from God, and goeth unto God,
riseth from supper, and layeth aside his garments; and he took a toel, and girded himself.
Then he poureth ater into the basin, and began to ash the disciples’ feet, and to ipe them ith the toel hereith he as girded.
So he cometh to Simon Peter. He saith unto him, Lord, dost thou ash my feet?
Jesus ansered and said unto him, What I do thou knoest not no; but thou shalt understand hereafter.
Peter saith unto him, Thou shalt never ash my feet. Jesus ansered him, If I ash thee not, thou hast no part ith me.

For he kne him that should betray him; therefore said he, Ye are not all clean.

Ye call me, Teacher, and, Lord: and ye say ell; for so I am.
If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have ashed your feet, ye also ought to ash one another’ s feet.
For I have given you an example, that ye also should do as I have done to you.
Verily, verily, I say unto you, A servant is not greater than his lord; neither one that is sent greater than he that sent him.
If ye kno these things, blessed are ye if ye do them.
I speak not of you all: I kno hom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth my bread lifted up his heel against me.
