The disciples looked one on another, doubting of hom he spake.

Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? the ords that I say unto you I speak not from myself: but the Father abiding in me doeth his orks.
Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me: or else believe me for the very orks’ sake.
Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the orks that I do shall he do also; and greater \add orks\add* than these shall he do; because I go unto the Father.
And hatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that ill I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If ye shall ask anything in my name, that ill I do.
If ye love me, ye ill keep my commandments.
And I ill pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may be ith you for ever,
\add even\add* the Spirit of truth: hom the orld cannot receive; for it beholdeth him not, neither knoeth him: ye kno him; for he abideth ith you, and shall be in you.
I ill not leave you desolate: I come unto you.
Yet a little hile, and the orld beholdeth me no more; but ye behold me: because I live, ye shall live also.
In that day ye shall kno that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.
He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me: and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I ill love him, and ill manifest myself unto him.
Judas ( not Iscariot) saith unto him, Lord, hat is come to pass that thou ilt manifest thyself unto us, and not unto the orld?

But the Comforter, \add even\add* the Holy Spirit, hom the Father ill send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring to your remembrance all that I said unto you.
Peace I leave ith you; my peace I give unto you: not as the orld giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.

I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.

Already ye are clean because of the ord hich I have spoken unto you.
Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; so neither can ye, except ye abide in me.
I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same beareth much fruit: for apart from me ye can do nothing.
If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is ithered; and they gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.
If ye abide in me, and my ords abide in you, ask hatsoever ye ill, and it shall be done unto you.
Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; and \add so\add* shall ye be my disciples.
Even as the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you: abide ye in my love.

No longer do I call you servants; for the servant knoeth not hat his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I heard from my Father I have made knon unto you.

Ye did not choose me, but I chose you, and appointed you, that ye should go and bear fruit, and \add that\add* your fruit should abide: that hatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.

If the orld hateth you, ye kno that it hath hated me before \add it hated\add* you.

\add Some\add* of his disciples therefore said one to another, What is this that he saith unto us, A little hile, and ye behold me not; and again a little hile, and ye shall see me: and, Because I go to the Father?

A oman hen she is in travail hath sorro, because her hour is come: but hen she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for the joy that a man is born into the orld.
And ye therefore no have sorro: but I ill see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no one taketh aay from you.

His disciples say, Lo, no speakest thou plainly, and speakest no dark saying.

Simon Peter therefore having a sord dre it, and struck the high priest’ s servant, and cut off his right ear. No the servant’ s name as Malchus.

They therefore cried out, Aay ith \add him\add*, aay ith \add him\add*, crucify him! Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests ansered, We have no king but Cæsar.
Then therefore he delivered him unto them to be crucified.
They took Jesus therefore: and he ent out, bearing the cross for himself, unto the place called The place of a skull, hich is called in Hebre Golgotha:
here they crucified him, and ith him to others, on either side one, and Jesus in the midst.

They said therefore one to another, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, hose it shall be: that the scripture might be fulfilled, hich saith, They parted my garments among them, And upon my vesture did they cast lots.

When Jesus therefore sa his mother, and the disciple standing by hom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold, thy son!

The Jes therefore, because it as the Preparation, that the bodies should not remain on the cross upon the sabbath ( for the day of that sabbath as a high \add day\add*), asked of Pilate that their legs might be broken, and \add that\add* they might be taken aay.

After these things Jesus manifested himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and he manifested \add himself\add* on this ise.

( No this man obtained a field ith the reard of his iniquity; and falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst, and all his boels gushed out.

For it is ritten in the book of Psalms, Let his habitation be made desolate, And let no man dell therein: His office let another take.
Of the men therefore that have companied ith us all the time that the Lord Jesus ent in and ent out among us,
beginning from the baptism of John, unto the day that he as received up from us, of these must one become a itness ith us of his resurrection.
And they put forard to, Joseph called Barsabbas, ho as surnamed Justus, and Matthias.
And they prayed, and said, Thou, Lord, ho knoest the hearts of all men, sho of these to the one hom thou hast chosen,
to take the place in this ministry and apostleship from hich Judas fell aay, that he might go to his on place.

And hen the day of Pentecost as no come, they ere all together in one place.
And suddenly there came from heaven a sound as of the rushing of a mighty ind, and it filled all the house here they ere sitting.
And there appeared unto them tongues parting asunder, like as of fire; and it sat upon each one of them.
And they ere all filled ith the Holy Spirit, and began to speak ith other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
No there ere delling at Jerusalem Jes, devout men, from every nation under heaven.

And they ere all amazed and marvelled, saying, Behold, are not all these that speak Galilæans?
And ho hear e, every man in our on language herein e ere born?
Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and the dellers in Mesopotamia, in Judæa and Cappadocia, in Pontus and Asia,
in Phrygia and Pamphylia, in Egypt and the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and sojourners from Rome, both Jes and proselytes,
Cretans and Arabians, e hear them speaking in our tongues the mighty orks of God.

But Peter, standing up ith the eleven, lifted up his voice, and spake forth unto them, \add saying\add*, Ye men of Judæa, and all ye that dell at Jerusalem, be this knon unto you, and give ear unto my ords.
For these are not drunken, as ye suppose; seeing it is \add but\add* the third hour of the day;
but this is that hich hath been spoken through the prophet Joel:

And it shall be in the last days, saith God, I ill pour forth of my Spirit upon all flesh: And your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, And your young men shall see visions, And your old men shall dream dreams:
Yea and on my servants and on my handmaidens in those days Will I pour forth of my Spirit; and they shall prophesy.
And I ill sho onders in the heaven above, And signs on the earth beneath; Blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke:
The sun shall be turned into darkness, And the moon into blood, Before the day of the Lord come, That great and notable \add day\add*:
And it shall be, that hosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
Ye men of Israel, hear these ords: Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God unto you by mighty orks and onders and signs hich God did by him in the midst of you, even as ye yourselves kno;
him, being delivered up by the determinate counsel and foreknoledge of God, ye by the hand of laless men did crucify and slay:

Therefore my heart as glad, and my tongue rejoiced; Moreover my flesh also shall dell in hope:
Because thou ilt not leave my soul unto Hades, Neither ilt thou give thy Holy One to see corruption.
Thou madest knon unto me the ays of life; Thou shalt make me full of gladness ith thy countenance.

Till I make thine enemies the footstool of thy feet.

No hen they heard \add this\add*, they ere pricked in their heart, and said unto Peter and the rest of the apostles, Brethren, hat shall e do?

And he gave heed unto them, expecting to receive something from them.
But Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but hat I have, that give I thee. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, alk.
And he took him by the right hand, and raised him up: and immediately his feet and his ankle-bones received strength.
And leaping up, he stood, and began to alk; and he entered ith them into the temple, alking, and leaping, and praising God.
And all the people sa him alking and praising God:
and they took knoledge of him, that it as he that sat for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple; and they ere filled ith onder and amazement at that hich had happened unto him.
And as he held Peter and John, all the people ran together unto them in the porch that is called Solomon’s, greatly ondering.
And hen Peter sa it, he ansered unto the people, Ye men of Israel, hy marvel ye at this man? or hy fasten ye your eyes on us, as though by our on poer or godliness e had made him to alk?

The God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers, hath glorified his Servant Jesus; hom ye delivered up, and denied before the face of Pilate, hen he had determined to release him.

But the things hich God foreshoed by the mouth of all the prophets, that his Christ should suffer, he thus fulfilled.
Repent ye therefore, and turn again, that your sins may be blotted out, that so there may come seasons of refreshing from the presence of the Lord;
and that he may send the Christ ho hath been appointed for you, \add even\add* Jesus:

And it shall be, that every soul that shall not hearken to that prophet, shall be utterly destroyed from among the people.
Yea and all the prophets from Samuel and them that folloed after, as many as have spoken, they also told of these days.
Ye are the sons of the prophets, and of the covenant hich God made ith your fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.
Unto you first God, having raised up his Servant, sent him to bless you, in turning aay every one of you from your iniquities.
And as they spake unto the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,
being sore troubled because they taught the people, and proclaimed in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
And they laid hands on them, and put them in ard unto the morro: for it as no eventide.

and Annas the high priest \add as there\add*, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as ere of the kindred of the high priest.

if e this day are examined concerning a good deed done to an impotent man, by hat means this man is made hole;

be it knon unto you all, and to all the people of Israel, that in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, hom ye crucified, hom God raised from the dead, \add even\add* in him doth this man stand here before you hole.
He is the stone hich as set at nought of you the builders, hich as made the head of the corner.
And in none other is there salvation: for neither is there any other name under heaven, that is given among men, herein e must be saved.
No hen they beheld the boldness of Peter and John, and had perceived that they ere unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knoledge of them, that they had been ith Jesus.
And seeing the man that as healed standing ith them, they could say nothing against it.
But hen they had commanded them to go aside out of the council, they conferred among themselves,
saying, What shall e do to these men? for that indeed a notable miracle hath been rought through them, is manifest to all that dell in Jerusalem; and e cannot deny it.
But that it spread no further among the people, let us threaten them, that they speak henceforth to no man in this name.
And they called them, and charged them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John ansered and said unto them, Whether it is right in the sight of God to hearken unto you rather than unto God, judge ye:
for e cannot but speak the things hich e sa and heard.
And they, hen they had further threatened them, let them go, finding nothing ho they might punish them, because of the people; for all men glorified God for that hich as done.
For the man as more than forty years old, on hom this miracle of healing as rought.
And being let go, they came to their on company, and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said unto them.
And they, hen they heard it, lifted up their voice to God ith one accord, and said, O Lord, thou that didst make the heaven and the earth and the sea, and all that in them is:
ho by the Holy Spirit, \add by\add* the mouth of our father David thy servant, didst say, Why did the Gentiles rage, And the peoples imagine vain things?
The kings of the earth set themselves in array, And the rulers ere gathered together, Against the Lord, and against his Anointed:
for of a truth in this city against thy holy Servant Jesus, hom thou didst anoint, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, ith the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel, ere gathered together,
to do hatsoever thy hand and thy counsel foreordained to come to pass.
And no, Lord, look upon their threatenings: and grant unto thy servants to speak thy ord ith all boldness,

And hen they had prayed, the place as shaken herein they ere gathered together; and they ere all filled ith the Holy Spirit, and they spake the ord of God ith boldness.

having a field, sold it, and brought the money and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
But a certain man named Ananias, ith Sapphira his ife, sold a possession,

But Peter \add said\add* unto her, Ho is it that ye have agreed together to try the Spirit of the Lord? behold, the feet of them that have buried thy husband are at the door, and they shall carry thee out.

And great fear came upon the hole church, and upon all that heard these things.

and believers ere the more added to the Lord, multitudes both of men and omen:

No a certain Je named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus; and he as mighty in the scriptures.

and he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But hen Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the ay of God more accurately.
And hen he as minded to pass over into Achaia, the brethren encouraged him, and rote to the disciples to receive him: and hen he as come, he helped them much that had believed through grace;
for he poerfully confuted the Jes, \add and that\add* publicly, shoing by the scriptures that Jesus as the Christ.
And it came to pass, that, hile Apollos as at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper country came to Ephesus, and found certain disciples:
and he said unto them, Did ye receive the Holy Spirit hen ye believed? And they \add said\add* unto him, Nay, e did not so much as hear hether the Holy Spirit as \add given\add*.

insomuch that unto the sick ere carried aay from his body handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits ent out.

So mightily gre the ord of the Lord and prevailed.
No after these things ere ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, hen he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.

And about that time there arose no small stir concerning the Way.
For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, ho made silver shrines of Diana, brought no little business unto the craftsmen;
hom he gathered together, ith the orkmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye kno that by this business e have our ealth.
And ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned aay much people, saying that they are no gods, that are made ith hands:

and not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana be made of no account, and that she should even be deposed from her magnificence hom all Asia and the orld orshippeth.
And hen they heard this they ere filled ith rath, and cried out, saying, Great \add is\add* Diana of the Ephesians.
And the city as filled ith the confusion: and they rushed ith one accord into the theatre, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel.
And hen Paul as minded to enter in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
And certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent unto him and besought him not to adventure himself into the theatre.
Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly as in confusion; and the more part kne not herefore they ere come together.
And they brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jes putting him forard. And Alexander beckoned ith the hand, and ould have made a defence unto the people.

And hen the tonclerk had quieted the multitude, he saith, Ye men of Ephesus, hat man is there ho knoeth not that the city of the Ephesians is temple-keeper of the great Diana, and of the \add image\add* hich fell don from Jupiter?
Seeing then that these things cannot be gainsaid, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rash.
For ye have brought \add hither\add* these men, ho are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of our goddess.
If therefore Demetrius, and the craftsmen that are ith him, have a matter against any man, the courts are open, and there are proconsuls: let them accuse one another.
But if ye seek anything about other matters, it shall be settled in the regular assembly.
For indeed e are in danger to be accused concerning this day’s riot, there being no cause \add for it\add*: and as touching it e shall not be able to give account of this concourse.
And hen he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
And after the uproar ceased, Paul having sent for the disciples and exhorted them, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.
And hen he had gone through those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece.
And hen he had spent three months \add there\add*, and a plot as laid against him by the Jes as he as about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.

And there accompanied him as far as Asia, Sopater of Beroea, \add the son\add* of Pyrrhus; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
But these had gone before, and ere aiting for us at Troas.
And e sailed aay from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; here e tarried seven days.
And upon the first day of the eek, hen e ere gathered together to break bread, Paul discoursed ith them, intending to depart on the morro; and prolonged his speech until midnight.
And there ere many lights in the upper chamber here e ere gathered together.

And there sat in the indo a certain young man named Eutychus, borne don ith deep sleep; and as Paul discoursed yet longer, being borne don by his sleep he fell don from the third story, and as taken up dead.
And Paul ent don, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Make ye no ado; for his life is in him.
And hen he as gone up, and had broken the bread, and eaten, and had talked ith them a long hile, even till break of day, so he departed.
And they brought the lad alive, and ere not a little comforted.
But e, going before to the ship, set sail for Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, intending himself to go by land.
And hen he met us at Assos, e took him in, and came to Mitylene.
And sailing from thence, e came the folloing day over against Chios; and the next day e touched at Samos; and the day after e came to Miletus.
For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he as hastening, if it ere possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called to him the elders of the church.
And hen they ere come to him, he said unto them, Ye yourselves kno, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, after hat manner I as ith you all the time,
serving the Lord ith all loliness of mind, and ith tears, and ith trials hich befell me by the plots of the Jes;
ho I shrank not from declaring unto you anything that as profitable, and teaching you publicly, and from house to house,
testifying both to Jes and to Greeks repentance toard God, and faith toard our Lord Jesus Christ.
And no, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knoing the things that shall befall me there:
save that the Holy Spirit testifieth unto me in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.
But I hold not my life of any account as dear unto myself, so that I may accomplish my course, and the ministry hich I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
And no, behold, I kno that ye all, among hom I ent about preaching the kingdom, shall see my face no more.
Wherefore I testify unto you this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.
For I shrank not from declaring unto you the hole counsel of God.
Take heed unto yourselves, and to all the flock, in hich the Holy Spirit hath made you bishops, to feed the church of the Lord hich he purchased ith his on blood.
I kno that after my departing grievous olves shall enter in among you, not sparing the flock;
and from among your on selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to dra aay the disciples after them.
Wherefore atch ye, remembering that by the space of three years I ceased not to admonish every one night and day ith tears.
And no I commend you to God, and to the ord of his grace, hich is able to build \add you\add* up, and to give \add you\add* the inheritance among all them that are sanctified.
I coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.
Ye yourselves kno that these hands ministered unto my necessities, and to them that ere ith me.
In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring ye ought to help the eak, and to remember the ords of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
And hen he had thus spoken, he kneeled don and prayed ith them all.

And hen it came to pass that e ere parted from them and had set sail, e came ith a straight course unto Cos, and the next day unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:
and having found a ship crossing over unto Phoenicia, e ent aboard, and set sail.

And coming to us, and taking Paul’s girdle, he bound his on feet and hands, and said, Thus saith the Holy Spirit, So shall the Jes at Jerusalem bind the man that oneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.

What is it therefore? they ill certainly hear that thou art come.
Do therefore this that e say to thee: We have four men that have a vo on them;

these take, and purify thyself ith them, and be at charges for them, that they may shave their heads: and all shall kno that there is no truth in the things hereof they have been informed concerning thee; but that thou thyself also alkest orderly, keeping the la.

But as touching the Gentiles that have believed, e rote, giving judgment that they should keep themselves from things sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from hat is strangled, and from fornication.

For they had before seen ith him in the city Trophimus the Ephesian, hom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.

And as they ere seeking to kill him, tidings came up to the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem as in confusion.
And forthith he took soldiers and centurions, and ran don upon them: and they, hen they sa the chief captain and the soldiers, left off beating Paul.
Then the chief captain came near, and laid hold on him, and commanded him to be bound ith to chains; and inquired ho he as, and hat he had done.
And some shouted one thing, some another, among the crod: and hen he could not kno the certainty for the uproar, he commanded him to be brought into the castle.
And hen he came upon the stairs, so it as that he as borne of the soldiers for the violence of the crod;
for the multitude of the people folloed after, crying out, Aay ith him.
And as Paul as about to be brought into the castle, he saith unto the chief captain, May I say something unto thee? And he said, Dost thou kno Greek?
Art thou not then the Egyptian, ho before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the ilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?

And hen he had given him leave, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned ith the hand unto the people; and hen there as made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebre language, saying,

I am a Je, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city, at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict manner of the la of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as ye all are this day:

As also the high priest doth bear me itness, and all the estate of the elders: from hom also I received letters unto the brethren, and journeyed to Damascus to bring them also that ere there unto Jerusalem in bonds to be punished.

And I ansered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, hom thou persecutest.

came unto me, and standing by me said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And in that very hour I looked up on him.

For thou shalt be a itness for him unto all men of hat thou hast seen and heard.

And they gave him audience unto this ord; and they lifted up their voice, and said, Aay ith such a fello from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.

And hen they had tied him up ith the thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it laful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
And hen the centurion heard it, he ent to the chief captain and told him, saying, What art thou about to do? for this man is a Roman.

And the chief captain ansered, With a great sum obtained I this citizenship. And Paul said, But I am \add a Roman\add* born.

But on the morro, desiring to kno the certainty herefore he as accused of the Jes, he loosed him, and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul don and set him before them.

But hen Paul perceived that the one part ere Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Brethren, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees: touching the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.

And hen there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go don and take him by force from among them, and bring him into the castle.

And the chief captain took him by the hand, and going aside asked him privately, What is it that thou hast to tell me?
And he said, The Jes have agreed to ask thee to bring don Paul to-morro unto the council, as though thou ouldest inquire somehat more exactly concerning him.

And he called unto him to of the centurions, and said, Make ready to hundred soldiers to go as far as Cæsarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen to hundred, at the third hour of the night:

Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix, greeting.
This man as seized by the Jes, and as about to be slain of them, hen I came upon them ith the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he as a Roman.

hom I found to be accused about questions of their la, but to have nothing laid to his charge orthy of death or of bonds.
And hen it as shon to me that there ould be a plot against the man, I sent him to thee forthith, charging his accusers also to speak against him before thee.
So the soldiers, as it as commanded them, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
But on the morro they left the horsemen to go ith him, and returned to the castle:
and they, hen they came to Cæsarea and delivered the letter to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
And hen he had read it, he asked of hat province he as; and hen he understood that he as of Cilicia,
I ill hear thee fully, said he, hen thine accusers also are come: and he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s palace.
And after five days the high priest Ananias came don ith certain elders, and \add ith\add* an orator, one Tertullus; and they informed the governor against Paul.
And hen he as called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee e enjoy much peace, and that by thy providence evils are corrected for this nation,
e accept it in all ays and in all places, most excellent Felix, ith all thankfulness.
But, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I entreat thee to hear us of thy clemency a fe ords.
For e have found this man a pestilent fello, and a mover of insurrections among all the Jes throughout the orld, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
ho moreover assayed to profane the temple: on hom also e laid hold:
from hom thou ilt be able, by examining him thyself, to take knoledge of all these things hereof e accuse him.
And the Jes also joined in the charge, affirming that these things ere so.
And hen the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, Paul ansered, Forasmuch as I kno that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I cheerfully make my defence:
seeing that thou canst take knoledge that it is not more than telve days since I ent up to orship at Jerusalem:
and neither in the temple did they find me disputing ith any man or stirring up a crod, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city.
Neither can they prove to thee the things hereof they no accuse me.
But this I confess unto thee, that after the Way hich they call a sect, so serve I the God of our fathers, believing all things hich are according to the la, and hich are ritten in the prophets;
having hope toard God, hich these also themselves look for, that there shall be a resurrection both of the just and unjust.
Herein I also exercise myself to have a conscience void of offence toard God and men alays.
No after some years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings:
amidst hich they found me purified in the temple, ith no crod, nor yet ith tumult: but \add there ere\add* certain Jes from Asia—
ho ought to have been here before thee, and to make accusation, if they had aught against me.
Or else let these men themselves say hat rong-doing they found hen I stood before the council,
except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question before you this day.
But Felix, having more exact knoledge concerning the Way, deferred them, saying, When Lysias the chief captain shall come don, I ill determine your matter.
And he gave order to the centurion that he should be kept in charge, and should have indulgence; and not to forbid any of his friends to minister unto him.
But after certain days, Felix came ith Drusilla, his ife, ho as a Jeess, and sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.
And as he reasoned of righteousness, and self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix as terrified, and ansered, Go thy ay for this time; and hen I have a convenient season, I ill call thee unto me.
He hoped ithal that money ould be given him of Paul: herefore also he sent for him the oftener, and communed ith him.
But hen to years ere fulfilled, Felix as succeeded by Porcius Festus; and desiring to gain favor ith the Jes, Felix left Paul in bonds.
Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days ent up to Jerusalem from Cæsarea.
And the chief priests and the principal men of the Jes informed him against Paul; and they besought him,
asking a favor against him, that he ould send for him to Jerusalem; laying a plot to kill him on the ay.
Hobeit Festus ansered, that Paul as kept in charge at Cæsarea, and that he himself as about to depart \add thither\add* shortly.
Let them therefore, saith he, that are of poer among you go don ith me, and if there is anything amiss in the man, let them accuse him.
And hen he had tarried among them not more than eight or ten days, he ent don unto Cæsarea; and on the morro he sat on the judgment-seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.
And hen he as come, the Jes that had come don from Jerusalem stood round about him, bringing against him many and grievous charges hich they could not prove;
hile Paul said in his defence, Neither against the la of the Jes, nor against the temple, nor against Cæsar, have I sinned at all.
But Festus, desiring to gain favor ith the Jes, ansered Paul and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
But Paul said, I am standing before Cæsar’s judgment-seat, here I ought to be judged: to the Jes have I done no rong, as thou also very ell knoest.

If then I am a rong-doer, and have committed anything orthy of death, I refuse not to die; but if none of those things is \add true\add* hereof these accuse me, no man can give me up unto them. I appeal unto Cæsar.
Then Festus, hen he had conferred ith the council, ansered, Thou hast appealed unto Cæsar: unto Cæsar shalt thou go.
No hen certain days ere passed, Agrippa the king and Bernice arrived at Cæsarea, and saluted Festus.
And as they tarried there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;
about hom, hen I as at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jes informed \add me\add*, asking for sentence against him.

To hom I ansered, that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man, before that the accused have the accusers face to face, and have had opportunity to make his defence concerning the matter laid against him.
When therefore they ere come together here, I made no delay, but on the next day sat on the judgment-seat, and commanded the man to be brought.
Concerning hom, hen the accusers stood up, they brought no charge of such evil things as I supposed;
but had certain questions against him of their on religion, and of one Jesus, ho as dead, hom Paul affirmed to be alive.
And I, being perplexed ho to inquire concerning these things, asked hether he ould go to Jerusalem and there be judged of these matters.
But hen Paul had appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor, I commanded him to be kept till I should send him to Cæsar.
And Agrippa \add said\add* unto Festus, I also could ish to hear the man myself. To-morro, saith he, thou shalt hear him.

So on the morro, hen Agrippa as come, and Bernice, ith great pomp, and they ere entered into the place of hearing ith the chief captains and the principal men of the city, at the command of Festus Paul as brought in.

And Festus saith, King Agrippa, and all men ho are here present ith us, ye behold this man, about hom all the multitude of the Jes made suit to me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
But I found that he had committed nothing orthy of death: and as he himself appealed to the emperor I determined to send him.
Of hom I have no certain thing to rite unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I may have somehat to rite.
For it seemeth to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not ithal to signify the charges against him.
And Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth his hand, and made his defence:
I think myself happy, king Agrippa, that I am to make my defence before thee this day touching all the things hereof I am accused by the Jes:
especially because thou art expert in all customs and questions hich are among the Jes: herefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
My manner of life then from my youth up, hich as from the beginning among mine on nation and at Jerusalem, kno all the Jes;
having knoledge of me from the first, if they be illing to testify, that after the straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
And no I stand \add here\add* to be judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers;
unto hich \add promise\add* our telve tribes, earnestly serving \add God\add* night and day, hope to attain. And concerning this hope I am accused by the Jes, O king!
Why is it judged incredible ith you, if God doth raise the dead?
I verily thought ith myself that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
And this I also did in Jerusalem: and I both shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and hen they ere put to death I gave my vote against them.
And punishing them oftentimes in all the synagogues, I strove to make them blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto foreign cities.
Whereupon as I journeyed to Damascus ith the authority and commission of the chief priests,
at midday, O king, I sa on the ay a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them that journeyed ith me.
And hen e ere all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying unto me in the Hebre language, Saul, Saul, hy persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the goad.
And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus hom thou persecutest.

But arise, and stand upon thy feet: for to this end have I appeared unto thee, to appoint thee a minister and a itness both of the things herein thou hast seen me, and of the things herein I ill appear unto thee;
delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto hom I send thee,

to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the poer of Satan unto God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among them that are sanctified by faith in me.
Wherefore, O king Agrippa, I as not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:

but declared both to them of Damascus first, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judæa, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing orks orthy of repentance.
For this cause the Jes seized me in the temple, and assayed to kill me.
Having therefore obtained the help that is from God, I stand unto this day testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but hat the prophets and Moses did say should come;
ho that the Christ must suffer, \add and\add* ho that he first by the resurrection of the dead should proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles.
And as he thus made his defence, Festus saith ith a loud voice, Paul, thou art mad; thy much learning is turning thee mad.
But Paul saith, I am not mad, most excellent Festus; but speak forth ords of truth and soberness.
For the king knoeth of these things, unto hom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him; for this hath not been done in a corner.
King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I kno that thou believest.
And Agrippa \add said\add* unto Paul, With but little persuasion thou ouldest fain make me a Christian.
And Paul \add said\add*, I ould to God, that hether ith little or ith much, not thou only, but also all that hear me this day, might become such as I am, except these bonds.
And the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat ith them:
and hen they had ithdran, they spake one to another, saying, This man doeth nothing orthy of death or of bonds.
And Agrippa said unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cæsar.
And hen it as determined that e should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
And embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, hich as about to sail unto the places on the coast of Asia, e put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being ith us.
And the next day e touched at Sidon: and Julius treated Paul kindly, and gave him leave to go unto his friends and refresh himself.
And putting to sea from thence, e sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the inds ere contrary.
And hen e had sailed across the sea hich is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, e came to Myra, \add a city\add* of Lycia.
And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy; and he put us therein.
And hen e had sailed sloly many days, and ere come ith difficulty over against Cnidus, the ind not further suffering us, e sailed under the lee of Crete, over against Salmone;
and ith difficulty coasting along it e came unto a certain place called Fair Havens; nigh hereunto as the city of Lasea.
And hen much time as spent, and the voyage as no dangerous, because the Fast as no already gone by, Paul admonished them,
and said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that the voyage ill be ith injury and much loss, not only of the lading and the ship, but also of our lives.
But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the oner of the ship, than to those things hich ere spoken by Paul.

And because the haven as not commodious to inter in, the more part advised to put to sea from thence, if by any means they could reach Phoenix, and inter \add there; hich is\add* a haven of Crete, looking north-east and south-east.
And hen the south ind ble softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they eighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close in shore.
But after no long time there beat don from it a tempestuous ind, hich is called Euraquilo:
and hen the ship as caught, and could not face the ind, e gave ay \add to it\add*, and ere driven.
And running under the lee of a small island called Cauda, e ere able, ith difficulty, to secure the boat:
and hen they had hoisted it up, they used helps, under-girding the ship; and, fearing lest they should be cast upon the Syrtis, they loered the gear, and so ere driven.
And as e labored exceedingly ith the storm, the next day they began to thro \add the freight\add* overboard;
and the third day they cast out ith their on hands the tackling of the ship.
And hen neither sun nor stars shone upon \add us\add* for many days, and no small tempest lay on \add us\add*, all hope that e should be saved as no taken aay.

And hen they had been long ithout food, then Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have set sail from Crete, and have gotten this injury and loss.
And no I exhort you to be of good cheer; for there shall be no loss of life among you, but \add only\add* of the ship.
For there stood by me this night an angel of the God hose I am, hom also I serve,
saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must stand before Cæsar: and lo, God hath granted thee all them that sail ith thee.
Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even so as it hath been spoken unto me.
But e must be cast upon a certain island.
But hen the fourteenth night as come, as e ere driven to and fro in the \add sea of\add* Adria, about midnight the sailors surmised that they ere draing near to some country:
and they sounded, and found tenty fathoms; and after a little space, they sounded again, and found fifteen fathoms.
And fearing lest haply e should be cast ashore on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and ished for the day.
And as the sailors ere seeking to flee out of the ship, and had loered the boat into the sea, under color as though they ould lay out anchors from the foreship,
Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
Then the soldiers cut aay the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
And hile the day as coming on, Paul besought them all to take some food, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye ait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.
Wherefore I beseech you to take some food: for this is for your safety: for there shall not a hair perish from the head of any of you.
And hen he had said this, and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all; and he brake it, and began to eat.
Then ere they all of good cheer, and themselves also took food.
And e ere in all in the ship to hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
And hen they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throing out the heat into the sea.
And hen it as day, they kne not the land: but they perceived a certain bay ith a beach, and they took counsel hether they could drive the ship upon it.
And casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time loosing the bands of the rudders; and hoisting up the foresail to the ind, they made for the beach.
But lighting upon a place here to seas met, they ran the vessel aground; and the foreship struck and remained unmoveable, but the stern began to break up by the violence \add of the aves\add*.
And the soldiers’ counsel as to kill the prisoners, lest any \add of them\add* should sim out, and escape.
But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stayed them from their purpose; and commanded that they ho could sim should cast themselves overboard, and get first to the land;
and the rest, some on planks, and some on \add other\add* things from the ship. And so it came to pass, that they all escaped safe to the land.
And hen e ere escaped, then e kne that the island as called Melita.
And the barbarians shoed us no common kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us all, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
But hen Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out by reason of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

And hen the barbarians sa the \add venomous\add* creature hanging from his hand, they said one to another, No doubt this man is a murderer, hom, though he hath escaped from the sea, yet Justice hath not suffered to live.
Hobeit he shook off the creature into the fire, and took no harm.

But they expected that he ould have sollen, or fallen don dead suddenly: but hen they ere long in expectation and beheld nothing amiss come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he as a god.
No in the neighborhood of that place ere lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius; ho received us, and entertained us three days courteously.
And it as so, that the father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery: unto hom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laying his hands on him healed him.
And hen this as done, the rest also that had diseases in the island came, and ere cured:
ho also honored us ith many honors; and hen e sailed, they put on board such things as e needed.
And after three months e set sail in a ship of Alexandria hich had intered in the island, hose sign as The Tin Brothers.
And touching at Syracuse, e tarried there three days.
And from thence e made a circuit, and arrived at Rhegium: and after one day a south ind sprang up, and on the second day e came to Puteoli;
here e found brethren, and ere entreated to tarry ith them seven days: and so e came to Rome.
And from thence the brethren, hen they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns; hom hen Paul sa, he thanked God, and took courage.
And hen e entered into Rome, Paul as suffered to abide by himself ith the soldier that guarded him.

And it came to pass, that after three days he called together those that ere the chief of the Jes: and hen they ere come together, he said unto them, I, brethren, though I had done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers, yet as delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans:
ho, hen they had examined me, desired to set me at liberty, because there as no cause of death in me.
But hen the Jes spake against it, I as constrained to appeal unto Cæsar; not that I had aught hereof to accuse my nation.
For this cause therefore did I entreat you to see and to speak ith \add me\add*: for because of the hope of Israel I am bound ith this chain.
And they said unto him, We neither received letters from Judæa concerning thee, nor did any of the brethren come hither and report or speak any harm of thee.
But e desire to hear of thee hat thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, it is knon to us that everyhere it is spoken against.

And hen they had appointed him a day, they came to him into his lodging in great number; to hom he expounded \add the matter\add*, testifying the kingdom of God, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the la of Moses and from the prophets, from morning till evening.
And some believed the things hich ere spoken, and some disbelieved.
And hen they agreed not among themselves, they departed after that Paul had spoken one ord, Well spake the Holy Spirit through Isaiah the prophet unto your fathers,
saying, Go thou unto this people, and say, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall in no ise understand; And seeing ye shall see, and shall in no ise perceive:

For this people’s heart is axed gross, And their ears are dull of hearing, And their eyes they have closed; Lest haply they should perceive ith their eyes, And hear ith their ears, And understand ith their heart, And should turn again, And I should heal them.
Be it knon therefore unto you, that this salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles: they ill also hear.
And he abode to hole years in his on hired delling, and received all that ent in unto him,
preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ ith all boldness, none forbidding him.
Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called \add to be\add* an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,
hich he promised afore through his prophets in the holy scriptures,
concerning his Son, ho as born of the seed of David according to the flesh,
ho as declared \add to be\add* the Son of God ith poer, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead; \add even\add* Jesus Christ our Lord,
through hom e received grace and apostleship, unto obedience of faith among all the nations, for his name’s sake;
among hom are ye also, called \add to be\add* Jesus Christ’s:
to all that are in Rome, beloved of God, called \add to be\add* saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. \b
First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is proclaimed throughout the hole orld.
For God is my itness, hom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of his Son, ho unceasingly I make mention of you, alays in my prayers
making request, if by any means no at length I may be prospered by the ill of God to come unto you.
For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;
that is, that I ith you may be comforted in you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.
And I ould not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you ( and as hindered hitherto), that I might have some fruit in you also, even as in the rest of the Gentiles.
I am debtor both to Greeks and to Barbarians, both to the ise and to the foolish.
So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you also that are in Rome.
For I am not ashamed of the gospel: for it is the poer of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Je first, and also to the Greek.
For therein is revealed a righteousness of God from faith unto faith: as it is ritten, But the righteous shall live by faith.
For the rath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, ho hinder the truth in unrighteousness;
because that hich is knon of God is manifest in them; for God manifested it unto them.

For the invisible things of him since the creation of the orld are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, \add even\add* his everlasting poer and divinity; that they may be ithout excuse:
because that, knoing God, they glorified him not as God, neither gave thanks; but became vain in their reasonings, and their senseless heart as darkened.
Professing themselves to be ise, they became fools,
and changed the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, and four-footed beasts, and creeping things.
Wherefore God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts unto uncleanness, that their bodies should be dishonored among themselves:
for that they exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and orshipped and served the creature rather than the Creator, ho is blessed for ever. Amen.
For this cause God gave them up unto vile passions: for their omen changed the natural use into that hich is against nature:

and likeise also the men, leaving the natural use of the oman, burned in their lust one toard another, men ith men orking unseemliness, and receiving in themselves that recompense of their error hich as due.
And even as they refused to have God in \add their\add* knoledge, God gave them up unto a reprobate mind, to do those things hich are not fitting;
being filled ith all unrighteousness, ickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malignity; hisperers,
backbiters, hateful to God, insolent, haughty, boastful, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
ithout understanding, covenant-breakers, ithout natural affection, unmerciful:
ho, knoing the ordinance of God, that they that practise such things are orthy of death, not only do the same, but also consent ith them that practise them.
Wherefore thou art ithout excuse, O man, hosoever thou art that judgest: for herein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest dost practise the same things.
And e kno that the judgment of God is according to truth against them that practise such things.
And reckonest thou this, O man, ho judgest them that practise such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?
Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering, not knoing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?
but after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up for thyself rath in the day of rath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;
ho ill render to every man according to his orks:
to them that by patience in ell-doing seek for glory and honor and incorruption, eternal life:
but unto them that are factious, and obey not the truth, but obey unrighteousness, \add shall be\add* rath and indignation,
tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that orketh evil, of the Je first, and also of the Greek;
but glory and honor and peace to every man that orketh good, to the Je first, and also to the Greek:
for there is no respect of persons ith God.
For as many as have sinned ithout the la shall also perish ithout the la: and as many as have sinned under the la shall be judged by the la;
for not the hearers of the la are just before God, but the doers of the la shall be justified;
( for hen Gentiles that have not the la do by nature the things of the la, these, not having the la, are the la unto themselves;
in that they sho the ork of the la ritten in their hearts, their conscience bearing itness thereith, and their thoughts one ith another accusing or else excusing \add them\add*);
in the day hen God shall judge the secrets of men, according to my gospel, by Jesus Christ.
But if thou bearest the name of a Je, and restest upon the la, and gloriest in God,
and knoest his ill, and approvest the things that are excellent, being instructed out of the la,
and art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them that are in darkness,
a corrector of the foolish, a teacher of babes, having in the la the form of knoledge and of the truth;
thou therefore that teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal?
thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou rob temples?
thou ho gloriest in the la, through thy transgression of the la dishonorest thou God?
For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, even as it is ritten.
For circumcision indeed profiteth, if thou be a doer of the la: but if thou be a transgressor of the la, thy circumcision is become uncircumcision.
If therefore the uncircumcision keep the ordinances of the la, shall not his uncircumcision be reckoned for circumcision?
and shall not the uncircumcision hich is by nature, if it fulfil the la, judge thee, ho ith the letter and circumcision art a transgressor of the la?
For he is not a Je ho is one outardly; neither is that circumcision hich is outard in the flesh:
but he is a Je ho is one inardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit not in the letter; hose praise is not of men, but of God.
What advantage then hath the Je? or hat is the profit of circumcision?
Much every ay: first of all, that they ere intrusted ith the oracles of God.
For hat if some ere ithout faith? shall their ant of faith make of none effect the faithfulness of God?
God forbid: yea, let God be found true, but every man a liar; as it is ritten, That thou mightest be justified in thy ords, And mightest prevail hen thou comest into judgment.
But if our unrighteousness commendeth the righteousness of God, hat shall e say? Is God unrighteous ho visiteth ith rath? ( I speak after the manner of men.)
God forbid: for then ho shall God judge the orld?
But if the truth of God through my lie abounded unto his glory, hy am I also still judged as a sinner?
and hy not ( as e are slanderously reported, and as some affirm that e say), Let us do evil, that good may come? hose condemnation is just.
What then? are e better than they? No, in no ise: for e before laid to the charge both of Jes and Greeks, that they are all under sin;
as it is ritten, There is none righteous, no, not one;
There is none that understandeth, There is none that seeketh after God;
They have all turned aside, they are together become unprofitable; There is none that doeth good, no, not so much as one:
Their throat is an open sepulchre; With their tongues they have used deceit: The poison of asps is under their lips:
Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness:
Their feet are sift to shed blood;
Destruction and misery are in their ays;
And the ay of peace have they not knon:
There is no fear of God before their eyes.
No e kno that hat things soever the la saith, it speaketh to them that are under the la; that every mouth may be stopped, and all the orld may be brought under the judgment of God:
because by the orks of the la shall no flesh be justified in his sight; for through the la \add cometh\add* the knoledge of sin.
But no apart from the la a righteousness of God hath been manifested, being itnessed by the la and the prophets;
even the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ unto all them that believe; for there is no distinction;
for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God;
being justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus:
hom God set forth \add to be\add* a propitiation, through faith, in his blood, to sho his righteousness because of the passing over of the sins done aforetime, in the forbearance of God;
for the shoing, \add I say\add*, of his righteousness at this present season: that he might himself be just, and the justifier of him that hath faith in Jesus.
Where then is the glorying? It is excluded. By hat manner of la? of orks? Nay: but by a la of faith.
We reckon therefore that a man is justified by faith apart from the orks of the la.
Or is God \add the God\add* of Jes only? is he not \add the God\add* of Gentiles also? Yea, of Gentiles also:
if so be that God is one, and he shall justify the circumcision by faith, and the uncircumcision through faith.
Do e then make the la of none effect through faith? God forbid: nay, e establish the la.
What then shall e say that Abraham, our forefather, hath found according to the flesh?
For if Abraham as justified by orks, he hath hereof to glory; but not toard God.
For hat saith the scripture? And Abraham believed God, and it as reckoned unto him for righteousness.
No to him that orketh, the reard is not reckoned as of grace, but as of debt.
But to him that orketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is reckoned for righteousness.
Even as David also pronounceth blessing upon the man, unto hom God reckoneth righteousness apart from orks,
\add saying\add*, Blessed are they hose iniquities are forgiven, And hose sins are covered.
Blessed is the man to hom the Lord ill not reckon sin.
Is this blessing then pronounced upon the circumcision, or upon the uncircumcision also? for e say, To Abraham his faith as reckoned for righteousness.
Ho then as it reckoned? hen he as in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision:

and he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith hich he had hile he as in uncircumcision: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be in uncircumcision, that righteousness might be reckoned unto them;
and the father of circumcision to them ho not only are of the circumcision, but ho also alk in the steps of that faith of our father Abraham hich he had in uncircumcision.
For not through the la as the promise to Abraham or to his seed that he should be heir of the orld, but through the righteousness of faith.
For if they that are of the la are heirs, faith is made void, and the promise is made of none effect:
for the la orketh rath; but here there is no la, neither is there transgression.

For this cause \add it is\add* of faith, that \add it may be\add* according to grace; to the end that the promise may be sure to all the seed; not to that only hich is of the la, but to that also hich is of the faith of Abraham, ho is the father of us all
( as it is ritten, A father of many nations have I made thee) before him hom he believed, \add even\add* God, ho giveth life to the dead, and calleth the things that are not, as though they ere.
Who in hope believed against hope, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that hich had been spoken, So shall thy seed be.
And ithout being eakened in faith he considered his on body no as good as dead ( he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah’s omb;
yet, looking unto the promise of God, he avered not through unbelief, but axed strong through faith, giving glory to God,
and being fully assured that hat he had promised, he as able also to perform.
Wherefore also it as reckoned unto him for righteousness.
No it as not ritten for his sake alone, that it as reckoned unto him;
but for our sake also, unto hom it shall be reckoned, ho believe on him that raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,
ho as delivered up for our trespasses, and as raised for our justification.
Being therefore justified by faith, e have peace ith God through our Lord Jesus Christ;
through hom also e have had our access by faith into this grace herein e stand; and e rejoice in hope of the glory of God.
And not only so, but e also rejoice in our tribulations: knoing that tribulation orketh stedfastness;
and stedfastness, approvedness; and approvedness, hope:
and hope putteth not to shame; because the love of God hath been shed abroad in our hearts through the Holy Spirit hich as given unto us.
For hile e ere yet eak, in due season Christ died for the ungodly.
For scarcely for a righteous man ill one die: for peradventure for the good man some one ould even dare to die.
But God commendeth his on love toard us, in that, hile e ere yet sinners, Christ died for us.
Much more then, being no justified by his blood, shall e be saved from the rath \add of God\add* through him.
For if, hile e ere enemies, e ere reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, shall e be saved by his life;
and not only so, but e also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through hom e have no received the reconciliation.
Therefore, as through one man sin entered into the orld, and death through sin; and so death passed unto all men, for that all sinned:—
for until the la sin as in the orld; but sin is not imputed hen there is no la.
Nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over them that had not sinned after the likeness of Adam’s transgression, ho is a figure of him that as to come.

And again he saith, Rejoice, ye Gentiles, ith his people.
And again, Praise the Lord, all ye Gentiles; And let all the peoples praise him.
And again, Isaiah saith, There shall be the root of Jesse, And he that ariseth to rule over the Gentiles; On him shall the Gentiles hope.
No the God of hope fill you ith all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, in the poer of the Holy Spirit.
And I myself also am persuaded of you, my brethren, that ye yourselves are full of goodness, filled ith all knoledge, able also to admonish one another.
But I rite the more boldly unto you in some measure, as putting you again in remembrance, because of the grace that as given me of God,
that I should be a minister of Christ Jesus unto the Gentiles, ministering the gospel of God, that the offering up of the Gentiles might be made acceptable, being sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
I have therefore my glorying in Christ Jesus in things pertaining to God.
For I ill not dare to speak of any things save those hich Christ rought through me, for the obedience of the Gentiles, by ord and deed,
in the poer of signs and onders, in the poer of the Holy Spirit; so that from Jerusalem, and round about even unto Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel of Christ;
yea, making it my aim so to preach the gospel, not here Christ as \add already\add* named, that I might not build upon another man’s foundation;
but, as it is ritten, They shall see, to hom no tidings of him came, And they ho have not heard shall understand.
Wherefore also I as hindered these many times from coming to you:
but no, having no more any place in these regions, and having these many years a longing to come unto you,
hensoever I go unto Spain ( for I hope to see you in my journey, and to be brought on my ay thitherard by you, if first in some measure I shall have been satisfied ith your company)—
but no, \add I say\add*, I go unto Jerusalem, ministering unto the saints.
For it hath been the good pleasure of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor among the saints that are at Jerusalem.

Yea, it hath been their good pleasure; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, they oe it \add to them\add* also to minister unto them in carnal things.
When therefore I have accomplished this, and have sealed to them this fruit, I ill go on by you unto Spain.
And I kno that, hen I come unto you, I shall come in the fulness of the blessing of Christ.
No I beseech you, brethren, by our Lord Jesus Christ, and by the love of the Spirit, that ye strive together ith me in your prayers to God for me;
that I may be delivered from them that are disobedient in Judæa, and \add that\add* my ministration hich \add I have\add* for Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints;
that I may come unto you in joy through the ill of God, and together ith you find rest.
No the God of peace be ith you all. Amen. \b
I commend unto you Phoebe our sister, ho is a servant of the church that is at Cenchreæ:
that ye receive her in the Lord, orthily of the saints, and that ye assist her in hatsoever matter she may have need of you: for she herself also hath been a helper of many, and of mine on self.
Salute Prisca and Aquila my fello-orkers in Christ Jesus,
ho for my life laid don their on necks; unto hom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles:
and \add salute\add* the church that is in their house. Salute Epænetus my beloved, ho is the firstfruits of Asia unto Christ.
Salute Mary, ho bestoed much labor on you.
Salute Andronicus and Junias, my kinsmen, and my fello-prisoners, ho are of note among the apostles, ho also have been in Christ before me.
Salute Ampliatus my beloved in the Lord.
Salute Urbanus our fello-orker in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.

Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brethren that are ith them.
Salute Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints that are ith them.
