They are of the orld: therefore speak they \add as\add* of the orld, and the orld heareth them.
We are of God: he that knoeth God heareth us; he ho is not of God heareth us not. By this e kno the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.
Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is begotten of God, and knoeth God.
He that loveth not knoeth not God; for God is love.
Herein as the love of God manifested in us, that God hath sent his only begotten Son into the orld that e might live through him.
Herein is love, not that e loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son \add to be\add* the propitiation for our sins.
Beloved, if God so loved us, e also ought to love one another.
No man hath beheld God at any time: if e love one another, God abideth in us, and his love is perfected in us:
hereby e kno that e abide in him and he in us, because he hath given us of his Spirit.
And e have beheld and bear itness that the Father hath sent the Son \add to be\add* the Saviour of the orld.
Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God abideth in him, and he in God.
And e kno and have believed the love hich God hath in us. God is love; and he that abideth in love abideth in God, and God abideth in him.
Herein is love made perfect ith us, that e may have boldness in the day of judgment; because as he is, even so are e in this orld.
There is no fear in love: but perfect love casteth out fear, because fear hath punishment; and he that feareth is not made perfect in love.
We love, because he first loved us.
If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother hom he hath seen, cannot love God hom he hath not seen.
And this commandment have e from him, that he ho loveth God love his brother also.
Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is begotten of God: and hosoever loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him.
Hereby e kno that e love the children of God, hen e love God and do his commandments.
For this is the love of God, that e keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.
For hatsoever is begotten of God overcometh the orld: and this is the victory that hath overcome the orld, \add even\add* our faith.
And ho is he that overcometh the orld, but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God?
This is he that came by ater and blood, \add even\add* Jesus Christ; not ith the ater only, but ith the ater and ith the blood.
And it is the Spirit that beareth itness, because the Spirit is the truth.
For there are three ho bear itness, the Spirit, and the ater, and the blood: and the three agree in one.
If e receive the itness of men, the itness of God is greater: for the itness of God is this, that he hath borne itness concerning his Son.
He that believeth on the Son of God hath the itness in him: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he hath not believed in the itness that God hath borne concerning his Son.
And the itness is this, that God gave unto us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
He that hath the Son hath the life; he that hath not the Son of God hath not the life. \b
These things have I ritten unto you, that ye may kno that ye have eternal life, \add even\add* unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God.
And this is the boldness hich e have toard him, that, if e ask anything according to his ill, he heareth us:
and if e kno that he heareth us hatsoever e ask, e kno that e have the petitions hich e have asked of him.

If any man see his brother sinning a sin not unto death, he shall ask, and \add God\add* ill give him life for them that sin not unto death. There is a sin unto death: not concerning this do I say that he should make request.
All unrighteousness is sin: and there is a sin not unto death.
We kno that hosoever is begotten of God sinneth not; but he that as begotten of God keepeth himself, and the evil one toucheth him not.
We kno that e are of God, and the hole orld lieth in the evil one.

And e kno that the Son of God is come, and hath given us an understanding, that e kno him that is true, and e are in him that is true, \add even\add* in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life.
\add My\add* little children, guard yourselves from idols.
The elder unto the elect lady and her children, hom I love in truth; and not I only, but also all they that kno the truth;
for the truth’s sake hich abideth in us, and it shall be ith us for ever:
Grace, mercy, peace shall be ith us, from God the Father, and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love. \b
I rejoice greatly that I have found \add certain\add* of thy children alking in truth, even as e received commandment from the Father.
And no I beseech thee, lady, not as though I rote to thee a ne commandment, but that hich e had from the beginning, that e love one another.
And this is love, that e should alk after his commandments. This is the commandment, even as ye heard from the beginning, that ye should alk in it.
For many deceivers are gone forth into the orld, \add even\add* they that confess not that Jesus Christ cometh in the flesh. This is the deceiver and the antichrist.
Look to yourselves, that ye lose not the things hich e have rought, but that ye receive a full reard.
Whosoever goeth onard and abideth not in the teaching of Christ, hath not God: he that abideth in the teaching, the same hath both the Father and the Son.
If any one cometh unto you, and bringeth not this teaching, receive him not into \add your\add* house, and give him no greeting:
for he that giveth him greeting partaketh in his evil orks. \b
Having many things to rite unto you, I ould not \add rite them\add* ith paper and ink: but I hope to come unto you, and to speak face to face, that your joy may be made full.
The children of thine elect sister salute thee.
The elder unto Gaius the beloved, hom I love in truth.
Beloved, I pray that in all things thou mayest prosper and be in health, even as thy soul prospereth.
For I rejoiced greatly, hen brethren came and bare itness unto thy truth, even as thou alkest in truth.
Greater joy have I none than this, to hear of my children alking in the truth.
Beloved, thou doest a faithful ork in hatsoever thou doest toard them that are brethren and strangers ithal;
ho bare itness to thy love before the church: hom thou ilt do ell to set forard on their journey orthily of God:
because that for the sake of the Name they ent forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles.
We therefore ought to elcome such, that e may be fello-orkers for the truth.
I rote somehat unto the church: but Diotrephes, ho loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not.

Therefore, if I come, I ill bring to remembrance his orks hich he doeth, prating against us ith icked ords: and not content thereith, neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and them that ould he forbiddeth and casteth \add them\add* out of the church.
Beloved, imitate not that hich is evil, but that hich is good. He that doeth good is of God: he that doeth evil hath not seen God.
Demetrius hath the itness of all \add men\add*, and of the truth itself: yea, e also bear itness; and thou knoest that our itness is true. \b
I had many things to rite unto thee, but I am unilling to rite \add them\add* to thee ith ink and pen:
but I hope shortly to see thee, and e shall speak face to face. Peace \add be\add* unto thee. The friends salute thee. Salute the friends by name.
Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to them that are called, beloved in God the Father, and kept for Jesus Christ:
Mercy unto you and peace and love be multiplied. \b

Beloved, hile I as giving all diligence to rite unto you of our common salvation, I as constrained to rite unto you exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith hich as once for all delivered unto the saints.

For there are certain men crept in privily, \add even\add* they ho ere of old ritten of beforehand unto this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.
No I desire to put you in remembrance, though ye kno all things once for all, that the Lord, having saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterard destroyed them that believed not.
And angels that kept not their on principality, but left their proper habitation, he hath kept in everlasting bonds under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.

Even as Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities about them, having in like manner ith these given themselves over to fornication and gone after strange flesh, are set forth as an example, suffering the punishment of eternal fire.
Yet in like manner these also in their dreamings defile the flesh, and set at nought dominion, and rail at dignities.
But Michael the archangel, hen contending ith the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing judgment, but said, The Lord rebuke thee.
But these rail at hatsoever things they kno not: and hat they understand naturally, like the creatures ithout reason, in these things are they destroyed.
Woe unto them! for they ent in the ay of Cain, and ran riotously in the error of Balaam for hire, and perished in the gainsaying of Korah.

These are they ho are hidden rocks in your love-feasts hen they feast ith you, shepherds that ithout fear feed themselves; clouds ithout ater, carried along by inds; autumn trees ithout fruit, tice dead, plucked up by the roots;
ild aves of the sea, foaming out their on shame; andering stars, for hom the blackness of darkness hath been reserved for ever.
And to these also Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying, Behold, the Lord came ith ten thousands of his holy ones,
to execute judgment upon all, and to convict all the ungodly of all their orks of ungodliness hich they have ungodly rought, and of all the hard things hich ungodly sinners have spoken against him.
These are murmurers, complainers, alking after their lusts ( and their mouth speaketh great selling \add ords\add*), shoing respect of persons for the sake of advantage.
But ye, beloved, remember ye the ords hich have been spoken before by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ;
that they said to you, In the last time there shall be mockers, alking after their on ungodly lusts.
These are they ho make separations, sensual, having not the Spirit.
But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit,
keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.
And on some have mercy, ho are in doubt;
and some save, snatching them out of the fire; and on some have mercy ith fear; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh. \b
No unto him that is able to guard you from stumbling, and to set you before the presence of his glory ithout blemish in exceeding joy,
to the only God our Saviour, through Jesus Christ our Lord, \add be\add* glory, majesty, dominion and poer, before all time, and no, and for evermore. Amen.

The Revelation of Jesus Christ, hich God gave him to sho unto his servants, \add even\add* the things hich must shortly come to pass: and he sent and signified \add it\add* by his angel unto his servant John;
ho bare itness of the ord of God, and of the testimony of Jesus Christ, \add even\add* of all things that he sa.
Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the ords of the prophecy, and keep the things that are ritten therein: for the time is at hand. \b
John to the seven churches that are in Asia: Grace to you and peace, from him ho is and ho as and ho is to come; and from the seven Spirits that are before his throne;
and from Jesus Christ, \add ho is\add* the faithful itness, the firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth. Unto him that loveth us, and loosed us from our sins by his blood;
and he made us \add to be\add* a kingdom, \add to be\add* priests unto his God and Father; to him \add be\add* the glory and the dominion for ever and ever. Amen.
Behold, he cometh ith the clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they that pierced him; and all the tribes of the earth shall mourn over him. Even so, Amen.
I am the Alpha and the Omega, saith the Lord God, ho is and ho as and ho is to come, the Almighty.
I John, your brother and partaker ith you in the tribulation and kingdom and patience \add hich are\add* in Jesus, as in the isle that is called Patmos, for the ord of God and the testimony of Jesus.
I as in the Spirit on the Lord’s day, and I heard behind me a great voice, as of a trumpet

saying, What thou seest, rite in a book and send \add it\add* to the seven churches: unto Ephesus, and unto Smyrna, and unto Pergamum, and unto Thyatira, and unto Sardis, and unto Philadelphia, and unto Laodicea.
And I turned to see the voice that spake ith me. And having turned I sa seven golden candlesticks;
and in the midst of the candlesticks one like unto a son of man, clothed ith a garment don to the foot, and girt about at the breasts ith a golden girdle.
And his head and his hair ere hite as hite ool, \add hite\add* as sno; and his eyes ere as a flame of fire;
and his feet like unto burnished brass, as if it had been refined in a furnace; and his voice as the voice of many aters.
And he had in his right hand seven stars: and out of his mouth proceeded a sharp to-edged sord: and his countenance as as the sun shineth in his strength.
And hen I sa him, I fell at his feet as one dead. And he laid his right hand upon me, saying, Fear not; I am the first and the last,
and the Living one; and I as dead, and behold, I am alive for evermore, and I have the keys of death and of Hades.
Write therefore the things hich thou saest, and the things hich are, and the things hich shall come to pass hereafter;

the mystery of the seven stars hich thou saest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks are seven churches.
To the angel of the church in Ephesus rite: These things saith he that holdeth the seven stars in his right hand, he that alketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks:
I kno thy orks, and thy toil and patience, and that thou canst not bear evil men, and didst try them that call themselves apostles, and they are not, and didst find them false;
and thou hast patience and didst bear for my name’ s sake, and hast not gron eary.
But I have \add this\add* against thee, that thou didst leave thy first love.
Remember therefore hence thou art fallen, and repent and do the first orks; or else I come to thee, and ill move thy candlestick out of its place, except thou repent.
But this thou hast, that thou hatest the orks of the Nicolaitans, hich I also hate.
He that hath an ear, let him hear hat the Spirit saith to the churches. To him that overcometh, to him ill I give to eat of the tree of life, hich is in the Paradise of God.
And to the angel of the church in Smyrna rite: These things saith the first and the last, ho as dead, and lived \add again\add*:
I kno thy tribulation, and thy poverty ( but thou art rich), and the blasphemy of them that say they are Jes, and they are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.

Fear not the things hich thou art about to suffer: behold, the devil is about to cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days. Be thou faithful unto death, and I ill give thee the cron of life.
He that hath an ear, let him hear hat the Spirit saith to the churches. He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death.
And to the angel of the church in Pergamum rite: These things saith he that hath the sharp to-edged sord:

I kno here thou dellest, \add even\add* here Satan’s throne is; and thou holdest fast my name, and didst not deny my faith, even in the days of Antipas my itness, my faithful one, ho as killed among you, here Satan delleth.

But I have a fe things against thee, because thou hast there some that hold the teaching of Balaam, ho taught Balak to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed to idols, and to commit fornication.
So hast thou also some that hold the teaching of the Nicolaitans in like manner.
Repent therefore; or else I come to thee quickly, and I ill make ar against them ith the sord of my mouth.

He that hath an ear, let him hear hat the Spirit saith to the churches. To him that overcometh, to him ill I give of the hidden manna, and I ill give him a hite stone, and upon the stone a ne name ritten, hich no one knoeth but he that receiveth it.
And to the angel of the church in Thyatira rite: These things saith the Son of God, ho hath his eyes like a flame of fire, and his feet are like unto burnished brass:
I kno thy orks, and thy love and faith and ministry and patience, and that thy last orks are more than the first.

But I have \add this\add* against thee, that thou sufferest the oman Jezebel, ho calleth herself a prophetess; and she teacheth and seduceth my servants to commit fornication, and to eat things sacrificed to idols.
And I gave her time that she should repent; and she illeth not to repent of her fornication.
Behold, I cast her into a bed, and them that commit adultery ith her into great tribulation, except they repent of her orks.
And I ill kill her children ith death; and all the churches shall kno that I am he that searcheth the reins and hearts: and I ill give unto each one of you according to your orks.
But to you I say, to the rest that are in Thyatira, as many as have not this teaching, ho kno not the deep things of Satan, as they are ont to say; I cast upon you none other burden.
Nevertheless that hich ye have, hold fast till I come.
And he that overcometh, and he that keepeth my orks unto the end, to him ill I give authority over the nations:
and he shall rule them ith a rod of iron, as the vessels of the potter are broken to shivers; as I also have received of my Father:
and I ill give him the morning star.
He that hath an ear, let him hear hat the Spirit saith to the churches.

And to the angel of the church in Sardis rite: These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars: I kno thy orks, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and thou art dead.
Be thou atchful, and establish the things that remain, hich ere ready to die: for I have found no orks of thine perfected before my God.

Remember therefore ho thou hast received and didst hear; and keep \add it\add*, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not atch, I ill come as a thief, and thou shalt not kno hat hour I ill come upon thee.
But thou hast a fe names in Sardis that did not defile their garments: and they shall alk ith me in hite; for they are orthy.
He that overcometh shall thus be arrayed in hite garments; and I ill in no ise blot his name out of the book of life, and I ill confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.
He that hath an ear, let him hear hat the Spirit saith to the churches.

And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia rite: These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth and none shall shut, and that shutteth and none openeth:
I kno thy orks ( behold, I have set before thee a door opened, hich none can shut), that thou hast a little poer, and didst keep my ord, and didst not deny my name.
Behold, I give of the synagogue of Satan, of them that say they are Jes, and they are not, but do lie; behold, I ill make them to come and orship before thy feet, and to kno that I have loved thee.
Because thou didst keep the ord of my patience, I also ill keep thee from the hour of trial, that \add hour\add* hich is to come upon the hole orld, to try them that dell upon the earth.
I come quickly: hold fast that hich thou hast, that no one take thy cron.

He that overcometh, I ill make him a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go out thence no more: and I ill rite upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, the ne Jerusalem, hich cometh don out of heaven from my God, and mine on ne name.
He that hath an ear, let him hear hat the Spirit saith to the churches.
And to the angel of the church in Laodicea rite: These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true itness, the beginning of the creation of God:
I kno thy orks, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I ould thou ert cold or hot.
So because thou art lukearm, and neither hot nor cold, I ill spe thee out of my mouth.
Because thou sayest, I am rich, and have gotten riches, and have need of nothing; and knoest not that thou art the retched one and miserable and poor and blind and naked:

I counsel thee to buy of me gold refined by fire, that thou mayest become rich; and hite garments, that thou mayest clothe thyself, and \add that\add* the shame of thy nakedness be not made manifest; and eyesalve to anoint thine eyes, that thou mayest see.
As many as I love, I reprove and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent.
Behold, I stand at the door and knock: if any man hear my voice and open the door, I ill come in to him, and ill sup ith him, and he ith me.
He that overcometh, I ill give to him to sit don ith me in my throne, as I also overcame, and sat don ith my Father in his throne.
He that hath an ear, let him hear hat the Spirit saith to the churches. \b

After these things I sa, and behold, a door opened in heaven, and the first voice that I heard, \add a voice\add* as of a trumpet speaking ith me, one saying, Come up hither, and I ill sho thee the things hich must come to pass hereafter.
Straightay I as in the Spirit: and behold, there as a throne set in heaven, and one sitting upon the throne;
and he that sat \add as\add* to look upon like a jasper stone and a sardius: and \add there as\add* a rainbo round about the throne, like an emerald to look upon.
And round about the throne \add ere\add* four and tenty thrones: and upon the thrones \add I sa\add* four and tenty elders sitting, arrayed in hite garments; and on their heads crons of gold.
And out of the throne proceed lightnings and voices and thunders. And \add there ere\add* seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, hich are the seven Spirits of God;
and before the throne, as it ere a sea of glass like unto crystal; and in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, four living creatures full of eyes before and behind.
And the first creature \add as\add* like a lion, and the second creature like a calf, and the third creature had a face as of a man, and the fourth creature \add as\add* like a flying eagle.

And the four living creatures, having each one of them six ings, are full of eyes round about and ithin: and they have no rest day and night, saying, \pi1 Holy, holy, holy, \add is\add* the Lord God, the Almighty, ho as and ho is and ho is to come.
And hen the living creatures shall give glory and honor and thanks to him that sitteth on the throne, to him that liveth for ever and ever,
the four and tenty elders shall fall don before him that sitteth on the throne, and shall orship him that liveth for ever and ever, and shall cast their crons before the throne, saying, \pi1
Worthy art thou, our Lord and our God, to receive the glory and the honor and the poer: for thou didst create all things, and because of thy ill they ere, and ere created.
And I sa in the right hand of him that sat on the throne a book ritten ithin and on the back, close sealed ith seven seals.
And I sa a strong angel proclaiming ith a great voice, Who is orthy to open the book, and to loose the seals thereof?
And no one in the heaven, or on the earth, or under the earth, as able to open the book, or to look thereon.
And I ept much, because no one as found orthy to open the book, or to look thereon:
and one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not; behold, the Lion that is of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, hath overcome to open the book and the seven seals thereof.

And I sa in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain, having seven horns, and seven eyes, hich are the seven Spirits of God, sent forth into all the earth.
And he came, and he taketh \add it\add* out of the right hand of him that sat on the throne.

And hen he had taken the book, the four living creatures and the four and tenty elders fell don before the Lamb, having each one a harp, and golden bols full of incense, hich are the prayers of the saints.

And they sing a ne song, saying, \pi1 Worthy art thou to take the book, and to open the seals thereof: for thou ast slain, and didst purchase unto God ith thy blood \add men\add* of every tribe, and tongue, and people, and nation,
and madest them \add to be\add* unto our God a kingdom and priests; and they reign upon the earth.
And I sa, and I heard a voice of many angels round about the throne and the living creatures and the elders; and the number of them as ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands;
saying ith a great voice, \pi1 Worthy is the Lamb that hath been slain to receive the poer, and riches, and isdom, and might, and honor, and glory, and blessing.

And every created thing hich is in the heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and on the sea, and all things that are in them, heard I saying, \pi1 Unto him that sitteth on the throne, and unto the Lamb, \add be\add* the blessing, and the honor, and the glory, and the dominion, for ever and ever.
And the four living creatures said, Amen. And the elders fell don and orshipped. \b
And I sa hen the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying as ith a voice of thunder, Come.
And I sa, and behold, a hite horse, and he that sat thereon had a bo; and there as given unto him a cron: and he came forth conquering, and to conquer.
And hen he opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, Come.

And another \add horse\add* came forth, a red horse: and to him that sat thereon it as given to take peace from the earth, and that they should slay one another: and there as given unto him a great sord.
And hen he opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying, Come. And I sa, and behold, a black horse; and he that sat thereon had a balance in his hand.
And I heard as it ere a voice in the midst of the four living creatures saying, A measure of heat for a shilling, and three measures of barley for a shilling; and the oil and the ine hurt thou not.
And hen he opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying, Come.

And I sa, and behold, a pale horse: and he that sat upon him, his name as Death; and Hades folloed ith him. And there as given unto them authority over the fourth part of the earth, to kill ith sord, and ith famine, and ith death, and by the ild beasts of the earth.
And hen he opened the fifth seal, I sa underneath the altar the souls of them that had been slain for the ord of God, and for the testimony hich they held:
and they cried ith a great voice, saying, Ho long, O Master, the holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dell on the earth?

And there as given them to each one a hite robe; and it as said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little time, until their fello-servants also and their brethren, ho should be killed even as they ere, should have fulfilled \add their course\add*.
And I sa hen he opened the sixth seal, and there as a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the hole moon became as blood;
and the stars of the heaven fell unto the earth, as a fig tree casteth her unripe figs hen she is shaken of a great ind.
And the heaven as removed as a scroll hen it is rolled up; and every mountain and island ere moved out of their places.
And the kings of the earth, and the princes, and the chief captains, and the rich, and the strong, and every bondman and freeman, hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains;
and they say to the mountains and to the rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the rath of the Lamb:
for the great day of their rath is come; and ho is able to stand?
After this I sa four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding the four inds of the earth, that no ind should blo on the earth, or on the sea, or upon any tree.
And I sa another angel ascend from the sunrising, having the seal of the living God: and he cried ith a great voice to the four angels to hom it as given to hurt the earth and the sea,
saying, Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till e shall have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads.
And I heard the number of them that ere sealed, a hundred and forty and four thousand, sealed out of every tribe of the children of Israel:
Of the tribe of Judah \add ere\add* sealed telve thousand; Of the tribe of Reuben telve thousand; Of the tribe of Gad telve thousand;
Of the tribe of Asher telve thousand; Of the tribe of Naphtali telve thousand; Of the tribe of Manasseh telve thousand;
Of the tribe of Simeon telve thousand; Of the tribe of Levi telve thousand; Of the tribe of Issachar telve thousand;
Of the tribe of Zebulun telve thousand; Of the tribe of Joseph telve thousand; Of the tribe of Benjamin \add ere\add* sealed telve thousand.

After these things I sa, and behold, a great multitude, hich no man could number, out of every nation and of \add all\add* tribes and peoples and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, arrayed in hite robes, and palms in their hands;

And the shapes of the locusts ere like unto horses prepared for ar; and upon their heads as it ere crons like unto gold, and their faces ere as men’s faces.

And I sa another strong angel coming don out of heaven, arrayed ith a cloud; and the rainbo as upon his head, and his face as as the sun, and his feet as pillars of fire;

And the kings of the earth, ho committed fornication and lived antonly ith her, shall eep and ail over her, hen they look upon the smoke of her burning,
standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Woe, oe, the great city, Babylon, the strong city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.
And the merchants of the earth eep and mourn over her, for no man buyeth their merchandise any more;

merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stone, and pearls, and fine linen, and purple, and silk, and scarlet; and all thyine ood, and every vessel of ivory, and every vessel made of most precious ood, and of brass, and iron, and marble;

and cinnamon, and spice, and incense, and ointment, and frankincense, and ine, and oil, and fine flour, and heat, and cattle, and sheep; and \add merchandise\add* of horses and chariots and slaves; and souls of men.
And the fruits hich thy soul lusted after are gone from thee, and all things that ere dainty and sumptuous are perished from thee, and \add men\add* shall find them no more at all.
The merchants of these things, ho ere made rich by her, shall stand afar off for the fear of her torment, eeping and mourning;
saying, Woe, oe, the great city, she that as arrayed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, and decked ith gold and precious stone and pearl!
